N. Jackson.wikitext:
{{Infobox character |games =none |mentions =FO76 |image =Enclave Symbol (FO3).png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |affiliation =[[Enclave (Fallout 76)|Enclave]] |role =Communications expert
Computer scientist |rank =Captain |actor =[[Peter McHugh]] |edid =NPCM_EN_CaptainJackson |formid ={{ID|003cb044}} }} '''Captain N. Jackson''' was an [[Appalachia]]n [[Enclave (Fallout 76)|Enclave]] officer. ==Background== An Enclave officer in charge of field operations, Jackson was overseeing the mounting of communications dishes throughout Appalachia. He doubted the usefulness of using humans instead of robots for work, and complained about it after a near-fatal incident that [[Donnelley|Sergeant Donnelley]] suffered while installing a surveillance dish.[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#RE: Surveillance Dishes]] However, Jackson was more than just a technician. He was also a gifted computer scientist and did, in fact, correctly figure out how the Appalachian missile defense worked. The complexity of the system took three sticks of chalk to explain to [[Ragnarsdottir|Major Ragnarsdottir]] and centered on the fact that unless the system believed Appalachia was under direct threat, the DEFCON would remain at low levels. His discovery was the primary reason behind [[Thomas Eckhart|President Eckhart's]] decision to conduct false flag operations to trick the system.[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#Tricking DEFCON]] Dismayed and demoralized by the brazen disregard for American life, Jackson and other loyalists of [[Ellen Santiago]] staged an open revolt. Fighting off robots and Eckhart's troops, Jackson and Ragnarsdottir revived Santiago, who gladly assumed leadership of the uprising.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#8.5.2|Whitespring surveillance recording 8.5.2.]] However, while Eckhart was placed under arrest, the uprising ultimately failed. [[MODUS]], under the threat of destruction, retaliated against the humans by detonating the weapons lab, killing General Santiago as well as rupturing a toxin tank that leaked into the air circulation system. MODUS promptly sealed the bunker, dooming all within, including Jackson.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#Assaultron|Whitespring surveillance recordings; Assaultron]] ==Appearances== Captain N. Jackson is mentioned {{In|FO76}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Enclave}} [[Category:Fallout 76 mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 Enclave characters]] [[ru:Капитан Джексон]]

{{Infobox character |games =none |mentions =FO76 |name =Major Ragnarsdottir |image = |status =Deceased |dod =c. 2085|dod verified=yes |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |affiliation =[[Enclave (Fallout 76)|Appalachian Enclave]] (formerly)

But I'll talk to some people. I mean, [[MODUS]] can call in flying robots with a thought. Why isn't he doing it?}} '''Major Ragnarsdottir''' was a member of [[Thomas Eckhart]]'s [[Enclave (Fallout 76)|division]] of the [[Enclave]] at [[the Whitespring bunker]] in [[Appalachia]] until his death circa 2085. He is mentioned {{In|FO76}}. ==Background== Ragnarsdottir was a military officer under President Thomas Eckhart in the Appalachian Enclave at the Whitespring bunker. Ragnarsdottir's background is unclear; he may have either been present in the Whitespring bunker ever since the [[Great War]], or he may have been a member of then-[[Ellen Santiago|Colonel Ellen Santiago]]'s unit in the [[United States Armed Forces]] in [[Washington, D.C.]] who chose to follow her to Appalachia to search for surviving government forces before discovering (and subsequently joining) the Enclave circa 2081.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#5.2.4|Whitespring surveillance recording 5.2.4]]
{{Small|Corresponding to November 27, 2081, based on the [[Whitespring dating system]]}}[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#5.3.1|Whitespring surveillance recording 5.3.1]]
{{Small|Corresponding to December 24, 2081, based on the [[Whitespring dating system]]}}{{Ref|(Note)}} In any case, Ragnarsdottir was known to be a major in the Appalachian Enclave's military command structure after the arrival of Ellen Santiago's unit to the Whitespring bunker.{{Ref|(Note)}} By the time that Eckhart declared himself president, Ragnarsdottir had become responsible for managing various military and scouting assignments and liasing with [[MODUS]] and other staff. When [[Donnelley|Sergeant Donnelley]] nearly fell to his death while installing survey communications dishes in [[Charleston]], Ragnarsdottir agreed to [[N. Jackson|Captain N. Jackson's]] request to ask if MODUS could install the dishes with its own robots.[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#RE: Surveillance Dishes|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; military work station, RE: Surveillance Dishes]] In another instance, Ragnarsdottir assigned [[Felix Parson|Ltc. Felix Parson]] to investigate the disappearance of the research team at [[Tanagra Town|Remote Lab 1.2]], on request from [[Norris|Dr. Norris]] from the science team.[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#RE: Remote Lab 1.2|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; military work station, RE: Remote Lab 1.2]][[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#{ERROR!} RE: Remote Lab 1.2 Access Code|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; military work station, {ERROR!} RE: Remote Lab 1.2 Access Code]] The major also made frequent ammo requisitions to the bunker's production team, but these were denied due to the inability for [[Plasma cartridge (Fallout 76)|plasma cartridge]] production to match his demands, and the major was instead reprimanded by President Eckhart to have his men be more sparing with ammo.[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#RE: Ammunition Requisition|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; military work station, RE: Ammunition Requisition]] ===Revolt=== After Santiago was promoted to general, Ragnarsdottir and his men were put to work on accessing the [[Appalachian Automated Launch System]] to retaliate against [[China]].[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#ARCHIVE: Ellen Santiago {Gen.}|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; archival terminal, ARCHIVE: Ellen Santiago {Gen.}]] This included work to ensure safe passage through [[Site Alpha]],[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#Accessing the Silos|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; archival terminal, Accessing the Silos]] decode the [[Silo Alpha code piece|Silo Alpha launch codes]] (not Ragnarsdottir's specialty, as he and his brothers were self-admittedly "recess men"),[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#The Code Pieces|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; archival terminal, The Code Pieces]] and elevate [[DEFCON]] to gain access to the [[nuclear keycard]]s. After he heard [[Jefferson Grey|Agent Jefferson Grey]]'s idea to trick DEFCON by spreading Chinese [[Liberator]] robots, Ragnarsdottir had his first doubts about Eckhart's plans: if even this turned out not to work, how much further would they be willing to go? Per his report to Santiago, Ragnarsdottir did not like "putting Appalachia through hell," but felt it was their best way to "win [the] war" at this point... but only if it could be done in a "managed way."[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#Tricking DEFCON|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; archival terminal, Tricking DEFCON]] As Eckhart scaled up the plans to achieve DEFCON 1, unleashing [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|super mutants]] and other creatures on Appalachia, General Santiago broke ranks, threatening to leave with her men, but was instead pacified with an injection and kept in a medically-induced coma by Eckhart.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#6.9.7|Whitespring surveillance recording 6.9.7]]
{{Small|Corresponding to June 30, 2083, based on the [[Whitespring dating system]]}} Eventually, once Eckhart took the final step of unleashing the [[scorchbeast]]s (inadvertently dooming the region via the [[Scorched Plague]]), Ragnarsdottir, Jackson, and all the others unwilling to destroy Appalachia revolted, with the major and the captain waking Santiago to inform her of the situation and regain her leadership.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#8.5.2|Whitespring surveillance recording 8.5.2]]
{{Small|Corresponding to February 25, 2085, based on the [[Whitespring dating system]]}} On Santiago's orders, Ragnarsdottir and the others placed Eckhart under arrest and moved to destroy MODUS and the bunker's systems to prevent them from being used against Appalachia in the future. Ragnarsdottir went to secure the bunker entrance, while Donnelley and others were sent to plant explosives on MODUS' memory banks. However, while Ragnarsdottir succeeded, the others only managed to damage, not destroy, MODUS.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#8.5.4|Whitespring surveillance recording 8.5.4]]
{{Small|Corresponding to February 27, 2085, based on the [[Whitespring dating system]]}} MODUS retaliated and destroyed the weapons lab, causing a deadly biological agent to leak into the air circulation system, then placed the bunker under quarantine, fatally suffocating Ragnarsdottir and all other human inhabitants of the bunker.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#Assaultron|Whitespring surveillance recordings; Assaultron]] ==Notes== * {{Note|(Note)}} Ragnarsdottir's origins are unclear. The following notes on chronology are made using the estimated [[Whitespring dating system]]; thus, the date numbers may be slightly off, but the relative order of events should be correct. ** The earliest confirmable source in which Ragnarsdottir's name appears, chronologically, is in the terminal entry "[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#RE: Ammunition Requisition|RE: Ammunition Requisition]]," at which point Thomas Eckhart had already become president (circa October 2082, based on [[Whitespring surveillance recordings#6.1.0|Whitespring surveillance recording 6.1.0]]), postdating Ellen Santiago's arrival. ** There is one other possibly earlier source, but it is based on removed content: The missing Enclave lab at Tanagra Town has a removed terminal which references the Enclave's discovery of [[scorchbeast]]s{{Removed}} [[Tanagra Town terminal entries#2.5|Tanagra Town terminal entries; terminal, 2.5]] circa January 2082 (dated based on [[Whitespring surveillance recordings#5.4.8|Whitespring surveillance recording 5.4.8]]). This is the earliest time that the lab's failure which Ragnarsdottir was tapped to investigate, mentioned in the entry "[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#RE: Remote Lab 1.2|RE: Remote Lab 1.2]]," can have occurred, and it still postdates Ellen Santiago's arrival. ** In [[Whitespring surveillance recordings#2.9.6|Whitespring surveillance recording 2.9.6]], a much earlier recording circa 2079, an Enclave officer is heard talking, and Eckhart refers to him as a major. This character is most likely not Ragnarsdottir, as their voices are completely different (the officer is voiced by [[Dave B. Mitchell]], while Ragnarsdottir is voiced by [[Jason Linere-White]]). ==Appearances== Major Ragnarsdottir is mentioned {{In|FO76}}. ==Behind the scenes== The surname "Ragnarsdottir" follows patronymic Icelandic naming conventions, being a combination of the father's first name and the suffix -son for a male child and -dóttir for a female child. However, the character of Ragnarsdottir is referred to with male pronouns, while "Ragnarsdottir" literally means "Ragnar's daughter." ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Enclave}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Fallout 76 Enclave characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 mentioned-only characters]] [[ru:Майор Рагнарсдоттир]]

But we've tried half-measures. If we're going to overcome DEFCON, we need to be committed.|sound=Thomas Eckhart.ogg}} '''Thomas Eckhart''' was the last Secretary of Agriculture in the [[United States government]] before the [[Great War]] and subsequently the president of the [[Enclave (Fallout 76)|Appalachian detachment]] of the [[Enclave]] between [[Timeline (2050-2099)#2083|2083]]-[[Timeline (2050-2099)#2086|2086]]. Eckhart consolidated power within the [[the Whitespring bunker|Whitespring Congressional Bunker]], all while seeking to resume the war against [[China]] using [[Appalachia]]'s nuclear stockpile. Eckhart's plan to lower the [[DEFCON]] level enough to access the nukes, involving releasing mutated [[scorchbeast]]s into the region, made him ultimately responsible for the spread of the [[Scorched Plague]]. ==Background== Thomas Eckhart's drive and dedication eventually led him to the position of Secretary of Agriculture in the last United States [[Last Cabinet of the United States|administration]], where he became a fervent promoter of the idea of a preemptive nuclear strike on China,The precise reasons for his fervent anti-communism are not directly stated, but a terminal entry not used in the game sheds light on this. See [[#Behind the scenes|this section]] for details. an idea that was consistently dismissed by the powers that be, with Eckhart recommended to focus on pursuing the goals of his department.[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#I'm Sorry, Thomas|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; Archival terminal, Data Archives, ARCHIVE: Thomas Eckhart {Pres*}, I'm Sorry, Thomas]] However, his ardent opposition to [[communism]] and fervent nationalism led to him becoming a natural candidate for selection into the innermost enclave of power of the United States government. The relatively benign Department of Agriculture was the perfect cover for funding [[the Whitespring bunker]], with money funneled from the department's coffers under Secretary Eckhart's oversight at a grand scale.[[Charleston Capitol Building terminal entries#Subject: Intelligence Committee|Charleston Capitol Building terminal entries; Senator Blackwell's terminal, Login, Correspondence, T., Subject: Intelligence Committee]] The amount of time and money spent by the department did not escape notice, especially from [[Sam Blackwell|Senator Sam Blackwell]] of Appalachia and his contacts. However, the senator did not manage to blow the lid off the project.[[Charleston Capitol Building terminal entries#Subject: Dept. of Agriculture|Charleston Capitol Building terminal entries; Senator Blackwell's terminal, Login, Correspondence, T., Subject: Dept. of Agriculture]] ===Rise to Power=== When the early warning systems activated on [[Great War|October 23, 2077]], as Enclave and regular government officials alike scrambled for shelter from the coming nuclear war, Eckhart was already in position beneath the Whitespring. He was one of the few to make it to safety. Only a select few other members of the Enclave made it to safety, including the Secretary of the Interior and a number of high-ranking officers. The rest were left to fend for themselves.[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#Cabinet Nuclear Alarm Logs|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; Archival terminal, Data Archives, ARCHIVE: Top Secret, Cabinet Nuclear Alarm Logs]] All non-Enclave personnel who arrived at the Whitespring bunker were rounded up and shot, including members of Congress who thought that a Congressional bunker would save their lives.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#1.1.2|Whitespring surveillance recording 1.1.2]] The survivors were horrified to learn that connections to [[Raven Rock]] and the [[Last President of the United States|President]] at [[Enclave Oil Rig|Control Station ENCLAVE]] were lost, leaving them isolated.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#1.1.5|Whitespring surveillance recording 1.1.5]] However, it played right into Eckhart's plans, allowing him to seize the opportunity and lead the fight against communism. After gathering the survivors in the conference room, Eckhart informed them of the isolation and the death of the [[Last Secretary of the Treasury|Secretary of the Treasury]] due to "radiation sickness," then announced himself as the new leader of their "little enclave," as per the [[Wikipedia:United States presidential line of succession|line of presidential succession]].[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#1.1.7|Whitespring surveillance recording 1.1.7]] He then offered them a choice: Using the Whitespring to continue the war against communism and the enemies of America, until no enemies stand against them, or opposing his plans. As the Enclave was supposed to be the bastion of democracy, he called for a vote with their feet. Everyone who supported his idea of using the facility and Appalachian resources was asked to stand at the left side of the room, by the entrance. The rest were to stand against the wall on the opposite side. Many sided with [[Swafford|General Swafford]], who opposed continuing the now pointless war. Eckhart was disappointed but prepared. He had his supporters exit the room, while [[MODUS]] sealed the opposition inside, filling it with a toxic gas. Although the purges entrenched Eckhart's control, he only had 48 people left to "save" democracy with. He wasted no time in briefing the survivors on his plan that involved the complete eradication of communism using any means necessary, with no moral or ethical constraints. It was total war and no option was off-limits, even a repeat of the nuclear nightmare.[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#Meeting Transcript - Entry 1.3.2|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; Mutation serum terminal: A-G, Meeting Transcripts, Meeting Transcript - Entry 1.3.2]] Eckhart had not forgotten his idea of resolving the great ideological struggle with nuclear weapons. However, the biggest obstacle in his plan to use the Appalachian nuclear network was the fact that all but one general, [[T. Harper]], was eliminated in the "vote." He needed a general for his war plan and he needed more people for the Enclave to survive. He ordered MODUS to assign an escort to Harper around the clock, while scouts were to keep out an eye for potential candidates for "recruitment."[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#1.3.3|Whitespring surveillance recording 1.3.3]] By mid-2080,The years are calculated basing on the surveillance recordings, assuming that they follow a Year.Month.Day format and are relative to the activation of the facility on October 23, 2077 (1.1.1). the [[Responders]] became a natural source of recruits, though many would require brainwashing in order to be pressed into the Enclave's ranks. Eckhart was keenly aware that torture would not lead the United States back to supremacy, so he was elated when scouts under [[Ragnarsdottir|Major Ragnarsdottir]] revealed that [[West Tek]]'s FEV research survived the nuclear blasts and, despite his hatred for the Chinese, that a Chinese infiltration base at [[Mama Dolce's Food Processing]] near Morgantown was secured by [[Jefferson Grey|Agent Grey]]. Both of these would become vital parts of his plans. The scouts also revealed that the election system could be hacked, in order to allow Eckhart to become the President of the United States, and by extension, the Enclave.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#2.9.6|Whitespring surveillance recording 2.9.6]] ===Path to the Presidency=== {{sidebar enclave}} [[file:F76 AVA.png|left|thumb|The [[AVA]] system centralized in the bunker, used by Eckhart to grab the title of President for himself.]] However, the path forward proved rocky. Apart from multiple casualties sustained in the process of perfecting [[Fallout 76 mutations|mutation serums]], the plan for unleashing nuclear devastation on China were hampered by the automated safeguards built into the nuclear arsenal. Simply having a general on hand to access the nuclear silos wasn't going to lead to nuclear launches. As work continued on advancing Eckhart's plans, the Enclave experienced a sudden windfall in late 2082, as a group of soldiers led by [[Ellen Santiago|Colonel Ellen Santiago]] arrived at the bunker, acting on rumors they heard about the bunker. With no sensible alternatives, Santiago led her men from the still smoldering remains of [[Washington, D.C.]] to Appalachia, arriving at Eckhart's doorstep. Eckhart was elated to have a veteran at his disposal and lured her into service with promises of revenge against the Chinese.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#5.2.4|Whitespring surveillance recording 5.2.4]] With an influx of veterans, the work towards the eradication of communism advanced at a rapid pace. The experiments with mutations continued in parallel with work on accessing the nuclear arsenal, resulting in many working serums, and the first [[scorchbeast]]s, accidentally created when Enclave scientists exposed irradiated bats to biochemical experiments the previous year. Eckhart ordered further study of the creatures in controlled habitats at the abandoned AMS mining complexes while keeping the officer corps in the dark.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#5.4.8|Whitespring surveillance recording 5.4.8]] He was making a disastrous mistake, but Eckhart had no time for reflection. Just three months later, in January 2083, Eckhart's men completed reprogramming the Appalachian election machines. Although General Harper expressed reservations about mobilizing men to vote for Eckhart, granting him the title of president, the secretary believed it was necessary to give the men of the Enclave an authority to look up to. They only knew two: God and the President, and there was no way to create the former.[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#Meeting Transcript - Entry 5.7.8 (Partial)|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; Cabinet room terminal, Meeting Transcripts, Meeting Transcript - Entry 5.7.8 (Partial)]] ===Planning War=== Eckhart wasted no time in asserting his authority over his subordinates, especially Colonel Santiago. In one instance, he revoked a sergeant's permission to leave the bunker and search for his wife in the region, berating the colonel for giving special leave in wartime and potentially leading an outsider to learn about the bunker and join the Enclave as a "little housewife." Santiago had no choice but to accept Eckhart's stance. However, Eckhart's heavy-handed approach started to make the colonel reconsider her decision to join without full knowledge of what was going on at the Whitespring.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#6.1.0|Whitespring surveillance recording 6.1.0]] The situation deteriorated in late 2083 when General Harper died of heart failure brought on by radiation poisoning. Eckhart's plan for nuclear retaliation crumbled before his very eyes as MODUS attempted in vain to shock the general's heart to life.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#6.2.1|Whitespring surveillance recording 6.2.1]] With his plan thrown off the rails, Eckhart salvaged the situation by sending Santiago to [[Camp McClintock]] and making her earn an automatic promotion to general by exploiting the same system that gave him the presidency. Santiago succeeded, although the way in which she earned the stars disgusted her.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#6.2.4|Whitespring surveillance recording 6.2.4]][[Whitespring surveillance recordings#6.9.7|Whitespring surveillance recording 6.9.7]] Still, it worked for Eckhart. Not only did he have a general and thus the means to access the silos,[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#Accessing the Silos|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; Data Archives, ARCHIVE: Ellen Santiago {Gen.}, Accessing the Silos]] he could also offload the task to seek out nuclear launch codes to her and her men. The search was complicated by the way in which the codes were distributed, assigned to aide de camps to carry on their backs or delivered by [[National Catastrophe Relief Auxiliary]] automated [[Cargobot]]s,[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#The Code Pieces|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; Data Archives, ARCHIVE: Ellen Santiago {Gen.}, The Code Pieces]] but also the fact that even with the key and codes they could not launch without somehow tricking the automated system into raising the alert level to DEFCON 1. Eckhart and Agent Grey already had a plan in motion for this occasion, aiming to use the [[liberator]]s, [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|super mutants]] and the mighty scorchbeasts to unleash hell upon Appalachia and trick the system into believing an invasion was underway. Although everyone wanted to win the war, putting Appalachia through hell was making many reconsider, especially Major Ragnarsdottir, who explained the situation to Santiago.[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#Tricking DEFCON|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; Data Archives, ARCHIVE: Ellen Santiago {Gen.}, Tricking DEFCON]] As the soldiers struggled with their consciences, Eckhart took time to order an assassination of former Senator Sam Blackwell. Remembering the threat he posed before the Great War from his alignment with the [[Free States]], Eckhart realized Blackwell was still in possession of a Senate ID, which would allow access to the bunker, so he sent agents to find and eliminate the former senator. The senator's sudden appearance at [[Harpers Ferry]], and subsequent elimination of an Enclave operative before disappearing again, left Eckhart furious.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#6.6.1|Whitespring surveillance recording 6.6.1]] ===Falling Down=== Believing all the cards to be in his possession, Eckhart ordered the attempts to raise the DEFCON levels to begin. Liberators and super mutants were unleashed on Appalachia, but all they managed to achieve was barely a tick on the DEFCON counter. Angry with the half-measures and lack of success, Eckhart planned to move ahead with even more radical attempts. However, his single-minded pursuit of nuclear capability and the sheer amount of blood shed in the process finally broke the straw. General Santiago realized that revenge against the Chinese was not worth paying such a steep price and confronted Eckhart in July [[Timeline#2084|2084]], threatening to leave with her men. Eckhart tried his usual flattery and playing on Santiago's thirst for revenge, but she remained adamant. Realizing that he was in danger of losing, Eckhart instead chose to incapacitate her with a knock-out agent and keep her in an artificially-induced coma until he had need of her clearance. With no one left to oppose him, Eckhart unleashed the scorchbeasts on Appalachia. The terror and destruction they caused was ultimately successful, raising the alert level to DEFCON 1 by June [[Timeline#2086|2086]]. Dismayed and demoralized by the brazen disregard for American life, Santiago's loyalists and members of Eckhart's officer corps staged an open revolt. Fighting off robots and Eckhart's troops, [[N. Jackson|Captain N. Jackson]] and one-time Eckhart supporter Major Ragnarsdottir revived Santiago, who gladly assumed leadership of the uprising.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#8.5.2|Whitespring surveillance recording 8.5.2.]] However, while Eckhart was placed under arrest, the uprising ultimately failed. Santiago's decision to destroy MODUS backfired and the AI turned on all human members of the Enclave. After an explosion tore out a large part of MODUS' memory, the damaged AI retaliated with an explosion in the weapons lab that killed General Santiago and ruptured a toxin tank that leaked into the air circulation system. MODUS promptly sealed the bunker, dooming all within, including President Thomas Eckhart.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#Assualtron|Whitespring surveillance recordings; Assaultron]] ==Appearances== Thomas Eckhart is mentioned only {{In|FO76}}. ==Behind the scenes== * An unimplemented terminal entry provides additional backstory on Eckhart, stating that he was the son of disgraced American businessman [[Joseph Eckhart]], and was embarrassed at the age of 16 by his father's damning indictment of [[United States of America|U.S.]] capitalism and defection to [[China]]. Bereft of good standing or a company to rule, as it was liquidated and distributed to worker's advocacy programs worldwide, Eckhart turned his bitterness into a single-minded pursuit of power with the goal of eradicating communism and its adherents once and for all.[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#Eckhart Renounces Citizenship!]] ==References== {{References|2}} {{Navbox Enclave}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Fallout 76 mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 Enclave characters]] [[Category:Enclave presidents]] [[Category:Pre-War politicians]] [[Category:Post-War politicians]] [[Category:Department of Agriculture]] [[pl:Thomas Eckhart]] [[ru:Томас Экхарт]] [[zh:Thomas Eckhart]]

'''General T. Harper''' was a high-ranking official of the [[Enclave (Fallout 76)|Enclave]] in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
General Harper was one of several generals stationed in [[the Whitespring bunker]] when the bombs dropped. After Secretary of Agriculture [[Thomas Eckhart]] had himself nominally elected president, he held a vote on whether to continue the war with [[China]]. Those who voted for continuing the war lined up near the room's only exit and those against lined up at the far wall. After the pro-war voters left, everyone still inside was gassed by [[MODUS]] on orders from Eckhart. Harper, being the only general that voted to continue the war, became integral to Eckhart's plans. He ordered MODUS to assign an escort to Harper around the clock, while scouts were to keep out an eye for potential candidates for "recruitment."<ref>[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#1.3.3|Whitespring surveillance recording 1.3.3]]</ref>

After [[N. Jackson]] discovered the way to get inside the Appalachian missile silos, the Enclave held a staff meeting that Harper attended. He questioned the motive behind the mission, and how many men would be mobilized just to vote for [[Thomas Eckhart]] and grant him the title of president. However, Eckhart believed it was necessary to give the men of the Enclave an authority to look up to.<ref>[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#Meeting Transcript - Entry 5.7.2 (Partial)|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; Meeting Transcript - Entry 5.7.2 (Partial)]]</ref>

Despite this, Harper remained loyal to Eckhart and continued to act as a significant military advisor to him. However, he died in [[Timeline#2083|2083]] from [[radiation]] poisoning, as Eckhart's desperate attempts at resuscitation were unsuccessful.<ref>[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#6.2.1|Whitespring surveillance recording 6.2.1]]</ref><ref>[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries#GEN T. Harper|The Whitespring bunker terminal entries; GEN T. Harper]]</ref>

I'd rather eat [[Cram (Fallout 76)|Cram]] every day and never see the sun again than be stuck here... alone.|sound=Abigayle Singh.ogg|Abbie about how how everyone she knows is dead|[[Everyone is gone]]}} '''Abigayle "Abbie" Singh''' was one of the last surviving members of the [[Free States]]. ==Background== Abigayle Singh was a member of the Free States, the last surviving member when the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] discovers her [[Abbie's bunker|bunker]]. She entered her bunker at a young age along with her father [[Niraj Singh|Niraj]], brother [[Calvin Singh|Calvin]], dog Dax, along with three members of the Cohen family, including [[Daniel Cohen]]. Her mother, [[Geneva Singh|Geneva]], was already deceased before they entered the bunker. They all would ride out the [[Great War]] in this bunker. Many of her [[Abbie's bunker terminal entries|terminal entries]] located in the bunker described the difficult living conditions stuck in the bunker, especially on her mental health. When the surface was hospitable enough, Abbie and her family left the bunker in 2079 and began to explore Appalachia along with the other members of the Free States, although they mainly stayed around [[the Mire]] region. At some point, Dax disappeared, and Abbie figured the dog was dead and blamed it on Calvin.[[Abbie's bunker terminal entries#Dax|Abbie's bunker terminal entries; Abbie's terminal, Dax]] Her father heard a message from [[Raleigh Clay]] about survivors attempting to rebuild life at [[Harpers Ferry]], which the Singhs and Cohens agreed to. Although Abbie was not keen on the idea of going to Harpers Ferry, she worked briefly with [[Ella Ames]] in her clinic there, working alongside [[Martha Clay]] as well, but resigned due to social difficulties dealing with the [[Responders]].[[Letter of resignation (Harpers Ferry)|Letter of resignation; Harpers Ferry]] Ella was studying [[Deathclaw (Fallout 76)|deathclaw]] feces due to their radiation properties and named their droppings "bone meal." With the help of Abbie, Ella was able to develop a tracker to help her find the bone meal.[[Ella's research]] A paper note indicates that Abbie was known and respected by [[Juan Diego Sunday|JD Sunday]] and [[Jesus Sunday]].[[Reminder (Fallout 76)|Reminder]] Abbie offered to repair a broken radio belonging to [[Delia Webb]] for free. She also knew [[R. Fields]] and expressed to them about considering going south to [[Watoga]].[[Where are you?]] Unfortunately, in 2086, Harpers Ferry was attacked by a massive [[Scorched]] outbreak and their work on rebuilding the town was lost. To combat the Scorched, her father began to work on a system called the [[Scorched Detection System]] (SDS) which her father instructed her on once she was old enough and in case of his death. Suffering from Parkinson's,[[Niraj's confession]] he eventually died, along with Calvin.[[Abbie's bunker terminal entries#A New Beginning|Abbie's bunker terminal entries; Abbie's terminal, A New Beginning]] The Cohens were killed by the Scorched. In late 2095, Abbie would eventually become one of the main contacts of the Free States to the Responders and the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]], with [[Maria Chavez]] curious about what the Brotherhood's cryptic message "[[Fort Defiance|Defiance]] has fallen" meant. As a result, Maria sent Abbie a [[Tammy (Fallout 76)|woman]] through the [[Savage Divide]] to check on her, with unclear results.[[Mission to Abigayle]] Being one of the last surviving members of the Free States, and the only person that knew the SDS inside and out, Abbie set up a series of recordings for any survivors to finish what the Free States started. She noted that at some point, she was certain everyone that she knew was dead; she regretted all her time working on the SDS, feeling that life would have been better if everyone simply stayed in their bunkers, as it meant they would at least be alive and she would not have to deal with her crushing loneliness.[[Everyone is gone]] She was unable to finish her work on the SDS, so she packed up a bag and went to the [[Top of the World]] to find [[Hank Madigan]]'s [[Uplink (quest item)|uplink]], although there is no evidence Abbie found it as it is still in a cache in the basement of the [[Pleasant Valley Ski Resort]] and [[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]] does not mention meeting Abbie, leaving Abbie's fate unknown. The Vault 76 residents pick up where she left off with the [[Early Warnings]] quest. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |quests started = * [[The Missing Link]] * [[Early Warnings]] * [[Reassembly Required]] * [[Coming to Fruition]] * [[Defiance Has Fallen]] }} ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|You took me away from my friends and my life all on your stupid promise that things were going to be fine! That this was best! And is it? I can't do this on my own. I don't want to do this on my own. I just want things back the way they were. I miss my mom... and my dad. You guys are supposed to be here.|sound=Abigayle Singh 003cb267_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Howdy stranger! Er... oh god, I can't believe I said that. This is stupid. You're all alone. No one to hear, no one judging... and you can't say a simple line. Great.|sound=Abigayle Singh 003cb262_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Hey there...! Survivor? Bleh, equally terrible. Caleb Carson.wikitext:
{{Infobox character |games =FO76 |image =FO76 Caleb Carson Bones.jpg |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |affiliation =[[Free States]] |role =Member |location =[[Carson family bunker]] |family =[[Elizabeth Carson]] - wife
[[Madeleine Carson]] - daughter
[[Max Carson]] - son |notes =[[Caleb's note]] }} '''Caleb Carson''' was an early member of the [[Free States]]. ==Background== Caleb Carson was the husband of [[Elizabeth Carson]] and father of [[Madeleine Carson|Madeleine]] and [[Max Carson]]. Prior to the [[Great War]], he and his family lived in [[Berkeley Springs]], where Caleb's neighbors [[Bill (Berkeley Springs)|Bill]] and [[Stan (Berkeley Springs)|Stan]] had confronted him, angered that he had joined the [[Free States]]. His neighbors felt he should be helping the people of Berkeley Springs instead of building a bunker.[[Berkeley Springs terminal entries#Fed Up|Berkeley Springs terminal entries; terminal, Fed Up]] The community was so outraged at his support of the Free States that the entire Carson family was banned from the [[Harpers Ferry Clinic]], and Elizabeth was denied her medication.[[Caleb's note]][[Harpers Ferry terminal entries#The Carson Family|Harpers Ferry terminal entries; Ella's terminal, The Carson Family]] Caleb became so frustrated, that he considered sending his family to the safety of the bunker before it was complete. Despite his efforts to protect the family, his wife and children died. Feeling that his decision to support the Free States had led caused his family to perish, Caleb took his own life, leaving behind only [[Caleb's note|a note]] next to his [[Skeleton (Fallout 76)|skeleton]]. ==Appearances== Caleb Carson's skeleton appears only {{In|FO76}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Free States}} [[Category:Fallout 76 mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Free States characters]] [[ru:Калеб Карсон]]

Courtney Kelly.wikitext:
{{Infobox character |games =FO76 |image =FO76 Courtney Kelly.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Female |family = |affiliation =[[Free States]] |role =Hunter |location =Northeast of the [[ransacked bunker]] |quests =[[Tracking Unknowns]] |hair color ={{Tooltip|Warm black|HairColor11WarmBlack}} |eye color ={{Tooltip|Blind|FemaleEyesCorpse}} |hairstyle ={{Tooltip|Young at Heart|HairFemale05}} |level =6 |derived =[[Action Points]]: 50 |special ={{SPECIAL|0,0,0,0,0,0,0}} |aggression =Unaggressive |confidence =Cowardly |assistance =Helps Allies |factions =W05_Loot_CorpseSettlerFaceM01 |class =Citizen |combat style=Default |CK race =HumanRace |notes =[[Courtney's note]] |edid =SFL02_Track_CourtneyCorpse |formid ={{ID|003e4d0a}} |refid ={{ID|0001be18}} }} '''Courtney Kelly''' is a deceased hunter and member of the [[Free States]] whose body can be found in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Courtney was a member of [[Duncan McKann]]'s failed expedition to track down [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|ghouls]] from the [[Valley Galleria]]. She and fellow expedition member [[Jacqueline Murphy]] were wounded early on in the expedition and were left in the care of the expedition's [[Mister Gutsy (Fallout 76)|Mister Gutsy]], [[Hardball]], to recuperate.[[Hardball]]: ''"I have wounded to protect, and re-establishing communications with Duncan McKann is vital."''
([[Hardball/Dialogue]]) However, Courtney did not survive the ordeal and perished along with Jacqueline. Their corpses can be found northeast of the [[ransacked bunker]], past the rock wall. Before she died, Courtney left behind a [[Courtney's note|note]], asking the finder to find a home for her two cats, Lulu and Misty, and even made some suggestions regarding who might be considered a suitable carer.[[Courtney's note]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Tracking Unknowns]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem =[[Courtney's note]]
Random settler loot |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Courtney Kelly appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Free States}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Free States characters]] [[ru:Кортни Келли]]

Duncan McKann.wikitext:
{{Infobox character |games =FO76 |image =FO76 Duncan McKann.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |affiliation =[[Free States]] |role =Hunter |family =[[Lettie McKann]] (wife) {{icon|dead}}
[[Micah McKann]] (son) {{icon|dead}}
[[Lucas McKann]] (son) {{icon|dead}} |location =[[Dyer Chemical]] |quests =[[Tracking Unknowns]] |actor =[[Brian Krause]]
[[Mark Lampert]]{{Ref|(Note)}} |holotapes =[[Lucy's holotape]] |voice type =NPCM_SFL02_Duncan |edid =SFL02_Track_DuncanCorpse |formid ={{ID|003eb39a}} |refid ={{ID|00332a0e}} }} '''Duncan "Dunkie" McKann''' is a deceased member of the [[Free States]] found in [[Dyer Chemical]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Duncan McKann was the leader of a missing hunting group, investigated during [[Tracking Unknowns]]. Although he was not originally a member of the Free States, Duncan changed his tune after the [[Great War]], when the Free States emerged from their bunkers and began rebuilding [[Harpers Ferry]], quickly becoming adept at hunting. Despite the hardship caused by the War, McKann and his family (his wife [[Lettie McKann|Lettie]] and two sons [[Micah McKann|Micah]] and [[Lucas McKann|Lucas]]) remained together, happy to have survived. Family life continued, with everyone pulling their weight, Duncan teaching his boys baseball (even if his wife was better than he was), snoring regularly and even doing the dishes from time to time.[[Happy anniversary!]] The peace ended when the McKanns were attacked by a pack of [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|feral ghouls]], that killed everyone in the McKann family except Duncan, the lone survivor. He succumbed to grief and vowed revenge. When he learned of a pack of ghouls who had turned [[Valley Galleria]] into their home, he took lead of a hunting party consisting of [[Courtney Kelly]], [[Jacqueline Murphy]], [[Randy Calloway]], [[Kendyll Sims]], [[Terrance Quince]], [[Jackson Lake]], and [[Annie Garcia]] from Harpers Ferry to follow their trail. In his single-minded pursuit, he led the whole hunting party to their deaths. Courtney Kelly and Jacqueline Murphy fell in the woods north of the Galleria,[[Tracking Unknowns]] Randy Calloway was shot by [[Nari Samir]], and Kendyll Sims was eventually killed by McKann himself when she objected to his murder of the ghouls after recognizing one as [[Lucy Harwick]], a former resident of Harpers Ferry.[[Lucy's holotape]][[Randy's holotape]] The others' causes of death are unknown, but their lack of report back to Harpers Ferry indicates that they were killed one way or another during the hunt. McKann died when he stormed the control room containing [[Lucy Harwick]] and [[Sara Samir]] and was mortally wounded by a gunshot. He killed both women before succumbing to his wounds, finally satisfied at having avenged his family. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Tracking Unknowns]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Flannel shirt and jeans (Fallout 76)|Flannel shirt and jeans]] |weapon = |otheritem =[[Happy anniversary!]] |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Duncan McKann appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==Behind the scenes== {{Note|(Note)}} Upon ''Fallout 76''{{'}}s release in 2018, Duncan's lines in [[Lucy's holotape]] were all voiced by [[Brian Krause]]. However, at some point in late 2022 (either with ''[[Expeditions: The Pitt]]'' or ''[[Nuka-World on Tour (update)|Nuka-World on Tour]]'', based on available gameplay footage from the time), Duncan's first three lines in the holotape were rerecorded and replaced with a performance by audio director [[Mark Lampert]] for unknown reasons. However, Duncan's other voice lines (the ones at the end of the holotape) were unchanged, effectively creating a situation where Duncan has two voice actors in the same holotape, with both Krause and Lampert voicing the character. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Free States}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Free States characters]] [[ru:Дункан Маккенн]]

Wow. Who would've thought a little radiation would turn this world upside down? We were down in those bunkers for what, a couple years? There's no way radiation did all this by itself in that amount of time.|Ella on [[the Mire]]|[[Ella's log: The Mire]]|sound=Ella Ames.ogg}} '''Ella Ames''' was a member of the [[Free States]] and one of the occupants of [[Ella Ames' bunker]]. ==Background== Before the [[Great War]], Ella Ames earned a Ph.D. in medical science from [[Vault-Tec University]][[Camp Venture terminal entries#Ella Ames|Camp Venture terminal entries; terminal, Ella Ames]] and worked as a doctor. She also had knowledge of holistic medicine taught to her by her mother.[[Ella Ames' bunker terminal entries#Research Studies|Ella Ames' bunker terminal entries; Ella's terminal, Research Studies]] [[West Tek research center (Fallout 76)|West Tek research center]] attempted to recruit Ella, but she turned them down and later joined the [[Free States]]. West Tek would later plan to use her father's failing health as an opportunity to pursue recruitment further.[[West Tek research center terminal entries#Sub: Recruitment|West Tek research center terminal entries; front desk terminal, Sub: Recruitment]] Ella survived the Great War in her bunker. A couple of years later, the Free States members emerged from their bunkers. On July 15, 2079, Ella recorded a [[Ella's log: The Mire|holotape]], expressing her shock at seeing the newly formed [[The Mire|Mire region]]. On May 2, 2080, Ella recorded another [[Ella's log: Harpers Ferry|holotape]] about how rebuilding [[Harpers Ferry]] was tough work. She had recently met a group of [[Responders]], including [[Derek Castle]], who offered to help. Ella attended survival training at [[Camp Venture]] with a group of other Free States members in [[Timeline#2081|2081]]. The [[Edward Hayes|trainer]] took special notice of her, noting her impressive skills around firearms, dressing game and even wrestling. Ella provided vital medical services for the other members of the Free States. She also conducted research on the flora and fauna of the Mire, which had become much more heavily mutated than in other parts of [[Appalachia]], and developed theories on their origins.[[Ella's research]] During the rebuilding of Harpers Ferry, Ella set up a a clinic with the help of the Responders.[[Restoring order (holotape)|Restoring order]] She was excited to work with [[Abigayle Singh|Abigayle "Abbie" Singh]], but Abbie resigned due to social difficulties from dealing with the Responders.[[Letter of resignation (Harpers Ferry)|Letter of resignation]] Ella also extensively studied the [[Scorched]] and the [[Scorchbeast]]s following the Free States' loss of Harpers Ferry to the Scorched. She discovered that if a Scorchbeast is blasted with a certain frequency, it disorients it long enough for fighters to be able to go in and defeat it.[[Madigan encounter]] She attempted preliminary work into analyzing new [[Fallout 76 diseases|diseases]] and developing a radiation shield known as [[RadShield]]. Ella was also studying [[Deathclaw (Fallout 76)|deathclaw]] feces due to their radiation properties and named their droppings "bone meal." With the help of Abbie, Ella was able to develop a tracker to help her find the bone meal. Ella helped [[Niraj Singh]] with the [[Scorched Detection System]], as she discovered the Scorched have a unique, albeit weak, radiation signature. Niraj tasked Ella with delivering Abbie a [[Niraj's confession|holotape]] in case he died. [[Jacob Lerner]] and [[Charlie Walker]] were both attracted to Ella. While Ella did not find Charlie highly intelligent, she found him easy on the eyes, and he offered himself as a subject for her research experimentation. To retrieve flowers for Ella as part of her research, Charlie convinced Jacob to go to the [[Valley Galleria]] on what was unknown to Jacob to be essentially a suicide mission. Although Jacob found the flowers and barely survived, Charlie confronted Jacob outside the building, murdered him, and delivered the flowers to Ella himself.[[Jacob's holotapes]] Ella perished sometime before [[Timeline#2102|2102]]. Her body can be found on the upper level of [[Southhampton Estate]] in the Mire. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |dead=yes |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[An Organic Solution]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Flannel shirt and jeans (Fallout 76)|Flannel shirt and jeans]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Ella Ames appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==Gallery== FO76 Ames family.png|Ella (back left) with her family ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox Free States}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Free States characters]] [[Category:Vault-Tec University characters]] [[ru:Элла Эймс]]

{{Infobox character |games =FO76 |image =FO76 Jacob Lerner.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |affiliation =[[Free States]]
[[Ella Ames]] - romantic interest
[[Charlie Walker]] - rival
[[Scott Wiemer]] - friend |role =Member |location =[[Valley Galleria]] |family =[[Karly O'Reilly]] |hair color ={{Tooltip|Dirty blond|HairColor19DirtyBlond}} |eye color ={{Tooltip|Blind|MaleEyesCorpse}} |hairstyle ={{Tooltip|Geiger Countered|ATX_HairMale23}} |level =6 |derived =[[Action Points]]: 50 |special ={{SPECIAL|0,0,0,0,0,0,0}} |aggression =Unaggressive |confidence =Cowardly |assistance =Helps Allies |factions =Loot_CorpseBase |class =Citizen |combat style=Default |CK race =HumanRace |actor =[[Ray Chase]] |voice type =NPCM_FS_Jacob |holotapes =[[Jacob's holotapes]] |edid =FS_JacobCorpse |formid ={{ID|00439977}} |refid ={{ID|0037084c}} |dialogue = }} '''Jacob Lerner''' was a member of the [[Free States]] sent by [[Ella Ames]] to retrieve samples from [[Valley Galleria]]. ==Background== After the [[Great War]], Jacob helped with the rebuilding of [[Harpers Ferry]], assisting [[Ella Ames]] with her medical endeavors despite his lack of training.[[Harpers Ferry terminal entries#Jacob|Harpers Ferry terminal entries; Ella's terminal, Jacob]] He was one of the Free Staters to attend the survival training course run by [[Eddie Hayes]] at [[Camp Venture]].[[Camp Venture terminal entries#March Roster|Camp Venture terminal entries; terminal, March Roster]] In an attempt to impress Ella and outdo [[Charlie Walker]], with whom he was vying for her affections, Jacob agreed to go to the [[Valley Galleria]] to retrieve flowers. The Galleria had been used as a sanctuary for [[ghoul]]s, however most had gone [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|feral]] by the time Jacob arrived. He became trapped, having used all his ammo and lost his [[Machete (Fallout 76)|machete]]. After managing to survive on junk food and [[Nuka-Cola (Fallout 76)|Nuka-Cola]] for several days, he sneaked past the ghouls with the flowers. He was then shot in the back by Charlie, who returned the flowers to Ella.[[Jacob's holotapes]] His body can be found in the parking lot outside. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =Random Free States outfit |weapon = |otheritem =[[Jacob's holotapes|Jacob's holotape 4]] |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Jacob Lerner appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Free States}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Free States characters]] [[ru:Джейкоб Лернер]]

Jacqueline Murphy.wikitext:
{{Infobox character |games =FO76 |image =FO76 Jacqueline Murphy.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Female |family ={{cut}} [[Robbie (cut)|Robbie]] - brother |affiliation =[[Free States]] |role =Hunter |location =Northeast of the [[ransacked bunker]] |quests =[[Tracking Unknowns]] |holotapes ={{Cut}} [[Jacqueline's holotape]] |hair color ={{Tooltip|Chestnut brown|HairColor20ChestnutBrown}} |eye color ={{Tooltip|Blind|FemaleEyesCorpse}} |hairstyle ={{Tooltip|Beta Rays|ATX_DLC03_HairFemale37}} |level =6 |derived =[[Action Points]]: 50 |special ={{SPECIAL|0,0,0,0,0,0,0}} |aggression =Unaggressive |confidence =Cowardly |assistance =Helps Allies |factions =W05_Loot_CorpseSettlerFaceM01 |class =Citizen |combat style=Default |CK race =HumanRace |dialogue = |voice type ={{Cut}} NPCF_SFL02_Jacqueline |actor ={{Cut}} [[Stephanie Komure]] |edid =SFL02_Track_JacquelineCorpse |formid ={{ID|003e4d0b}} |refid ={{ID|00018fe4}} }} '''Jacqueline Murphy''' is a deceased hunter and member of the [[Free States]] whose body can be found in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Jacqueline was a member of [[Duncan McKann]]'s failed expedition to track down [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|ghouls]] from the [[Valley Galleria]].[[Tracking Unknowns]] She and fellow expedition member [[Courtney Kelly]] were wounded early on in the expedition and were left in the care of the expedition's [[Mister Gutsy (Fallout 76)|Mister Gutsy]], [[Hardball]], to recuperate.[[Hardball]]: ''"I've reason to believe their party was ambushed and a distress beacon deployed, but the signal is too weak to find. {{Tooltip|Your duty is to find a signal booster.|Officially giving instructions.}} {{Tooltip|Possible search locations include: Harpers Ferry or the Valley Galleria Electronic Store.|Official, stating information.}} {{Tooltip|Hmm. Initial readings indicate non-hostile.|To himself.}} As a member of the Free States and protector of Harpers Ferry, I hereby conscript you into service. {{Tooltip|I have wounded to protect, and re-establishing communications with Duncan McKann is vital.|Sounding official.}} {{Tooltip|Attach the booster, release the Cargobot, and wait for the distress signal ping to reach your Pip-Boy. Follow the ping. Find the party. Dismissed! Once you've acquired the booster, proceed to the Survival Training Center and call down a Cargobot using this passcode.|Officially giving instructions.}}"''
([[Hardball/Dialogue]]) Jacqueline did not survive the ordeal and perished along with Courtney. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Tracking Unknowns]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem =Random settler loot |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Jacqueline Murphy appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==Behind the scenes== {{FO76CC}} Jacqueline originally would have had her own [[Jacqueline's holotape|holotape]], in which she was voiced by [[Stephanie Komure]], but this holotape was [[Fallout 76 cut content|cut]] from the game. In it, she describes how the ill-fated expedition was her first hunting trip after being allowed to go by her brother, [[Robbie (cut)|Robbie]]. She was nervous about proving herself to the party, despite her reputation as the best shot on [[Harpers Ferry]] guard duty.{{Cut}} [[Jacqueline's holotape]] {{FO76CC|end}} ==References== {{References}} '''Non-canon''' {{References|group=Non-canon}} {{Navbox Free States}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Free States characters]] [[ru:Жаклин Мёрфи]]

Jesus Sunday.wikitext:
{{Infobox character |games =FO76 |image =Jesus Sunday.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |affiliation =[[Free States]] |location =Near [[Sunday Brothers' cabin]] |role =Corpse |family =[[Juan Diego Sunday|Juan Diego "JD" Sunday]] (brother)
[[Carmen (Vault-Tec University)|Carmen]] (cousin) |quests = |actor =[[Eric Lopez]] |holotapes =[[Jesus Sunday's holotapes]] |voice type =NPCM_LC146_JesusSunday |edid =LC146_JesusSunday_VOICEONLY |formid ={{ID|003cde99}} |refid ={{ID|003cde9a}} }} {{Quotation|I killed them all, but they got in a lucky shot, and I don't think I'm going to last much longer. Probably better this way. This whole thing... what I did... it reminds me of a passage I read in the Bible once. "Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer; and you know that no murderer has eternal life present in him." I guess... I proved that one right.|[[Jesus Sunday's holotape - Part 5]]|sound=Jesus Sunday.ogg}} '''Jesus Sunday''' is a deceased member of the [[Free States]] whose body can be found in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Jesus lived with his brother, [[Juan Diego Sunday|JD]], at the [[Sunday Brothers' cabin]]. The two lived quite well for survivors and they had supplies, although they had some issues where their crops mysteriously disappeared. A paper note, [[Reminder (Fallout 76)|Reminder]], indicates that he knew [[Abigayle Singh]], another Free States member. The brothers briefly visited [[Harpers Ferry]] to try to assist the [[Free States]] effort there.[[Jesus Sunday's holotape - Part 1]] He had many disagreements with his brother's girlfriend, [[Brianna Hawke]], which led to escalating confrontations as he felt she was just playing with his heart in order to get supplies.[[Jesus Sunday's holotape - Part 2]], [[Jesus Sunday's holotape - Part 3]], [[Jesus Sunday's holotape - Part 4]] The tensions resulted in Jesus accidentally killing his brother during a physical confrontation, as JD fell from a cliff to his death.[[Jesus Sunday's holotape - Part 5]] Brianna found out that he killed JD and brought her group to the cabin. They tried to kill Jesus, but he killed them all. However, one of them was able to fatally injure Jesus, killing him. His corpse can be found on a small cliff near their cabin. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem =[[Jesus Sunday's holotape - Part 5]] |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Jesus Sunday appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Free States}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Free States characters]] [[ru:Хесус Сандей]]

Juan Diego Sunday.wikitext:
{{Infobox character |games =none |mentions =FO76 |image =Atx playericon freestates 01.webp |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |affiliation =[[Free States]] |family =[[Jesus Sunday]] (brother)
[[Brianna Hawke]] (girlfriend)
[[Carmen (Vault-Tec University)|Carmen]] (cousin) |role =Brewmaster }} '''Juan Diego "JD" Sunday''' was the brother of [[Jesus Sunday]] and lived at the [[Sunday Brothers' cabin]]. ==Background== JD, who described himself as an "amazing brewmaster," was in charge of the Sunday Brothers' alcohol and moonshine distillery operations.[[Sunday Brothers' cabin terminal entries]] He respected [[Abigayle Singh]].[[Reminder (Fallout 76)|Reminder]] Even though the brothers lived quite well and had supplies in their situation, JD was very depressed by the post-apocalyptic world they lived in, but met his ex-girlfriend named [[Brianna Hawke]] at [[Harpers Ferry]]. JD and Brianna had dated before the [[Great War]].[[Brianna Hawke's diary]] She eventually became his girlfriend again and his mood cheered up, although he began to emotionally distance himself from his brother.[[Jesus Sunday's holotape - Part 2]] After an attack on Harpers Ferry, Brianna showed up at the brothers' cabin with a small group of survivors. Jesus claimed Brianna had conned JD, pretending to love him in order give herself and her friends an invite to their bunker. [[Brianna Hawke's diary]] supports this, saying she felt the two brothers had snobbish attitudes and reveals she and her group had been stealing from the brothers' land, having raided the food in their field. However, it is ambiguous if she truly fell in love with JD and if her opinion of him changed when he began giving her supplies. Jesus declined Brianna's invite, opposing JD. Jesus then knocked JD unconscious and fired warning shots to scare Brianna's group away.[[Jesus Sunday's holotape - Part 3]] Weeks later, Jesus thought JD had let go of Brianna, but it turned out they were secretly exchanging notes and that JD had been giving her supplies.[[Jesus Sunday's holotape - Part 4]] Jesus tried to confront JD about how Brianna was a bad influence. A physical altercation happened between the brothers, and Jesus accidentally killed JD by shoving him off a cliff, unsure if JD slipped or if he pushed too hard. Brianna found out what happened and Jesus and Brianna's group ended up killing each other.[[Jesus Sunday's holotape - Part 5]] ==Appearances== Juan Diego "JD" Sunday is mentioned only {{In|FO76}}. ==References== {{references}} {{Navbox Free States}} [[Category:Fallout 76 mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Free States characters]]

'''Kendyll Sims''' is a deceased member of the [[Free States]], found in [[Dyer Chemical]] in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
Kendyll Sims was one of the most capable sharpshooters in [[Harpers Ferry]], even before the Free States returned to the town in the wake of [[Great War]].<ref>[[Restoring order (holotape)]]</ref> She was a member of [[Duncan McKann]]'s failed expedition to track down [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|ghouls]] from the [[Valley Galleria]].<ref>[[Tracking Unknowns]]</ref> When the expedition finally cornered the ghouls in [[Dyer Chemical]], Kendyll recognized [[Lucy Harwick]] when she spoke and was distressed by McKann's desire to kill the group despite them clearly being in control of their mental faculties. McKann shot and killed Kendyll when she turned her gun on him after this revelation.<ref>[[Lucy's holotape]]</ref><ref>[[Randy's holotape]]</ref>

'''Kora''' was a member of the [[Free States]] some time before [[Timeline#2102|2102]].

==Background==
Kora's corpse is part of the [[Free States Loner]] random encounter. On her person is [[the government's plan]]. In a nearby duffle bag, [[Kora's journal entry]] can also be found.

Like many other members of the Free States, Kora distrusted the [[United States government]]. She suspected that the government planned the [[Great War]] to get rid of the lower class and most of the middle class as well, allowing bureaucrats and members of the military free reign to "restore whatever order they want." However, she argues that the nuclear aftermath was worse than anticipated for them.<ref>[[The government's plan]]</ref>

Kora survived the Great War in a bunker, though at some point [[Strangler plant|Strangler vines]] managed to grow through the concrete wall and into the bunker's water purifier and air purifier, destroying both. She speculated that she could stay with other members of the Free States, but had heard some of them wanted to help other survivors - the same ones that "ridiculed us... killed [[Caleb Carson|Caleb's]] family... even found two dead bodies outside my own bunker trying to break in." She instead decided to take the rest of her supplies and head west, though she died before leaving [[the Mire]].<ref>[[Kora's journal entry]]</ref>

REAL people with thoughts and feelings, and all those other things that make us all human!|[[Lucy's holotape]]|sound=Lucy Harwick Real People.ogg}} '''Lucy Harwick''' was a [[ghoul]] who lived in [[Appalachia]] sometime prior to [[Timeline#2102|2102]]. ==Background== Lucy Harwick was a pre-[[Great War|War]] aesthetician who stayed in [[Harpers Ferry]] after the bombs fell. When the [[Free States]] decided to help rebuild, she joined [[Ella Ames]] in providing medical services to the beleaguered population.[[Harpers Ferry terminal entries#Open for Business|Harpers Ferry terminal entries; Ella's terminal, Open for Business]][[Ella's log: Harpers Ferry]] Problems for Lucy started with [[Daniel Whitby]], a boy who suffered exposure to radiation and started changing into a [[ghoul]]. As Harpers Ferry and the Free Staters were constantly fighting off hordes of [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|ghouls]] in the aftermath of the War, she hid him away while she looked for a cure. When people found out what she was doing, Lucy was forced to flee.[[Harpers Ferry terminal entries#Daniel Whitby|Harpers Ferry terminal entries; Ella's terminal, Daniel Whitby]] Lucy too eventually turned into a ghoul. However, she rejected the term "ghouls" instead referring to her and her kind as "the Changed." After she realized that she was not the only one who was experiencing physical changes as a result of the radiation, she created a home for others like her at the [[Valley Galleria]] and left notes around Appalachia, welcoming others experiencing the same physical changes to join them.[[Lucy Harwick's note]] She soon gathered several followers, including [[Sara Samir]] who had been turned into a ghoul and her sister [[Nari Samir|Nari]] who had not.[[Nari's holotape]] The support from those who were unaffected gave Lucy hope for a future where ghouls were no longer shunned and reviled because they were changed.[[Lucy's journal]] However, hunting parties from Harpers Ferry were a constant threat to the group. One of these parties, led by [[Duncan McKann]], was a particular threat, as Duncan was waging a one-man war on all ghouls, trying to drown out the memories of losing his family to a pack of [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|ferals]]. Lucy realized the threat that Duncan posed and moved to find a new, better hideout for her group. Eventually, she found the perfect spot: the underground section of [[Dyer Chemical]], a reinforced location with secure locks that would allow her to keep everyone safe. Despite her precautions, Duncan tracked the group to their new location and Lucy was killed in the ensuing confrontation with him.[[Lucy's holotape]] During [[Tracking Unknowns]], her corpse can be found in the [[Dyer Chemical]] sewers, next to that of [[Sara Samir]]. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Undershirt & jeans (Fallout 76)|Undershirt & jeans]] |weapon = |otheritem =[[Lucy's holotape]] |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Lucy Harwick appears only {{In|FO76}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox Free States}} [[Category:Fallout 76 ghoul characters]] [[Category:Free States characters]] [[ru:Люси Харвик]]

As a non-ghoul, her presence in the group gave Lucy hope for a future where ghouls were no longer shunned and reviled because they had changed.[[Lucy's journal]] When [[Duncan McKann]] threatened the group and they moved to the sewers beneath [[Dyer Chemical]], as the only non-ghoul in the group, special arrangements had to be made to protect her from the radiation. I repeat, the Rover unit is damaged and requires immediate repairs.|sound=Niraj Singh 002e5b00_1.ogg}} '''Niraj Singh''' was a member of the [[Free States]]. ==Background== Niraj moved his family to a [[Abbie's bunker|bunker]] prior to the [[Great War]]. Two years after the bombs fell, Niraj helped the Free States in rebuilding [[Harpers Ferry]] after hearing from [[Raleigh Clay]]. He was working on an air filter contraption to help with the brutal storms.[[Restoring order (holotape)|Restoring order]] However, following a seven-year effort, Harpers Ferry was overwhelmed by the [[Scorched]] and Niraj fled back to the bunker with his family. After that, Niraj devoted his time and effort to devising ways to fight the Scorched, for which he established the [[Scorched Detection System]].[[Abbie's bunker terminal entries#Niraj's terminal|Niraj's terminal]] He worked on the system with [[Ella Ames]] and he tasked her with delivering a [[Niraj's confession|holotape]] to his daughter [[Abigayle Singh|Abigayle]] in the event of his death. Niraj was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease and kept his illness hidden from his children.[[Niraj's confession]] Knowing that he would not live long, Niraj taught his daughter so she could finish the Scorched Detection System. Niraj eventually died. ==Notes== Niraj voices the minor event [[Always Vigilant]]. {{Infobox character |games =none |mentions =FO76 |image =Photo_patriciaraleighclay_d.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |affiliation =[[Free States]] |role =Co-founder |family =[[Patricia Clay]] - wife {{Icon|dead}}

This here's Raleigh Clay on a priority message recording. Our sensors have picked up some seismic activity in the area which only means one thing. A [[Strangler heart|Strangler Heart]]'s been picked up in the vicinity and its vine-infested creatures won't be far behind. To anyone listening, take down that Heart before it controls too many creatures and things get out of hand!|sound=Raleigh Clay 00336b46_1.ogg}} '''Raleigh Clay''' was a founding member of the [[Free States]]. ==Background== In addition to being the figurehead of the [[Free States]] movement, Raleigh was also best friends with Senator [[Sam Blackwell]] for over forty years.[[Family and so-called friends]] He lived in [[Harpers Ferry]] for all of his life before the [[Great War]].[[Harpers Ferry proposal]] Due to his founding of and open affiliation to the Free States, he was the target of many government-led attacks and derision in the eyes of the public,[[Overseer's log - Free States]][[Charleston Capitol Building terminal entries]] which were contributing factors to the Free States' secession from America. The mayor of Harpers Ferry, [[Miranda Vox]], shunned the Free States and demanded for Raleigh to leave town, upon which he and his family retreated into their personal [[Raleigh Clay's bunker|bunker]]. After the Great War, Raleigh emerged with his family. Using his Free States connections, he made an attempt at stabilizing the dangerous region of [[the Mire]] and to help the civilians that used to chastise the Free Staters. When Miranda Vox, who also survived the War, asked for help with rebuilding Harpers Ferry, Raleigh and his daughter [[Martha Clay|Marty]] went to investigate and found the town in a pitiful condition. Raleigh would have left them to die, but Marty sympathized with the survivors and proposed that they help rebuild Harpers Ferry. Raleigh eventually agreed, and they accomplished this by fortifying the town and teaching its citizens how to survive. It wasn't long until the Free States became involved with other groups. Raleigh, at first, was supportive of cooperation with the [[Responders]] but had been wary of the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]] due to their demands for supplies. Shortly afterward, Raleigh led the push for the Free States to take over the [[Harpers Ferry Armory]] and use it as the staging ground for Free States operations after the war, as well as a way to prepare for any aggressions from the Brotherhood to try and get resources from them.[[Protecting our own]] After seven years of reconstruction, their work came undone. In 2086, the [[Scorched]] and [[Scorchbeast]]s overwhelmed the town, killing many and causing the Free States to retreat to their bunkers.[[Abbie's bunker terminal entries#The Scorched 2|Abbie's bunker terminal entries; Niraj's terminal, The Scorched]] [[Patricia Clay|Raleigh's wife]] and Marty were among those killed. Raleigh and his other children survived and retreated to their bunker, but he was left in despair at his family's losses and angered by the non-presence of his oldest friend, Sam Blackwell (who had, unbeknownst to Raleigh, died by then at the hands of an [[Jefferson Grey|Enclave assassin]]). This did not deter him from continuing to look out for the Free States, sending out a warning to abandon efforts to recover Harpers Ferry and stay in hiding.[[Raleigh Clay's bunker terminal entries#Scorchbeasts|Raleigh Clay's bunker terminal entries; outgoing notifications station, Scorchbeasts]] In the wake of Harpers Ferry's destruction, he was also a key part in the development of the [[Scorched Detection System]], an early warning system against the Scorched with [[Niraj Singh]], [[Ella Ames]], [[Edward Hayes]], and later Niraj's daughter [[Abigayle Singh|Abigayle]]. One of the system's other names, "Operation Cooldown," was made in memoriam of Marty. Eventually, the research bore fruit, and Raleigh helped to set up the network of Scorched detectors.[[Raleigh Clay's bunker terminal entries#Early Thoughts|Raleigh Clay's bunker terminal entries; terminal, Early Thoughts]][[Raleigh Clay's bunker terminal entries#First Plan|Raleigh Clay's bunker terminal entries; terminal, First Plan]][[Raleigh Clay's bunker terminal entries#Promising Results|Raleigh Clay's bunker terminal entries; terminal, Promising Results]] He also oversaw the development and implementation of [[Scorchbeast lure]]s around the Mire, further working on instructing people how to use them.[[Raleigh Clay's bunker terminal entries#Scorchbeasts|Raleigh Clay's bunker terminal entries; outgoing notifications station, Scorchbeast Lures]] Raleigh's work as the Free States' leader continued past the fall of the Brotherhood in 2095, when he sent out teams to scavenge equipment from [[Camp Venture]][[Abbie's bunker terminal entries#Fort Defiance|Abbie's bunker terminal entries; Abbie's terminal, Fort Defiance]] and the following year, when he sent a team into the Cranberry Bog to investigate the Brotherhood's final transmission, "Defiance has fallen."[[Defiance mission report]] By 2102, Raleigh's bunker has been abandoned, but there is no evidence of his death. ==Notes== Raleigh's voice is heard on a recorded message during the [[Heart of the Swamp]] event. ==Related holotapes== * [[Family and so-called friends]] * [[Harpers Ferry proposal]] * [[Madigan encounter]] * [[Protecting our own]] ==Appearances== Raleigh Clay is mentioned only {{In|FO76}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox Free States}} [[Category:Fallout 76 mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Free States characters]] [[ru:Рейли Клэй]] [[zh:Raleigh Clay]]

'''Randy Calloway''' is a deceased member of the [[Free States]] found south of [[Haven Church]] in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
After [[Great War|the bombs fell]], Randy graduated from the Virginia Endurance and Survival Training center (later [[Camp Venture]]) along with several other Free Staters.<ref>[[Camp Venture terminal entries#March Roster]]</ref> He was friends with [[Ella Ames]], accompanying her as she conducted her experiments on [[strangler pod]]s, once shooting a [[Gulper (Fallout 76)|gulper]] with his shotgun to protect her.<ref>[[Ella's research#Flower Power]]</ref>

Randy was a member of [[Duncan McKann]]'s failed expedition to track down [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|ghouls]] from the [[Valley Galleria]].<ref>[[Tracking Unknowns]]</ref> When they cornered the ghouls and realized that they were harmless, sentient beings that just wanted to be left alone, Randy could not bring himself to kill them.<ref>[[Randy's holotape]]</ref> He was shot by [[Nari Samir]] in the ensuing confrontation, but not before activating a distress beacon which is still operational years later.
