One]]|sound=Sam Blackwell.ogg}} '''Senator Samuel "Sam" Blackwell''' was a [[United States of America|United States]] senator representing the [[Appalachia|Appalachian Territory]] in the [[United States Congress|U.S. Congress]] before the [[Great War]], serving on both the Intelligence and Nuclear Energy committees.[[Intelligence memo - 8/16/77]] Very popular and winning 73% of the vote due to his pro-union stance, Blackwell also became a pivotal figure of the [[Free States]] movement before being forced into hiding. ==Background== Blackwell started his public life as a union activist, brokering deals between disenfranchised miners and regional powerhouses like [[Garrahan Mining Company|Garrahan Mining]] and [[Hornwright Industrial]]. His star would only continue to rise during his re-election to the United States Senate, winning with a staggering 73% of the popular vote.[[The Sam Blackwell Interview]] Blackwell gained notoriety among fellow politicians for his consistent stance favoring the people, rather than the elites, and asking uncomfortable questions, like the purpose of building automated nuclear silos across Appalachia or the apparent timing discrepancies between civilian and military nuclear attack warnings, enough to be threatened with imprisonment by the powers that be more than once.[[Back off Sam]] Blackwell was effectively a senatorial muckraker, routinely causing scuffles in committees when he pointed out conflicts of interests and exposed corruption. In one instance, he humiliated a fellow senator, [[Clark (senator)|Senator Clark]], before the Senate Committee on Nuclear Energy, when he revealed that Clark's push for lifting the ban on extracting uranium from the largest deposit in the United States (situated beneath a national park) was motivated by the stake the senator had purchased in [[Atomic Mining Services]].[[Committee meeting notes]] Unofficially, Blackwell also made inquiries into the bizarre investments made by the [[Department of Agriculture]] in Appalachia and the activities of the department's secretary, [[Thomas Eckhart]].[[Charleston Capitol Building terminal entries]] It would take Blackwell's open support of the Appalachian [[Free States]] movement, a group of local survivalists with separatist overtones before his popularity would begin to wane. But as minor scuffles between the Free States and police broke into open violence, Blackwell's support for the Free States only grew, as did calls for his resignation. However, his staunch opposition to Ballot Measure 6, which would rapidly accelerate the automation of Appalachia and deprive people of jobs and income, kept him popular. However, they also made him a target for [[Daniel Hornwright]]. To eliminate the senator from the picture, Hornwright's CEO contracted a goon, a reliable fixer [[Harper Rosiak]] he's hired before, to silence the senator without killing him.[[Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries#TO:|Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries; CEO's terminal, TO:]] Rosiak's chosen avenue to achieve this was to issue threats against Blackwell's daughter, [[Judith Blackwell|Judith]], under the guise of "sticking [his] nose where it doesn't belong."[[We're coming for you]] Convinced it was a retaliation for his investigation into Eckhart's activities, Blackwell vanished.[[Sam Blackwell: "No" on Measure 6]] Calls to his [[Charleston]] office and home went unanswered, and Judith stopped showing up for classes at VTU. Multiple search parties were organized by police and concerned citizens, but produced no results. His last public appearance, so to speak, was in [[Quinn Carter]]'s ''[[Charleston Herald]]'' interview, where he issued a damning indictment of the government and its indifference to the plight of the common man and called for Americans to find shelter away from cities while there was still time. Branded as a traitor by some,[[CARTER AND BLACKWELL - TRAITORS!]] the senator's actions resulted in an accelerated election to replace him as the Appalachian Territory's senator and gained widespread notoriety.[[The Whitespring bunker terminal entries]] Although his daughter stood by him, his wife, [[Emily Blackwell|Emily]], filed for divorce, granted shortly before the Great War.[[Record of divorce: The Blackwells]] His enemies also started digging into his life, trying to smear his name by painting him as unreliable, due to the onset of an unnamed neurodegenerative disease. ===Post-War life=== After the Great War, Blackwell lived in his personal bunker (the entrance of which is disguised as an [[Abandoned waste dump|abandoned toxic waste disposal site]] to deter any curious explorers) together with his daughter, Judith. Although the bunker provided shelter, Blackwell continued to develop issues with memory and lucidity that could be treated with meds his daughter concoted or scavenged for, such as [[Mentats (Fallout 76)|Mentats]].[[Sam_Blackwell's_bunker_terminal_entries#Mentats Are Key|Sam Blackwell's bunker terminal entries; Judy's terminal, Mentats Are Key]] Judith suggested that he keep a journal to keep his memory active while she gathered ingredients to make more meds. She also listened to endless calls for help on the radio, though no one responded. Sam was disheartened, realizing that few listened to his pleas for people to help each other.[[Sam Blackwell's bunker terminal entries#Judy Says I Should Write|Sam Blackwell's bunker terminal entries; Sam's terminal, Judy Says I Should Write]] Though life was far from idyllic, it was safe, for a time. Blackwell still feared discovery and retaliation. When, one day, Judith failed to return from her mushroom foraging (preparing an unappetizing mushroom and [[Dandy Boy Apples (Fallout 76)|Dandy Boy Apple]] casserole), Blackwell tracked her down after cycling through foraging spots, finding her in conversation with two other men. He waited for them to leave, then confronted his daughter back at the bunker, leading to a fight between them. He was sorry about the fight, less so about the reason for it, but was still scared of losing Judy.[[Sam Blackwell's bunker terminal entries#Judy, I'm Sorry|Sam Blackwell's bunker terminal entries; Sam's terminal, Judy, I'm Sorry]] This made his first encounter with the [[scorchbeast]]s, experienced while outside hunting, much more horrifying. He saw the scorchbeast, a monster "the size of a [[Chryslus Corvega|Corvega]]," looking right at him, 500 yards away, while perched on top of a ridge. He barely made it into the bunker, where Judith assumed that it might have been a hallucination caused by his deteriorating neurological state. Just to be safe, however, she also ensured her father always took the biggest gun with him when he went outside.[[Sam Blackwell's bunker terminal entries#Some Kind of Bat|Sam Blackwell's bunker terminal entries; Sam's terminal, Some Kind of Bat]] Judy fell ill from an unspecified illness that reminded Sam of both a pre-war illness and similar symptoms being reported in Harpers Ferry at the time. On February 15, [[Timeline#2084|2084]], his daughter died as a result. She died practically in his arms, right as he was preparing to carry her to [[the Whitespring]], ready to trade his life for hers. He never got the chance.[[Sam Blackwell's bunker terminal entries#Judy's Gone|Sam Blackwell's bunker terminal entries; Sam's terminal, Judy's Gone]] The bereaved Blackwell reconnected with the Free States at [[Harpers Ferry]]. Having disappeared so long ago, and in the aftermath of the war other matters taking precedent over a missing senator, everyone either didn't know who he was or pretended that they didn't. [[Raleigh Clay]] put him to work at the armory, cleaning weapons away from other people. However, while Blackwell's neurological state steadily worsened,[[Sam Blackwell's bunker terminal entries#Been a While|Sam Blackwell's bunker terminal entries; Sam's terminal, Been a While]] he was far from gone. He identified an [[Enclave]] operative in town, noticing how the newcomer was staring him down. He then tracked him down outside of the town walls, as he was making a recording. Sam killed him, making it look like an animal attack with messy cuts, throwing pieces of him in the river. Although it caused a wave of fear in the town, concerned about wildlife attacking people, it did not fool the Enclave. A cloaked [[Vertibird]] passed over the town looking for him the following night. Sam fled to his shelter once it disappeared.[[Sam Blackwell's bunker terminal entries#They Found Me|Sam Blackwell's bunker terminal entries; Sam's terminal, They Found Me]] [[Thomas Eckhart|President Thomas Eckhart]], still bitter over Blackwell's involvement and investigation of his activities as Secretary of Agriculture, issued a kill order. It was rapidly a moot point for Blackwell, struggling to live on after his daughter's passing. [[Jefferson Grey|Agent Jefferson Grey]] breached the outer defenses of the bunker, then the inner, finally killing the senator in his inner sanctum. However, when Grey reset power for the security systems to gain entry, it also meant resetting the lures.[[Operation Summary - Blackwell]] ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|In my time as senator, I became aware of plans made by those in power... plans of an unconscionable nature.|sound=Fo76 sam blackwell unconscionable nature 0007179f 3.ogg}} ==Appearances== Sam Blackwell is mentioned {{In|FO76}}. ==Gallery== FO76_Sam_Blackwell's_bunker_(Blackwell's_skeleton).jpg|Blackwell's skeleton F76 Voting Poster 2.png|Poster regarding the senator's vacant seat ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox Free States}} [[Category:United States Congress]] [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Free States characters]] [[Category:Pre-War politicians]] [[pt:Sam Blackwell]] [[ru:Сэмюэл Блэквелл]] [[uk:Сем Блеквелл]] [[zh:Sam Blackwell]]

Babe, you and I are moving up in the world.|Brody to [[Olivia Rivers]]|[[Presidential Cottage security recording]]|sound=Brody Torrance Moving Up.ogg}} '''Brody Torrance''' was a member of the [[Cutthroats]] [[Raiders (Fallout 76)|raider gang]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Before the [[Great War]], Brody lived at [[Torrance House]], next door to the Rivers family, including their daughter [[Olivia Rivers|Olivia]].[[Riverside Manor terminal entries#6/8/86|Riverside Manor terminal entries; Olivia's terminal, Personal Journal, 6/8/86]] As one of the many survivors of the War in [[Appalachia]], Brody struggled to survive in the nightmarish reality of the wasteland at the same time as three other girls who were roughly his age. In November [[Timeline#2078|2078]], they were found by the Rivers family rifling through the garage of the [[Riverside Manor]]. [[Clarissa]], [[Eve Devoir|Eve]], and [[Amy Thomas|Amy]] found a new home under the wings of the Rivers' family, but Brody was turned away.[[Riverside Manor terminal entries#11/11/78|Riverside Manor terminal entries; Olivia's terminal, Personal journal, 11/11/78]][[Riverside Manor terminal entries#11/11/78|Riverside Manor terminal entries; Study terminal, Personal journal, 11/11/78]] Brody survived the nuclear winter, but the situation only worsened. Eventually, he joined the [[Savage Divide]] raiders, finally making ends meet under one of [[David Thorpe]]'s trusted lieutenants. He survived the fierce campaign waged on the raiders by the [[Order of Mysteries]] until [[Timeline#2086|2086]] when he was assigned to a checkpoint out on the edge of raider-controlled space. [[Olivia Rivers]], resentful of her mother's rule over the Order and looking for inroads into the raiders so that she could usurp leadership for herself, recalled Brody from eight years prior and realized he could be her way in. Olivia attacked this checkpoint on June 8, effortlessly killing everyone but Brody, sparing him save for a nick to the leg.[[Riverside Manor terminal entries#11/11/78|Riverside Manor terminal entries; Olivia's terminal, Personal journal, 6/8/86]][[Jake's letter]] He took up Olivia's offer to give her information about the raider organization in exchange for betraying the Order. As Brody was the only survivor of [[Mack Frazier]]'s veteran crew, David Thorpe was initially skeptical when Torrance came to him. However, without any other leads, he played along and allowed Brody to continue working with Olivia.[[Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries#6-9-86: RE: Checkpoint Massacre|Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries; Brody's terminal, Pleasant Valley IntraMail, 6-9-86: RE: Checkpoint Massacre]] Thorpe's trust did not seem to pay off at first, as on July 1, nearly a month later, Torrance was 200 caps behind on his quota and Thorpe was still losing men to the Order's attacks.[[Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries#7-1-86: Quotas|Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries; Brody's terminal, Pleasant Valley IntraMail, 7-1-86: Quotas]] When Brody forwarded Olivia's proposition of a deal - a blank check for anything she wanted in return for the Order - Thorpe's patience was at the end.[[Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries#7-19-86: RE: Deal|Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries; Brody's terminal, Pleasant Valley IntraMail, 7-19-86: RE: Deal]] He was ready to have Torrance killed, but decided to give him one last chance when Olivia offered him a token of her trustworthiness - intelligence on an Order supply run in [[Summersville]]. Thorpe assigned five men and Brody to Summersville where Olivia had advised that one of the Mistresses would be. Thorpe included an ultimatum to Brody - to either return with the Mistress' head or his own would be substituted. The planned ambush was botched when one of Brody's men jumped too early and Olivia was forced to kill the target, [[Allison Long]], herself to prevent the operation from being a disaster.[[Riverside Manor terminal entries#7/24/86|Riverside Manor terminal entries; Olivia's terminal, Personal journal, 7/24/86]] No one would know of this and Brody delivered the girl's head to Thorpe. As a reward, Brody was immediately promoted to lieutenant, provided with seven raiders of his own choosing, and quarters in the Black Diamond Lodge, where only the most trusted raiders were quartered. His sole mission became the elimination of the Order. Brody continued to work with Olivia to destroy the Order. By mid-September, they had successfully ambushed three Mistresses all over Appalachia. Olivia made a new offer to Thorpe which he agreed to after these successes. In exchange for [[Cryptos]], Thorpe would grant Olivia, and Brody, anything which was within his power to grant.[[Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries#9-13-86: RE: Spruce Knob Ambush|Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries; Brody's terminal, Pleasant Valley IntraMail, 9-13-86: RE: Spruce Knob Ambush]] On September 20, Olivia delivered Cryptos on a [[Project Siphon holotape]], loaded with all the mainframe data and all the Order's planned mission assignments for the next two months. Thorpe recognized the opportunity and immediately assigned Rose and Torrance to map out ambushes to reduce the Order's numbers until the Manor could be safely attacked. He also had his tech crew start trawling the data for other leads.[[Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries#9-20-86: RE: Motherload|Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries; Brody's terminal, Pleasant Valley IntraMail, 9-20-86: RE: Motherload]] As the Order crumbled, Olivia's cover was blown and she was forced to slaughter her way through the Order's ranks. When she notified Brody, he immediately informed Thorpe of the development. Brody was assigned to tie up any loose ends and destroy the Order for good.[[Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries#11-16-86: RE: Finale|Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries; Brody's terminal, Pleasant Valley IntraMail, 11-16-86: RE: Finale]] Brody watched from hiding as Olivia met, fought, and killed [[Shannon Rivers|her mother]] at [[Seneca Rocks]]. He then double-crossed and killed Olivia, revealing that Olivia was never to get into the Raiders in the first place. Once her mother and the rest of the Order were destroyed, Thorpe had ordered Brody to kill Olivia, not wanting to risk her turning on the Raiders like she did her own mother, bringing the Order to an end in November [[Timeline#2086|2086]].[[Shannon Rivers' recording]] ==Related holotapes== * [[Presidential Cottage security recording]] * [[Shannon Rivers' recording]] ==Appearances== Brody Torrance is mentioned only {{In|FO76}}. ==References== {{references}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox original raiders FO76}} [[Category:Fallout 76 mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Cutthroats]] [[ru:Броди Торренс]]

{{Infobox character |games =FO76 |image =FO76 Big Bend Tunnel raider corpse.png |image desc =Next to Sweeney's final entry |race =[[Human]] |gender =Female |affiliation =[[Cutthroats]] (formerly) |role =Raider (formerly)
Group leader |edid =Loot_CorpseRaiderFemale04 |formid ={{ID|0009733c}} |refid ={{ID|003cf7f3}} }} {{Quotation|All these years, I wondered if it was possible to come back. If people could come back from the horrible things we've done; if I could come back from the horrible things I've done. For a couple of years there, I started to believe maybe it was. But it isn't. I can't come back from the things I did as a Cutthroat. Humanity can't come back from nuking ourselves to Hell. And now it seems we're all gonna die as a result of it.}} '''Carol Sweeney''', identified as a '''raider corpse''' in-game, is a deceased former [[Raiders (Fallout 76)|raider]] from the [[Cutthroats]] who took refuge in [[Big Bend Tunnel]]. ==Background== Carol Sweeney was an affluent tourist visiting [[Pleasant Valley Ski Resort]] when the [[Great War]] began. Like the other tourists seeking for survival, Carol became a raider and joined the [[Cutthroats]]. However, Carol did not stay with the Cutthroats for long. When [[David Thorpe]] caused [[the Christmas Flood]] in December 2082 that devastated [[Charleston]], Carol was appalled at what Thorpe had done and guilt-ridden for becoming an accessory to mass murder, striking out shortly after the Flood. She and a few other raiders left the Cutthroats. Carol became the default leader of the group which took shelter in [[Big Bend Tunnel]], setting up a community at the western end of the tunnel in January 2083.[[Scattered journal pages]] Attempts to explore the eastern end were suspended after a November 2085 trip resulted in her witnessing the [[scorchbeast]]s digging themselves out from under the ground. Despite that, the group built a self-sufficient community in and around the western end of the tunnel, scavenging, foraging, and even setting up a little agriculture. In May 2088, her community came into contact with the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]] under Knight [[Melissa Reische]]. The group formed a trading relationship, exchanging what weapon parts and tech salvage they could find and exchanging it for supplies from Reische. While Sweeney considered it a one-sided exchange, the Brotherhood kept trading with them and in 2093 learned that the reason was to keep their community going. Sweeney considered the words, realizing that she has been stuck thinking of herself as a former Cutthroat, rather than a survivor. Reische gave her hope. Carol also realized that while she might have imagined a different future while vacationing at Pleasant Valley, the hard life in the new world was strangely simpler and more peaceful than the pre-War chaos. Like others throughout [[Appalachia]], Carol's peace was shattered by the advancement of the [[Scorched]]. The increasing presence in the tunnels limited contact with the Brotherhood contingent. In summer 2095, Sweeney and her group managed to reestablish contact with the eastern end, only to find that Knight Reische's contingent was gone. Sweeney was distraught, as she thought Melissa would have left a parting note at least. She put a ban on any trips to the eastern end, setting up a patrol and rigging multiple traps to keep the scorched at bay. However, it didn't help, as they came from the west. By spring 2097, her group was one of the last few remaining survivors in Appalachia, completely surrounded by the Scorched. The horde appeared on the trails of two former Cutthroats who came to them for shelter. Originally thinking it a ploy to get her to drop her guard, she realized they were genuine in the fear. However, a few hours later, before they could abandon the settlement, the scorched descended on the camp and quickly pushed everyone back into the tunnels, sealing their fate. Trapped deep within the Big Bend Tunnel, Sweeney had enough time to ruminate on her fate, accepting death as just penance for her actions in life. ==Appearances== Carol Sweeney appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==References== {{references}} {{Navbox original raiders FO76}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Cutthroats]]

I just don't want anything bad to happen to you.|David to [[Rosalynn Jeffries]] on a secret pre-[[Great War|War]] ski trip|[[Rosalynn and David's ski trip]]|sound=David Thorpe.ogg}} '''David Thorpe''' is the former leader of the [[Cutthroats]] in [[Appalachia]]. He was turned into a [[Scorched]]. ==Background== David Thorpe was an executive at the [[Arktos Pharma (company)|Arktos Pharma]], using ruthless business tactics to ensure Arktos dominated the pharmaceutical market. Depressing wages and aggressive, unwavering commitment to negotiation terms were standard practice at Arktos when David was at the table.[[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]]: ''"Best bet is Arktos Pharma, David's old corporate stooge job."''
([[Rose (Fallout 76)/Dialogue#70|Rose's dialogue]])[[Board meeting]][[Thorpe: 10/03/2077 9:34am]] Although he was married with a [[Rita Thorpe|wife]] and children at home, he also had a mistress, [[Rosalynn Jeffries]], and regularly frequented the [[Pleasant Valley Ski Resort]] with her, covering up these escapades as business trips to [[Washington, D.C.]][[Note to self (Wastelanders)|Note to self]] It was during one such escapade that the [[Great War]] happened, trapping him, Rosalynn, and scores of other resort guests in the mountains. Although he was already planning to divorce his wife for Rosalynn when the bombs fell,[[Rosalynn and David's ski trip]] the loss of his wife and child was a savage blow for David and it was only through Rosalynn's constant support that he managed to pull through.[[Strange Bedfellows]] Despite his dedication to Rosalynn, he still held much love for his wife. His side as a ruthless executive allowed him to quietly build support among the surviving resort guests, now forming Appalachia's nascent [[Raiders (Fallout 76)|raider gangs]] after the brutal winter of 2077. David rose to power against the original raider leader [[Harland McClintock]] by offering an alternative, more violent path to future success. When David killed two [[Responders]] who traveled to [[Top of the World]] to offer their help to the survivors there, Harland and his wife [[Margie McClintock|Margie]] tried to put David on trial and exile him for his deeds.[[Harland's up to no good]] This ended poorly for the McClintocks, with the group splintering off to form the gang which would be known as the [[Diehards]]. The Responders would ultimately blame David for encouraging the Pleasant Valley survivors' violent tendencies and turning them into fully-fledged raiders.[[The Christmas Flood (holotape)|The Christmas Flood]] When David became leader, Rosalynn made a [[David's trophy|trophy]] for him with a skull and "World's Best Boss" on it. On their anniversary, David stole chems for her and they spent the night under the stars near [[Ripper Alley]], with David remarking how he had never seen her happier.[[Photo of Rosalynn's memorial]] In [[Timeline#2082|2082]], David was prepared to propose to Rosalynn, but she was captured during a raid on [[Charleston]] in pursuit of a Christmas gift for David.[[Interrogation: Doe, Jane]] David incorrectly believed that the Responders had killed Rosalynn. Mad with grief over losing his family again, David ordered an attack on the [[Summersville Dam]], using [[Mini nuke (Fallout 76)|mini nukes]] stolen by the [[Blackwater Bandits]] from the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]] to blow up the dam and flood Charleston. In doing so, he also inadvertently killed Rosalynn, who was actually trapped in the jail cells of the [[Charleston Capitol Building]]. This incident would come to be known as [[the Christmas Flood]]. Some Cutthroats such as [[Carol Sweeney]] were so appalled that they splintered away from David.[[Scattered journal pages]] [[File:FO76 190721 Shine 2.png|thumb|250px|David's [[Rosalynn Jeffries' shrine|shrine]] for Rosalynn]] Though he put on the facade of a powerful warlord, David deeply mourned Rosalynn. He created a Miss Nanny in her image, christened [[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]], giving her some semblance of Rosalynn's personality, but as Rose notes, only the "fun" and upbeat side. As he was unable to recover Rosalynn's remains, David also erected a [[Rosalynn Jeffries' shrine|secret shrine]] to his old flame east of [[Ripper Alley]], not wanting other raiders to view him as "soft" and to give himself a sense of closure on the last personal connection he would ever have. David also began to drink himself into a stupor. David's raider gang endured and thrived despite the setbacks. A years-long guerrilla campaign waged by the [[Order of Mysteries]] took its toll on the raider clans, but David remained in control, attracting more and more recruits. The campaign came to an end when [[Olivia Rivers]], bitter and resentful of her [[Shannon Rivers|mother]]'s leadership, decided to defect by using [[Brody Torrance]] as a way to make inroads with the raiders. As Brody was the sole survivor of [[Mack Frazier]]'s veteran crew, David was initially skeptical of the proposal. However, without any other leads, he played along and allowed Torrance to work with Olivia to take down the Order.[[Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries#6-9-86: RE: Checkpoint Massacre|Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries; Brody's terminal, 6-9-86: RE: Checkpoint Massacre]] Despite the slow start, the investment paid off with the Order of Mysteries eventually being wiped out in November [[Timeline#2086|2086]], with Olivia facing her own mother in a final confrontation that led to Shannon Rivers' death. Olivia soon joined her mother when Brody mortally wounded her, making it clear David had no further use for Olivia and did not want to take the chance that she would turn on him like she had done with her mother.[[Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries#11-16-86: RE: Finale|Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries; Brody's terminal, 11-16-86: RE: Finale]] In [[Timeline#2086|2086]], [[Harpers Ferry]] was destroyed by the Scorched, which began pushing through [[the Mire]] and into the [[Savage Divide]] in the following years. By 2092, David recognized the threat, seeing panic spread and his empire beginning to crumble before his eyes, but he refused to leave his position or stop his activities. Privately, he had finally found peace at the loss of Rosalynn and came to believe that she was there with him in spirit.[[Unsent letter#Strange Bedfellows|Unsent letter]] In late [[Timeline#2096|2096]], he imprisoned [[Hank Madigan]], hoping to extort the Responders and [[Free States]] in exchange for the [[Scorched Detection System]] [[Uplink (quest item)|uplink]] which Madigan was carrying. Ultimately, he succumbed to the Scorched Plague when it ravaged the Savage Divide and was killed around 2102 by a [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] of [[Vault 76]].Events of [[Key to the Past]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Key to the Past]] }} ===Quests=== [[Key to the Past]]: The Vault Dweller of Vault 76 is tasked by [[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]] with mercy killing David and retrieving the Cutthroats' piece of the Raider stash code. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =Random raider armor |weapon =Random Scorched weapon |otheritem = |ondeath =[[Cutthroats key fragment]] }} ==Notes== Rose the robot comments positively of David, viewing him as having leadership skills and charisma, calling him a full package, as well as being tall, dark, and handsome. Rose also says David could be quite an emotional guy. She does not think [[Meg Groberg]] holds a candle to David. ==Appearances== David Thorpe appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. He was expanded upon in ''[[Wastelanders]]'' with the holotapes [[Board meeting]], [[Note to self (Wastelanders)|Note to self]] and [[Thorpe: 10/03/2077 9:34am]]. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox original raiders FO76}} [[Category:Scorched characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 raiders]] [[Category:Cutthroats]] [[Category:Arktos Pharma characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 unique creatures]] [[it:David Thorpe]] [[pt:David Thorpe]] [[ru:Дэвид Торп]] [[zh:David Thorpe]]

'''Edie Stevens''' is a deceased woman whose remains are found within [[wendigo cave]] in [[Appalachia]] {{In|FO76}}. 

==Background==
Edie was the wife of [[Morris Stevens]], the former leader of the [[Gourmands]]. Both she and her husband were exiled for violating the gang's code, which states to not feast on other members, after the half-eaten body of [[Gregory (Gourmands)|Gregory]] was discovered in Morris' room.<ref>[[Bolton Greens terminal entries#Entry 05|Bolton Greens terminal entries; Gourmand's terminal, Entry 05]]</ref><ref>[[Bolton Greens terminal entries#Entry 06|Bolton Greens terminal entries; Gourmand's terminal, Entry 06]]</ref> 

Following their exile, the couple lived in the wendigo cave together.<ref>[[Gourmands note]]</ref> While Morris went out for hunting, he did not share the meat with Edie, forcing her to live off of whatever remains he left for her. She also noted that both of them were changing.<ref>[[Edie's note]]</ref> In the end, Edie was killed and devoured by her husband.<ref>[[Morris's end]]</ref>

Always will.|Freddie in a holotape to her girlfriend|[[Freddie Lang's holotape]]|sound=Freddie Lang Wish the Bombs.ogg}} '''Alfreda "Freddie" Lang''' is a [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|glowing one]] at [[Blackwater Mine]] in [[Appalachia]], {{in|FO76}}. ==Background== Shortly before the [[Great War]], Freddie travelled to the Appalachian mountains, having heard ski season was beginning and the resorts were turning on their snowblowers. Since her [[LGBT representation in the Fallout series|girlfriend]], [[Lucie]], did not like skiing, Lang left without telling her to avoid arguing with her about the trip. While Lang was away, the War occurred, and Freddie believed that Lucie died. She felt guilty for Lucie's death, wishing that she had told her about the ski trip so they could have died together.[[Freddie Lang's holotape]] Lang survived the war, and remained in the mountains. She became the leader of the [[Blackwater Bandits]], one of the gangs that made up the first wave of [[Raiders (Fallout 76)|Appalachia's raiders]]. The Bandits made their home in the [[Blackwater Mine]] and were known for their stealth, being skilled enough to steal mini nukes from the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]].[[Blackwater Mine terminal entries#Low on chems|Blackwater Mine terminal entries; Blackwater Bandits terminal, Low on chems]] Lang did not trust her gang well enough to let her guard down or reveal too much of her personality beyond the rough facade of raider boss, so she used the former supervisor's terminal as a diary to confide thoughts which she felt would show too much vulnerability.[[Blackwater Mine terminal entries#Finally in!|Blackwater Mine terminal entries; Blackwater Bandits terminal, Finally in!]] [[Rob (Fallout 76)|Rob]], another member of the gang, tinkered with the [[Blackwater Mine: Innovations|uranium pump]] inside the mine. Over the course of several months, Rob accidentally and unknowingly released a substantial amount of [[radiation]] into mine as a result of his drunken tinkering.[[Blackwater Mine terminal entries#Radiation Leak|Blackwater Mine terminal entries; Blackwater Bandits terminal, Radiation Leak]] The gang remained unaware of the radiation leak, and Lang believed it was an illness which had not subsided in a world without medical care. Lang traded the stolen mini nukes to the [[Cutthroats]] for additional chems, so that the Bandits could continue to offset the effects of the "illness."[[Blackwater Mine terminal entries#People gettin' sick|Blackwater Mine terminal entries; Blackwater Bandits terminal, People gettin' sick]] By 2096, the effects of radiation exposure were visible on Lang when she visited the raiders at the [[Top of the World]], being described by [[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]] as "Not her usual bright and spirited self. Real sick. Her hair looked awful." After continued exposure, the Bandits died or ghoulified as a result of the radiation, and Freddie turned into a [[glowing one]]. Freddie left a final message on her terminal, with visible signs of mental decline, stating she intended to go deeper into the mine, where the radiation felt good.[[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]]: ''"Ah whatever, it's not like you can radio back. Anyhoo! If I recall, we completely lost track of the Blackwater Bandits back in '96. Freddie wasn't looking too good last time we saw her alive. Not her usual bright and spirited self. Real sick. Her hair looked awful.''"
([[Rose (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Rose's dialogue]])[[Blackwater Mine terminal entries#Help|Blackwater Mine terminal entries; Blackwater Bandits terminal, Help]] Freddie remained in the mine until confronted by a [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] searching for the [[Blackwater Bandits key fragment]]. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Key to the Past]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Key to the Past]]: The [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|player character]] must kill Freddie to retrieve the Blackwater Bandits' [[Blackwater Bandits key fragment|piece of the raider stash code]]. After Kerry's death, Mark sent out a public memo asking for a new roommate, sharing rent between the roommates at 55 [[Cap (Fallout 76)|caps]] per month.[[Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries#Roommate Wanted|Pleasant Valley cabins terminal entries; Common room terminal, Roommate Wanted]] At some point, Kerry went to Lewisburg after receiving intel from [[Brody Torrance]] that a member of the [[Order of Mysteries]] would be there.[[Kerry's orders]] Once there, he staked out the area, and it was decided that an ambush would be carried out from the rooftops during the Spring Garden Festival.[[Easy pickins]] However, the ambush failed, resulting in the death of Kerry and several other raiders.Kerry's corpse, along with other [[raider corpse]]s on the Lewisburg rooftops. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Initiate of Mysteries]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem =[[Kerry's orders]] |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== * Kerry's body uses the template of a [[raider corpse]]. I'm destroying that stupid [[Diehards key fragment|key fragment]].|[[Margie McClintock's holotape]]|sound=Margie McClintock.ogg}} '''Margaret "Margie" McClintock'''[[Pleasant Valley Ski Resort terminal entries#Reset User Passwords|Pleasant Valley Ski Resort terminal entries; Pleasant Valley network administration, reset user passwords]] is the deceased former leader of the [[Diehards]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Margie was the leader of the [[Diehards]], one of the gangs that made up [[Appalachia]]'s [[Raiders (Fallout 76)|raiders]]. However, they did not trust her much. Margie had been trying to convince the other gangs that they needed to create backups of their key fragments. She had her own room at the [[Sunnytop Ski Lanes]]. Margie confided in a fellow Diehard named [[Vincent Fried]]. She was, much unlike other raiders, taking measures to protect the residents of the [[Palace of the Winding Path]] from other gangs and only resorted to killing innocents when there was no other option. Margie and her husband also wanted [[David Thorpe]] to be exiled due to his killings of innocent people.[[Harland's up to no good]] However, many of the survivors they shook down refused to hand over goods and often even fired back, forcing the gang to constantly have to kill innocents for supplies.[[Concerns with Margie]] Along with the sudden disappearance of the Palace's residents, Margie eventually fell into a depressive state.[[Sunnytop Ski Lanes terminal entries#RE: Disappearance|Sunnytop Ski Lanes terminal entries; Vincent Fried's terminal, RE: Disappearance]] She eventually decided to take her own life through a chem overdose and hoped Vincent would be a more successful leader.[[Margie McClintock's holotape]] Her corpse can be found on the top floor of the Palace of the Winding Path, along with a [[Margie's goodbye note|goodbye note]] next to her. The Diehards would be led by [[Meg Groberg]] and flee Appalachia for their safety. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem =[[Margie's goodbye note]] (backpack) |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Margie McClintock appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox original raiders FO76}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Diehards]] [[pt:Margie McClintock]] [[ru:Марджи Макклинток]]

They took Milo out onto a rowboat with his belongings and drowned him in the [[Twin Lakes]], dumping his possessions in the water next to him.<ref>[[Raider note (Fallout 76)|Raider note]]</ref>

Need more... find... more...|[[Morris's end]]|sound=Morris's_end.ogg}} '''Morris Stevens''', later known as the '''Progenitor Wendigo''', was the former leader of the [[Gourmands]], one of the five [[Raiders (Fallout 76)|raider]] groups of [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Leader of the cannibalistic raiders known as the [[Gourmands]], Morris led the group with his wife, [[Edie Stevens|Edie]]. Though the Gourmands had established a code of 'never eat your own', a recent shortage of their food supply, as well as Stevens' increasingly depraved fixation with cannibalization, would lead to him and his wife murdering one of the Gourmands, whose half-eaten corpse was discovered by the rest of the gang.[[Bolton Greens terminal entries#Entry 05|Bolton Greens terminal entries; Entry 05]] Morris, despite his place as leader, was expelled from the Gourmands with Edie.[[Morris Stevens' holotape]][[Gourmands note]] They took shelter within the [[wendigo cave]], where his fixation worsened to the point that he devoured his wife and mutated into a [[Wendigo#Progenitor wendigo|wendigo]].[[Edie's note]][[Morris's end]] As the Progenitor Wendigo, he continued to prey on his former gang and other raiders in the region to the point where a considerable bounty was placed on his head, though none would come to successfully claim it.[[Raider's note (Fallout 76)|Raider's note]] Stevens was killed once the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] of [[Vault 76]] followed his trail in order to retrieve the [[Gourmands' key fragment|key fragment]] he still had in his possession. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Key to the Past]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Key to the Past]]: The [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|player character]] is tasked by [[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]] with retrieving the [[Gourmands' key fragment|Gourmands' piece]] of the Raider stash code, carried by Stevens. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =[[Gourmands' key fragment]] }} ==Appearances== Morris Stevens appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==Gallery== FO76_Morris_Stevens.png|Morris on alert ==References== {{references}} {{Navbox original raiders FO76}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Wendigo characters]] [[Category:Gourmands]] [[es:Morris Stevens]] [[pt:Morris Stevens]] [[ru:Моррис Стивенс]]

And maybe we'll forget any of this ever happened.|Rosalynn threatening [[Melody Larkin]]|[[Interrogation: Doe, Jane]]|sound=Fo76 rosalynn jeffries 002cb4ed 1.ogg}} '''Rosalynn Jeffries''', nicknamed '''Rose''' by [[David Thorpe]], was a [[Raiders (Fallout 76)|raider]] and girlfriend of the [[Cutthroats]]' leader, David Thorpe. She acted as the Cutthroats' second-in-command and managed to survive for five years after the [[Great War]]. ==Background== With her lover David Thorpe, Rosalynn would visit the [[Top of the World]] ski resort before the Great War. David was cheating on his wife [[Rita Thorpe|Rita]] with Rosalynn and had been for some time. The ski resort was one of their getaways. After the resort trip, David was going to divorce his wife and marry Rosalynn, but those plans were changed by the Great War.[[Rosalynn and David's ski trip]] Trapped at the Top of the World, with no help in the foreseeable future from the government or anyone else, Rosalynn and David (along with all the others vacationing at the resort) decided they had little choice but to become raiders, taking everything they needed to survive. The Cutthroats were the raider gang that emerged from the Top of the World. Along with the Cutthroats, many other gangs would go on to terrorize Appalachia, but the Cutthroats were the most powerful and feared of all of them. A perpetual thorn in the side of the [[Responders]] and [[Charleston Emergency Government]], David Thorpe would become its leader and Rosalynn Jeffries his second in command. To celebrate David's leadership, Rosalynn made a [[David's trophy|trophy]] for him with a skull and "World's Best Boss" on it. Rosalynn relished her new role in life as a raider, taking full advantage of to fully indulge in her chem addiction. On their anniversary, David stole chems for her and they spent the night under the stars near [[Ripper Alley]], with David remarking how he had never seen her happier.[[Photo of Rosalynn's memorial]] She would lead many raiding parties over the first couple of years after the Great War, but her final raid would be on Christmas Eve. On December 24, [[Timeline#2082|2082]], Rosalynn would lead a large raiding party into [[Charleston]] during Christmas, hoping to bring something nice back as a present for David.[[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]]: ''"Hey, it's you: whatever your name was. You got those key fragments for me? {{Tooltip|I'll take those for safekeeping. There's just one more little thing.|draw out the word "one"}} {{Tooltip|David had a mistress named Rosalynn. She wound up doing something stupid out of love for the man.|A little annoyed, as if this person was in direct competition for David's affection}} {{Tooltip|Tried to lead a raid on Charleston on Christmas Eve so she could bring him back something nice. Got herself killed in the process.|She looks down on Rosalynn's action, even though she's talking about the person she's effectively modeled after.}} {{Tooltip|We never were able to recover the body. I would have gone to do this myself, but well, it's... personal.|Serious. Even though she's scamming the player here, this is a personal issue. She doesn't want to be reminded that she's a facsimile of someone else}} {{Tooltip|Now, in order to create the cache master key from those passwords you got, I need the holotape program she had with her when she died.|Informative.}} You might have to look through the town's records to find out where they buried her body. I'd start with the Capitol Building. {{Tooltip|That's the last thing, I swear. Then we're golden.|She realizes that she's asking for more and more.}} Meet me at the cache in the basement of the ski lodge when you've got that holotape!"''
([[Rose (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Rose's dialogue]]) This raid would be repelled, but not without eight Responders losing their lives and twenty-four more receiving injuries in the process. Rosalynn would be the only raider taken alive, and her party would lose seven before the rest fled. During her interrogation by [[Melody Larkin]], the Responders told Rosalynn that they were going to use her false death as a way to anger David Thorpe and get him off the Top of the World, thereby cutting off the head of the Cutthroats, once and for all.[[Interrogation: Doe, Jane]] In her jail cell, Rosalynn wrote a [[Rosalynn's note|note]] to David, expressing her love for him and apologizing for getting caught. While the false news of Rosalynn's death did enrage David, he wouldn't fall into their hands quite so easily. Instead of coming down from the Top of the World, David blew up the [[Summersville Dam]] with a [[Mini nuke (Fallout 76)|mini nuke]] he stole from the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]]. This would later be known as "[[the Christmas Flood]]," that would wipe most of Charleston off of the map. Rosalynn would perish in this flood too, accidentally killed by her own lover.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Here are your keys. {{Tooltip|David had a mistress named Rosalynn. She wound up doing something stupid out of love for the man.|A little annoyed, as if this person was in direct competition for David's affection}} {{Tooltip|Tried to lead a raid on Charleston on Christmas Eve so she could bring him back something nice. Got herself killed in the process.|She looks down on Rosalynn's action, even though she's talking about the person she's effectively modeled after.}}"''[[The Christmas Flood (holotape)]] [[File:FO76 190721 Shine 2.png|thumb|250px|David's shrine created in Rosalynn's memory]] Her body still lies in the jail cells of the [[Charleston Capitol Building]]. At some point before 2082, Rosalynn's behavior and voice were used in creating the personality of the [[Miss Nanny (Fallout 76)|Miss Nanny]] [[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]], the current leader of the Cutthroats. I love this thing!|sound=Rose Emergency Alert.ogg}} '''Rose''' is the ''de facto'' leader of the [[Cutthroats]] [[Raiders (Fallout 76)|raider]] faction in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Initially thought by the [[Vault 76 overseer]] to be a human that had sheltered themselves away at the apex of the [[Top of the World]] ski resort and thus survived the ravages of the [[Scorched Plague]], the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] that eventually makes their way to the observation deck finds that Rose is not what the Overseer had in mind. Rose is a heavily modified [[Miss Nanny (Fallout 76)|Miss Nanny]] and self-proclaimed leader of the Appalachian raider gangs. Her behavior and voice are based on that of long-deceased raider [[Rosalynn Jeffries]], the mistress of former [[Cutthroats]] leader, [[David Thorpe]]. Her exterior has shown many signs of customization, such as a scrap metal 'mohawk', wrapped chains, and various 'tattoos' painted on her chassis. Thorpe sealed away several old memory banks within her, modifying her original Rosalynn programming.[[Strange Bedfellows]] Rose is also programmed to have a chem addiction like Rosalynn and requests the Vault Dweller give her any they have; her inability to use them as a robot is shown to be a complex she has, and so she desperately tries in her attempts to get high off them anyway, even claiming she has in order to keep up the act. Even with the raiders returning in 2103, Rose plans to remain at the Top of the World, for several reasons: Leaving the landmark would be tantamount to betraying David; the [[Toxic Valley]] white powder would be hell on her filters; and perhaps most importantly, [[Meg Groberg]] would likely trash her on the spot if she ever came back. Rose admits she likely "pissed off" Meg a few times back in the day. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |essential = |essential until = |ghost =yes |ghost until = |dead = |hostile = |ally = |affinity = |temp companion = |factions = |factions hostile = |quests started = * [[Signal Strength]] * [[Flavors of Mayhem]] * [[Key to the Past]] * [[Strange Bedfellows]] |quests involved = * [[The Missing Link]] * [[Reassembly Required]] |events started = |events involved = |encounters = |locations = |wares = |caps = |gold = |scrip = |medical services = |heal = |cure cripple = |cure radiation = |cure mutation = |cure disease = |cure addiction = |bonus = |bonuscd = |bonusdur = |other = }} ===Summary=== * She offers the player character tips of dubious usefulness, canned recruitment drives, and stories that give greater insight into the worldview of the raiders that once terrorized Appalachia. * Rose broadcasts her [[Top of the World Radio|personal radio channel]] from the Top of the World. The range of the channel is expanded once the player character completes [[Signal Strength]]. Upon beginning the quest, she starts broadcasting a new radio signal to keep tabs on the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]], though she mostly uses it to mockingly fake stereotypical radio broadcasts. * She sends the Vault Dweller on various tasks both for practical purposes, as well as her own cruel amusement. This includes giving the player character [[Flavors of Mayhem|a test]] to become a raider, as well as assisting them with finding a special [[Key to the Past|raider stash]]. ===Quests=== * [[Signal Strength]]: Rose requests the player character repair a radio for her in exchange for access to the [[Top of the World]] uplink chamber * [[Flavors of Mayhem]]: Rose will task the player character with learning the tactics used by the five raider gangs that once existed in [[Appalachia]] to see which works the best. * [[Key to the Past]]: Rose needs help locating five holotape key fragments dispersed among the five raider gangs to access a cache of supplies. * [[The Missing Link]]: Rose has information about [[Hank Madigan]] but will not divulge it until one assists her with various tasks. * [[Reassembly Required]]: The player character must search for a [[holotape for Rose]] in the desk of [[Abigayle Singh|Abbie]] to convince Rose to help set up the communications uplink. * {{Icon|FO76WL}} [[Strange Bedfellows]]: Rose is instrumental in getting to the new raider leader at [[the Crater]]. To lure Meg to the Top of the World, Rose requests a broadcast with David's voice to be played. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Notes== * In [[Top of the World]], a [[Rosalynn and David's ski trip|holotape recording]] between David Thorpe and Rosalynn Jeffries can be found. Ironically, Rosalynn's behavior and voice are later used to create Rose. * Despite being heavily modified in both appearance and programming, certain parts of her default Ms. Nanny programming affect Rose, such as wanting to give the Vault Dweller a bath,Rose: ''"Look, I don't want to be rude, but besides getting us what we need, there's another reason I want you hurry up and get outta here. [[Raiders (Fallout 76)|Raiders]] |role =Gang leader |location =[[Huntersville]] |hair color ={{Tooltip|Deep brown|HairColor18DeepBrown}} |eye color ={{Tooltip|Light brown|MaleEyesHumanLightBrown}} |hairstyle ={{Tooltip|Combover|HairMale18}} |facial hair ={{Tooltip|Honest Abe|BigBeard21}} |quests =[[Key to the Past]] |level =10 |special ={{SPECIAL|0,0,0,0,0,0,0}} |derived =[[Action Points]]: 100 |aggression =Unaggressive |confidence =Cowardly |assistance =Helps Nobody |factions =PlayerFaction |class =Citizen |combat style=Default |CK race =HumanRace |actor =[[Brian Krause]] ([[Trappers' warning]]) |edid =MTNL01_Corpse |formid ={{ID|004e35e6}} |refid ={{ID|004e35ec}} |dialogue = }} '''Walter Griswold''' is the deceased former leader of the [[Trappers (Fallout 76)|Trappers]] [[Raiders (Fallout 76)|raider gang]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== During the [[Great War]], Walter Griswold survived in what would become the [[Savage Divide]] region of Appalachia. When the survivors of the area's ski resorts formed into raider gangs,''[[Fallout 76 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide]]'' p.5: ''"'''RAIDERS'''''
''The Raider groups of Appalachia were bloodthirsty psychopaths who terrorized the other survivors, taking whatever they wanted from them. Expert scavengers, the Raider groups of Appalachia were surprisingly ingenuous when it came to salvaging old world technology. After the bombs fell, several wealthy tourists on Appalachian ski holidays reverted to their baser instincts. Selfishness turned to violence, and these entitled elitists became vicious Raiders."''
([[Fallout 76 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide faction profiles]]) Walter became the leader of the Trappers, a gang that made [[Explosive bait|improvised explosives]] and booby traps their specialty.[[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Hey, you're back! I guess you found it huh? I'm just going to assume ya did and move on.|Excited that the player didn't die. Anxious to move on though.}} Let's check with the Trappers next. They had a camp out near the Devil's Backbone so they could keep an eye out along the road from the southeast. {{Tooltip|We never did find out what happened to them. We were spread pretty thin by the time they disappeared. Someone, or something, probably got to them.|stress "-thing" on "something"}} Maybe they left a note behind or some other clue. They were real outdoorsy types. Liked camping and hunting. Be careful searching the camp for their piece of the key. {{Tooltip|If it wasn't obvious, they were really into traps.|She feels that she has to explain this to the player even though it's painfully obvious.}}"''
([[Rose (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Rose's dialogue]])[[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]]: ''"This one time, Chuck-he was the guy who came up with this crazy idea-laid out explosive bait along the trail after a raid. When the Responders came looking for us with their tracking dogs, well...Let's just say the hounds lost their scent. You know, because their heads were blown off. Ah whatever, you get what I'm saying."''
([[Rose (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Rose's dialogue]]) The Trappers were part of an uneasy alliance with the other gangs that made up Appalachia's raiders, to protect against the other [[Fallout 76 factions|factions]] and creatures of the region. As part of the alliance, the gangs kept their best loot in a safe and split the key amongst the five gang leaders.[[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Ah! Oh good, it's just you. What do you want?|Surprised, as if you just snuck up on her, but quickly relieved. She's a bit jumpy.}} {{Tooltip|I feel like I trust you enough now to let you in on a little secret.|She's being frank with the player.}} {{Tooltip|My old Raider pals left a cache of treasures behind when they all checked out. Problem is it's locked away and I can't get in there.|This frustrates her a little bit. She's been dying to know what's inside.}} {{Tooltip|Double problem: No one trusted each other enough to give anyone complete access to the treasure.|Doubly annoyed.}} So they split up the key. See, each gang's leader had a holotape with their own personal password on it. {{Tooltip|Find 'em all so I can patch 'em together and make the master key. It's more technical than that, but you wouldn't understand.|She talks down to the player a little bit, because she assumes she's way smarter than they are.}} {{Tooltip|Then, we'll have ourselves access to all that wonderful treasure. I'll probably even give you a fair share of the loot. Promise.|Excited. Even though she's being sincere, there should be a little doubt that she'll actually come through with her promise.}} Check out Blackwater Mine first. That's the last place we heard from Freddie Lang, the leader of the Blackwater Bandits. Pretty sure she had a terminal there. Might be worth a look-see."''
([[Rose (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Rose's dialogue]]) Walter Griswold and the Trappers decided to make [[Trapper's camp|their camp]] at the [[Devil's Backbone]], a rock formation just outside [[Huntersville]].[[Trappers' warning]] At some point, after hearing a commotion coming from the town, Walter sent a scout to investigate. The scout came back reporting of some "[[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|big ol' green 'uns]]" ransacking the town. Wanting to see for himself, Walter and the scout returned to the town just in time to see the super mutants fighting the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]]. When it appeared that the Brotherhood was going to lose [[Battle of Huntersville|the battle]], Walter and the scout retreated to their camp. Walter began to [[Trappers' warning|record himself]] explaining what happened and appealing to the other gangs for help in clearing out the super mutants from [[Huntersville]], before being attacked by the super mutants at their camp. The attack was repelled, and the Trappers began to plan for a counterattack but waited for reinforcements. The reinforcements never arrived,[[Trappers note]] either because the other gangs never received Walter's call for help ([[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]] claims she and the [[Cutthroats]] never heard what happened to the Trappers) or because the other raider groups were already spread too thin and were unable to provide assistance. The camp was attacked again, but this time the attack was more damaging: the super mutants captured Walter and several other members and took them to Huntersville. The surviving Trappers, leaderless and angered at the perceived betrayal of the alliance, fled the area, while Walter himself died in the town proper, where his corpse can still be found years later. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Key to the Past]] }} ===Quests=== [[Key to the Past]]: The [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] from [[Vault 76]] is contacted by [[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]] to reassemble the key to the safe containing the raider gang's main loot and needs to recover the Trappers key fragment from Walter's body in Huntersville. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Bandana (Fallout 76)|Camo bandana]] (non-playable)

I hope you can find me soon. Until then, be safe and... I love you. I... should have told you much sooner, in person.|[[Message for Jeff]]|sound=Amy Kerry.ogg}} '''Amy L. Kerry''' is a deceased associate of the [[Responder]]s in [[Appalachia]], found dead at [[Cow Spots Creamery]]. ==Background== Amy L. Kerry was a [[Vault-Tec University]] student, turned amateur scientist. She was also the girlfriend of [[Jeff Nakamura]] and an acquaintance of the Responders. Some time after [[The Christmas Flood]] happened in 2082, Jeff encountered Amy and attempted a marriage proposal but Amy sorrowfully declined before he even had the chance to make it, feeling focusing on rebuilding Appalachia was more important.[[The big day]] In 2095, Amy began staying around the [[Tygart water treatment]] site where she stayed in a trailer and had her own terminal where she wrote entries documenting her life.[[Tygart water treatment terminal entries]] Jeff would sometimes visit her and send messages to her terminal. Despite constant pressure from the group to join the Responders, Amy opted to remain separate from them but continued working on a project to create a program to monitor the environment for contamination by the [[Scorched]] with their assistance. The frequent requests for her to join caused her friction with Jeff and [[Maria Chavez]]. One day, Amy got bit by a [[Mole rat (Fallout 76)|mole rat]] and became quite ill. She thought she was done for, but Jeff came to visit her by chance. It made Amy realize how compassionate and noble Jeff was and how important he was in her life. However, loose lips at the Responders HQ ended up leading to the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]] catching wind of the project, which led to them trying to procure information and project assets from the Responders at gunpoint. However, even after being talked down by Maria, the Brotherhood would continue looking for Amy and her research. Amy learned that the Brotherhood was after her and she theorized that they were after her technology to use for their own purposes, even to create weapons. Amy noticed signs that the Brotherhood were close to finding her so she abandoned her trailer and went into hiding, as she refused to give the Brotherhood anything following the way they had treat Jeff and his fellow Responders. She left a [[Message for Jeff|holotape]] for Jeff, telling him he could find her at the place where they had their first date: [[Cow Spots Creamery]]. However, Amy apparently overlooked that a message from Jeff on her terminal also mentioned the location of the date. Her body can be found at the Cow Spots Creamery with a [[Message for Jeff|note]] for Jeff imploring him to share her research with the Responders. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = [[Ratty skirt (Fallout 76)|Ratty skirt]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =[[Amy's note]]
[[Pre-War money (Fallout 76)|Pre-War money]] }} ==Notes== * Amy mentions Jeff is her boyfriend in one of her terminal entries, though she apparently rarely, if ever, told Jeff that she loved him, as seen by her final message, making it one of her regrets. * It is unclear if Jeff met Amy before or after the Great War. He mentions he regained a positive mood after the Christmas Flood when he either met or re-met her. However, the photograph of them appears to depict them pre-War with clean clothing in front of a house and a car that do not appear damaged. ==Related holotapes== * [[The big day]] * [[Message for Jeff]] ==Appearances== Amy Kerry appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Responders}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Responder characters]] [[Category:Vault-Tec University characters]] [[ru:Труп Эми Келли]]

{{Quotation|Hello. This is Doctor Claire Hudson, and if you're hearing this, it means you must have completed my work and inoculated yourself. '''Doctor Claire L. Hudson''' was the [[Responders]]' chief medical officer and responsible for researching the [[Scorched]],<ref>[[Morgantown Airport terminal entries#Scorched research|Morgantown Airport terminal entries; Scorched research]]</ref><ref>[[Anti-Scorched tactics]]</ref> including the development of a cure for the [[Scorched Plague]] as part of the Inoculation Project.<ref>[[Morgantown Airport terminal entries#Personnel Files|Morgantown Airport terminal entries; Personnel Files]]</ref>

==Background==
Doctor Hudson was based in [[AVR Medical Center]], as the laboratory there had sufficient equipment for her to conduct her research.<ref>[[AVR Medical Center terminal entries#July 6th, 2096]]</ref> The goal was for her to develop a vaccine in time for the [[Fire Breathers]]' final mission to seal [[Big Bend Tunnel]] and prevent the [[Scorched]] from crossing the [[Savage Divide]],<ref name=firebreathers>[[AVR Medical Center terminal entries#October 20th, 2096]]</ref> but her efforts were hampered when the Sympto-Matic machine she was using blew a fuse and she was unable to get a replacement.<ref name=firebreathers/><ref>[[AVR Medical Center terminal entries#September 2nd, 2096]]</ref>

She was still at the AVR Medical Center when she got word of the Responders taking their final stand against the Scorched at [[Morgantown Airport]].<ref name=attack>[[AVR Medical Center terminal entries#November 7th, 2096]]</ref> Despite the vaccine not yet being finished, she decided to abandon her post to try and make it back to the airport, hoping to be able to help any Responders who were still alive. Before she departed, she left instructions regarding how to make the vaccine for the Scorched Plague, hoping it might help whoever might [[An Ounce of Prevention|find them in the future]].<ref name=attack/>

==Notes==
Claire's voice is heard on an [[Claire Hudson/Dialogue|automated broadcast]] after completing the quest [[An Ounce of Prevention]].

==Appearances==
Doctor Claire Hudson is mentioned only {{In|FO76}}.

It's okay, I am trying to be good now though.|[[Survivor story: Colonel]]}} '''Colonel''' is a deceased [[Responders|Responder]] found in [[Flatwoods]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Colonel can be heard telling his story in the holotapes [[Survivor story: Colonel]] and [[Survivor story: Responder Colonel]]. He was a troublemaker and prankster before the [[Great War]] and felt guilty for the war and the mutations, believing his father's words that bad things would not have happened had he behaved. He missed his father, who disappeared after the bombs dropped. Colonel left a note for his father in the [[Flatwoods meeting hall]], saying he would be waiting in the church with cereal, games and a sleeping bag for each of them.[[Dear daddy]] The Responders' database reveals he became a Responder as a volunteer[[Volunteer certificate]] when he was thirteen and was tasked with being the caregiver for the other children.[[Flatwoods terminal entries#Colonel|Flatwoods terminal entries; self-serve registration kiosk, Colonel]] He eventually became a full Responder approximately five years later. He mainly helped find people in Appalachia and get them to safety, along with teaching them how to survive. He also came to comprehend why his father left him behind, which drove him to make sure that he would take care of the younger children in the care of the Responders.[[I forgive you, dad]] By the time that [[Vault 76]] opens and the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] are released into Appalachia, Colonel has passed away. His body can be found on the front porch of a red house in Flatwoods, south of the overpass, next to the body of a raider. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =[[Survivor story: Responder Colonel]] }} ==Related holotapes== * [[Survivor story: Colonel]] * [[Survivor story: Responder Colonel]] ==Appearances== Colonel appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Responders}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Responder characters]] [[Category:Flatwoods characters]] [[ru:Колонэл]]

This is Dassa Ben-Ami, signing off for now.|sound=Dassa Ben-Ami.ogg}} '''Dassa Ben-Ami''' is a deceased member of the [[Responders]] found in [[Flatwoods]], [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Dassa was an anthropology student at [[Vault-Tec University]] studying for her Ph.D. in anthropology. While printing her thesis, the [[Great War]] broke out and she rushed to [[Vault 76]]. However, her father, a [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] employee, was only able to get two reservations into the vault. Dassa refused to go, insisting that he and her younger brother go to the vault instead of her. Returning home to [[Charleston]], Dassa survived on her own before enlisting with the [[Responders]]. Throughout her years as a Responder, she specialized in leadership, assisting with the recovery after [[the Christmas Flood]] and created the Survivor Stories, a series of holotapes recorded by survivors of the War that wanted to preserve their stories.[[Survivor story: Dassa Ben-Ami]] Dassa's last check-in was on November 5, [[Timeline#2096|2096]].[[Flatwoods terminal entries#Ben-Ami, Dassa|Flatwoods terminal entries; self-serve registration kiosk, Ben-Ami, Dassa]] She died sometime after that but prior to [[Timeline#2102|2102]], and her body was left on a stretcher in the [[Flatwoods]] church. In 2103, it was moved to the cemetery behind the church, where it can be found next to the corpse of [[Buzz Yates|"Buzz" Yates]]. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem =[[Survivor story: Dassa Ben-Ami]]

Hank Madigan.wikitext:
{{Infobox character |games =FO76 |image =Madigan.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |quests =[[The Missing Link]] |affiliation =[[Responders]]
[[Fire Breathers]]
[[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]] (formerly) |location =[[Top of the World]] |role =Fire Breather |eye color =MaleEyesHumanHazel |hairstyle =Tough Enough |height =1.00 |level =1 |derived =[[Action Points]]: 100 |special ={{SPECIAL|0,0,0,0,0,0,0}} |aggression =Unaggressive |confidence =Cowardly |assistance =Helps Nobody |class =Citizen |combat style=Default |CK race =HumanRace |voice type =NPCM_MTR06_HankMadigan |actor =[[Larry Herron]] |dialogue =[[Hank Madigan/Dialogue]] |edid =MTN_MQ_MadiganCorpse |formid ={{ID|004e25a1}} |refid ={{ID|00510456}} }} {{Quotation|This is a real game changer, [[Raleigh Clay|Raleigh]]... if what you say is true.|sound=Hank Madigan.ogg}} '''Hank Madigan''' was a member of the [[Responders]], a lieutenant of the [[Fire Breathers]], and a former member of the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]]. ==Background== After the Great War, Madigan initially enrolled with [[Taggerdy's Thunder]] and became a member of the Appalachian Brotherhood of Steel. He remained with the organization for years, afterward joining the [[Responders]]. Together with Melody, Madigan formed the Fire Breathers, an elite fighting unit of the Responders dedicated to fighting in the [[Ash Heap]] and preventing the [[Scorched]] from taking over. As a member of the Fire Breathers, Madigan continued to run independent operations over the mountains, which involved making a run at the [[AMS corporate headquarters]] in [[Watoga]]. He was responsible for the discovery that depleted ultracite laced munitions could inflict heavy damage against the Scorched, after he recovered research from [[Atomic Mining Services]].[[Message from Hank Madigan]] During this mission to AMS, Madigan also found leads for the [[Excavator power armor]] developed by the [[Garrahan Mining Company]].[[Charleston Fire Department terminal entries#Excavator Armor|Charleston Fire Department terminal entries; Fire Breathers master terminal, Excavator Armor]][[Madigan scouting report - Garrahan]] After the fall of the Brotherhood, Madigan ventured beyond the mountains into [[the Mire]] and made contact with the [[Free States]], after being caught at [[Raleigh Clay's bunker]] attempting to "figure out" one of the [[scorchbeast]] lures which had been set up there. When he learned that the device was one that could lure and disorient a scorchbeast long enough for a team of militants to eliminate it, he asked for proof, but [[Raleigh Clay]] told him that they were not willing to just share their discoveries with an ex-Brotherhood member and that he had some serious trust to earn.[[Madigan encounter]] He was also told that the device would already be completed if not for the raiders of the [[Savage Divide]]. In late 2096, determined to earn the trust of Clay and to save Appalachia from the [[Scorched Plague]], Madigan attempted to broker peace between the Responders and the raiders at the [[Top of the World]] in order to install the scorchbeast lure but was instead imprisoned in a cage by the [[Cutthroats]] leader [[David Thorpe]]. Thorpe hoped to extort the Responders and Free States in exchange for the [[Scorched Detection System]] [[Uplink (quest item)|uplink]] that Madigan was carrying. Although Madigan gave them information, the Cutthroats left Madigan to starve to death in the cage, although it is ambiguous if it was intentional as there are many indicators that the Cutthroats had been taken out by the Scorched Plague. The Cutthroats also destroyed Madigan's uplink and kept it in a cache in the basement of the [[Pleasant Valley Ski Resort]]. His corpse remains in the steel cage near [[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]] who mentions she was not present when Madigan died. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Fire Breather uniform]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Related holotapes== * [[Message from Hank Madigan]] * [[Madigan scouting report - Garrahan]] * [[Madigan encounter]] * [[Welcome to the Fire Breathers]] * [[Fire Breathers final exam briefing]] ==Notes== The name internally used by the game for this corpse incorrectly duplicates the name of [[Darion Jones]]. ==Appearances== Hank Madigan appears only {{In|FO76}}. ==Behind the scenes== In an unused holotape, Hank Madigan is mentioned as part of Marine Recon.{{Unused}} [[Maria Chavez]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Sergeant Madigan, is it?|Interrogating a new recruit.}}"''

Maria Chavez: ''"{{Tooltip|And why is that, exactly? Brotherhood's been a good ally to us. Taking you on could be seen as an act of bad faith. |Curious. This guy's suggesting the Brotherhood aren't the good guys you thought they were.}}"''
