The apocalypse and all. I know that seems weird but... I have freedom now. I can actually help people... I even met [[Garry Wilkins|somebody]], a volunteer who delivers supplies. Imagine that, right? Even when you think everything is over, it's... it's not.|[[Survivor story: Miguel Caldera]]|sound=Miguel Caldera.ogg}} '''Miguel Caldera''' is a deceased member of the [[Responders]] in [[Appalachia]], who plays a notable role in the faction backstory {{in|FO76}}. As a gay man, he is a part of the [[LGBT representation in the Fallout series|diverse representation of LGBT people in the game]]. ==Background== Prior to the [[Great War]], Miguel was a programmer working for [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]]. Burdened by soul-crushing office programming jobs, he longed for nothing more than to live in the country and focus on hiking.[[Survivor story: Miguel Caldera]] He also previously worked for the [[United States Space Administration]], where he wrote the encryption algorithm for the [[Deep Sleep project]]'s flight recorder as well as the [[Arachne]] killswitch program for the project's mainframe AI, [[ATHENA]][[U.S.S.A. encryption key program]][[Arachne]] After the bombs fell, he survived for several years alone in the wilderness, camping in the woods with a [[Protectron (Fallout 76)|Protectron]] which he had hacked to guard him as he slept. He met [[Dassa Ben-Ami]] one day when she was hunting for rabbits and agreed to join the Responders,[[Volunteer training program: Shelter]] acing their survival training programs.[[Morgantown Airport terminal entries#Hello, World!|Morgantown Airport terminal entries; Miguel's Journal, Hello, World!]] His main reasons for doing so were his fear of [[scorchbeast]]s and his desire to no longer live alone.[[Morgantown Airport terminal entries#The Cause|Morgantown Airport terminal entries; Miguel's Journal, The Cause]]: As a programmer, he became a boon for the Responders, becoming responsible for training volunteers and developing programs for robots and automated kiosks to take over tasks, in addition to reprogramming robots to fulfill roles needed by the Responders' operations. He also helped train others in outdoors survival, leaning on the experience he had gained since the War.[[Morgantown Airport terminal entries#Programming Again|Morgantown Airport terminal entries; Miguel's Journal, Programming Again]] His first major personal achievement was the creation of [[Mr. Fluffy]], a Protectron bodyguard and assistant. The robot, stitched together from countless damaged Protectrons, had an attitude problem and was none too pleased by its name (metallic surfaces are by definition not fluffy, and the failure to compute aggravated Fluffy's neural network).[[Morgantown Airport terminal entries#Mr. Fluffy|Morgantown Airport terminal entries; Miguel's Journal, Mr. Fluffy]] One day, during a supply run between [[Morgantown Airport]] and [[Flatwoods]], he met a volunteer responsible for delivering supplies named [[Garry Wilkins]], and they fell in love.[[Morgantown Airport terminal entries#Despair in Flatwoods|Morgantown Airport terminal entries; Miguel's Journal, Despair in Flatwoods]] As Garry was stationed at the Flatwoods outpost at the time, Miguel often made excuses to spend time there, including by programming elaborate systems which needed his attention. They eventually transferred to Morgantown Airport, where Miguel turned his attention to leading advanced survival training classes, as well as continuing his engineering and programming duties. At the same time, he was developing a reset program to make Mr. Fluffy less unconventional, including stopping him from staying at his side all the time, which he believed to be ruining his sex life.[[Morgantown Airport terminal entries#Reset Program|Morgantown Airport terminal entries; Miguel's Journal, Reset Program]] After Garry was killed during a [[Scorched]] attack on the airport, Miguel retreated to the woods after burying him in the Responder graveyard nearby. He took Mr. Fluffy with him and left [[Maria Chavez]] a message to tell her where he had gone, saying that he had to "figure things out."[[Morgantown Airport terminal entries#This is it.|Morgantown Airport terminal entries; Miguel's Journal, This is it.]] His last check in with the Responders was at Morgantown Airport on 15 June [[Timeline#2096|2096]].[[Flatwoods terminal entries#Caldera, Miguel|Flatwoods terminal entries; self-serve registration kiosk, Caldera, Miguel]] By the time the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] finds him, he lies dead in his camp near the airport, next to his destroyed tent. Mr. Fluffy questions his body as to why he didn't follow his own advice about building defenses and why he decided to cook [[Appalachili]], with an aroma that the robot states could be detected clear from the airport tarmac. This was a deliberate decision, mirroring the way that he claimed he wanted to die - not in an office, but with "a pot of [[Delbert Winters|Delbert]]'s chili, in the woods, and under the beautiful stars."[[Morgantown Airport terminal entries#Peace, Appalachia|Morgantown Airport terminal entries; Miguel's Journal, Peace, Appalachia]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |dead =yes |quests involved =[[Tentative Plans]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Flannel shirt and jeans (Fallout 76)|Flannel shirt and jeans]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Related holotapes== * [[Survivor story: Miguel Caldera]] * [[Volunteer training: Camping 101]] * [[Volunteer training program: Shelter]] ==Appearances== Miguel Caldera appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]'' and is mentioned in its update ''[[Wastelanders]]''. ==Behind the scenes== * Miguel is voiced by [[Eric Lopez]], who also voiced [[Scott Turner]] and [[Jesus Sunday]], among others. * In localized versions of the game, Miguel's voice is dubbed by Cédric Dumond (French) and José Manuel Pinto (Spanish). ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox Responders}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Responder characters]] [[Category:Vault-Tec characters]] [[Category:United States Space Administration characters]] [[ru:Мигель Калдера]]

None of the other Volunteer Bots had idiotic names.|sound=Mr. Fluffy 004f679b_1.ogg|Mr. Fluffy, on his situation and nickname}} '''Mr. Fluffy''' is a [[Responders|Responder]] [[Protectron (Fallout 76)|Protectron]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Mr. Fluffy is a [[Responders|Responder]] [[Protectron (Fallout 76)|Protectron]] that was hacked by [[Miguel Caldera]] to act as a personal bodyguard.[[Survivor story: Miguel Caldera]][[Morgantown Airport terminal entries#Mr. Fluffy|Morgantown Airport terminal entries; Miguel's terminal, Mr. Fluffy]] He was named Mr. Fluffy after a dog which was killed while Caldera was testing a bug with the Veterinary Bots,[[Morgantown Airport terminal entries#BUG: Veterinary Bot attacks animals.|Morgantown Airport terminal entries; Miguel's terminal, BUG: Veterinary Bot attacks animals.]] a nickname which the Protectron eternally resented.Mr. Fluffy: "''It's not enough that I am tethered to an invisible point forever, but the nickname? So uncouth. None of the other Volunteer Bots had idiotic names.''"
([[Mr. Fluffy/Dialogue|Mr. Fluffy's dialogue]]) His curmudgeonly personality may be a result of an unsolved bug that turned him into "a jerk." Miguel believed he had a fix for the bug but didn't get a chance to implement it before his death.[[Morgantown Airport terminal entries#BUG: Volunteer Bot personality becomes "mean"|Morgantown Airport terminal entries; Miguel's terminal, BUG: Volunteer Bot personality becomes "mean"]] Mr. Fluffy was with Miguel when he died and his Protectron programming prevented him from deviating from Miguel's final orders for him to guard the campsite and his body, even long after the latter's death,Mr. Fluffy: "''His last orders to me were... "Guard the Campsite, Mr. Fluffy."''"
([[Mr. Fluffy/Dialogue|Mr. Fluffy's dialogue]])Mr. Fluffy: "''You know, I've been tethered to Miguel for years. Years. Standing here with his rotten corpse... and you know what? I hate camping.''"
([[Mr. Fluffy/Dialogue|Mr. Fluffy's dialogue]]) expressing anger at how he had died in such a fashion, ignoring his own advice and instructions to others.Mr. Fluffy: "''{{Tooltip|Miguel, you should have followed your own advice and built turrets and walls and all those things. Why didn't you?|Angry at Miguel for dying in such a dumb way}}''"
([[Mr. Fluffy/Dialogue|Mr. Fluffy's dialogue]]) However, in his years of isolation, he had come to miss the act of watching volunteers set up their C.A.M.P.s, expressing excitement when he sees a volunteer doing so.Mr. Fluffy: "''{{Tooltip|It's been so long since I've had to monitor a volunteer who was building a camp. Did... did I miss this? I suppose so.|At first, excited... but then contemplative. The robot realizes that the thing it once hated was better than the world it now lives in.}}''"
([[Mr. Fluffy/Dialogue|Mr. Fluffy's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Tentative Plans]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Mr. Fluffy appears only {{In|FO76}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox robots}} {{Navbox Responders}} [[Category:Fallout 76 robots and computers]] [[Category:Protectron characters]] [[Category:Responder characters]] [[ru:Мистер Пушок]]

Trust me.|[[Survivor story: Sofie]]|sound=Sofie Yates.ogg}} '''Sofie Yates''' was a member of the [[Responders]] in [[Appalachia]] before seemingly having committed suicide by [[Timeline#2102|2102]]. ==Background== Sofie Yates was a volunteer candidate with the Responders and had been a student in Delbert's volunteer training class since January 20, [[Timeline#2096|2096]]. She was assigned to live at 10 Church Road.[[Flatwoods terminal entries#Yates, Sofie|Flatwoods terminal entries; Self-serve registration kiosk, People Directory, Yates, Sofie]] However, despite being a volunteer candidate for them, she did not believe in the Responders' mission. Sofie may not have been sound of mind after the bombs fell going by her [[NOTHING HELPS!|note]] to [[Tabitha (Fallout 76)|Tabitha]] and her [[Survivor story: Sofie|survivor's story]], in which she claimed she lived off cat food in a [[Super-Duper Mart (company)|Super-Duper Mart]] near her parents' corpses. She lamented that no one came to rescue her and advises listeners against helping others. She believed it was better to drop the sick off in the mountains and was stopped by [[Delbert Winters]] for trying. She implied that she had a part in his death, remarking that he would not be teaching anymore. She can be found dead with a blood spatter behind her head and a discarded [[Pipe gun (Fallout 76)|pipe auto pistol]] beneath her hand, seemingly having shot herself. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions univ |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Road leathers (Fallout 76)|Road leathers]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =[[Survivor story: Sofie]] }} ==Appearances== Sofie Yates appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==Behind the scenes== The voice actor script notes in the [[Survivor story: Sofie]] holotape states Sofie killed [[Delbert Winters]]. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Responders}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Responder characters]] [[Category:Flatwoods characters]] [[ru:Софи Йейтс]]

'''Steelheart''' is a [[Protectron (Fallout 76)|Protectron]] at [[Morgantown]] in [[Appalachia]]. 

==Background==
Steelheart is a part of the [[Back on the Beat]] event in Morgantown in which the player character escorts the robot in a city patrol. Steelheart was created by the [[Responders]] in order to stop the ghouls, Raiders and others from attacking Morgantown.<ref>[[Morgantown terminal entries#Purpose and Implementation|Morgantown terminal entries; Responders HQ terminal, Purpose and Implementation]]</ref> Steelheart is the first known repurposed police Protectron used by the Responders. Upon starting the event and activating Steelheart, one can find more of his backstory. The event is repeatable whenever Steelheart's battery is recharged.

So you can keep going.|sound=Vault 76 overseer 00402a82_1.ogg|The overseer discussing her past}} The '''Vault 76 overseer''', known in-game as simply the '''overseer''', is one of the main characters of ''[[Fallout 76]]''. She is the former leader and [[overseer]] of [[Vault 76]]. In [[Timeline#2102|2102]], she left the Vault prior to [[Reclamation Day]] on a mission from [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]], leaving her [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|vault dwellers]] to salvage [[Appalachia]] on their own, albeit with some care packages she left along the way. In [[Timeline#2103|2103]], she re-emerged in Appalachia and united with the dwellers of her Vault, assisting with the human resettlement of the region. Her two main goals were to help the dwellers find a way to create a widespread [[Nuka-Cola Vaccinated|vaccine]] against the [[Scorched Plague]], and to establish a new currency, [[gold bullion]], which could lead to a progressive new order to help maintain peace in the wasteland. ==Background== ===Pre-War=== [[File:F76 Personal Matters.png|thumb|left|200px|A room in her childhood home]] She was likely born sometime in the 2040s or 2050s. The only child of a couple from [[Sutton]], the overseer was a driven woman from the start. Whether it was running through a cornfield maze, getting straight A's in every possible subject or leading a troupe of [[Pioneer Scouts]], she was always hitting life hard and fast, with barely any time left for herself.[[Overseer's journal, entry 1]] Her father was a teacher, and her mother was a miner working for one of [[Appalachia]]'s many conglomerates. Together, they led a happy, content life, an American idyll, against a backdrop of the ever-worsening international situation and the [[Sino-American War]].[[Overseer's journal, entry 2]] [[File:F76 Morgantown High School.png|thumb|200px|left|The high school she attended]] She was one of the best students at the [[Morgantown High School]], spending most of her time in the library honing her skills. However, tragedy struck when her mother was killed in a mining accident. In [[Appalachia|West Virginia]], this was a common family story, but it did not make a difference for the future overseer. She withdrew into the library, seeking shelter among books, while her father tried to put the pieces back together. She fell in love with [[Evan (Fallout 76)|Evan]] around the same time, and found his arms particularly attractive. He graduated a year earlier than her and went to work in the mines like her mother, who had introduced the two. After her mother's death, Evan stuck with her, bringing her lunch to the library each day after his shift was over.[[Overseer's journal, entry 3]] The other pivotal event in her life was the career fair at Morgantown, where she met the [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] team. In her eyes, it was "like a light turned on." She decided to dedicate herself to protecting families, the future, and [[United States of America|America]]. With her grades, it was a matter of course for her to be accepted into the [[Vault-Tec University]]. Upon receiving her letter, she immediately visited her mother's grave with her father, the two of them just happy to have her stay in West Virginia. After four years of learning and breathing Vault-Tec, and a field posting at the [[Vault-Tec Agricultural Research Center]], the overseer finally graduated, with a degree in [[nuclear fusion]][[:File:FO76_Overseer_VTU_Diploma.webp|Vault 76 Overseer's diploma]] and honors in the overseer track. Her studies also included courses in expression, circuitry, commercial geography, physical training, computer science, mechanical drawing, and first aid. She was fast-tracked for an overseer position, skipping years of waiting, and at [[Vault 76]] to boot, a promising Vault in Appalachia. When she learned the news, she was ecstatic and danced around the living room. Evan proposed on the spot and she accepted his proposal. This marriage was never able to come to fruition. While she and Evan moved in together, her father died a few months after this. [[File:Fo76 intro possible overseer.png|thumb|150px|left|The overseer during the ceremony for Vault 76 in 2076]] On July 4th, 2076, she attended the opening ceremony of Vault 76's completion.[[Overseer's journal, entry 4]] She soon learned the truth about the Vaults, the [[Societal Preservation Program]], and the experiments that were going to be carried out on the dwellers. Although Evan wanted her to go public with the information, she hesitated. While she knew that experimenting on other dwellers was ethically wrong, the goal of finding the most suitable people to repopulate, to understand humanity pushed to the extremes, was a goal she could understand and empathize with. She justified it as necessary for the survival of humanity. Vault-Tec found out about her in short order, but instead of retaliating, the corporation instead took her into confidence after seeing how she agreed with much of their perspective, although there is no confirmation of her knowing about some of Vault-Tec's more sinister experiments. She was initially slated to be the overseer of [[Vault 101]] in Washington, D.C. due to her engagement with Evan; only by entering Vault 76 as an unmarried woman could she remain in Appalachia. She chose Vault 76 over Evan, and while she felt guilty over her decision, she expressed her belief that Evan was not Vault 76 material and that she had done what she thought was best for the world, as well as enforcing her desire to remain in her home state.[[Overseer's journal, entry 5]] If the overseer had attempted to enter Vault 76 with Evan, the corporation would have had to give Evan a spousal exemption, and the Vault had a long list of candidates more qualified than a mere miner, such as a civil engineer and a cousin to a Vault-Tec executive. The overseer broke off her engagement, betraying Evan and leaving him on the surface. ===Post-War=== [[File:Fo76 intro slide 12.png|thumb|right|250px|The overseer leading a Vault-Tec course about Pip-Boys to Vault 76 residents]] Although the early years were difficult, as the overseer was the youngest among the Vault residents, surrounded by the ''creme de la creme'' of society, she eventually gained their trust and learned to cooperate. At one point, she was awarded with the distinction of "Vault Dweller of the Year."[[:File:FO76WL Overseer's home desk.png|Plaque in the overseer's home]] She served at her post for 25 years, until [[Reclamation Day]], on October 23, [[Timeline#2102|2102]]. On that day, the overseer left Vault 76 several hours ahead of the others. A prepared recording greets the player character through the intercom while instructing them to leave the Vault. After ensuring the well-being of every Vault inhabitant for 25 years, she was directed by Vault-Tec to secure three nuclear silos, namely [[Site Alpha|Sites Alpha]], [[Site Bravo|Bravo]] and [[Site Charlie|Charlie]], for them, even if it meant going against the [[United States Armed Forces]]. She left a holotape for [[Pennington]] to give to the player character asking for assistance in her dangerous task. Scouting Appalachia for the silos, she also left a trail of holotape logs and journals for these individuals to find, and to help follow her.[[Overseer's log - Vault 76]] [[File:FO76 Overseers camp.png|thumb|250px|The [[overseer's camp]] near [[the Wayward]]]] Besides her Vault-Tec mandated job of finding the nuclear silos, the overseer journeyed to various locations in Appalachia to view what had become of her homeland. After realizing that Appalachia was initially bereft of human presence near the Vault but rife with mutants and rogue bots, she deployed her [[CAMP|C.A.M.P.]] at the crossroads north of [[Flatwoods]], setting up a rallying point for the dwellers. Against her advice, she left it behind, so that the dwellers could use it, while she moved south into Flatwoods.[[Overseer's log - C.A.M.P.]] Flatwoods was even more depressing than her first impressions, abandoned and ruined. She encountered her first [[Scorched]] victim there and realized that the situation was even worse than anticipated. The next stop was trying to find remnants of the [[Responders]].[[Overseer's log - Flatwoods]] Morgantown Airport was a nightmare. She remembered taking flight lessons at the airport, but after its fall to the scorchbeasts and their minions, it was a wasteland. The overseer analyzed the Scorched, observing them from afar and realized the terrible truth: The disease took over its host, eventually burning them from the inside out, creating petrified, fragile corpses that fell apart. She was then attacked by a [[scorchbeast]], which put the final variable into the equation, its source. The already daunting task of controlling the military's nuclear potential became a desperate fight against an extinction-level event.[[Overseer's log - Morgantown]] Although the Responders proved to be a dead-end, the automated training they left behind came in use. She moved south to [[Charleston]], tracking down the [[Fire Breathers]]. She realized these daring men and women fought the scorched more than anyone and resolved to find them.[[Overseer's log - Firehouse]] [[File:FO76 Evan.png|thumb|250px|Evan transformed into a Scorched]] Besides her Vault-Tec directive, the overseer took a small detour, to visit places associated with her past. She eventually managed to find her fiancé Evan, who turned into a Scorched after succumbing to the [[Scorched Plague]]. Heartbroken, she locked him up in a warehouse basement atop Mount Blair and picked up the trail, focusing on the job at hand. Still, she asked [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] who heard her message to put him out of his misery, as she worked towards securing the nukes and containing the plague.[[Overseer's journal, entry 6]] The trail led her to the Top of the World, where she encountered [[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]], briefly. Rose's crude ways and demands for a quid pro quo did not agree with the overseer and she forged on, taking the [[Free States]] on.[[Overseer's log - Top of the World]] Although she despised them as traitors and secessionists who turned their backs on America, she needed to know what they knew and what they wanted to do.[[Overseer's log - Free States]] The breadcrumb trail continued to [[Charleston]] and the capitol building, where the office of the disgraced [[Sam Blackwell|Senator Sam Blackwell]] was located. At this point, dealing with the demented automated systems began to grate on the good overseer.[[Overseer's log - Charleston]] Unable to continue, she turned to the other clues found during her investigation, namely, the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Appalachian Brotherhood of Steel]]. She picked up the trail at [[Camp Venture]], continuing to their fortified headquarters at what was once [[Fort Defiance|Allegheny Asylum]].[[Overseer's log - Camp Venture]] She realized they were a military outfit descended from the [[United States Army|Army]] at Allegheny, and that they knew how to fight the Scorched. However, the secure elevator installed by the Brotherhood stood in her way. The only way get through it was to enlist.[[Overseer's log - Allegheny]] She headed to [[Camp McClintock]], where the automated training system put her through her paces and eventually accepted her into the Army, as Overseer Private/Private Overseer (she never really decided on which one sounded better).[[Overseer's log - McClintock]] Having traveled up and down Appalachia, finding the remnants of what has been and what could have been, she realized what destroyed her beloved West Virginia - discord. Instead of cooperating, the various groups grew apart from each other, closed ranks, and refused to work with each other. The Brotherhood, the Responders, Free States, and especially the [[Raiders (Fallout 76)|raiders]], all refused to cooperate long term and paid the price, as they all went extinct. She was determined to lead by example and not let others fall into the same trap.[[Overseer's log - Fort Defiance]] However, even as an Army soldier, her rank was too low to fool the automated systems at any of the silos. She never reached [[the Whitespring bunker]], and was thus unable to gain a promotion, left with nothing to show for her effort and the fear that someone might figure out how to access them, sooner or later.[[Overseer's log - Site Alpha]][[Overseer's log - Site Bravo]][[Overseer's log - Site Charlie]] [[File:FO76 Mountainside Bed & Breakfast (Overseer's log).png|thumb|250px|The overseer's implied blood from her injuries at the [[Mountainside Bed & Breakfast]]]] Even after surviving a [[mole miner]] attack in the mountains,[[Overseer's log - Mountainside]] her hopes were almost completely crushed when her Vault family, the people she sacrificed everything for, started launching nukes manufactured by the [[Appalachian Automated Launch System]], away from [[fissure site]]s and into other areas. She still hoped for their redemption, but something told her that the nuclear arms race would only get worse before it got better.[[Overseer's log - Nuke launch]] Aside from the nukes, other factors such as the Scorched Plague and seeing her neighborhood in ruins demotivated her from staying in Appalachia. Exploring the region firsthand and seeing all the destruction in Appalachia and the lack of survivors further dismayed her. As a result, she temporarily left Appalachia, needing time to get away from the region and emotionally process all that happened. ===''Wastelanders''=== {{Quotation|Broadcasting to the people of Vault 76. This is the Overseer. We need to talk. Face to face. I've missed all of you, but this isn't just about a reunion. We have work to do. I'll be waiting in Sutton.|Vault 76 overseer|[[Overseer's broadcast]]|sound=Overseer's broadcast.ogg}} In [[Timeline#2103|2103]], one year after Vault 76 opened, the overseer, like many Vault Dwellers, was shocked to see people coming back to Appalachia.''[[Wastelanders]]'' trailer As a result, knowing that her Vault 76 family would need guidance again with information pertaining to the newcomers to the area, the overseer set up her new home in the town of [[Sutton]], only a short distance up the road from where her [[Overseer's camp|C.A.M.P.]] had been set up when she left Vault 76 a year ago. She also set up a radio broadcast for the Vault Dwellers, imploring them to reunite with her. [[File:FO76WL Overseer dweller.png|thumb|250px|The overseer with a Vault Dweller]] When Vault Dwellers found her at her new house, she took them downstairs to meet her Mr. Handy assistant [[Davenport]], and explain the details regarding Appalachia becoming populated again, but also asking them if they took care of the Scorched Plague with finding the inoculation that the [[Responders]] had been working on at [[AVR Medical Center]] before they and the other factions were wiped out by the [[Scorched]] and [[scorchbeast]]s. Her concern is justified: If the newcomers are not given the inoculation, they could fall victim to the Scorched Plague and the threat of the Scorched getting beyond Appalachia would start all over again. To prevent this, she asks them to travel to [[the Crater]] and [[Foundation]], meet the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|settlers]] and [[Crater Raiders|raiders]], and convince them to be given the inoculation to ensure if they are attacked by the scorchbeasts, they will be safe from the Plague and can fight back against them alongside the Vault Dwellers to ensure they can't threaten the lands beyond Appalachia. [[File:FO76WL Overseer fighting Scorched.png|thumb|250px|left|The overseer assists in creating Scorched vaccines at the Nuka-Cola plant]] Once the leaders of the two factions agree to have their groups inoculated, the overseer joins with the Vault Dwellers as they travel to the [[Kanawha Nuka-Cola plant]] to use their own blood and inherent antibodies to mass-produce the inoculation to deliver to the settlers and raiders, thus protecting them from the Scorched Plague.[[The New Arrivals]] The overseer would participate in the distribution effort, visiting the Crater at some point.[[Meg Groberg]]: ''"Your Overseer came through on the wide distribution over here. Guess we'll hold off on raidin' that old Nuka plant... for now."''
([[Meg Groberg/Dialogue#61|Meg Groberg's dialogue]]) After inoculating the settlers and raiders, the decision is made to then investigate [[Vault 79]], the real reason everyone is returning to Appalachia due to rumors of treasure being hidden in the Vault and everyone wanting to get a piece of it, including the settlers and raiders. [[File:F76WL OO Meeting Probot.png|thumb|250px|The overseer visiting her former university]] Traveling back to her alma mater, [[Vault-Tec University]] in [[Morgantown]] with one of the Vault Dwellers, the overseer learns from the [[Professor-bot]] now in charge of VTU that her access to the university's restricted wing has been revoked. Only when one passes the overseer exam in the Simulation Vault does the Professor-bot grant them access. The group must progress through a maintenance area accessed from the simulation Vault, guarded by some of the campus' surviving security robots. Once finding the restricted wing, the overseer discovers that Vault 79 had been built by Vault-Tec to preserve the United States' gold bullion reserves from Fort Knox in the event of nuclear war, and is heavily fortified to prevent theft. The overseer realizes only two factions would have the knowledge and skill to break into Vault 79 to get at the gold; the settlers and the raiders. As a result, she asks the Vault Dweller to speak to their respective leaders, [[Paige]] and [[Meg Groberg]], to see if one or both of the groups would be willing to join forces with the individuals to access Vault 79 and retrieve the gold. She later learns of the success in getting into Vault 79 with either the Settlers or Raiders and is happy to know that it looks like Appalachia will soon be getting back on its feet thanks to the gold and her intentions for it being put to good use. ===After ''Wastelanders''=== After the conclusion of the ''Wastelanders'' questline, the overseer will remain in her home in Sutton. As of [[Timeline#2104|2104]], she is still active in the effort to inoculate the people of Appalachia against the Scorched Plague, having given vaccines to [[Patricia Myers]] at [[Nuka-World on Tour (location)|Nuka-World on Tour]].[[Nuka-World on Tour terminal entries#Visitors|Nuka-World on Tour terminal entries; manager's terminal, Visitors]] ==Personality== {{Quotation|One of these days, I'm going to drill that cynicism out of your head. But fine. Moan and groan all you want. You've earned the right. I guess I'll just hold on to hope for the both of us.|sound=Vault 76 overseer 005896a3 1.ogg}} The overseer is a kind, idealistic and altruistic woman, enjoying listening to radio plays such as [[The Silver Shroud]] with her parents when she was younger. She was driven with the desire to be the best at whatever she did, trying to get straight As; she could not just be a pioneer scout, but wanted to be a leader. She is a bit stubborn in this regard, such as whenever she has an idea she thinks she is good. For example, she commits to the idea of breaking into Vault 79 to take its gold and start a new economy, refusing to take no as an answer. However, she was also molded by Vault-Tec to fulfill the corporation's motives. Vault-Tec presented itself as humanity's savior, and she was impressed by the claims that it would protect America. She had a pragmatic view of the Societal Preservation Program, but she also kept it a secret from the general public because a part of her could see the benefits of it, showing that she is not immune to being a bit selfish in order to try to protect her own life in the face of a nuclear war, since if she tried to become a whistleblower, Vault-Tec would have most likely dismissed her overseer position and left her to die outside a Vault. She was also influenced by Vault-Tec propaganda to believe that Free States were traitors, showing her instilled patriotism. While in Vault 76, she found living with the same group of people a challenge. Still, she could never stop thinking about Evan constantly for 25 years, trying to comfort herself that he survived and that they would reunite someday. She does appear to have some survivor's guilt, saying, ''"I wish I could say I would've made another choice. That I would've picked dying in this house together when the bombs fell."'' She realizes how incredibly fortunate she is to even be alive when nearly all of humanity died. [[File:FO76WL Overseer cornered.png|thumb|250px|The overseer fighting a feral ghoul]] After experiencing the wasteland, she became more cynical, especially after seeing what Evan became. Despite the horror, she does not let go of her dream of her Vault Dwellers being able to reclaim the world. She does change her tune about Vault-Tec as well, breaking Vault-Tec protocol to leave her C.A.M.P. behind, and also admitting, ''"I thought they had let me into their plans. That we were... special. But now I'm wondering if we were all just one big experiment to them. Just like everyone else."'' Although she needed a year to get away from Appalachia due to how traumatizing its destruction was, she eventually returned, determined to assist her Vault Dwellers she briefly left behind. Exhausted, she also stops worrying about the morality of the Societal Preservation Program, and whether or not she and her Vault Dwellers are free from Vault-Tec's plans. She understands that no matter how much a human being regrets the past and wishes it could have been changed, as well as their life choices, mentally healthy people must move forward from the pain of the past, and try to build healthy futures for themselves with wisdom and resolve. She also recognizes that people need to try to start seeing the world through their own eyes, and now realizes organizations can have dangerous power that can control the way people think, with Vault-Tec and her being no exception. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion =yes |ghoul =yes |quests started =* [[Reclamation Day]] * [[Overseer's Mission]] * [[Personal Matters]] * [[The New Arrivals]] * [[An Ounce of Prevention]] * [[Overseer, Overseen]] |quests involved =* [[First Contact]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Reclamation Day]]: The overseer's recorded message asks the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] to leave Vault 76. * [[First Contact]]: When the Vault Dweller leaves Vault 76 for the first time, they are tasked with finding their overseer in [[Flatwoods]]. * [[Overseer's Mission]]: Player characters are tasked with finding her logs as she scouts for the nuclear silos. * [[Personal Matters]]: Player characters are tasked with finding her personal journals that have been left in places important to her. * [[The New Arrivals]]: The overseer tasks one with inoculating the settlers and raiders to protect them from the [[Scorched Plague]]. * [[An Ounce of Prevention]]: The overseer may give this quest if the quest has not been started yet and if the Vault Dweller talks to her once they are level 20 or higher. She requests the Vault Dweller get vaccinated against the Scorched Plague. * [[Overseer, Overseen]]: The overseer goes to Vault-Tec University and encourages the Vault Dweller to help her begin a gold-based currency by finding a way into Vault 79. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = [[Vault 76 overseer jumpsuit]]
[[Eyeglasses (Fallout 76)|Eyeglasses]] |weapon = Random ranged weapon |otheritem = |ondeath = }} {{Inventory |game =FOS |title =yes |image =FoS 76 Overseer.png |apparel =[[Sturdy vault suit]] |weapon = }} ==Related holotapes== {{Columns|2| Overseer's log: * [[Overseer's log - Vault 76]] * [[Overseer's log - C.A.M.P.]] * [[Overseer's log - Flatwoods]] * [[Overseer's log - Morgantown]] * [[Overseer's log - Firehouse]] * [[Overseer's log - Top of the World]] * [[Overseer's log - Free States]] * [[Overseer's log - Camp Venture]] * [[Overseer's log - Allegheny]] * [[Overseer's log - McClintock]] * [[Overseer's log - Charleston]] * [[Overseer's log - Fort Defiance]] * [[Overseer's log - Grafton]] * [[Overseer's log - Site Alpha]] * [[Overseer's log - Site Bravo]] * [[Overseer's log - Site Charlie]] * [[Overseer's log - Nuke launch]] * [[Overseer's log - Mountainside]] Overseer's journal: * [[Overseer's journal, entry 1]] * [[Overseer's journal, entry 2]] * [[Overseer's journal, entry 3]] * [[Overseer's journal, entry 4]] * [[Overseer's journal, entry 5]] * [[Overseer's journal, entry 6]] }} ==Notes== * Prior to the release of ''[[Wastelanders]]'', the overseer's name or likeness was never confirmed in-game, although a cartoon depiction of her is shown in the [[Personal Matters]] quest achievement graphic. A woman resembling this depiction can be seen sitting on the seat closest to the lectern during the speech about the completion of Vault 76 in the [[Fallout 76 intro|opening cutscene]], as well as in the opening slides where the Vault Dwellers are being trained for Reclamation Day. In-game files, including an NPC simply named "Overseer" confirm that this woman is indeed the overseer. She existed in the game's files but was not used anywhere in-game prior to ''Wastelanders''. * When in the overseer's childhood home in [[Sutton]], one can view her [[Vault-Tec University]] diploma on the wall where she majored in "nuclear fusion" and her SPECIAL stats are listed on it in addition to other course scores. However, the lines beside her SPECIAL stats are skewed, with 8 numbers listed instead of 7. No name is visible on her diploma. * According to her report on the [[Top of the World]] building, she is shown to have an extreme intolerance for profanity. ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|Good morning, Vault 76. This is the Overseer. I hope you all enjoyed the party last night. Even those who may have overindulged and... overslept. But it's time to get up and get out there. We've been locked away long enough. Today... is Reclamation Day. It may be time to leave, but I'll never forget the day you all entered Vault 76. You come from every walk of life, every race, color, and creed. But you all share one very important trait. You are this country's best and brightest. But more importantly... you'll always be my family.|sound=Overseer announcement.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Please, I gave 76 everything. You were all so brilliant. The first few years were hard, but we learned to trust each other. You learned to trust me. I was young... So young... Younger than most of you. But you accepted me as your Overseer.|sound=Fo76 overseer please 0003d4e8 2.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|The more I travel this godsforsaken 'Wasteland,' the more I realize what truly destroyed [[Appalachia|West Virginia]]. And what destroyed any chance the survivors had of... actually surviving. Mistrust. All these divergent groups... [[Responders]], [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]], whatever. Separately, they had everything necessary to beat the odds. Brains, brawn, and bravado to spare. And what did they do? Close ranks. Get paranoid. Refuse to work with one another. And it cost them all their lives. People of Vault 76, if you're listening, do NOT fall into the same trap.|sound=FO76 Overseer The more.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Look, I believe in Vault 76. I still do. That's why I know we'll get past this. I can't undo the nukes being used, but we can build a better future together.|sound=Vault 76 overseer 00402a65_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Abandoned you? Do you have ANY idea how hard it was to walk out that Vault door on my own? Knowing I might not see any of you ever again? Breaking Vault-Tec protocol to leave behind my C.A.M.P.? The holotapes? The care packages? All with the vague hope that they might keep you all safe? I've never stopped being your Overseer. Never.|sound=Vault 76 overseer 004286cb_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|That's added your blood sample as an ingredient. I guess that technically makes you Nuka-Cola's newest flavor? Actually, maybe don't think about that too much.|sound=Vault 76 overseer 003fe440_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|If there's anything I've learned in all this, it's that humans can and will abuse technology. So, I agree with the Brotherhood's stance on collecting and containing technology... To a degree. Our world has become wild, deadly. People need to be able to protect themselves-not out of some classic American principle, but out of survival. If they plan to hoard away weaponry, they must offer protection in return. And I can't imagine they have the numbers, or possibly the will, to do so.|sound=Vault 76 overseer 005e6574_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Damn, that was a big hit...|sound=Vault 76 overseer 005904ef 1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Getting too old for this...|sound=Vault 76 overseer 005904e8 1.ogg}} ==Appearances== The Vault 76 overseer appears in ''[[Fallout 76]]'', first appearing physically as an interactive character in the ''[[Wastelanders]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. Before the update, she could only be seen in the opening video and in an achievement icon, as well as her voice being present in holotapes. She also appears in ''[[Fallout Shelter]]''. ==Behind the scenes== [[File:FO76 5th Ani 3.png|thumb|250px|The overseer seen during the [[Fallout 76 5th Anniversary]]]] * The overseer is voiced by [[Adrienne Barbeau]]. Quest designer [[William Shen]] praised her performance, saying she was "amazing in the booth" and "just came in there and belted."[https://youtu.be/41_kixGZM3U?t=3400 Writing the Worlds of Bethesda (reference starts at 56:40)]:
Kenneth Vigue: ''"Voiced by the amazing Adrienne Barbeau."''
[[William Shen]]: ''"She was amazing in the booth, by the way. Like, just came in there and belted, it was great."'' ** Barbeau delivered a three minute speech in-character as the overseer for the [[Fallout 76 5th Anniversary]]. In it, the overseer talked about how proud she was of her Vault Dwellers and their accomplishments, and the friendships they made. Seeing the Vault 76 community support itself reassured her that her choice to return to Appalachia was the right one. ** In localized versions of the game, her voice is dubbed by Evelyne Grandjean (French), Maki Izawa (Japanese) and Elena Ruiz de Velasco (Spanish). * William Shen and [[Emil Pagliarulo]] worked on the writing of the overseer's logs. The development team realized that there needed to be a character guiding the player through the events of the world (as the game initially launched without living humans), so the character of the overseer actually came relatively late in development.[https://youtu.be/41_kixGZM3U?t=3373 Writing the Worlds of Bethesda (reference starts at 56:13)]:
[[William Shen]]: ''"Emil and I worked on the overseer's notes together, cause we realized, 'Oh, we kinda need a character that's leading you through everything that's happening in the world and giving you a sense of purpose.' Because for a while, it was just like, 'Hey, the Vault's opened. And get out there.' And then we needed a through line. So the character of the overseer actually came really late."'' * Before work began on ''Wastelanders'', there were plans to have a [[Fallout 76 developers|developer]] enter the game and play as the overseer, so that the community would realize that it was a human player, and not an AI controlling her. However, they soon realized that this was not a sustainable idea because of server sizes.[https://www.twitch.tv/videos/704158228?t=00h36m39s QuakeCon at Home 2020 (NL): Interview with Jeff Gardiner and Mark Tucker (reference starts at 0:36:39)] (dead link) * During ''Wastelanders''{{'}} development, Shen was initially wary to let the player get rid of the overseer's logs, but eventually relented and found that it helped conclude part of the overseer's story to turn in her tapes to her.[https://youtu.be/41_kixGZM3U?t=3428 Writing the Worlds of Bethesda (reference starts at 57:08)]:
[[William Shen]]: ''"Well, y'know, during the Wastelanders update, we actually brought the overseer back and we actually made her a character you can interact with. So that was a lot of fun. It was great to like, also come back to her story and try to have the conclusion for it. Like, you can finally give her all the tapes, right? Like, that was a big thing."''
Kenneth Vigue: ''"I was so glad. I was getting OCD with them in my..."''
William Shen: ''"I was like... 'cause I had an argument about it, I was like, 'No, they're quest objects, we should just hold onto them...' They're like, 'Will, we want to get rid of these tapes. We don't want the tapes anymore. Let me turn in the tapes.' I was like, 'Okay, fine, we'll change the tapes! So, get rid of the tapes, it's fine.'"'' ==Gallery== ===''Fallout 76''=== Fallout 76 overseer trailer.png|The original ''Fallout 76'' trailer in which her hair appears very dark, almost black Fo76 '''Poole''' is a [[Mister Handy (Fallout 76)|Mister Handy]] in [[Vault 76]].

==Background==
Poole is one of the Mister Handies that serves Vault 76. He is in charge of Station #6 (Get a Job!) on [[Reclamation Day (event)|Reclamation Day]], where it offers a [[Pen (Fallout 76)|pen]] and [[Black-rim glasses (Fallout 76)|black-rim glasses]], and advice for the sorts of roles that [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] exiting the vault can play in the wasteland.

Poole has remained at this station even years past Reclamation Day, all because of the last few dwellers who are still staying in the Vault. He 
has grown tired of its role, and has taken to pleading for the stragglers to finally leave.

You got a lot more to prove to be one of us.|sound=Axel 0059ef1c_1.ogg}} '''Axel''' is a member of the [[Crater Raiders]] at [[the Crater]]. ==Background== Axel joined the raiders at some point before their return to [[Appalachia]]. He guards the main bridge into [[the Crater]]. He is generally honest but will lie to protect those he cares about.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What's the scoop on Axel?"''
[[Meg Groberg]]: ''"Good kid. Seems to be pretty honest, unless he’s protecting someone he cares about. Then, he’s got a reliable tendency to lie for them and be the fall guy."''
([[Meg Groberg/Dialogue#175|Meg Groberg's dialogue]]) Once, he protected his best friend [[Creed]] from being beaten by [[Surge]] for cheating during a card game by covering for him and was beaten himself.[[Creed]]: ''"Heh, more than you'd think. He'd rather get in trouble himself than see someone else suffer. Why, just a couple weeks back, I was playing cards, and I may have used some slight of hand to give myself an edge. Surge figured it out, but Axel stepped in and told her he slipped me an extra ace card when he was dealing. Saved my ass, but got his own beat. Then Barb ratted on him, told Surge he was just lying to protect me, and Surge just beat his ass again."''
([[Creed/Dialogue#99|Creed's dialogue]]) Ironically, Creed is shown not being above throwing Axel under the bus to protect himself, as Creed lies about Axel working with [[Lev]]. Axel will even risk death or exile by covering for his girlfriend [[Barb (Wastelanders)|Barb]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Any chance she could be working for Lev?"''
Axel: ''"What? No, that's crazy! I'm the one working for Lev, not Barb!"''
Vault 76 resident: ''"I don't believe you'd risk exile or death for someone you’re having a little fling with. It has to be someone else."''
Axel: ''"Whoa, uh... no need to go asking anyone else any questions. Really, it was me!"''
([[Axel/Dialogue#151|Axel's dialogue]]) Barb compares Axel to being like a puppy dog who likes to think he can protect everybody, but is not as tough as he thinks he is. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[From Russia With Lev]] }} ===Quests=== [[From Russia With Lev]]: Axel can be interrogated to determine who the snitch is. {{Infobox incomplete|FO76WL}} {{for|other people named Barb|Barb}} {{Infobox character |games =FO76, FO76WL |image =Barb_Wastelanders.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Female |family =[[Creed]] - brother

[[Lev's crew]] (formerly) |role = |location =[[The Core|Crater Core]] |quests = |karma = |level = |tag skills = |derived = |voice type =W05_NPCF_Barb |actor =[[Sandra Saad]] |dialogue =[[Barb (Wastelanders)/Dialogue]] |edid =W05_Raider_Barb |formid ={{ID|0053c248}} |refid ={{ID|0053c232}} }} {{Quotation|Uh, I like long walks along nature trails and hate it when assholes like you ask too many questions.|sound=Barb 0056dd02_1.ogg}} '''Barb''' is a member of the [[Crater Raiders]] located inside the [[Crater Core]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== After her parents died, Barb and her older brother [[Creed]] survived together in the wasteland keeping each other alive. Eventually, both of them joined the raiders sometime prior to the group's return to Appalachia, after hearing they could make their own fortune and that the raiders didn't care where they came from. Despite depending on her brother in the past, she now views him as a coward because he does not want to engage in raiding and she feels he gets her into trouble. She feels he has always been a loser.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What can you tell me about Creed?"''
Barb: ''"You want to know about my brother? Creed's a coward, always has been."''
([[Barb (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#142|Barb's dialogue]]) She is currently dating her brother's best friend, [[Axel (Wastelanders)|Axel]], whom she thinks is just like a puppy dog that is not as tough as he thinks.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you know about Axel?"''
Barb: ''"A lot. Me and Axel are shacking up. He's like a puppy dog who likes to think he can protect everybody, but he's not as tough as he thinks he is."''
([[Barb (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#143|Barb's dialogue]]) [[Meg Groberg]] likes Barb, but is aware how she has a self-preserving attitude and is willing to lie to keep up her reputation.[[Meg Groberg]]: ''"I like Barb, but she's all about self-preservation. She's quick to lie to save her own ass, but loves seeing someone else fall from grace. She'll snitch if she knows someone else is guilty."''
([[Meg Groberg/Dialogue#177|Meg Groberg's dialogue]]) She is described by her brother as being a troublemaker who lies to cover herself up; she once killed [[Wren (raider)|Wren]]'s dog because the dog would not stop barking and got away with it because Wren believed her alibi. Barb is said to dislike children, once not deciding to cover for [[Ra-Ra]] after she stole some of Meg's snacks, having told Meg the truth. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |killable = yes |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[From Russia With Lev]] }} ===Quests=== * [[From Russia With Lev]]: Barb is the snitch and must be made to tell [[Lev]]'s location. Depending on the player's actions, the player may threaten her not to deal with Lev again, or choose to kill her. **If Barb is killed, she will say "screw you!" and not go down without a fight. The raiders underground will not react to Barb attacking the Vault Dweller, and Barb apparently can not go upstairs. ***Outside, Axel and Creed will somehow already know Barb is dead in an omniscient manner. Axel may say, ''"I can't believe Barb's dead! I mean, that's what happens to traitors, but... oh Barb."'' and Creed may say, ''"Barb's really dead. She was my little sister. I mean, it had to be done, for everyone's safety, but... man.... I don't know what to do now."'' These lines are part of their idle dialogue as the player can not have a conversation about it. ***Meg can be informed later; she replies she figured Barb was the mole on account of the Vault Dweller killing her. Meg brushes it off, saying she isn't mad since she said earlier to take care of the problem by any means necessary. Meg says she would only be upset if she said not to kill Barb and this order was defied. Meg finishes up the conversation by saying she can live with sending a not-so-subtle message to everyone else if people decide to become traitors. There will be a small gain of Raider reputation. **If Barb is alive, the player may tell Meg that Barb was the mole which will result in a small gain of Raider reputation. Meg will spare Barb but keep her in line. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Survivalist's outfit]] |weapon =Combat sniper rifle |otheritem = |ondeath =Combat sniper rifle

Blackeye: ''"Bones doesn't let anything go. It can get old fast but we're used to it. Blackeye sure beats the hell out of Heather though."''
([[Blackeye/Dialogue#85|Blackeye's dialogue]]) is a member of the self-proclaimed "[[Blackwater Bad Boys]]" [[Crater Raiders]] group at [[Ohio River Adventures]]. ==Background== Blackeye worked as a first grade teacher before the [[Great War]], though she says that she was never one for "soft living."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What was your life like before the war?"''
Blackeye: ''"Would you believe it if I told you I was a school teacher? Don't get the wrong idea though. I was never one for soft living."''
([[Blackeye/Dialogue#95|Blackeye's dialogue]]) She prefers robbing [[Foundation]] [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|settlers]] to disciplining her class over things like turning in spelling homework,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"The life of a school teacher was a hard one, huh?"''
Blackeye: ''"You ever try to herd a horde of seven year olds, much less enforce turning in their spelling homework? Yeah, I didn't think so."''
([[Blackeye/Dialogue#86|Blackeye's dialogue]]) especially on a Monday.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Disciplining children... are those skills that transfer over to being a raider?"''
Blackeye: ''"You joking? I'll take holding up some Foundation chumps over my old 1st grade class any day of the week. Especially on a Monday."''
([[Blackeye/Dialogue#87|Blackeye's dialogue]]) After joining the Raiders, she lived in [[the Crater]] for a time before becoming part of the group sent to establish an outpost at Ohio River Adventures with [[Fishbones]] and [[Gills]], where they could coordinate the trade of [[Mirelurk (Fallout 76)|mirelurk]] products such as [[Mirelurk egg (Fallout 76)|eggs]] and [[Softshell mirelurk meat (Fallout 76)|softshell meat]]. Although Gills was later replaced by [[Bruiser (Wastelanders)|Bruiser]], the group successfully built up the location. Fisheyes, wanting to keep up morale, gave Blackeye her nickname in reference to an incident where she accidentally hit herself in the face with a plank of wood on her first day.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Blackeye, huh? What's her deal?"''
[[Fishbones]]: ''"Really pulls her weight around here. She's a sharp one and deadly too, but a bit of a klutz. Earned herself a little pet name too. First day workin' out here, tripped over a loose board and smashed her face up. Been callin' her Blackeye ever since. Pretty sure she loves it."''
([[Fishbones/Dialogue#66|Fishbones' dialogue]]) Despite being a talented sharpshooter, she is described as a klutz by Fishbones. Blackeye, Bones and Bruiser now lead the outpost, though they have recently been having troubles with mirelurks attacking the docks. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = * ''[[Raider Fish Camp]]'' |quests involved = }} ===Other interactions=== Blackeye can be sold [[Mirelurk (Fallout 76)|mirelurk]] meat as way to increase [[Wastelanders reputations|reputation]] with the Raiders, but only one product per day. [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] will need to wait a day before selling new product to her, especially collecting it from helping [[Fishbones]] defend the water purifier from mirelurks. Blackeye requires 15 [[Mirelurk egg (Fallout 76)|mirelurk eggs]], 10 [[Mirelurk meat (Fallout 76)|mirelurk meat]], 5 [[Softshell mirelurk meat (Fallout 76)|softshell mirelurk meat]], or 1 [[Queen mirelurk meat (Fallout 76)|queen mirelurk meat]]. Giving her a piece of mirelurk queen meat earns more reputation than regular or softshell mirelurk meat. Occasionally, when delivering the meat to Blackeye, she'll possibly reward Dwellers with some random items, such as weapons or mirelurk products. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =Random raider outfit |weapon =Random ranged weapon |otheritem =[[Stimpak (Fallout 76)|Stimpak]] x1 |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Blackeye appears {{In|FO76WL}}. ==Gallery== Blackeye.png|Full view of Blackeye ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox raiders FO76}} {{Navbox original raiders FO76}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders raider characters]] [[Category:Crater Raiders characters]] [[Category:Diehards]] [[ru:Фингал]]

{{Infobox character |games =FO76, FO76WL |image =FO76WL Bruiser portrait.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |affiliation =[[Blackwater Bad Boys]], [[Crater Raiders]] |role =Member |location =[[Ohio River Adventures]] |quests = |hair color ={{Tooltip|Dark brown|HairColor14DarkBrown}} |eye color ={{Tooltip|Brown|MaleEyesHumanBrown}} |hairstyle ={{Tooltip|Rad Rage|ATX_HairMale17}} |facial hair ={{Tooltip|Playboy|Beard17}} |level =1 |derived ={{Derived stats FO4|hp=534|ap=50}} |special ={{SPECIAL|8,4,0,0,0,5,0}} |aggression =Aggressive |confidence =Foolhardy |assistance =Helps Friends and Allies |factions =W05_CraterRaiderFaction |class =raiderClass |combat style=csRaiderRanged |CK race =HumanRace |voice type =W05_NPCM_
GenericRaider01 |actor =[[Andrew Kishino]] |dialogue =[[Bruiser (Wastelanders)/Dialogue]] |edid =LvlRaiderMale_WL059 |formid ={{ID|00595298}} |refid ={{ID|0055bdec}} }} {{Quotation|Only thing better than a short conversation is no conversation.|sound=Bruiser 0057cf6d_1.ogg}} '''Bruiser''' is a member of the [[Crater Raiders]] sub-group known as the [[Blackwater Bad Boys]] at [[Ohio River Adventures]] {{in|FO76WL}}. ==Background== Bruiser once lived in a [[Vault]]; according to [[Fishbones]], Bruiser's memories of pre-[[Great War|War]] life before the Vault are muddled.[[Fishbones]]: ''"Anyways, Bruiser didn't remember much about his life before the Vault... not even his name. Been Bruiser ever since."''
([[Fishbones/Dialogue|Fishbones' dialogue]]) Bruiser claims that he was, at one time in his life, a "warrior" who fought in an arena alongside a team of at least seventy, and that many people traveled to see him; he says that he wore heavy armor, while a war band played loud music and beautiful girls performed acrobatics nearby.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What was your life like before all of this?"''
Bruiser: ''"I don't remember much, but I was a mighty warrior that fought in an arena. Hundreds of people came to watch me from all over. I wore heavy armor... and a band played war music... with drums and great, powerful horns. Oh, and beautiful girls! There were beautiful girls doing acrobatics."''
([[Bruiser (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Bruiser's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"It sounds like you must have enjoyed it. You remember it well and fondly."''
Bruiser: ''"Those were great times. I had a team too. Real comrades. We marched into battle together to crush our enemies. There must have been seventy of us."''
([[Bruiser (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Bruiser's dialogue]]) If the player character points out that his description of the event sounds similar to a game of [[Football|American football]], Bruiser will reject the notion, adamant about his memories as a fighter.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I think you might have been playing a game called football."''
Bruiser: ''"Football? What's that?"''
Vault 76 dweller: ''"You work with a team to move a ball past your opponents defense to score points."''
Bruiser: ''"A game? No. I was a mighty combatant. That sounds like the lousiest game I've ever heard of. I bet those Foundation wimps play it. Weaklings."''
([[Bruiser (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Bruiser's dialogue]]) Eventually, Bruiser's memories faded and he forgot even his own name. At some point, he left the Vault he lived in and ended up in [[Appalachia]]. After helping establish [[the Crater]], [[Fishbones]], [[Gills]] and [[Blackeye]] were sent to establish an outpost at Ohio River Adventures, where they could coordinate the trade of [[Mirelurk (Fallout 76)|mirelurk]] products such as [[Mirelurk egg (Fallout 76)|eggs]] and [[Softshell mirelurk meat (Fallout 76)|softshell meat]]. While making the trip southwest, Fishbones woke up one night to Bruiser "beating the tar" out of Gills, who was on night watch. Bones figured that he had found Gills' replacement, as Gills could no longer walk from the beating he received. Bruiser, Bones and Blackeye now lead the outpost, though they have recently been having troubles with mirelurks attacking the docks. Bruiser is not one for conversation;Bruiser: ''"Only thing better than a short conversation is no conversation."''
([[Bruiser (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Bruiser's dialogue]]) he prefers to let his fists do the talking for him,Bruiser: ''"I let my fists do the talkin'."''
([[Bruiser (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Bruiser's dialogue]]) makes liberal threats of violence against those who annoy him,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Ever consider meditating at the end of the day? Clearing your head and taking a deep breath?"''
Bruiser: ''"Jokes. Yeah, jokes are funny. Real funny until I push you off the dock."''
([[Bruiser (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Bruiser's dialogue]]) and relishes in the chance to inflict physical harm.Bruiser: ''"I like to punch things, 'specially faces."''
([[Bruiser (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Bruiser's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Sometimes when I get angry I just count to 10 and say to myself, 'It'll be ok.'"''
Bruiser: ''"I could count to 10 and punch you in the face if you'd like."''

A little help goes a long way out here.|sound=Fishbones 0055b26a_1.ogg}} '''Fishbones''', often nicknamed '''Bones''' and whose real name is '''Billy''',Fishbones' associated voice type is W05_NPCM_Billy_CB. is the leader of the [[Crater Raiders]] sub-group known as the [[Blackwater Bad Boys]], based at [[Ohio River Adventures]]. ==Background== Fishbones attended leadership workshops before the [[Great War]], indicating he worked in a corporate setting.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You guys all go by nicknames. Whose idea was that?"''
[[Blackeye]]: ''"That's all Bones. Claims it's good for morale. Says it's something he learned in a leadership workshop back before the war."''
([[Blackeye/Dialogue]]) After the war, he joined up with the raiders at some point and was present during the founding of [[the Crater]], along with [[Blackeye]].[[Blackeye]]: ''"I've been working under Fishbones for awhile now. We both were part of the original gang back at Crater."''
([[Blackeye/Dialogue]]) Although he helped build up the settlement, he was sent far away from the headquarters as part of a supposed promotion, as he believes the other raiders saw him as a threat to their leadership;A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"So you're out here because someone wanted you out of the way?"''
Fishbones: ''"Pretty much. We were a great team too, but they don't see it that way. So I got promoted and relocated and they don't have to deal with me no more."''
([[Fishbones/Dialogue]]) Fishbones suspects this was because his leadership was too efficient for them.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Maybe they thought you were the right guy for the job out here."''
Fishbones: ''"I don't buy it. They wanted me to think this was a promotion so I wouldn't cause trouble. Worked too, till I got here and saw what was cut out for me."''
([[Fishbones/Dialogue]]) They sent him to establish an outpost at Ohio River Adventures with [[Blackeye]] and [[Gills]], where they could coordinate the trade of [[Mirelurk (Fallout 76)|mirelurk]] products such as [[Mirelurk egg (Fallout 76)|eggs]] and [[Softshell mirelurk meat (Fallout 76)|softshell meat]]. During their time at the outpost, Fishbones also added extra ingredients to their meat, alleging that it's not dangerous or harmful,[[Fishbones]]: ''"Anyways, we found a way to stretch Mirelurk meat. Made it real profitable. Can't taste a difference and it won't kill yah or nothin'."''
([[Fishbones/Dialogue]]) yet keeps customers coming back.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You're putting something in the Mirelurk meat?"''
Fishbones: ''"Better believe it. It triples profits. We got a couple of extra ingredients, actually. Keeps customers coming back too, 'cause its so tasty of course."''
([[Fishbones/Dialogue]]) While making the trip southwest, Bones woke up one night to [[Bruiser (Wastelanders)|Bruiser]] "beating the tar" out of Gills, who was on night watch. Bones figured that he had found Gills' replacement, as Gills could no longer walk from the beating he received. Bones, Bruiser, and Blackeye now lead the outpost, though they have recently been having troubles with mirelurks attacking the docks. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = * ''[[Defend the Raider Camp from attack]]'' |quests involved = }} ===Other interactions=== Fishbones occasionally needs help defending the [[Water purifier (Fallout 76)|water purifier]] from attacks by [[Mirelurk (Fallout 76)|mirelurks]]. It can lead even the most righteous down the darkest of paths.|sound=Caleb Fisher 00590a86_1.ogg}} '''Caleb Fisher''' is a technician for the [[Crater Raiders]] located inside the [[The Core|Crater Core]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Fisher was born and raised among the [[Amish]]. After the [[Great War]], he began to lose his faith and no longer believed in the god he was raised to worship, as many church leaders saw their survival as vindication of their beliefs. Not wanting to be associated with such a mindset, Fisher used his Rumspringa, an Amish coming-of-age process, to leave the church.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Are you a religious man, Fisher?"''
Caleb Fisher: ''"Once upon a time. It's hard to shake what you're brought up to believe since birth, no matter how bad this world turns."''
Resident: ''"How do you go from Amish to here?"''
Caleb Fisher: ''"After the war, my faith... wavered. Anyone could understand that. But to some in my community, it vindicated them. They believed their survival meant they walked the true path. I couldn't be among that mind set, so I used Rumspringa as my chance to leave."''
([[Caleb Fisher/Dialogue#295|Caleb Fisher's dialogue]]) He put his faith in hard work and other human beings who could prove themselves instead. After leaving, Fisher joined with Lev's gang before he met [[Meg Groberg|Meg]]'s raiders, and his time with them convinced him that his faith was detrimental to his survival. He likes Lev's ruthless style of leadership more than Meg, believing that her "heart" is a risk. However, he knows that Lev would not hesitate to get rid of [[Lucky Lou|Lou]], so he often sides with Meg to keep Lev in line and preserve his friendship with Lou. Fisher's and Lou's friendship is so close that Lou wishes Fisher to have his belongings after his death.[[Lou's goodbye note]] Despite his upbringing, he is highly skilled with technology. He is responsible for the thankless job of setting up and maintaining much of [[the Crater]]'s infrastructure, but often complains due to the constant amount of work shoved on him by the other raiders.[[The Core terminal entries#Water Purifier|The Core terminal entries; Fisher's terminal, Water Purifier]] He was the one who created [[Weasel|Weasel's]] vocal collar, adapted from the research of [[Eddie Harrison]] which he found in [[Monongah]].[[The Core terminal entries#Vox Collar|The Core terminal entries; Fisher's terminal, Vox Collar]] He also refurbished an old suit of [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]] power armor into [[Raider power armor (Fallout 76)|raider power armor]].[[The Core terminal entries#Power Armor|The Core terminal entries; Fisher's terminal, Power Armor]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |killable =yes |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Cheating Death]] * [[From Russia With Lev]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Cheating Death]] - Fisher knows where [[Lucky Lou|Lou]] has gone, and the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] must ask him to find out. With [[Charisma (Fallout 76)|Charisma]] 8+, [[Strength (Fallout 76)|Strength]] 8+, or by having hacked his terminal ([[Fallout 76 perks#Intelligence|Hacking 3]]), he will answer directly, providing a tracking signal which points to the [[Carleton Mine]]. Otherwise, he will mislead the residents to [[Kogan]] at the [[Crater watchstation]], after which he will tell the truth. * [[From Russia With Lev]] - Fisher betrays [[Meg Groberg|Meg]] and joins [[Lev|Lev's]] gang along with [[Surge]]. He is found at Lev's hideout at the [[Poseidon Energy Plant WV-06|Poseidon Energy Plant South Expansion]] in full [[Raider power armor (Fallout 76)|raider power armor]] and will attack the Vault Dweller. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Raider waster outfit]]

And do I get any thanks? Well, I do. But I could use more.|sound=Caleb Fisher 0059f145_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|I feel bad about misleading you. Once you bring Lou back, I hope bygones will be bygones.|sound=Caleb Fisher 0055553e_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|I believe Faith is a weakness in this world. It's just the mannerisms I can't seem to shake.|sound=Caleb Fisher 00590a84_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Lev gave us orders to kill anyone coming here from Crater. That includes you!|sound=Caleb Fisher 0056fa19_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|I didn't want to do this, but you and Meg are forcing my hand!|sound=Caleb Fisher 0056fa22_1.ogg}} ==Appearances== Caleb Fisher appears {{In|FO76WL}}. ==Behind the scenes== Caleb is voiced by actor [[Chris Andrew Ciulla]], using what appears to be an emulation of a Pennsylvania Dutch accent, though some German intonations are present as well. I think I'm onto something here..|sound=Creed 0059ef36_1.ogg}} '''Creed''' is a [[Crater Raiders|Crater Raider]] found outside in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== After their parents died, Creed and his younger sister [[Barb (Wastelanders)|Barb]] survived together in the [[wasteland]] keeping each other alive. Eventually, both of them joined the Raiders sometime before their return to Appalachia. Creed is well known in [[the Crater]] as both a coward[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What can you tell me about Creed?"''
[[Barb (Wastelanders)|Barb]]: ''"You want to know about my brother? Creed's a coward, always has been."'' and a pushover.[[Meg Groberg|Meg]]: ''"Creed's kind of a liar, but only up 'til a point. He's a major pushover. If you put enough pressure on him, he'll always buckle and come clean with the truth."'' He once stole [[chems]] from [[Ae-Ri]] but admitted to being the thief after being asked only three times.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Why do you say he’s a coward?"''
[[Barb (Wastelanders)|Barb]]: ''"'Cause it's true. Just last week, he stole some chems from Ae-Ri's store. Instead of shutting up or pinning it on someone else, he caved after Ae-Ri asked him. Three times was all it took. Did you do it? No. Did you do it? No. Did you do it? Yes. I mean, that's not exactly how it went down, but might as well have been. What an idiot. Now he's paying her back and then some."'' He also stole some tools from [[Caleb Fisher]] to fix up a [[Power armor (Fallout 76)|power armor suit]] he found but gave them back after being grilled, with Fisher also confiscating the power armor.[[Axel (Wastelanders)|Axel]]: ''"He recently "borrowed" some tools from Fisher. Now, Fisher's not a very confrontational kind of guy, but he kept grilling Creed about it, and Creed eventually told him everything. Turns out Creed was just trying to rebuild a suit of power armor he found. When Fisher found out, he took it to rebuild himself. Probably the right call. Creed would have wrecked it."'' Creed views his sister affectionately, despite her tendency to snitch on him, although she has a poor opinion of her older brother. He also thinks of [[Axel (Wastelanders)|Axel]] as his best friend.Creed: ''"Axel? He's my best buddy. Is something wrong? Did he cover for Barb again and get himself into trouble? She doesn't deserve him."'' He dislikes [[Lev]], after he made several passes towards his sister.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Would she ever work for Lev?"''
Creed: ''"No way. That creepy old Russian used to make passes at her. It was ugly. Barb always used to complain about him, until I told Meg about it. Meg finally threatened his manhood with a shotgun and told him to step off. He backed down."'' He looks down on the [[Cult of the Mothman]] and the idea of the [[Mothman]] being a god, saying if there is a god, it is the [[Mega sloth]]. He says he would not mind starting a Cult of the Megasloth. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[From Russia With Lev]] }} ===Quests=== [[From Russia With Lev]] - Creed can be interrogated, but he ultimately is not the snitch and doesn't know where Lev is. If the player kills the snitch, Creed can be informed of it. He is a bit distraught and taken aback, but claims it had to be done for everyone's safety. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Survivalist's outfit]] |weapon =Random ranged weapon |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Creed appears {{In|FO76WL}}. ==See also== * [[Things to remember]] ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox raiders FO76}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders raider characters]] [[Category:Crater Raiders characters]] [[ru:Крид]]

Gail thinks they need to find their own Ra-Ras.|Gail regarding super mutants|sound=Gail 0059f162_1.ogg}} '''Gail''' is a [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|super mutant]] who came to [[Appalachia]] in [[Timeline#2103|2103]]. She is loyal to the [[Crater Raiders]]. ==Background== Gail left her home sometime long before 2103 and, in the following years, found herself alone with nobody to take care of her. During this time, she found [[Ra-Ra]], who had been abandoned by her own companions, and they quickly bonded because of their solitude.The [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Who is Ra-Ra?"''
Gail: ''"{{Tooltip|Ra-Ra is precious little human girl. Gail met Ra-Ra years ago.|She had fondness for Ra-Ra}} Ra-Ra was alone. Gail was alone. Now Ra-Ra and Gail are together. Ra-Ra take care of Gail. Gail take care of Ra-Ra. Ra-Ra is what matters most to Gail."''
([[Gail/Dialogue|Gail's dialogue]]) Since then, they have protected and watched out for each other, with Gail becoming a surrogate mother to Ra-Ra. Gail and Ra-Ra came to Appalachia in 2103, and she was introduced to [[Meg Groberg]] by Ra-Ra, who had found Meg and brought her to help them out when Gail had needed aid. Impressed by Meg's acceptance of her being a super mutant, and by Meg's additional assistance in caring for Ra-Ra, they chose to join the raiders at [[the Crater]].The Vault Dweller: ''"How did you two end up with Meg?"''
Gail: ''"Meg good human. Ra-Ra found Meg when Gail needed help. Meg didn't care that Gail was Super Mutant. She help Gail anyway. Meg help raise Ra-Ra and protect her. She take care of us, and we help her in return."''
([[Gail/Dialogue|Gail's dialogue]]) However, her relationship with the other raiders such as [[Lev]] and [[Surge]] is shakier, especially because they find her unnatural and freakish. Gail feels frustrated by the fact that the rest of the raiders make up excuses to not help her when she needs it, claiming her temperament is too poor to offer assistance. She insists that if she is angry, it is precisely due to the lack of help. She also has a disparaging opinion of other super mutants but believes that they would benefit from the same type of friendship she has found with Ra-Ra. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =Yes |temp companion =Yes |ghoul =yes |quests involved =* [[Fun and Games]] * [[Buried Treasure]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Fun and Games]]: [[Meg Groberg]] tasks the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] of [[Vault 76]] with recruiting Gail and [[Ra-Ra]] for the [[Vault 79]] heist. Gail agrees to join, so long as the Vault Dweller first helps her find Ra-Ra and ensure her safety. * [[Buried Treasure]]: Gail is part of the Vault 79 heist team, acting as the crew's "muscle," and follows the Vault Dweller as a temporary companion for the majority of the heist. When disabling the security system, she will be forced to use a biometric scanner due to [[Johnny Weston]]'s hacking attempt failing, and the Vault Dweller must talk her through the scanning process. ===Other interactions=== After the Vault 79 heist is over, Gail and Ra-Ra will return to their room in the Crater Core. Gail can be spoken to, and replying positively to one of her dialogue options will result in a small gain in [[Wastelanders reputations|Raider reputation]]. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon =[[Minigun (Fallout 76)|Minigun]] |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|Gail always ready to shoot and smash!|sound=Gail 00583448_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Time to fight, human friends!
