It'd be a shame if you were to get injured before your next fight.|sound=Glenn 0042f4fd_1.ogg}} '''Glenn''', initially known as simply the '''arena guard''', is a member of [[Sargento|Sargento's]] [[Sargento's gang|gang]] at the [[Watoga Civic Center]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Glenn shares that he dislikes his name, but never had the heart to change it even though "everyone else around here changed theirs after civilization fell."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What's your name?"''
Glenn: ''"{{Tooltip|Glenn. I never liked it, but I never had the heart to change it even though everyone else around here changed theirs after civilization fell..|He didn't change his name, out of respect for his dead parents, but he's too tough to admit it. Still, this gets him thinking.}}"''
([[Glenn/Dialogue#144|Glenn's dialogue]]) After the war, as either a teenager or young adult, Glenn met Sargento in the [[Capital Wasteland]] while trying to rob his gang. This landed the two in a fist fight. Though Sargento won the fight, he was impressed with Glenn and offered him a job as a caravan guard.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How'd you get to be a guard here?"''
Glenn: ''"Funny story. I ran into Sargento and his gang out in the Capital Wasteland. I was just a scrappy kid at the time, and I stole cans of food from them. Got caught, and wound up in a fist-fight with the boss-man himself. I decked him hard with a sucker punch, but he laughed it off, and offered me a job as a caravan guard. When we settled here, I just kept at it. Only now, instead of keeping jerks away, I keep them in."''
([[Glenn/Dialogue#140|Glenn's dialogue]]) After the founding of the arena at the Civic Center, Glenn transitioned to being a guard there. He claims to not be very fond of family, and as such does not have a wife or children. He claims that his job is very boring, but also suggests there are some fights he rather enjoys. One fight in particular stands out to him; he claims a volunteer mounted a [[Yao guai (Fallout 76)|yao guai]], before severing its head with some barbed wire. He admits he is saddened by the fact that she has not returned to put on another spectacle.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What's the craziest thing you've seen in the Arena?"''
Glenn: ''"{{Tooltip|This whole thing's pretty new, so there's not much, but...|He's trying to think of something interesting to tell the player about.}} {{Tooltip|Oh! Oh! This one gal, a volunteer, not a slave mind you, she climbs up on the back of this huge Yao Guai and starts riding it around.|He suddenly remembers a good story to tell.}} It's thrashing around, trying to get at her, but she pulls out this length of rusty barbed wire and saws its damn head off. Then she tosses it into Sargento's lap and spits at his feet. The most badass thing I've ever seen. She left with her prize and never came back. Too bad."''
([[Glenn/Dialogue#132|Glenn's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[The Ol' Weston Shuffle]] }} ===Quests=== [[The Ol' Weston Shuffle]]: During this quest, Glenn is first known as the "arena guard." He will tell the player character to enter the arena when it is their turn. If, before the final round, [[Johnny Weston]] convinces [[Maximum Maddie]] to throw the match, he will ask the player character to distract the arena guard. During this conversation, one can learn about the guard, including his name and his past. Once his name is learned and the conversation is ended, his in-game name will change from "arena guard" to "Glenn." ==Inventory== {{Missing data|Inventory|FO76}} {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon =Random ranged weapon |otheritem =[[Stimpak (Fallout 76)|Stimpak]] x1 |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Glenn appears only {{In|FO76WL}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders raider characters]]

If you can't change with the times, then the rest of us will pick you off one by one. Or I guess in the case of the Christmas Flood, over a thousand at a time.|sound=Gnash 00599389_1.ogg}} '''Gnash''' is an independent raider found living in an outdoors shack in [[Charleston]] in [[Appalachia]], met {{in|FO76}}. ==Background== A textbook example of a psychopathic raider, Gnash originally came to Appalachia with [[Meg Groberg]]'s raiders, who settled down at the [[Crater]]. As a fan of pillaging and murder, he became disappointed with Meg's leadership and preference for garden variety robbery and extortion.Vault 76 dweller: "'' Can you tell me more about you? "''
Gnash: "''{{tooltip|I'm your worst nightmare. Hahaha... just kidding. Maybe. You can call me Gnash.|He's bored, not interested in talking to the player or about himself and ready to leave the conversation at any moment }} I came to Appalachia with those sorry excuses for Raiders who are holed up in Crater now. Their leader, Meg, couldn't even hack it as Cutthroat and had to start her own gang. They don't do nearly enough stealing and killing, if you ask me. "'' Her vision of the raiders was not at all what he wanted out of Appalachia, namely new loot and new victims to torture and murder for fun. Gnash: "''I heard that there was people coming back here in search of some treasure."'' {{tooltip|I'm not really interested in that sort of thing, but I couldn't pass up having some new victims! |Excitedly talking about the people being his victims like they're a brand new toy }} Where there's people, there's things to be stolen and lives to be ruined. "'' He left after deciding that the Crater raiders were merely [[Foundation]] settlers, except with studs and leather, setting out across the region to learn more about the original [[Raiders (Fallout 76)|raider gangs]] that formed in the region before the [[Scorched]] wiped most of them out. Gnash: "''I got tired of the Raiders acting like those Foundation babies but with studs and leather, and left to find out more about the gangs that were here. After I heard about what had happened here in Charleston, I knew I had to see all of the destruction myself. Plus I hear there's some sort of Responder training set up around here. I'd love to do my part and help keep them extinct. "'' While he appreciates the [[Blood Eagles]] for their affinity for violence and torture, he stays independent, especially since it means he doesn't have to share his drugs with anyone else. Vault 76 dweller: "''Have you heard of the Blood Eagles? They seem more your style. "''
Gnash: "''I like their appreciation for violence and the finer things in life, like torture… But for now I'm happy on my own. Less people to share my chems with that way. "'' In his travels, he managed to piece together the history of the raiders and developed a particular appreciation for the [[Cutthroats]]' brand of chaos and mayhem, particularly [[David Thorpe]]'s decision to destroy [[Charleston]] in the [[Christmas Flood]]. In fact, he is infatuated with the late Thorpe, jealous that [[Rose]] managed to snatch him up - although he has a disturbing appreciation for the atrocity perpetrated by David in her apparent memory. Vault 76 dweller: "''What was so great about the Cutthroats? "''
Gnash: "''The Cutthroats didn't let anyone walk over them and weren't afraid to use any means necessary to get what they wanted. {{tooltip|This destruction is from a MINI NUKE David used against the Responders when they took his girlfriend... honestly I don't know what he saw in her... |Trails off in jealousy at the end. }} I wish I could've heard the Responders crying and screaming while they all drowned like the helpless rats they were. "'' The destroyed Charleston attracted him so much that he erected a small camp in what was once downtown, settling down to revel in the death and destruction around him. He wishes he could have joined the original Cutthroats,Vault 76 dweller: "''What are you doing in Charleston? "''
Gnash: "''Thought I'd stop by, witness the death and destruction of Charleston and the Responders. Thanks to David Thorpe and the Cutthroats, the greatest gang to ever exist, we have this waterfront destination right here in Appalachia! Too bad they all got killed by the Scorched though, I would've loved to join them. "'' and continues their attempt to eradicate the [[Responders]] by keeping tabs on the nearby [[Fire Breathers]]' training course, keen to kill anyone who tries to complete it. He hates the Responders with a passion, Vault 76 dweller: "''The Responders got what was coming to them. "''
Gnash: "''Ha ha! Hell yeah, they did! They never should have underestimated David and the Cutthroats. Just sad I wasn't here to witness it, or to get me a few Responder heads myself. "'' considering them to be weak and worthy of contempt for trying to help people in a world that, as far as Gnash is concerned, is now predicated on violence. To Gnash, the strongest should survive and the weaklings will perish, killed by Gnash and his ilk. Vault 76 dweller: "''Why don't you like the Responders? All they wanted to do was help people. "''
Gnash: "''The only thing good about them was they gave supplies to weaklings and made it easier for raiders to steal. {{tooltip|Society is gone. If you can't change with the times, then the rest of us will pick you off one by one. |Emphasis on gone }} Or I guess in the case of the Christmas Flood, over a thousand at a time. "'' Gnash doesn't have need for anything beyond mayhem, drugs and alcohol. If visitors do not have these ready, Gnash would rather be left alone.Gnash: "''I don't know you, You ain't my friend. I only need three things in this world: chaos, chems, and a cold beer. If you're not putting up any, then you can move along. "'' He is open to flirtation and casual sex with particularly attractive people, to the point of sharing his drug stash. Vault 76 dweller: "''[Charisma 8+] You know, I have a thing for bad boys. "''
Gnash: "''{{tooltip|I'm not your typical bad boy…|Considering how they want to respond to the player flirting }}"''
If Charisma <8: "''{{tooltip|...and sorry, you're not my type. You could probably use this... and maybe a cold shower.|Scoff, disgusted }}"''
If Charisma >8: "''{{tooltip|...but we do have that in common. Maybe I'll take you on a raid with me sometime and we can celebrate after.|Flirty, suggestive }} {{tooltip|Do some chems... bathe in the blood of our enemies... here's a taste, for now. |}}"'' He'll even take pity on wannabe raiders and share his stash with them too, as long as they aren't serious about trying to rob him of caps. Vault 76 dweller: "''[Strength 8+] Give me all your caps! "''
Gnash: "''{{tooltip|I like your style! I think all those Buffouts might be going to your head though, try this.|Laughing, not at all threatened }} {{tooltip|And just so you know... if you ever try to take my caps by force, you and my blade will be getting real well-acquainted. |Gets dark and threatening }}"'' ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |ghost =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved = |other = See below. }} ===Other interactions=== * The player can threaten him for caps using a Strength 8+ check. Gnash reacts positively to the threat, assuming the Vault Dweller must be on Buffout and gives them an Addictol, but threatens the Vault Dweller that if they really do touch his caps, they will meet his knife (which is an idle threat, as he cannot be hurt). * The player can say they have a thing for bad boys with a Charisma 8+ check, regardless of the Vault Dweller's gender. Gnash says the Vault Dweller is not their type, but posits taking them on a raid and celebrating after, then gives them a Psycho. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Road leathers (Fallout 76)|Road leathers]]
[[Raider waster outfit|Raider waster eyepiece]] |weapon =Random ranged weapon and frag grenades |otheritem =Random amounts of pre-War money and stimpaks |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Gnash appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]'', introduced in the ''[[Wastelanders]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. ==Gallery== FO76WL Gnash.png|Gnash's living space ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox raiders FO76}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders raider characters]] [[Category:Crater Raiders characters]] [[Category:Charleston characters]] [[ru:Грызло]]

I'm surprised he'd come to save me. That's... great! What's the plan?|sound=Hal Gleeson 0042f4bb_1.ogg}} '''Hal Gleeson''' is a [[Slavery|slave]] at the [[Watoga Civic Center]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Hal has been good friends with [[Johnny Weston]] before the [[Great War]]. They did jobs together and were partners, so much so that Johnny considered Hal the only real friendship and "only real thing in general" he ever had.[[The Core terminal entries]] Hal and Johnny went their own ways when Johnny joined [[Meg Groberg]]'s [[Crater Raiders|crew]]; Hal thought him and Johnny would be better off on their own, but Johnny decided to stay with Meg. Hal did not approve of Johnny's relationship with Meg, and Johnny posits Hal may have been jealous. On their last job, Hal ripped Johnny off and took more than his fair share of the cut then lied about it. By the time Johnny found out, Hal had already left under the guise of not wanting to settle down at [[the Crater]]. He became a slave by [[Sargento]]'s [[Sargento's gang|gang]]. He refused to just give up, however, and began working on his escape. For weeks, he quietly dug out the wall behind the bookshelf with a rusty spoon. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion =yes |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[The Ol' Weston Shuffle]] }} ===Quests=== [[The Ol' Weston Shuffle]]: The main objective of the quest is to free Hal from slavery, as instructed by [[Johnny Weston]]. However, after Hal is freed, Johnny reveals that the true motive for freeing Hal was so that Johnny could personally kill him, and Hal dies at the end of the quest for having previously betrayed Johnny. Johnny then feels incredibly remorseful after, feeling he can never forgive himself for succumbing to revenge. ==Notes== If the player fails during the arena match, after a gun fight with various gang members, Johnny will be found waiting outside Hal's room. Johnny will enter Hal's room, surprising him, but Johnny will kill Hal before he even has the chance to leave his room. Sargento will also never be met. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = [[Harness (Fallout 76)|Harness]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Hal Gleeson appears only {{In|FO76WL}}. ==Behind the scenes== Hal's method of using an object to dig a hole and cover it up with an object to prevent suspicion is similar to the plot of the film ''The Shawshank Redemption''. ==Gallery== FO76WL The Ol' Weston Shuffle confronting Hal.png|Hal about to be killed by Johnny ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox companions FO76}} {{Navbox raiders FO76}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders raider characters]] [[Category:Crater Raiders characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 slave characters]] [[ru:Хэл Глисон]]

'''Hijack''' is a [[Crater Raiders|Crater Raider]] seeking to become one of [[Meg Groberg]]'s top men.

==Background==
Before the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] are about to burrow into [[Vault 79]], Hijack kidnaps [[Penelope Hornwright]] and holds her for ransom in the Cave section of [[Hornwright Industrial headquarters]]. Furthermore, he and his gang use furniture to damage [[The Motherlode (robot)|the Motherlode]]'s intelligence module. The residents must deal with him to secure Penelope Hornwright's safety or else be unable to breach Vault 79.

===Quests===
* [[Division of Wealth]]: During the quest, Hijack will confront the player character with having kidnapped [[Penelope Hornwright]]. The player character has several options in dealing with him, including intimidating him, negotiating and promising a cut of [[gold bullion]], or killing him and his gang of raiders.
** A [[Charisma (Fallout 76)|Charisma]] of at least 8 is needed to start a peaceful negotiation and a further [[Intelligence (Fallout 76)|Intelligence]] of 8 to "promise" him and his gang a cut of the gold (upholding this is optional).
**A [[Strength (Fallout 76)|Strength]] of 8 to intimidate him and his gang into leaving.
**An [[Endurance (Fallout 76)|Endurance]] of 8 will frighten him and his gang into leaving.
** Simply attacking him and his gang.

([[Johnny Weston/Dialogue|Johnny Weston's dialogue]]) However, his career was ultimately a failure, describing himself as a "bum" living on the streets of New York City when the bombs dropped in [[Timeline#2077|2077]]. It is uncertain how much of his background is truth and how much is fabrication,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Where are you from originally?"''
Johnny Weston: ''"{{Tooltip|I don't like talking about it, but I know you'll keep it secret. My dad was military. I saw army bases all over the country as a kid. When the bombs dropped, I was a bum. ([[Johnny Weston/Dialogue|Johnny Weston's dialogue]])Johnny Weston: ''"I don't really talk about it. I'm from all over. I used to see a lot of military bases as a kid, until I struck out on my own. When the bombs dropped, I was living in New York. Or maybe, Boston. Or coulda been Detroit, or LA. Maybe even England. Sorry you don't get to know. No one does. I've got my reasons for keeping it that way, and I'm safer for it."''
([[Johnny Weston/Dialogue|Johnny Weston's dialogue]]) though his claim of breaking into the [[Federal Reserve Bank of New York]] seems plausible, as his biometrics exist in surviving government database backups, tied to a felony conviction — which he claims to have suffered only because his crew bailed on him.Johnny Weston: ''"Funny thing. [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I thought there wasn't a system you couldn't beat?"''
Johnny Weston: ''"{{Tooltip|Hey, that was the only one. I was young and stupid back then, and only got caught because my crew bailed on me.|Defensive.}} I've learned a lot since then. I'll get this one."''
([[Johnny Weston/Dialogue|Johnny Weston's dialogue]]) During his time as a freelance raider, he was close friends with [[Hal Gleeson]] both before and after the War. They did jobs together and Hal turned out to be the most solid partner Johnny had. Working together transformed into a lasting relationship and mutual feelings.[[The Core terminal entries#Hal (deceased)|The Core terminal entries; terminal, Hal (deceased)]] Eventually, Johnny became involved with [[Meg Groberg]]'s raiders, infiltrating the gang and blending in. When Meg finally realized what he did, rather than stringing him up she invited him for drinks, and eventually the two shacked up. Johnny's relationship with Hal deteriorated over Meg, as Hal seemed jealous. When Meg's group finally returned to [[Appalachia]] and settled at [[the Crater]], Johnny joined them.Johnny Weston: ''"The story goes that I infiltrated the gang simply by acting the part. For weeks, everyone just assumed I belonged. But there's more to it. When Meg found out, she wasn't even mad. We had drinks, then shacked up. I trust you enough to say that Meg and I have a physical relationship. Beyond that, it just so happens my skill set benefits her whole operation. Now I stick around with her crew and everyone profits. I followed her around until we settled here. You know the whole business with Hal and all that. He never approved of my arrangement with Meg. I think it got him jealous."''
([[Johnny Weston/Dialogue|Johnny Weston's dialogue]]) His unique skill set benefited the raiders handsomely, as Johnny is an expert at infiltration and confidence games, giving raiders a lot of soft power. The arrangement is a mutually beneficial exchange, rather than any sort of formal subordination.Johnny Weston: ''"{{tooltip|So here's what's what. I used to run jobs with my partner Hal. Hal's a dear old friend. Known him since before the war.|Looking back with fondness.}} Hal and I went our separate ways when I joined up with Meg's crew. Now he's being held as a slave by a group of unsavory hooligans out by Watoga, and being forced to do... who knows what. I've got a plan to free him."''
([[Johnny Weston/Dialogue|Johnny Weston's dialogue]]) Settling at the Crater came at a cost, as Hal refused to put down roots and separated from Johnny, going his own way. Johnny realized too late that Hal didn't just leave him: He betrayed him, taking a far greater cut of their last job together than he said, taking it with him and disappeared into the wastelands. Weston hated the fact that his best friend betrayed him like that, and vowed vengeance - no matter how much pain it would cause him.Johnny Weston: ''"Hal ripped me off. On our last job, he took way more than his fair share of the cut, then lied about it. By the time I found out, he had decided to part ways under the guise of not wanting to settle down at the Crater. {{Tooltip|I needed to send a message that no one pulls a fast one on Gentleman Johnny Weston, not even my best friend, Hal.|Deadly serious.}}"''
([[Johnny Weston/Dialogue|Johnny Weston's dialogue]]) He got his chance when he was scoping out the [[Watoga Civic Center]] and the raiders occupying it for Meg. While the raiders were rejected out of hand as candidates for the Crater crew, as Meg abhors slavery, Weston spotted Hal tending to the spectators in the luxury boxes. Spotting his opportunity, he began to plan how to get inside to free Hal,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Watoga's pretty big. Where do we find Hal?"''
Johnny Weston: ''"{{Tooltip|These guys run a deadly arena competition out of the old civic center.|"These GUYS," not "THESE guys"}} Meg asked me to scope it out and find out what their deal was. See if maybe we could get them to join us. It was clear these weren't the type of people we wanted in our crew. Slavery's a big no-no with Meg, and these folks are all about it. But, while I was betting on one of the matches, I spotted Hal waiting on people hand and foot in one of the arena's luxury boxes."''
([[Johnny Weston/Dialogue|Johnny Weston's dialogue]]) so that he can kill Gleeson for betraying him. Johnny rationalizes it as a small mercy that would ultimately save Hal from a fate worse than death, namely, a lifetime of [[slavery]],Johnny Weston: ''"In this business, you gotta be cold. Look at it this way: All at once, I got my revenge and saved him from a lifetime of servitude. Think of it as a small mercy."''
([[Johnny Weston/Dialogue|Johnny Weston's dialogue]]) and prefers to bury his feelings for him, as killing Hal will evidently be the most difficult act in Johnny's life thus far. Until that happens, he operates out of his quarters in [[the Core]], standing out from the other raiders thanks to his spotless black suit. Given that keeping them clean is extremely difficult, it's a feat that he manages it.Johnny Weston: ''"{{Tooltip|Damn it! Do you know how hard it is to find clean suits out there!|Hit in combat.}}"''
([[Johnny Weston/Dialogue|Johnny Weston's dialogue]]) When not in the field, he passes time by playing cards with other raiders and is no stranger to cheating at them. [[Bless y'all's hearts]] Once knowledge of [[Vault 79]] reaches Meg, he begins to prepare for the raid, in case there are any survivors in the Vault who might need to be manipulated, twisted, cajoled, or otherwise convinced to give the raiders what they want.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"No offense, but I don't know why we need you for the job."''

([[Meg Groberg/Dialogue|Meg Groberg's dialogue]]) {{Small|'''Note''': Spoken if Johnny was killed by the player and Meg was lied to that it was a heroic sacrifice.}} ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |essential until =[[Buried Treasure]] begins |temp companion =Yes |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[The Ol' Weston Shuffle]] * [[Buried Treasure]] * [[Secrets Revealed]] }} ===Quests=== * [[The Ol' Weston Shuffle]]: The [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] of [[Vault 76]] must convince Johnny to join the heist on [[Vault 79]]. Although he is already on board, Johnny wants something in exchange. He asks the Vault Dweller to pose as a slave so that they can infiltrate [[Sargento]]'s gang at the [[Watoga Civic Center]] and free Hal Gleeson from slavery. To do this, Johnny invents the character of "Reginald P. Humphries," an [[United Kingdom|English]] man who became stuck in [[Washington, D.C.]] when the airplanes stopped running. After the Vault Dweller fights through their matches (or simply kills all of Sargento's gang) and breaks Hal Gleeson out of captivity, Johnny meets with the two of them. Although Hal was once Johnny's best friend, it is revealed that the true purpose of this mission was so that Johnny could kill Hal and tie up loose ends from when Hal attempted to betray him. Johnny believes that his relationship with Meg caused Hal to become jealous of him. However, Johnny later comes to regret killing Hal, remarking that he loved Hal like a brother.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You're really going to do me in like you did Hal? How's that going for you?"''
Johnny Weston: ''"{{Tooltip|Damn it... That was the hardest thing I've ever had to do. Hal was my partner. My best friend. I loved him like... like a brother.|This cuts him deep. I might even miss you less, since you went and mentioned Hal.|Getting upset with the player for bringing up a painful memory.}}"''
([[Johnny Weston/Dialogue|Johnny Weston's dialogue]]) * [[Buried Treasure]]: Johnny is part of the Vault 79 heist team, and is tasked with disabling the security system. However, he accidentally triggers a sensor which detects him as an ex-convict, leading him to pause and ask the Vault Dweller for advice. If he is lied to and encouraged to proceed, he will be killed by [[Automated turret (Fallout 76)|laser turrets]]. If he is told to stop, he will survive, and will accompany as a temporary companion for the rest of the quest. Either way, he is unable to accomplish his task and an alternate plan must be used. * [[Secrets Revealed]]: If Johnny survives Buried Treasure, he will continue following the player character as a temporary companion. ** After dealing with the Vault reactor and collecting the [[gold bullion]], Johnny will attempt to betray the Vault Dweller, and must then be killed or convinced to stand down with Charisma 4+, then a Charisma 8+ check or by bringing up his previous betrayal of Hal. ** After bringing up his betray against Hal, and asking him if he regrets it, A further Charisma 12+ check can be used to encourage him to give some of his cut of the gold (50 bullion) to the Vault Dweller as an apology for the attempted betrayal when the raid is completed. ** At the end of the quest, after making the final choice of how to split the gold, Johnny can be talked to in the gold operations center. If the deal with Meg was respected, he will be thankful and friendly. '''Kogan''' is the leader of the [[Crater Raiders]] outpost at the [[Crater watchstation]] in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
Kogan is in charge of the raiders at the Crater watchstation and can be found inside of its worksite. He is a typical "tough guy," and does not appreciate anyone talking back to or questioning him. He is especially dismissive of [[Vault 76]] [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|vault dwellers]], and will express surprise that [[Meg Groberg|Meg]] is even working with "chumps" like [[vault]] dwellers.

[[Meg Groberg]]: ''"Least when it comes to dyin'. Lou's got a knack for cheatin' death. He was up in Pittsburgh, 70 years old, when shit went down. They say a real honest-to-goodness A-bomb fell straight in his living room. Thing didn't go off. A dud."''
([[Meg Groberg/Dialogue#14|Meg Groberg's dialogue]]) is a member of [[the Crater]] [[Crater Raiders|Raiders]] hiding out in [[Carleton Mine]]. ==Background== Lou was born around 2007. Before the [[Great War]], Lou was an engineer who lived in [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|Pittsburgh]]. He was 70 years old when the bombs dropped, making him nearly 100 years old in present time. Rumors around [[the Crater]] say that an atomic bomb fell straight into his living room, but it was a dud and failed to go off. This was the origin of his nickname "Lucky Lou," a reference to his ability to turn a curse into a blessing, and he went on to defy death in at least a dozen more incidents. As the [[radiation]] poured into Pittsburgh, Lou became a [[ghoul]], something that has haunted him ever since. After Lou joined up with the raiders, he became respected by people like [[Meg Groberg]], [[Caleb Fisher]] and [[Weasel]], even if some of his friends were disgusted by his appearance.[[Caleb Fisher]]: ''"He's always a little surly. It's possible it's on account of his condition. But, he's had years to adjust. Sure, some of the others don't like the way he looks, but they still respect him. I say, I don't know a soul who wouldn't take a bullet for Lou. Not that he needs it. Every curse somehow turns into a blessing for him. However, because of his condition, Lou is frightened that he will eventually go feral. In fact, if I were still a religious man, I would say God watches over him and has special plans for Lou here on this Earth. Lou's one of the luckiest men alive. He's over ninety-five years old and still fit as a fiddle, sharp as a tack. I've witnessed over a dozen times where something should have rightly killed any normal man, but not Lou."''
([[Caleb Fisher/Dialogue#236|Caleb Fisher's dialogue]]) Lou was one of the few people to play with [[Ra-Ra]] when no one else would and she views him as a friend. He lived in a small room resembling a bunker in the underground area of the [[the Core|Crater Core]]. Although many of the Crater raiders would take a bullet for Lou, his worries of turning feral spiraled him into deep depression. These feelings were planted and amplified by [[Lev]], who despised ghouls and wanted Lou in particular out of the way to sabotage the raiders' heist plans.[[Lou's log: Engine room]][[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"It's bad enough he wants to die without you trying to kill him."''
[[Lev]]: ''"Who do you think put idea of going feral into Lou's head? Much easier to get away with it if he kills himself."''
([[Lev/Dialogue#63|Lev's dialogue]]) Not wanting to take any chances, Lou would rather take his own life over possibly going feral and attacking his friends. He left behind a [[Lou's goodbye note|goodbye note]] entrusting his belongings to Fisher, showing the depths of their friendship, and went to hole up in [[Carleton Mine]] in order to find a decent way to kill himself. Unable to simply "pull the trigger," Lou constructed a number of death traps that would result in his demise, including a machine-powered shotgun blast,[[Lou's log: New plan]] several [[Automated turret (Fallout 76)|automated turrets]] scavenged from the [[Fort Atlas|ATLAS Observatory]],[[Carleton Mine terminal entries#Turrets|Carleton Mine terminal entries; Lou's engineering notes, Turrets]] and even a makeshift building that would collapse in on itself.[[Lou's log: Chamber]] However, none of these contraptions worked despite multiple trials, living up to Lou's status as someone who would always cheat death. Left with few options, Lou decided to take the last resort of simply detonating explosives. If the collapse of the mine would not kill him, then at least he would be trapped inside and unable to hurt anybody.[[Lou's log: Cave-in]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion =yes |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Cheating Death]] * [[From Russia With Lev]] * [[Buried Treasure]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Cheating Death]]: As a demolitions expert, Lou is needed for the [[Vault 79]] heist. However, he is missing from the Crater, and his location - Carleton Mine - must first be discovered, then he must be tracked down in the mine and convinced to join the crew. Lou agrees to join on the condition that the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] helps him commit suicide after the heist. * [[From Russia With Lev]]: Lou was attacked by Lev's gang in the cavern entrance of Vault 79 and left to be killed by a [[Yao guai (Fallout 76)|yao guai]]; he must be rescued, and then his [[Lou's remote detonator|remote detonator]] for the explosives on the Vault door must be recovered from Lev. * [[Buried Treasure]]: Lou triggers the explosives to bring down the Vault door and enable the start of the heist, then stays outside with [[Meg Groberg]], ostensibly to ensure the stability of the area. ===Other interactions=== * If Lou is spoken to in the [[Crater Core]], he will mention that he is trying to offload his explosives and offer a random grenade or mine. * After completing [[Secrets Revealed]], Lou can be spoken to about his previous deal with the Vault Dweller, where he will voice his hesitation to go through with suicide. All options in the conversation will eventually lead him to conclude that he is determined to go on living, and the player character will gain a small amount of [[Wastelanders reputations|raider reputation]]. Afterwards, he will continue occasionally offering random explosives. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Gray knit cap (Fallout 76)|Gray knit cap]]

([[Caleb Fisher/Dialogue#93|Caleb Fisher's dialogue]]) ==Background== Meg's mother died by suicide in the aftermath of the [[Great War]] which gave her the determination to keep surviving in a depressing world.Meg Groberg: ''"I knew a lot of people chose to end it all after the war. My own mother was in that boat. World's a depressing place now, but we gotta survive."''
([[Meg Groberg/Dialogue|Meg Groberg's dialogue]]) Meg was never a proud American, feeling the country was not worth fighting for, and she was happy when the establishment was destroyed by the War.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"The Overseer has a plan to restablish currency. I'm doing it for America."''
Meg Groberg: ''"Hah! That's a good one! The America I knew was never worth fighting for, if you ask me. I'm glad the establishment got all blown to hell."''
([[Meg Groberg/Dialogue#309|Meg Groberg's dialogue]]) At some point before the [[Scorched Plague]] entered the [[Savage Divide]], Meg became concerned about the chaos surrounding contact with the other raider gangs being lost; she wondered what happened to [[Margie McClintock]] and feared the Diehards would be next. She sent a message to [[Vincent Fried]], asking him if he wished to leave Appalachia with her group. Meg's group then splintered off from the Diehards and left Appalachia entirely with several other Diehards. During this time, they ventured from Appalachia to [[the Commonwealth]] to [[Washington D.C.]], raiding and gathering new members along the way.Meg Groberg: ''"{{tooltip|We've traveled the Wasteland from the Commonwealth to DC. We take... whatever we want. And we want that vault. Who's going to stop us? You?"|Said in a sinister voice.}}''
([[Meg Groberg/Dialogue|Meg Groberg's dialogue]]) Meg met [[Johnny Weston]], a man who had infiltrated her gang by blending in with the other raiders. When Meg found out that he had simply slipped into the gang, she reacted positively and the two shared drinks. They eventually "shacked up," and continue a physical relationship with each other.[[Johnny Weston]]: ''"The story goes that I infiltrated the gang simply by acting the part. For weeks, everyone just assumed I belonged. But there's more to it. When Meg found out, she wasn't even mad. We had drinks, then shacked up. I trust you enough to say that Meg and I have a physical relationship. Beyond that, it just so happens my skill set benefits her whole operation. Now I stick around with her crew and everyone profits. I followed her around until we settled here. You know the whole business with Hal and all that. He never approved of my arrangement with Meg. I think it got him jealous."''
([[Johnny Weston/Dialogue|Johnny Weston's dialogue]]) In 2103, Meg returned to Appalachia with her raider group, having grown exponentially in the previous years, to take ownership of the crashed ''Valiant-1'' space station, dubbing it [[the Crater]].[[Fallout 76 loading screens#Location|Fallout 76 Wastelanders loading screens]]: ''"When the Diehards Raider gang returned to Appalachia, they settled in the area of the crashed space station and named their new home the Crater."''[[Raider punk]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Crater expelled this Raider scumbag for hurting other Diehards. That's not how we do things. Apparently they took up residence at this place.|The speaker is a Raider so they have venom for this person}}"''
([[Raider punk/Dialogue#500|Raider punk's dialogue]]) It was also upon learning of the residents of [[Vault 76]] having been colonizing the region in the past year that Meg decided it was time to let the Vault Dwellers know that Appalachia belonged to the Raiders and they were taking it back. After the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] returns to Appalachia by way of the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force]], Meg assigns [[Burke (Steel Dawn)|Burke]], [[Pierce (Steel Dawn)|Pierce]], and [[Sheena]] to fight and/or sabotage the returning Brotherhood as part of the [[War Party]]. As Meg and the other raiders have previous experience dealing with the Brotherhood before they left Appalachia, she believes that they are dangerous, and the only interaction she desires to have with them is putting bullets in them.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Any thoughts on the Brotherhood of Steel?"''
Meg Groberg: ''"Thoughts? What I got for them are bullets. Luckily I got some folks who are real passionate about taking those bucketheads down. You wanna know more, you talk to Pierce over in the War Room. It's behind Ae-Ri's shop. Just don't get in the way. You'll regret it."''
([[Meg Groberg/Dialogue#12|Meg Groberg's dialogue]]) ==Personality== [[File:FO76WL Meg.png|thumb|200px|Meg leading the Crater Raiders]] {{Quotation|Meg leads the Raiders at Crater with a cool head and pragmatic nature, but she won't hesitate to employ violence if she or her people are threatened.|[[Fallout 76 loading screens|''Fallout 76'' loading screen]]}} Meg views the raider lifestyle as necessary in order to get by in their world, feeling it justifies a lot of their actions and that they are still on the "right" path.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You really think you guys are on the "right path"?"''
Meg Groberg: ''"You're damn right I do. This ain't the world it used to be, Seven-Six. Things change, people change. Adapt or die, ya dig?"''
([[Meg Groberg/Dialogue#202|Meg Groberg's dialogue]]) While she was a member of the Diehards, Meg believed that Margie McClintock's ideal of the pacifist raider life was unrealistic and often disobeyed the Diehards' standing order to not fire unless fired upon.[[Concerns with Margie]] Even though [[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]] and Meg have a mutual dislike for each other with Meg calling Rose a bitch, Rose supports Meg's raider lifestyle, asking, "You don't think Meg and her crew are alive today because they were fair, do ya? You gotta live a little! Be daring! Screw someone over and never look back!" Despite this, she is shown to be merciful at times, such as sparing [[Barb (Wastelanders)|Barb]]'s life if she is revealed as the mole. Meg is shown to have a non-confrontational side as she chooses not to directly confront Barb, instead dropping hints so Barb can correct her course, showing that Meg still retains faith in others. A similar instance occurs when Meg hears Foundation are considering breaking into the vault. Meg gives a veiled threat to the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]], warning, "All I'm sayin' is, be a real shame if someone I know were thinkin' the grass was greener over there. They might want to think a little harder." As a leader, she hates discrimination and sees value in diversity. She values people like the super mutant [[Gail]] and the ghoul [[Lucky Lou]], the former for her strength and devotion for protecting [[Ra-Ra]], and the latter for his skills in explosives. She once said, "Recruitment is better. Kill only for food and supplies." [[Gnash]] claims Meg tried to be part of the brutal [[Cutthroats]] but did not prove herself to them, resulting in her starting her own gang. Another instance of Meg's empathy is upon finding out Ra-Ra stole her snack cakes, Meg took pity and allowed her to eat the rest. Meg's leadership is controversial and viewed as poor among some Raiders for various reasons, particularly to [[Lev]], [[Surge]], [[Caleb Fisher]] and [[Hal Gleeson]]; a common complaint is that they feel Meg does not go far enough as a Raider. For example, Lev viewed her as weak, mentioning she would never strike Foundation. Johnny's terminal claims Meg was planning "a lot" of raids on them, although it is not clarified if these plans were delayed or dropped. Lev's opinion of Meg resulted in the formation of [[Lev's crew]]. Hal left Meg because he felt he and Johnny would be better off on their own. While Rose views Meg as a step above Margie, Rose does not think Meg holds a candle compared to [[David Thorpe]]. Meg highly values her connections to the loyal members of her group; she can be quite trusting and unaware of the dangers of certain people which is shown to have consequences. For example, Ra-Ra played outside Crater with only Gail to watch over her, which nearly killed Ra-Ra due to the lack of better supervision. Meg likes Barb, despite that Barb is a mole cooperating with Lev. Meg is unaware of Lev's plotting and his attempt at killing Lou. During the vault raid, Meg's trust of Johnny results in her bringing him along for the raid; Johnny attempts to secretly murder the Vault Dweller when Meg is not present. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =Yes |ghost =Yes |ghoul =yes |quests started =* [[Cheating Death]] * [[Fun and Games]] * [[From Russia With Lev]] * [[Buried Treasure]] |quests involved =* [[Strange Bedfellows]] * [[Overseer, Overseen]] * [[Siding with Crater]] * [[Secrets Revealed]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Strange Bedfellows]]: Meg is first encountered after being summoned by [[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]] to the Top of the World to meet with the Vault Dwellers. The invitation was per the request of the [[Vault 76 overseer]], so that her group could be given the vaccine to the [[Scorched Plague]]. Meg is hesitant to accept due to her distrust of the vault dwellers. If she is unable to be swayed with Charisma or Intelligence 12+, she offers a compromise: help her lieutenant [[Aldridge]] with an attack on the Scorched near the [[Philippi Battlefield Cemetery]] and she will consider having her raiders inoculated, while also granting the vault dwellers access to the Crater, [[Crater watchstation]], and [[Ohio River Adventures]], rendering her Raiders no longer hostile to the vault dwellers. When the vault dwellers return with the news that Aldridge and his team were wiped out by the Scorched, Meg finally agrees to have her raiders inoculated. Upon returning with the vaccine, she is initially puzzled to find it comes as a new flavor of [[Nuka-Cola (Fallout 76)|Nuka-Cola]], but nonetheless accepts it and expresses gratitude to the vault dwellers. * [[Overseer, Overseen]]: Meg must be spoken to in order to enlist the raiders' help for breaking into [[Vault 79]]. * [[Cheating Death]]: A demolitions expert is needed to break into Vault 79. Meg asks the vault dwellers to find and recruit [[Lucky Lou]], who has gone missing. * [[Fun and Games]]: Meg asks the vault dwellers to recruit [[Gail]] and [[Ra-Ra]] for the raid on Vault 79 as she needs some muscle and someone small who can sneak around locked doors via the ventilation ducts. * [[The Ol' Weston Shuffle]]: Meg asks the vault dwellers to recruit Johnny Weston for the raid on Vault 79 to help deal with the security defenses. * [[Siding with Crater]]: Meg must be spoken to by the vault dwellers to confirm that they have cast their lot with the raiders for the raid on Vault 79 and not the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]]. * [[From Russia With Lev]]: Meg asks the vault dwellers to check on Lou outside Vault 79. After hearing about his attempted murder by [[Lev]], she asks the vault dwellers to root out Lev's mole in the Crater, then find and kill Lev and his gang. She can also be informed about Lev's benefactor [[Rocco]] (whether he was spared and convince to flee Appalachia or killed) as well as the identity of the mole, [[Barb (Wastelanders)|Barb]], for minor raider [[Wastelanders reputations|reputation]] gains. * [[Buried Treasure]]: Meg and the heist team are gathered outside Vault 79 for the raid. She and Lou stay outside, citing the need to guard the flank and ensure no betrayals are attempted, but she asks the vault dwellers to ensure that Johnny pulls his weight to be deserving of the large cut of the loot that he demands. * [[Secrets Revealed]]: Meg shows up in the Gold Operations Center near the end of the quest to ensure the vault dwellers follow through with their deal after siding with the Raiders to break into the Vault. Depending whether the gold bullion was distributed as agreed, or the deal was broken in whatever form, she will respond varyingly. ===Effects of player's actions=== * Meg can be chosen over Paige and his Settlers for a raid on Vault 79 after telling her the vault is where the United States' gold bullion reserves were stored and could make the Raiders rich beyond their dreams. * While distributing the gold, if the player selects "It's best we give some to [[Foundation]]. AC will hold 250 bars for them. You'll get the rest." then the game will act as if this is a final choice and there will be no option to back out of this. Meg enters an uproar, saying "screw you" and claims the Vault Dweller broke their deal, even though the wording could be seen as a suggestion. Meg then says the Raiders will have to steal that gold back in the future, and tells the Vault Dweller to think about that. Meg says she should be pissed enough to shoot the Vault Dweller dead, but mentions the Vault Dweller did good things for Ra-Ra and Lou earlier, but says she has a spike outside the Crater Core with the Vault Dweller's name on it in case they ever betray her again. * After the vault raid, if the gold bullion was not distributed according to plan, speaking to Meg will lead her to mention that she had to convince her faction not to start hostilities with the vault dwellers, and although their position in the Crater has fallen somewhat, she would rather have people of their skills on her side rather than as enemies. Choosing a further dialogue option to tell her that Foundation is weak will result in a minor raider reputation gain. ** Whether or not the Vault Dweller betrays Meg plays minor importance during [[Property Rights]]. If she was betrayed, Pierce will not accept the Vault Dweller's status as a raider to be a viable option. * If Johnny is killed, Meg is very upset by his death, mentioning she will need time to process it. The Vault Dweller may choose to expose Johnny's betrayal. If the betrayal is not exposed, Meg will think Johnny died a hero, but if Johnny is exposed post-mortem, then Meg will wonder how sincere Johnny was and if he was just using her and the Raiders all along. She also may have two reactions to Johnny's betrayal, either victim blaming the Vault Dweller for killing him, or by saying the Vault Dweller did what they had to do, although it is unclear what determines this reaction. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Stalker outfit]] |weapon =[[Combat rifle (Fallout 76)|Combat rifle]] |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|Bullshit. Shit...|sound=Meg Groberg 00586b08_1.ogg}} ==Appearances== Meg Groberg appears {{In|FO76}}. She was introduced as a full character in the ''[[Wastelanders]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. Before the update, she was only heard in the [[Concerns with Margie]] holotape, which has a different voice actress ([[Dawnn Lewis]]). The holotape can still be found and her lines were not re-dubbed. She was also mentioned in a [[Sunnytop Ski Lanes terminal entries#Margie.3F|terminal entry]]. Her ''Wastelanders'' voice actor ([[Mara Junot]]) returned to make new comments for the ''[[Steel Dawn]]'' update. ==Behind the scenes== [[File:FO76WL Meg face.png|thumb|200px|Close-up of Meg Groberg]] * Meg has central heterochromia eyes with brown on the inside and blue on the outside. She also wears indigo eyeliner on her lower eyelids, and her hands are covered in grime. * Groberg is a surname from Israel. It is an extremely rare surname used by very few people, the most well known being former soldier {{w|Florent Groberg}} and a Mormon named {{w|John H. Groberg}}. * One of Meg's quotes is, "As my old man woulda said, I admire your chutzpah." Chutzpah means "audacity" in Hebrew. * Meg is voiced by [[Mara Junot]], who also voiced [[Elsie Taylor]] and [[Lacey Drummond]]. In localized versions of the game, her voice is dubbed by Chieko Miyazaki (Japanese) and Isabel Donate (Spanish). Meg's English and Japanese voice actresses share the same roles in ''Wastelanders'', but this is not the case for the Spanish dub. * Meg is the most profane character in all of ''Fallout 76'', with 36 shits, 26 damns, 12 asses, 5 fucks and 2 bitches. ==Gallery== FO76WL Meg trailer.png|Meg in a ''Wastelanders'' trailer FO76WL Meg cropped.jpeg|Meg in a ''Wastelanders'' trailer FO76WL Raider Meg Groberg.png|Meg Groberg in the Crater Core FO76WL Meeting Meg.png|Meeting Meg at the [[Top of the World]] during [[Strange Bedfellows]] FO76WL Raider heist.png|Meg with her crew during the [[Vault 79]] raid Meg_Groberg_quest_icon.png|Quest sprite Raiders WW.png|Meg with [[Johnny Weston]] and [[Lev]] in ''[[Fallout: Wasteland Warfare]]'' ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox original raiders FO76}} {{Navbox raiders FO76}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Fallout 76 mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders raider characters]] [[Category:Crater Raiders characters]] [[Category:Diehards]] [[es:Meg Groberg]] [[ru:Мег Гроберг]] [[zh:Meg Groberg]]

Am I the only one concerned about the smell?|sound=Mortimer 00592768_1.ogg}} '''Mortimer''' is a [[Mister Handy (Fallout 76)|Mister Handy]] associated with [[the Crater]] [[Crater Raiders|Raiders]]. After the conclusion of [[Secrets Revealed]], he appears as a [[gold bullion]] [[Fallout 76 vendors|vendor]] in [[The Core|the Crater Core]]. ==Background== Mortimer joins the Raiders in an effort to obtain gold from trading with both them and the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]]. He has great plans for the gold, from re-engineering a new body to force the robots at [[the Whitespring Resort]] to show him respect,Mortimer: "''Once I've enough gold to engineer a new body, those insolent robots at Whitespring will have to respect me.''"
([[Mortimer (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#47|Mortimer's dialogue]]) to giving himself a gold paint job,Mortimer: "''I wonder how much gold bullion it'll take to re-engineer my body. I think the color will quite suit me, don't you?''"
([[Mortimer (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#48|Mortimer's dialogue]]) to purchasing weapons modifications for himself,Mortimer: "''Perhaps [[Vault 79]] has some weapons modifications I could make use of.''"
([[Mortimer (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#49|Mortimer's dialogue]]) and even to use it to acquire a fourth arm.Mortimer: "''A fourth arm could really show a certain robot I know who's boss.''"
([[Mortimer (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#50|Mortimer's dialogue]]) Despite being willing to trade with the Raiders, Mortimer looks down on them.Mortimer: "''Ah, beautiful gold, what plans I have for you. Not that any undesirables around here would ever understand.''"
([[Mortimer (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#54|Mortimer's dialogue]]) He views the Crater Core as a "hole in the ground" unfit for "a Handy of my stature,"Mortimer: "''This hole in the ground is no proper living quarters for a Handy of my stature.''"
([[Mortimer (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#46|Mortimer's dialogue]]) and despises the interior decorating therein.Mortimer: "''The decor here is lacking to say the least. I mean, really, a dead animal? Am I the only one concerned about the smell?''"
([[Mortimer (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#53|Mortimer's dialogue]]) He also dislikes [[Ra-Ra]] for bothering him.Mortimer: "''Don't let that little girl near me. She keeps trying to make me play with her, and don't get me started on the fingerprints.''"
([[Mortimer (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#51|Mortimer's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares =[[Fallout 76 plans|Unique plans]] for [[gold bullion]] |caps = |currency =[[Legendary scrip]] {{icon|scrip|18px|link=[[Legendary scrip]]}} |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved = }} ===Effects of player's actions=== After the events of [[Secrets Revealed]], the last quest in the main ''Wastelanders'' questline, Mortimer will arrive at the Crater Core and become available as a merchant. He sells rare plans to the Vault Dwellers in exchange for [[gold bullion]], with plan rarity dependent on one's [[Wastelanders reputations|reputation]] with the Raiders. ==Inventory== For his inventory, see "Raiders" and "Both factions" sections [[Fallout_76_reputations#Raiders_2|here]]. ==Appearances== Mortimer appears {{In|FO76WL}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox vendors FO76}} {{Navbox raiders FO76}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders robots and computers]] [[Category:Wastelanders bullion merchants]] [[Category:Wastelanders raider characters]] [[Category:Mister Handy characters]] [[ru:Мортимер (Wastelanders)]]

{{Infobox incomplete|FO76WL}} {{Infobox character |games =FO76, FO76WL |image =FO76 Munch.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |affiliation =[[Crater Raiders]] |role = |location =[[The Crater]] |quests = |alignment = |level =66 |tag skills = |derived = |actor =[[Dave Fennoy]] |dialogue =[[Munch/Dialogue]] |edid =W05_Raider_Munch |formid ={{ID|003fbc04}} |refid ={{ID|0040b2ad}} }} {{Quotation|Scrappy, ain't ya? Didn't anyone ever tell you, "Respect your elders, or get a bullet in the brain"? Given all that, I'd say I got the right to call you whatever I want, kid. And seeing as how I'm in a good mood, I'll leave your skull intact. This "old man" survived the war, endured the aftermath, and is still standing. And I didn't need no cozy vault to do it.|sound=Munch 0055af7c_1.ogg}} '''Munch''' is a member of the [[Crater Raiders]] at [[the Crater]]. ==Background== [[File:FO76 081120 Yellow bungalow.png|thumb|left|200px|Munch's bungalow]] Munch lives in a yellow bungalow in the northern part of the Crater. He describes himself as the resident historian,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Who are you?"''
Munch: ''"The name is Munch. Most people would probably say I'm just a crotchety old man with a shotgun, heh. But if you ask me, I'm what you'd call the resident historian, story teller, guru type around here."''
([[Munch/Dialogue#236|Munch's dialogue]]) though he freely admits he bends the truth about history.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"So, you're lying to them?"''
Munch: ''"Pfft, semantics. That old world is long gone. There's just us to rebuild all this shit. Why waste time on tellin' 'em how things used to be? I intend to spice it up. Let these kids be amazed by possibility. Those are the minds I want rebuilding this world."''
([[Munch/Dialogue#228|Munch's dialogue]]) Some of his writings on topics, such as the [[The Great War (note)|Great War]], [[A Whale of a Tale|whales]] and the [[The Nova Orbital station|space station he resides in]], can be found in his tent. He claims aliens are real and are what brought down the space station in the first place, and are probably working to dominate the planet. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Wasteland trapper outfit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Munch appears only {{In|FO76WL}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox raiders FO76}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders raider characters]] [[Category:Crater Raiders characters]] [[ru:Манч]]

Grown-ups are so boring sometimes.|sound=Ra-Ra 0059f182_1.ogg}} '''Ra-Ra''' is a [[child]] living with the [[Crater Raiders]] in [[The Core|the Crater Core]]. ==Background== Ra-Ra was found by [[Gail]], who acts as a surrogate mother to her. Since then, they have protected and taken care of each other. She is the only child living in [[the Crater]] and is disappointed that she has no other children to play with. She also does not know her actual name, and claims to be an only child. Ra-Ra owns a stuffed rabbit toy called Bunnabun that she is very fond of. When encountered, she can be seen creating colorful [[Chalk (Fallout 76)|chalk]] drawings on the floor. Recently, Ra-Ra and Gail were playing "I Spy" by the [[Grafton Lake]]. Gail mentioned seeing something ugly, brown, and coming right at them. The animal took Bunnabun so Ra-Ra chased it into a pipe. She encountered robots and hid from them. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |ghost =yes |temp companion =yes |ghoul =yes |quests involved =*[[Fun and Games]] * [[Buried Treasure]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Fun and Games]]: Ra-Ra insists that the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] must help her find her toy, which was stolen by a [[Radrat (Fallout 76)|Radrat]], before she will return to the Crater. She will crawl through the vents of [[Grafton Steel Underground]], opening locked doors and occasionally throwing [[Pulse grenade (Fallout 76)|pulse grenades]] to the Dwellers to help them fight the robots in the Underground. * [[Buried Treasure]]: Ra-Ra joins the raid on [[Vault 79]], again climbing through vents to help the group progress. Later on, Gail takes Ra-Ra back for her own safety. ===Effects of player's actions=== * Partly through Fun and Games, Ra-Ra will ask for food from the Dwellers. Should one choose to give her some, they will gain a small amount of [[Wastelanders reputations|Raider reputation]]. * If one was nice to her in dialogue throughout Fun and Games, she will agree to help them open an optional locked door to gain access to the [[prototype steel mill paint]] power armor helmet. Otherwise, she will refuse, and the helmet will be unobtainable. * If the player was nice to her, she will also agree to unlock a room which contains the [[Slug Buster]] during Buried Treasure. * If Johnny is killed during Buried Treasure by the turrets, Ra-Ra is quite nonchalant to seeing a man gunned to death by bullets in front of her, commenting, ''"Uh, I think Johnny's dead."'' She does make a passing comment saying she can't believe Johnny is dead and that she will probably have nightmares later. ==Inventory== {{Missing data|Inventory|FO76}} {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|No! This is a debt being paid back, nothing more.|sound=Ronny 005a0da3_1.ogg}} '''Ronny''' is a raider in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Ronny is the niece of [[Edwin (Wastelanders)|Edwin]], the leader of [[Edwin's gang|a gang]] of raiders. With Edwin being sick, Ronny has taken over leadership of the gang. During [[Thicker Than Water]] she helps [[Beckett (Wastelanders)|Beckett]] and the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] gain access to the [[Watoga Underground]] to finally kill the leader of the [[Blood Eagles]], [[the Claw]]. In the aftermath of aforementioned events, Edwin retires and Ronny officially declares herself the leader of the gang. Beckett mentions she will occasionally visit the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]'s [[CAMP|C.A.M.P.]], as long as Beckett's bar is open.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What's Ronny up to now, anyway?"''
[[Beckett (Wastelanders)|Beckett]]: ''"Now that Edwin's retired, Ronny is the full-time leader of the gang. She said she'll swing by your C.A.M.P. once in a while and say hello... as long as the bar's open, of course."''
([[Beckett (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Beckett's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Thicker Than Water]] }} ===Quest=== [[Thicker Than Water]]: Ronny meets Beckett and the Vault Dwellers at the entrance to the Watoga Underground, explains the situation, and hands over the [[Watoga Underground key|key]]. ===Effects of player's actions=== * If the Vault Dweller asks Ronny why she hasn't visited their C.A.M.P., Ronny sarcastically mentions she thought it would be better if her gang didn't know where all the Vault Dweller's valuables are. * If [[Frankie Beckett]] is killed, Beckett mentions he talked to Ronny and she buried Frankie for him because he did not deal with burying his brother himself. If Frankie survived, Beckett mentions she will help with Frankie's recovery from his addictions. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Fashionable raider outfit]]

There's a lot of profit to be made on a prime killer like this.|sound=Sargento 0042f45e_1.ogg}} '''Sargento''' is the leader of an independent [[Sargento's gang|gang]] of [[raiders]] who deal in [[slavery]] and hold fighting tournaments in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Sargento and his gang operated in the [[Capital Wasteland]] at one time. He met [[Glenn]] while the gang was being robbed by him and ended up in a fist fight. He was impressed with Glenn and offered him a job as a caravan guard.[[Glenn]]: ''"Funny story. I ran into Sargento and his gang out in the Capital Wasteland. I was just a scrappy kid at the time, and I stole cans of food from them. Got caught, and wound up in a fist-fight with the boss-man himself. I decked him hard with a sucker punch, but he laughed it off, and offered me a job as a caravan guard. When we settled here, I just kept at it. Only now, instead of keeping jerks away, I keep them in."''
([[Glenn/Dialogue#140|Glenn's dialogue]]) As of 2103, they have set up shop in the [[Watoga Civic Center]], and run a fighting arena where they pit slaves against dangerous creatures. [[Johnny Weston]] describes Sargento as a "two-bit wanna-be Roman emperor"[[Johnny Weston]]: ''"It was purely personal. Hal crossed me. I had to be the one to do him in, not some two-bit wanna-be Roman emperor like Sargento."''
([[Johnny Weston/Dialogue#74|Johnny Weston's dialogue]]) and a "sick bastard." However, he also never goes back on a deal and stays committed.[[Johnny Weston]]: ''"Sargento's a sick bastard, but he's a man of his word, if nothing else. He's not the type to renege on a deal."''
([[Johnny Weston/Dialogue#114|Johnny Weston's dialogue]]) Sargento also wants to keep his clientele at the arena entertained, to the point of suggesting ridiculous or overly vague themes. He leaves notes for [[Carl Madeiros]], a technician in the gang, with ideas for new match types. One of Sargento's suggestions was simply "[[Chainsaw (Fallout 76)|chainsaws]]." When asked what this meant, Sargento only replied "Chainsaws! You know, grgzgzghghgh pow! Make it happen!"[[Ideas for new match types]][[Watoga Civic Center terminal entries#Chainsaws|Watoga Civic Center terminal entries; Civic Center tech terminal]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[The Ol' Weston Shuffle]] }} ===Quests=== [[The Ol' Weston Shuffle]]: After the player character wins their matches in this quest, Sargento will come out to the arena to buy the player character as a new slave. After this, he will make them drink from the "Winner's Cup," knocking them out. Sargento will then disappear from the game.Sargento: ''"Alright, my new slave. Time to celebrate with a drink from the Winner's Cup! Bottoms up!"''

Surge: ''"They call me Surge. As in surgeon, but I'm no doctor. I can put a round in a [[Mole rat (Fallout 76)|molerat]]'s buck teeth at a thousand meters though."''
([[Surge/Dialogue#320|Surge's dialogue]]) is a member of the [[Crater Raiders]] residing inside the [[The Core|Crater Core]]. ==Background== Surge was trained to shoot from a young age "as soon as [she] could hold a pistol straight" by her father and became an expert marksman with surgical precision, earning her nickname. Her father was no pushover either, once killing three [[Yao guai (Fallout 76)|yao guai]] with only a pistol. However, even that could not prevent his death from heart failure.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You look pretty comfortable with that rifle."''
Surge: ''"My Da had me shooting as soon as I could hold a pistol straight. He's gone now. Killed three yao-gaui{{sic}} with a pistol once, but couldn't stop his own ticker from quitting on him."''
([[Surge/Dialogue]]) After he died, Surge wandered the [[Appalachian Trail]] and met [[Lev]] as he fought [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|super mutants]], joining him and ending up at [[the Crater]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How did you end up here?"''
Surge: ''"After my Da died, I walked the Appalachian trail. Figured why not. Spotted [[Lev]] in a firefight with some super mutants through my scope. Thought to myself 'now that’s a man I need to know better.'"''
([[Surge/Dialogue#315|Surge's dialogue]]) Like Lev, she dislikes [[Meg Groberg]]'s open-arms policy of allowing all sorts of mutants to join the raiders, believing that it will end up getting them killed one day. She derogatorily views [[Lucky Lou]] as a "walking corpse" and [[Gail]] a "green-skinned monster" and thinks both of them are unnatural freaks. According to Meg, Surge never respected her as a leader. She also dislikes [[Johnny Weston]] and his propensity for cheating at cards. However, she is fond of [[Molly (Wastelanders)|Molly]] and her drinks.[[Bless y'all's hearts]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |killable =yes |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[From Russia With Lev]] }} ===Quests=== * [[From Russia With Lev]]: Surge betrays Meg and joins [[Lev]]'s gang at the [[Poseidon Energy Plant WV-06]]. This attitude of mine is what keeps me alive and respected around here... and you should learn from that, rook.|sound=Wren 0055af73_1.ogg}} '''Wren''' is a member of the [[Crater Raiders]] at [[the Crater]]. ==Background== Wren was born several years after the [[Great War]] so the post-apocalyptic world is all she has ever known. Wren's father was a member of the [[Diehards]], and Wren was born and raised as part of the gang. Facing the growing threat of the [[Scorched Plague]], Wren and her father were among those who abandoned [[Margie McClintock]] and fled [[Appalachia]] under [[Meg Groberg]]'s lead; with both viewing the region as a deathtrap they were only too willing to leave. Her father ultimately died sometime before [[Timeline#2103|2103]], outside of Appalachia.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Dragged back? Were you here before with Meg?"''
Wren: ''"Pretty much born and raised a Diehard 'til we bailed on Margie. And a damn good thing we did, too. If them Scorched wiped out the Responders and the Brotherhood, you bet your ass they'd be pickin' us off like flies. {{Tooltip|Unlike you vault dwellers and the Free States, we didn't have any cozy little bunkers to hole up in.|Spiteful.}} But now that you're out... Welcome to the world of survival, rook."''
([[Wren (raider)/Dialogue#71|Wren's dialogue]])Wren: ''"My daddy's probably rollin' in his grave knowing Meg brought us here."''
([[Wren (raider)/Dialogue#68|Wren's dialogue]]) When Meg and the raiders chose to return to the region in 2103, Wren greatly disagreed but was eventually convinced by Meg, though she is still somewhat resentful of the choice.Wren: ''"I can't believe I let Meg talk me into coming here. My dad always said they left this place for a damn good reason."''
([[Wren (raider)/Dialogue#45|Wren's dialogue]]) After setting up at [[the Crater]], Wren became the raiders' communications expert, also coordinating scouting efforts and analyzing threats in the surrounding region for security purposes.[[The Crater terminal entries#--> Potential Threats|The Crater terminal entries; terminal, --> Potential Threats]] The amount of work she undertakes and the lack of help she receives has left her greatly annoyed by the other raiders' seeming incompetence, and she even marvels at how their gang has managed to survive. Because of her young age of 18, and because she is not capable of much heavy lifting, Wren is often pushed around by the other raiders. As a result, she has developed a hostile attitude towards those around her, even warning the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] of [[Vault 76]] that if they cross her, she will slit their throat faster than they can "cry for mommy."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"[Strength] I could break you in half, so you better start explaining."''
Wren: ''"Fine. As you've noticed, I ain't exactly a heavy lifter, and on account of me being eighteen years old, people like to think they can push me around. So that's why I got this attitude. But make no mistake, rook. You cross me, and I'll slit your throat faster than you can cry for mommy."''
([[Wren (raider)/Dialogue#218|Wren's dialogue]]) The white powder covering the [[Toxic Valley]] tends to break the Crater comms electronics,Wren: ''"I'm gettin' real tired of cleaning all this white crap out of my equipment... but better here than the Ash Jeap, I guess."''
([[Wren (raider)/Dialogue#67|Wren's dialogue]]) and from time to time Wren needs to replace the [[radio vacuum tube]]s, asking for the Dwellers for help. She is curious about the technology [[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]] has at her place at the [[Top of the World]], and is pondering to ask permission from Meg to visit it.Wren: ''"I wonder what kind of tech Rose has up there at Top of the World. I'll have to see if Meg will let me do some recon."''
([[Wren (raider)/Dialogue#64|Wren's dialogue]]) She is also not keen on people taking [[chems]].Wren: ''"Hope you got a stimpak on you. You want to die, you take that business elsewhere."''
([[Wren (raider)/Dialogue#57|Wren's dialogue]]) According to [[Creed]], Wren used to own a dog, however, it would not stop barking. [[Barb (Wastelanders)|Barb]] killed the dog and she got away with it because Wren believed her alibi. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started =* [[The Importance of Communication]] |quests involved = }} ===Quests=== * [[The Importance of Communication]]: Once every other day, Wren asks the player characters to track down three [[broken radio vacuum tube]]s to replace the ones in her equipment being constantly damaged by the [[Toxic Valley]]'s environment, rewarding them for ensuring her equipment remains in working condition. Using the right reply when returning with the vacuum tubes can earn either extra reputation or caps from Wren as thanks. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Leather coat (Fallout 76)|Leather coat]] |weapon =Random ranged weapon |otheritem =[[Stimpak (Fallout 76)|Stimpak]] x1 |ondeath = }} ==Notes== *Wren regards the [[Nuka-Cola Vaccinated|Nuka-Cola cure for the Scorched Plague]] produced by the Vault Dweller as "nasty."Wren: ''"You better not be here expecting me to drink something nasty again for the the sake of humanity... cuz that ain't happenin'."''
([[Wren (raider)/Dialogue#69|Wren's dialogue]]) *Wren mentions she is 18 and because she was introduced in ''Wastelanders'', her year of birth is likely 2085. However, because the timeline moved to 2104 and 2105 with updates, and she still mentions she is the same age, it could also be interpreted as 2086 or 2087. [[Julie (Wastelanders)|Julie]] is also similar, as she will always mention she is 23. ==Appearances== Wren appears {{In|FO76WL}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox original raiders FO76}} {{Navbox raiders FO76}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders raider characters]] [[Category:Crater Raiders characters]] [[Category:Diehards]] [[ru:Рен]]

Do as much as you can and be proud of it.|sound=Aubrie Willem 0042afd7_1.ogg}} '''Aubrie Willem'''[[Aubrie's note]] is a member of the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] residing in [[Foundation]]. ==Background== A medical practitioner with over thirty years of experience, Aubrie Willem is one of the co-founders of Foundation and its primary medical doctor. Prior to the [[Great War]], he lived in [[State#Pennsylvania|Pennsylvania]] and worked as a medical practitioner.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''All I know is there's an inoculation and you need to convince Paige to let me help you.''
Aubrie Willem: ''I was a doctor back in Pennsylvania. If Paige needs convincing you can tell him I'm behind you all the way. After experiencing those... Scorched, first hand? That's not something I want to lose anymore people to.'' He was asked by [[Paige]] to set up an observation camp nearby.Paige: ''I'll tell you what. One of my own is a doctor. Aubrie. I sent him ahead to start up an observation camp. Get the lay of things. You talk to him about this. If he's convinced, then I'm convinced, too. Deal?'' He was the only survivor of a [[Scorched]] attack and fled to a [[secluded cave]]. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Here to Stay]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Here to Stay]]: Before Paige agrees to let the Settlers get inoculated, Aubrie must be convinced. ===Effects of player's actions=== Depending on the player's actions, he will either return to Foundation to inform Paige of the reality of the Scorched Plague or remain in quarantine, eventually leading him to commit suicide. If convinced to return to Foundation, he can be found in his office, and will thank the player for telling him there is a vaccine to the Scorched Plague so he wouldn't have to quarantine himself to protect the rest of the Settlers from becoming infected themselves. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Surveyor outfit (Fallout 76)|Surveyor outfit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Aubrie appears {{In|FO76WL}}. ==Gallery== FO76WL Aubrie dead.png|Aubrie, if he commits suicide in quarantine following [[Here to Stay]] Foundation WW.png|Aubrie with [[Paige]] and [[Ward (Wastelanders)|Ward]] in ''[[Fallout: Wasteland Warfare]]'' ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Foundation}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Settler characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[ru:Обри]]
