I really like it, especially the fireflies.|sound=Davie Taylor 00429a2a_1.ogg}} '''Davie Taylor''' is a member of the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] residing in [[Foundation]]. ==Background== Davie was born in post-[[Great War|War]] [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|Pittsburgh]] to [[Elsie Taylor|Elsie]] and [[Derrick Taylor]], the former an enforcer for the raider gangs controlling the ruined city and the latter an enslaved worker. Davie is the child of an unintended pregnancy. Neither of them had enjoyed their situation in the Pitt, and Davie's birth was what spurred them to make a getaway. They succeeded, but always kept on the move, never staying in the same spot for more than a week. Elsie considered that was not the way to rise a child, but all that finally changed when they reached [[Foundation]].[[Elsie's story]] Davie is happy with his life in Foundation, though he longs to meet other kids his age regardless of who they are.Davie Taylor: ''"If you meet any other kids around here, tell me. I'll play with them, even if they're raiders."''
([[Davie Taylor/Dialogue#57|Davie Taylor's dialogue]]) He also self-professedly has a somewhat mischievous side, doing things such as chasing Foundation's [[Chicken (Fallout 76)|chickens]] and sneaking to play outside the town walls.Davie Taylor: ''"Sometimes I like to chase the chickens. Don't tell anyone, they'll get mad."''
([[Davie Taylor/Dialogue#56|Davie Taylor's dialogue]])Davie Taylor: ''"I'm not supposed to go outside town ... but sometimes I do."''
([[Davie Taylor/Dialogue#55|Davie Taylor's dialogue]]) Davie is also learning how to hack robots thanks to [[Penelope Hornwright]]'s teachings.Davie Taylor: ''"Penny's really nice. She's teaching me how to hack robots and all that."''
([[Davie Taylor/Dialogue#88|Davie Taylor's dialogue]]) He enjoys reading and when he is disappointed he is almost done with a book series, he becomes entertained by the thought of continuing the story as a writer himself.Davie Taloy: ''"Yeah, I'm just at the end of a book series. Kinda sad to think it's gonna be over soon."''
([[Davie Taylor/Dialogue#12|Davie Taylor's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = * [[Davie's Secret Mission]] {{cut}} |quests involved = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Child shirt and jeans]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Notes== If it rains, Davie can be heard excitedly saying, "It's slippy out, yeah!" ==Appearances== Davie Taylor appears only {{In|FO76WL}}. ==Gallery== FO76 Foundation Davie's Artwork.png|Davie's artwork ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Foundation}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Settler characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[ru:Дэйви Тэйлор]]

I guess nowhere's really "good" to raise a family any more.|sound=Derick Taylor.ogg}} '''Derrick Taylor''' is a member of the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] residing in [[Foundation]]. ==Background== Derrick was born and raised in [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|Pittsburgh]], stating his roots go back to at least four or five generations.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Where are you from?"''
Derrick: ''"Pittsburgh. Born and bred. My roots went back there four or... five? Generations. Had to leave though. It's... Just don't go north. Trust me."''
([[Derrick Taylor/Dialogue#248|Derrick Taylor's dialogue]]) After the [[Great War]], the city fell on the hands of [[raiders]], taking many civilians as slaves, including Derrick, who worked at rebuilding the city for their enslavers. At some point, he met a raider enforcer by the name [[Elsie Taylor|Elsie]]. Both shared their distaste at their jobs, and eventually fell in love. They wanted to leave, and after having a child, [[Davie Taylor|Davie]], as a result of an unintentional pregnancy, they orchestrated an escape. Derrick hates guns, but that day Elsie made him use one, though he never hit anything he aimed at. They managed to escape, and during the next years, Derrick and his family always kept moving, never staying on the same spot for more than a week. Elsie considered that was not the way to raise a child, but all that finally changed when they arrived at [[Foundation]].[[Elsie's story]] Ever since settling in Foundation, Derrick has had much work as a carpenter and constructor.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Can you tell me about any of the others?"''
[[Ward (Wastelanders)|Ward]]: ''"I'm not a gossip. Waste of time running your mouth about other peoples problems. But I can tell you that the Taylors are good people. Derrick is a fine carpenter. And Elsie know how to handle herself in a fight."''
([[Ward (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#163|Ward's dialogue]]) He and Elsie are highly protective of their son Davie, as he is one of the first of the post-War generation. Derrick has little to say of Pittsburgh other than that [[Appalachia]] is leagues above the former city.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Is the land here really that good?"''
Derrick: ''"Whole stretches of country up north is just cratered. And the few fields that'll grow anything, let's just say what comes out of the ground makes the geiger counter go crazy. Appalachia's deadly -- but at least here we stand a chance."''
([[Derrick Taylor/Dialogue#245|Derrick Taylor's dialogue]]) If questioned about his past in the Pitt, Derrick prefers not to talk about it, advising [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] not to go north, ever. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Fieldhand Needed!]] {{cut}} }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Fisherman's overalls (Fallout 76)|Black fisherman's overalls]]
[[Wedding ring (Fallout 76)|Wedding ring]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Derrick Taylor appears {{In|FO76WL}}. ==Behind the scenes== * Derrick is erroneously referred to as "Derrick Hale" in the ''Fallout 76'' credits. This is because Derrick's voice actor, [[Neil Kaplan]], also voiced [[Emerson Hale]]. * Derrick appears to have an interest in cooking. Elsie mentions he baked a pie. [[Penelope Hornwright]] has some cut [[Founder's Hall terminal entries|terminal entries]] after moving to Foundation in which her terminal mentions Derrick brought her a casserole. ==Gallery== FO76WL Foundation Musical Trio.png|Derrick, [[Elsie Taylor|Elsie]] and [[Samuel (Wastelanders)|Samuel]] playing music ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Foundation}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Settler characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[ru:Деррик Тэйлор]]

I guess I'm most known for being a great shot, but I also help out with stuff that needs building.|sound=Elsie Taylor 0058eca2_1.ogg}} '''Elsie Taylor''' is a member of the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] residing in [[Foundation]]. ==Background== A former enforcer from [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|the Pitt]], Elsie was unhappy with life as a raider and longed for a change. Falling in love with then-enslaved [[Derrick Taylor]] and having a [[Davie Taylor|son]] with him only solidified her desire to leave, although it was an unintentional pregnancy. They eventually staged a bloody escape in which she killed eight raiders on the way out. She suffered a cracked rib and a bullet grazed her scalp, but managed to keep her husband completely unharmed. The raiders stopped looking for them after she ambushed the first hunting party they sent. During the next years, Elsie and her family always kept moving, never staying on the same spot for more than a week. Elsie considered that was not the way to raise a child, but all that finally changed when they arrived at Foundation.[[Elsie's story]] She is known around Foundation for her skilled marksmanship, making her one of the few skilled lookouts for the settlement.Settler: ''"Aren't you tired of being on watch, Elsie?"''
''Elsie Taylor: ''"Nah, I am an angel of death with this bad boy. What more could I want?"''
Settler: ''"Hmm... dunno. Maybe some bourbon?"''
''Elsie Taylor: ''"Thank you, ma'am. I will definitely take you up on that, next break I take."''
([[Settlers (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Settler]] and [[Elsie Taylor/Dialogue|Elsie Taylor's dialogue]]) Additionally, Elsie also helps with the Settlers' construction efforts. Elsie claims family is the only thing that matters to her. She is training her son Davie how to shoot so that he can protect himself, but hopes that they can build up Foundation enough that he won't have to ever use a gun. Elsie is contemplating to get a [[Dog (Fallout 76)|dog]] to guard her house if the settlement keeps prospering.Elsie: ''"Maybe if this place keeps going, I should get a dog to help me guard the house."''

General rule: they keep the good stuff in the back.|sound=Fred Radcliff 00405c82_1.ogg}} '''Sergeant Fred Radcliff''' is a former [[United States Army|U.S. Army]] soldier in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Sergeant Radcliff first enlisted into the Army during the onset of the [[Sino-American War]], and was immediately shipped off to the frontlines. He described himself as a "dumb kid" who survived thanks to his squadmates, [[Oliver Fields|Captain Fields]] and [[Thompson (Wastelanders)|Sergeant Thompson]], watching out for him, with him only losing one toe to frostbite as compared to Thompson, who lost three.[[The Old Guard, Vol 14: Ch 2]] Radcliff is the squad's technical expert, and he describes himself as highly knowledgeable about all manner of robots and systems. All three, as well as several military working dogs, including [[Lucky (Wastelanders)|Private Lucky]], were later part of the original team responsible for moving the gold reserves at [[Fort Knox]] to [[Vault 79]]. However, the Vault closed, and they were left outside when the [[Great War]] struck. Equipped in their [[power armor]], they wandered for years, always staying near [[Appalachia]], deciding to return after hearing it was safe enough to come back.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How did you end up here?"''
[[Oliver Fields]]: ''"Thompson, Radcliff and I were all part of the team at Fort Knox that moved the gold here. The vault shut before we could get in though. We wandered the wasteland, always staying nearby. Once we heard it was safe, we came here. Damn glad we did too."''
([[Oliver Fields/Dialogue|Oliver Fields' dialogue]]) Before reaching Appalachia though, they ended up in [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|the Pitt]] and attempted to save the civilians there, but were unsuccessful. In the aftermath, seeing Captain Fields wounded, Radcliff ruminated on their survival and considered simply retiring and forgetting the past. However, they were convinced to hang on after once again hearing the broadcast from [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|military remnants]] back in Appalachia, and became convinced to return "home." On their return trip, the soldiers ended up following and observing the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] as they made their journey from the Pitt to Appalachia. Eventually, they all agreed to a meeting with the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] at the [[ransacked bunker]].[[Paige]]: ''I had to reach out to some... specialists who've been shadowing us since the Pitt. They've all agreed to meet, but they want to talk to you first.''
([[Paige/Dialogue|Paige's dialogue]]) Radcliff also has quite a sense of humor and will often make jokes even during life-or-death situations. Upon reaching [[Foundation]], Radcliff and [[Jen]] begin to constantly bicker. While Captain Fields excuses Jen due to her young age, he doesn't approve Radcliff's conduct since he is old enough to behave.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Can you tell me about the other people here?"''
[[Oliver Fields]]: ''"They're all upstanding folk. Paige wouldn't let them in if they weren't. Only personal problem I've got is Radcliff and Jen constantly sniping at each other. Most of us wish they would just shack up and get it over with."''
([[Oliver Fields/Dialogue|Oliver Fields' dialogue]]) Radcliff will also express his desire to finally retire from his military life and settle down as a farmer.Fred Radcliff: ''"No offense to Fields or Thompson, but I'm thinking about retiring to one of those farmsteads. Grow some crops, take naps, escape Lucky's drool."''

However, [[Penelope Hornwright]] is missing and must be rescued. * [[All That Glitters]]: Radcliff, Jen and Penelope Hornwright begin to break into [[Vault 79]]. The security system and [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|feral ghouls]] must be fought, and Radcliff and Jen will assist in fighting them as temporary followers. * [[Secrets Revealed]]: After locating the surviving [[Secret Service (Fallout 76)|Secret Service]] agents, Radcliff and Jen assist in restarting the vault reactor. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Army fatigues (Fallout 76)|Dirty Army fatigues]] |weapon =[[Assault rifle (Fallout 76)|Assault rifle]] |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Notes== * After completing [[Secrets Revealed]] for the Settlers, Radcliff will disappear from Foundation. * When talking to Radcliff after completing the quest Secrets Revealed by siding with Foundation, he will make a comment on how zero casualties had occured, but makes an exception for [[Chase Terrier|Digger]] even if the player had convinced [[Derek Garrison|AC]] to spare him. ==Appearances== Radcliff appears {{In|FO76WL}}. ==Behind the scenes== * Sergeant Radcliff, [[Oliver Fields|Captain Fields]], [[Thompson (Wastelanders)|Sergeant Thompson]], [[Lucky (Wastelanders)|Private Lucky]], [[Odysseus]], and [[Angel (Wastelanders)|Angel]] are all identified as members of [[The Old Guard, Vol 14: Ch 2|The Old Guard]]. This unit has the second largest Military Working Dog detachment in the continental United States and works closely with the U.S. Secret Service, identical to their role in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. * After preparing a brain during Duty Calls, Radcliff will call the player character "chef brainardee," referencing the canned pasta brand Chef Boyardee.Fred Radcliff: ''"All right, look at you. The chef supreme of brains. Chef brainardee. Chef des brains-ine."''

Did you know that I'd be all alone out there?!|Jen confronting her [[Mochou|mother]]|sound=Jen 00583e92_1.ogg}} '''Jen''' is a member of the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] residing in [[Foundation]]. She is the youngest scavenger in Foundation, having learned from her parents. ==Background== Jen was born after the [[Great War]]. Her parents had a complicated relationship, both former [[China|Chinese]] spies who fell in love despite it being forbidden. Despite her heritage, she has lived in America for her entire life, mostly in the [[Capital Wasteland]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Where did you all come from?"''
Jen: ''"Oh, I joined up with them north of here a while back. They seem to be from all over this region. My family used to live in what's now the Capital Wasteland."''
([[Jen/Dialogue|Jen's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What's China like?"''
Jen: ''"I honestly have no idea. I was born here sometime after the war and I've lived here my whole life. Mostly in the Capital Wasteland. My parents didn't talk about it much. I know they didn't want to go back, that they weren't supposed to have me or fall in love with each other. We were just a normal family of survivors, except sometimes my parents had to go do things. Then one day my mom just never came home."''
([[Jen/Dialogue#88|Jen's dialogue]]) About 11 years ago when she was a teenager,Jen: ''"The entry you're looking for would have been broadcast daily since about... 11 years ago."''
([[Jen/Dialogue#38|Jen's dialogue]]) her mother [[Mochou]] mysteriously disappeared, leaving her and her [[Jen's father|father]] alone. Assuming she was dead, the two moved on. However, a year later during winter, her father thought he might have a chance to reunite with Mochou after hearing a radio signal, but it turned out to be a raider trap and he was killed. Jen buried him in his [[Chinese stealth armor (Wastelanders)|stealth suit]] because she was unable to remove it. Jen also began to forget her mother's face and what she looked like. In 2103, Jen arrived at [[Appalachia]] from the Capital Wasteland. She soon met up with [[Paige]] and his group of [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] somewhere north of [[Spruce Knob]]. Since then, she has fallen in with the residents at [[Foundation]], working mostly as a scout for the settlement.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you do around here?"''
Jen: ''"Mostly, I keep an eye on the area around Foundation. I look for good things to bring back, and keep and eye out for anything hazardous. If the super mutants are on the move, or a bunch of scorched move into the area, Ward needs to know as soon as possible."''
([[Jen/Dialogue#142|Jen's dialogue]]) She is also pulling her weight as a talented electrical engineer,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What's "the next part" that you mentioned?"''
Jen: ''"I need to find someone good with robots. I'm alright with electrical stuff, but it's a software issue."''
([[Jen/Dialogue#62|Jen's dialogue]]) familiar with all sorts of high end, especially Chinese technology, but does not give that away for fear of how Great War survivors might react. However, she is not adept at hacking and usually collaborates with other people when working on robots.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You should ask Doctor Penelope Hornwright for help when you see her."''
Jen: ''"I feel like I recognize that name... is she good with robots? I can do electrical stuff but hacking and whatnot is beyond me."''
([[Jen/Dialogue#76|Jen's dialogue]]) She and the Foundation settlers were planning to pick apart one of the [[air purifier]]s in the [[Ash Heap]] in order to make them work again.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You probably recognize her last name from her family business."''
Jen: ''"Ohh, of course! We were planning to pick apart one of those air purifiers to see if we could get them going again. I'll have to ask her about that too."''
([[Jen/Dialogue#206|Jen's dialogue]]) Jen is good friends with [[Samuel (Wastelanders)|Samuel]], who occasionally joins her on scavenging hunts.[[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settler]]: ''"Hiya Davie, how're you today?"''
[[Davie Taylor]]: ''"Ah, I'm okay. A little bored, though."''
Settler: ''"Did you hear that Jen and Samuel found a bunch of comics on the last scavenger run?"''
Davie Taylor: ''"Wow, really? I gotta ask Dad if we can trade for some. Thanks!"''
([[Settlers (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Settler]] and [[W05 Settler DavieTaylor.txt|Davie Taylor's dialogue]]) Since [[Penelope Hornwright]]'s arrival, Jen and the doctor have become friends and colleagues. Jen states Penny is very smart and will teach her "loads of fun things" involving tech. The two have also been working on the [[Recalibrated Liberator|Liberator]] that the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] brought them. Jen is hoping to turn it into a "soothing personal assistant,"[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"So are you and Penny friends now?"''
Jen: ''"Sure, Penny's great. She's super smart and has promised to teach me loads of fun things. We've been working on overhauling that little liberator you nabbed. I'm making it into a soothing personal assistant. Or that's the goal. It's still a work in progress!"''
([[Jen/Dialogue#144|Jen's dialogue]]) and has named it "Reco."Jen: ''"Hey, have you seen Reco wandering around?"''
([[Jen/Dialogue#74|Jen's dialogue]]) Jen has also befriended the dog [[Lucky (Wastelanders)|Private Lucky]], with whom she occasionally cuddles.Jen: ''"Sorry, can't talk. Private Lucky and I have an important mission to go on. Operation: Cuddle Time."''
([[Jen/Dialogue#4|Jen's dialogue]]) She gets along with [[Thompson (Wastelanders)|Thompson]]. However, she does not get along with [[Oliver Fields]] and [[Fred Radcliff]], the former because he reminds her of her parents while the latter because he makes unfunny jokes. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion =yes |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Invisible Ties]] * [[Duty Calls]] * [[Division of Wealth]] * [[All That Glitters]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Invisible Ties]]: The player character must track down a functioning Chinese stealth suit for Jen but stumbles across a familial connection to Jen. * [[Division of Wealth]]: Jen waits in [[Freddy Fear's basement]] with the rest of the group. * [[All That Glitters]]: Jen helps the player character break into Vault 79 by bypassing laser grids. ===Other interactions=== After the completion of Invisible Ties, Jen will award the player character with plans for the Chinese stealth armor and helmet. She will also give them a note, [[Note from Jen]], which states that she managed to find plans for standard Chinese stealth armor, though it is not as advanced as the prototype she wore. At this point in the story, however, she had not yet used or worn the stealth suit, having only just acquired it earlier in the quest. ===Effects of player's actions=== Jen has multiple endings and outcomes as a result of the player's actions during the main quest of Wastelanders. A choice will be presented during Invisible Ties to either kill Mochou, or with a high enough Charisma or Intelligence, convince her to spare Mochou. * If the player character is able to convince Jen to find a way to spare Mochou, Jen will stay in Foundation after [[All That Glitters]]. During the quest she will mention she's going to help her mother settle in Foundation, and her plans of finding a doctor that can change Mochou's face thanks to a tip from [[Samuel (Wastelanders)|Samuel]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What're you going to do now?"''
Jen: ''"I'm going to help my mom get settled in at Foundation, show her all our decadent consumerist ways. Samuel told us about a doctor who can change your face... so we might look at doing that down the road. If they can do it for a ghoul."''
([[Jen/Dialogue#382|Jen's dialogue]]) "[[Jen's journal, entry 1]]" can then be found on the table in her room. Mochou can also be found in Jen's room, now wearing a [[laundered dress (Fallout 76)|green laundered dress]] instead of the stealth armor. * If the player character chooses to kill Mochou, Jen will express disappointment and ask to talk once she gets back to Foundation. She will continue to work with Foundation until All That Glitters, in which she will mention she's going to bury her mother beside her father to the north in the Capital Wasteland, and that she's considered asking Samuel to accompany her. After the quest, she will be removed from the Founder's Hall, leaving only the "[[Jen's goodbye]]" holotape in her room, which details her wishes to leave Foundation. * If the player chooses to treat her poorly during [[Invisible Ties]], Jen will steal a portion of the gold during the Vault 79 raid and leave entirely, leaving a [[Jen's goodbye|message]] for the Vault Dweller behind. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Nuka-World geyser shirt & jeans (Fallout 76)|Nuka-World geyser shirt & jeans]]

This can be seen during the Vault 79 raid, where they will occasionally lightly argue or fight. But they will also kill Jen, and I can't risk that.|sound=Mochou 00590a37_1.ogg}} '''Agent Mochou''' is a former spy for the [[People's Liberation Army]] featuring in the Settler questline {{in|FO76WL}}. ==Background== A lifelong agent trained from birth in the [[China|People's Republic of China]] for this singular purpose,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"So you were a spy before the war, too?"''
Mochou: ''"Yes. I was trained from childhood to do this job. It's all I knew, I never chose any of this. It was either follow orders or die."''
([[Mochou/Dialogue#195|Mochou's dialogue]]) Mochou, under the threat of death, was assigned to the American theater and worked closely with other communist operatives against the American war effort. Orders and a lifetime of being shaped to think as Chinese commanders wanted her to think resulted in an incredibly capable and loyal agent until the [[Great War]] happened and Mochou realized the two superpowers both lied to their people, manipulating them like puppets. Once she saw the puppeteers, she realized she wanted nothing to do with any of it; she did not wish to return to China and fled into the wasteland instead. Mochou fell in love with a [[Jen's father|man]] who was another Chinese spy and she gave birth to [[Jen]] sometime after the War; both the relationship and Jen's birth were forbidden under the Chinese orders.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What's China like?"''
[[Jen]]: ''"I honestly have no idea. I was born here sometime after the war and I've lived here my whole life. Mostly in the Capital Wasteland. My parents didn't talk about it much. I know they didn't want to go back, that they weren't supposed to have me or fall in love with each other. We were just a normal family of survivors, except sometimes my parents had to go do things. Then one day my mom just never came home."''
([[Jen/Dialogue#88|Jen's dialogue]]) Jen's parents taught her Chinese, how to scavenge in the wasteland to survive, and taught a healthy skepticism of capitalism, though not the principles of communist thought. The family lived together in the [[Capital Wasteland]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Where did you all come from?"''
[[Jen]]: ''"Oh, I joined up with them north of here a while back. They seem to be from all over this region. My family used to live in what's now the Capital Wasteland."''
([[Jen/Dialogue#|Jen's dialogue]]) Mochou assumed that all governments had fallen, including China. However, she was wrong: Another pre-War asset, loyal to the communist cause beyond nuclear fire,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Someone tracked you down? Who?"''
Mochou: ''"{{Tooltip|Another pre-war asset, very loyal to the cause. They only come here occasionally to check up on us... but trust me, you don't ever want to meet them.|uncomfortable even talking about them}}"''
([[Mochou/Dialogue#207|Mochou's dialogue]]) tracked her down using trackers embedded in her gear, and presented an ultimatum: Follow orders or have her and her family be killed. Sometime around 2092,[[Jen]]: ''"The entry you're looking for would have been broadcast daily since about... 11 years ago."''
([[Jen/Dialogue#38|Jen's dialogue]]) she abandoned her family, disappearing overnight, to avoid dragging them into the invisible war.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Why didn't you just leave after the bombs fell?"''
Mochou: ''"I did! They tracked me down with tracers in my gear, years later. I thought everything was all over, that the governments were all gone, that I was free. If I had known, I would have thrown it all away and just hoped for the best. I thought holding on to it would save my life, but I was wrong. So wrong."''
([[Mochou/Dialogue#202|Mochou's dialogue]])Mochou: ''"If I give you this suit then they'll come for you... and they'll find me. Maybe not tomorrow, but eventually. They will kill me for it. I don't care if I die, I may as well already be dead. But they will also kill Jen, and I can't risk that."''
([[Mochou/Dialogue#177|Mochou's dialogue]]) Jen and her father moved on, assuming Mochou had died, and Jen began to forget her mother's face and what she looked like. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |killable = yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Invisible Ties]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Invisible Ties]]: Mochou is located as part of the quest and depending on the player character's decisions, she will die, become estranged from her daughter, or join the settlers at [[Foundation]]. ===Effects of player's actions=== * If Mochou is spared and settles in [[Foundation]], [[Samuel (Wastelanders)|Samuel]] will tell her and [[Jen]] about a doctor who can change Mochou's face.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What're you going to do now?"''
[[Jen]]: ''"I'm going to help my mom get settled in at Foundation, show her all our decadent consumerist ways. Samuel told us about a doctor who can change your face... so we might look at doing that down the road. If they can do it for a ghoul."''
([[Jen/Dialogue#382|Jen's dialogue]]) * If the player character chooses to kill Mochou, which can only be done if the dialogue to attack Mochou while talking to Jen is chosen, Mochou's essential status will be disabled and Jen will shout, "Wait!" Mochou can be killed and she will not fight back. A [[Chinese officer sword (Fallout 76)|Chinese officer sword]] can be looted from Mochou. Jen will mention she needs a moment and asks to talk once she gets back to Foundation. She will continue to work with Foundation until [[All That Glitters]], in which she will mention she's going to bury her mother beside her father to the north in the [[Capital Wasteland]]. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Chinese stealth armor (Wastelanders)|Chinese stealth armor]] (initially)

That's where I come in.|sound=Paige.ogg}} '''Paige''' is the de facto leader of the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] living at [[Foundation]] in [[Appalachia]]. While not the sole leader of Foundation and Paige does not refer to himself as their leader and views himself as merely being in charge of construction, he is said to be the closest member they have resembling a main leader.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Tell me about Paige."''
[[Heather Ellis]]: ''"He's the closest Foundation has to a leader, I guess. I never got to know him real well, but he always seemed like a decent guy. Honest, reliable, cares about the people, that kind of stuff."''
([[W05 Dialogue HeatherEllis.txt|Heather Ellis' dialogue]]) His leaderly role has resulted in much of the settlement's success.[[Davenport]]: ''"You've met Paige, yes? The success of the Foundation settlement owes much to his steady leadership. It is therefore necessary that we keep well-apprised of his condition. A photograph would serve that purpose well."''
([[W05 Davenport.txt|Davenport's dialogue]]) ==Background== Right after the [[Great War]], Paige and other survivors took the last train out of [[Union Station (Washington, D.C.)|Union Station]] in [[Washington, D.C.]] As they left the Capital they saw the toxic green air lingering above the city.[[Paige's journal, entry 1]] Paige and his group eventually reached [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|the ruins of Pittsburgh]] in [[State#Pennsylvania|Pennsylvania]], where they would stay until it became too dangerous, and they had to leave. Led by Paige, a large group of [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|settlers]] went south, arriving in [[Appalachia]] and setting up the settlement known as [[Foundation]] at [[Spruce Knob]]. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started =* [[Trade Secrets]] * [[Invisible Ties]] * [[Duty Calls]] |quests involved =* [[Here to Stay]] * [[Siding with Foundation]] * [[Division of Wealth]] * [[All That Glitters]] * [[Secrets Revealed]] * [[Photo Opportunity|Daily: Photo Opportunity]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Here to Stay]]: The [[Vault 76 overseer]] asks the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] to warn him of the threat of the Scorched Plague to the Settlers and have them inoculated with the vaccine. Paige is initially hesitant to trust them and asks that they meet with [[Aubrie Willem]] and tell him of the threat. If Aubrie agrees to the vaccine, then Paige will support it as well. Once Aubrie is found and told of the threat and has it passed back to Paige, he will agree to have his Settlers inoculated. He is a little surprised later to find the vaccine comes as a new flavor of [[Nuka-Cola (Fallout 76)|Nuka-Cola]], but nonetheless expresses his gratitude for protecting his Settlers from the Scorched and Scorchbeasts. * [[Trade Secrets]] - Paige suggests finding someone who can provide a drilling machine capable of breaking into Vault 79, so that the Settlers do not have to use the reinforced Vault front door instead, believing that the [[The Motherlode (robot)|Motherlode]] drill from [[Hornwright Industrial]] could help. * [[Invisible Ties]] - Paige suggests speaking to [[Jen]] about finding a stealth suit that could help bypass the security lasers preventing further entry into the Vault should they be tripped and trigger a security lockdown. * [[Duty Calls]] - Paige remembers some [[United States Army]] special forces that have been tailing the Settlers from the Pitt that could help scavenge the tools needed to bypass the RobCo automated defense turrets serving as the final line of defense in Vault 79 and sends the Vault 76 Dwellers to rendezvous with them by signaling them with waving the [[Flag of the United States|Stars and Stripes]] to get their attention. ===Other interactions=== * Paige can be chosen over [[Meg Groberg]] and her raiders for a raid on [[Vault 79]] after telling him of the Vault being where the United States' gold bullion reserves have been stored and how it could help rebuild Appalachia's economy. If he is, he will appear at the end of [[Secrets Revealed]]. The Vault Dweller may agree with his deal or betray him. * If the vault was raided with the raiders, unlike Meg, Paige won't have anything to comment. * If the player did not get on Foundation's good side during [[Supplying Demands]], such as by killing [[Mike Tiller]], Paige will say he heard about what happened from [[Gloria Chance]] and says the Vault Dweller has a lot of guts coming to Foundation. He also says it's a good thing the Vault Dweller wasn't dealing with him directly. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Steel worker uniform|Clean steel worker uniform]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Paige appears {{In|FO76WL}}. His voice actor returned to make new comments for the ''[[Steel Dawn]]'' update. ==Behind the scenes== * Paige is voiced by [[Beau Billingslea]], best known as the English voice of [[w:c:cowboybebop:Jet Black|Jet Black]] in ''[[wikipedia:Cowboy Bebop|Cowboy Bebop]]''. In localized versions of the game, his voice is dubbed by Pedro Tena (Spanish). * In Bethesda's ''Inside The Vault'', Paige is described as the former head of the [[Construction Workers Union]] in [[Washington, D.C.]][https://fallout.bethesda.net/en/article/4AMkQUo7C67TNCgOiVVNZw/fallout-76-inside-the-vault-new-arrivals-coming-to-appalachia-in Fallout 76: Inside The Vault - New Arrivals Coming To Appalachia In Wastelanders]: ''"Led by Paige, the former head of a Construction Workers Union in Washington D.C., the Settlers are a hard-working and industrious crew, primarily made up of people who are well-versed in how to construct and run a city. After hearing that Appalachia might offer some refuge from the trials of the Wasteland, they made their way into the area in hopes of finding a safe place to begin rebuilding. They broke ground at Spruce Knob, began repurposing its existing buildings, cleared the surrounding trees, and a fledgling city has begun taking shape, which they’ve dubbed “Foundation”. These Settlers may know their way around construction equipment, but they have no idea what challenges you and others have faced in Appalachia during the past year. It may be mutually beneficial to seek them out to share your experiences and lend a helping hand toward their efforts."'' * At some point between the trailer release and final release, Paige's hair was changed from a short haircut to balding. ==Gallery== FO76WL Paige alternate.png|Paige smoking Paige.jpg|Paige in the ''Wastelanders'' trailer Foundation WW.png|Paige with [[Aubrie Willem]] and [[Ward (Wastelanders)|Ward]] in ''[[Fallout: Wasteland Warfare]]'' ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox Foundation}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Settler characters]] [[ru:Пейдж (Wastelanders)]] [[zh:Paige (Wastelanders)]]

I've seen plenty of folks try to save the world since things went to hell, and all of them had their problems.|sound=Penelope Hornwright 0040c247 1.ogg}} '''Doctor Penelope "Penny" Hornwright''' is a [[ghoul]] scientist in [[Appalachia]]. Before the [[Great War]], she served as the senior operations executive at [[Hornwright Industrial]]. ==Background== Born March 4, [[Timeline#2048|2048]], to [[Daniel Hornwright|Daniel]] and [[Evelyn Hornwright]], Penny attended [[Vault-Tec University]], from which she graduated summa cum laude in [[Timeline#2070|2070]] with a double major in Business Administration and Geological Science.[[Penelope Hornwright's resume]] She held two internships prior to her graduation: one in the operations department of Hornwright Industrial in the summer of [[Timeline#2068|2068]] and one in the automation department of [[Atomic Mining Services]] (AMS) in the summer of [[Timeline#2069|2069]], where she helped to establish business agreements between AMS and Hornwright Industrial.[[AMS corporate headquarters terminal entries#Partnership Report: Hornwright|AMS corporate headquarters terminal entries; CEO Kilson's terminal, Partnership Report: Hornwright]] After graduation, she was immediately placed at the head of Hornwright Industrial's operations department. Her first day of work was in mid-2073.[[Hornwright Industrial notice]] She pursued a ruthless policy of automation at all costs like her father. She supported her father's automation policies, stopping only when it came to actually physically hurting people, such as during the [[Timeline#2077|2077]] protests when she was forced to hire strikebreakers to deal with rioting miners. When her father realized that she detested the job, he commissioned a robotic solution the problem, rather than force her to toughen up.[[Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries#Personal Entry 04|Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries; CEO's terminal, Personal Entry 04]] However, when it came to cleaning up the damage, she showed a tenacity worthy of her father. After the [[Rockhound]] was recovered by the National Guard, she instituted 24-hour shifts, demanding that the workers accelerate the repairs to improve the company's bottom line.[[Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries#Archived Message - 10.12.77|Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries; terminal: Jeffery Vaccarro, Archived Message - 10.12.77]] Penny was also responsible for perverting the original purpose of the air purifiers supplied by the [[Clear Skies Alliance]], turning them into ash forges capable of extracting heavy minerals from the polluted air.[[Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries#Log Notes 8.29.77|Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries; Penny Hornwright's lab terminal, Log Notes 8.29.77]][[Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries#Personal Entry 03|Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries; CEO's terminal, Personal Entry 03]] When [[Evelyn Hornwright|her mother]] succumbed to cancer in 2076,[[Charleston Herald - Tragedy Hits Hornwright]] Penny moved on quickly, realizing that the alternative was slowly withering away, eaten alive by the cancerous cells.[[Hornwright Estate terminal entries#Outgoing Mail System - Entry 01|Hornwright Estate terminal entries; Penny Hornwright's terminal, Outgoing Mail System - Entry 01]] Despite her father unraveling and slowly succumbing to paranoia and obsessions centering on [[the Motherlode]] project, she still cared for him. She was planning to marry [[Bryce Garrahan]], son of the owner of Hornwright's business competitor, [[Garrahan Mining Company|Garrahan Mining]]. The two had known each other since they were children and had fallen in love despite the divide between their wealthy families. She and Bryce were planning to tell her father about their plans but it is uncertain if they succeeded in doing so before the bombs fell.[[Hornwright Estate terminal entries#Outgoing Mail System - Entry 04|Hornwright Estate terminal entries; Penny Hornwright's terminal, Outgoing Mail System - Entry 04]][[Garrahan Estate terminal entries#GME-10-20-077|Garrahan Estate terminal entries; Bryce Garrahan's terminal, GME-10-20-077]] Some time between [[Timeline#2083|2083]] and [[Timeline#2084|2084]], Penny had a daughter. Not long after, she and her family came upon a [[Vault]] with a faulty door and negotiated with its residents to allow entrance for her daughter and the rest of her family in exchange for repairing the Vault door, knowing that she would be stuck outside. The repairs were successful, saving the Vault's residents from outside radiation in the process, but she was dosed and became a ghoul.[[Paige's journal, entry 2]][[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How did you become a ghoul?"''
Penelope Hornwright: ''"{{Tooltip|Well, not long after things went to hell, I ran across a Vault with a faulty door. It was perfectly fine inside, but the door mechanism was shot. I negotiated with those inside and they agreed to take my family in if I could close it. Closing it could only be done from the outside and would result in lethal radiation. Imagine my surprise to end up like this! It has definite advantages though. Sometimes. I miss my nose, though.|calm, matter of fact}}"''
([[Penelope Hornwright/Dialogue#156|Penelope Hornwright's dialogue]]) She adopted a habit of wandering and avoiding settlements and large groups, knowing that most tended to shoot ghouls on sight no matter whether they were feral or not. At one point, she traveled with a survivor group through [[Charlotte, North Carolina|Charlotte]] and passed herself off as human by wearing a balaclava to cover her face; however, she was eventually found out and forced out of the city.[[Founder's Hall terminal entries#Personal Entry 1|Founder's Hall terminal entries; Penelope's terminal, Personal Entry 1]] Returning to Appalachia at some point in 2103, she witnessed the construction of [[Foundation]] from afar. Penny also realized she was being chased by an unknown creature, and decided to head to her family's former [[Hornwright Estate|estate]] to hide from it - not knowing it was actually [[The Motherlode (robot)|the Motherlode]], recognizing her senior Hornwright Industrial credentials. ===Trade Secrets timeline=== Penny may be contacted by a [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] from [[Vault 76]], who was looking for assistance in using the Motherlode to enter [[Vault 79]] and claim the [[Gold bullion|treasure]] it contained. In exchange for her help, Penny asked for a safe place to live in the settlement of Foundation.Events of [[Trade Secrets]] Since Penny's arrival at Foundation, she has become friends with [[Jen]]. The two have been working on the [[Recalibrated Liberator|Liberator]] that the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] brought them, with Jen hoping to turn it into a soothing personal assistant.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"So are you and Penny friends now?"''
[[Jen]]: ''"Sure, Penny's great. She's super smart and has promised to teach me loads of fun things. We've been working on overhauling that little liberator you nabbed. I'm making it into a soothing personal assistant. Or that's the goal. It's still a work in progress!"''
([[Jen/Dialogue#144|Jen's dialogue]]) Penny has also been teaching [[Davie Taylor]] how to hack robots.[[Davie Taylor]]: ''"Penny's really nice. She's teaching me how to hack robots and stuff."''
([[Davie Taylor/Dialogue#88|Davie Taylor's dialogue]]) Her presence is not appreciated by [[Maggie Williams]] due to the history between their families; Maggie keeps an eye on her and mentions that Penny's face is like a metaphor for the ugliness of the Hornwright family showing up on the outside.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You know Penny Hornwright is in Foundation, right?"''
Maggie Williams: ''"Yeah, I know she's in town. I've been keeping an eye on her. Shame about her face... I guess the Hornwright's ugliness is finally showin' up on the outside."''
([[Maggie Williams/Dialogue|Maggie Williams' dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion =yes |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Trade Secrets]] * [[Invisible Ties]] * [[Division of Wealth]] * [[All That Glitters]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Trade Secrets]]: Penny is found in the safe room under the [[Hornwright Estate]], tasking the residents with recovering several components in order to control the Motherlode. * [[Invisible Ties]]: Penny helps Jen find out the location of her mother's stealth suit. * [[Division of Wealth]]: Penny is kidnapped by [[Hijack]] and his crew of raiders and must be rescued. Afterward, she sends the residents through [[Hornwright Industrial headquarters|the Cave]] in order to recalibrate the Motherlode. * [[All That Glitters]]: The residents help Penny and the Settler heist team raid Vault 79. She eventually becomes concerned for her safety, and the residents can choose to have her stay with the crew or have her return to [[Foundation]]. ===Other interactions=== * If [[Mochou]] returned to Foundation alive, Penny comments she has been catching up with her and that they share a lot in common. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Lab coat (Fallout 76)|Lab coat]]

Like at all.|sound=Samuel 0058eca1_1.ogg}} '''Samuel''' is a member of the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|settlers]] residing in [[Foundation]]. ==Background== Samuel arrived at [[Foundation]] some time in [[Timeline#2103|2103]]. [[Elsie Taylor]] notes he is one of the settlement's newer citizens.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Can you tell me about the others?"''
[[Elsie Taylor]]: ''"Best way to get to know someone is either to fight them or share a meal. I recommend sharing a meal. Samuel is one of our newer citizens. Maybe you can be his friend. He's from a Vault, like you."''
([[W05 Settler ElsieTaylor.txt|Elsie Taylor's dialogue]]) He claims that he is from a [[Vault]] similar to that of the [[Vault 76]] [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|dwellers]]. With liberal vaguenesses, he describes its location as far away and well hidden, insisting that those inquiring would not have heard of it, and that he does not even know how to get back to it; this strongly indicates that he is lying, or at the very least has something to hide.{{Ref|(Note)}}[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How did you end up here?"''
Samuel: ''"I came from a Vault, just like you. {{Tooltip|You've never heard of it. Its{{sic}} really far away. And hidden. Like really hidden. I don't even know how to get to it. Like at all.|He's lying}}"''
([[Samuel (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Samuel's dialogue]]) Samuel claims that he misses living in the Vault, but is likewise glad to be free of some manner of "tests" with which he was involved; other residents of Foundation seem to believe Samuel's claims and call him "dweller."Samuel: ''"The only time I miss being inside the Vault is when the weather's bad ... or if there's a nuke."''
([[Samuel (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Samuel's dialogue]])Settler: ''"Hey, how's it going Samuel?"''
Samuel: ''"You know me, I'm just happy we found this place. Sick of not having a roof over my head."''
Settler: ''"You miss that vault living, dweller?"''
Samuel: ''"Nope, no more tests for me. Just give me chill tunes and a cold Nuka-Cherry, thank you."''
([[Samuel (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Samuel's dialogue]]) The apparel that Samuel wears is from [[Vault-Tec University]], but he never addresses this further. Samuel is light hearted, and enjoys playing [[Nuka Tapper]], although expresses his frustration at losing his saved games.Samuel: ''"Can't believe I lost my Nuka Tapper saves, ugh."''
([[Samuel (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Samuel's dialogue]]) He is also an avid lyricist, though some residents try to avoid being an audience to it.Settler: ''"Hey Samuel."''
Samuel: ''"{{Tooltip|Hey. I'm writing some lyrics for a song, listen to this.... She's long, she's tall. She's got ways, she's got means. Oh oh oh, she's a queen. Oh oh-|Just reading the lyrics like poetry? Or do we do some singing?}}"''
Settler: ''"{{Tooltip|Oh uh, I don't actually have the time to uh, stop and really listen right now. Besides, you should ask Jen or something.|really trying to get out of listening to bad song lyrics}}"''
Samuel: ''"{{Tooltip|Oh hey, yeah man. That makes sense. Take it easy!|Unflappable, doesn't even occur to you that he doesn't want to hear your bad poetry}}"''
([[Settlers (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Settler]] and [[Samuel (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Samuel's dialogue]])Settler: ''"What you been up to, Samuel?"''
Samuel: ''"I got a lot of things in motion right now, you know how it is. Some construction, some scavenging, and got my songwriting of course... How about you?"''
Settler: ''"Oh uh, well I'm supposed to take all of these chems from Doc Aubrie or my gums will start ah... bleeding again. You know."''
Samuel: ''"Oh uh... yikes, man. You do that."''
([[Settlers (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Settler]] and [[Samuel (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Samuel's dialogue]]) Samuel attempts to use regional words such as "yinz," "hoagies" and "jawn," though he expresses confusion with the terms and says he cannot keep up, referring to the different dialects that are found in Foundation's diverse populace.Samuel: ''"Is it yinz... or youse... or y'all? I can't keep up."''
([[Samuel (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Samuel's dialogue]])Samuel: ''"What the heck is a jawn anyway? I just don't get it."''
([[Samuel (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Samuel's dialogue]])Samuel: ''"I could really go for a hoagie ... er, sandwich."''
([[Samuel (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Samuel's dialogue]]) At Foundation, [[Ward (Wastelanders)|Ward]] is still trying to figure out what Samuel is best at; in the meantime, Samuel mostly works on whatever is needed.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What's your job here?"''
Samuel: ''"Little bit of this and a little bit of that. Whatever needs doing. Ward says he's still trying to figure out what I'm best at."''
([[Samuel (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Samuel's dialogue]]) At the moment, though, he is fairly occupied with repairs[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"See you later."''
Samuel: ''"Let me know if you see any repairs I should add to my list. The evergrowing, unending list...."''
([[Samuel (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Samuel's dialogue]]) and scavenging. After the [[Vault 79]] heist, Ward assigns him as Foundation's [[gold bullion]] trader.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What's your job here?"''
Samuel: ''"For a while I was just kicking around doing odd jobs. But Ward gave me an important job. I'm in charge of the gold bullion exchange."''
([[Samuel (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Samuel's dialogue]]) He is also good friends with [[Jen]], who occasionally joins in scavenging hunts.Settler: ''"Hiya Davie, how're you today?"''
[[Davie Taylor]]: ''"Ah, I'm okay. A little bored, though."''
Settler: ''"Did you hear that Jen and Samuel found a bunch of comics on the last scavenger run?"''
[[Davie Taylor]]: ''"Wow, really? I gotta ask Dad if we can trade for some. Thanks!"''
([[Settlers (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Settler]] and [[W05 Settler DavieTaylor.txt‎|Davie Taylor's dialogue]]) He also states that she has a style he can respect.Samuel: ''"Jen's got style that I can respect. You know what I mean?"''
([[Samuel (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Samuel's dialogue]]) It is implied that Samuel has a romantic interest in her,Settler: ''"Hey Samuel."''
Samuel: ''"Hey. I'm writing some lyrics for a song, listen to this... She's long, she's tall. She's got ways, she's got means. Oh oh oh, she's a queen. Oh oh-"''
Settler: ''"Oh uh, I don't actually have the time to uh, stop and really listen right now. Besides, you should ask Jen or something."''
Samuel: ''"Oh hey, yeah man. That makes sense. Take it easy!"''
([[Settlers (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Settler]] and [[Samuel (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Samuel's dialogue]]) though it is never shown whether or not she shares this interest. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |ghost =yes |wares =* [[#Merchandise|See inventory]] * [[Lunchbox (Fallout 76)|Lunchbox]] x3 * [[Perfect bubblegum]] |gold =yes |quests involved =* [[A Refreshing Outlook]] {{cut}} }} ===Other interactions=== After the events of [[Secrets Revealed]], the last quest in the ''Wastelanders'' main questline, Samuel will become available as a merchant, as Ward assigns the gold bullion exchange to him. ===Effects of player's actions=== Despite not participating in the ''Wastelanders'' questline, Samuel has different outcomes involving Jen. * If [[Mochou]] was spared in [[Invisible Ties]], during [[All That Glitters]] Jen will mention she's going to help her mother settle in Foundation, and that she has plans of finding a doctor that can change Mochou's face thanks to a tip from Samuel.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What're you going to do now?"''
[[Jen]]: ''"{{Tooltip|I'm going to help my mom get settled in at Foundation, show her all our decadent consumerist ways.|joking}} Samuel told us about a doctor who can change your face... so we might look at doing that down the road. If they can do it for a ghoul."''
([[Jen/Dialogue|Jen's dialogue]]) * If the player character chooses to kill Mochou, Jen will continue to work with Foundation until All That Glitters, in which she will mention she's going to bury her mother beside her father to the north in the [[Capital Wasteland]], and that Samuel will accompany her. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[VTU T-shirt and jeans]]
[[VTU trucker cap]]
Vault-Tec backpack |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ===Merchant inventory=== Samuel sells rare plans. The availability of merchandise depends on one's reputation with the Foundation Settlers. He only trades in {{icon|gold bullion}}[[gold bullion]]. For his inventory, see "Settlers" and "Both factions" sections [[Fallout_76_reputations#Rewards|here]]. ==Notes== * {{Note|(Note)}} The script notes for the line in which Samuel claims to be from a Vault directly state "He's lying," but this is never further elaborated outside of the one line and script note. * In one line of dialogue, Samuel uses the term "hoagie" before catching himself and correcting his wording to "sandwich." "Hoagie" is the preferred term for a sandwich in both [[Philadelphia]] and [[The Pitt|Pittsburgh]]. In another line, however, Samuel expresses confusion over the term "jawn," which is popularly used in Philadelphia, further contributing to the obfuscation of his true origins. He says that he cannot "keep up" with usage of "yinz" (popularly used in southwestern Pennsylvania including Pittsburgh), "youse" (popular in many areas of the United States including Philadelphia), and "y'all" (popular in the southern United States). ==Appearances== Samuel appears {{In|FO76WL}}. ==Gallery== FO76WL Samuel.png|Samuel FO76WL Foundation Musical Trio.png|[[Derrick Taylor|Derrick]], [[Elsie Taylor|Elsie]] and Samuel playing music ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox vendors FO76}} {{Navbox Foundation}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders bullion merchants]] [[Category:Settler characters]] [[ru:Сэмюэл (Wastelanders)]]

But I've never seen one of them volunteer to go sniffing for mines.|sound=Thompson 00555e5e_1.ogg}} '''Sergeant Thompson''' is a former [[United States Army|U.S. Army]] soldier in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Sergeant Thompson has been fighting under the command of [[Oliver Fields|Captain Oliver Fields]] since the [[Sino-American War]], where she lost three toes to frostbite while her squadmate [[Fred Radcliff|Sergeant Radcliff]] only lost one. Thompson specializes as a military dog handler, and was responsible for training and handling a team of military working dogs.[[The Old Guard, Vol 14: Ch 2]] All three were later part of the original team responsible for moving the gold reserves at [[Fort Knox]] to [[Vault 79]]. However, the Vault closed, and they were left outside when the [[Great War]] struck. For years, they wandered, always staying near [[Appalachia]], deciding to return when they heard it was safe enough to come back.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How did you end up here?"''
[[Oliver Fields]]: ''"Thompson, Radcliff and I were all part of the team at Fort Knox that moved the gold here. The vault shut before we could get in though. We wandered the wasteland, always staying nearby. Once we heard it was safe, we came here. Damn glad we did too."''
([[Oliver Fields/Dialogue|Oliver Fields' dialogue]]) Before reaching Appalachia though, they ended up in [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|the Pitt]] and attempted to save the civilians located there. Captain Fields was wounded, and was only saved because Thompson ordered her dogs [[Angel (Wastelanders)|Angel]] and [[Odysseus]] to defend him. They were able to escape, although Angel lost a front leg in the fighting. Following their failure, the squad considered leaving their military lives behind, but were convinced to keep going after once again hearing the broadcast from [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|military remnants]] in Appalachia, and chose to return "home." During their journey, they ended up following and observing the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] as they undertook the same trip from the Pitt to Appalachia. Once in [[State#West Virginia|West Virginia]], the team all agreed to a meeting with the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] at the [[ransacked bunker]].[[Paige]]: ''"I had to reach out to some... specialists who've been shadowing us since the Pitt. They've all agreed to meet, but they want to talk to you first."''
([[Paige/Dialogue|Paige's dialogue]]) Thompson was responsible for raising and training the squad's military dog, [[Lucky (Wastelanders)|Private Lucky]], ever since he was a puppy, and trained him to accept the clicking sound of a [[Nuka-Cola (Fallout 76)|Nuka-Cola]] [[Cap (Fallout 76)|bottlecap]] as a positive stimulus.Thompson: ''"I don't use treats with Lucky anymore. Whenever I rewarded him as a puppy, I clicked a Nuka-Cola cap. Now I just click the cap and he's happy and fit."''
([[Thompson (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Thompson's dialogue]]) She is also an enthusiastic fan of the [[Mistress of Mystery]], and is eager to talk to others who are in the know.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"I'm the last member of the Order of Mysteries."''
[[Oliver Fields]]: ''"And I'm the King of the moon!"''
Thompson: ''"As in the Mistress of Mysteries? Do you have the Blade of Bastet? The Voice of Set? The Eye of Ra?"''
Oliver Fields: ''"Sergeant, stand down."''
Thompson: ''"Yes, sir. Let's talk later!"''
([[Oliver Fields/Dialogue|Oliver Fields']] and [[Thompson (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Thompson's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved ={{Bull}}[[Duty Calls]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Duty Calls]]: Sergeant Thompson is one of the United States Army soldiers met inside the ransacked bunker. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Army fatigues (Fallout 76)|Army fatigues]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Thompson appears only {{In|FO76WL}}. ==Behind the scenes== Sergeant Thompson, [[Oliver Fields|Captain Oliver Fields]], [[Fred Radcliff|Sergeant Radcliff]], [[Lucky (Wastelanders)|Private Lucky]], [[Odysseus]], and [[Angel (Wastelanders)|Angel]] are all identified as members of [[The Old Guard, Vol 14: Ch 2|The Old Guard]]. Their presence is a nod to the real-world [https://oldguard.mdw.army.mil/specialty-platoons/k9-detachment 947th Military Police Detachment], part of the U.S. Army’s 4th Battalion, 3d U.S. Infantry Regiment, otherwise known as The Old Guard. This unit has the second largest Military Working Dog detachment in the continental United States and works closely with the U.S. Secret Service, identical to their role in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Foundation}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:United States Armed Forces characters]] [[Category:Settler characters]] [[ru:Сержант Томпсон]]

Some day you may wake up and not like what you see in the mirror.|sound=Ward 0042afca_1.ogg}} '''Ward''' is a member of the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] residing in [[Foundation]] {{In|FO76WL}}. ==Background== A reformed raider who joined [[Foundation]] after parting ways with the raiders, Ward initially hid his past from the Settlers, ashamed and afraid of being ostracized. His life changed when he discovered an old self-help manual, ''Be Better Than Your Worst Self'' by [[Bryce Jayhart]]. Although just one volume of 30 (at a pre-War price of $999 per copy), it changed his life for the better.[[Ward's journal]] He revealed his past to the rest of Foundation, risking exile or worse. Instead, they have forgiven him and allowed him to continue his reform. Since then, he has continued practicing the steps outlined by Jayhart, taking a daily inventory of ways he improved over his "yesterday self" and being ever mindful of the ability to improve. He even had "I'm better than this" tattooed in an unobtrusive place. Although he formally answers to [[Paige]], Ward is in charge of the day-to-day operations of Foundation.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What can you tell me about the others?"''
[[Samuel (Wastelanders)|Samuel]]: ''"Ward's in charge out here. Oh, he'll say he ain't, but he is. Of course he reports to Paige for the big stuff. When he points, they all jump. I reckon it's because he always puts Foundation ahead of himself. As for the rest of them, I'm still getting to know everyone."''
([[Samuel (Wastelanders)/Dialogue|Samuel's dialogue]]) He will issue commands to people and many people follow them without question because of his selfless attitude. This is to the extent that people look to Ward for guidance and he may be considered a de facto leader of Foundation along with Paige.[[Fallout 76 loading screens#Location|''Fallout 76 Wastelanders'' loading screens]]: ''"The Settlers at Foundation rely on cooperation and collaboration, but respect the guidance of Paige and Ward, who are the closest the settlement has to leaders."'' When the [[Vault 76]] [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|vault dwellers]] arrive at Foundation, Ward is looking for "vital" equipment that has gone missing and will ask for their help. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started =* [[Vital Equipment]] |quests involved =* [[From Russia With Lev]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Vital Equipment]]: Once a day, Ward asks the player characters to recover a piece of Foundation's equipment that was recently stolen, providing a [[Foundation property tracker|tracking device]] on their [[Pip-Boy 2000 Mark VI]]'s radio to help track it down. Once it is recovered and returned to Foundation, he rewards players for recovering the equipment and is more grateful if they offer to donate their reward to help out Foundation. * [[From Russia With Lev]]: After dealing with [[Lev]] and before reporting to [[Meg Groberg]], the Vault Dweller may do the optional task of speaking to Ward to learn more about [[Rocco]]. Ward will be angry, but will mention that Rocco was exiled from Foundation for sowing discord among the people and ammo and weapons gone missing. Ward will mark the player character's map where Rocco is hiding, at [[Spruce Knob Boat Rental]]. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Cowboy hat (Atomic Shop)|Cowboy hat]]

If they keep coming back, then that's when the guns come out.|sound=Ward 0053c2b8_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Me? Nah. I'm no more in charge than one of the turrets. We'll bring civilization back to this corner of the country.|sound=Derek Garrison 0058fa1f_1.ogg}} '''Derek Garrison''', also known by the nicknames '''AC''' and '''Dirk''', is the leader of the [[Secret Service (Fallout 76)|Secret Service]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Derek is the agent in charge of the operations within [[Vault 79]] (giving him his nickname "AC"). He was put in charge thanks to Secret Service regulations.[[Reginald Stone's journal]] His job is to try to create a new [[currency]] backed in [[Gold bullion|gold]]. According to him, he and his fellow Secret Service members will bring back civilization to the [[East Coast]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you do here?"''
Derek Garrison: ''"Agent in charge. That's why they call me AC. I direct this whole operation. It's my job to try and establish a new, gold backed currency. We'll bring civilization back to this corner of the country."''
([[Derek Garrison/Dialogue#75|Derek Garrison's dialogue]]) Derek recorded a [[First days in Vault 79|holotape]] about being able to hear the bombs drop from within the vault during the [[Great War]]. Derek survived a coup attempt by [[Shorty (Wastelanders)|Shorty]] and spent the time afterward just listening to the radio. When [[Mercedes Stern]] was pregnant with [[Maggie Stern|Maggie]], he threw a baby shower for her.[[Chase Terrier's journal]] However, now he faces a new crisis. The vault's reactor has malfunctioned, turning many of his former subordinates into [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|feral ghouls]] who in turn killed more [[Secret Service agent|agents]]. He and several others managed to lock themselves into a secure, though small and poorly supplied, part of the vault where they await an unlikely rescue.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What happened down here?"''
Derek Garrison: ''"We were doing routine work in this part of the vault when the reactor went. Next thing we knew half our people were turned into monsters trying to kill us. Worse, the fighting activated the security systems and robots. It was either lock ourselves in here or die. That was almost three months ago. We're running out of food and water, so it's a good thing you showed up."''

Aside from the new skin condition that is.|sound=Chase Terrier 0054ee14_1.ogg}} '''Chase "Digger" Terrier''' is a [[Secret Service (Fallout 76)|Secret Service]] agent in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Chase is one of the Secret Service agents trapped in [[Vault 79]]. He is an engineer and tinkerer, as he had attempted to make an automated vacuum cleaner (later made into a scrap heap upon eating [[Derek Garrison]]'s shoes),[[Reginald Stone's journal]] and later made a crib and toys for [[Maggie Stern]] before she was born.[[Chase Terrier's journal]] Although he is not her father, he considers everyone as belonging to her. He survived [[Shorty (Wastelanders)|Shorty]]'s mutiny years prior and was in the vault reactor area when it began to malfunction. Due to the high radiation, he became a [[ghoul]]; though the others he was with died (like [[Grills]] and [[Shiny]]) or turned into [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|feral ghouls]] (like [[Bubba]] and [[Mac (Wastelanders)|Mac]]),Chase Terrier: ''"Bubba, Mac, and a bunch of others all became ghouls, but crazy and bloodthirsty. They attacked Grills and Shiny and the ones that didn't turn. Tore them to pieces before they even knew what was happening."''
([[Chase Terrier/Dialogue#13|Chase Terrier's dialogue]]) he alone managed to survive with his sanity intact and eventually stabilized the reactor.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"We're here to help. AC opened the door for us."''
Chase Terrier: ''"Thank god. I thought I was going to die here. I'm Agent Chase with the Secret Service. Digger to my friends. I was on the reactor team when it malfunctioned. A lot of them ended up looking like me, except their minds are melted too. The ones that didn't change are all dead now. I was able to stabilize the reactor, but it won't come online with the radiation levels this high."''
([[Chase Terrier/Dialogue#109|Chase Terrier's dialogue]]) However, Chase refuses to finish fixing the reactor because he is afraid he could turn feral if he attempts to.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Why haven't you already vented the reactor chamber?"''
Chase Terrier: ''"The radiation made all of them into feral ghouls. If I take any more, it might happen to me too."''
([[Chase Terrier/Dialogue#108|Chase Terrier's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |killable =yes |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Secrets Revealed]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Secrets Revealed]]: Digger has been trapped in the reactor area of the vault since the malfunction. When [[Derek Garrison]] opens the reactor door, Digger explains what must be done to fix the reactor. After venting the radiation, Digger returns to his former colleagues and his fate must be decided - he can be killed or spared by talking with Derek Garrison. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Black suit (Fallout 76)|Dirty black suit]]

We can't take that chance.|sound=Mercedes Stern 0059daf4_1.ogg}} '''Mercedes "Mercy" Stern''' is a [[Secret Service (Fallout 76)|Secret Service]] agent in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Mercedes is one of the Secret Service agents located in [[Vault 79]] who became trapped inside it over a decade ago. She runs security and was a three-time marksman champion.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What are you in charge of?"''
Mercedes Stern: ''"Security. I'm the muscle. I do whatever it takes to keep visitors like you in line. I was a three time marksman champion and held the course record for simulation kills in hostage drills. Never got to actually use in the field before the [[Great War|bombs dropped]]."''
([[Mercedes Stern/Dialogue#109|Mercedes Stern's dialogue]]) In her free time, she practices martial arts.[[Reginald Stone's journal]] After being in the vault for nearly fifteen years, she became pregnant by one of the men. It was not a planned pregnancy according to her [[Mercedes Stern's journal|journal]] in which she was in disbelief and expressed feelings of horror, thinking she and her baby would die in the vault. She was taken care of by [[Cole Carver]] during this time. Although Mercy has not revealed who the father is and none of them claimed the baby, the agents took fatherly roles and decided to help raise [[Maggie Stern|Maggie]] together.[[Chase Terrier's journal]] Mercy is also very protective of her daughter, Maggie, and is willing to put down any potential threats to her safety without a second thought.Mercedes Stern: ''"[[Chase Terrier|Digger]] is a ghoul now. What if he does something to my daughter? We can't take that chance."''
([[Mercedes Stern/Dialogue|Mercedes Stern's dialogue]]) According to Maggie, Mercy taught her how to shoot a gun when she was only four years old. She survived [[Shorty (Wastelanders)|Shorty]]'s mutiny years earlier as well as the more recent reactor malfunction. She and a few other agents as well as her daughter locked themselves in a small part of the vault to protect themselves from [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|feral ghouls]] and rogue security systems. Now, they are running out of supplies and will need rescue.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What happened down here?"''
[[Derek Garrison]]: ''"We were doing routine work in this part of the vault when the reactor went. Next thing we knew half our people were turned into monsters trying to kill us. Worse, the fighting activated the security systems and robots. It was either lock ourselves in here or die. That was almost three months ago. We're running out of food and water, so it's a good thing you showed up."''

Maggie Stern.wikitext:
{{Infobox incomplete|FO76WL}} {{Infobox character |games =FO76, FO76WL |image =FO76 Maggie Stern.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Female |family =[[Mercedes Stern|Mercy]] - mother |affiliation =[[Secret Service (Fallout 76)|Secret Service]] |age =10-11[[Mercedes Stern's journal]] |age verified=yes |role = |location =[[Vault 79]] |quests =[[Secrets Revealed]] |level =50 |derived = |voice type =W05_NPCF_Magdelena
Stern_Child |actor =[[Michaela Dietz]] |dialogue =[[Maggie Stern/Dialogue]] |edid =W05_SecretService_MaggieStern |formid ={{ID|005427a8}} |refid ={{ID|0054EE28}} }} {{Quotation|Mess with me and my mom will fuck you up.|sound=Maggie Stern 00544d1a_1.ogg}} '''Magdalene[[Chase Terrier's journal]] "Maggie" Stern''', called '''Pita''' (Pain in the Ass) by her peers, is an underage [[Secret Service (Fallout 76)|Secret Service]] agent living in [[Vault 79]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Maggie Stern is the daughter of [[Mercedes Stern]]. She was born of an unintentional pregnancy in [[Vault 79]], though Mercedes has opted not to reveal the identity of the father. Instead, the male agents all stepped up to co-father the child, each contributing in their own way to help raise her, using this generosity as a way to come together and cope. Maggie was raised to become a child agent, while also developing a rude attitude, earning her the nickname of "PITA" (short for pain in the ass).[[Reginald Stone]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Agent Stern should never have had a child. That little brat is a pain in the ass. But we just call her PITA for short.|see it as a breach of regulations to have a child}}"'' She claims to have training in shooting firearms and to have her own personal silenced [[10mm pistol (Fallout 76)|10mm pistol]] with a light frame and short barrel, with her mother wanting to give her a calibrated [[.44 pistol (Fallout 76)|.44 pistol]] with a short scope and comfort grip for her birthday.Maggie Stern: ''"Mom says I can get a calibrated .44 with a comfort grip and a short scope for my birthday. I still get to keep my light frame 10mm short barrel with the silencer though."'' Born after [[Shorty (Wastelanders)|Shorty]]'s mutiny, Maggie had not experienced any major conflict until recently when the vault reactor malfunctioned, causing most [[Secret Service agent|agents]] in the vault to either die or become [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|feral ghouls]]. She, her mother and a few other agents managed to lock themselves in part of the vault, though they are running out of supplies and will perish without rescue.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What happened down here?"''
[[Derek Garrison]]: ''"We were doing routine work in this part of the vault when the reactor went. Next thing we knew half our people were turned into monsters trying to kill us. Worse, the fighting activated the security systems and robots. It was either lock ourselves in here or die. That was almost three months ago. We're running out of food and water, so it's a good thing you showed up."'' ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Secrets Revealed]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Secrets Revealed]]: Maggie and others need to be saved by restarting the vault reactor. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Black suit (Fallout 76)|Dirty black suit]]

You aren't the only one with a req for equipment.|sound=Reginald Stone 00543a2b_1.ogg}} '''Reginald "Regs" Stone''' is a member of the [[Secret Service (Fallout 76)|Secret Service]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Reginald was a Secret Service member in [[Vault 79]], although he was never field agent material, like [[Mercedes Stern]] and [[Cole Carver]]; however, he is an accomplished requisition officer, as he is highly strict with rules (his nickname Regs, short for both "Reginald" and "regulations" reflects this).[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"So what's the deal with Regs?"''
[[Cole Carver|Slick]]: ''"His full name is Reginald Stone, but we all call him Regs. He was never field agent material, like Mercy and me. But he's a great requisition guy. Just mind your P's and Q's. He's totally by the books."''
([[Cole Carver/Dialogue#132|Slick's dialogue]]) Even after two years inside [[Vault 79]], Reginald made sure that all the gold was stored and accounted for.[[Reginald Stone's journal, entry 712]] After the failed mutiny of [[Shorty (Wastelanders)|Shorty]], he started reading more often, mostly old manuals.[[Reginald Stone's journal]] He was also the one who helped Mercedes give birth to [[Maggie Stern]].[[Chase Terrier's journal]] However, Reginald now faces a new problem. He and others are trapped in a small, under-supplied area after the vault's reactor malfunctioned, releasing [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|feral ghouls]] and rogue security robots. He now awaits an unlikely rescue.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What happened down here?"''
[[Derek Garrison|AC]]: ''"We were doing routine work in this part of the vault when the reactor went. Next thing we knew half our people were turned into monsters trying to kill us. Worse, the fighting activated the security systems and robots. It was either lock ourselves in here or die. That was almost three months ago. We're running out of food and water, so it's a good thing you showed up."''
