{{ID|00558473}} (male) }} '''Secret Service agents''' are eight deceased members of the [[Secret Service (Fallout 76)|Secret Service]] in [[Vault 79]]. ==Background== These agents were assigned to Vault 79 to protect the [[United States of America|United States]]' gold reserves, which had been moved there from [[Fort Knox]]. At some point, some of the agents became frustrated with being locked inside the vault, a growing group led by [[Shorty (Wastelanders)|Shorty]]. Shorty approached [[Reginald Stone]], expressing his frustration, but Regs dismissed his complaints. Shorty then led a mutiny attempting to replace [[Derek Garrison]] as the agent in charge. It killed several Secret Service agents. More agents were killed when the vault's reactor failed, turning those near the radiation into [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|feral ghouls]], who killed several survivors of the mutiny. [[Chase Terrier]]: ''"Bubba, Mac, and a bunch of others all became ghouls, but crazy and bloodthirsty. They attacked Grills and Shiny and the ones that didn't turn. Tore them to pieces before they even knew what was happening."''
([[Chase Terrier/Dialogue|Chase Terrier's dialogue]]) Eight deceased agents can still be found throughout the vault, in its abandoned areas. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Secret Service underarmor]] or

BOY! [[Pip-Boy 2000 Mark VI|Boy is key!]] BOY. IS. KEY!|sound=Crane 004247fb_1.ogg}} '''Crane''' is a [[Scorched]] kept hidden on the second floor of [[the Wayward]]. ==Background== An adventurer who came to the region seeking the fabled Treasure of Appalachia, Crane had early success when he discovered what he thought was the location of the treasure in [[Gauley Mine]]. Crane managed to partially map its layout, even uncovering a code to access the secure storage of the [[RobCo Auto-Cache 001|RobCo Auto-Cache #001]].[[Crane's map]] Crane was unable to access the treasure, as the cache required a [[Pip-Boy 2000 Mark VI|Pip-Boy 2000]] to register with the pre-[[Great War|War]] computers. While he was in Gauley Mine, Crane also awoke the dormant Scorched deep within and became infected with the [[Scorched Plague]] before he could get the Pip-Boy he needed. He escaped, but the infection had already begun to transform him. When he arrived back at [[the Wayward]], his skin began to change in the night. He sat on the front porch until [[Duchess]] found him mid-transformation. Crane kept himself in control but knew he could not resist the Scorched hive mind for much longer. At his request, Duchess restrained him and locked Crane in the Wayward's second floor storeroom. Here, he would completely succumb to the Scorched Plague and utter only a single phrase over and over again: ''"Boy is key!"'' Duchess would keep Crane's fate secret from everyone else at the Wayward but would have to deal with the fallout of other treasure hunters and opportunists looking for Crane, such as the [[Free Radicals]]. While escaping from Gauley Mine, Crane also inadvertently led the Scorched to the Wayward. [[Polly (Wastelanders)|Polly]] and [[Sol]] attempted to finish them off before the Scorched overran the solitary bar, which in turn led to the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] having to save Polly and Sol and discovering the RobCo Auto-Cache.Events of [[Strength in Numbers]] Duchess would reveal Crane's fate to the Dwellers upon their return, allowing them be the deciding factor on Crane's fate. Whichever the choice was, the Dwellers would be able to access the treasure using [[Crane's map]] and the [[RobCo experimental cache keycard]] he still had on his person.Events of [[The Elusive Crane]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[The Elusive Crane]] }} ===Quests=== [[The Elusive Crane]]: Crane is revealed to have been held in the Wayward's storage closet the entire time. After a conversation with [[Duchess]] and [[Sol]], the player character can either euthanize Crane, let Solomon do it instead, or let Crane live. With any of the outcomes, the player character will either be given or loot [[Crane's map]] and the experimental RobCo key. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Raider pathfinder outfit|Raider pathfinder mask]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =[[Crane's map]]
[[RobCo experimental cache keycard]] }} ==Appearances== Crane appears {{In|FO76WL}}. ==Bugs== {{Platforms|ps4}} Crane may spawn already deceased, causing Duchess to admonish the player character even though they did not kill him.{{Verify|verified}} ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Scorched characters]] [[ru:Крейн]]

{{Infobox character |games =FO76, FO76WL |image =FO76WL_Wayward_Mort.jpg |race =[[Ghoul]] |gender =Male |family = |affiliation = |role =Independent contractor |location =[[The Wayward]] |quests =[[Wayward Souls]]

RAHHH! ...Seriously? Nothing? Shit. I thought it was funny. Overall, though, being a ghoul, mixed bag. Can't say I'd recommend it as a lifestyle choice.|sound=Mordecai McCoy.ogg}} '''Mordecai "Mort" McCoy''' is a bar patron at [[the Wayward]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== On the day of the [[Great War]], Mort survived by hiding in the back of a truck, recalling that was like being in a hurricane. An avid explorer, Mort has visited most locations in [[the Forest]] and has figured out how [[CAMP|C.A.M.P.s]] work. He is a good source of insight on both of those topics. Describing himself as an "independent operator," Mort is often hired whenever people need to go through [[radiation]] to get something. He is a frequent patron of the Wayward and a friend of [[Duchess]], helping her when she needs assistance while racking up his bar tab at the same time. However, because of the help he provides, she grants forgiveness for his tab.[https://fallout.bethesda.net/en/article/66xOu1a7PVALlBVPohGqjL/fallout-76-inside-the-vault-meet-duchess-and-mort Inside the Vault - Meet Duchess and Mort] He also mentions paying a visit to [[WV Lumber Co.]] some time ago to find the place was originally crawling with [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|super mutants]]. After speaking to Duchess about dealing with the [[Free Radicals|group]] that [[Batter]] belongs to, Mort can be spoken with to offer some holotapes on [[CAMP|C.A.M.P.s]] he put together to help out the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]], especially if the player characters are just fresh out of the vault from being created and completing "[[Reclamation Day]]." He also mentions that, due to his ghoul physiology, he's able to head into irradiated areas safely where others like them due to their human physiology would, as he put it, soak up so much radiation that, "they'd be as cooked as a TV dinner." ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |ghoul =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Wayward Souls]] * [[Hunter for Hire]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Wayward Souls]]: Mort is first seen upon entering the Wayward for the first time, hiding while [[Batter]] holds [[Duchess]] at gunpoint, demanding information on someone named [[Crane (Wastelanders)|Crane]]. Even if the player character intervenes and tries to talk Batter down, most SPECIAL-enhanced conversation choices result in Batter still being shot and killed by Mort, or in a joint effort by Mort and the player characters. * [[Hunter for Hire]]: Mort offers a few alternatives to dealing with the [[Free Radicals]]; namely by seeking out others at [[Anchor farm]] and the [[Tyler County Fairgrounds]] for help and information. ===Other interactions=== * If one chose to join the Free Radicals during Hunter for Hire, Mort can later be found being restrained and on his knees by the Free Radicals upon returning to the Wayward near the conclusion of [[The Elusive Crane]]. If [[Roper]] and his crew are convinced to depart in peace without further conflict, Mort will be released and return to his usual stool at the counter now that Roper and the Free Radicals have been pacified and won't disturb the Wayward again. * If [[Polly (Wastelanders)|Polly]] was given a body she was unhappy with, this will unlock a possible variant of a random conversation in which Mort asks about her new body and she thanks him for saying it is not that bad. * After the completion of [[Secrets Revealed]], Mort will express annoyance that the treasure of Appalachia is "useless" [[gold bullion]] and not a more immediately useful resource.Mordecai McCoy: ''"Did you hear? Someone found the damn treasure and it turns out to be... gold! How useless is that?! A cave full of snack cakes would be more productive! Eh, someone else's problem. What's going on?"''
([[Mort/Dialogue#24|Mordecai McCoy's dialogue]]) ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Black vest and slacks (Wastelanders)|Black vest and slacks]] (non-lootable) |weapon =[[10mm pistol (Fallout 76)|10mm pistol]] |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== * Mort was the first ghoul character shown in ''Wastelanders'' previews. * Mort is one of the few ghouls in the ''Fallout '' series to have a full head of hair. * Mort may not always be in the Wayward. Changing servers can spawn him inside. * Mort can be seen crouch-walking away from the bar area to get behind Batter. If players linger in the entrance area for even a little, they will miss it. * A random conversation may occur between Duchess and Mort in which they discuss [[The Giant Teapot]] and Duchess' grandmother. Another conversation may occur between Sol and Mort where they mention [[Jide]]. ==Related holotapes== *[[Mort's edu-tape 01: Placing your C.A.M.P.]] *[[Mort's edu-tape 02: Building at your C.A.M.P.]] *[[Mort's edu-tape 03: Powering your C.A.M.P.]] *[[Mort's edu-tape 04: Mutations!]] ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|Glad to hear Vault-Tec actually took care of some of their people.|sound=Mort 00572db6_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Allergies. Learned the hard way I can't stand within 10 feet of a strawberry. Heh, come on man, that's a joke. Truth is, I was outside on doomsday. Now you see, I drove security and I was coming back from a pick-up in the truck, when I feel this rumble, quiet... then a whole lot less quiet. The truck is hit with this wind. And there was like someone dropped a hurricane on it. I can hear it, battering the truck. Bang! Bang! Bang! Like it's got a grudge against it. And then I unlock the door into the back and then... Bang, I wake up, man, and it's crazy. Somehow in the back of the truck. Alive and kicking. All it cost me was my skin and any opportunity for someone liking me for anything other than my lovely personality. That was the day I became, well, they call us Ghouls. Not the most flattering name but still, beats being vaporized.|sound=Mort 0040f641_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|For real, Duchess? A nurse? Like little white hat and candy stripes?|sound=Mort 0042a950_1.ogg}} ==Appearances== Mort appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]'', introduced in the ''[[Wastelanders]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. ==Behind the scenes== * Mort is voiced by [[Jason Mewes]], who is best known for the role of Jay in the duo of [[wikipedia:Jay and Silent Bob|Jay and Silent Bob]], characters that often appear in the works of [[wikipedia:Kevin Smith|Kevin Smith]], who plays Silent Bob. ** Before the release of ''Wastelanders'', Mewes voicing Mort was confirmed on stage during a preview of the update at Bethesda Game Days 2020.[https://youtu.be/pV9d5OS8IzM?feature=shared&t=715 Bethesda Game Days 2020: Fallout 76: Wastelanders Preview (11:55)] * In localized versions of the game, Mort's voice is dubbed by Benjamin Penamaria (French). ==Gallery== Fo76_Mort.jpg|Mort sitting at the bar inside [[The Wayward]] FO76WL Mort.jpg|Mort in Wastelanders promotional material FO76WL Mort hostage.png|Mort being held hostage by the Free Radicals ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders ghoul characters]] [[ru:Мордекай МакКой]]

Here.|Polly if she has been given an Assaultron body|sound=Polly 0042d24d 1.ogg}} '''Polly''' is an [[Assaultron (Fallout 76)|Assaultron]] working for [[Duchess]]. ==Background== Polly was Duchess' robot, which she used as protection to prevent assaults and robberies at [[The Wayward]], in addition to using her as a servant and assistant. According to Duchess, her personality was based on a boxer who was an ex-girlfriend of her programmer; [[Sol]] instead believes her personality was modeled after Duchess herself. [[Sol]], a friend of Duchess, managed to convince her that Polly was "a lot more than that," seeing "a real lady" in the robot. While searching for Crane's treasure in [[Gauley Mine]], Sol and Polly were overwhelmed by [[Scorched]], and Sol took a bullet to the leg. Seeing him go down, Polly went berserk on the [[Scorched]], but ended up losing her [[Polly's old head|head]], disconnected from her Assaultron body. When the player character discovers Polly, her head must be picked up to clear the cave of the [[Scorched]] and return to The Wayward. When they are back at The Wayward, Polly's head is placed in a [[moonshine jug]], as the player character goes to [[Duncan & Duncan Robotics]] in [[Summersville]] to attach a transmitter to a pristine robot which will become her new body. The body can be either an Assaultron body, a [[Mister Handy (Fallout 76)|Mister Handy]] body, or a [[Protectron (Fallout 76)|Protectron]] body. Afterwards, the body is retrieved by Sol and Duchess, and Polly can be seen in the reception area of the bar after it formally opens with the body the player character has chosen. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =Yes |temp companion =Yes |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Strength in Numbers]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Strength in Numbers]]: Polly and Sol must be rescued from Gauley Mine. Darkly we stride, tall and powerful, through this tunnel of death.|sound=Aries 00581ecf_1.ogg}} '''Aries''', formerly known as '''Calvin "Cal" van Lowe''', is an employee of the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] at [[Big Bend Tunnel]]. Before adopting a new identity as Aries and finding Blue Ridge, Calvin was a [[Cryptids|cryptid]] hunter, inventor, and engineer working for the [[Bysshe Company]] prior to the [[Great War]]. He currently resides in a decorated train car in front of [[Big Bend Tunnel east]]. He is a major supporting character {{in|FO76}}. ==Background== ===Early life=== Calvin van Lowe was born around the 2050s. He grew up in [[Lewisburg]], West Virginia, where his parents ran [[Van Lowe Taxidermy]]. His childhood was defined by small town America and the shop. The siblings inherited the shop in the wake of their parents' passing. [[Shelley van Lowe|Shelley]], inherited the family business, though Calvin still maintained a residence and office in the building.[[Life with Calvin]] Growing up, he became fearful about the idea of dying, particularly about him being forgotten, dying alone and having no friend to read his eulogy. His fear of death became a driving force - and also led him to adopt a backup plan, to record a series of [[Protocol Adonais (holotapes)|holotapes]] to be his legacy.[[Protocol Adonais (holotapes)]][[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"'Protocol Adonais' -- what does that even mean?"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|Spent my entire life before the bombs being afraid of dying. Had me doing stuff that, even today, I'm not proud of.|Sincere, but kind of nonchalant}} {{Tooltip|I pushed everyone away. Except the fear. That never left. All alone, except for me... and the fear.|Sincere}} {{Tooltip|The most frightening thought was dying alone, forgotten. No friend to read my eulogy.|Growing dark, glum}} {{Tooltip|So, I made a plan: if the moment came, I'd record one myself. It... ended up going on a little longer than expected.|Perking up, then finally joking around again}} {{Tooltip|In the end, I guess it's just a journal of my thoughts... and instead of proving my death, it's proof I'm still alive.|Nostalgic, sincere}} {{Tooltip|Cool name, though, right?|And it's gone again}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) His sister considered him as always being "the odd sort," but highly intelligent. In adolescence, he developed an obsession with cryptids, and later on co-founded a club with his friends [[Scott Conroy|Scott "Scoot" Conroy]] and [[Ray Gary]]: the [[Truth Seekers]], devoted to hunting cryptids spotted in West Virginia.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Truth Seekers Meeting Archive|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, Truth Seekers Meeting Archive]] However, the group disbanded after Calvin enrolled in [[Vault-Tec University]] in August [[Timeline#2072|2072]],[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#07/29/2072|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, 07/29/2072]] though his interest in cryptids never disappeared and he continued his search for the [[Sheepsquatch]], with which he had a particular fascination.[[Note to self (Wild Appalachia)|Note to self]] He was a frequent buyer at [[Priblos' Curios]], a small store dedicated to selling cryptid merchandise, and was a friend of the owner [[Raymond Priblo]].[[Letter to Calvin requested]] He is said to have nearly bought the store's stock.[[Raymond's pep talk]] Soon after graduation, he found work at a major out-of-state energy corporation, the [[Bysshe Company]]. While his mental acuity and cognitive skills were rated extremely high by professional psychologists at the company, they also observed that he suffered from a [[wikipedia:Dissociation (psychology)|dissociative]] view of the social world and had limited ability to contextualize stimuli. He was also reported as experiencing frequent mood swings, indicative of non-functional interpersonal relationships and attachments to the contextualized world around him.[[Blacksheep dossier]] ===Bysshe Blacksheep=== [[file:FO76 Van Lowe Taxidermy (board).jpg|left|thumb|200px|Calvin's conspiracy board.]] In [[Timeline#2077|2077]], Calvin returned to [[Lewisburg]]. Instead of the controlled self his sister remembered from before his departure to Morgantown, he appeared to be the old, tormented Calvin again: going out in the middle of the night and locking himself away all day. He moved back into [[Van Lowe Taxidermy]], where he and Shelley shared a residence.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Receipt: 10/7/2077|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, Receipt: 10/7/2077]][[Life with Calvin]] His sister had doubts about whether Calvin was truly employed by Bysshe, or if he had just relapsed into his old habits. Calvin did in fact remain a Bysshe employee, though he was engaged in a far more sinister scheme. As "Blacksheep,"[[Calvin's security code]] working under [[Bo-Peep]] as handler, with [[Big Bad Wolf]] providing security, he was part of Operation Mary's Little Lamb: a corporate initiative to stage Sheepsquatch sightings around Lewisburg in order to drive property values down and allow the company to move in and buy up the devalued property. This way, the Bysshe Company could utilize Lewisburg to access a natural gas deposit underneath the town.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"The Sheepsquatch Imposter... Bysshe... What's the truth behind it all?"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|Okay... Fine. All these secrets are getting heavy to lug around all day.|Friendly}} {{Tooltip|Bysshe wanted Lewisburg for some natural gas deposit under it or something. I, a loyal and brilliant employee of theirs, happen to come from there.|Sincere, but a little spite}} Since I'd sold my soul to the man already, it wasn't far beyond me to comply. Even if a little maliciously. {{Tooltip|What started as an attempt to utilize a local legend to scare people off, spiraled into me falling into my old ways.|Getting a little glum near the end.}} {{Tooltip|Obsession. Fear. Paranoia. Became so obsessed with finding the real Sheepsquatch that I made some... unfortunate miscalculations...|Getting a bit grim}} {{Tooltip|Many years and multiple spit-roasted Sheepsquatches later, I emerged the man you see today. Unafraid and no longer alone.|Playful again}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) As a local to Lewisburg, Bo-Peep was enthusiastic about Calvin and pushed for the project, arranging for funds and necessary technology.[[Bo-Peep's note on Calvin]] While staying at his sister's home, Calvin sold the title to the taxidermy store to Bysshe, behind Shelley's back,[[Property deed]] ensuring that they could build a sophisticated robotics lab into the foundations of the store in secret. The construction was rapid, finishing by September 27, 2077, and attracting only minor noise complaints from the neighbors.[[Noise complaint]] Calvin focused on the project, planning to use a disguised [[Assaultron (Fallout 76)|Assaultron]] to stage a series of sightings on the western side of Lewisburg.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Check-in #1|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; assembly platform, Check-in #1]] He had moved into Van Lowe's Taxidermy to avoid raising his sister's suspicion, but the project started waking up old demons and feeding his obsession with the cryptids again - so much that he recorded a holotape to remind himself that the Sheepsquatch was not real. Another complication was that the technology provided by Bysshe was not up to snuff. The first Assaultron was impossible to keep running, much less able to accommodate the custom routines necessary for the project. Calvin requested an upgraded robot from Bysshe,[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Check-in #2|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; assembly platform, Check-in #2]] which provided a superior replacement that Calvin found perfect for his purposes. However, the sightings did not generate the public attention Calvin hoped for, causing him to resolve to be more "aggressive."[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Check-in #3|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; assembly platform, Check-in #3]] Though corporate fixer Big Bad Wolf remained skeptical of Calvin's projects, he continued to support the operations, as the company wanted any return on the investments made thus far. The lack of progress and demand for results compounded, leading to Calvin missing his scheduled check-in and receiving his first (and only) warning.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Check-in #4|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; assembly platform, Check-in #4]] Calvin was reminded of what the consequences were: a second failure to check-in would result in the whole project being scrapped and the Wolf cleaning up all traces of Bysshe's involvement. Frustrated by the threats, he resolved to make the Assaultron into a proper [[imposter Sheepsquatch]] for extra authenticity.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Check-in #5|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; assembly platform, Check-in #5]] However, the damage was done and even Bo-Peep, once his advocate at Bysshe, became concerned, especially after Wolf showed Calvin's psychiatric evaluation to her. She resolved to see the job through, believing that Calvin's new approach was pure science, rather than social engineering. Calvin failed at the latter, but the former was playing to his strengths. Wolf arranged a meeting to receive a report in person, unaware that Calvin was about to make a grave mistake.[[Wolf's letter to Bo-Peep]] [[file:FO76WA Van Lowe Taxidermy secret lab far.png|right|thumb|200px|Calvin's workshop and site of the accident.]] The new approach required Calvin to make modifications to the Assaultron's core behavioral subroutines. Around October 18, 2077, Calvin started the process: skipping through the manual and hastily signing liability waivers, Calvin inserted a holotape with the sheepsquatch behavior into the console, uploading it to the Assaultron. He then set the parameters for "sheepsquatch mating rituals," in an attempt to hasten finding the actual creature. However, the Assaultron identified the request as conflicting with the company's HR guidelines and promptly filed a report. Calvin reacted instantly, trying to execute an administrative override and preventing the company from being notified. Rather than override, the Assaultron understood the command as over''write'' and asked for confirmation. Calvin confirmed the request, realizing too late that he was replacing the original Assaultron programming, overwriting it completely with the sheepsquatch personality. The robot mauled Calvin, before escaping the shop into Appalachia.[[Behavioral reprogramming]] Its first steps led to [[Bastion Park]], where Bo-Peep met a grisly end, vaporized by the Assaultron's head laser.[[Crime scene notes]] Calvin survived, barely, with a damaged face, unable to walk, and with internal bleeding. His emergency stash of medical supplies saved his life, barely, and he started recording his legacy holotapes, Protocol Adonais.[[Protocol_Adonais_(holotapes)#Protocol_Adonais_#1|Protocol Adonais #1]] Unfortunately, he missed his second check-in, leading to the Big Bad Wolf starting the clean-up. By the time Wolf arrived at the taxidermy shop, Calvin was gone,[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#!!! - EMERGENCY CHECK-IN - !!!|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; assembly platform, !!! - EMERGENCY CHECK-IN - !!!]] after he unsuccessfully tried to secure medical aid through Bysshe's network, only to be rejected.[[Harpers Ferry tunnel terminal entries#Terminal|Harpers Ferry tunnel terminal entries; terminal]] Rather than hunt him down, Wolf focused on recapturing the loose Imposter Sheepsquatch.[[Pylon ambush site terminal entries#Note: Capture Procedure|Pylon ambush site terminal entries; Bysshe remote robotics terminal, Note: Capture Procedure]] Shelley van Lowe, completely unaware of Calvin's work with Bysshe, filed a missing persons report. Any attempt at finding him was cut short by the Great War.[[Wanted: Sheepsquatch]] ===Aftermath=== Calvin survived, barely, hiding in [[Uncanny Caverns]]. He greeted the nuclear holocaust of the [[Great War]] with a recitation of Adonais by Percy Bysshe Shelley, before emerging into post-nuclear Appalachia.[[Protocol_Adonais_(holotapes)#Protocol_Adonais_#2|Protocol Adonais #2]] After the bombs settled, Shelley began circulating [[Sheepsquatch ate my brother!|posters]] around Appalachia, hoping that someone would be able to bring her some closure with regards to what happened to her brother.[[Wanted: Sheepsquatch]] Eventually, she gave up and moved on, settling in [[Kentucky]]. She left Calvin a note in case he ever returned.[[Discarded letter]][[Libby Wen]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Is there no one else from your family that can run shipments for you, Carver?|Hesitant to bring it up}}"''
[[Carver Timmerman]]: ''"Well my mom used to do this before she got sick. And I guess Shelley could, but then we'd be down a trapper. {{Tooltip|Why do you ask? I'm not very good at this, am I?|Feels bad}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman]] and [[Libby Wen/Dialogue|Libby Wen's dialogue]]) Calvin had other priorities, however. Although the wounds were slowly healing, he was in constant pain, pushing through the pain to talk. He moved north, to [[Welch]], to try and find his old friend and fellow Truth Seeker [[Ray Gary]]. He found him on the upper floor of Gary's home, badly injured in a wheelchair and lamenting his wife, [[Laura (Wild Appalachia)|Laura]], having not returned from a scavenging trip. Slipping in and out of lucidity, Ray realized who Calvin was, happy to see his friend again after the bombs. Although he did not explicitly name the Sheepsquatch, Ray said that "it" was real and had been what injured him. Calvin responded with a solemn "I know." Unable to make Ray realize that Laura was gone, Calvin left Ray a bottle of [[Whiskey (Fallout 76)|whiskey]] and departed.[[Welch terminal entries#Laura's gone, day 12|Welch terminal entries; terminal, Laura's gone, day 12]][[Welch terminal entries#Laura's gone, day 16|Welch terminal entries; terminal, Laura's gone, day 16]] Adopting a new name, Aries, Calvin left Appalachia, moving to [[Kentucky]] and starting work for an outfit known as the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]]. As a caravan guard, he was initially only assigned to the company's routes within Kentucky, but Aries returned to Appalachia around [[Timeline#2103|2103]], as Blue Ridge expanded operations into the area, now safe from the [[Scorched Plague]]. Aries developed a chipper, trickster-like persona over the decades since the Great War, in a complete change from the previous gloomy, brooding engineer he once was. The return to his home region certainly played a role, with Aries indulging in his penchant for drama to the point that it astonished even [[Eugenie]], who had known Aries since he started work in Kentucky.[[Protocol_Adonais_(holotapes)#Protocol_Adonais_#4|Protocol Adonais #4]] He still has an interest in all things cryptic, bizarre, and generally strange, though he keeps his obsessions under wraps with a healthy dose of humor.Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|Well, looks like the Truthseeker's Club of Lewisburg took on some new members.|Impressed}} {{Tooltip|The real question isn't what it was, it's how many more are out there?|Thinkaboutit}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) His encyclopedic knowledge of these topics makes him an odd, but welcome addition to the team, while his insistence on wearing a mask all the time has led to good-natured ribbing. [[Herschel Klein]] jokingly theorizes that Aries is actually an alien stuck on earth, forced to make caravan runs to make ends meet.[[Herschel Klein]]: ''"{{Tooltip|You know that guard we got, Aries? He's got an encyclopedic knowledge of everything strange: cryptids, aliens, killer robots.|Telling a secret, but he's full of BS}} {{Tooltip|I've been working on a theory: he IS an alien. His spaceship was destroyed when the bombs fell, and now he's stuck working for us just to get by.|All BS}} {{Tooltip|Poor guy. Must miss his home planet something awful.|Sympathetic}}"''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue#36|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) In reality, Aries is neither an alien nor a ghoul, simply a scarred human. The mask is necessary to keep his injuries stable and help him breathe, as having his face "ripped off" left long-term damage he was unable to fix.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What's with the mask?"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|Oh just a little something to help me breathe... and to keep my jaw attached.|Nonchalant}} {{Tooltip|You know what they say: play with fire, get burned. Play with killer robots, get your face ripped off.|It's a real saying, promise}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) The mask stabilizes his injuries and facilitates breathing, allowing him to work as a caravan guard like any other fighter.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"If you don't mind me asking, what happened to you?"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|You mean the voice? The mask? It's not so much what, but who. And, uh, I think you've already been acquainted. It's my special reward for standing between a robot and love... Love that, uh, some one may have programmed it to seek out.|Coy}} {{Tooltip|I do not recall that programming requiring ripping the face off of any human in its path. Or hunting down Bysshe employees for that matter...|Suddenly realizing something}} {{Tooltip|But... Isn't mother nature amazing?|And it's gone}} {{Tooltip|It never hurts to ask. But the reason I'm wearing the mask did. A lot. Can't breathe without this thing now.|Snarky}} {{Tooltip|If you ever think 'hey, I'm going to try and play God today.' Don't. Trust me.|Nonchalant}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) Years of difficulty breathing due to blood caked up in his throat became manageable, with the added bonus of becoming unrecognizable to any Bysshe robots (the encounter left him with a deep fear of killer robots)[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Wait, a killer robot?"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|What!? Where!?|Slight panic}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) or former employees. Aries struggled the most with his legacy, in particular since his sister worked for the same caravan company he joined. It was a reason for him to stay, but he still struggled to figure out whether he should fade into obscurity or reveal himself to his family.Aries: "''For years, I could barely breathe through the blood caked up in my throat. But little by little I found my footing again. Even back then, there all sorts of shit you could get mixed up in. Mistakes you made weren't just wiped clean when the bombs fell. So, I searched, and searched, until I didn't. That life ended with this caravan route. Found something here that gave me a reason to stay."''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) '''Note:''' This line is heard during [[Riding Shotgun|Event: Riding Shotgun]]. ===Aiding the Brotherhood=== {{Quotation|Hello there, brave and venerable Knight Errant of the kingdom of Atlas, the fraternity of technology, the-- (sigh) Hey.|Aries to a Vault 76 dweller who joined the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force]]}} Aries' return to Appalachia was a way to resolve his internal stalemate, while making a positive impact on the world. Aries believes that positive change occurs despite the world's resistance to it, and that effort makes a difference - no matter how difficult it is at first.Aries: ''"This world resists the positive changes we try to bring to it, but ever so slowly, our efforts make a difference."''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) While Blue Ridge was busy blazing a trail into Appalachia through [[Big Bend Tunnel]], Aries got the opportunity to provide more substantial aid. While he was technically just a caravan guard,[[Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries#Staff and Clients for Appalachia|Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries; terminal, Staff and Clients for Appalachia]] his Bysshe credentials and knowledge were instrumental when [[Leila Rahmani|Paladin Leila Rahmani]] of the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force]] investigated a string of wastelander disappearances. Aries was crucial in navigating the [[Harpers Ferry tunnel]] where the disappearances occurred, which also happened to be used by Blue Ridge as a potentially safer alternative to other routes into Appalachia. Blue Ridge ceased using the tunnel, however, after a full caravan of about 15 people went missing en route, which alerted the Brotherhood.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What can you tell me about this train tunnel?"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|The train tunnel itself isn't so important, but underneath is a top-secret gas pipeline running all the way out of the region.|Almost excited by the secret tunnel}} {{Tooltip|It's a pretty discrete route. Safe too, comparatively. Cept, uh, the most recent trip.|Kind of proud of himself, then realizing its insensitive}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]])[[Caravan manifest]]Events of the quest [[Out of the Blue]]. [[file:FO76SR Aries poster.png|right|thumb|200px|"''There's a trick to getting in. Gimme one shake of a Lambsquatch's tail to get it open. Let's see... Thirty days past September... Carry the two..''"]] Paladin Rahmani suspected Blue Ridge of foul play, which was not helped by Aries' and [[Joanna Mayfield]]'s reluctance to explain their role with the tunnel. Aries was a prime suspect, as he was involved in travel through the Harpers Ferry tunnel until it was sealed up. Eventually, Joanna agreed to provide aid and ordered Aries to return to the tunnel with the Brotherhood and investigate it.[[Joanna Mayfield]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Harpers Ferry. The train tunnel. Mind showing our guests the route?|To the point}}"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|Oh crap. You really want to go back there?|He knows he will have to, but complaining anyway}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries]] and [[Joanna Mayfield/Dialogue#316|Joanna Mayfield's dialogue]]) The "crime scene" was sealed up thanks to Aries himself, who set off a bogus gas leak to seal the tunnel off.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Okay, but what's the bad news?"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|The bad news is that I can't unseal that door.|Response to question: What's the bad news then?}} Here's the quick version: clever little me locked that door by setting off a bogus gas leak alarm. {{Tooltip|But... It looks like in order to lift the lock-down, you need to verify there's actually no gas leak. The door is real picky like that.|Maybe it was a bad idea...}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) Although he never worked at the Harpers Ferry tunnel specifically before the Great War, Aries' knowledge of Bysshe procedures and technology[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How do you know so much about this place?"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|Er... In a past life I used to work with these pencil pushing sociopaths in suits.|Doesn't REALLY want to talk about this}} {{Tooltip|Well, not at this facility, but I was in-the-know about their various nefarious dealings in the region.|Trying to wrap it up quick}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) allowed the group to unseal the tunnel (albeit with some difficulty) and survive attacks by [[strangler]]-infested [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|feral ghouls]], granting them access to the deepest reaches of the infrastructure secretly built by Bysshe to ship natural gas out of the region unnoticed. Rahmani's suspicion of Aries only grew the deeper they went, spurred on by Aries' eccentric antics, coupled with Bysshe's arcane security measuresAries: ''"{{Tooltip|There's a trick to getting in. Gimme one shake of a Lambsquatch's tail to get it open.|Nonchalant}} {{Tooltip|Let's see... Thirty days past September... Carry the two...|Examining a calendar}}"''
[[Leila Rahmani|Paladin Rahmani]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Is this for real?|Lost patience (witnessing Aries hammer the wall to open a door)}}"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|And viola! It's just a little further ahead. Please, after you.|Intentionally says viola instead of voila.}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries]] and [[Leila Rahmani/Dialogue|Leila Rahmani's dialogue]])[[Command parameters]] and a [[Imposter Sheepsquatch|Sheepsquatch-mimicking Assaultron]] lurking in the tunnel. The latter in particular caused Aries' old demons to briefly resurface. Rahmani almost lashed out at Aries, suspecting an elaborate cover-up on part of Blue Ridge,Aries: ''"Your boss looks like she's about to strangle me with one of those vines. Something happen in there?"''
[[Leila Rahmani|Paladin Rahmani]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Aries, between the Feral Ghouls, the strangler vines and that insane sheep robot, I've about reached my limit with this place... and your antics.|Pretty pissed}} I don't know if this is some kind of trap, or elaborate cover-up, but we need to get through that door and get answers. Now."''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|Whoa, whoa, trap? Where's this coming from? Hold on, did you say "sheep robot"? Like the baa-baa kind, or the killer robot kind?|Initially taken aback, then only cares about the sheep robot. This REALLY interests him.}}"''
Paladin Rahmani: ''"{{Tooltip|Aries. The door. Now. Please.|Pretty pissed}}"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|Okay, just give me a second. Yeesh.|Offended, sarcastic}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries]] and [[Leila Rahmani/Dialogue|Leila Rahmani's dialogue]]) though she relented when Aries finally led them to the caravan stop. Rahmani and her aide located enough intel to implicate [[Edgar Blackburn]] and [[Hellcat Company]] as major suspects, simultaneously clearing Blue Ridge's name. The Paladin apologized to Aries for jumping to conclusions, though she ruled out sharing [[Hellstorm missile launcher|Hellstorm launchers]] with him as compensation.Paladin Rahmani: "''{{tooltip|Aries... I owe you an apology.|Hesitation}} My rash behavior was unfitting of my position, and frankly, unfair to you."''
Aries: "''{{tooltip|Eh, water under the bridge. All of my best friendships start with misplaced suspicion of mass kidnapping.|Nonchalant}}"''
Paladin Rahmani: "''{{tooltip|I will... take your word for it. I am sorry, either way.|Trying very hard to be nice}}"''
Aries: "''{{tooltip|If you really want to make it up to me, I've heard you guys have some killer rocket launchers to spare.|worth a shot}}"''
Paladin Rahmani: "''{{tooltip|Absolutely not.|Shutting it down.}}"''
 ===Adonais=== Having contributed to saving Appalachia, Aries returned to making caravan runs with Blue Ridge and trying to decide his legacy. The first step was recovering his old [[Protocol Adonais (holotapes)|Adonais holotapes]], tracking the major events in his life from the mauling by the impostor sheepsquatch to the present day. The tapes were lost all over Appalachia in his travels, and he elected to hire the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dwellers]] to help recover them.Aries: "''{{tooltip|There's this thing I started... It's called... (ahem)... Protocol Adonais.|Unsure at first, buying in at the end. Ado-nay-is (similar to Adonis)}} {{tooltip|Hold for suspenseful stinger...|He actually says this out loud. Not a script note.}} {{tooltip|There's a series of Holotapes that were recorded over time as a part of this protocol. I need to retrieve them so I can finalize the process.|Straight forward}} I'll give you the coordinates to the most recent one. You should be able to track them down in reverse order from there."''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) He had caps to pay for the recovery, but he did not have the time to do it himself.Vault 76 dweller: "''And you'll be funding this adventure, right?"''
Aries: "''Yeah, yeah. Travel expenses will be reimbursed. Just hold off on the mini-bar, keep your receipts."''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) The complete set of holotapes made it clear to the dwellers who he originally was ("food for the sheepsquatch," "felled at the hands of his own creation," as he says), and made Aries trust them. With everything they had experienced together, Aries chose to let them decide what his own legacy would be. In an unusually serious turn of events, Aries requested them to decide whether he should reunite with his family, or fade into obscurity.Aries: "''{{tooltip|I am-- or was-- Calvin van Lowe, supposed food for the Sheepsquatch, fool who was felled at the hands of his own creation.|Playing it up a bit}} {{tooltip|But figuring that out isn't the reason I sent you on this grand tour. There's one more tape-- and I have it here.|Serious again}} {{tooltip|Take it. Either burn it, or give it to one of the merchants here named Carver Timmerman. I want the decision left to fate. But you'll have to do.|Somewhat serious}} {{tooltip|You can listen, if you want to know why. Or just burn them and be done with it. Up to you. I've sat on this for too long, time for this coin to land.|A bit painful to say}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) Aries realized it was a difficult burden to bear,Vault 76 dweller: "''This is too much responsibility, Aries."''
Aries: "''{{tooltip|I... know. You're right. But that's the job. Caps in exchange for deciding my legacy. Sounds fair to me.|Sympathetic at first, hardening up}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) but he was unable to decide, despite spending years thinking on the issue. Aries attributed his indecision to being a "wild card," but would abide by any decision made by the dwellers.Vault 76 dweller: "''If you went through the trouble of recording this, you've already decided."''
Aries: "''{{tooltip|You'd think that right? Well I'm a wild card, pal. You know that.|Almost playful}} {{tooltip|Give 'em away or burn 'em. I'll still sleep easy either way. It's the indecision I'm stuck on.|Sincere}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) More specifically, Aries was conflicted on whether or not he should reveal his true identity to [[Carver Timmerman]]. Unbeknownst to Carver, Aries is his step-uncle. Shelley van Lowe, Aries' sister, had married [[Deborah Timmerman]] after the Great War. Shelley and Deborah raised Carver together after his father, [[Gregory Timmerman]], was presumed dead (having perished in [[the Burning Mine]]).Events of the quest [[Costa Business: Carver]].[[Protocol Adonais (holotapes)|Protocol Adonais #6]] Carver had heard stories of his "Uncle Calvin" from Shelley, but did not know that he was alive. If Carver is shown the holotape [[Protocol Adonais (holotapes)|Protocol Adonais #6]], he is shocked to discover his familial connection to Aries. Although he is excited to know that his Uncle Calvin is alive, he finds that difficult to balance having already known Aries, and being slightly freaked out by his eccentricities. However, Carver knows that Aries has a good heart and will continue to keep him safe on the caravan routes.[[Carver Timmerman]]: "''{{tooltip|It's so hard to wrap my head around. I've always wondered about my uncle Calvin... and it's really exciting to know he's alive.|Unsure, mixed confusion and hope}} {{tooltip|But, I'd be lying if I said that Aries didn't kind of... freak me out.|Deflating}}"''
Vault 76 dweller: "''I think we all feel that way. But he's a good guy."''
Carver Timmerman: "''{{tooltip|Oh, I know he's got a good heart. He always goes out of his way to keep me safe...|Sincere}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries]]' and [[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) Aries says he will also continue to spend time with Carver, as he is a good kid, and the time they spend together is rewarding. He does not have the courage yet to face Shelley himself, though he will leave a letter with Carver to deliver to her.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How are things with your family?"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|I don't have the courage to face Shelley in person just yet... But I did leave a letter with Carver.|Slight shame}} {{Tooltip|Next time he heads back, I asked him to deliver it to her... He's a good kid. Spending time with him has been... pretty fulfilling, actually.|Still a bit shy}} {{Tooltip|He's more of a fainting lamb than a Sheepsquatch, and that's all right by me. Preferable, actually.|Sincere, playful}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) No matter how his story is resolved by the Vault 76 dwellers, they can thank him for finally explaining everything, to which Aries will reply that he is proud of himself for holding back on his "tragic origin story" for so long.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Thanks for explaining... finally."''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|You've got to admit, I've been real patient about revealing my tragic origin story. Pretty proud of myself.|playful}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries' dialogue]]) The only unresolved question on Aries' mind is how exactly there was another Imposter Sheepsquatch in the Harpers Ferry tunnel. He had attempted to research [[Scott Conroy|Scoot Conroy]]'s terminal at one point, but did not find anything definitive and became terrified by the idea that the Imposter Sheepsquatch was repopulating.[[Protocol Adonais (holotapes)|Protocol Adonais #5]] Aries speculates that the "sheepsquatch mating rituals" program could have, someway somehow, actually created a [[Imposter Sheepsquatch#Sheepsquatch Imposterling|Sheepsquatch Imposterling]]. However, in typical Aries fashion, he playfully brushes off the notion when asked about it.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I thought there was only one Imposter robot... But in Harper's Ferry..."''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|Oh, I know. It's been bugging me for a while now. Maybe you heard my, uh, breakdown at Scoot's cabin.|Serious}} {{Tooltip|I'm not sure how, but I think it's... reproducing. The special program I installed, it could... Well...|growing concern}} {{Tooltip|Eh. I'm sure it's nothing.|forget it, playful}}"''

Calvin van Lowe was first mentioned in the ''[[Wild Appalachia]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]], while Aries was introduced in the ''[[Wastelanders]]'' update. The ''[[Steel Reign]]'' update expanded upon Aries' character and indirectly revealed that he was Calvin van Lowe. The ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'' update concluded his story and confirmed the connection, with the quest [[Protocol Adonais]]. ==Behind the scenes== ===Identity=== * Developer [[Carl McKevitt]] contributed to the design and writing of Aries' character, describing it as a passion project.[https://bethesda.net/en/article/mpXV9tE26pbzYSZfAnR9W/carl-mckevitt-senior-quest-designer-at-bethesda-game-studios Carl McKevitt, Senior Quest Designer at Bethesda Game Studios] * McKevitt confirmed that Aries is a human around 50 years old and not a ghoul.BGS_Carl ([[Carl McKevitt]]) [https://web.archive.org/web/20230508182710/https://i.imgur.com/uSqzaQq.png on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord]BGS_Carl ([[Carl McKevitt]]) [https://web.archive.org/web/20230506213909/https://i.imgur.com/yUDMASB.png on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord] * A reappearance of Calvin had been planned since the [[Lying Lowe]] quest line was first introduced.BGS_Carl ([[Carl McKevitt]]) [https://web.archive.org/web/20230506202228/https://i.imgur.com/nzb3i8G.png on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord] The Lying Lowe quest line was specifically designed to have a different kind of resolution than other content in the game, insofar as the player does not actually find Calvin van Lowe dead, or find any concrete proof of his supposed death. This opened the possibility for him to make a return. McKevitt stated that he never anticipated that Calvin would return as a caravan guard, but while writing characters for Riding Shotgun, he saw a "now-or-never" opportunity to subtly reintroduce Calvin. With ''Steel Reign'', Aries' identity was openly revealed as he began to interact with other characters and his story could be expanded,[https://youtu.be/zP5kLYdY0KE?t=4499 Fallout 76 New Mothman Event Dev Dive with Bethesda's Carl McKevitt and Jon Rush (1:14:59)] then concluded with ''Once in a Blue Moon''. * [[Wikipedia:Aries (astrology)|Aries]] is the Latin word for ''ram'', commonly associated with zodiac sign. More specifically, a ram is a male bighorn sheep, a reference to Calvin's obsession with the Sheepsquatch. * His surname being "van Lowe" in the field of cryptid research may allude to the Lowe Hotel, which originally housed the Mothman Museum in the early 1990s. ===Development=== * The holotapes featuring Calvin van Lowe's voice, as they first appeared in ''[[Wild Appalachia]]'', were voiced by [[William Salyers]]. The character of Aries, introduced in ''[[Wastelanders]]'', was voiced by [[Lucien Dodge]]. The [[Protocol Adonais (holotapes)|Protocol Adonais holotapes]], introduced in ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'', were also voiced by Lucien Dodge. The original ''Wild Appalachia'' holotapes were not revoiced and still feature Salyers. * In a developer article spotlighting McKevitt's work on ''Fallout 76'', he discussed writing for Aries and the importance of balancing wanting to tell the character's story, with making them a part of the player's story. ''"I really, really want to tell players about who [Aries] is, what he does and why he does it. But I have to remind myself: he isn't there just to tell his story, he's there to be a part of the player's story."'' * Aries intentionally says "viola" instead of "voila" during the events of Out of the Blue. McKevitt and a dialogue editor agreed that it would be a good addition and in-character for Aries to say the wrong word. McKevitt stated that he received many community reports from players who assumed it was a typo that made its way into the voice line.BGS_Carl ([[Carl McKevitt]]) [https://web.archive.org/web/20230513091135/https://i.imgur.com/IeiciQq.png on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord] * McKevitt stated that any glitches that reveal Aries' face are not intended to be his "true" appearance and that he does not have a confirmed in-game appearance. It is actually what [[Kieran Kennedy]]'s first model looked like in initial designs, before he was aged up to match the voice actor. As Kieran was the first guard implemented, his actor template was duplicated to Aries, who kept the old face model, obscured by the mask.BGS_Carl ([[Carl McKevitt]]) [https://web.archive.org/web/20230509132332/https://i.imgur.com/Mqr41AM.png on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord] * Colin was going to be Calvin's original name during an early point in his development, but McKevitt opted for Calvin as it was the name of his childhood pet hamster as well as the name of his ''[[Fallout 3]]'' player character.BGS_Carl ([[Carl McKevitt]]) [https://web.archive.org/web/20230513190235/https://i.imgur.com/M9KpTtZ.png on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord] {{FO76CC}} * There is a cut NPC intended to be Calvin's corpse in the game files (Editor ID zzz_P01B_Lying_CalvinVanLoweCorpse and Form ID {{ID|00478d3e}}) named "Colin Van Lowe." There is also a cut [[Fallout 76 keys|key]] named [[Colin van Lowe's password]]. {{FO76CC|end}} ==Gallery== FO76OB Aries keyart.jpg|Art of Aries from ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'' keyart, showing parts of his face FO76 Aries.png|Aries in his previous location at [[Big Bend Tunnel west]] FO76SR Joanna Aries.png|Aries with [[Joanna Mayfield]] during [[Out of the Blue]] FO76SR Aries poster.png|Aries unlocking a secret gate mechanism behind a pin-up poster FO76SR Rahmani Aries.png|[[Leila Rahmani]] and Aries during Out of the Blue FO76SR Aries knife.png|Aries sharpening his knife as he waits FO76OB Big Bend Tunnel East - Aries.jpg|Aries in his train car home FO76OB Carver Timmerman feat Aries.jpg|Calvin van Lowe (Aries) with [[Carver Timmerman]] during [[Protocol Adonais]] FO76 bm protocoladonais.png|Aries in the [[Protocol Adonais]] quest animation Aries WW.png|Aries in ''[[Fallout: Wasteland Warfare]]'' Aries 2 WW.png|Aries in ''Fallout: Wasteland Warfare'' ==References== {{Ref box}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox companions FO76}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wild Appalachia mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Blue Ridge Caravan Company characters]] [[Category:Vault-Tec University characters]] [[Category:Bysshe Company characters]] [[Category:Fallout: Wasteland Warfare characters]] [[ru:Кэлвин ван Лоу]] [[zh:艾瑞斯]]

But, um... do you think you could make that an [[Old Possum]] instead?|Carver to [[Libby Wen]]|sound=Carver Timmerman 00581ed5_1.ogg}} '''Carver Timmerman''' is a [[Fallout 76 vendors|merchant]] and client of the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]], shipping caravans of furniture and furs through [[Big Bend Tunnel]], found at its [[Big Bend Tunnel west|west entrance]] {{in|FO76}}.Carver Timmerman: ''"We're just hauling some furniture and furs, but so far that hasn't stopped the Blood Eagles from trying to rob us."''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver's dialogue]]) Unbeknownst to Carver, he is also the step-nephew of [[Aries]]. ==Background== [[File:Lewisburg Timmermans house.png|thumb|left|200px|Carver's childhood home in [[Lewisburg]] which survived the bombs.]] Born before the [[Great War]] to [[Gregory Timmerman|Gregory]] and [[Deborah Timmerman]] in [[Lewisburg]], Carver is a young man with a complex family history. Deborah's father ran an interior decorating business, working closely with Van Lowe Taxidermy. The relationship continued after she married Gregory and inherited the business.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Receipt: 8/2/2077|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, Receipt: 8/2/2077]] The relationship took on a new dimension when Deborah and [[Shelley van Lowe]], owner of the taxidermy shop developed feelings for each other since at least January 2076,[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Receipt: 1/11/2076|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, Receipt: 1/11/2076]] developing into love,[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Receipt: 4/2/2076|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, Receipt: 4/2/2076]] with the tacit acceptance of Gregory.[[G. Timmerman, last words]] Carver does not remember anything from Lewisburg, as he was merely an infant when Shelley's brother, [[Calvin van Lowe]], abruptly returned and then suddenly disappeared,[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Refund Order: 10/19/2077|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, Refund Order: 10/19/2077]] with the [[Great War]] following. While Greg, Deborah, and Shelley tried to survive in Lewisburg, the [[Ash Heap]]'s environment was too poisonous for humans, especially the young and sickly Carver. He was losing weight rapidly and developed a severe cough by mid-November, leading Deborah to ask Shelley for help.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Pending Response: 11/17/2077|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, Pending Response: 11/17/2077]] Coupled with the recent disappearance of Gregory on a supply run,[[Note from Greg]] they had little reason to stay and moved on to [[Kentucky]], where they found a new life and set up a business dealing in furs and furniture.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Please Read, From Shelley|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, Please read, from Shelley]] Carver grew up in Kentucky (or what was once Kentucky, Carver himself is unsure, as while he studied geography as a child, it feels like a waste of time to him as an adult)Carver Timmerman: ''"Well I was born around here actually, but my mom moved us sometime after the war. Now we've live in a settlement out in what used to be Kentucky, I guess. Maybe it still is Kentucky? I don't know, I tried reading some old geography text books as a kid, seemed like a waste of time now, though."''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue#144|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) under the care of his two mothers, with Shelley effectively adopting him as her own child. All he knows of his father are the scant few mentions of Gregory from Deborah. This ignorance led to curiosity, then an identity crisis,Carver Timmerman: "''Oh, ha. Yeah, I guess that can get pretty confusing. So my mom-- my birth mom, I mean-- is Debbie. She handles all the orders and stuff for our stock. {{tooltip|My other mom is Shelley-- she's from Lewisburg too. They both left town during the war and fell in love, I think.|Proud}} {{tooltip|As long as I can remember, Shelley's been my mom, too. She's helped raised me since I was a baby.|Sincere}} {{tooltip|But mom says that dad died just after the bombs. He never made it out of Lewisburg. That's all I know.|This feels distant to him; more a curiosity than trauma}} {{tooltip|And... don't get me wrong. My family is perfect. I wouldn't trade it for anything. But, learning about him could be like... learning about me? Maybe?|Genuine-- but unsure about the logistics of it}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) and a haunting need to know more about where he comes from and who he is.Carver Timmerman: "''Problem is, I was born there... In Lewisburg, I mean. Wasn't old enough to remember it, but I've heard about it... and about my Dad. {{tooltip|He never made it out with us. Mom doesn't say much, just that we all lived there before the war.|Still down}} {{tooltip|I can't get my mind off it. It's all I think about these days... I wish I could learn more about him.|A bit pleading, lost}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) Suffering from a long-lasting identity crisis, Carver's self-esteem and confidence suffered, affecting him all the way into adulthood. While he dearly loves both of his mothers (especially Shelley, whose courage and strength he admires), he does wish he had more family to help him find a proper sense of self, or at the very least learn something more about his lost father.Vault 76 dweller: "''Shelley from Lewisburg? Like Shelley van Lowe?"''
Carver Timmerman: "''{{tooltip|Oh! You must have followed those posters. Yep! That's Shelley. She tells me stories about her brother, Calvin, all the time. Sheepsquatch excluded.|Ears perked up}} {{tooltip|Shelley is normally so brave and strong all the time, but I love to see how she gets when she talks about him... Her eyes are just... different.|Admiring, then soft}} {{tooltip|Would have been cool to have an uncle, too, but I guess a Sheepsquatch ate him or something!|Taking this in stride, even attempting a joke}} {{tooltip|... Oh, that's probably kind of dark. Sorry.|Realizing "too soon"}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) Carver would get a chance to fulfill his wish in 2103, as [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] expanded into [[Appalachia]]. With Deborah sick and unable to work the caravan trail and Shelley occupied with sourcing furs for their outfit, Carver was pressedVault 76 dweller: "''Caravan work sounds tough for someone like him.''"
[[Vinny Costa]]: "''Well, it ain't really by choice neither. One of his moms used to run the route, but came down with somethin' nasty some time back. His other mom's their primary trapper, so it falls to lil' Carvey-boy to man the Brahmin.''"
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) into the role of a merchant.[[Libby Wen]]: ''"Is there no one else from your family that can run shipments for you, Carver?"''
Carver Timmerman: ''"Well my mom used to do this before she got sick. And I guess Shelley could, but then we'd be down a trapper. Why do you ask? I'm not very good at this, am I?"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman]] and [[Libby Wen/Dialogue|Libby Wen's dialogue]]) Nervous, unsure of himself, and considered fragile even by the head of the company,[[Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries#Staff and Clients for Appalachia|Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries; Joanna Mayfield's terminal, Staff and Clients for Appalachia]][[Discarded letter]][[Libby Wen]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Is there no one else from your family that can run shipments for you, Carver?|Hesitant to bring it up}}"''
Carver Timmerman: ''"Well my mom used to do this before she got sick. And I guess Shelley could, but then we'd be down a trapper. {{Tooltip|Why do you ask? I'm not very good at this, am I?|Feels bad}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver]] and [[Libby Wen/Dialogue|Libby's dialogue]]) Carver had to adapt and work the trail. The desire to know more about his father intensified with his proximity to Lewisburg, eating away at him.Carver Timmerman: "''Problem is, I was born there... In Lewisburg, I mean. Wasn't old enough to remember it, but I've heard about it... and about my Dad. {{tooltip|He never made it out with us. Mom doesn't say much, just that we all lived there before the war.|Still down}} {{tooltip|I can't get my mind off it. It's all I think about these days... I wish I could learn more about him.|A bit pleading, lost}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) However, [[Vinny Costa]], the head of operations, would never spare guards for a personal errand.Vault 76 dweller: "''So, take a stroll over to Lewisburg. It's close."''
Carver Timmerman: "''Oh, I have... I've even gotten as close as my old house-- or at least what I think is my old house. But it's just too dangerous... Especially alone. Vinny would never let me borrow a guard for something personal, either."''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) Vinny actually sees that Carver has the makings of a capable worker, but simply needs help to step into the role. Vinny is unaware of the struggle within Carver,Vault 76 dweller: "''I'm not really looking for a baby sitting gig."''
Vinny Costa: "''{{tooltip|Well you're in luck, ya joker, because this ain't that. Carver's a big boy. Just needs help steppin' into those shoes. You don't want to help, walk.|Annoyed}}"''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) but has noticed that Carver is distracted and liable to halt all of his shipments until he figures himself out.Vault 76 dweller: "''I'm looking for some work."''
Vinny Costa: "''{{tooltip|That's good, cuz I have some. Carver Timmerman. He's a merchant. Young pup. Very easily distracted.|Straight to business}} More so than ever, too. So I think ya know the deal by now. I want that kid at least knowin' left from right before I okay anymore of his shipments."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]])Carver Timmerman: "''{{tooltip|Focus? That's... kind of tricky. My minds been stuck on... stuff. Mainly Lewisburg, really.|A bit bummed}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) ===Relationships=== Carver's most important relationships are with his mothers and, though he knows little about him, his late father. While he has pieced together that something more was going on between the three than either Deborah or Shelley told him, Carver is non-judgmental. Insulting his family over their relationship is a surefire way to gain Carver's ire, or at least make him try and stand up for them.Vault 76 dweller: "''Sounds like your mom was two-timing him with Shelley. He died alone."''
Carver Timmerman: "''{{tooltip|Hey... That's too much... You can't, like... talk about them like that. I always suspected there was more to the story, but... That's just not...|Offended. Trying to stand up, as best he can}} {{tooltip|I'll take the letter after all... I need to see this for myself... You know, later.|Still offended but trying to simmer down the tension}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) However, it is learning about his father and his last hours that truly helps Carver find himself and the confidence he so desperately needs.Vault 76 dweller: "''[Charisma 4+] You won't grow from this if you don't read it yourself. Here."''
Carver Timmerman: "''{{tooltip|You're right... Let me take a look...|Coming around to it}} {{tooltip|Huh... That's... Wow. I didn't realize all that was going on...|Taking time to read}} {{tooltip|That's a lot to handle... But I'm really glad to know he was thinking of me up until the end...|Hard to hear, but good to hear}} {{tooltip|Thank you for finding this... and making me see it for myself.|Sincere}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) He has difficulty finding common ground elsewhere, including other men. He tried talking with [[Kieran Kennedy]] about his father, but Kieran gruffly told him that "Your past is not who you are. You are not just your father's son, you are yourself first," which did little to inspire confidence or reduce Carver's anxiety about his identity.Vault 76 dweller: "''Forget your dead dad. Be your own man."''
Carver Timmerman: "''{{tooltip|Kieran said something similar. Uh, worded a little more nicely, though... N-no offense.|Understands, not buying it}} {{tooltip|"Your past is not who you are. You are not just your father's son, you are yourself first."|Imitating a tough guy voice, poorly}} {{tooltip|B-b-but your way of putting it works too. Heh. Wish it were that simple, but it's... I don't know how to explain. I just know it'll help.|Trying not to offend}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) Similarly, Vinny is intimidating to the young Timmerman. While technically he is not his boss and Blue Ridge works for the merchants, Carver cannot help but see Vinny as a superior and fears disapproval or trouble the most.Vault 76 dweller: "''Vinny mentioned you've been distracted on the road."''
Carver Timmerman: "''{{tooltip|He did? Oh man, I must be in trouble. I don't want my boss being mad at me.|A bit of panic}} {{tooltip|Oh wait, Shelley said he's not my boss, technically he works for us... Am I in trouble, or not? Please help.|Comically lost}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) However, Vinny pales in comparison with [[Aries]]. Carver is unaware that Aries' [[Assault gas mask (Fallout 76)|gas mask]] conceals his step-uncle, the long lost Calvin van Lowe. As a result, Carver finds Aries' antics scary and believes they mean that Aries considers him a pathetic weakling and a loser. He even unsuccessfully petitioned [[Joanna Mayfield]] to avoid pairing him with Aries on caravan runs.[[Discarded letter]] Aries simply freaks Carver out, although should Carver discover the family connection, he is surprised but happy, and finds a sense of connection with him.Carver Timmerman: "''{{tooltip|It's so hard to wrap my head around. I've always wondered about my uncle Calvin... and it's really exciting to know he's alive.|Unsure, mixed confusion and hope}} {{tooltip|But, I'd be lying if I said that Aries didn't kind of... freak me out.|Deflating}}"''
Vault 76 dweller: "''I think we all feel that way. But he's a good guy."''
Carver Timmerman: "''{{tooltip|Oh, I know he's got a good heart. He always goes out of his way to keep me safe...|Sincere}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries]]' and [[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) The opposite situation occurred with [[Libby Wen]], a Blue Ridge guard. Carver has a crush on Libby and has actually asked Vinny to be paired with her on runs, even going as far as suggesting he is ready to do back-to-back runs to convince him. Vinny paired Libby and Carver together, but mentioned this to Libby. Libby confronted Carver on the trail during a slow moment. Neither shaming nor humiliating him, she explained that she is the wrong person, a caravan run is the wrong time for a date, and going behind her back with Vinny was the absolute worst way to arrange one. At the same time, she did not shut him down, treating it as an unfortunate screw-up, but allowing Carver to start over once he got over it.Carver Timmerman: ''"Oh, hi Libby! I didn't know you were on duty for this run."''
[[Libby Wen]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Vinny told me you were asking if I could be put on this shift with you.|A little annoyed, a little teasing. She's not upset about this, but she's also not cool with it either}} {{Tooltip|He even said you were willing to do back to back runs to make it happen.|Teasing}}"''
Carver Timmerman: ''"{{Tooltip|I... Okay, that's embarrassing. I was just hoping to...|Flustered}}"''
Libby Wen: ''"{{Tooltip|Carver. This is the wrong time, I'm the wrong person, and that was definitely the wrong way to do it.|Direct, but not shaming.}}"''
Carver Timmerman: ''"{{Tooltip|I'm, uh, don't know what you mean, I was just...|Trying to play it off. Not working}}"''
Libby Wen: ''"{{Tooltip|You know exactly what I mean. Let's take it from the top: Hi Carver, how are you today?|Trying to be a little reassuring - "listen, you fucked up, it's fine, let's start over."}}"''
Carver Timmerman: ''"{{Tooltip|Libby, I... uh... I'm good. Thanks for asking.|Embarrassed, trying to get over it}}"''
Libby Wen: ''"{{Tooltip|Great.|A little more chipper}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver]] and [[Libby Wen/Dialogue|Libby's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion =yes |perk = |wares =* Bulk materials * [[Plan: Long rustic bench]] * [[Plan: Office chairs]] * [[Plan: Resort chairs]] |caps =yes |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |events involved =[[Riding Shotgun]] |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Costa Business: Carver]] * [[Protocol Adonais]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Riding Shotgun]]: Carver is one of the three possible variants of the event. He will be assigned to the guard Libby Wen, with their banter and exchanges focusing on his unsuccessful attempts to turn a run into a date. * [[Costa Business: Carver]]: With Carver's performance slipping too far, Vinny halts Carver's shipments and asks the Dwellers to help him figure out left from right. Carver asks them to find anything that would shed light on his father's fate, starting with the old Timmerman home in [[Lewisburg]].Vault 76 dweller: "''I could check out your old house. Carver Timmerman: "''{{tooltip|You mean it? That'd be... great! I can mark my old house on your map... I can't believe you're doing this!|Sincere}} {{tooltip|Anything you can find to help me learn more about him would just be amazing... Thank you!|Gracious}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) The trail leads to [[The Burning Mine]] and Gregory's last words. At the end, the player can choose to simply summarize the letter for him or, with Charisma 4+, persuade him to face his past and read the letters himself, helping him grow into his own man. Gregory's heirloom lighter may also be returned to Carver. * [[Protocol Adonais]]: Aries asks to either burn all the [[Protocol Adonais (holotapes)|holotapes]] or give them to Carver, deciding his legacy. This also determines the future of the Van Lowe siblings and the closure of their story arc: If given to Carver, Aries will visit Carver in the office and the two will awkwardly accept their family connection. Aries will also continue to spend time with Carver, considering him a good kid, and seeing time they spend together as rewarding. While he does not have the courage yet to face Shelley himself, he will slowly edge towards rebuilding bridges he burned, starting with a letter Carver will deliver to her.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How are things with your family?"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|I don't have the courage to face Shelley in person just yet... But I did leave a letter with Carver.|Slight shame}} {{Tooltip|Next time he heads back, I asked him to deliver it to her... He's a good kid. Spending time with him has been... pretty fulfilling, actually.|Still a bit shy}} {{Tooltip|He's more of a fainting lamb than a Sheepsquatch, and that's all right by me. Preferable, actually.|Sincere, playful}}"''
