Just ghouls there, doing what we can to survive.|sound=Eugenie 00584b24_1.ogg}} '''Eugenie''' is a client and merchant of the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] at [[Big Bend Tunnel east]] {{in|FO76}}. She is one of the possible merchants traveling with pack [[Brahmin (Fallout 76)|brahmin]] through [[Big Bend Tunnel]] during the [[Riding Shotgun]] event. ==Background== Born and raised near [[Appalachia]], Eugenie survived the [[Great War]], but was exposed to enough [[radiation]] to trigger [[ghoul]]ification. Forced to leave her fellow survivors, she dodged bigots for years, evading attempts to kill her just for who she became. Eventually, she joined a group of like-minded ghouls, the [[Revenants]], and lived at [[Radiant Hills]] for almost a decade.Vault 76 dweller: "''Where are you from?"''
Eugenie: "''Well, I was born and raised not far from here. I ended up leaving not long after becoming a ghoul. Let's say that things got a little dangerous. Nowadays, I live in a small compound out in the hills. Just ghouls there, doing what we can to survive."''
([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie's dialogue]]) While safe, she felt that she was stuck there, afraid to venture out. She finally got up and decided to take her chances, gathering supplies, caps, and venturing out to become a merchant. As it turned out, coming into town with goods is an excellent way to make people talk to ghouls (and the firepower she carries ensures they stay civilized).Eugenie: ''"You know, I've been doing this traveling merchant thing for a while now. I spent damn near a decade stuck in our compound, hiding from people that would kill us on sight just for being who we are. I've found that rolling into town with supplies and caps to trade eases up the tension, get's people talkin' to you again. The fact that I'm strapped to the teeth in fire power doesn't hurt neither. But some people, like the Blood Eagles... there's no discussion to be had."''
([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie's dialogue]]) Eventually, she contracted the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] for protection, making regular runs through the [[Big Bend Tunnel]], ferrying weapons, ammunition, and explosives. The company believes her to still be closely tied to the compound,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault dweller]]: "''Anything about Eugenie I should know?''"
[[Vinny Costa]]: "''We've been guardin' for her a while now. Sells guns, explosives, the good stuff. She, and her gear, come from some ghoul community somewheres way off. She won't talk about it much. Normally I don't gotta worry 'bout her. Lately, that ain't the case.''"
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) and [[Joanna Mayfield]] would like nothing more than Eugenie recruiting more traders for Blue Ridge, on top of the generous commission Eugenie provides.[[Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries#Staff and Clients for Appalachia|Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries; Blue Ridge terminal, Staff and Clients for Appalachia]]: "''Client / Merchant : Eugenie (Arms and Ammunition)
''>> Very valuable client, lots of commission. Reminder: get her to recruit more people from her compound to sell wares.''" As a result, she receives preferential rates, as free agents have to pay significantly more.Vault 76 dweller: "''She's fine-- hey, did you know she moved out from that ghoul compound? I read all about it."''
[[Vinny Costa]]: "''She what? She moved outta that place? Shit, kid, you shoulda said that sooner. Ain't no way I can overlook it: her being a free agent changes some, uh... pricing options. You don't know it but you just made my day, pal. Probably ruined ol' Eugenie's year but eh, she'll be fine."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) In reality, Eugenie has moved out of Radiant Hills and set up her own network of contacts to source her wares from. However, she remains in touch with the Revenants through letters. Though they are simple updates on what is going on in Radiant Hills, she treasures them as a reminder that she can always come back. While her fellow ghouls do miss her greatly,[[Eugenie's letter]] she is reluctant to return and sell for them again. She prefers being her own boss,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: "''What was it about?''"
Eugenie: "''It's from someone back at the compound I come from.. er, came from. We were a community of ghouls holed up in the hills. I haven't told anyone here, but I've actually moved out. All my guns and gear come from my own connections these days-- not that I'd tell Vinny that. The letters, though... Are just ordinary updates on life. And a reminder that I can always come back. I left for... good reason. I don't regret it. But... some folks here are just... family. Plus, if I went back... I'd be selling for them again.''" *sighs* "''I know I'm being vague, but I could still use some advice. What do you think?''"
([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie's dialogue]]) and she never liked what the Revenants were doing with the proceeds she generated, though she does not specify what exactly was going on to lead her into conflict with the residents of Radiant Hills.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault dweller]]: "''It'd help if you could tell me why you left.''"
Eugenie: "''Let's just say I didn't like what they were doing with their cut of the business.''"
([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie's dialogue]]) Nevertheless, she maintains cordial contact with her friends, such as [[Jaye Vo]], whom Eugenie encourages to overcome her insecurities about ghoulification and accept herself.[[Letter to Jaye]] She has also written to [[Kevan Asherton]], trying to convince him and [[Maddox Mullen]] that she is living proof that ghouls and humans living and working together is possible, but she also accepts the idea that the other Revenants will never see change their mind about their reclusive, isolationist defenses.[[Eugenie's response]] Eugenie is used to traveling through the Big Bend Tunnel. While she prefers [[Libby Wen]] for her professionalism,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How about Libby Wen?"''
Eugenie: ''"Don't tell the others, but Libby is my guard of choice. Things just run a lot more smoothly with her at the helm. Her family basically raised her like it was boot camp. I know they drive her batty, but they sure brought her up right. She's a real professional."''
([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie's dialogue]]) she is often paired with [[Kieran Kennedy]]. The gruff, silent guard stands in stark contrast to the chatty, joking Eugenie,Eugenie: "''We'll be carrying a load of premium arms and ammunition, so I'd appreciate an extra touch of care. {{tooltip|Hopefully the reward for getting me there in one piece will more than compensate for any bullets you... invest.|Deliberately paced word play. ([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie]] and [[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) and the two developed a healthy respect for each other. Eugenie gently teases Kieran about his brooding attitude from time to time,Eugenie: "''{{tooltip|So, how's the family?|Slightly teasing because she knows he hates small talk.}}"''

([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie]] and [[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) and even feigns ignorance just to get him talking.Eugenie: "''That was a tough fight. Why don't we try taking the roads over the mountains next time?"''

([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie]] and [[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) This unlikely bond is useful, as every run through the tunnel means going through a throng of [[Blood Eagles]].Eugenie: ''"Expect armed resistance-- never been a run that hasn't had it. ([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie's dialogue]]) She also knows [[Tommy Ten-Toes]] and played darts with him during a stay at [[Middle Mountain Pitstop]], beating the former mobster. It appears that their preferred variant is the 301 version of the game.[[:File:FO76OB Middle Mountain Pitstop darts.png|Darts at the Pitstop]] The Revenants remain her biggest weakness and liability. She misplaced one of the letters she received, leaving it in [[Summersville]], and the fact has been weighing on her. [[Vinny Costa]], her manager, noticed that her distractions: Eugenie was daydreaming, wandering off the trail and losing track of cargo - and since she is a top earner for the company, anything happening to her would impact the bottom line severely.Vault 76 dweller: "''Got any work that needs doing?"''

([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) What complicates the issue are second thoughts about leaving Radiant Hills:Eugenie: "''Well hey there, what brings you here?''"

([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie's dialogue]]) on one hand, the other ghouls are practically her family and she still cares about them.Vault 76 dweller: "''Being with people you care about is important. Think it through."''

[[Ushanka hat (Fallout 76)|Raider scavenger hat]]{{Unused}} |weapon =[[.44 pistol (Fallout 76)|.44 pistol]] |otheritem =[[Backpack (Fallout 76)|Blue Ridge Caravan backpack]] |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Eugenie appears {{In|FO76WL}}. Her character was expanded upon in the ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'' and ''[[Ghoul Within]]'' updates. ==Behind the scenes== * Quest designer [[Carl McKevitt]] was a contributor to Eugenie's design and writing.BGS_Carl ([[Carl McKevitt]]) [https://web.archive.org/web/20230514153247/https://i.imgur.com/k8bXCba.png on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord] * According to McKevitt, Eugenie's line "let's get a ''mooove'' on" (a [[Brahmin (Fallout 76)|Brahmin]]/cow joke) was actually an unintentional pun. Although the line had existed in the script (without the "moo" part in move), voice actress [[Marisha Ray]] realized the potential for the joke, alongside the voice director for the session, and delivered it that way. McKevitt was not present for Eugenie's voice recording session, as he was visiting family at the time, and only discovered the joke later. * Eugenie's background, including living with a compound of ghouls, was originally left vague throughout her dialogue as of ''Wastelanders'', as she only said that it was a commune in the hills to the north and did not mention anyone by name. Her [[Eugenie's letter|letter]] and dialogue in the ''Once in a Blue Moon'' update provided some more minor details, including mentioning the characters [[Kevan Asherton|Kev]] and [[Jaye Vo|Jaye]]. It was not until the ''Ghoul Within'' update that the faction of the [[Revenants]] and their headquarters at [[Radiant Hills]] in the northern [[Savage Divide]] were fully introduced, making it clear that they are the ghouls mentioned by Eugenie. However, Eugenie did not receive any new dialogue for the update, and she has no unique interactions if the player character has met or even joined the Revenants. ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox vendors FO76}} {{Navbox companions FO76}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders ghoul characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders merchants]] [[Category:Blue Ridge Caravan Company characters]] [[Category:Revenants characters]] [[ru:Евгения]]

Especially when you're not just taking care of yourself.|Kieran on why he joined the company|sound=Kieran Kennedy 0058391b_1.ogg}} '''Kieran Kennedy''' is an employee of the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] at [[Big Bend Tunnel west]] in [[Appalachia]], {{in|FO76}}. He is a potential guard for the caravan leading [[Brahmin (Fallout 76)|brahmin]] through Big Bend Tunnel during the event [[Riding Shotgun]]. ==Background== A gruff man of few words, Kieran is an "old associate" of [[Vinny Costa]] from before the [[Great War]]. They have known each other for some thirty years, since at least [[Timeline#2074|2074]], and Kieran has apparently been a grim, frowning man just as long. Kieran alludes to a similarly grim childhood: he says that while growing up, he had few chances to be a kid, and as a result has very little knowledge of what it means to have a childhoodVault 76 dweller: "''Kids need the chance to be kids. Don't overthink it."''
Kieran Kennedy: "''Guess you're right. Even growing up before the war, I didn't have many chances to be a kid. Anything is better than nothing."''
([[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) and even less of what it means to have fun.Vault 76 dweller: "''Can't you just go yourself? It's right there."''
Kieran Kennedy: "''No. Not right now anyway. And even if I did... I'm not sure I have the eye for it. Fun isn't really my strong suit."''
([[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) His strong suit is violence. He is exceptionally strong and still in excellent physical condition despite his age, working under Vinny as a caravan guard for the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]]. He is not quick to anger, but anyone testing his patience with insults might get to learn if he can truly "rip out their tongue through their bellybutton," according to Vinny. Vault 76 dweller: "''The slacker is done slacking. Pay up."''
Vinny Costa: "''Kieran could rip your tongue out through your bellybutton, so I'd watch your mouth. But if he's back to work, a deal's a deal. Get outta my sight quick enough and I may have some more work for you tomorrow. Scram."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) While Kieran tried numerous other jobs in the past, they did not pan out, and he always returned to what he knew best.[[Eugenie]]: ''"Ever consider a less dangerous line of work, Kieran?"''
Kieran Kennedy: ''"Yes. Many times in the past."''
Eugenie: ''"So... I'm guessing it didn't work out, huh? I don't think I could picture you doing something more mundane. Kieran the fisherman. Kieran the bar tender. Kieran the... professional singer."''
Kieran Kennedy: ''"It did not."''
([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie]] and [[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) He has a no-nonsense attitude towards work, focusing on the objectives first and any extra opportunities second.Eugenie: "''Oh, and if anyone wants to scout ahead, there may be some extra cargo lying around from our less successful ventures. Kieran Kennedy: "''Right: our priority is protecting the Brahmin, not going on a killing spree or a treasure hunt."''
Eugenie: "''Not that there's ever any shortage of hooligans to kill and treasure to find."''
([[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) Although it is not specified exactly what jobs he did for Vinny, Kieran is more than just a hired gun: he has some knowledge of handling explosive charges and can bring down blockades without killing the caravan or bringing the [[Big Bend Tunnel]] down whenever the Blood Eagles try to block Blue Ridge from crossing.Eugenie: "''That was practically an army. We must have gotten them all, right?"''
Kieran Kennedy: "''Blockade ahead. We'll need to knock it down. I'll set some charges to clear the rubble. Watch my back. They must be looking to stall us. Expect a serious fight ahead."''
Eugenie: "''More coming! They're going full force because they knew the "ghoul merchant" was coming through. They always think we're a quick score... Let's make them regret it."''
([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie]] and [[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) He also easily picks out enemy commandersKieran Kennedy: "''Damn. They've got the gate closed. Looks heavily guarded. That one up top looks like a captain. We need to take him out first."''
([[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) and understands the reasons for bothering with the Tunnel in the first place, such as the lack of cover when going overland or using the tunnel to neutralize enemy number advantage.Eugenie: "''That was a tough fight. ([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie]] and [[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) Kieran is usually paired with [[Eugenie]], a [[ghoul]] weapons merchant, making regular runs with premium armaments and ammunition through Big Bend. ([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie]] and [[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) and while she has complained at times about his gruff nature and tendency towards responding in a combination of sighs and monosyllabics,[[Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries#Deleted Entries|Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries; Vinny Costa's terminal, Deleted Entries]] the two have developed a rapport. Eugenie gently teases him about his disdain towards small talk, in fact,Eugenie: "''{{tooltip|So, how's the family?|Slightly teasing because she knows he hates small talk.}}"''
Kieran Kennedy: "''Fine... Safe."''
([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie]] and [[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) as she realizes he has a good heart, even if the exterior is "about as fun as a swamp itch."[[Eugenie]]: "''When he's not brooding, he's moody. But, Kieran has a good heart, I know that for a fact. About as fun as swamp itch, though.''"
([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie's dialogue]]) [[Joanna Mayfield]] respects him as a dependable worker and is familiar with his family situation, even going as far to set aside toys for them.[[Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries#Staff and Clients for Appalachia|Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries; terminal, Staff and Clients for Appalachia]] Kieran started a family, adopting at least five children and setting up a homestead, though Vinny warned him he was not cut out for the family life.Vault 76 dweller: "''Kieran was concerned about his kids. I helped him sort it out.''"
Vinny Costa: "''Kieran with them damn kids... I warned him he wasn't cut out for playin' house. Glad you figured it out for him.''"
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) The adopted children run the homestead on their own,BGS_Carl ([[Carl McKevitt]]) [https://web.archive.org/web/20230508074226/https://i.imgur.com/900zGqJ.png on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord] protected by [[Dorothy (Wastelanders)|Dorothy]], a guard hired by Kieran to keep them safe whenever he is away earning caps. Dorothy is practically part of the family, all of whom stay in touch with Kieran through letters. "Uncle K.", as he is called by [[Hannah (mentioned)|Hannah]], is frequently away, but the homestead runs well on its own thanks to the older kids and Hannah, who also looks after the youngest ones and teaches them how to read and write.[[Dear Uncle K.]] Kieran's kids are his weakness, in fact. As he never experienced a proper childhood, he does not know how to give them what he feels is a proper childhood. He has been conflicted about his role as an adoptive father, to the point that his performance started slipping and Vinny noticed.[[Vinny Costa]]: "''He's one of my old crew, from ways back. He's not known for clownin' around, so if somethin's eatin' him, we should fix it.''"
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) While Kieran provides his adopted family with caps, food and safety, he is concerned that he should provide more than that. The [[Great War]] and the fallout that followed may have robbed them of their chance at a childhood, but he is unsure he should keep it that way. [[Nuka-World on Tour (location)|Nuka-World on Tour]] seems like an opportunity to give them a bit of the childhood back, even if Kieran is well aware Appalachia is too dangerous for them to visit. He hopes to bring home a couple of souvenirs,Vault 76 dweller: "''Hey Kieran, Vinny says you're not pulling your weight."''
Kieran Kennedy: "''He always says that. But... yeah, fine. Guess I've been distracted. I've got these kids I watch back home, outside Appalachia. The only reason I do this work is to send caps back to them. But... I'm starting to worry that they need more than protection and money. They've had their whole chance at childhood robbed from them. Had my eye on this place called Nuka-World, just down the road. Some traveling carnival. The type of thing they'd love to see. The journey here, though... Too dangerous for them. Wouldn't risk it. The road is no place for kids like them. But I've been thinking... Maybe I could bring back a few toys or souvenirs from there. Think you'd be able to do that for me? It'd really help out."''
([[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) to bring out some of the childlike wonder.Vault 76 dweller: "''Why do you need the souvenirs again?"''
Kieran Kennedy: "''For the kids I watch back home. Safety and security are really all I can provide for them. Hopefully you can find some things that'll bring out their child... like... wonder?"''
([[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) At the same time, he is worried that souvenirs would only remind them of the fact they cannot visit the carnival, and of a world destroyed by their parents' generation, and that this would only end up making them sadder.Vault 76 dweller: "''Here's your souvenirs."''
Kieran Kennedy: "''I see. I've... been reconsidering. I'm starting to think that the souvenirs will only make them sadder. To see something from a place, a time, they can't go to. "''
([[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) The alternative is to prepare them for reality and the grim world they are facing.Vault 76 dweller: "''You're right. No sense dreaming about the past."''
Kieran Kennedy: "''Right. They're growing up in a different world from us. I need to prepare them for reality. Thanks, either way. I'll see if Carver wants to sell these or something."''
([[Kieran Kennedy/Dialogue|Kieran Kennedy's dialogue]]) However, as Kieran admits, he may be overthinking it a fair bit. While there are no kids at the Appalachian caravan camp, Kieran does get to try at being a parental figure. [[Carver Timmerman]] struggles with not knowing his father well, and when he asked Kieran about it, he provided the best guidance he could: "Your past is not who you are. You are not just your father's son, you are yourself first."Vault 76 dweller: "''Forget your dead dad. Be your own man."''
Carver Timmerman: "''{{tooltip|Kieran said something similar. Uh, worded a little more nicely, though... N-no offense.|Understands, not buying it}} {{tooltip|"Your past is not who you are. You are not just your father's son, you are yourself first."|Imitating a tough guy voice, poorly}} {{tooltip|B-b-but your way of putting it works too. Heh. Wish it were that simple, but it's... I don't know how to explain. I just know it'll help.|Trying not to offend}}"''

([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Blue Ridge Caravan outfit]] |weapon =[[Double-barrel shotgun (Fallout 76)|Double-barrel shotgun]] |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Kieran Kennedy appears {{In|FO76WL}}. His character was expanded upon in the ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'' update. ==Behind the scenes== * Quest designer [[Carl McKevitt]] was a writer for Kieran; McKevitt also created much of the rest of the Blue Ridge Caravan Company. * On the Bethesda Game Studios official Discord, Carl clarified that Kieran has no living blood relatives, and that his children are adopted. * Kieran's face was initially much younger, with black hair and the "Anchorage" hairstyle, before he was aged up to match the voice actor. As Kieran was the first guard implemented during development, his actor template was duplicated to [[Aries]], who kept the old face model, just obscured by the mask.BGS_Carl ([[Carl McKevitt]]) [https://web.archive.org/web/20230509132332/https://i.imgur.com/Mqr41AM.png on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord] * Carl also stated that Kieran's name is a very subtle nod to one of his favorite video game protagonists, even if Kieran's final appearance in-game makes the reference "practically non-existent." While he initially did not reveal who exactly this protagonist was, he stated that there were some clues left behind, including Eugenie's line about past jobs.BGS_Carl ([[Carl McKevitt]]) [https://web.archive.org/web/20230508183749/https://i.imgur.com/VfeTZel.png on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord] ** This reference is to [[w:c:yakuza:Kazuma Kiryu|Kazuma Kiryu]], the main protagonist of the ''[[wikipedia:Yakuza (series)|Yakuza]]'' series. Both of their initials are "K.K." (Kiryu and Kieran, in particular, having the same first syllables), while Eugenie mentions Kieran as a [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uUyIgaakqHk fisherman], [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pHFWUgOuEvs bartender], and [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MJbE3uWN9vE professional singer] - all jobs Kiryu has taken on. Additionally, Kieran and Kiryu have adopted daughters with similar names; Kiryu adopted [[w:c:yakuza:Haruka Sawamura|Haruka Sawamura]] and Kieran adopted [[Hannah (mentioned)|Hannah]]. Carl McKevitt is a noted fan of the ''Yakuza'' series and cited the games' influence on him in a Bethesda.net article.[https://bethesda.net/en/article/mpXV9tE26pbzYSZfAnR9W/carl-mckevitt-senior-quest-designer-at-bethesda-game-studios Carl McKevitt, Senior Quest Designer at Bethesda Game Studios] ==Gallery== FO76OB Kieran keyart.jpg|Kieran in the ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'' keyart FO76WL SQ01 Kieran Kennedy.jpg|Kieran FO76 Kieran watching.png|Kieran watching with binoculars at Big Bend Tunnel west ==References== {{References}} '''Notes''' {{References|group=Note}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox companions FO76}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Blue Ridge Caravan Company characters]] [[ru:Киран]]

I've always been a good shot, so I may as well get paid for it.|A bit sad}}|sound=Libby Wen 00581ee9_1.ogg}} '''Elizabeth "Libby" Wen''' is a caravan guard and employee of the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] at [[Big Bend Tunnel west]] {{in|FO76WL}}. ==Background== Descended from an [[United States of America|American]] military family, the dark-haired Libby is the daughter of a [[United States Marine Corps|U.S. Marine]] and a mother who also held a military job. As a result, living with him was like always being around a drill sergeant, even after the bombs dropped, with mother being no different. Libby left home in order to pursue her own career, leaving her brother and sister to help at home. Since she was a lousy worker, but a good shot, she figured she might as well get paid for it.[[Carver Timmerman]]: ''"If you don't mind me asking, why did you become a caravan guard, Libby?"''
Libby Wen: ''"Honestly? I just needed a reason to get away from my family for a while. I guess I can count myself lucky to have any family at all... But, I never really found my place with them. My dad was a Marine, and in a way he still is. Like living with a drill sergeant. Mom is no better, she had a military background, too. My brother and sister are more than enough for helping the camp. Not for me. I've always been good at shooting, so I may as well get paid for it."''
Carver Timmerman: ''"I can understand that... Plus, we get to travel."''
Libby Wen: ''"{{Tooltip|See the world and all that? Maybe I'm a Marine after all. Dad must be so proud.|"See the world" said like an advertisement. With a chuckle. Sarcasm at the end}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman]] and [[Libby Wen/Dialogue|Libby Wen's dialogue]]) The Wen family camp is located far from [[Appalachia]], near the [[Capital Wasteland|capitol]], and since finding work with [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]], she spends most of her time with the caravans.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Where are you from?"''
Libby Wen: ''"Originally? Pretty far from here, closer to the capitol. My family has a camp there, but these days I'm mostly traveling with the caravan."''
([[Libby Wen/Dialogue|Libby Wen's dialogue]]) While she resents the atmosphere at home, comparable to a boot camp, rather than a family home, it has turned her into a professional warrior: Calm and collected under fire, with caravan runs under her protection smoother than any other. Her character was expanded upon in the ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'' update. ==Behind the scenes== Libby's voice lines were re-recorded for the ''Once in a Blue Moon'' update, although she is still voiced by [[Grace Lynn Kung]] in both ''Wastelanders'' and ''Once in a Blue Moon''. According to [[Carl McKevitt]], this was done because she was receiving new dialogue for the update anyway, and the team wanted to make her stand out more than she originally did in ''Wastelanders''. McKevitt was unavailable to be present for Libby's initial voiceover session, and felt that his original script notes were insufficient for capturing the concept of the character. With ''Once in a Blue Moon'', the team further workshopped Libby's character and got closer to the original vision. Specifically, Libby was meant to be seen as looked down upon due to her young age and inexperience, despite being very capable. With ''Wastelanders'', she was more "stone cold" than intended, while ''Once in a Blue Moon'' made her more "weird and fun."[[File:FO76OB Libby Wen re-recorded.png|1px]][[:File:FO76OB Libby Wen re-recorded.png|BGS_Carl (Carl McKevitt) on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord]]: ''"We rerecorded all of her lines. Same actress, but we wanted to make the character stand out more, and be more inline with the original vision for her. I wasn't available when we initially recorded her, and I didn't include sufficient notes on her. So we workshopped her a bit since we were going to be recording a bunch of new stuff for her anyway. She's very weird now and I love it. Can't hear most of it until her quest though"''[[File:FO76OB Libby revoice.png|1px]][[:File:FO76OB Libby revoice.png|BGS_Carl (Carl McKevitt) on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord]]: ''"Just popped in to do my dailies: wanted to clear this up, though. Libby was re-voiced but NOT re-cast. The first time around I was unavailable to join in the recording session, and also provided some... less than helpful script notes. That ended up with Libby being pretty far off the the mark from what I was aiming for. Libby was meant to be looked down on by older members of the caravan for her age and inexperience (despite her high skill, and according to Eugenie, probably being the most capable guard.) The key issue before is that she was just a stone-cold bad ass. This didn't really sell the story that anyone doubted her. When we brought the VA back in, we workshopped some ideas as a group and ended up with this latest (and so weird and fun) performance. Maybe a very different Libby, but I'm super happy with how she turned out. The VA really reinvented the character in a way I never would have imagined."'' ==Gallery== FO76OB Libby keyart.jpg|Libby in the ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'' keyart FO76 Libby face.png|Libby Wen FO76 Libby.png|Libby Wen FO76 Libby Carver.png|Libby and Carver at Big Bend Tunnel east before the ''Once in a Blue Moon'' update FO76WL SQ03 Libby Wen.jpg|Libby located at Big Bend Tunnel west ==References== {{References|2}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox companions FO76}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Blue Ridge Caravan Company characters]] [[ru:Либби Уэн]]

([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) Afterward, Rudy's brothers designated him as their man on the road. This new job for Rudy has kept him at [[Big Bend Tunnel]] in [[Appalachia]], selling canned goods, water and family recipes to prospective clients.Rudy Fernandez: ''"The usual, food, water, various delicious secret family recipes that I'll take to the grave. That sort of thing."''
([[Rudy Fernandez/Dialogue|Rudy Fernandez's dialogue]]) While working with Blue Ridge, Rudy has kept his role as resident comedian alongside running deliveries and selling special food items like [[pepperoni roll]]s, the latter of which he will talk about at length. During caravans through Big Bend Tunnel, Rudy is often paired with [[Aries]] as his guard.Events of [[Riding Shotgun]]. Rudy likes Aries, but is frequently perturbed by his macabre personality.Rudy Fernandez: ''"{{Tooltip|I like you, Aries, but you're freaking me the hell out.|Getting nervous}}"''
([[Rudy Fernandez/Dialogue|Rudy Fernandez's dialogue]]) Rudy has also kept the memory of his ''abuela'' and her cooking close to him. In addition to his current gastronomic wares, Rudy has been attempting to recreate the old recipe for his ''abuela''{{'}}s pozole. Rudy also aims to sell the recipe and [[Rudy's Canned Pozole|canned servings of the pozole]], which would create revenue for both the Fernandez family cannery and Blue Ridge.Rudy Fernandez: ''"Okay, maybe I've been a little distracted. I'm trying to recreate an old home recipe my Abuela used to make when I was a kid. I mean, if I can make it like I remember, then maybe we can sell it. Bring in a few more caps for the caravan, and some to send home, too."''
([[Rudy Fernandez/Dialogue|Rudy Fernandez's dialogue]]) During the quest [[Costa Business: Rudy]], manager [[Vinny Costa]] takes note of Rudy's hyperfocus, saying that it has led to Rudy being distracted on caravans.[[Vinny Costa]]: ''"Rudy's been distracted lately, not really paying attention. Sure he ain't a guard or anything like that but its{{Sic}} not good for business. Gonna get himself killed, or worse lose the merchandise. Do me a favor and see if you can find out what it is he keeps daydreamin' about."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) Rudy will ask the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dwellers]] to seek out the ingredients he needs for the pozole, so that it can be taste-tested and eventually added to his list of wares.[[Rudy's shopping list]] Rudy cannot go out himself due to his responsibilities at Big Bend Tunnel, and funding a caravan for a shopping trip would rack up fees and upset his brothers.Rudy Fernandez: ''"I need someone to go scavenge some ingredients for me. I got a good base going but I don't have everything. There's something missing. I can't leave 'cause I have responsibilities here. And my brothers would kill me if they knew I was wracking up caravan fees for a shopping trip, heh. Think you could find a few things for me?"''
([[Rudy Fernandez/Dialogue|Rudy Fernandez's dialogue]]) After the ingredients are gathered and Rudy makes the stew, the Vault Dwellers can sample the pozole and offer their opinion on it.Vault 76 dweller: ''"[Sample the stew] Sure, I'll try some."''
Rudy Fernandez: ''"Don't leave me in suspense now! How's it taste?"''
([[Rudy Fernandez/Dialogue|Rudy Fernandez's dialogue]]) He will be emotional and thankful if told that the pozole would make his ''abuela'' proud.Vault 76 dweller: ''"Hey this is pretty good. Your Abuela would be proud!"''
Rudy Fernandez: ''"Aw, you're gunna make me tear up. Here, take some for the road. A-and, hey, glad you like it!"''
([[Rudy Fernandez/Dialogue|Rudy Fernandez's dialogue]]) If he is told that the pozole is too burnt, he will panic and attempt to market it as "lightly barbequed."Vault 76 dweller: ''"Do you know Esme from the Refuge? Because you really know how to burn a soup."''
Rudy Fernandez: ''"Who? What? Ah. No that... That wasn't supposed to happen. Uh, uh- no worries though! I can just market this batch as "lightly barbequed." I-I'll have to try again 'til I get it just right. Luckily I have plenty of ingredients now. Thanks for that. Oh! One last thing..."''
([[Rudy Fernandez/Dialogue|Rudy Fernandez's dialogue]]) Regardless, Rudy will refine the recipe and begin selling it.Vault 76 dweller: ''"Tried Rudy's soup yet? It was pretty awful."''
[[Vinny Costa]]: ''"Really? Batch I tasted wasn't so bad. Must have improved his recipe. He started selling it now."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) Even if a "lightly barbequed" label does not work out,Vault 76 dweller: ''"How'd the "lightly barbequed" stew turn out?"''
Rudy Fernandez: ''"The "lightly Barbequed" angle didn't go down so well, but the next batch came out great!"''
([[Rudy Fernandez/Dialogue|Rudy Fernandez's dialogue]]) Rudy also sends the recipe and pozole back home to his brothers. Rudy says that it is not quite how they remembered it, but still made them nostalgic. However, Rudy's brothers rebuffed his subsequent request to return to work at the cannery; Rudy was just happy to make them laugh. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion =yes |perm companion = |perk = |wares =*Food |caps = yes |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |events involved = [[Riding Shotgun]] |quests started = |quests involved = [[Costa Business: Rudy]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Riding Shotgun|Event: Riding Shotgun]]: Rudy may be one of the candidates that will need to be guarded. He will be guarded by [[Aries]]. * [[Costa Business: Rudy]]: Rudy is trying to create a Mexican family recipe to sell the meal, and needs ingredients. Collect the five ingredients on Rudy's shopping list. Return to Rudy and choose to sample [[Rudy's Canned Pozole]] or not. If sampled, an opinion can be given to him. ===Other interactions=== * If the player has the [[Herbivore]] mutation, they can tell Rudy that they do not eat meat, causing Rudy to be embarrassed that he offered the pozole. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Letterman's jacket and jeans (Fallout 76)|Letterman's jacket and jeans]]
[[Newsboy cap (Fallout 76)|Newsboy cap]]
[[Black-rim glasses (Fallout 76)|Black-rim glasses]] |weapon = |otheritem =[[Backpack (Fallout 76)|Blue Ridge Caravan backpack]] |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== * Rudy has a slight stutter, which can be seen in several lines of dialogue with him, though it is not ever acknowledged by himself or any other character.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Oh, look at the time! I better get going."''
Rudy Fernandez: ''"{{Tooltip|Wait, wait, wait! Don't-don't-don't leave without hearing me out! Please?|backtracking a bit. almost begging.}}"''
([[Rudy Fernandez/Dialogue|Rudy Fernandez's dialogue]])Rudy Fernandez: ''"Ah, th-th-tha-thats too bad. Well if you ever change your mind come back and I'll have a sample for ya."''
([[Rudy Fernandez/Dialogue|Rudy Fernandez's dialogue]]) * Rudy could previously be found in a tent at [[Big Bend Tunnel west]] prior to the ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'' update. He was moved to permanently reside at [[Big Bend Tunnel east]] with the aforementioned update. ==Appearances== Rudy Fernandez appears {{In|FO76WL}}. This is a reference to a similar line spoken by the [[w:c:elderscrolls:Khajiit|Khajiit]] in ''[[wikipedia:The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim|The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim]]'', another [[Bethesda Softworks]] title (''"Khajiit has wares, if you have coin."''). [[Carl McKevitt]], who contributed to much of the Blue Ridge Caravan Company's design and writing, including Rudy, confirmed that this was intentional.BGS_Carl ([[Carl McKevitt]]) [https://web.archive.org/web/20230429091148/https://i.imgur.com/XVCTYZ6.png on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord] ==Gallery== FO76OB Rudy keyart.jpg|Rudy in the ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'' keyart FO76WL Rudy Fernandez.jpg|Rudy at [[Big Bend Tunnel west]] before ''Once in a Blue Moon'' FO76WL SQ04 Rudy Fernandez.jpg|Rudy sitting ==References== {{References|2}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox vendors FO76}} {{Navbox companions FO76}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders merchants]] [[Category:Blue Ridge Caravan Company characters]] [[ru:Руди Фернандес]]

Vinny Costa.wikitext:
{{Infobox character |games =FO76, FO76WL, FO76OB |image =FO76WL_Vinny_Costa.png |name =Vincent Costa |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |affiliation =[[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] |role =Manager |family =[[Luca Costa]] - nephew |location =[[Big Bend Tunnel east]] |nicknames =Vinny |events =[[Riding Shotgun]] |quests =[[Costa Business]] |level =14 |derived = |actor =[[Chris Andrew Ciulla|Chris Ciulla]] |dialogue =[[Vinny Costa/Dialogue]] |edid =E05_Caravan_VinnyCosta |formid ={{ID|0056f557}} |refid ={{ID|0056f558}} }} {{Quotation|We're always looking for another gun to hire. We're in the business of shooting anyone that gets between our merchants and their destination. If you're interested in joining up, just ask me. I'll let you know if we've got a caravan ready to roll out. Just be ready for a fight. We've been real popular lately, if you catch my meaning. It can turn into a regular fireworks show in there.|sound=Vinnie Costa 00573ec5 1.ogg}} '''Vincent "Vinny" Costa''' is a supervisor and head of operations for the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] in [[Appalachia]], found at [[Big Bend Tunnel east]] {{in|FO76WL}}. ==Background== Vinny works as the head of operations of the Blue Ridge Caravan Company's operations in the [[Big Bend Tunnel]] and all around Appalachia, organizing caravans and hiring guns for hire to escort them throughout the territory. Vinny has known [[Joanna Mayfield]] since well before the [[Great War]], during the company's heyday trucking goods through the [[Blue Ridge Parkway]], and is, in fact, one of the few who can call her by the nickname Jo.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Who is in charge of the Blue Ridge Caravan Company?"''
Vinny Costa: ''"That would be Ms. Joanna Mayfield. Or Jo. But newcomers don't get to call her "Jo." So don't. She's been in charge of things since before the war, when we was running trucks up and down the Blue Ridge Parkway. She's running things from our headquarters, well away from here, but she's been planning a visit. We'll see."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) He will even compromise and do favors for her, like posting [[Vera Thornberg]] at the [[Middle Mountain Pitstop]],Vault 76 dweller: "''What can you tell me about Vera?"''
Vinny Costa: "''{{tooltip|She's our rookie. Set her up with an easy gig up at the Middle Mountain Pitstop as a favour to Joanna.|Asked about Vera. Exposition on the location.}} {{tooltip|Hearin' she has her head in the clouds lately, makin' all sorts of silly mistakes. Need someone to go snap her out of it.|Asked about Vera. Exposition on the problem.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) as she pulled him out of his old life and helped him find a way forward, abandoning the temptations of the mob lifestyle for a position as Blue Ridge's Head of Operations.[[Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries#Staff and Clients for Appalachia|Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries; Blue Ridge terminal, Staff and Clients for Appalachia]] Vinny has been involved in organized crime since before the bombs dropped, and brought some members of his former crew onboard after the apocalypse. [[Kieran Kennedy]] and [[Tommy Ten-Toes]] are two of these former associates, and Vinny has explicitly forbidden them from speaking about the past.Tommy Ten-Toes: "''{{tooltip|Workin' for Blue Ridge is a lot easier than running jobs for... Wait a minute, Vinny said no talkin' bout that.|Almost let slip that he used to work in the mob (even tho no one actually asked). Thinks he got the upper hand}}"''
([[Tommy Ten-Toes/Dialogue#51|Tommy Ten-Toes' dialogue]]) Additionally, he regards connecting Blue Ridge up north, near the coast, to be a waste of time, due to "too many burned bridges" there.[[Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries#Northern Routes|Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries; Vinny Costa's terminal, Northern Routes]] Vinny runs a tight ship in general and was selected by Joanna to lead the push into Appalachia, along with a hand-picked crew of guards and merchants, building on Joanna's impressive work east of Appalachian. There is some friction: Aside from morale issues that cropped up during the stay in Appalachia, he also has his nephew, [[Luca Costa|Luca]], to take care of. As much as he loves him, Luca doesn't get a free ride on account of blood ties,Vault 76 dweller: ''"What's it like being related to Vinny?"''
Luca Costa: ''"It's got its perks, no-one wants to start shit with the boss' nephew, y'know? But Vinny's not the coddling type either, I don't get a free pass."''
([[Luca Costa/Dialogue|Luca Costa's dialogue]]) but has issues pulling his weight. Vinny also has to deal with [[Aries]], whom he considers a freak and does not enjoy dealing with him,Vault 76 dweller: ''"Really? The other members don't need help?"''
Vinny Costa: ''"Eh, everyone else is fine. {{Tooltip|Only thing that'll fix my nephew Luca's problems is my boot up his ass. Love the kid and all, but there's no talkin' sense to him.|Not a big concern for him}} As for Minerva and the big lug? She's our top performer, no troubles there-- and Tommy's a pro. {{Tooltip|I guess there's Aries, but, uh... I wouldn't ask my worst enemy to talk to that freak longer than they have to.|Side of the mouth}} {{Tooltip|You could always ask him what he's got going on, but, uh... Good luck with that.|But me? no thanks.}}"''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]])Vault 76 dweller: ''"How about the other members?"''
Vinny Costa: ''"{{Tooltip|Eh, everybody else is doin' all right. With Jo at the helm, we're normally runnin' pretty smooth. We're about back to that now, thanks to you.|Not TOO appreciative}} Granted, my nephew Luca will always be a pain, and Aries will always be a creep, but, uh... Let's see. Ah, right. There's Minerva and Tommy. Hard to pin down, but when I see 'em, they always seem chipper. She's got good deals, too. Make sure you peruse if you bump into her. Oh, and if ya see Tommy Ten-Toes... While I know he can't count that high, tell him he still owes me 50 caps."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) on account of his flippant attitude and constant mocking (not sparing Vinny's baldness,Vault 76 dweller: "''Have any leads on work around here?"''
Aries: "''{{tooltip|If you look carefully, you can see a shiny glint from the top of Vinny Costa's dome. It's like a distress flare that says: help me.|Mocking. Vinny is totally bald.}} He's right there, so... If there's something that needs doing, Vinny will pay you for it."''
 which is a major source of embarrassment for him).Vault 76 dweller: "''Okay, I'll get out of your hair."''
Vinny Costa: "''You got real smart fuckin' mouth, you know that?"''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) However, Vinny does not pull rank, as he is first and foremost a businessman who looks out for the interests of his company. Appalachia turned out to be a gold mine for Blue Ridge. As they are one of the only outside sources of trade goons, the supplies they bring through Big Bend can reach [[Foundation]], [[the Crater]], and many more, smaller settlements, then sell for a high price. Even raiders give them safe passage,Vault 76 dweller: "''Where is the caravan headed?"''
Vinny Costa: "''All over Appalachia. We ship to Foundation, Crater, a few smaller settlements here or there. Once we're west of Big Bend, the routes open up. Since we're one of the few sources of outside cargo coming in, even the folks up in Crater give us a pass."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) with the noted exception of the [[Blood Eagles]]. While Blue Ridge has secured both sides of the Big Bend Tunnel, the tunnel itself is plagued by constant attacks and security posts established within are frequently taken down in the process. Vinny relies on his guard cadre to keep the merchants safe, which also makes him extremely concerned about their morale and well-being.Events of [[Costa Business]]. While he will hire people to fix the morale issues, due to his position as manager he will not think twice about exploiting the information provided for the benefit of the company, such as greatly increasing the commission for [[Eugenie]], if informed that she is sourcing her stock independently, rather than the compound Joanna was hoping to establish a trade route to,Vault 76 dweller: "''She's fine-- hey, did you know she moved out from that ghoul compound? I read all about it."''
Vinny Costa: "''She what? She moved outta that place? Shit, kid, you shoulda said that sooner. Ain't no way I can overlook it: her being a free agent changes some, uh... pricing options. You don't know it but you just made my day, pal. Probably ruined ol' Eugenie's year but eh, she'll be fine."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) or punishing [[Libby Wen]] by posting her to a safe, boring trade route if told that she is sourcing her spare parts from non-Blue Ridge traders.Vault 76 dweller: "''Is Libby shooting straight again?"''
Vinny Costa: "''Couldn't get much concrete info, but you were on to somethin' all right. I've moved Libby to a, uh, lower energy post for now. Maybe teach her a thing or two about keepin' contacts outside the network. Well, her dead-eye is back, that's for sure. Still totting that goofy old gun, though."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) He does have a softer side: He has much more patience with Kieran, his former associate, even if he disapproves of his life choices (establishing and looking after his family), and is quite protective of [[Carver Timmerman]]. He sees the makings of a capable merchant in the young Timmerman, and would like to help him step into adulthood.Vault 76 dweller: "''I'm not really looking for a baby sitting gig."''
Vinny Costa: "''{{tooltip|Well you're in luck, ya joker, because this ain't that. Carver's a big boy. Just needs help steppin' into those shoes. You don't want to help, walk.|Annoyed}}"''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) However, while Vinny will pay a contractor, he will not use company assets to solve the problem for him.Vault 76 dweller: "''So, take a stroll over to Lewisburg. It's close."''
Carver Timmerman: "''Oh, I have... I've even gotten as close as my old house-- or at least what I think is my old house. But it's just too dangerous... Especially alone. Vinny would never let me borrow a guard for something personal, either."''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) Overally, Vinny balances personal sympathy with professional concerns. This includes rebuffing Luca's attempts to sell his homemade explosives as Blue Ridge merchandise.Vault 76 dweller: ''"Why doesn't Vinny want to sell them?"''
Luca Costa: ''"He's worried about them not being up to par, but they're good quality. Uncle Vinny just doesn't want any, uh, mishaps. Accidental detonations and such. Says it'd look bad on the business. They're as safe as any other explosives. Mostly. Once it's foolproof I'll convince him."''
([[Luca Costa/Dialogue|Luca Costa's dialogue]]) Vinny dismissed them as "homemade cherrybombs,"[[Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries#%5BIntelligence_10+%5D_Recover_Deleted_Entries|Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries; Vinny Costa's terminal, Employee Complaints]] but Luca continues to sell them off the books as he hopes to have Vinny officially distribute his wares eventually - once he gets the recipe just right.Luca Costa: ''"Once I get the recipe sorted I'm gonna convince Uncle Vinny to start distributing my explosives. Who doesn't need a bomb every now and then."''
([[Luca Costa/Dialogue|Luca Costa's dialogue]]) Vinny is not on great terms with everyone in his team, but it is not something that bothers him, as long as they do their job right. His preference for short, to-the-point communication leads to some issues being ignored or misinterpreted: [[Rudy Fernandez]] believes that Vinny is not as focused on the good of the company as he declares to be, as while he pays a generous bonus for lost cargo recovered from Big Bend, the merchandise is not returned to the merchants. Rudy feels it suggests Vinny runs a business on the side, selling the loot himself.[[Rudy Fernandez]]: ''"Everyone says the same thing: "guard the Brahmin." Sure, that's important, but me? I'd aim for those caches. Vinny pays a mean bonus for those things. Between you and me, I think he sells it himself. I sure as hell haven't gotten any missing pepperoni rolls sent back my way, if you know what I mean."''
([[Rudy Fernandez/Dialogue#142|Rudy's dialogue]]) The latest problems for Vinny, beyond morale, is the future of Blue Ridge. He is starting to see wisdom in Joanna's decision to focus on strengthening their position and consolidating their power. The more Blue Ridge spreads out, the weaker it gets, and with the routes growing ever more dangerous, the future is very much in flux. With other settlements building up in Appalachia, Vinny is starting to realize that Blue Ridge similarly placing down roots in the area could be a smart move.[[Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries#Western Routes|Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries; Vinny Costa's terminal, Western Routes]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |ghost =yes |events started =[[Riding Shotgun|Event: Riding Shotgun]] |quests started =[[Costa Business]] |quests involved = }} ===Quests=== * [[Riding Shotgun|Event: Riding Shotgun]]: Speaking to Vinny provides the option of starting this promptable event, in which Vinny calls for a trader and a caravan guard to make their way through Big Bend Tunnel, accompanied by the player character. * [[Costa Business]]: Vinny is the main quest giver for these seven non-repeatable daily side quests. Each deals with a different member of his crew and has the player resolving a major morale issue undercutting their performance at work, with a variety of outcomes, depending on how the player handles the situation and whether they inform Costa of what was truly happening. The crew involved in the quests are [[Costa Business: Kieran|Kieran Kennedy]], [[Costa Business: Eugenie|Eugenie]], [[Costa Business: Rudy|Rudy Fernandez]], [[Costa Business: Libby|Libby Wen]], [[Costa Business: Herschel|Herschel Klein]], [[Costa Business: Vera|Vera Thornberg]], and finally [[Costa Business: Carver|Carver Timmerman]]. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Mobster suit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Vinny Costa appears only {{in|FO76WL}}. His character was expanded upon in the ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'' update. ==Gallery== FO76WL SQ Vinny Costa.jpg|Vinny FO76 bm costabusiness.png|Vinny in the Costa Business icon ==References== {{References|2}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Once in a Blue Moon human characters]] [[Category:Blue Ridge Caravan Company characters]] [[ru:Винни Коста]]

W05_MQ_001P_BatterFaction |class =raiderClass |combat style=Default |CK race =HumanRace |voice type =W05_NPCM_Batter_Wayward |actor =[[Josh Robert Thompson]] |dialogue =[[Batter/Dialogue]] |edid =W05_Wayward_Batter |formid ={{ID|00405eaa}} |refid ={{ID|0040bd10}} }} {{Quotation|Lady, I will paint the walls with you if you don't tell me where Crane's treasure is, right now!|Batter to Duchess|sound=Batter 0040bce5_1.ogg}} '''Batter''' is a member of the [[Free Radicals]] raider gang in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Batter was sent by [[Roper]], leader of the Free Radicals, to get information on [[Crane (Wastelanders)|Crane]] from [[Duchess]] at [[the Wayward]]. Roper: ''"Always figured it'd take someone coloring with a full box of crayons to find us our prize."''
([[Jacky (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#89|Jacky]] and [[Roper/Dialogue#87|Roper's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |killable = yes |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Wayward Souls]] }} ===Quests=== [[Wayward Souls]]: Batter is holding up Duchess at the Wayward, being interrupted by the player characters. '''Daniel''' is a man living at [[Anchor Farm]] in [[Appalachia]]. 

==Background==
Daniel migrated into Appalachia with his family, seeking to rebuild there. He has no interest in "The Treasure of Appalachia," and simply wants a peaceful place to live in privacy.

When arriving, Daniel and his group were accosted by the [[Free Radicals]] to provide food and supplies to them every month. A woman in Daniel's group, [[Maggie (Wastelanders)|Maggie]], stood up to the raiders, refusing to cooperate, and Daniel killed her on the spot to preserve the peace. With the offer of being given protection by the gang, Daniel agreed to personally deliver monthly shipment supplies to [[Roper]]'s gang at their base of operations at the [[WV Lumber Co.]]<ref>[[Agreement with Radicals]]</ref> Once a month, Daniel goes with [[Murray (Wastelanders)|Murray]] to deliver food, ammo and scrap.

Currently, he resides at the Anchor Farm with his child [[Hannah (Wastelanders)|Hannah]], a man named [[Xavier]], a man named Murray, and a woman named [[Ursala]].

===Quests===
[[Hunter for Hire]]: The Vault Dweller is referred to visit the Anchor farm by [[Mordecai McCoy]] who mentions Daniel's family has had to deal with the Free Radicals already. Daniel may be questioned and he will only give the password to their hideout if the Vault Dweller passes a Perception 3+, Charisma 3+, or Strength 3+ check. Alternatively, the [[Agreement with Radicals]] holotape may be found to confront Daniel instead.

===Other interactions===
{{Cleanup|More information about Danie's possible rewards and drop rates should be added.}}
* Once the holotape Agreement with Radicals is found, Daniel can be confronted with the revelation that he killed [[Maggie (Wastelanders)|Maggie]]. Daniel shows no regret and doubles down on his actions. He further justifies the murder explaining that Maggie was going to get the rest of the Anchor settlers killed by opposing the Free Radicals. He felt she would not listen and views his actions as being pragmatic and doing what he had to in order to keep his daughter safe in a nasty situation.
* If Roper has been killed, Daniel can be spoken to and he mentions he already knows. A grateful Daniel will give some supplies, potentially [[Recipe: Brain bombs]] or [[Recipe: Blackberry honey crisp]]. He may also give [[Recipe: Cutting fluid]], known for being a rare plan which has a 20% chance to be given.
**However, Roper must be killed before [[The Elusive Crane]] if the player chose not to join the gang, otherwise he will not appear in the lumber mill, locking the player out of the rewards. If the player joins the gang, Roper can be killed anytime and Daniel will give the rewards.

'''Friedrich (GM-05)'''<ref>[[The Whitespring Resort terminal entries#Week of 10/11/77|The Whitespring Resort terminal entries; Maintenance room terminal, Maintenance Logs; Week of 10/11/77]]</ref> is a [[Mister Gutsy (Fallout 76)|Mister Gutsy]] serving as a [[Fallout 76 vendors|vendor]] at [[the Whitespring Resort]] in [[Appalachia]].            

==Background==
Friedrich is one of the robotic vendors that the Whitespring Resort replaced their human staff with shortly before the [[Great War]].<ref>[[The Whitespring 2080 Initiative]]</ref> He resides in the Artisan's Corner store of the Whitesprings' mall area and mainly sells components and crafting materials for the player character to use at the various crafting benches in his store.

He was programmed to offer Wilderness Survival classes from December 15, 2078 to January 15, 2079. Although touted as survival classes, they covered topics such as taxidermy, fencing and hunting big game with flamethrowers,<ref>[[The Whitespring Resort terminal entries#Class Schedule|The Whitespring Resort terminal entries; Artisan's Corner terminal, Class Schedule]]</ref> rather than any topics with any practical survival value.<ref>[[The Whitespring staff meeting, 12.27.79]]: "''{{tooltip|Friedrich's classes are a joke, but the guests have been pitching in.|Not well. Friedrich is a robot teaching useless survival courses.}}''"</ref>

I was glad to leave that shithole, especially after what happened to my pops.|Maggie regarding [[Monongah]]|sound=Maggie Williams.ogg}} '''Maggie "Mags" Williams''' is a settler living in the [[Appalachia]]n town of [[Foundation]]. ==Background== Maggie was born and raised in [[Monongah]] by her father [[Earle Williams|Earle]], with her mother, a suspected chem addict, leaving the family early on.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Are you from Monongah?"''
Maggie Williams: ''"Yep, born and raised in that dying mining town. I was glad to leave that shithole, especially after what happened to my pops."''
([[Maggie Williams/Dialogue|Maggie Williams' dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What about your mom?"''
Maggie Williams: ''"What about her? She left us early on. Who knows what got to her first; the chems or the bombs."''
([[Maggie Williams/Dialogue|Maggie Williams' dialogue]]) She gave her father a [[Earle's pocket watch|pocket watch]] with "Love you Pops ♡ Mags" engraved on it. The watch had a photograph of Maggie and her father inside and he always kept it with him. After her father and some of his miner colleagues got trapped inside [[Monongah Mine]], due to [[Deke Sykes]] blowing up the entrance in January [[Timeline#2076|2076]],[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How did he end up in Monongah Mine?"''
Maggie Williams: ''"He and some other townsfolk got some liquid courage one night and decided to go up to the mine. I knew that damn [[Bourbon (Fallout 76)|bourbon]] would be the end of him somehow. They kept goin' on about getting the last of what they could before that [[Deke Sykes]] from Hornwright Industrial closed up the mine. Well, that son of a bitch ended up blastin' the entrance closed with everyone still inside."''
([[Maggie Williams/Dialogue|Maggie Williams' dialogue]]) she tried to gain entry to the mine to search for her father, but was unsuccessful due to too much rubble being in the way. She was told by the workers that her father was somewhere else, although she did not entirely believe them and suspected the workers were paid by [[Hornwright Industrial]] to keep silent or the company didn't want to deal with the expenses of a rescue mission. With no one offering to help her clear the rubble just to make sure anyway, Maggie clawed at the rubble until her hands bled, but she was forced to be escorted away and all she could do was hope that the workers were being truthful.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Why didn't anyone try to get them out?"''
Maggie Williams: ''"You don't think I tried?! I clawed at the rubble until my hands bled and they had to drag me away. They told me that my pops ran off, and said the others left Monongah since there was no more work. I think it was some sort of cover up. They either got paid off by the Hornwrights to keep quiet, or they didn't want to deal withe the expenses of a rescue mission."''
([[Maggie Williams/Dialogue|Maggie Williams' dialogue]]) Two and a half decades later, Maggie resides in Foundation and wishes to find closure on her father. She accepts that her father must be dead from either starvation or radiation, although hopes he did not suffer in his final moments. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started =[[Something Sentimental]] |quests involved =[[A Colossal Problem]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Something Sentimental]]: Maggie asks the player character to find her father in Monongah Mine and suggests using a nuke to blow open the entrance. She also wishes for the player character to find her father's [[Earle's pocket watch|pocket watch]] which is engraved and has a photograph of Maggie and her father inside. * [[A Colossal Problem]]: Maggie needs to be given Earle's pocket watch. ===Other interactions=== * The player character may choose to be truthful about her father's fate or lie to her. Maggie becomes angered if she is lied to about nothing being found, not believing the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]], though the player can keep the pocket watch. If she is told about the pocket watch, this will reward 300 XP whether or not the full truth is told. She is also surprised if she is called Mags, noting only her father called her that. * [[A father's goodbye]], picked up near the beginning of Monongah Mine, can be given to Maggie who is thankful to hear her father's voice. * Once [[Penelope Hornwright]] moves to Foundation, Maggie can be asked for her thoughts. Due to her past experiences with the Hornwright family, who engaged in unfair worker practices, she is wary towards the only surviving member, Penny, and remarks that Penny's current ghoulish appearance is a reflection of who is she as a person.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You know Penny Hornwright is in Foundation, right?"''
Maggie Williams: ''"Yeah, I know she's in town. I've been keeping an eye on her. Shame about her face... I guess the Hornwright's ugliness is finally showin' up on the outside."''
([[Maggie Williams/Dialogue|Maggie Williams' dialogue]]) ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Miner uniform]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Maggie Williams appears in ''[[Fallout 76]]'', introduced in ''[[The Legendary Run (update)|The Legendary Run]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. ==Gallery== Steel Dawn promo art.jpg|Maggie seen in the bottom left of the art for ''Steel Dawn'' FO76SD Maggie.png|Maggie on the ''Steel Dawn'' art ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox Foundation}} [[Category:Settler characters]] [[Category:The Legendary Run human characters]] [[fr:Maggie Williams]] [[ru:Мэгги Уильямс]]

Never forget your pops loves you more than anything.|sound=A_father's_goodbye.ogg}} '''Earle Williams''' is a unique [[wendigo colossus]] located inside the [[Monongah Mine]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Earle Williams worked at a [[Monongah Mine|local mine]] just outside [[Monongah]] before the [[Great War]]. He was a single father to [[Maggie Williams|Maggie]] after his wife left early on.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Do you have any other family?"''
[[Maggie Williams]]: ''"It was just me and my pops. We didn't need anyone else. I guess now it's just me."''
Vault Dweller: ''"What about your mom?"''
[[Maggie Williams]]: ''"What about her? She left us early on. Who knows what got her first; the chems or [[Great War|the bombs]]."''
([[Maggie Williams/Dialogue|Maggie Williams' dialogue]]) [[Hornwright Industrial]] bought the rights to the mine in April [[Timeline#2075|2075]], replacing the workers with [[Auto-Miner]]s.[[Hornwright's proposal]][[Monongah Mine terminal entries#Supervisor's Notes - 04.14.75|Monongah Mine terminal entries; Mining supervisor's terminal, Supervisor's Notes - 04.14.75]][[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Why was Monongah dying?"''
[[Maggie Williams]]: ''"Hornwright Industrial came swoopin' in like they were our saviors, and gave the town a bunch of money for the mining rights. They took away jobs from the miners thanks to their robots, took everything they could from the mine, and then left us high and dry."''
([[Maggie Williams/Dialogue|Maggie Williams' dialogue]]) At first, this seemed like a blessing to the town which was plagued by financial hardship.[[Monongah terminal entries#Meeting Minutes 04.02.75|Monongah terminal entries; Town Council terminal, Meeting Minutes 04.02.75]] The Auto-Miners quickly and efficiently extracted all [[coal]] from the mine, fully exhausting every vein in January 2076. As Hornwright Industrial prepared to leave the mine that January,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"When did this happen?"''
[[Maggie Williams]]: ''"This was back in January of '76, after Hornwright cleaned out everything they could from the mine."''
([[Maggie Williams/Dialogue|Maggie Williams' dialogue]])[[Monongah Mine terminal entries#Supervisor's Notes - 01.07.76|Monongah Mine terminal entries; Mining supervisor's terminal, Supervisor's Notes - 01.07.76]] Williams and some other townsfolk drunkenly decided to steal some supplies from the mine before everything was taken away. Shortly thereafter, supervisor [[Deke Sykes]] blew up the entrance with everyone still inside.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How did he end up in Monongah Mine?"''
[[Maggie Williams]]: ''"He and some other townsfolk got some liquid courage one night and decided to go up to the mine. I knew that damn [[Bourbon (Fallout 76)|bourbon]] would be the end of him somehow. They kept goin' on about getting the last of what they could before that [[Deke Sykes]] from Hornwright Industrial closed up the mine. Well, that son of a bitch ended up blastin' the entrance closed with everyone still inside."''
([[Maggie Williams/Dialogue|Maggie Williams' dialogue]]) Though Maggie tried to dig her father out with her bare hands, she was pulled away by others from Monongah and lied to that he and the others had simply skipped town. She didn't believe them and reasoned they were either paid off by the Hornwrights or were unwilling to pay for a rescue mission.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Why didn't anyone try to get them out?"''
[[Maggie Williams]]: ''"You don't think I tried?! I clawed at the rubble until my hands bled and they had to drag me away. They told me that my pops ran off, and said the others left Monongah since there was no more work. I think it was some sort of cover up. They either got paid off by the Hornwrights to keep quiet, or they didn't want to deal withe the expenses of a rescue mission."''
([[Maggie Williams/Dialogue|Maggie Williams' dialogue]]) Meanwhile, in the mine, Williams and the others were facing a difficult decision: there was no food in the mine, but one of the miners, [[James (Monongah Mine)|James]], died from injuries sustained from the entrance collapsing. Several survivors agreed to [[cannibalism|cannibalize]] his corpse, including Williams, though others refused and stated they would rather die and be eaten than eat another person.[[One choice]] At first, Williams questioned whether he should eat a corpse, saying it "didn't seem right to him." After some time, as he and the others continued to eat those who died of starvation, he felt his sanity slip away, in part due to the lack of a day and night cycle. Eventually, his hunger got the best of him and he found himself wanting to eat those not yet dead.[[Earle's journal]] Williams also left Maggie a [[A father's goodbye|holotape]]. Everyone's content just... trying to get by.|sound=Russell Dorsey 005b66f7_1.ogg}} '''Initiate Russell Dorsey''' is a recruit in the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force]] at [[Fort Atlas]] in [[Appalachia]]. A great admirer of the Brotherhood even before his recruitment, Dorsey worked with [[Vault 76]]'s former [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|dwellers]] to renovate [[ATLAS Observatory]] into a base for the Brotherhood. Following their arrival from [[New California|California]], Dorsey was granted the rank of Initiate. He currently greets new arrivals at Fort Atlas and is enthused to talk about the Brotherhood and his role in it.[[Dorsey's diary]] ==Background== Hailing from [[State#Maryland|Maryland]], Dorsey arrived in [[Appalachia]] around 2103, and moved in at [[Foundation]] with the rest of the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]]. While on scouting missions, he came across the remnants of the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Appalachian Brotherhood of Steel]], culminating in a growing obsession with the Brotherhood, fueled by his findings of records and logs at [[Fort Defiance]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How do you know about the Brotherhood in the first place?"''
Russell Dorsey: ''"I left Maryland headed west, and hooked up with some of the original Foundation folks. Once here, I did patrols for them, scouting for supplies. Ended up finding some stuff the local Brotherhood left behind. That led me to Fort Defiance. Scary place. I had to move quick, but I'd found some logs and records. {{Tooltip|Frankly, I got a little obsessed. It was like the Round Table and Dad's Navy stories, all together! And now they're coming back!|excited, but a bit embarrassed by his own enthusiasm}}"''
([[Russell Dorsey/Dialogue|Russell Dorsey's dialogue]]) While he enjoyed his time at Foundation, he wanted to do more than just resettle the land.Russell Dorsey: ''"I used to work with the folks at Foundation. Hard workers, but I wanted something more than just settling."''
([[Russell Dorsey/Dialogue|Russell Dorsey's dialogue]]) He also encountered the [[Crater Raiders|Raiders]] at [[the Crater]], considering them nice, yet tough, but unable to see past their own profits.Russell Dorsey: ''"Those Crater types are tough, and nicer than you'd think, but they can't see past their own profit."''
([[Russell Dorsey/Dialogue|Russell Dorsey's dialogue]]) His father was part of the [[United States Navy|Navy]], and served as inspiration for his resolve to put in the effort to help the Brotherhood, as Dorsey was unable to join the now-defunct [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"This seems like a lot of effort. Why are you doing all this?"''
Russell Dorsey: ''"Honestly? I feel like I've needed this my whole life. Dad was Navy, back before the war. Always said it straightened him out, gave him purpose. Growing up in this...I wanted something...more. If the military still existed, I'd have joined that, but that's all over now. I wanted something bigger than just surviving. This feels like what I've been waiting for."''
([[Russell Dorsey/Dialogue|Russell Dorsey's dialogue]]) Upon hearing a broadcast from the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force]], Dorsey journeyed to ATLAS Observatory and took control of the derelict facility, seeking to organize supplies, build fortifications, and otherwise make the facility operational for their arrival.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"I'm here to help. What needs doing?"''
Russell Dorsey: ''"Message they broadcast was kinda garbled, but it seemed clear the Brotherhood has chosen ATLAS as a base. Makes sense they'd be looking to have supplies waiting when they get here. A group like that's going to want to be operational ASAP."''
([[Russell Dorsey/Dialogue|Russell Dorsey's dialogue]]) He closed off the entrance of the observatory to contain the guard robots, and began constructing additions on to the observatory, utilizing repaired [[Protectron (Fallout 76)|construction protections]], using hacking knowledge gained from a former [[RobCo Industries|RobCo]] employee named [[Greg (Fallout 76)|Greg]] to trick them into seeing him as a supervisor.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What's with all the robots around here?"''
Russell Dorsey: ''"Found them here when I came out. Pretty hostile bunch at first, but I learned a trick from a guy that used to work for RobCo. They've got a maintenance backdoor hardwired into them. Tricked them all into thinking I ran the joint, then put them to work. Pretty good, right? Got 'em doing a lot of the heavy lifting and such on the project. Makes my life a lot easier."''
([[Russell Dorsey/Dialogue|Russell Dorsey's dialogue]]) He hopes to utilize his efforts at ATLAS to convince the returning Brotherhood into seeing him as a valuable asset,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Do you think the Brotherhood is looking for new members?"''
Russell Dorsey: ''"Well, it sounds like they're coming out here to stay. I don't know if recruiting is in their plans, but I figure all this ought to make a convincing argument that I'm an asset they shouldn't pass up."''
([[Russell Dorsey/Dialogue|Russell Dorsey's dialogue]]) which ultimately paid off. He also left a [[Back in a bit|note]] asking anyone who passed by to not be a jerk by touching his stuff. After the Brotherhood contingent arrived, Dorsey was almost immediately made an official Initiate and can be found directly near the entrance of Fort Atlas, surrounded by Brotherhood hopefuls and other initiates. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Forging Trust]] * [[A Knight's Penance]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Forging Trust]]: Speaking to Dorsey is the first objective of the quest, in order to find out more about the Brotherhood. After asking him about speaking with the Brotherhood leaders, he freely admits that he is the wrong person to speak to and hints towards Knight Shin, who is located inside the fort's interior. * [[A Knight's Penance]]: Checking in with Dorsey is the first objective of this quest, following the events of ''Steel Dawn''. Dorsey informs about super mutant attacks taking place across the region, and hints that they may originate from the Uncanny Caverns. He asks to relay that information to Paladin Rahmani and Knight Shin inside the fort. ===Other interactions=== Russell was the main point of contact for the [[Fortifying ATLAS]] community event. He collected resources to build a base for the Brotherhood of Steel at the observatory and asked for the help of the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] from [[Vault 76]]. There were several crates surrounding him where Dwellers could drop off junk to contribute to the event during its run. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Combat armor (Fallout 76)|Combat armor right arm (Steel Dawn paint)]]
