She appears {{In|FO76SD}}. ==Background== ===Life on the West Coast=== Valdez is the daughter of a couple of early recruits in the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] known as the "Knights Valdez" and was enlisted by her parents into the organization as an apprentice [[Brotherhood of Steel ranks#Journeyman scribe|scribe]] at a young age. She spent most of her life in bunkers and raised by the Brotherhood. Under the tutelage of [[Hailey Takano|Scribe Hailey Takano]], Valdez learned to perform her role satisfactorily, taking a special interest in the operation of [[vertibird (Fallout 76)|vertibirds]] and other flying machines.[[Fort Atlas terminal entries#SCRIBE Valdez, Odessa|Fort Atlas terminal entries; Scribe Valdez's terminal, Brotherhood: Chapter Scrolls, SCRIBE Valdez, Odessa]] She is also skilled at programming code.Odessa Valdez: ''"Well, you know. Just trying to help where I can. Rusty nails and live wires are fun and all, but sometimes it's also nice to write code without having to get my hands dirty."''
([[Odessa Valdez/Dialogue|Odessa Valdez's dialogue]]) She feels, however, that being a scribe is merely the role her parents raised her into, instead of something she wishes to do as a life choice.Odessa Valdez: ''"Believe it or not, I didn't choose to be a Scribe. I was born into it. My parents chose this life for me. I've gotten used to it, but it isn't mine."''
([[Odessa Valdez/Dialogue|Odessa Valdez's dialogue]]) ===The expedition to Appalachia=== At some point prior or around [[Timeline#2103|2103]],[[Fort Atlas terminal entries#Brotherhood: Chapter Scrolls|Fort Atlas terminal entries; Scribe Valdez's terminal, Brotherhood: Chapter Scrolls]] Valdez volunteered for an expedition to [[Appalachia]] in the East Coast, excited at the chance of having an adventure like her peers. She took the place of Scribe Takano, who was unable to join due to health concerns. Valdez insisted Takano stay behind for her health as well. Valdez became the official scribe and keeper of the [[Codex|Scrolls]] of the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force]], and joined the original members of the expedition ([[Leila Rahmani|Paladin Rahmani]], [[Alan Connors|Knight Connors]], [[Matthew Thornberry|Knight Thornberry]], and [[Daniel Shin|Knight Shin]]) east across the wasteland. After many months of hiking, the team finally made it to [[Fort Atlas]], although Connors was killed in an incident while Thornberry went back to [[Lost Hills]]. Valdez took the loss very hard because Connors was like a fatherly mentor figure to her. ===Life at Fort ATLAS=== Valdez maintains her scribe duties and is in charge of repairing and monitoring technology. [[Marcia Leone]], despite her dislike of the Brotherhood, is known to respect Valdez. Valdez also plays hide-and-seek with her brother [[Maximo Leone|Max]]. She heard of the [[Rust Eagles]] and sent [[Pappas (Fallout 76)|Initiate Pappas]] to investigate the [[Metal Dome]]. Later, she sent [[Ellison|Initiate Ellison]] to investigate the [[Responders|reason]] for the [[Vertibird (Fallout 76)|vertibird]] flying near [[the Whitespring Resort]]. Valdez also once met with [[Grandma Junko]] and asked her about appliances. Valdez had to deal with the infighting between her two commanding officers, Paladin Leila Rahmani, and Knight Daniel Shin regarding the Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force's primary objective after arriving in Appalachia to rebuild the Brotherhood of Steel's influence in the area after it was wiped out previously with the deaths of [[Elizabeth Taggerdy|Paladin Elizabeth Taggerdy's]] Brotherhood chapter about 10 years prior. Aided by the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 residents]], Valdez is able to investigate the older workings of Fort Atlas, formerly the ATLAS Observatory, recovering an ultracite fuel cell that is later used by Rahmani and Shin to try and use an Enclave long-range transmitter to reestablish contact with [[Roger Maxson|Elder Roger Maxson]] and Lost Hills, but Rahmani, fearing punishment from the elders for what happened on their way to Appalachia, and Shin having remained ironclad to spilling that mistake to them once they could contact them again, destroys the transmitter, much to Valdez's shock and anger when they return to Fort Atlas later to deal with a super mutant assault on the base from the underground tunnels. ===Confronting Blackburn=== After the attack is repulsed and further evidence of the super mutants attacking other areas of Appalachia is found, Valdez joins a Vault Dweller with hitting [[Vault 96]] to capture [[Edgar Blackburn]], one of the civilians who came to Fort Atlas earlier for assistance from the Brotherhood, but was turned away by Shin, and has been using unwilling volunteers in his experiments to improve the [[Forced Evolutionary Virus]]. Rescuing several survivors including [[Cassie Halloway]] and getting them medical attention and evacuating them back to places like Foundation and Fort Atlas, Valdez and the Vault Dweller confront Blackburn who surrenders without a fight. When he later reveals that his colleagues are about to finish the F.E.V. at the [[West Tek research center (Fallout 76)|West Tek research facility]], Valdez is horrified by the consequences of if they are allowed to succeed. The Vault Dweller, along with Paladin Rahmani and Knight Shin, prevent the plan from coming to fruition, but only one of Valdez's superiors returns to Fort Atlas afterwards with the Vault Dwellers, revealing what became of the other one following the events at West Tek, and names the Vault Dwellers "Knight-Errant" in the Brotherhood. If the Vault Dwellers sided with Rahmani and spared Blackburn's colleagues [[Farha|Dr. Farha]], [[Nellie Wright]] and [[Jain (Steel Reign)|Dr. Jain]], they and their research will be placed under Valdez's supervision. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion =yes |ghoul =yes |quests started =* [[Mother of Invention]] |quests involved =* [[Forbidden Knowledge (Fallout 76)|Forbidden Knowledge]] * [[A Satisfied Conscience]] * [[The Catalyst]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Mother of Invention]]: Valdez challenges the Vault Dweller to investigate the lower area of Fort Atlas and its machinery to see how capable the Vault Dweller is of accurate analysis. This is the beginning of the Vault Dweller's recruitment into the Brotherhood. * [[Forbidden Knowledge (Fallout 76)|Forbidden Knowledge]]: Valdez is the recipient of the [[technical data]] if Mother of Invention is completed. * [[A Satisfied Conscience]]: Valdez and the Vault Dweller explore Vault 96 in search of the caravan survivors and [[Edgar Blackburn]]. * [[The Catalyst]]: Valdez appears at the very beginning and end of the quest. ===Other interactions=== * Valdez has her own [[Fort Atlas terminal entries#Scribe Valdez's terminal|terminal]] in Fort Atlas. She adds a new entry after [[The Best Defense]] is completed. * The Vault Dweller's performance during Mother of Invention can result in two different [[Valdez's letter of recommendation|letters of recommendation]]. If the "poor" letter is received, Valdez writes "nonexistent" for the Vault Dweller's technical ability. * Valdez may be the target of flirtation. She may react positively or negatively depending on interactions with her. She may also flirt back at a Vault Dweller regardless of gender, suggesting Valdez is [[LGBT representation in the Fallout series|LGBT+]]. {{Infobox character |games =FO76, FO76SD |image =FO76SD Shawn Hockman.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |role =Scavenger |location =[[Fort Atlas]] |quests =[[Forging Trust]] |level = |derived ={{Derived stats FO4|hp=75|ap=50}} |special ={{SPECIAL|0,4,0,0,0,5,0}} |aggression =Unaggressive |confidence =Average |assistance =Helps Nobody |factions = |class =raiderClass |combat style=Default |CK race =HumanRace |voice type =BS01_NPCM_ShawnHockman |actor =[[Faruq Tauheed]] |dialogue =[[Shawn Hockman/Dialogue]] |edid =BS01_ShawnHockman |formid ={{ID|005c2880}} |refid ={{ID|005c7173}} }} {{Quotation|The problem is that a couple of these Brotherhood clowns showed up and took a bunch of my stuff at gunpoint. I'm a peaceful man, I really am. Sure wasn't equipped to deal with armed thugs "requisitioning" the little I've managed to put together for myself. Never understood the Raiders. I like the quiet life, I don't need much, and I need trouble less. But after this, I get it. I came here to give the Brotherhood a chance to make things right. Else maybe I go to Crater and start doing things their way. At least they don't pretend to be the good guys.|sound=Shawn Hockman 005c9727_1.ogg}} '''Shawn Hockman''' is an independent scavenger operating in [[Appalachia]]. He is visiting [[Fort Atlas]] to protest after being robbed by [[Brotherhood of Zeal|a patrol]] claiming to be part of the [[Brotherhood of Steel]]. ==Background== Although he occasionally works with the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] of [[Foundation]] to get repairs and find inaccessible items, Shawn lives on his own and likes it that way, running independent scavenging jobs.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Would you tell me more about yourself?"''
Shawn Hockman: ''"I'm a scavenger, mainly. Always been pretty good with a set of tools, so I do all right for myself scrapping and fixing things. Trade what I find or fix with the folks at Foundation when I need something I can't get otherwise. Mostly, I like to be left alone."'' At some point, he was robbed at gunpoint by [[Brotherhood of Zeal|a group of power-armored men]] claiming to be from the [[Brotherhood of Steel]]. Regardless of whether or not the robbers were actually from the Brotherhood of Steel ([[Daniel Shin|Knight Shin]] insists they were not),A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Shawn Hockman was robbed by people claiming to be the Brotherhood."''
[[Daniel Shin|Knight Shin]]: ''"Impossible. Whatever happened, it was not us."''
A Vault Dweller: ''"Don't you want to find the people who did this?"''
Knight Shin: ''"There are countless brigands out there, civilian. It is not the job of the Brotherhood to hunt them down one by one for their crimes. I will say it bothers me to hear that someone is abusing the honor of the Brotherhood this way, but that does not change the facts."''
([[Daniel Shin/Dialogue|Knight Shin's dialogue]]) Shawn is frustrated that the Brotherhood would let people get away with this, especially in their name. The incident made him more sympathetic to the [[Crater Raiders|Raiders]], stating that they at least stand up for their own and "don't pretend to be the good guys."A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Tell me what the problem is."''
Shawn Hockman: ''"The problem is that a couple of these Brotherhood clowns showed up and took a bunch of my stuff at gunpoint. I'm a peaceful man, I really am. Sure wasn't equipped to deal with armed thugs 'requisitioning' the little I've managed to put together for myself. Never understood the Raiders. I like the quiet life, I don't need much, and I need trouble less. But after this, I get it. At least they don't pretend to be the good guys."''A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Would you really become a Raider because of this?"''
Shawn Hockman: ''"Listen, I don't have much. But what's mine is mine, and these people took that from me. The Brotherhood pretends like they're noble, but then they let this happen? In their name? Raiders don't act like something they're not, and at least the gangs defend their own."'' ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Forging Trust]] }} ===Quests=== [[Forging Trust]]: Shawn is one of four civilians inside Fort Atlas, each with their own problems and requests for the Brotherhood of Steel. Knight Shin requests that the player character interview these civilians, though ultimately Shin discards Shawn's problem. Because the robbers were not actually from the Brotherhood, Shawn's problems are of no concern to him. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Steel worker uniform]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Shawn Hockman appears {{In|FO76SD}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Steel Dawn}} [[Category:Steel Dawn human characters]] [[fr:Shawn Hockman]] [[ru:Шон Хокман]]

Just so me and some of my poor, innocent friends can protect ourselves from all the nasty folks out there.|sound=Tally Lang 005c975b_1.ogg}} '''Tally Lang''' is the leader of a group of [[Blood Eagles]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Ostensibly, Tally Lang is a poor, innocent orphan who has visited [[Fort Atlas]] to acquire guns from the recently-arrived [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force|Brotherhood of Steel]], so that she and her friends can properly defend themselves from the dangers of Appalachia.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"So I take it guns is what you're after?"''
Tally Lang: ''"Yeah, that's right. Big shiny guns! All the talk in the area is about these Brotherhood folks with their high-tech toys, and I thought, 'Tally, you gotta get some of that!' For self-defense, of course! Just so me and some of my poor, innocent friends can protect ourselves from all the nasty folks out there."''
([[Tally Lang/Dialogue#68|Tally Lang's dialogue]]) In reality, she is a raider, seeking to get ahold of hi-tech weaponry to make her gang more powerful.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"[Raider] C'mon, Tally. Trust me, I'm friends with Crater."''
Tally Lang: ''"Hey, ix-nay on the Ater-Cray! You trying to blow this for me? Listen, my gang could really use those guns, so don't screw this up for me. If anybody asks, just pretend like you bought the act, okay?"''
([[Tally Lang/Dialogue#76|Tally Lang's dialogue]]) Some time later, Tally and her group of Blood Eagles stormed into [[Vault 96]], trailing some [[Hellcat Company|Hellcats]] and looking to loot the vault. The group included [[Needles]], [[Eightball]] and [[Dillo]]. Their actions led to the death of [[Woods]] and many mercenaries. Tally's group accidentally becomes locked in. The Vault Dweller encounters Tally through an intercom and she requests for help, offering a vault keycard in exchange. Tally is apathetic towards any Blood Eagles the Vault Dweller killed prior, and does not care about trying to save the rest of the group who may be still stuck inside, saying they're not her problem. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |killable =yes |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Forging Trust]] * [[A Satisfied Conscience]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Forging Trust]]: Tally is one of four civilians inside Fort Atlas, each with their own problems and requests for the Brotherhood of Steel. Knight Shin asks that the player character interview these civilians, though ultimately Shin discards Tally's request. Shin vehemently denies the prospect of giving valuable weaponry to a wasteland civilian, and this can be reinforced with the suspicion that she may be a raider. * [[A Satisfied Conscience]]: Tally is in possession of a keycard needed to progress through the Vault but the Vault Dweller must save her and her gang members from attacking Mister Gutsies. The Vault Dweller may kill Tally and her gang. ===Other interactions=== Tally constantly denies that she is a raider when asked, although Knight Shin has his own suspicions about her. If the player character had [[Siding with Crater|sided with]] the Crater Raiders in order to access [[Vault 79]], they can affirm to Tally that they are friends with Crater, upon which she will quickly tell the player character to keep quiet about her association with the Raiders. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Tattered field jacket (Fallout 76)|Tattered field jacket]]

I should stop. Yeah. No need to be nervous. Nope. No reason at all.|sound=Erika Hewsen 006035c4_1.ogg}} '''Erika Hewsen''' is an initiate of the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Before Hewsen joined the [[Brotherhood of Steel]], she did not view herself as anyone important or remarkable in society. She grew up in a town that was being frequently attacked by [[super mutant]]s and [[raider]]s. It was then that [[Solomon Hardy|Doctor Solomon Hardy]] appeared and started teaching Hewsen most of what she knows today, while she tried to help him to the best of her ability. Eventually, the Brotherhood came to town and recruited Dr. Hardy as an initiate, who then recommended Hewsen to them, in turn leading to her recruitment as an initiate.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"So, what's your story, Hewsen?"''
Hewsen: ''"What- You want to know about me? Well, um... it's really not an interesting story. Really. I, uh, grew up in a town, and... Well, we were getting attacked a lot, by mutants and Raiders, and that's when Dr. Hardy came along. I helped him out all I could. So when he got recruited by the Brotherhood, I guess he, er, kind of recommended me, and... here I am?"''
([[Erika Hewsen/Dialogue#72|Erika Hewsen's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Who's Dr. Hardy?"''
Hewsen: ''"Another Initiate, and a great doctor. He taught me almost everything I know. I think he's been looking for a place to stay recently, to get some time away from the Fort. I mean- Not that he doesn't like it here or anything! Everyone needs some alone time! Right' I... I should just stop talking."''
([[Erika Hewsen/Dialogue#321|Erika Hewsen's dialogue]]) The recommendation was approved by [[Leila Rahmani|Paladin Rahmani]]. Hewsen would eventually find her way to [[Fort Atlas]] with the rest of the Brotherhood. She lacks self-confidence and is extremely reluctant to go on any field missions that could put her life in danger, preferring to help the group within safety.Erika Hewsen: ''"It's- It's a prank, right? I'm not really being called out for field work. Right?"''
([[Erika Hewsen/Dialogue#28|Erika Hewsen's dialogue]]) She also mentions she does not do well with really big changes. She is pretty sure that [[Daniel Shin|Knight Shin]] hates her, although she highly respects him and his leadership and wishes to make him proud. She once messed up saying the Brotherhood's motto in front of Shin, saying, "Vic adoriam" instead.Erika Hewsen: ''"'Vic adoriam'? Good going, Erika. Right in front of Knight Shin, too."''
([[Erika Hewsen/Dialogue#6|Erika Hewsen's dialogue]]) When Shin requests her on a mission, she thinks some terrible mistake must have happened and she was intended to be discharged instead.Erika Hewsen: ''"W-What? Knight Shin? A mission? Me? This has to be a mistake. Oh my god. I thought he hated me. Are you sure he didn't send you to, um... discharge me, or something?"''
([[Erika Hewsen/Dialogue#4|Erika Hewsen's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[A Knight's Penance]] }} ===Quests=== * [[A Knight's Penance]]: Initiate Hewsen joins [[Daniel Shin|Knight Shin]] and [[Norland|Initiate Norland]] in investigating reports of [[Uncanny Caverns]] being the potential source of a new outbreak of [[super mutant]]s in Appalachia. ===Other interactions=== * Hewsen will have new dialogue after the mission A Knight's Penance in which it is revealed she blames herself for Norland's death instead of Shin due to her panicking. She sullenly comments, "Initiate Norland was brave. I guess... I guess I just want to be a little more like him. She's... not militarily inclined.|sound=Norland 006035fb_1.ogg}} '''Initiate Norland''' is a recruit in the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Norland is from [[Ohio]], where his parents worked for the [[United States government]] before the [[Great War]]. After hearing about the Brotherhood's presence in Appalachia, and their commitment to preserving the world, Norland left home to join up, partly as a way to make up for his parents' role in the corrupt government that caused the Great War.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Pleased to make your acquaintance, Initiate. Do you mind introducing yourself?"''
Norland: ''"Sure, I can introduce myself. I come from Ohio. My parents worked in the government before the War. When I learned about the Brotherhood and what they're doing to preserve the world, I left home to do my part. Make up for my parents' contribution to causing this disaster, however small it was. It's a big responsibility, so I don't have time for much else. I need to be vigilant about my training if I'm going to become a Knight."''
([[Norland/Dialogue#110|Norland's dialogue]]) Norland is a loyal soldier and eager to serve, though [[Daniel Shin|Knight Shin]] will caution him about his limits.[[Daniel Shin|Knight Shin]]: ''"Initiate Norland, you take point. Stay in radio contact, and pull back as soon as you encounter danger. You may be eager to serve the Brotherhood, but being a good soldier is also about knowing your limits. Move out."''
Norland: ''"Roger. I'll make the Brotherhood proud, sir."''
([[Daniel Shin/Dialogue|Daniel Shin]] and [[Norland/Dialogue#313|Norland's dialogue]]) Nevertheless, Shin is impressed with Norland's capabilities as a soldier and thinks highly of him.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Is it really a good idea to send them off on their own?"''
[[Daniel Shin|Knight Shin]]: ''"Initiate Norland is highly capable, and I trust him to handle any situation that arises. But from what we've seen so far, I don't suspect there will be significant danger."''
([[Daniel Shin/Dialogue|Daniel Shin's dialogue]]) Norland, much like Shin, composes himself with strict etiquette, because he believes he and his fellow soldiers should act as representatives of the Brotherhood.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Woah, no need to be so formal."''
Norland: ''"Not trying to be formal, just following basic etiquette. We are all representatives of the Brotherhood of Steel. We should conduct ourselves as such."''
([[Norland/Dialogue#114|Norland's dialogue]]) He also cares about his fitness and can be seeing doing push ups in the dormitory. Although he trusts the judgment of [[Leila Rahmani|Paladin Rahmani]] and Knight Shin, Norland does have reservations about [[Erika Hewsen|Initiate Erika Hewsen]], as she does not seem "militarily inclined" to him.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you know about Initiate Hewsen?"''
Norland: ''"It's not my place to give an opinion on the other recruits. I trust the judgment of Paladin Rahmani and Knight Shin. That being said, I hope Initiate Hewsen is getting the support she needs to succeed here. She's... not militarily inclined."''
([[Norland/Dialogue#108|Norland's dialogue]]) Hewsen refers to Norland as Shin's favorite, and she admits to being sort of scared of Norland, viewing him as everything she is not. During the expedition to the [[Uncanny Caverns]], Norland and Hewsen get separated from the group, an event that leads to Norland's death by the hands of the [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|super mutants]]. It is said that he will be given a decent burial. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[A Knight's Penance]] }} ===Quests=== * [[A Knight's Penance]]: Under [[Daniel Shin|Knight Shin]]'s direction, Initiate Norland will join the squad investigating [[Uncanny Caverns]] as a potential source of the [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|super mutants]] in Appalachia. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Combat armor (Fallout 76)|Combat armor]] right arm

I try to be proud of what he's doing, happy that he's finally getting a chance to learn something special. Can't say I succeed all the time, but it helps.|Carol about Colin|sound=Carol Putnam 005dc167_1.ogg}} '''Carol Putnam''' is the owner of [[Lewis & Sons Farming Supply]] in [[Appalachia]], living there with the rest of her family. ==Background== Carol has been married to her husband [[George Putnam|George]] for twenty years.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How's the farm doing?"''
Carol Putnam: ''"We're getting to be self-sufficient soon. Greenhouse is getting there. George wants to restore the house, but we're fine in here."''
[[George Putnam]]: ''"The boys are going to want rooms of their own, dear. Don't act like you wouldn't mind being away from their snoring."''
Carol Putnam: ''"We've got other work needs doing first. If I can put up with your snoring for twenty years, I can deal with them."''
([[Carol Putnam/Dialogue|Carol]] and [[George Putnam/Dialogue|George Putnam's dialogue]]) She and her family returned to Appalachia in 2103 and made their home at the former farm supply store. The family first secured the barn before later returning to begin restoring the location. Carol claimed the Putnam's as rightful owners and inheritors of the location since George was a cousin of [[Lewis (Fallout 76)|Lewis]], the previous owner, who died during the [[Great War]] along with his family. Carol uses the threat of her husband George and his shotgun as a deterrent to would-be troublemakers.[[Notice: New owners]] Carol informed the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]] of a ghoul presence in the area which she believed had originated near Orwell Orchards based on the number of attacks in the area. After Carol's sons both express interest in joining the Brotherhood, she and George both agreed that one son could join, but the farm could not spare both of them. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Field Testing]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Flannel shirt and jeans (Fallout 76)|Flannel shirt and jeans]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Carol Putnam appears appears {{In|FO76SD}}. The Brotherhood can't be all brawn and no brains, right?|sound=Colin Putnam 005cf014_1.ogg}} '''Colin Putnam''' is a resident of [[Lewis & Sons Farming Supply]] in [[Appalachia]], living there with the rest of his family. ==Background== Colin and his family returned to Appalachia in 2103 and made their home at the former farm supply store. The family first secured the barn before later returning to begin restoring the location. Colin's father, [[George Putnam|George]], was a cousin of the store's previous owner Lewis, who had died alongside his family during the [[Great War]], and Colin's family claimed the farm supply store as the rightful inheritors. Colin repaired the [[Protectron (Fallout 76)|construction Protectron]] and [[Mister Handy (Fallout 76)|Mr. Handy]] which assist with work at the farm. According to his father, Colin loved books and would read anything he could get his hands on, like he was trying to suck the world in through words. Marty thinks of Colin as a nerd. Colin also mentions picking up his brother's chores, showing he is responsible. Colin was not content with his life on the farm, and he expressed interest in joining the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force|Brotherhood of Steel]], believing he could help change the world with access to their technology. If recruited, Colin moves to [[Fort Atlas]] and begins training to become a [[Brotherhood of Steel ranks#Journeyman scribe|scribe]]. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion =yes |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Field Testing]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Field Testing]]: Marty and Colin are both looking to join the Brotherhood of Steel; however, their mother will only let the Vault Dweller take one of them. The Vault Dweller can choose through dialogue to have Colin join the Brotherhood of Steel and have him become a temporary companion for the rest of the quest when raiding the [[Orwell Orchards bomb shelter]]. ===Effects of player's actions=== * If Colin is recruited during Field Testing, the player receives the [[Mind Over Matter]] weapon instead of [[the Farmhand]] for Marty. Colin then travels to [[Fort Atlas]] to await initiation in the lobby basement. * If Colin is recruited, he can be spoken to about the drastic decision [[Leila Rahmani]] made. Colin feels her choice was wrong. Instead of choosing between Rahmani and [[Daniel Shin]], Colin says he will agree with whatever [[Odessa Valdez]] says. Despite this, he openly prefers the leadership of Rahmani over Shin, feeling she is the heart of the Brotherhood. * If Marty is recruited, Colin can be updated about his brother's progress. Colin mentions he is still unhappy about not being chosen, feeling he is wasting away his life at the farm, saying farming isn't what he wants out of life. However, he is thankful for the Vault Dweller for helping him realize that he needs to become more proactive and independent, taking matters into his own hands in order to live his life the way he wants to. He asks the Vault Dweller to pass on a message that he is not mad at Marty. Colin mentions he sort of misses the ruckus Marty made. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Green shirt and combat boots (Fallout 76)|Green shirt and combat boots]] |weapon =[[Tricentennial paint|Tricentennial]] [[10mm pistol (Fallout 76)|10mm pistol]] |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Colin Putnam appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]'', introduced in the ''[[Steel Dawn]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. ==Gallery== FO76SD Colin.png|Colin Putnam at the Putnam residence FO76SD Colin Putnam 10mm Pistol Field Testing.png|Colin's pistol during [[Field Testing]] FO76SR Colin Putnam The Catalyst.jpg|Colin at Fort Atlas at the conclusion of [[The Catalyst]] ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox companions FO76}} {{Navbox Steel Dawn}} [[Category:Steel Dawn human characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 Brotherhood of Steel characters]] [[ru:Колин Патнам]]

Choose them carefully, kid.|sound=Dagger 005d2bb3_1.ogg}} '''Dagger''' is a member of the [[Blood Eagles]] in [[Appalachia]] and the leader of the eponymous [[Dagger's Den]]. ==Background== After arriving in Appalachia, Dagger chose to remain independent of the [[Crater Raiders|Raiders]] at [[the Crater]] for three reasons: first, she refused to be subordinate to someone else; two, they draw too much attention to themselves; and three, she does not want to deal with the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] at [[Foundation]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''Why don't you live in Crater?''"
Dagger: "''I'm not one to want to follow someone else's orders. I'd rather be the queen of my own castle. They draw too much attention to themselves, anyway, and I don't need to be dealing with those pansy Settlers."''
([[Dagger/Dialogue#11|Dagger's dialogue]]) According to her, she was not initially trying to start her own gang, but was tough and fearless enough that people just started to follow her. In fact, she claims, losing her raiders doesn't even worry her since more will come and join up.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''What made you want to start your own gang?''"
Dagger: "''I'm tough and not afraid to get shit done, so people just started following me and my orders. It wasn't my intention, it just happened naturally. I'm not too worried about replacing bodies, more raiders will come and want to join up. Hell, if you're ever looking to leave the Brotherhood of Steel, I'd consider letting you join my crew.''"
([[Dagger/Dialogue#8|Dagger's dialogue]]) At some point, she found a group of raiders that had somehow acquired weapons that originally belonged to the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]]. After "negotiations" failed, she took possession of the weapons.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''Weapons, what weapons? I'm here on behalf of the Retreat.''"
Dagger: "''Aw shit, you mean you didn't know about the weapons? The crate they came in may have had a Brotherhood of Steel insignia on them, but they're ours now. Don't even think about walking into my place and making demands, either. I won't let you take these weapons from us.''"
Vault Dweller: "''How did you even get these weapons?''"
Dagger: "''My gang and I came across a small group of Raiders and I couldn't help but notice these beauties sitting around. Let's just say negotiations didn't go over well, and now we're the owners. Who knows how that group got them from the Brotherhood...and who cares.''"
([[Dagger/Dialogue#135|Dagger's dialogue]]) When the [[villager]]s settled in the treehouses of [[the Retreat]], Dagger sent some [[Blood Eagles]] to pretend to want to join the group in order to spy on them. Once the villagers became more established and had a decent stockpile of supplies, the spies returned to Dagger. The next day, Dagger showed up and demanded some of their supplies.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''When did she start harassing you?''"
[[Jennie Brown]]: "''She sent some of her Blood Eagles to pretend like they wanted to be a part of our community around the time that we first got set up here. After we became established and got our own stockpile of supplies, those Blood Eagles disappeared and must've told here that we were now a worthy target. She showed up the next day with those sons of bitches, demanding a cut of our supplies. Now we're more careful about who we let in, so please forgive anyone who might be, ya know, standoffish.''"
([[Jennie Brown/Dialogue#14|Jennie Brown's dialogue]]) Since then, Dagger has been demanding weekly collections from the villagers and has been increasing her demands steadily in the hope they die off so she can claim the Retreat for herself.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''Do you have any useful information about Dagger?''"
[[Villager]]: "''I went out hunting shortly after one of her weekly collections and tracked her Lieutenants to see where her hideout is.''"
(Villager's dialogue)[[Dagger's journal]] According to her, she chose to extort them because they are weak and incapable of defending themselves, yet have plenty of supplies.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''Why did you choose to extort them?''"
Dagger: "''Easy. They're weak, they can't properly defend themselves, and they've got plenty of supplies. Also, they kinda seem like a freaky cult right? It can't be just me.''"
([[Dagger/Dialogue#19|Dagger's dialogue]]) Furthermore, she views their leader [[Jennie Brown]] as a "sickeningly sweet" woman who is a "pacifist and overall pathetic excuse for a human."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''What do you think about Jennie?''"
Dagger: "''From what a little Eagle told me, that woman is sickeningly sweet. I don't trust anyone that nice. If those villagers were smart, they'd watch out for that one.''"
([[Dagger/Dialogue#15|Dagger's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |killable =yes |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Disarming Discovery]] }} ===Quests=== [[Disarming Discovery]]: Dagger has been both harassing [[villager]]s of [[the Retreat]] as well as hording stolen [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood weapons]]. For these reasons, she must either be bribed using 300 caps, intimidated using a Strength 12+ check, or outright killed. Flirting with Dagger does not work. Dagger will turn hostile and attack if the Vault Dweller says her reward is a sense of peace and a good night's sleep. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Blood Eagle leather jacket and jeans]] |weapon =[[Hellstorm missile launcher]] |otheritem = |ondeath =[[Throne room key (Steel Dawn)|Throne room key]] }} ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|I'm tough and not afraid to get shit done, so people just started following me and my orders. Such a sad waste of life.|sound=Gloria Chance 005e57dc_1.ogg}} '''Gloria Chance''' is a member of the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Gloria is a member of the Settlers located in [[the Foundation supply room]] who is in charge of keeping stock of the settlement's supplies along with her husband, [[Tad Chance|Tad]]. She made contact with the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]] in the hopes of purchasing weapons in exchange for food and other supplies, and has been waiting for a response from [[Leila Rahmani|Paladin Rahmani]].Gloria Chance: "''You must be here about that shipment of BlamCo Mac & Cheese! Great, I was starting to get worried.''"
[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault dweller]]: "''Negative, ma'am, I'm with the Brotherhood of Steel. I'm here on behalf of Paladin Rahmani.''"
Gloria Chance: "''Oh, how professional of you! You say you're with Paladin Rahmani? That's fantastic, I didn't think she'd get back to us so quickly. How can I help you, uh, sire...? Your Majesty? Your Steeliness?''"
Vault dweller: "'' 'Initiate' will do, thanks. I'm here to discuss Paladin Rahmani's trade deal.''"
Gloria Chance: "''Ah right, about that... Originally we were hoping to purchase some weapons in exchange for food and supplies, but we may need to work something else out. After all, our last purchase is more than enough firepower for the time being.''"
([[Gloria Chance/Dialogue#35|Gloria Chance's dialogue]]) However, they recently have gotten their hands on stolen Brotherhood weapons.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault dweller]]: "''These weapons don't belong to you. They're property of the Brotherhood.''"
[[Tad Chance]]: "'' 'Cept they do, though. We bought 'em. I've got receipts, if you want to see 'em. They're handwritten, but we keep everything on the books here.''"
Gloria Chance: "''If they belonged to your crew originally, well... That's tough luck for sure... And I feel for you guys, I do. But look around us: what's not second-hand property anymore? Everything used to belong to somebody, right? Really, though, once you get things settled over by the lookout tower, I'm sure we can work something out.''"
([[Tad Chance/Dialogue#254|Tad]] and [[Gloria Chance/Dialogue#261|Gloria Chance's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Supplying Demands]] }} ===Quests=== [[Supplying Demands]]: Gloria is the one to speak to about a trade deal between the Brotherhood of Steel and the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]]. She must also be convinced to return the stolen weaponry, as she is very reluctant to the idea and tells the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] they were last seen with [[Mike Tiller]] and that they can work something out later. If Mike is killed and Gloria is informed he was murdered, Gloria will express horror and call it murder. Tad will be angered and order the Vault Dweller to give the weapons back and go away. The Vault Dweller can agree and tell them to "go nuts" and blow themselves up with them, or pass a Strength +2 check to refuse, demand supplies from Foundation or else the Vault Dweller will kill them. If the latter choice occurs, Tad calls the Vault Dweller a "jack-booted piece of shit" but Gloria reluctantly agrees because she doesn't want to start a war with the Brotherhood of Steel. Gloria says to let Rahmani know they're unsatisfied with this result. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = [[Worker outfit|Worker hat]]

'''Ian Orwell'''<ref>[[Orwell Orchards terminal entries#Ian Orwell's terminal|Orwell Orchards terminal entries; Ian Orwell's terminal]]</ref> was a man who lived at [[Orwell Orchards]] in [[Timeline#2077|2077]].

==Background==
Ian was a farmer at Orwell Orchards, a farm that had fallen into massive debt, failing to be profitable in years.<ref name="1115OO">[[Orwell Orchards terminal entries#2077 - 11 - 15]]</ref> For this reason, Ian applied for loans at a bank in [[Charleston]] to help alleviate the farm's hard times and massive debt, but was denied multiple times.<ref>[[Cheryl's journal]]</ref> After participating in the October [[West Virginia Lottery Company|Lucky Hits lottery]], he learned he had won the lottery, although the representative to deliver the money was to come in November.<ref name="1115OO" /> He had constructed a shelter under the farm, with he and his wife taking shelter in it when the bombs fell.

Around Christmas 2077, Ian and his wife, Cheryl, decided to have a child, and Ian surprised his wife with a baby crib he had previously bought.<ref>[[Orwell Orchards terminal entries#2077 - 12 - 25]]</ref> By mid-March 2078, they had not succeeded in their goal of parenthood, and the shelter began to fall apart, with numerous appliances failing or needing to be repaired.<ref>[[Orwell Orchards terminal entries#2078 - 03 - 16]]</ref> By September 2078, the combined factors of collecting radiation and failing equipment began to make themselves known, with the two left only with air, food, and water. Although they made up for it by golfing and reading, the effects of radiation had began to take their toll on Ian, resulting in heavy weight loss, hair loss, and illness.<ref>[[Orwell Orchards terminal entries#2078 - 09 - ??]]</ref>

Sometime later, despite increasing protests, Ian maintained his position of staying in the shelter, despite the worsening radiation effects. He vowed to keep Cheryl safe in the shelter at any cost, so he chose to imprison her against her will in the supply room.<ref>[[Orwell Orchards terminal entries#2078 - ?? - ??]]</ref> After this, Cheryl escaped the supply room by repairing the exit door button, waiting until Ian was showering, and taking the key while he was indisposed. Before leaving, she left a note addressed to anyone, including Ian, saying she still loved him. His [[skeleton (Fallout 76)|skeleton]] is found in the shelter shower.<ref>[[Trapped (Steel Dawn)|Trapped]]</ref>

==Appearances==
Ian Orwell is mentioned only {{In|FO76}}. The story of Orwell Orchards and Ian was expanded upon in the ''[[Steel Dawn]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]], which added his skeleton.

{{Infobox character |games =FO76, FO76SD |image =FO76SD Jennie Brown.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Female |family =Two grandchildren {{icon|dead}} |affiliation =[[Villager]]s |role =Leader |location =[[The Retreat]] |quests =[[Disarming Discovery]] |level = |derived = |voice type =BS01_NPCF_JennieBrown |actor =[[Anoush NeVart]] |dialogue =[[Jennie Brown/Dialogue]] |edid =BS01_JennieBrown |formid ={{ID|005c6c20}} |refid ={{ID|005cfa61}} ([[The Retreat]])

You know, darlin, I think a lot of people these days are just looking for some human companionship and kindness. There's enough to worry about in this world we live in, but having a family helps you carry that burden.|sound=Jennie Brown 005dc260_1.ogg}} '''Jennie Brown''' is the leader of the [[villager]]s at [[the Retreat]]. ==Background== Prior to the [[Great War]], Jennie lived with her family spending her days watching television and gossiping.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''What was your life like before the bombs fell?''"
Jennie Brown: "''Well, I spent my days watching television and gossiping with my gal pals. Nothing too exciting, but boy would I give anything to have one boring day again. I had a beautiful family with two precious grandbabies. I loved them bunches and bunches, more than anything in this whole wide world. This family I've created will never replace them, but it helps with the loss a little bit. Ya know what I mean?''"
([[Jennie Brown/Dialogue#26|Jennie Brown's dialogue]]) Her family perished in the War, and she dealt with this by offering companionship and kindness to survivors she met in the wasteland, with many deciding to follow her.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What made you gather all of these people together?"''
Jennie Brown: ''"I didn't really do it on purpose or anything, it just kinda happened. I think a lot of people these days are just looking for some human companionship and kindness. There's enough to worry about in this world we live in, but having a family helps carry that burden with you."''
([[Jennie Brown/Dialogue#23|Jennie Brown's dialogue]]) She became the leader of her new "little family", following a nomadic lifestyle and regularly recruiting people while traveling, going at least as far as [[State#Georgia|Georgia]].Jennie Brown: "''This place isn't quite Georgia, but the humidity's sure trying.''"
([[Jennie Brown/Dialogue#38|Jennie Brown's dialogue]])
{{Small|'''Note:''' This quote is ambient dialogue.}} The group eventually became too large to continue wandering, and so decided to settle down,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''Where did you live before the Retreat?''"
Jennie Brown: "''We were nomadic before we came to [[Appalachia]]. It worked out well because traveling around meant finding more people to add to our family. We've grown quite a bit, though, so it only made sense to set down some roots."''
([[Jennie Brown/Dialogue#4|Jennie Brown's dialogue]]) electing to settle in [[Appalachia]] after hearing talks about other groups returning to the region.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''Why did you want to come to Appalachia?''"
Jennie Brown: "''Even though we were able to get by well enough traveling, we grew past the point where it wasn't sustainable anymore and we needed reliable trade. While going from place to place, we started to hear talks about people coming back to Appalachia and it seemed as good of a place as any. Plus, I've got some youngins talking about starting families, bless their hearts. Kids need all the stability that they can get in this unstable world, so it made sense to find a place we could call home.''"
([[Jennie Brown/Dialogue#29|Jennie Brown's dialogue]]) They declined to join with the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] at [[Foundation]] because they wanted to keep their independence and to avoid "the drama" between Foundation and [[the Crater]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''Why don't you live in [[Foundation]] with the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]]?''"
Jennie Brown: "''We just want to be on our own and don't want to get wrapped up in the drama between Foundation and [[the Crater|Crater]].''"
([[Jennie Brown/Dialogue#12|Jennie Brown's dialogue]]) The group eventually chose to live in the treehouses in [[the Mire]] due to the tactical advantages living high above the ground presented.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''Why did you choose to live in treehouses?''"
Jennie Brown: "''Well, since we're higher up we've got good sight lines all around us and are able to protect ourselves pretty well from the local, uh, wildlife. These houses were already built too, which made it quicker for use to get set up. Besides, it makes me feel like a kid again!''"
([[Jennie Brown/Dialogue#8|Jennie Brown's dialogue]]) Describing herself now as the "mama hen" of her "little family," Jennie and her villagers have recently been threatened by a [[Blood Eagles]] leader named [[Dagger]].Jennie Brown: "''Hello there, stranger. What can I do for you?''"
[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''I'm here on behalf of the Brotherhood.''"
Jennie Brown: "''Well aren't you just the cutest Brotherhood member I've ever seen! My name is Jennie Brown and I'm the mama hen of this little familty here at [[the Retreat]]. Lately my kin have been harassed by a woman named [[Dagger]] and her [[Blood Eagles|Blood Eagle Raiders]]. She's causing all my people to go hungry and threatening our lives."''
([[Jennie Brown/Dialogue#72|Jennie Brown's dialogue]]) Initially, Dagger sent some spies who pretended they wanted to join the group right after settling in the treehouses. After Jennie and her group finished establishing a base, the spies left and reported back to Dagger. The following day, Dagger and her Blood Eagles showed up and demanded some of the group's stockpile,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''When did she start harassing you?''"
Jennie Brown: "''She sent some of her Blood Eagles to pretend like they wanted to be a part of our community around the time that we first got set up here. After we became established and got our own stockpile of supplies, those Blood Eagles disappeared and must've told here that we were now a worthy target. She showed up the next day with those sons of bitches, demanding a cut of our supplies. Now we're more careful about who we let in, so please forgive anyone who might be, ya know, standoffish.''"
([[Jennie Brown/Dialogue#14|Jennie Brown's dialogue]]) including food, water, and medical supplies.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''Do you have any useful information about Dagger?''"
[[Villager]]: "''I went out hunting shortly after one of her weekly collections and tracked her Lieutenants to see where her hideout is. I lost their trail and wasn't able to get the exact location, but I do know that they're somewhere to the southwest. If you find her, kill her. Her and her damn Blood Eagles are taking our food, water, [[Stimpak (Fallout 76)|stimpaks]], everything. All in exchange for allowing us to keep our lives.''"
(Villager's dialogue) Enough food is being taken that some people in the group are starting to go hungry,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''What supplies has she been taking?''"
Jennie Brown: "''Food and medical supplies, primarily, two of the most needed things in order to survive in this world, of course. We've been having to ration out our food so that everyone only gets one meal a day. That's not enough to live on and people are starting to go hungry.''"
([[Jennie Brown/Dialogue#20|Jennie Brown's dialogue]]) with at least one discontent villager considering joining Dagger instead of starving to death.[[The Dagger dilemma]] Dagger describes Jennie as a "sickeningly sweet" woman who is a "pacifist and overall pathetic excuse for a human."[[Dagger's journal]][[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''What do you think about Jennie?''"
Dagger: "''From what a little Eagle told me, that woman is sickeningly sweet. I don't trust anyone that nice. If those villagers were smart, they'd watch out for that one.''"
([[Dagger/Dialogue#15|Dagger's dialogue]]) However, Jennie mentions that if Dagger were not constantly accompanied by her [[Dagger's lieutenant|lieutenants]], then she would have already tried to kill Dagger herself.Jennie Brown: "''I'm telling you, if they didn't follow her everywhere she went, I'd have already tried to put her six feet under.''"

Whatever you need, I'll fight mutants, or ghouls, or Raiders, or...or... whatever!|sound=Marty Putnam 005cf026_1.ogg}} '''Marty Putnam''' is a resident of [[Lewis & Sons Farming Supply]] in [[Appalachia]], living in the [[Putnam residence]] with the rest of his family. ==Background== Marty and his family returned to Appalachia in [[Timeline#2103|2103]] and made their home at the former farm supply store. The family first secured the barn before later returning to begin restoring the location. Marty's father, [[George Putnam|George]], was a cousin of the store's previous owner Lewis, who had died alongside his family during the [[Great War]], and Marty's family claimed the farm supply store as the rightful inheritors. Marty expressed interest in joining the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force|Brotherhood of Steel]]. If recruited instead of his brother [[Colin Putnam|Colin]], Marty moves to [[Fort Atlas]] and begins training with the Brotherhood to become a [[Brotherhood of Steel ranks#Journeyman knight|knight]]. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion =yes |perm companion = |ghoul =yes |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Field Testing]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Field Testing]]: Marty and Colin are both looking to join the Brotherhood of Steel; however, their mother will only let the Vault Dweller take one of them. The Vault Dweller can choose through dialogue to have Marty join the Brotherhood of Steel and have him become a temporary companion for the rest of the quest when raiding the [[Orwell Orchards bomb shelter]]. ===Effects of player's actions=== * If Marty is recruited during Field Testing, the player receives [[the Farmhand]] weapon instead of the [[Mind Over Matter]] for Colin. Marty then travels to [[Fort Atlas]] to await initiation in the lobby basement. * If Colin is chosen, Marty can be informed how Colin is doing with the Brotherhood. Marty admits he was pretty sore about not being able to join, but that the choice made him think about his home life differently and to be more grateful for being able to live in a decent place. Upon hearing Colin is training to become a Scribe, Marty is jealous but glad for him, and tells the Vault Dweller to pass a message to not forget about his family. Marty also mentions Carol is handling the choice worse than George because Colin was her baby. * If Marty is recruited, he can be spoken to about the drastic decision [[Leila Rahmani]] made. Marty feels her choice was wrong, saying even if Rahmani's heart is in the right place, people need to follow orders to make things work, and he sides with [[Daniel Shin]]. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Letterman's jacket and jeans (Fallout 76)|Letterman's jacket and jeans]] |weapon =[[10mm pistol (Fallout 76)|10mm pistol]] |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|I... [[Tad Chance]]: "''Oh... Well. The stuff we got definitely has your logos on it. Some guys from the town watch took them out for testing a little earlier. I'm sure you can catch up with them, they normally practice at a small site they set up near the [[East Mountain lookout|East Mountain Lookout]], a bit North of here.''"
[[Gloria Chance]]: "''Oh that's right. Mike and them took the weapons out for a test drive. If you head over, I'm sure they'd let you take a look.''"
([[Tad Chance/Dialogue#234|Tad]] and [[Gloria Chance/Dialogue#238|Gloria Chance's dialogue]]) ordered by [[Ward (Wastelanders)|Ward]] at the [[East Mountain lookout]]. However, he paid little attention to the demonstration, preferring to work on a [[terminal]]. When another settler asked him to get off the terminal and help with the recording, he went to lock the terminal and then grabbed a rocket launcher incorrectly, causing it to fire and kill the other four settlers.[[Weapon demonstration]] Upon realizing what he had done, he was mortified and fled to the nearby [[Kerwood Mine]]. He decided to hide out of guilt, believing that the others would view him as a murderer.Mike Tiller: "''H-h-hold it right there. Don't come any closer!''"
[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''Okay, okay, let's just take a deep breath.''"
Mike Tiller: "''No, you don't understand. What I did, I... Oh, man... I'm Mike. Mike Tiller. Go to [[Foundation]], tell them you found me dead. Because... I'm... I'm never leaving! I'm not going back, you can't make me! They'll never believe me... They'll think I'm a murderer!''"
([[Mike Tiller/Dialogue#81|Mike Tiller's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |killable =yes |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Supplying Demands]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Supplying Demands]]: During this quest, it is up to the player to convince Mike to forgive himself for the incident and return to [[Foundation]], as well as to return the rocket launchers he took to their [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force|rightful owners]], or to kill him. ** If he is spared, he mentions Ward thought it would be best if he is no longer on guard duty, so he helps out Foundation in other ways. He mentions he still has trouble sleeping at night. ** If he is killed, the BOS weapons key can be obtained from his body. When reporting back to [[Gloria Chance|Gloria]] and [[Tad Chance]], the player may choose to lie by claiming there was an accident with the weapons, lie by claiming Mike "went nuts" and killed everyone, or come clean about his death. We could make use of that.|sound=Sheena 005d79c1_1.ogg}} '''Sheena''' is a member of the [[Crater Raiders]]' [[War Party]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== As a child, Sheena would always win at the [[Blast Radius board game (Fallout 76)|Blast Radius board game]] due to her strong tactical intellect. In 2103, Sheena is the tactician of the Crater [[War Party]] and plans out their operations against the Brotherhood under the orders of [[Meg Groberg]]. Sheena is one of the three raiders that inhabit [[the Crater war room]] along with [[Burke (Steel Dawn)|Burke]] and [[Pierce (Steel Dawn)|Pierce]]. She has known the two from back when she helped an imprisoned Pierce escape with Burke.[[Burke (Steel Dawn)|Burke]]: ''"My employer was holding Pierce prisoner. I was his guard. Even in that situation, Pierce treated me like a person. Not as a tool. He saw me. When Sheena arrived, we all escaped together. The rest is history."''
([[Burke (Steel Dawn)/Dialogue#206|Burke's dialogue]]) When [[Marcia Leone]] joins the gang, the young women become fast friends. Sheena is rather misanthropic, saying she does not give two craps about humanity, saying the species has done nothing but abuse and betray each other, also pointing out their world has been destroyed by nuclear warfare. She mentions she will only look out for her and her own, saying the rest do not matter.Sheena: ''"I don't give two craps about humanity. As a species, we've done nothing but abuse and betray each other. And beyond that, look at what we've done to this Earth. So I look out for me and my own. The rest don't matter."''
([[Sheena/Dialogue#177|Sheena's dialogue]]) In 2104, Sheena and Burke become imprisoned by the [[Hellcat Company]] in the basement laboratory of the [[AMS corporate headquarters]]. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Property Rights]] * [[Missing Persons]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Property Rights]]: After the confrontation with Pierce in the [[makeshift vault]], the Vault Dweller meets Sheena when Pierce refuses to cooperate. Sheena strikes a deal to trade intel for intel; she will reveal the source of where the Raiders found their weapons if the Vault Dweller returns her [[Sheena's holotape|holotape]] once it has been downloaded with Brotherhood information. The Dweller is free to refuse. * [[Missing Persons]]: Sheena and Burke go to the [[AMS corporate headquarters]], but there, they become captured and imprisoned in the basement by [[Kit]] and the [[Hellcat Company]]. The Vault Dweller and Marcia set out to rescue them. ===Other interactions=== * If one calls Burke a freak in conversation with them, Sheena will come to their defense, though Burke will remark that they are not surprised by such remarks anymore.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What a freak."''
[[Burke (Steel Dawn)|Burke]]: ''"..."''
Sheena: ''"Hey! Don't you fucking talk to Burke like that!"''
Burke: ''"It's okay. I'm not surprised anymore."''

{{Infobox character |games =FO76, FO76SD |image =FO76SD Tad Chance.jpg |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |family =[[Gloria Chance]] - wife |affiliation =[[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] |role =Supply keeper |location =[[Foundation supply room]] |quests =[[Supplying Demands]] |level = |derived = |voice type =BS01_NPCM_TadChance |actor =[[Damien Haas]] |dialogue =[[Tad Chance/Dialogue]] |edid =BS01_Settler_TadChance |formid ={{ID|005d2c6b}} |refid ={{ID|005d2c6f}} }} {{Quotation|Um... Good? I mean, they're weapons, right? Shouldn't weapons be dangerous? I'm not about to sign up for guard duty. I'm a lover, not a fighter, but...|sound=Tad Chance 005dcc99_1.ogg}} '''Tad Chance''' is a member of the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Tad Chance is one of the Settlers in charge of keeping stock of the supply room along with his wife, [[Gloria Chance|Gloria]]. However, they both have recently gotten their hands on stolen [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]] weapons.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''These weapons don't belong to you. They're property of the Brotherhood.''"
Tad Chance: "'' 'Cept they do, though. We bought 'em. I've got receipts, if you want to see 'em. They're handwritten, but we keep everything on the books here.''"
[[Gloria Chance]]: "''If they belonged to your crew originally, well... That's tough luck for sure... And I feel for you guys, I do. But look around us: what's not second-hand property anymore? Everything used to belong to somebody, right? Really, though, once you get things settled over by the [[East Mountain lookout|lookout tower]], I'm sure we can work something out.''"
([[Tad Chance/Dialogue#254|Tad]] and [[Gloria Chance/Dialogue#261|Gloria Chance's dialogue]]) Tad purchased the weapons at a good price from "a guy, who knows a guy" who declined to mention where he got them from.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: "''We need to talk about those weapons... now.''"
[[Gloria Chance]]: "''Okay, if you don't think it can wait.''"
Tad Chance: "''Well, I'm the one who spent all our [[Cap (Fallout 76)|caps]] on 'em, so the least I can do is be the one answering questions about 'em.''"
Vault Dweller: "''Where did you acquire these weapons?''"
Tad Chance: "''I know a guy, who knows a guy. I don't know the guy he knows, though. My guy buys this and that from caravans and traders. He drops by here when he finds something interesting. He didn't mention where he got these from. Just said he thinks he got a good deal on them. So he gave me a slightly less good deal.''"
([[Gloria Chance/Dialogue#246|Gloria]] and [[Tad Chance/Dialogue#248|Tad Chance's dialogue]]) When pressed, he acknowledges his group isn't disciplined, though Tad himself is wary of training, as he hates doing push-ups.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: [ [[Perception]] 8+ ] "''Your people lack discipline, not weaponry. Let us keep the weapons and we'll offer training.''"
Tad Chance: "''Well... Hard to argue with that. We're not exactly the most... disciplined bunch.''"
[[Mike Tiller]]: "''It's true... Maybe if I had proper training... this... wouldn't have happened.''"
[[Gloria Chance]]: "''Alright, the weapons are safer with you... But what would the Brotherhood need in return for training?''"
Vault Dweller: "''You can provide us surplus food supplies and any intel on unusual weaponry like this in the future.''"
Tad Chance: "''You're not going to make me do push-ups are you?''"
Gloria Chance: "'' 'Cause that would be the end of the world... Okay. We provide food, water, and the latest scoop on weird tech... And the Brotherhood provides us with training to better defend ourselves. Sounds pretty fair to me!''"
Vault dweller: "''It's a deal. Push-ups included.''"
Tad Chance: "''Aw shit...''"
([[Tad Chance/Dialogue#12|Tad Chance]], [[Mike Tiller/Dialogue#138|Mike Tiller]] and [[Gloria Chance/Dialogue#137|Gloria Chance's dialogue]]) A [[Got that thing you wanted|note]] reveals Tad is interested in obtaining collectibles such as figures and replicas.[[Got that thing you wanted]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Supplying Demands]] }} ===Quests=== [[Supplying Demands]]: Tad unknowingly purchased stolen Brotherhood weapons, and must be convinced to give them up after retrieving them from [[Kerwood Mine]]. If [[Mike Tiller]] was killed and Tad is informed he was murdered, Tad will be angered and order the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] to give the weapons back and go away. The Vault Dweller can agree and tell them to "go nuts" and blow themselves up with them, or pass a Strength +2 check to refuse, demand supplies from Foundation or else the Vault Dweller will kill them. If the latter choice occurs, Tad calls the Vault Dweller a "jack-booted piece of shit" but Gloria reluctantly agrees because she doesn't want to start a war with the Brotherhood of Steel. Before leaving, Tad says not to bother to see if the food the Brotherhood will be given will have spit because it will. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Settler laborer outfit|Settler laborer hat]]
[[Lumberjack outfit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Tad Chance appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]'', introduced in the ''[[Steel Dawn]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Foundation}} {{Navbox Steel Dawn}} [[Category:Steel Dawn human characters]] [[Category:Settler characters]] [[ru:Тед Ченс]]

Against the radiation, the mutants... the decay of civilization. We failed. But this doesn't have to be the end. There is so much good that we can still do. Please, spare us your wrath.|sound=Farha 00602e37_1.ogg}} '''Doctor Farha''' is a research colleague of [[Edgar Blackburn|Doctor Edgar Blackburn]] and [[Jain (Steel Reign)|Jain]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Prior to the [[Great War]], Farha was in university with Blackburn and she clashed with him on the ethical boundaries of research.[[FEV research logs]] After the War, she met [[Nellie Wright]], a prodigy of sorts, when Nellie broke through Farha's window while searching for scraps, as a wastelander trying to survive. Nellie was interested in Farha's research so Farha took her in and taught her.Doctor Farha: ''"I met Nellie when she broke through my window to search for scraps. As Wasteland survivors do. She was more interested in my research notes than my leftovers. So I took her in and taught her what I know."''
([[Farha/Dialogue#219|Doctor Farha's dialogue]]) She met Blackburn again and learned of his plans to revitalize the human race to help survive against threats such as disease and radiation. She was reluctant when Blackburn first described his aims, such as the testing that would be required. Despite this, she was convinced to aid Blackburn in his research efforts on the [[Forced Evolutionary Virus]], convinced of the need to adapt the human race for the hostile conditions of the wasteland, especially after pressure by Nellie. Farha also brought in Jain whom Blackburn already knew. Farha established a laboratory suitable for mass-production. Farha truly wanted her research to give humanity a better chance of surviving in the wasteland. However she would come to regret bringing Jain and Nellie onto the project, feeling as though she could not deter their enthusiasm. Due to the peer pressure, Farha became complicit with the killing of human test subjects. Not wanting the lives of the deceased to be for nothing, while realizing the project needed more human test subjects for their work to come to fruition, she found herself in a vicious and violent cycle.Doctor Farha: ''"It went too far, and quite frankly, I regret bringing the others onto this project. By the time I figured out that Dr. Blackburn was experimenting on humans, Nellie and Dr. Jain had already become passionate about the project. I was unable to convince them to pull back. I stayed in the hopes that my objections could save even one innocent person from being experimented on."''
([[Farha/Dialogue#221|Doctor Farha's dialogue]]) In 2104, Farha and her associates began the preparation of using their modified FEV into the air and water of Appalachia, which would affect the groundwater and likely other areas due to the precipitation cycle. They had their laboratory guarded by mercenaries of the [[Hellcat Company]]. She is described by Blackburn as being the leader of her group consisting of Jain and Nellie, and she mentions she takes full responsibility for the horrors of their actions. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |killable =yes |none = |dead = |quests started = |quests involved =[[The Catalyst]] |events started = |events involved = |encounters involved= |essential = |essential until = |ghost = |hostile = |ally = |temp companion = |ghoul =yes |other = |locations =* [[FEV production facility]] * [[Fort Atlas]] (optional) }} ===Quests=== [[The Catalyst]]: Farha and her team may be spared or killed depending on the Vault Dweller's influence. She tries to convince [[Daniel Shin]] to let her live, mentioning that universities no longer exist and the amount of people with formal educations are dwindling. She also exhibits interest in learning more about serums she has heard about and improving upon them. She says she mentions her work on FEV went too far and regrets bringing Nellie and Jain onto the project, and was unable to convince them to pull back. ===Other interactions=== If her life was spared in the Catalyst, Farha can be found in Fort Atlas, sometimes smoking. She comments [[Odessa Valdez]] is an excellent supervisor. She says the Vault Dweller made the right choice in sparing her life, saying indifference is easy and compassion much more difficult, and that her goals are aligned with the Brotherhood because they wish to help humanity. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Lab coat (Fallout 76)|Lab coat]]
