An eccentric bartender found at the [[Blue Ridge office]] in [[Appalachia]], Herschel deals in drinks and outlandish rumors while also attempting to work on a writing career. ==Background== Herschel Klein serves as a bartender for the Blue Ridge Caravan Company's bar at the [[Big Bend Tunnel west|western entrance]] to the [[Big Bend Tunnel]], though he also claims to be an author, an aspiring playwright, and a "reveler of life."Herschel Klein: ''"Herschel Klein, author, reveler of life, an aspiring playwright, and on certain occasions, bartender... at your service.''"
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) According to [[Vinny Costa]], Herschel simply "showed up one day" and has worked for Blue Ridge ever since, as Vinny is more than happy to let Herschel's bar collect more revenue for the company.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Tell me more about Herschel."''
[[Vinny Costa]]: ''"What's to know? He showed up one day. Pours drinks for Blue Ridge now so we can make some extra caps. The rest is him just bein' a pain in my neck."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) Although Herschel's eccentricities have occasionally gained Vinny's ire, Herschel is still a good bartender who can pour an exceptional drink, and as such, is tolerated by his co-workers at Blue Ridge.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Something's wrong with that man. He's back to work though."''
[[Vinny Costa]]: ''"Yeah, he ain't right in the head, but he pours a good drink. He's a pain, but you get used to it after a while."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) As a bartender, Herschel also trades rumors and often outright embellishments. Some of his outlandish rumors include that the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]] is actually a traveling theater troupe with members coming all the way from [[State#Florida|Florida]],[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Heard any rumors lately?"''
Herschel Klein: ''"So, the Brotherhood of Steel, right? I heard a rumor it's all fake. Just a traveling theater troupe. They've got a different con in every town. One of my regulars said he saw that Paladin Rahmani lady doing a trapeze act down in Florida. True Story!"''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) that everyone is actually just in a [[memory lounger]] simulation in [[Hoboken]], [[New Jersey]],[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Heard any rumors lately?"''
Herschel Klein: ''"Here's one I heard: we're all just living in a simulation. That's right: none of this is real. Die here and you'll wake up in a memory lounger somewhere in Hoboken, New Jersey. To be honest, I'm not sure which reality is worse! Thank you, thank you... I'm here all week!"''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) that [[Aries]] is an [[alien]] stuck after his spaceship was destroyed during the [[Great War]],[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Heard any rumors lately?"''
Herschel Klein: ''"You know that guard we got, Aries? He's got an encyclopedic knowledge of everything strange: cryptids, aliens, killer robots. I've been working on a theory: he IS an alien. His spaceship was destroyed when the bombs fell, and now he's stuck working for us just to get by. Poor guy. Must miss his home planet something awful."''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) that the [[Crater Raiders|Raiders]] in [[the Crater]] are actually astronauts that came down with the space station,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Heard any rumors lately?"''
Herschel Klein: ''"Rumor has it that the folks in the Crater are actually astronauts that came down with that space station... but their mission is top secret. Or, at least, that's what one of them told me last time they mugged me. Said he couldn't tell me what the caps were for. Highly classified."''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) that becoming a [[ghoul]] is actually a side effect of excessive [[Nuka-Cola]] consumption,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Heard any rumors lately?"''
Herschel Klein: ''"You know them ghouls? Well, I heard the bombs got nothing to do with it. It's just a side effect of drinking too much Nuka-Cola. Really, a dentist came through here telling me all about it. Said sugary drinks work a number on your teeth a few years, then, pow, you're a ghoul."''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) and that an intelligent society of [[Mole rat (Fallout 76)|mole rats]] thrives beneath [[Appalachia]].Herschel Klein: ''"You know, not half bad. And, you want to know something else I just heard? I heard that there's an intelligent and civilized mole rat society that lives underneath Appalachia. Lovely architecture, too. I kid you not!"''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) Though bartending is his primary focus as his day-to-day job, Herschel is serious about his writing aspirations, if in his own strange way. He is saddened by the fact that more people are not interested in his work, and claims to be working on an autobiography, ''My Life at the End of the World: A Herschel Klein Story'', with a foreword by the [[Mister Handy (Fallout 76)|Mister Handy]] [[Billingsley]] from [[Bolton Greens]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What is the Blue Ridge Caravan Company?"''
Herschel Klein: ''"Always with the questions about Blue Ridge. Never 'hello fine barkeep, what's your story?' No one's interested in reading the latest draft of'' 'My Life at the End of the World: A Herschel Klein Story' ''With a special foreword written by Billingsley of the Bolton Greens. Fine. The Blue Ridge Caravan Company is a caravan company. Hard as it is to believe, given its incredibly cryptic and non-descriptive name, I know. People pay us money to get things from one place to another place. If you want work, head over to the East side of the tunnel and talk to Vinny."''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) Herschel's lack of success in his hopeful career as a post-[[Great War|War]] author takes focus in the quest [[Costa Business: Herschel]]. A particularly nasty case of writer's block has affected Herschel to the point that Vinny Costa has noticed. In his roadblock, Herschel becomes slightly more self-deprecating than usual,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Just get back to serving the wine, instead of drinking it."''
Herschel Klein: ''"Ha! Oh uh, you're serious? You know, if I wasn't so busy being pathetic, I'd really give you knock in the... eh, who am I kidding. Help me out, will you"''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Sure, this doesn't sound crazy at all. But I'll do it."''
Herschel Klein: ''"I know, I know, I sound like a schmuck. Can't you see I'm desperate though. I'm begging you. Many thanks and yada yada yada."''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]])Herschel Klein: ''"What, are you here to watch the show? "A Paltry and Pitiful Putz", starring yours truly, the washed up has-been... Herschel Klein."''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) which Vinny refers to as "whining."[[Vinny Costa]]: ''"Hey, so... did ya fix Herschel's whinin' yet or what?"''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) To regain his motivation, Herschel asks the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] to investigate one of the many rumors he has heard. Herschel has heard of a supposed ghostly writer named [[Jacque]] haunting the [[Torrance House]]. Herschel wants to read Jacque's writing to gain inspiration for his own works, so that he may "share [Herschel's] brilliance and beauty with the world."Herschel Klein: ''"See, I've got a nasty case of writer's block. Honest, I'm telling you, I'm on the rocks. Is life worth living if you can't share your brilliance and beauty with the world? You know, I think I just figured out what I need though. I know this sounds crazy, but listen, rumor has it that there's uh... this ghost... that, well... uh writes. Or wrote. Is it writes or wrote? If it's a ghost would it be past tense... anyway, nevermind that. His name's Jacque or something or other. You ever heard of Torrance House? Sounds like he just litters the place with pages of his writings. Remarkable writings might I add. Hey, if he doesn't want them I'll take them! Go have a look around that house for me, and bring me back some of those writings. That's the ticket!"''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Why do you want a ghost's writings again?"''
Herschel Klein: ''"Look, I know you don't believe me. I barely believe me too. Thing is though, those writings might be exactly what I need to cure my writer's block. Thing is though, those writings might be exactly what I need to cure my writer's block. Herschel needs his inspiration, I'm begging you!"''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) Although Herschel is aware that the story of Jacque may sound as ridiculous as his other rumors,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Let's back up. Are you kidding me?"''
Herschel Klein: ''"Whether it's real or whether it's a joke, what does it matter? It's not like I want to steal his ideas, I just want to "borrow" a few. For good luck and inspiration. And any extra you find, for good measure. That doesn't hurt nothing, does it?"''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) it does turn out to have a nugget of truth in it, if slightly misguided. Jacque is actually a [[Protectron (Fallout 76)|Protectron]] who produced a series of jeering [[Writings of Jacque|notes]] directed at a [[Blood Eagles|Blood Eagle]] named [[Striker]].[[Writings of Jacque]] If told about Jacque, Herschel will express surprise at both of the facts that the writings were real[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dwellers]]: ''"I found your ghost writings. Herschel Klein: ''"What? You did? I can't believe it. You mean they actually exist? Alright, who's the comedian?"''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) and were actually produced by a [[robot]] (though he says the latter should be kept between him and the Vault Dwellers).[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Well you see, Jacque was actually a malfunctioning robot."''

Herschel Klein: ''"Well I'll be. The chances of something like that. One in a million! You don't think he'll come to haunt me now do you? Meh, what'll it matter, maybe he could be my ghostwriter."''
([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) and Vinny remarks that Herschel has started to have conversations with thin air, though he still bartends just fine.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Herschel back to his old self yet?"''

([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) Either way, Herschel becomes reinvigorated and resumes work on his writings, as well as serving drinks without complaint.Herschel Klein: ''"I'll be honest. ([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) Even if Jacque's writings turn out to "stink," that is beside the point:Herschel Klein: ''"His writings stink! They stink I'm telling you. ([[Herschel Klein/Dialogue|Herschel Klein's dialogue]]) Herschel expresses his gratitude by promising to include the Vault Dwellers in one of his stories, which he puffs up as a rare honor, in typical Herschel fashion.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Don't mention it. ([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) is the head of the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] {{in|FO76}}. ==Background== ===Beginnings=== Descended from a family of truckers, Joanna Mayfield worked with shipping practically her whole life, earning her stripes hauling cargo up and down [[Appalachia]], primarily the [[Blue Ridge Parkway]]. She inherited the trucking business from her grandfather around [[Timeline#2073|2073]], due to the death of her father. She continued to manage the company, earning the loyalty of manager [[Vinny Costa]] and his crew. The [[Great War]] forced her to adapt, but not to surrender. Joanna decided to swap eighteen-wheelers for hardy [[brahmin]], re-founding the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] in the wake of the apocalypse, now as its owner and proprietor.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What can you tell me about the Blue Ridge Caravan Company?"''
Joanna Mayfield: ''"Well I suppose I could tell ya just about anything you want to know, darlin'. I am the owner and proprietor after all. But I'll save us both a little time and give ya the whitepaper version... Started out as a trucking company, hauling up and down the roads of Appalachia. The Blue Ridge parkway in particular, if the name didn't give it away. I inherited the business from my Granpappy. My dear ol' daddy wasn't exactly around well enough to take over himself. God rest his soul. But, being the entrepreneur I am, I didn't give in. Swapped eighteen wheelers for Brahmin backs and trucked on... so to speak. And now, here we are. Serving Appalachia with safe and efficient travel and merchandise.''"
([[Joanna Mayfield/Dialogue|Joanna Mayfield's dialogue]]) Over the next 25 years, she built it up into a professional outfit, providing security, commerce, and safe travel along the Blue Ridge Parkway.[[Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries#.28Draft.29 Company Speech|Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries; terminal, (Draft) Company Speech]] Joanna prioritized self-sufficiency above all else, rejecting offers of collaboration from [[Brotherhood of Steel|paramilitary groups]] to maintain independence.Vault 76 dweller: "''Why did you avoid contact with the Brotherhood of Steel?''"
Joanna Mayfield: "''I've spent two and a half decades fostering a self-sufficient, well-guarded and valuable service, all without some [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force|jackbooted overlords]] lookin' over us. The only thing the Brotherhood can offer is telling us what we can and can't do... and try to take a slice of my pie while they're at it. And thus, I have chosen to politely decline any collaboration between our organizations.''"
([[Joanna Mayfield/Dialogue|Joanna Mayfield's dialogue]]) While she jokes about refusing raises to contractors,Joanna Mayfield: "''If you're here for a pay raise, keep walking. If you're here for a chat, well... I suppose I've got a minute."''
([[Joanna Mayfield/Dialogue|Joanna Mayfield's dialogue]]) she pays them well, to the point that [[Kieran Kennedy]] could afford to hire a live-in guard for his adopted family.[[Dear Uncle K.]] She also does not tolerate intimidation of her employees as a means to an end.Vault 76 dweller: ''"Want me to rattle her cage a little? Make her see sense?"''
[[Vinny Costa]]: ''"While I appreciate the initiative *laughs*, Joanna would have my hide. Just go see what's makin' her mind wander and help put a stop to it."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) Joanna has a good eye for people, keeping close tabs on her head of operations, Vinny Costa, to keep him on the straight and narrow, setting aside toys to gift to Kieran's children, and making sure that [[Libby Wen]] and [[Carver Timmerman]] do not burn themselves out while doing runs for the company.[[Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries#Staff and Clients for Appalachia|Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries; terminal, Staff and Clients for Appalachia]] ===Expansion into Appalachia=== By 2103, the company was ready to expand north into [[Appalachia|West Virginia]], thanks to the containment of the [[Scorched Plague]] and humanity returning once more to the region. Vinny Costa spearheaded the initial push into the region, setting up operations centered around the [[Big Bend Tunnel]], providing a more or less safe route beneath the mountains and providing access to the western parts of Appalachia. Joanna planned for a visit to the region once operations were underway. A year later, she finally arrived, setting up an [[Blue Ridge office|office]] at the western end of the tunnel in order to investigate a string of disappearances tied to Blue Ridge operations. Clients who paid for safe transit had disappeared under unclear circumstances, and she wanted to both prevent a panic among customers and identify the culprits without scaring them off. Her internal investigation coincided with the arrival of the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force]], which also took interest in the matter. Joanna did not trust the Brotherhood, considering [[Leila Rahmani|Paladin Rahmani's]] investigations an attempt at "oppression and regulation" that her enterprise could do without.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Hold on, if you knew, why lie to Art Knapp? Why refuse our help?"''
Joanna Mayfield: ''"Plain and simple, I wanted to handle this internally. I didn't want news of this stirring up a panic, maybe causing the perpetrators to flee. Our clients paid us for safe transport, and we failed them. It was our responsibility to solve it... discreetly. I'm sure you can appreciate that. As for deceiving Mr. Knapp... I dislike fibbin', but sometimes you've got to play your cards close to your chest. Especially when lives are at stake."''
[[Leila Rahmani]]: ''"I don't buy it. Sounds more like you were trying to prevent future clients from being scared off. It makes me wonder if this sudden cooperation isn't in the interest of helping others... Maybe you've just been caught."''
Joanna Mayfield: ''"I'd be offended by these accusations, if it didn't weave such a fascinating story. Are you planning to sell that as a dime novel? Well... If you're wondering why my organization would choose to dodge your calls, examine the attitude with which you've started this conversation. This pseudo-authority you're flaunting is exactly the type of oppression and regulation that my free enterprise can do without."''
([[Joanna Mayfield/Dialogue|Joanna Mayfield's dialogue]] and [[Leila Rahmani/Dialogue|Leila Rahmani's dialogue]]) The secrecy, dodging answers, and ultimately lying to [[Art Knapp]] had the effect of making Joanna and her company a prime suspect. Rather than take drastic action, Paladin Rahmani decided to try subterfuge, assuming that Mayfield would be unfamiliar with her. Joanna saw through the ruse immediately: She finally agreed to the meeting, because Mayfield's own investigation had hit a brick wall, despite identifying multiple missing people after combing through company records.Vault 76 dweller: "''What else can you tell me about the caravan that went missing?"''
Joanna Mayfield: "''{{tooltip|Not much, I'm afraid. Whoever's behind this has been discrete up to this point.|Regretful}} After the train tunnel, we started looking over our records and notice more and more people had gotten "lost" on our runs. But we haven't been able to pin down a common factor yet... or any sign of where they ended up. {{tooltip|I'd be very much interested in hearing what y'all uncover. |Grateful}}"''
([[Joanna Mayfield/Dialogue#316|Joanna Mayfield's dialogue]]) Dealing with the Brotherhood was necessary to solve the mystery and prevent the Blue Ridge name from being tarnished.[[Leila Rahmani]]: ''"Ms. Mayfield. My name is Leila, I had made an appointment to speak with you."''
Joanna Mayfield: ''"Please, Joanna is just fine, dear... And while all this cloak and dagger hub-bub is flattering, why don't we cut to the chase... Paladin Rahmani.''"
Leila Rahmani: ''"Well, that was short lived. Okay, Joanna, it appears I've underestimated you."''
Joanna Mayfield: ''"And lookie there, you've got one of these famous Vault Dwellers in tow. Hm. Familiar looking too. Say, you've done some work for me haven't you? Yeah, that's right... Riding shotgun with my crew through Big Bend?"''
Leila Rahmani: ''"I'd appreciate if the job offers were saved for later. We're here on pressing business."''
Joanna Mayfield: ''"Okay, Paladin, down to brass tacks then. It's not an accident that I've finally opted to meet witcha, after playing hard to get for so long. We know you're interested in the folk that've gone missing. We are too. Been looking into it for a spell now.''"
([[Joanna Mayfield/Dialogue|Joanna Mayfield's dialogue]] and [[Leila Rahmani/Dialogue|Leila Rahmani's dialogue]]) While still standoffish, Mayfield and Rahmani agreed on a course of action. The two agreed to a joint investigation of the caravan camp in the [[Harpers Ferry tunnel]], sealed up by [[Aries]].Joanna Mayfield: ''"{{Tooltip|Harpers Ferry. The train tunnel. Mind showing our guests the route?|To the point}}"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|Oh crap. You really want to go back there?|He knows he will have to, but complaining anyway}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries]] and [[Joanna Mayfield/Dialogue#316|Joanna Mayfield's dialogue]]) While Rahmani's attitude grated on Joanna, it was Aries who truly put the strain on Rahmani's patience. His antics while investigating the tunnelAries: ''"{{Tooltip|There's a trick to getting in. Gimme one shake of a Lambsquatch's tail to get it open.|Nonchalant}} {{Tooltip|Let's see... Thirty days past September... Carry the two...|Examining a calendar}}"''
[[Leila Rahmani|Paladin Rahmani]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Is this for real?|Lost patience (witnessing Aries hammer the wall to open a door)}}"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|And viola! It's just a little further ahead. Please, after you.|Intentionally says viola instead of voila.}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries]] and [[Leila Rahmani/Dialogue|Leila Rahmani's dialogue]]) almost led Paladin Rahmani to conclude that it was Joanna's attempt at an elaborate coverup,Aries: ''"Your boss looks like she's about to strangle me with one of those vines. Something happen in there?"''
[[Leila Rahmani|Paladin Rahmani]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Aries, between the Feral Ghouls, the strangler vines and that insane sheep robot, I've about reached my limit with this place... and your antics.|Pretty pissed}} I don't know if this is some kind of trap, or elaborate cover-up, but we need to get through that door and get answers. Now."''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|Whoa, whoa, trap? Where's this coming from? Hold on, did you say "sheep robot"? Like the baa-baa kind, or the killer robot kind?|Initially taken aback, then only cares about the sheep robot. This REALLY interests him.}}"''
Paladin Rahmani: ''"{{Tooltip|Aries. The door. Now. Please.|Pretty pissed}}"''
Aries: ''"{{Tooltip|Okay, just give me a second. Yeesh.|Offended, sarcastic}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries]] and [[Leila Rahmani/Dialogue|Leila Rahmani's dialogue]]) until they finally arrived at the caravan stop and uncovered evidence identifying [[Edgar Blackburn]] and the [[Hellcat Company]] as parties responsible for the mass kidnapping.Paladin Rahmani: "''{{tooltip|Aries... I owe you an apology.|Hesitation}} My rash behavior was unfitting of my position, and frankly, unfair to you."''
Aries: "''{{tooltip|Eh, water under the bridge. All of my best friendships start with misplaced suspicion of mass kidnapping.|Nonchalant}}"''
Paladin Rahmani: "''{{tooltip|I will... take your word for it. I am sorry, either way.|Trying very hard to be nice}}"''
Aries: "''{{tooltip|If you really want to make it up to me, I've heard you guys have some killer rocket launchers to spare.|worth a shot}}"''
Paladin Rahmani: "''{{tooltip|Absolutely not.|Shutting it down.}}"''
([[Aries/Dialogue|Aries']] and [[Leila Rahmani/Dialogue|Leila Rahmani's dialogue]]) Joanna was pleased with the results of the investigation. While she did not plan to make a habit out of helping "jackbooted overlords", as she called them, she was glad to have helped the Brotherhood clear her company's name.Vault 76 dweller: "''We found the people who went missing in the Harper's Ferry train tunnel."''
Joanna Mayfield: "''{{tooltip|So I heard. While I don't plan to make a habit of it, I'm glad we were able to lend the Brotherhood a hand in this particular instance.|Satisfied, but cautious}}"''
([[Joanna Mayfield/Dialogue#316|Joanna Mayfield's dialogue]]) As the company continued to expand their operations in Appalachia, Joanna helped set up a job at the [[Middle Mountain Pitstop]] for [[Vera Thornberg]], the daughter of a pre-War Blue Ridge trucker whom Joanna knew well.Vault 76 dweller: ''"What's so important about getting these photos?"''
[[Vera Thornberg]]: ''"Well I was plannin' on visiting the pitstops of my Daddy's old trucker route from before the bombs dropped. I know seeing those old places would just warm his heart, specially since he hasn't had a mind to travel since Momma passed. *Sighs* But, I can't just abandon my post after Joanna went to all the trouble getting it for me. Plus I'm not sure if I'd last one minute out there alone."''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]])Vault 76 dweller: ''"How long have you been with running the shop?"''
[[Vera Thornberg]]: ''"Joined up a while back thanks to my Daddy knowin' Joanna from before the bombs dropped. This cabin area was converted recently into our new pitstop, allowin' the caravanners to rest and trade Brahmin. Been here since."''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) Overall, under Joanna's leadership, Blue Ridge as a company has operated smoothly, something that Vinny Costa recognizes as a comfortable normalcy.Vault 76 dweller: ''"How about the other members?"''
[[Vinny Costa]]: ''"Eh, everybody else is doin' all right. With Jo at the helm, we're normally runnin' pretty smooth. We're about back to that now, thanks to you."''

Very nice.|sound=Minerva 00602b69_1.ogg}} '''Minerva''' is a [[gold bullion]] [[Fallout 76 vendors|vendor]] selling rare [[Fallout 76 plans|plans]] and [[Fallout 76 recipes|recipes]] at discount, working for the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] in [[Appalachia]], {{in|FO76}}. She deals in gold bullion and is protected by her bodyguard, [[Tommy Ten-Toes]] and her [[Brahmin (Fallout 76)|brahmin]] [[Minos]]. She has traveled with the Blue Ridge Caravan Company in the past, and has worked with [[Aries]].[[Caravan manifest]] In gameplay terms, she is a discounted gold bullion merchant, offering a selection of unique plans for purchase at a 25% discount. However, her offer is limited and she rotates between four locations each week. ==Background== Minerva lived in [[Washington, D.C.]] as a child before the [[Great War]], managing to survive the bombs inside a library functioning as a secondary shelter. After wandering through the wasteland from group to group, her talents finally caught the attention of a [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company|Blue Ridge Caravan]] group. She joined up and ended up as an apprentice to a bookseller, learning how to copy books by hand. Over time, the bookseller turned into a friend and mentor. After his passing, she took over his caravan and expanded its inventory, switching from selling printed media to more practical items, including schematics and recipes. She considers Blue Ridge to be more than just a business party; to her, the faction is an actual family, and she could not ask for a better one.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You're with the Blue Ridge Caravan Company?"''
Minerva: ''"Sure am. Been with 'em since I was pint sized brainy brat. I'm originally from DC. Survived the bombs thanks to my local library seconding as a bomb shelter. Wound up wandering from group to group, until my talents caught the eye of some Blue Ridge folk passing through. Ended up being an apprentice for a book salesman, rewriting books by hand. He was a dear friend and great mentor. After he passed, I took over his caravan. Switched from books to something a little more catered for the modern survivor's needs, though. But Blue Ridge are my business partners and my family... And I couldn't ask for a better one."''
([[Minerva/Dialogue|Minerva's dialogue]]) She has one key advantage in her line of work: an exceptional memory and the capability to copy any schematic, plan or recipe she sees in perfect detail, not unlike a human copying machine.Vault 76 dweller: "''What sort of things do you sell here?"''
Minerva: "''{{tooltip|You'd think with all the carnival barking I do, I wouldn't get this question much. But alas, here I go answering it again.|Not too snarky, more laughing at herself}} My caravan sells recreations of all sorts of rare plans and recipes, at discounted prices no less. {{tooltip|I've got what you'd call... a photographic memory. If I've seen it, I can picture it, and draw it exactly so.|Proud of herself}} {{tooltip|'The human copying machine,' they say, but I suspect that name will lose its veneer once anyone that remembers copying machines has died off.|A little side joke}} {{tooltip|If you're interested in plans at unbeatable prices, I'm the best that the Blue Ridge Caravan Company has.|Sales pitch}}"''
([[Minerva/Dialogue|Minerva's dialogue]]) She claims she is able to copy them down to 1/100th of a millimeter. Regardless of the truth of this claim, her plans are indistinguishable from the originals.Minerva: "''{{tooltip|Behold! Picture perfect copies of plans and recipes! Hand-drawn from my photographic memory, you'd never know these weren't the real thing!|carnival barker, like she's describing the eight wonder of the world}}"''
([[Minerva/Dialogue|Minerva's dialogue]]) This makes her very popular on the caravan trail, but since she recreates the materials by hand, her offer is limited. Carpal tunnel syndrome is particularly unpleasant in the wasteland, where few treatments survive.Vault 76 dweller: "''I thought you make all this from memory. Why can't you just offer everything all the time?"''
Minerva: "''{{tooltip|My mind may be unending, but I can only draw so much before my wrist snaps in two.|chuckling at the idea}} Not many treatments for carpal tunnel syndrome in the Wasteland, you know."''
([[Minerva/Dialogue|Minerva's dialogue]]) She primarily relies on observations she makes during her troubles to update and rotate the stock, and remains on the move to keep her stock fresh.Vault 76 dweller: "''How long will you be here?"''
Minerva: "''Not long. So if you've got your eye on something act fast. My stock is constantly rotating with new and exciting observations from my travels. But that also means you're unlikely to see the same thing on back to back visits, so grab what you can while I'm here."''
([[Minerva/Dialogue|Minerva's dialogue]]) Her talents would make her an excellent preservationist, but she is amused by the suggestion of using it for anything other than making a profit. Trade is the only thing she knows and she likes it that way.Vault 76 dweller: "''A photographic memory? Isn't this a waste of your talent?"''
Minerva: "''{{tooltip|And what else could I be spending my talent on, pray tell? Turning a profit is all I know, and I ever want to know.|Not being mean, but also humored by the question... Like really?}}"''
([[Minerva/Dialogue|Minerva's dialogue]]) She works closely with [[Tommy Ten-Toes]], a ghoulified former mob enforcer. While she calls him a "big goofy teddy bear," she trusts him entirely to keep her and the caravan safe, and may have observed him rip out someone's sternum for stealing from the caravan in the past.Vault 76 dweller: "''What's with the big Ghoul in the hat?"''
Minerva: "''Tommy? Well it wouldn't be a caravan without someone riding shotgun. He may seem intimidating, but he's a big goofy teddy bear. Loves to chat, so say hi. {{tooltip|Try and steal something, though, and he will rip your sternum out. I've seen him do it. Very graphic.|Maybe true, maybe not, but playful delivery}}"''
([[Minerva/Dialogue|Minerva's dialogue]]) Tommy likes Minerva, although his underwhelming intellect makes him unable to understand why Minerva's work is so popular among wastelanders.Vault 76 dweller: "''What's it like working for Minerva?"''
Tommy Ten-Toes: "''{{tooltip|To be clear: Tommy don' work for Minerva. Tommy works for the Blue Ridge Caravan Company.|Not upset by this, just being clear}} But... seeing as I only ever gets paired wit Minerva, I guess it don' make much difference. {{tooltip|Anyways, she's all right. You know that she draws them pictures of guns and stuff herself right? And people are actually buyin' em?|Thinks the customers are dumb (even though he's pretty dumb)}} {{tooltip|Maybe I should sell some drawins too. I draw animals real good. Like dem kangaroos. Oh, and rhinoceroses.|Going off on a tangent}} {{tooltip|I love rhinoceroses... Ya ever been ta the zoo? I miss zoos.|Has totally lost the plot}}"'' He appreciates her silver tongue and spirit,Tommy Ten-Toes: "''{{tooltip|Minerva's got a real way with them words. Not like Tommy. That's me. I'm Tommy. Tommy Ten-Toes. How ya' doin'?|Not realizing how off the rails he is}}"''
([[Tommy Ten-Toes/Dialogue|Tommy Ten-Toes' dialogue]]) and the two are considered by [[Vinny Costa]] to be an excellent team.Vault 76 dweller: "''How about the other members?"''
Vinny Costa: "''Ah, right. There's Minerva and Tommy. Hard to pin down, but when I see 'em, they always seem chipper."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) This is still the case even after the [[Chattanooga]] incident, which involved Minerva, Tommy's ten-toed foot, and an unfortunate dog. The two kept working together, but Minerva prohibited Tommy from ever taking shoes off in front of customers again.Vault 76 dweller: "''Hold on a second, ten toes... on one foot?"''
Tommy Ten-Toes: "''{{tooltip|Oh yeah. You wanna see 'em? Oh, sorry, Minerva said I can't be takin' my shoes off in front of customers no more.|Excited and then bummed}} {{tooltip|Especially afta' what happened in Chattanooga. That poor lil' doggie...|Whatever happened to that doggie, it can't be good.}}"''
([[Tommy Ten-Toes/Dialogue|Tommy Ten-Toes' dialogue]]) Minerva has mastered the art of sale, styling herself as a merchant who is appreciated primarily by people with a refined, special taste.Minerva: "''Aha, you could have gone to any old merchant, but you, my friend, have that special refined taste. Very nice."''
([[Minerva/Dialogue|Minerva's dialogue]]) At the same time, she promotes her wares in the manner of a carnival barker, emphasizing the range of her offer, accurate copying and prices well below those of the competition.Minerva: "''{{tooltip|I sell plans, schematics, and recipes supreme. From weapons to armors, and all things between.|Playful rhythm, like a carnival barker}} {{tooltip|Drawn from my memory: a human copying machine. All found at prices that you've never seen!|emphasis on "my", continue the rhythm}}"''
([[Minerva/Dialogue|Minerva's dialogue]])Minerva: "''{{tooltip|My photographic memory allows me to share plans from far and wide at prices that can't be beat!|carnival barker}} {{tooltip|Every schematic and recipe recreated to perfection. Satisfaction guaranteed!|Salesman}}"''
([[Minerva/Dialogue|Minerva's dialogue]]) While her limited selection of goods is primarily to avoid injuring her wrist, she turned it around and integrated it into her marketing, telling prospective buyers that they should make a purchase on the spot, as she likely will not be carrying the item next time.Minerva: "''{{tooltip|Hello, Appalachia! ([[Minerva/Dialogue|Minerva's dialogue]]) She also has a knack for rhymesMinerva: "''{{tooltip|See a plan that strikes your fancy? Better pick it up today. ([[Minerva/Dialogue|Minerva's dialogue]]) and instinctively understanding her target audience. ([[Minerva/Dialogue|Minerva's dialogue]]) casual camaraderie and bad puns at [[Foundation]],Minerva: "''{{tooltip|People of Foundation, I come bearing tidings of low prices! ([[Minerva/Dialogue|Minerva's dialogue]]) and the Brotherhood of Steel's unique jargon at [[Fort Atlas]].Minerva: "''{{tooltip|Nothing says 'Ad Victoriam' like great prices and rare finds! ([[Minerva/Dialogue|Minerva's dialogue]])Minerva: "''{{tooltip|Friends and patrons, today is the day. Even if you are, it's pretty rude to make sudden unwarranted diagnoses of people you just met.|Nellie, when called a sociopath.|sound=Nellie Wright 00602e7b_1.ogg}} '''Nellie Wright''' is a researcher recruited for [[Edgar Blackburn]]'s research on the [[Forced Evolutionary Virus]]. ==Background== A prodigy of sorts, Nellie met [[Farha]] when she broke through Farha's window while searching for scraps, as a wastelander trying to survive. Nellie was interested in Farha's research so Farha took her in and taught her.[[Farha|Doctor Farha]]: ''"I met Nellie when she broke through my window to search for scraps. As Wasteland survivors do. She was more interested in my research notes than my leftovers. So I took her in and taught her what I know."''
([[Farha/Dialogue#219|Doctor Farha's dialogue]]) Nellie was brought in by Farha to assist Edgar Blackburn's research on the [[Forced Evolutionary Virus]], convinced of the need to adapt the human race for the hostile conditions of the wasteland. Her enthusiastic support of Blackburn's ideas convinced Farha to acquiesce to Blackburn's request for aid, and Farha could not talk Nellie out of it. Nellie also worked alongside [[Jain (Steel Reign)|Jain]]. When caught by the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force|Brotherhood of Steel]], unlike Farha, Nellie exhibits little to no remorse and tries to justify her actions for working on the project, often smiling at the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] during their conversation. She claims she would not mind being kidnapped and experimented on for their project, claiming other kidnappers do far worse than their group.Nellie Wright: ''"To improve the human race. If I was kidnapped for our experiments, I wouldn't mind. Most kidnappers do much worse."''
([[Nellie Wright/Dialogue#228|Nellie Wright's dialogue]]) Nellie also defends herself with her age, saying she is too young to die. Nellie also has a knife on her and when asked to hand over her arms, Nellie tries to play dumb and does not hand it over.Nellie Wright: ''"I, uh, I don't have any arms. Well, unless you mean human arms, because I've got two of those. But they're mine. You can't have 'em."''
([[Nellie Wright/Dialogue#246|Nellie Wright's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |killable =yes |none = |dead = |quests started = |quests involved =[[The Catalyst]] |events started = |events involved = |encounters involved= |essential = |essential until = |ghost = |hostile = |ally = |temp companion = |ghoul =yes |other = |locations =* [[FEV production facility]] * [[Fort Atlas]] (optional) }} [[The Catalyst]]: Nellie and her team may be spared or killed depending on the Vault Dweller's influence. * If the Vault Dweller decides to execute their group, Jain and Farha cower in fear as Nellie tries to kill [[Daniel Shin]] with a knife. Shin is marked as essential, Nellie and her team are killed. * If her life was spared in The Catalyst, she can be found in [[Fort Atlas]]. She says she would tell the Vault Dweller what she's working on, but they would not be able to understand. She bets that they can't recite Pi to a thousand digit. She is annoyed because the Brotherhood has too many restrictions, wondering how she can accomplish anything. She also says, "Nothing to see here, except the coolest science you've ever seen." ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Lab coat (Fallout 76)|Lab coat]] |weapon =[[Cultist dagger]] |otheritem = |ondeath =[[Cultist dagger]] }} ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|I heard when the Brotherhood breaks down your door they say, "Ad victory! Hand over your arms!" Is that true?|sound=Nellie Wright 00602e79_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|We're advancing science itself. The cost doesn't matter. No offense to Dr. Jain, but West Tek wasn't doing science. They were only burning ants with a magnifying glass by comparison.|sound=Nellie Wright 00602c46_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Hey, you want to stay and watch us change the world, fine by me. I'll be making history.|sound=Nellie Wright 00602c16_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Why? Because it's the frontier of science! It's the next step in our self-guided evolution as a species! Why wouldn't we do this?|sound=Nellie Wright 00602c58_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Wrong? Who says? What does morality have to do with any of this? So people got hurt. That's nothing compared to what we'll accomplish.|sound=Nellie Wright 00602c41_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|All of them? No. Humans are broken in so many ways we can't fix. But we can keep them from dying from radiation or getting sick because the water's poison. We can make it so they don't have to be afraid of the world around them anymore.|sound=Nellie Wright 00602c2a_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|To improve the human race. If I was kidnapped for our experiments, I wouldn't mind. Most kidnappers do much worse.|sound=Nellie Wright 00602e71_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|You're not really gonna kill us, are you? I'm awfully young to die. You can fit a lot of experiments into sixty more years.|sound=Nellie Wright 00602e7d_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|I'd tell you what we're working on, but you wouldn't understand it.|sound=Nellie Wright 00604156_1.ogg}} ==Appearances== Nellie Wright appears only {{In|FO76SR}}. ==Gallery== FO76SR Blackburn group.png|Nellie's final moment with Edgar Blackburn Nellie knife.png|Nellie trying to kill [[Daniel Shin]] with a knife ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox Steel Reign}} {{Navbox antagonists}} [[Category:Steel Reign human characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 scientists]] [[Category:Antagonists]] [[ru:Нелли Райт]]

{{ID|00605F1B}} (The Crater) }} {{Quotation|Well, they call me Tommy Ten-Toes on accounts of my ten toes... on the one foot.|sound=Tommy Ten-Toes 00602d59_1.ogg}} '''Tommy Ten-Toes''' is a caravan guard for the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How's life as a caravan guard?"''
Tommy Ten-Toes: ''"Oh you know. None too bad, none too good. A lot of walkin'. A bit of shootin'. Mostly just standin' around, trying ta look all intimadatin' like."''
([[Tommy Ten-Toes/Dialogue#33|Tommy Ten-Toes' dialogue]]) He accompanies [[Minerva]] on her travels through [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76}}. ==Background== A former mobster of Italian extraction, Tommy Ten-Toes was exposed to [[radiation]] and turned into a [[ghoul]] by the [[Great War]]. Despite his ghoulification, Tommy remains someone with a hulking physique, though he has much more brawn than he does brains. Fortunately for him, he fell in with the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] and works under [[Vinny Costa]], who ensures he keeps his mouth shut when it comes to talking about his past.Tommy Ten-Toes: "''{{tooltip|Workin' for Blue Ridge is a lot easier than running jobs for... Wait a minute, Vinny said no talkin' bout that.|Almost let slip that he used to work in the mob (even tho no one actually asked). Thinks he got the upper hand}}"''
([[Tommy Ten-Toes/Dialogue#51|Tommy Ten-Toes' dialogue]]) Vinny is perfectly aware of Tommy's shortcomings (including the apparent inability to count to fifty),[[Vault 76 dweller]]: "''How about the other members?''"
[[Vinny Costa]]: "''{{tooltip|Eh, everybody else is doin' all right. With Jo at the helm, we're normally runnin' pretty smooth. We're about back to that now, thanks to you.|Not TOO appreciative }} Granted, my nephew Luca will always be a pain, and Aries will always be a creep, but, uh... Let's see. Ah, right. There's Minerva and Tommy. Hard to pin down, but when I see 'em, they always seem chipper. She's got good deals, too. Make sure you peruse if you bump into her. Oh, and if ya see Tommy Ten-Toes... While I know he can't count that high, tell him he still owes me 50 caps.''"
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) but considers him a professional when it comes to protecting Blue Ridge merchants, especially Minerva, their top performer.Vinny Costa: "''As for Minerva and the big lug? She's our top performer, no troubles there-- and Tommy's a pro.''"
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) Tommy doesn't mind the job, though finds it a bit boring, as it mostly entails standing around looking intimidating, whenever he is not shadowing Minerva on the trail and ensuring no harm comes to her. Though they contrast heavily, Minerva is quite fond of Tommy. His lack of intellect is more than compensated for by his strength. Minerva allegedly saw him rip a thief's sternum out once.Vault 76 dweller: "''What's with the big Ghoul in the hat?"''
Minerva: "''Tommy? Well it wouldn't be a caravan without someone riding shotgun. He may seem intimidating, but he's a big goofy teddy bear. Loves to chat, so say hi. {{tooltip|Try and steal something, though, and he will rip your sternum out. I've seen him do it. Very graphic.|Maybe true, maybe not, but playful delivery}}"''
 Tommy is often unaware of his eccentricities, which leads him to misunderstand social interactionsTommy Ten-Toes: "''{{tooltip|Ho ho, thought you'd pull a fast one on Tommy Ten-Toes, eh? Nice try, pally.|Proud of himself for winning an argument (with no one)}}"''
([[Tommy Ten-Toes/Dialogue#51|Tommy Ten-Toes' dialogue]]) and drift off in conversation.Tommy Ten-Toes: "''{{tooltip|Minerva's got a real way with them words. Not like Tommy. That's me. I'm Tommy. Tommy Ten-Toes. How ya' doin'?|Not realizing how off the rails he is}}"''
([[Tommy Ten-Toes/Dialogue#51|Tommy Ten-Toes' dialogue]]) Although he loves talking, he is rather lonely, and only vaguely aware of it.Tommy Ten-Toes: "''{{tooltip|'Course they could talk ta me. I love talkin'. You, uh... you wanna talk ta me?|Emphasis on COULD. Realizes he's actually kind of lonely}}"''
([[Tommy Ten-Toes/Dialogue#51|Tommy Ten-Toes' dialogue]]) He likes working with Minerva (not ''for'' her, as they both are part of Blue Ridge), though he does not really understand why her plans are so popular with customers. He considers them just drawings, and occasionally thinks about selling some of his own drawings. He believes he is quite good at portraying animals, such as [[Creature#Kangaroo|kangaroos]] and [[Creature#Rhinoceros|rhinoceroses]]. He loves the latter and was a frequent visitor at zoological gardens before the War. He misses them dearly.Vault 76 dweller: "''What's it like working for Minerva?"''
Tommy Ten-Toes: "''{{tooltip|To be clear: Tommy don' work for Minerva. Tommy works for the Blue Ridge Caravan Company.|Not upset by this, just being clear}} But... seeing as I only ever gets paired wit Minerva, I guess it don' make much difference. {{tooltip|Anyways, she's all right. You know that she draws them pictures of guns and stuff herself right? And people are actually buyin' em?|Thinks the customers are dumb (even though he's pretty dumb)}} {{tooltip|Maybe I should sell some drawins too. I draw animals real good. Like dem kangaroos. Oh, and rhinoceroses.|Going off on a tangent}} {{tooltip|I love rhinoceroses... Ya ever been ta the zoo? I miss zoos.|Has totally lost the plot}}"''
([[Tommy Ten-Toes/Dialogue#54|Tommy Ten-Toes' dialogue]]) Tommy was originally called Tommy the Nose (which he misinterpreted as knowing a lot, rather than his distinct nose), but received his current nickname after radiation turned him into a ghoul. The loss of Tommy's nose was compensated by an increase in the number of toes: Tommy has ten toes on one foot, for a total of fifteen on both (which also appears to be the upper limit on his ability to count).Vault 76 dweller: "''How did you get your name?"''
Tommy Ten-Toes: "''{{tooltip|Well, they call me Tommy Ten-Toes on accounts of my ten toes... on the one foot.|Casual, nothing unusual here!}} {{tooltip|They used to call me Tommy the Nose. Pretty sure it's 'cause I nose a lot. I nose about business, I nose about guns. I nose it all.|Thinks "nose" is "knows"}} {{tooltip|But, uh, after getting all Ghouly they stopped calling me the nose... Maybe they don't think I nose it like I used to.|He's a ghoul now (and thus has no nose). He clearly doesn't understand the connection.}} {{tooltip|But, I got these toes, though. More than I can count! Oh wait, fifteen. Fifteen toes. See? Tommy still nose.|All over the place, but proud of himself at the end}}"''
([[Tommy Ten-Toes/Dialogue#59|Tommy Ten-Toes' dialogue]]) He used to show his mutated foot to customers, until an unfortunate incident in [[Chattanooga]], which involved Minerva and an unfortunate dog. Ever since, he is forbidden from taking his boots off in front of customers.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Hold on a second, ten toes... on one foot?"''
Tommy Ten-Toes: "''{{tooltip|Oh yeah. You wanna see 'em? Oh, sorry, Minerva said I can't be takin' my shoes off in front of customers no more.|Excited and then bummed}} {{tooltip|Especially afta' what happened in Chattanooga. That poor lil' doggie...|Whatever happened to that doggie, it can't be good.}}"''
([[Tommy Ten-Toes/Dialogue#59|Tommy Ten-Toes' dialogue]]) On a more positive note, Tommy played darts with [[Eugenie]] during a stay at [[Middle Mountain Pitstop]], with the former mobster narrowly losing to the arms merchant. It appears that their preferred variant is the 301 version of the game.[[:File:FO76OB Middle Mountain Pitstop darts.png|Darts at the Pitstop]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |ghost =yes |locations =* [[Foundation]] * [[The Crater]] * [[Fort Atlas]] * [[The Whitespring Resort]] |others = Tommy provides some flavor and background information on Minerva and his life. }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Blue Ridge Caravan outfit]]
[[Battered fedora (Fallout 76)|Battered fedora]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Tommy Ten-Toes appears only {{In|FO76SR}}. ==Behind the scenes== * Quest designer [[Carl McKevitt]] contributed to Tommy Ten-Toes' writing and design. In July 2021, he said that Tommy is his personal favorite out of the characters he has worked on.[[Fallout 76 developer statements#Carl McKevitt: Tommy Ten-Toes, 2021 Jul 14|''Fallout 76'' developer statements; Carl McKevitt: Tommy Ten-Toes, 2021 Jul 14]] * His name is very similar and rhymes with the name of [[Bobbi No-Nose]], a ghoul in ''[[Fallout 4]]''. ** Bobbi's nickname refers to a trait all ghouls share. In the same vein, Tommy's nickname refers to a trait generally universal to all people. ==Gallery== FO76SR Tommy Ten Toes.png ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox Steel Reign}} [[Category:Wastelanders ghoul characters]] [[Category:Blue Ridge Caravan Company characters]] [[ru:Томми Десять-Пальцев]]

We can't spare them on the farm, though, too much work to do. One, maybe, long as you swear to look out for him. Reckon you'd best ask the wife, though.|sound=George Putnam 005d950c_1.ogg}} '''George Putnam''' is a resident of [[Lewis & Sons Farming Supply]] in [[Appalachia]], living there with the rest of his family. ==Background== George has been married to his wife [[Carol Putnam|Carol]] for twenty years.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How's the farm doing?"''
[[Carol Putnam]]: ''"We're getting to be self-sufficient soon. Greenhouse is getting there. George wants to restore the house, but we're fine in here."''
George Putnam: ''"The boys are going to want rooms of their own, dear. Don't act like you wouldn't mind being away from their snoring."''
Carol Putnam: ''"We've got other work needs doing first. If I can put up with your snoring for twenty years, I can deal with them."''
([[Carol Putnam/Dialogue|Carol]] and [[George Putnam/Dialogue|George Putnam's dialogue]]) He and his family returned to Appalachia in 2103 and made their home at the former farm supply store. The family first secured the barn before later returning to begin restoring the location. [[Lewis (Fallout 76)|Lewis]], the previous owner who had died alongside his family, was George's cousin, and Carol claimed the Putnams were the rightful owners and inheritors of the location.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"This is your farm? The signs outside said "Lewis & Sons.""''
[[Carol Putnam]]: ''"Might not be Lewis, or Sons, but this here's ours."''
George Putnam: ''"Lewis was a cousin o' mine, back in the day, God rest his soul. He and his family didn't make it when the bombs fell. We were looking a good place to put down roots when we heard it was safe to come back to West Virginia. I told Carol we ought to see if this place was still here."''
Carol Putnam: ''"Even after all these years, there was enough salvageable tools and such to make starting a farm easier here than your average homestead. Didn't see any point in updating the sign."''
([[Carol Putnam/Dialogue|Carol Putnam's]] and [[George Putnam/Dialogue|George Putnam's dialogue]]) Carol uses the threat of George and his shotgun as a deterrent for would-be troublemakers.[[Notice: New owners]] After George's sons both express interest in joining the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force|Brotherhood]], he and Carol both agree that one son could join, but the farm could not spare both of them. George is more lenient of Marty and Colin joining the Brotherhood than Carol is. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Field Testing]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =Overalls underarmor (non-lootable) |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== George Putnam appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]'', introduced in the ''[[Steel Dawn]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]] and is mentioned in ''[[One Wasteland For All]]''. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Steel Dawn}} [[Category:Steel Dawn human characters]] [[ru:Джордж Патнам]]

{{Infobox character |games =FO76, FO76SR |name =Cassie Halloway |image =FO76 Cassie.png |image desc = |race =[[Human]] |gender =Female |affiliation =[[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] |role = |rank = |location =[[Vault 96]]
[[Foundation supply room]] |family =Unnamed grandfather {{Icon|dead}}[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Tell me more about yourself."''
[[Art Knapp]]: ''"Ain't much to tell. Been a farmer, one way or another, all my life. My daddy before me, and so on. Set up in these parts after I heard it was safe again. Turned out there's plenty of Raiders fixin' to take what ain't nailed down. Ain't much use bellyachin' about it, but neither am I just gonna roll over and let some bullies take what's mine."''
([[Art Knapp/Dialogue|Art Knapp's dialogue]])
Unnamed mother[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Slow down a second, what's the full situation?"''
[[Leila Rahmani]]: ''"Mr. Knapp's niece, Cassie-"''
[[Art Knapp]]: ''"Cassie Halloway, my sister's girl. About twenty somethin'."''
Leila Rahmani: ''"Right, Ms. Halloway apparently paid the Blue Ridge Caravan Company to transport her to Appalachia. It would appear she never arrived. However, the people Mr. Knapp spoke with at Blue Ridge claim she was never a client to begin with."''
Art Knapp: ''"'Cept thems damn liars. I got letters from Cassie. She spells them out, plain as day. 'I'm travelin' with Blue Ridge something or other.'"''
Leila Rahmani: ''"Right. All caught up, Initiate?"''
([[Leila Rahmani/Dialogue|Leila Rahmani's]] and [[Art Knapp/Dialogue|Art Knapp's dialogue]])

Not that sorry, though. He did it anyway, and lots of folks died at his hands. So I hope he died badly.|sound=Cassie Halloway 00605055_1.ogg}} '''Cassie Halloway''' is a member of the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Prior to traveling to Appalachia, Cassie lived as a farmer[[Caravan manifest]][[Cassie's journal]] "out West" and remained in contact with her uncle in [[Appalachia]], [[Art Knapp]], by writing letters to him.[[Leila Rahmani]]: ''"Mr. Knapp here has come to us with another missing persons case."''
[[Art Knapp]]: ''"My niece, Cassie. Cassie Halloway. She paid some caravin' folk to help her travel here from out West. Sent me some letters just before she set out. Them letters arrived just fine, but she didn't. I went and spoke with them caravanners and they tell me that my Cassie never set out with 'em at all. Those, er, Blue Mountain whatsit..."''
Leila Rahmani: ''"The Blue Ridge Caravan Company."''
([[Leila Rahmani/Dialogue|Leila Rahmani's]] and [[Art Knapp/Dialogue|Art Knapp's dialogue]]) At some point, she decided to move to [[Foundation]] and help them with farming. Cassie traveled alongside a [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company|Blue Ridge caravan]] that took 15 days of walking before reaching [[the Mire]]. After staying the night in an [[Harpers Ferry tunnel|old train tunnel]] to avoid a major [[radstorm]], the caravan was ambushed by [[Hellcat Company]] [[Hellcat mercenary|mercenaries]], and all members of the caravan were captured.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How'd you end up here?"''
Cassie Halloway: ''"Came in on a Blue Ridge caravan. Doc was there, too. Had some people slip away in the night, but the guide said it happens - people turn back, that kind of thing. Then one night we shelter from a storm and those Hellcat goons ambush us. Capture us all. Spent days in a cart or something, blindfolded, before they dumped me here."''
([[Cassie Halloway/Dialogue|Cassie Halloway's dialogue]]) They were then brought to cells in [[Vault 96]] and were used as unwilling test subjects by [[Edgar Blackburn]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Is everybody all right in there?"''
Cassie Halloway: ''"We're locked in some weird cell, in a frozen Vault, being held prisoner by some lunatic in a lab coat who experiments on us. We're peachy, how are you?"''
([[Cassie Halloway/Dialogue|Cassie Halloway's dialogue]]) Cassie was tested on like the other members of the caravan; Blackburn decided to dose her with [[Fallout 76 diseases|diseases]] such as sludge lung for "testing incubation and immune response times" - though she claims she's "holding up" and "some of the others are in worse shape."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Are you hurt?"''
Cassie Halloway: ''" I'm not injured. Got lucky - the doc didn't do any surgery on me. That nutjob was dosing me with diseases, though. Said he was 'testing incubation and immune response times.' Weird thing is, he kept apologizing. Got a bad case of Sludge Lung now, but I'm holding up. Some of the others are in worse shape."''
([[Cassie Halloway/Dialogue|Cassie Halloway's dialogue]]) Cassie, along with [[Ashmore]], [[Petersen (Steel Reign)|Petersen]] and [[Wilkins (Steel Reign)|Wilkins]] are the only known survivors. Cassie tried to look out for them in their desperate situation. After the ordeal and her rescue by the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] and [[Odessa Valdez]], Cassie finally reached Foundation, where she is currently helping at the [[Foundation supply room|supply room]]. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |dead = |quests started = |quests involved =[[A Satisfied Conscience]] |events started = |events involved = |encounters involved= |essential =yes |essential until = |ghost =yes |hostile = |ally = |temp companion = |wares = |caps = |currency = |medical services = |heal = |cripple = |cure disease = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |cure mutation = |bonus = |romance = |other = |locations =* [[Vault 96]] * [[Foundation supply room]] }} ===Quests=== [[A Satisfied Conscience]] - Cassie is being held prisoner in a cell in [[Vault 96]]. She must be released before confronting [[Edgar Blackburn]]. ===Other interactions=== * After completing [[A Satisfied Conscience]], Cassie can be found in the [[Foundation supply room]]. * After completing [[The Catalyst]], Cassie can be informed Blackburn is dead. She admits she almost felt sorry for him, but not that sorry because he killed people and hopes he died badly. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = [[Lumberjack outfit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Cassie Halloway appears only {{In|FO76SR}}. ==Gallery== FO76SR Cassie locked up.png|Cassie locked in [[Vault 96]] with [[Ashmore]] Cassie Halloway.png|Cassie in the [[Foundation supply room]] FO76SR Cassie eating.png|Cassie eating ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox Foundation}} {{Navbox Steel Reign}} [[Category:Steel Reign human characters]] [[Category:Settler characters]] [[ru:Кэсси Холлоуэй]]

I think I can go easy knowing someone's going to take out those Blood Eagles. Make better choices than I did.|Woods before her death|sound=Woods 005fd5c0_1.ogg}} '''Corporal Woods''' is a mercenary and member of the [[Hellcat Company]]. ==Background== Woods was part of the mercenary company hired by [[Edgar Blackburn|Doctor Edgar Blackburn]] to guard [[Vault 96]],[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Who are you?"''
Corporal Woods: ''"Name's Woods. Corporal Woods, Hellcat Company. Mercenaries. We got hired by this creep of a doctor to guard the place...among other things. Promised us salvage rights here when he was done. Don't think we're gonna collect on that."''
([[Woods/Dialogue#33|Corporal Woods' dialogue]]) and to kidnap new subjects for the doctor.[[FEV research logs#FEV research log .23112|FEV research log #112]] She and her squad were stationed at the vault's entrance when it was overrun by [[Blood Eagles]],[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What happened here?"''
Corporal Woods: ''"Our squad was guarding the entrance here when we were overrun by Blood Eagles. Killed everyone. Me, too. I just haven't kicked it yet."''
([[Woods/Dialogue#36|Corporal Woods' dialogue]]) leaving her struggling with a fatal gutshot.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How'd a mercenary squad get overrun by Blood Eagles?"''
Corporal Woods: ''"Our own fault. We got lazy. This place is so far out of the way, nobody ever passes by. Kind of the point. We figured we'd be shooing off the occasional stray scavenger that came poking around. This lot sent grenades through the entrance before we knew they were there. Rushed us while we were recovering. I took a bullet in the gut. Bastards left me to die slowly, because they thought it was funny."''
([[Woods/Dialogue#124|Corporal Woods' dialogue]]) When the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] finds her, she is fully aware that she is about to die,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"There must be something I can do to help you."''
Corporal Woods: ''"That's kind, but it's a little late for that. I've seen enough gutshots in my time to know a stimpak and bandages aren't going to fix this. This one's got my name on it. God knows I've done enough to deserve it."''
([[Woods/Dialogue#113|Corporal Woods' dialogue]]) and shows remorse over her actions while under contract with the doctor.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Doctor? What was going on here?"''
Corporal Woods: ''"Yeah. Blackburn. Real unnerving guy, even before we found out what he was doing. Kidnapping was just the start of it. We should've cut ties then, contract or no. Even mercs should have lines they don't cross. I'd say I didn't have a choice, but we're mercenaries. We do it for the money, not some noble ideal. Nobody to blame but ourselves."''
([[Woods/Dialogue#322|Corporal Woods' dialogue]]) As the Vault Dweller says goodbye to her, she wishes for them to "put some bullets in those Blood Eagles,"[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You made your choices, Woods. Goodbye."''
Corporal Woods: ''"You're not wrong. I guess I deserve that. Hope you'll put some bullets in those Blood Eagles when I'm gone."''
([[Woods/Dialogue#98|Corporal Woods' dialogue]]) and also tells them to "give them hell," before she finally succumbs to her wounds.Corporal Woods: ''"I'm fading fast, kid. Think this is it. Those damn Blood Eagles are still inside. Give 'em hell for me."''
([[Woods/Dialogue#32|Corporal Woods' dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |quests started = |quests involved =[[A Satisfied Conscience]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Mercenary outfit (Fallout 76)|Mercenary outfit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances == Woods appears only {{In|FO76SR}}. ==Gallery== Corporal Woods Corpse.png|Corporal Woods' corpse after she succumbs to her wounds ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Steel Reign}} [[Category:Steel Reign human characters]] [[Category:Hellcat Company characters]] [[ru:Вудс]]

Let the dust and flames and fumes fill you; let it soak into your throats. Let it show you the Truth!|sound=Interpreter Clarence 00629a63_1.ogg}} '''Interpreter Clarence''' is a member of the [[the Enlightened]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76NM}}. ==Background== Clarence was part of a group of cult members, whose other constituents were Observers [[Errol]], [[Johanna]], and [[Marlon]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Wait, there's more of you?"''
Interpreter Clarence: ''"Yes. I was accompanied by three Observers: Errol, Marlon, and Johanna. You will find them tending to the ritual pyres in the far reaches of this sacred site. If you speak, do not be offended by the absence of their minds. They are but humble witnesses to his wisdom, and have much left to learn from him."''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Interpreter Clarence's dialogue]]) Together, they undertook a long trip from [[the Lantern]] to [[Point Pleasant]], in order to see the home of the [[Wise Mothman]],[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Where do you come from?"''
Interpreter Clarence: ''"We have ventured from our place of study, the Lantern, far from here. During the time of the Equinox, myself and a group of Observers make the perilous trip to the Wise One's homeland."''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Interpreter Clarence's dialogue]]) and to commune with him.Interpreter Clarence: ''"Weary we are, for far we have traveled... All for the sake of his voice. All for the sake of his wisdom..."''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Interpreter Clarence's dialogue]]) Clarence possesses an open posture and friendly demeanor towards visitors,Interpreter Clarence: ''"A child approaches. Do they seek wisdom?"''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Interpreter Clarence's dialogue]])Interpreter Clarence: ''"I am Interpreter Clarence, of the Wise Mothman's Enlightened. How may I be of service to you, child?"''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Interpreter Clarence's dialogue]])Interpreter Clarence: ''"I must thank you, child! We witness glory thanks to your efforts!"''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Interpreter Clarence's dialogue]]) as long as they do not belong to the "Dim Ones" sect of the [[Cult of the Mothman]] who worship the red-eyed Mothman.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"I've been attacked by Mothman Cultists before. Why are you different?"''
Interpreter Clarence: ''"Do not mistake us for the Dim Ones. Followers of the red-eyed pretender. Fools, who flee from his wisdom, and cling to a false god -- a flawed, vision-less 'holy' Mothman. They seek violence because facing a 'worthy' death is far less frightening than facing the Truth."''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Interpreter Clarence's dialogue]]) He is always in pursuit of knowledge,Interpreter Clarence: ''"The light has drawn you to us. Speak. There is much to learn."''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Interpreter Clarence's dialogue]]) and has already made significant progress towards enlightenment, as he acts as an interpreter of the Enlightened.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Observers? Is that some kind of rank?"''
Interpreter Clarence: ''"Those of us who endeavor to find the Truth in the Wise One's words go through several stages of learning. The Observer is the larva. One who knows their place, and knows there is much more to come. For the knowledge of ignorance, of our place, is an essential first step. A bug must first know it's a bug. I, as an Interpreter, am a pupa, surrounding myself in a cocoon of his words; absorbing... Casting form from them. The venerable Wise Charles, who graces us with his company, has broken from his cocoon. He, and very few like him, may flutter and dance in the light of his infinite wisdom for the remainder of his bright but fleeting existence."''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Interpreter Clarence's dialogue]]) During the [[The Mothman Equinox|equinox]], he can be found on the roof of the [[Mothman Museum]] in Point Pleasant, accompanying [[Charles (Cult of the Mothman)|Wise Charles the Forewarned]]. The festival's hourly rituals are conducted by the Observers [[Marlon]], [[Johanna]], and [[Errol]]. Regarding their various eccentricities, Clarence apologizes for "the absence of their minds."Interpreter Clarence: ''"If you speak, do not be offended by the absence of their minds. They are but humble witnesses to his wisdom, and have much left to learn from him."''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Clarence's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |essential = |essential until = |ghost =yes |ghost until = |dead = |hostile = |ally = |affinity = |temp companion = |factions = |factions hostile = |quests started = |quests involved = |events started = * [[The Mothman Equinox]] |events involved = |encounters = |locations = |wares = |caps = |gold = |scrip = |medical services = |heal = |cure cripple = |cure radiation = |cure mutation = |cure disease = |cure addiction = |bonus = |bonuscd = |bonusdur = |other = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Cultist enlightened robe]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== [[File:76 NOTM Beholder glance.jpg|thumb|Looking at the camera instead of the player|241x241px]] * For unclear reasons, he may stare directly into the player's camera (including third-person camera or [[photomode]]), rather than focusing on the player character. The only one who can show me what I must see. Who I must see.|sound=Observer Errol 0062dbb8_1.ogg}} '''Observer Errol''' is a member of [[the Enlightened]] in [[Appalachia]] {{In|FO76NM}}. During the seasonal [[The Mothman Equinox|Equinox festival]], he can be found tending the sacred pyre within the church at [[Point Pleasant]]. ==Background== === Origin === The [[Cult of the Mothman]] were a pre-War group who survived by taking shelter in the [[Lucky Hole Mine]],[[Exodus (note)|''Exodus'']] and [[the Enlightened]] are a sect who left the mine early due to their disgust at the cultural influence of [[the Interloper]], catalyzed by further spiritual revelations.[[His Priestess]][[Catechism of Hilary|''Catechism of Hilary'']] They fled the state with the prophet [[Charles (Cult of the Mothman)|Charles]] to form their own church, headquartered at a place called [[the Lantern]]. Errol appears to be a young man, making it unlikely he was one of the original pre-War cultists. He does not explicitly specify whether he was part of the founding group or joined the sect later. He says ''"Before my first communion, I was lost. A rabid dog eating table scraps."''Observer Errol: ''"{{Tooltip|Before my first communion, I was lost. A rabid dog eating table scraps. Now he has shown me to my seat at the finest restaurants... For the finest meals.|Appreciative}}"''
([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]]) This is inconclusive verbiage, but seems to imply that Errol was a wastelander who joined the Enlightened. === Life at the Lantern === Observer Errol has become more satisfied with his life since his first communion. He now relies on visions from the [[Wise Mothman]] to hunt,Observer Errol: ''"{{Tooltip|The Wise One is the only one who understands. The only one who can show me what I must see. Who I must see.|To himself}}"''
([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]]) pursuing the targets shown to him.Observer Errol: ''"{{Tooltip|"I am ready, Wise One, show me. Show me who is next..."|Pleading, excited}}"''
Observer Errol: ''"{{Tooltip|"I must feast, Wise One, please, show me..."|Pleading, excited}}"
''([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]]) His hunts often take him far from the Lantern (but never as far as [[Point Pleasant]]).Observer Errol: ''"{{Tooltip|I miss the Lantern's glow. My hunts often send me far from home, but never like this. I can barely see its shine from here.|Missing his home. The Lantern is a location.}}"''
([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]]) Errol feels that his peer [[Johanna]] understands his faith, and wonders what revelations the Wise One has granted her.''"Johanna seems to understand. I wonder what the Wise One has shown her..."''
([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]]) He is envious of [[Marlon|Observer Marlon's]] ability to hear [[Auditory hallucinations|disembodied voices]], and resents him for "wasting" this gift.Observer Errol: ''"{{Tooltip|Those voices he hears... What do they tell him? How can I hear them too? What prey can they reveal to me?|To himself, a bit jealous}} {{Tooltip|They are wasted on him. He bickers and cowers. He holds a gift, and he wastes it.|A bit spiteful}}"''
([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]]) Errol presents human sacrifices to the Wise Mothman. He does not understand why the Wise One always leaves when his victims begin to scream, and blames this on the unworthiness of his victims. ===Attending the Equinox=== [[File:FO76 icon quest mothmanequinox.gif|left|frameless]]Errol, alongside fellow Observers [[Johanna]] and [[Marlon]], is part of a group led by [[Clarence (Fallout 76)|Interpreter Clarence]], caregiver to [[Charles (Cult of the Mothman)|Wise Charles the Forewarned]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Wait, there's more of you?"''
[[Clarence (Fallout 76)|Interpreter Clarence]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Yes. I was accompanied by three Observers: Errol, Marlon, and Johanna.|"Yohanna"}} You will find them tending to the ritual pyres in the far reaches of this sacred site. {{Tooltip|If you speak, do not be offended by the absence of their minds. They are but humble witnesses to his wisdom, and have much left to learn from him.|Somewhat sympathetic to them}}"''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Interpreter Clarence's dialogue]]) Together, they undertake a journey from the Lantern to [[Point Pleasant]], to hold an [[The Mothman Equinox|Equinox festival]] at the home of the [[Wise Mothman]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Where do you come from?"''
[[Clarence (Fallout 76)|Interpreter Clarence]]: ''"We have ventured from our place of study, the Lantern, far from here. During the time of the Equinox, myself and a group of Observers make the perilous trip to the Wise One's homeland."''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Interpreter Clarence's dialogue]]) During the Equinox, he can be found tending the pyre inside the Point Pleasant church on the east edge of town, where he guards the [[Sacred tome|sacred tomes]]. He occasionally expresses homesickness, and says he can barely see the shine of the Lantern from his current vantage. He explains that each communion ceremony will enable the [[Sacred tome|sacred tomes]] to reveal more Truth to the reader, and expresses disgust at the [[Vine barricade|vines]] which seem to deliberately disturb his pyre.''"With each communion, the tomes here should reveal more Truth to you. How enviable..."'' ([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]])Observer Errol: ''"{{Tooltip|Filthy, disgusting vines...|Disgusted}}"''
([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]]) When his pyre is cleared, he tasks the players to slay the heretic clergy of the [[Cult of the Mothman|Followers of the Winged One]] and rip the [[Mothman glasses|glowing red glasses]] from their skulls.''"Look for eyes that glow. They believe themselves to be the pretenders incarnate. Rip those silly glasses from their skulls."''''"The ritual cannot begin if they still live. Hunt them."''''''''([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]])''' Errol says the ritual cannot begin if they still live, and their deaths will enable his pyre to burn brightly.Observer Errol: ''"{{Tooltip|The ritual cannot begin if they still live. Hunt them|Devilish command}}."''
([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]])Observer Errol: ''"{{Tooltip|Their deaths please me. This pyre will burn brightly now.|Satisfied}}"''
([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]]) After the pyres have been lit, Errol encourages the players to breathe in the [[neurotoxic dust]] which engulfs the town.Observer Errol: ''"{{Tooltip|"Breathe in the dust... Let it guide you... Let it show you..."|Intoxicated on the chemicals}}"''
''([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]])'' If the summoning is successful, he will travel to the rooftop of the [[Mothman Museum]] and kneel before the Wise One, begging for visions of his next victims. Throughout the festival, [[Charles (Cult of the Mothman)|Wise Charles the Forewarned]] can be found sitting in his wheelchair here, whispering contextless phrases such as ''"I... was... mis.. take... en..."'' and ''"No... he... wants... them... spared... fool[.]"'' == Personality == Observer Errol's speech is sinister and quiet, marked by a distinctive Southern drawl. He speaks ponderously and euphemistically, filling the silence of the church with his macabre musings. His lines tend towards vocalized introspection rather than acknowledging and focusing on the player character. He expresses interest in human sacrifice and [[cannibalism]].Observer Errol: ''"{{Tooltip|Mmm. Your smell. Alluring. Makes me want to... rip you open.|Likes what he... smells?}}"''
([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]]) He hunts people, and seems to have a strong sense of smell. He claims the Wise One has shown him to "the finest meals." He seems to enjoy inflicting violence in general,Observer Errol: ''"{{Tooltip|I envy the blood your lot spills during our ritual. But alas, my duties as Observer prevent me from participating in the festivities.|Feels left out}}"''
([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]])Observer Errol: ''"{{Tooltip|The Wise One always leaves when they begin to scream. Why? Does he not find them worthy? Or me? Surely not.|To himself, slight confusion}}"''
([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]]) especially upon the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] of [[Foundation]].Observer Errol: ''"Ah, Foundation. I wish I could walk among its people... Waiting for him to show me which of their flock to bring to slaughter."''
([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]]) He also takes pleasure in the deaths of [[Cultist|prophets]] of the [[Cult of the Mothman|Winged One]]. In one of his greeting lines, Errol declares to the player character that their smell is alluring and he would like to ''"...rip you open."'' Errol envies the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]]' ignorance, as he should like to learn the contents of the [[Sacred tome|sacred tomes]] over again. He wonders if you are able to peer upon all six, and if you are able to derive knowledge from the tomes which still escapes him.''"Your eyes. They are like my own. Learning. Hungry... Perhaps hungrier still. Do the tomes here tell you more than me I wonder?"'' ([[Errol/Dialogue|Observer Errol's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character == ===Interactions overview === {{Interactions FO76 |ghost =yes |essential =yes |quests started = |quests involved =* [[The Mothman Equinox]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Cultist enlightened robe]]
