At one point, apparently prompted by the rhyming word "sterile," Dane declares ''"My name's not Errol!"''Dane: ''"{184}{}{Sterile! We're all going to be hideous, sterile freaks! Sterile! Sterile! Sterile! My name's not Errol! Sterile!}"''
([[DANE.MSG|Dane's dialogue]]) **Both characters wear hooded purple robes, cinched by a cord. ==Behind the Scenes== For one of Errol's idle lines, ''"I see... Oh, I see... (chuckle)"'', the script notes say ''"Hearing a secret, devious."'' This would seem to indicate that Errol is experiencing an [[Auditory hallucinations|auditory hallucination]] which he believes to be revelatory. In 2020, ''Fallout 76'' developer Ferret Baudoin mentioned that some script notes are designed to achieve a specific performance, and may imply information that is non-canonical.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lRqFmxlISLk Fallout 76 Lore Dive with Bethesda's Ferret Baudoin and the Fallout Lorecast!] ==Appearances== Observer Errol appears only {{In|FO76NM}}. ==Bugs== During the first Equinox, some of Errol's subtitles erroneously read "Interpreter Clarence." Alongside fellow Observers [[Errol]] and [[Marlon]], she accompanies [[Clarence (Fallout 76)|Interpreter Clarence]] each [[The Mothman Equinox|Mothman Equinox]] in a seasonal pilgrimage from [[the Lantern]] to [[Point Pleasant]].A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Wait, there's more of you?"''
[[Clarence (Fallout 76)|Interpreter Clarence]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Yes. I was accompanied by three Observers: Errol, Marlon, and Johanna.|"Yohanna"}} You will find them tending to the ritual pyres in the far reaches of this sacred site. {{Tooltip|If you speak, do not be offended by the absence of their minds. They are but humble witnesses to his wisdom, and have much left to learn from him.|Somewhat sympathetic to them}}"''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Interpreter Clarence's dialogue]]) Together, they reclaim the homeland of the [[Wise Mothman]].A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Where do you come from?"''
[[Clarence (Fallout 76)|Interpreter Clarence]]: ''"We have ventured from our place of study, the Lantern, far from here. During the time of the Equinox, myself and a group of Observers make the perilous trip to the Wise One's homeland."''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Interpreter Clarence's dialogue]]) Johanna seeks the company of the Wise One, whom she calls "Poppa," and strives to bring him joy.Johanna: ''"{{Tooltip|You seek his wisdom, yes? I seek his company.|Emphasis on I}}"''
([[Fallout 76 characters|Observer Johanna's dialogue]])Observer Johanna: ''"{{Tooltip|We have traveled so very far to be here. I know he is happy to see our little faces, so it is all worth it.|Excited}}"''
([[Johanna/Dialogue|Observer Johanna's dialogue]]) ==Background== Johanna is a member of the Enlightened who lives at the Lantern. Her brother [[Jelle]] once served the cult alongside her, but he was eaten by "[[Mothman#Mothman hatchling|little ones]]" after he foolishly attempted to clone the Wise Mothman.Observer Johanna: ''"{{Tooltip|My brother Jelle, he tried to clone him, you know? So foolish. His wisdom was not his at birth. The little ones, they eat poor Jelle.|Jelle: Yell-uh}}"''
([[Johanna/Dialogue|Observer Johanna's dialogue]]) Her strong accent and unusual speech patterns suggest her first language may be Romanian. Her favorite equinox is [[the Mothman Equinox]],Observer Johanna: ''"{{Tooltip|You know, the Mothman Equinox is my favorite Equinox. What's your favorite Equinox?|Playful}}"''
([[Johanna/Dialogue|Observer Johanna's dialogue]]) and her nose feels "very tingly" when the planets align.Observer Johanna: ''"{{Tooltip|Do you also feel the tingle in your nose when the planets align? It is very tingly.|Curious}}"''
([[Johanna/Dialogue|Observer Johanna's dialogue]]) She ponders over how many equinoxes she might see in her lifetime,Observer Johanna: ''"{{Tooltip|How many Equinoxes will I live to see I wonder? Could this be my last? One can only hope, yes?|Death does not scare her}}"''
([[Johanna/Dialogue|Observer Johanna's dialogue]]) as Observer Marlon informed her about the risks of prolonged inhalation of the [[neurotoxic dust|dust]] during the ritual.Observer Johanna: ''"{{Tooltip|They say the dust may harm us if we breathe it too long. Who said so? Observer Marlon. Well, THEY told him. They told him, he told me.|Referring to the voices in marlon's head}}"''
([[Johanna/Dialogue|Observer Johanna's dialogue]]) However, this does not keep her from embracing the dust.Observer Johanna: ''"{{Tooltip|Mm! The dust! How I missed the dust! Enter into my lungs, pretty dust!|Gleeful}}"''
([[Johanna/Dialogue|Observer Johanna's dialogue]]) She also has family. Her mother wanted to come to Point Pleasant, but never saw "him" again.Observer Johanna: ''"{{Tooltip|My Mother, she wanted to be here. She never saw him again. Oh, Poppa...|Feels bad for her mother}}"''
([[Johanna/Dialogue|Observer Johanna's dialogue]]) She misses her "Poppa."Observer Johanna: ''"{{Tooltip|I miss him so whenever he is not here with me, my Poppa...|Sad}}"''
([[Johanna/Dialogue|Observer Johanna's dialogue]]) During the equinox, Johanna is tending to the waterside pyre on the western side of town. She is anxious to see the Wise Mothman again,Observer Johanna: ''"{{Tooltip|I can't wait to see him. It's been so long. He's missed so many of my birthdays, you know.|Talking as if a kid has been naughty}}"''
([[Johanna/Dialogue|Observer Johanna's dialogue]]) and will be overjoyed if the summoning ritual succeeds.Observer Johanna: ''"{{Tooltip|I'm so happy to see him again. I wish to cry. I'm so happy!|Ecstatic}}"''
([[Johanna/Dialogue|Observer Johanna's dialogue]])Observer Johanna: ''"{{Tooltip|Mother would be so glad. It is so good to see him.|Ecstatic}}"''

([[Marlon/Dialogue|Observer Marlon's dialogue]])Observer Marlon: ''"{{Tooltip|I can't! I won't! You cannot make me... No, you can't! No... Fine.|To voices. Stubborn then giving up}}"''
([[Marlon/Dialogue|Observer Marlon's dialogue]])Observer Marlon: ''"{{Tooltip|Keep it down will you?|To a voice}}"''

{{For|other characters named Charles|Charles}} {{Infobox character |games =FO76, FO76NM |name =Wise Charles the Forewarned |nicknames =Brother Charles |image =FO76 character moth wisecharles.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |affiliation =[[The Enlightened]]
[[Cult of the Mothman]] (formerly) |rank =Wise |events =[[The Mothman Equinox]] |location =[[Point Pleasant]] |hair color ={{Tooltip|Gray|HairColor09Gray}} |eye color ={{Tooltip|Blind Scarred|MaleEyesHumanBlindScarred}} |hairstyle ={{Tooltip|Chemical Storm|ATX_DLC03_HairMale47}} |facial hair ={{Tooltip|Doomsday Prepped|BigBeard16}} |level =1 → 66 |str =0 |per =4 |end =0 |chr =0 |int =0 |agi =5 |lck =0 |derived ={{Derived stats FO4|hp=35 → 800|ap=50}} |aggression =Unaggressive |confidence =Average |assistance =Helps Nobody |factions =CaptiveFaction |class =raiderClass |combat style=Default |CK race =HumanRace |actor = |designer = |voice type =E07_NPCM_WiseCharles |dialogue =[[Wise Charles/Dialogue]] |edid =E07A_Mothman_WiseCharles |formid ={{ID|0061739A}} |refid ={{ID|006160F9}} }} {{Quotation|I hear nothing... everything...|sound=Wise Charles 0062dbe5_2.ogg}} '''Wise Charles the Forewarned''', formerly known as '''Brother Charles''', is a member of [[the Enlightened]] who lives at [[the Lantern]]. He was first a mentioned-only character in ''[[Fallout 76]]'', before appearing fully in the ''[[Night of the Moth]]'' update. Charles was a member of the pre-War [[Cult of the Mothman]] at [[Point Pleasant]] in [[Appalachia]], and his vision mobilized them to take shelter before the War. Each [[The Mothman Equinox|Mothman Equinox]], he travels to his former home town to participate in summoning the [[Wise Mothman]]. ==Background== === The Cult at Point Pleasant === Before the [[Great War|War]], Charles was a respected member of the [[Cult of the Mothman]], who participated in worshipping the red-eyed [[mothman]] at the church hidden beneath the [[Mothman Museum]] in [[Point Pleasant]]. Judging by the wheelchair found near the pulpit here, he was probably already a wheelchair user at this time. The cult conducted a ritual to summon the mothman on October 21, [[Timeline#2077|2077]], hoping to gain insight related to some imminent disaster. While most of the cultists did not see anything, an unknown preacher proclaimed that "Brother Charles saw the Mothman appear out of the corner of his eye, and heard [[Auditory hallucinations|whispers]] of impending disaster." The omen warned that a terrible flood would sweep Appalachia within the following day, and the cult must seek higher ground in order to survive. On October 22, the preacher proclaimed that the cult must stand upon the rooftops of Point Pleasant and wait out this flood, and that those who refused to heed this warning were turning their back on the mothman.[[Sermon: Summoning the Mothman]][[Sermon: Impending doom|''Sermon: Impending doom'']] Despite the specific and strongly-stated nature of this resolution, a group ultimately fled Point Pleasant with Charles, and arrived at the [[Lucky Hole Mine]] before the Great War. Years later, [[the Enlightened]] recounted the events of this same ritual in a tome called ''[[Exodus (note)|Exodus]]''. In their retelling, the Cult of the Mothman are described as worshippers of the "Pretender Mothman." The Enlightened attest that, despite the misguided nature of this ritual, Charles was blessed with a warning of "fire and flood" from the purple-eyed [[Wise Mothman]]. The tome also claims it was Charles himself who then guided his brethren to the safety of the [[Lucky Hole Mine]].[[Exodus (note)|''Exodus'']] ===The Lucky Hole Mine=== It seems an unknown group, which included an eerie old woman, had long lived within this mine, after frightening away the security staff over a period of at least several days.[[Lucky Hole Mine terminal entries]] After their first visitation, a security guard called [[Fort Defiance|Allegheny Asylum]] to ask about escaped patients, which places the event no later than March 2061.[[Herald editorial on Allegheny Asylum]] This post-War cult at the mine appears to have mythologized these events,[[His home]] suggesting these groups merged when Charles' group arrived on October 22 or 23, 2077. One mothman cultist, [[Jeff Lane]], stayed in Point Pleasant after the War,[[Interloper]], a tape found in Jeff Lane's room in Point Pleasant. and coveted the knowledge of a being he called "[[the Interloper]]" before leaving Point Pleasant. His relationship to these events is unclear. He eventually made it to the Lucky Hole Mine as well.[[The Chosen]], a tape found at Jeff Lane's campsite at the entrance of the mine. After the Point Pleasant group sheltered within, some followers "turned to darker worship," and the mine found themselves divided by a spiritual conflict. A figure called the [[First Priestess of the Wood]] rose to prominence at this time, and under her guidance, the cult cared for a creature deep within the mine, which they called the [[The Interloper|Firstborn of the Wood]].[[His Priestess]][[His birth]] An underground spring formed, providing the group with water, and the Priestess' followers attributed this miracle to the Firstborn.[[His springs]] Some members were disturbed by these developments, and shunned the followers of the Priestess, accusing them of heretical worship. They condemn these post-War religious concepts with disparaging terms such as "the Deceiver," "the Pretender Mothman," and "[[the Interloper]]."[[False Gods of Appalachia]][[Catechism of Hilary]] ===Exodus=== After the fallout settled, some of Charles' followers left with him. This was difficult due to Charles' paraplegia. They were frightened of the challenges which they encountered in the wasteland and wished to return to the mine, but Charles implored them not to, and spoke of safety beyond the hills they called home. Charles fled [[Appalachia]] with the Enlightened, and the group eventually founded a church they called [[the Lantern]]. They began to follow the amaranthine [[Wise Mothman]], whom they considered a single mortal being. They espouse that the "Wise One" does not desire to be worshipped. Charles became an esteemed leader of the emerging spiritual movement. He earned the title of "Wise," along with at least four other members, each of whom has a distinct subtitle. Charles' full title is "Wise Charles the Forewarned." They came to refer to those who decided to stay in the mine as "the Dim Ones," and condemn their idolatry of the red-eyed feral mothmans. Those "Dim Ones" now refer to themselves as "the Followers of the Winged One." ===Current history=== Although Charles is blind, unresponsive, and wheelchair-bound, he has journeyed to Point Pleasant on a pilgrimage in order to summon the Wise Mothman during the [[The Mothman Equinox|Equinox]], where he is at the height of his power.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Where do you come from?"''
[[Clarence (Fallout 76)|Interpreter Clarence]]: ''"We have ventured from our place of study, the Lantern, far from here. During the time of the Equinox, myself and a group of Observers make the perilous trip to the Wise One's homeland."''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Interpreter Clarence's dialogue]]) He is assisted by [[Clarence (Fallout 76)|Clarence]], [[Johanna]], [[Marlon]] and [[Errol]]. The Enlightened believe the cocoon of his mind is cracking openA [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"[Perception 10+] His head appears a bit larger than usual."''
[[Clarence (Fallout 76)|Interpreter Clarence]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Our meager form is but a shell, a cocoon. He has broken from it, and his vessel has become a cup overflowing with vision.|A bit gross of a subject}}"''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Clarence's dialogue]]) in this final stage of his life.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Observers? Is that some kind of rank?"''
[[Clarence (Fallout 76)|Interpreter Clarence]]: ''"Those of us who endeavor to find the Truth in the Wise One's words go through several stages of learning. The Observer is the larva. One who knows their place, and knows there is much more to come. For the knowledge of ignorance, of our place, is an essential first step. A bug must first know it's a bug. {{Tooltip|I, as an Interpreter, am a pupa, surrounding myself in a cocoon of his words; absorbing... Casting form from them.|Personal pride}} {{Tooltip|The venerable Wise Charles, who graces us with his company, has broken from his cocoon.|With respect}} {{Tooltip|He, and very few like him, may flutter and dance in the light of his infinite wisdom for the remainder of his bright but fleeting existence.|With awe and respect}}"''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Clarence's dialogue]]) His head is visibly swelling, and his eyes glow. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |quests started = |quests involved =[[The Mothman Equinox]] }} ===Other interactions=== If Charles is interacted with on the roof of the Mothman Museum, he only says [[Wise Charles/Dialogue|cryptic things]]. He talks of a woman knowing things and that she should be left alone. He also mentions Kanawha, and something about a cord which "lies" being cut. He calls out to [[Wallace (Fallout 76)|Wallace]], and seems to want Wallace to answer back. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Pastor's vestments (Fallout 76)|Pastor's vestments]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== * Until the ''Night of the Moth'' update, the character of Brother Charles was only mentioned in the note ''[[Sermon: Impending doom]]''. It was found in the church hidden beneath the [[Mothman Museum]], where a wheelchair could also be found. * In the sermon, an unknown preacher spoke for Brother Charles. Charles himself is encountered by the player during the events of ''Night of the Moth'', but he is no longer aware of his surroundings, and relies on Interpreter Clarence to speak on his behalf. The update also added a tome called ''[[Exodus (note)|Exodus]]'', in which [[Michaela|Interpreter Michaela]] (an [[The Enlightened|Enlightened]] scribe) records several claims regarding Charles made by [[Pearl (Night of the Moth)|Wise Pearl the Augur]]. Therefore, everything known about the character's previous actions and personality was told to us secondhand or thirdhand by other cultists; ** In ''Sermon: Impending doom'', the preacher conveyed that the Mothman had warned Charles that the group must seek high ground to survive an impending flood, to occur on the following day. The preacher then proclaimed that the group must go warn all the faithful to gather on the rooftops of Point Pleasant, or else they were turning their back on the Mothman. ** ''Exodus'' claims the Wise Mothman sent a warning of "fire and flood," and that it was Charles who "guided his brethren to safety in the [[Lucky Hole Mine]]." ** The pre-War sermon makes no mention of fleeing to a mine across state, and prescribes an incompatible course of action. It also does not mention fire. Conversely, the Enlightened tome makes no mention of the preacher's plan to stand on the rooftops. ** Additionally, it remains unclear if Charles was capable of speaking for himself at the time of the War, or if he was already dependent on his advocates to express himself. ''Exodus'' mentions that when the fledgling cult emerged from the mine, Charles quelled their fears by speaking of a sacred place "beyond the hills," and Interpreted Clarence raves about the unimaginable brilliance of Charles' ongoing transcendence, but none of these accounts particularly indicate if he was ever able to hold a full conversation or not. * The ''[[Mutation Invasion]]'' update introduced [[Steven Scarberry|Brother Scarberry]], who alludes to "the false prophet." The deployment of the line leaves it unclear if he is referring to the [[Wise Mothman]] or Wise Charles the Forewarned.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Interpreter Clarence walked me through the steps of the ritual."''
[[Steven Scarberry]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Oh, my apologies, I didn't realize that we were discussing the false prophet.|Mildly annoyed his dreams of Mothman were dashed away. Slightly sarcastic}} When people say 'Mothman' I assume they're talking about the 'Holy Mothman', and not the purple liar. {{Tooltip|But please, do go on. Tell me of the the stories of their glorified butterfly.|Sarcastic and a bit rude towards the Enlightened. Insulting the Rival cult and their beliefs}}"''
([[Steven Scarberry/Dialogue|Steven Scarberry's dialogue]]) * Charles' swollen cranium and glowing eyes are unique, and do not appear on any other NPCs in ''Fallout 76''. * He is one of the few characters in the ''Fallout'' series thus far known to be [[Disability representation in the Fallout series|wheelchair users]]. A series of slopes have been constructed across the architecture of Point Pleasant, which may enable his caretakers to easily move him around the town. The long sloped path leads to the roof of the Mothman Museum, where Charles can be encountered when the Mothman Equinox event is active. ** Following each festival, the Enlightened leave, and the Followers of the Winged One reclaim Point Pleasant. Though they have extensively profaned the town and the hidden church with their [[Vine barricade|vines]],[[Clarence (Fallout 76)|Interpreter Clarence]]: ''"{{Tooltip|The Dim Ones have attempted to contain our light. Destroy their vines encircling each pyre before we proceed.|Ire toward the "dim ones"}} {{Tooltip|Each pyre is attended by a Wise One's Observer. Only when the vines have been destroyed will the Observers instruct you on your next tasks.|Instructive, warning}} {{Tooltip|Hurry now, children, his patience does not run as deep as his wisdom.|Somewhat foreboding}}"''
([[Clarence (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Interpreter Clarence's dialogue]])[[Errol|Observer Errol]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Filthy, disgusting vines...|Disgusted}}"''
([[Errol/Dialogue|Errol's dialogue]])All Followers of the Winged One locations are completely overgrown with vines and natural totems identical to the ones found all over Point Pleasant. they do not disturb either of the wheelchairs, and the sermons from the eve of the War are still sitting on the pulpit beneath the museum. ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|Return... me...|sound=Wise Charles 0062dbe0_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Wallace... answer...|sound=Wise Charles 0062dbe1_2.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Kill... it...|sound=Wise Charles 0062dbe9_2.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|The cord... it lies... cut it...|sound=Wise Charles 0062dbf2_2.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Do not... believe her..;|sound=Wise Charles 0062dbec_2.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|A... disk... red... sauce...|sound=Wise Charles 0062dbf5_1.ogg}} ==Appearances== Wise Charles the Forewarned appears only {{In|FO76NM}}. Prior to the ''Night of the Moth'' update, he was mentioned only as "Brother Charles" in the note [[Sermon: Impending doom]] before being introduced as a full character. ==Gallery== 76 NOTM Answer.png 76 NOTM Contempt.png 76 NOTM Eyes Charles.png ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox Cult of the Mothman}} [[Category:Fallout 76 mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Night of the Moth characters]] [[Category:Cult of the Mothman characters]] [[Category:The Enlightened characters]] [[Category:Mythical figures]] [[ru:Мудрый Чарльз Предупрежденный]]

([[Botsmith Amp/Dialogue|Botsmith Amp's dialogue]]) She designs the ranged and exploding battle bots and considers her botsmithing to be superior to [[Beatrice the Wrench|Beatrice's]]. Prior to the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]]' arrival, she destroyed the scoreboard to claim the record for most kills in a single match.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you do here again?"''
Botsmith Amp: ''"{{Tooltip|I'm a Rust Eagle botsmith, of course. But you knew that just by looking around, didn't you?|Friendly, but treating the player like it should be obvious.}} {{Tooltip|If it shoots, shocks, or explodes, you know I made it.|If it shoots, shocks, or explodes, you know I made it.}} {{Tooltip|You're looking at the Rust Eagle recordholder for kills in a single arena match.|Proud of having the deadliest bots.}} {{Tooltip|Sure, Beatrice'll tell you that she has more kills overall, but I wiped that slate clean. Now, it's about what you've done lately.|Proud of the fact that she physically destroyed the old scoreboard when she says she wiped the slate clean.}}"''
([[Botsmith Amp/Dialogue|Botsmith Amp's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you do here again?"''
[[Beatrice the Wrench]]: ''"{{Tooltip|I'm the best damn botsmith the Rust Eagles have, and Buzzsaw knows it.|Proud of herself and her abilities.}} {{Tooltip|We used to count kills out in the arena. Right up until Amp 'accidentally' destroyed the board, anyway.|Bitter about the loss of public recognition for her kills record.}} {{Tooltip|All that shame lit a fire under her. Now, I got a real rival.|But happy now that she has a legitimate bot designer rival}}"''
([[Beatrice the Wrench/Dialogue|Beatrice's dialogue]]) She has a lot of respect for the [[Gladiators of Steel|Gladiators]] and their ability to coordinate as a team, but is critical of their inability to please the crowd.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you think of the Gladiators of Steel?"''
Botsmith Amp: ''"{{Tooltip|They're good at what they do, I'll give them that.|Begrudging.}} {{Tooltip|I've never seen a team so coordinated in the ring. I'll bet it has to do with that spotter they use.|Genuinely admires that they use tactics to win battles.}} {{Tooltip|But it's just so rote. Where's the art, the pageantry, the performance?|But ultimately, they just don't have the showmanship she's looking for.}}"''
([[Botsmith Amp/Dialogue|Botsmith Amp's dialogue]]) Although she gets upset when they trash her bots, she sees it as an opportunity to address a flaw in her design. Each match is another step forward on her path to creating the perfect, unstoppable killing machines.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Why do you keep making bots if they're destined to be destroyed?"''
Botsmith Amp: ''"{{Tooltip|Because one day, they won't be. And that's how you'll know you're in trouble.|Serious. She intends to use her champion killing machines once the games are all done.}} {{Tooltip|Sure, it hurts every time one of my bots gets turned into a heap of scrap.|Honest. She doesn't like seeing her creations get destroyed.}} {{Tooltip|But it's also one more flaw I can fix.|And that's why it's worth it.}}{{Tooltip||}}"''

{{ID|006214D9}} (dead) |refid = }} {{Quotation|Many may not know that when the Andromeda galaxy reaches its peak brilliance the new age of humanity will begin.|sound=The Emissary 0061f4a9_1.ogg}} '''The Emissary''' is a mysterious person [[Fallout 76 random encounters#Man in Black|randomly encountered]] in [[Appalachia]] {{In|FO76IB}}. ==Background== The Emissary can be found wandering Appalachia in rare scene-type random encounters. The Emissary makes vague references to the [[Alien (Fallout 76)|Zetan aliens]] and their invasion. The Emissary appears to be noting instructions for someone named CarolThe Emissary: ''"{{Tooltip|Carol, memo to the bosses. They have arrived in Appalachia.|Speaking into tape recorder.}}"''
([[The Emissary/Dialogue|The Emissary's dialogue]])The Emissary: ''"{{Tooltip|Carol, find out when Venus will be at its zenith.|Speaking into tape recorder.}}"''
([[The Emissary/Dialogue|The Emissary's dialogue]]) and mentions collecting samples for a material called Zetanium.The Emissary: ''"{{Tooltip|Results positive for Zetanium. Sample acquired for further consideration.|Speaking into tape recorder.}}"''
([[The Emissary/Dialogue|The Emissary's dialogue]]) The Emissary claims that "when the Andromeda galaxy reaches its peak brilliance," it will mark the beginning of a "new age" for the [[human]] race.The Emissary: ''"Many may not know that when the Andromeda galaxy reaches its peak brilliance the new age of humanity will begin."''
([[The Emissary/Dialogue|The Emissary's dialogue]]) The Emissary also makes references to "men from Mars,"The Emissary: ''"If I told you I believed in men from Mars, would you believe me? Where have you observed them?"''
([[The Emissary/Dialogue|The Emissary's dialogue]]) the [[Mysterious Guidestones]]The Emissary: ''"Have you seen the Mysterious Guidestones? Quite majestic, are they not? Some might say, otherworldly..."''
([[The Emissary/Dialogue|The Emissary's dialogue]]) and [[Flatwoods]], where a meeting is scheduled with a "friend."The Emissary: ''"Do you happen to know the way to Flatwoods? I'm meeting with... our friend there."''
([[The Emissary/Dialogue|The Emissary's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |quests started = |essential = |ally = |allyfurn = |wares = |caps = |bonus = |other = |romance = |encounters =[[Fallout 76 random encounters#Man in Black|Man in Black]] }} ===Other interactions=== If found during a random encounter, the Emissary will not be hostile to the player. If interacted with, there are no dialogue trees, though the Emissary will say a few lines, calling the player character a neighbor. Eventually, the Emissary will surround the player character in an electrical white light. When the fade-to-white is over, the Emissary will have vanished. If the Emissary is attacked enough, combat will be engaged. If killed, there is a chance that the Emissary may drop a [[Fallout 76 keys#Mysterious key|mysterious key]], which will lead to [[Homer Saperstein]]. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Black suit (Fallout 76)|Clean black suit]] |weapon =[[Laser gun (Fallout 76)|Automatic laser pistol]] |otheritem = |ondeath =Automatic laser pistol
[[Fusion cell (Fallout 76)|Fusion cell]] (6)
[[Fallout 76 keys#Mysterious key|Mysterious key]] }} ==Notes== * There are two versions of the random encounter with the Emissary. In one, the Emissary is alive, while in the other, the Emissary spawns dead. * The Emissary's random encounters are only enabled when [[Invaders from Beyond (event)|Invaders from Beyond]] is the current seasonal event, though the quest itself does not have to be active for the encounters to occur. ==Appearances== The Emissary appears only {{In|FO76IB}}. ==Behind the scenes== * The Emissary is based on the legend of the Men in Black, as made famous in the 1975 book ''[[Wikipedia:The Mothman Prophecies|The Mothman Prophecies]]''. Supposedly, the Men in Black are frightening, inscrutable agents in suits who appear in the wake of UFO sightings to harass witnesses. Described as slightly "off" in every possible way, their very presence is said to be disorienting. They often seem confused about how to navigate basic human situations, and have a great deal of trouble communicating. ** In ufological lore, Men in Black are believed to be disguised or hybridized extraterrestrials. ** In the Fortean philosophy discussed in ''The Mothman Prophecies'', Men in Black are understood as uncanny projections by some inarticulate force attempting to interact with humankind, possibly interdimensional, spiritual, or collectively psychic in origin. ** Skeptics have suggested that the urban legend has its origins in early ufological researchers fumbling interviews with rural witnesses, who were bewildered by the behavior of nerds in ill-fitting suits feigning government credentials. ** [[w:c:half-life:The G-Man|The G-Man]] from the ''Half-Life'' series is a well-known depiction of the ufological concept of the Men in Black. * An emissary is a representative agent on a special mission, usually an ambassador sent to characterize and secure a new diplomatic relationship. ==See also== * [[Homer Saperstein]] * [[Smiling Man|The Smiling Man]] ==References== {{References}} [[Category:Invaders from Beyond characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 random encounter characters]] [[ru:Посланник]]

Keep it running, we'll never finish building here if it breaks.|sound=Kenneth Dean 0064ee51_1.ogg}} '''Kenneth Dean''' is the deceased leader of the [[Foundation Outpost]]. ==Background== Kenneth was a member of the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] who led the construction of an outpost east of [[Foundation]]. While building the settlement, their supplies began to run thin, leading Kenneth to request more from Foundation. However, the crew became anxious over sightings of large shadows and figures running through the trees, stalking them. These sightings turned to loud noises that disturbed them through the night. Although construction of the outpost steadily continued, Kenneth and his people were put on edge by the disturbances. Finally, on June 26, Kenneth spotted what appeared to be some brutish figure rummaging through their equipment and scouting the area.[[Kenneth's journal]] Kenneth made a plan to assemble his crew and investigate more thoroughly, and hopefully run whatever it was out of their camp. However, three days later, the figures revealed themselves to be [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|super mutants]], who assaulted the outpost. As it was still under construction, their defenses were in poor shape. Kenneth took a position in the camp's watch tower, from which he could hear his crew being attacked. Kenneth eventually died there, hoping that one day someone would fight back against the mutants with more success than he had.Kenneth Dean: ''"Is anyone out there? This recording is a call for help. Our settler camp was attacked by mutants last night. Please help. My name is Kenneth Dean. We're south of Huntersville. I think I'm the last one alive and probably won't be much longer. The mutants have left... for now. Hurry and destroy their meat bags when you get here, that should drive them away if they come back. There is a machine in the crater, should take care of the radiation in the area. Keep it running, we'll never finish building here if it breaks."''
([[Kenneth Dean/Dialogue|Kenneth Dean's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |dead =yes |events started=[[Eviction Notice (event)|Event: Eviction Notice]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =Random [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settler]] outfit |weapon = |otheritem =Randomized loot |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== Kenneth's voice is heard during the introduction to [[Eviction Notice (event)|Event: Eviction Notice]], in which the participants kill super mutants in order to avenge Kenneth and his crew. ==Appearances== Kenneth Dean appears only {{In|FO76TM}}. ==Gallery== FO76TM Kenneth Dean overturned.png|Kenneth's corpse overturned using grenades FO76TM Kenneth Dean overturned 2.png|Another view of Kenneth ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Foundation}} [[Category:Test Your Metal characters]] [[Category:Settler characters]] [[ru:Кеннет Дин]]

Mire Magic Moonshine, made with the finest venom from some sizable salamanders.|sound=Moonshiner Ned 00623afb_1.ogg}} '''Moonshiner Ned''' is a [[Mister Handy (Fallout 76)|Mister Handy]] encountered in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Ned is a robot who once belonged to the Sunday brothers [[Jesus Sunday|Jesus]] and [[Juan Diego Sunday|J.D.]], and helped them in their moonshining operation. After the brothers' deaths, the Mister Handy lay dormant and deactivated in their [[Sunday Brothers' cabin|cabin]] basement. Years later, [[Slayer (Fallout 76)|Slayer]], a member of the [[Crater Raiders]] from [[the Crater]], led a small crew who, in June of an undated year, discovered the cabin. Seeing fit to claim it as their own, Slayer's crew scavenged the property, leading [[Asher (mentioned)|Asher]] to find Ned in the basement.[[Raider's journal entries|Raider's journal entry 1]] The next day, Slayer got the robot back online. It would not "shut up about making moonshine," but Slayer thought that starting such an operation would be a good fit for his gang.[[Raider's journal entries|Raider's journal entry 2]] They eventually named the Mister Handy "Moonshiner Ned," after a talkative drunk person that they had previously encountered. Ned spoke of making more moonshine and holding a jamboree, which Slayer and his gang saw as an opportunity to party.[[Raider's journal entries|Raider's journal entry 3]] By June 16, Slayer and his crew had finished setting up their fortifications at the bunker and decided to hold the party to celebrate, courtesy of Ned's moonshining efforts.[[Raider's journal entries|Raider's journal entry 4]] However, at the same time, the crew began to hear strange noises coming from the wilderness surrounding the cabin. Some of the raiders began to spot "[[Gulper (Fallout 76)|giant lizards]]" at the edge of the property. Ned was excited about this, saying that their [[Acidic gulper venom|venom]] makes the moonshine more special.[[Raider's journal entries|Raider's journal entry 5]] By June 29, all of the crew but Ned and [[Petey (raider)|Petey]] had left Slayer, as they were fearful of the creatures stalking the cabin and feeling weak from the strength of the moonshine. Slayer wrote that the creatures were drawing closer to the cabin, something that he invited in his drunken stupor.[[Raider's journal entries|Raider's journal entry 7]] Although Slayer and Petey are found dead throughout the property, Moonshiner Ned is still active, hoping to hold more [[Moonshine Jamboree|moonshine jamborees]]. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |ghost =yes |events started =[[Moonshine Jamboree]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== * Ned only appears physically during [[Moonshine Jamboree|Event: Moonshine Jamboree]]. After the event's conclusion, he will disappear from the game until the event starts again. * Ned uses the same character template as [[Crutchley]]. ==Appearances== Moonshiner Ned appears {{In|FO76TM}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox robots}} {{Navbox raiders FO76}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Fallout 76 robots and computers]] [[Category:Test Your Metal characters]] [[Category:Crater Raiders characters]] [[Category:Mister Handy characters]] [[ru:Самогонщик Нед]]

Fall in and let's head back to base.|sound=Pappas 006024f0_1.ogg}} '''Initiate Pappas''' is a member of the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force|Brotherhood of Steel]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Initiate Pappas is a member of a Brotherhood of Steel technology recovery team reporting to [[Odessa Valdez|Scribe Valdez]]. In order to observe and document the combat abilities of the [[Rust Eagles]]' battle bots, his team engages in pit fighting at the [[Metal Dome]] arena.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"The Brotherhood has a pit fighting team?"''
Initiate Pappas: ''"Well, not exactly. We're one of Scribe Valdez's technology recovery teams. An aggressive raider gang armed to the teeth with combat bots makes a dangerous neighbor. So, we learn about their capabilities firsthand. Our approach is... controversial inside the Brotherhood, but the Scribe goes to bat for us because we're a vital source of intel. Here, we're called the Gladiators of Steel and we've survived more than one clash in the arena. The Rust Eagles think we're here to impress them and make a name for ourselves. And we need them to keep believing that."''
([[Pappas (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Initiate Pappas' dialogue]]) He is open to the idea of adopting a stage name to use when fighting alongside his fellow [[Gladiators of Steel]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"So, does that mean you have a secret gladiator nickname?"''
Initiate Pappas: ''"No, not really. Why, do you have one in mind?"''
([[Pappas (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Initiate Pappas' dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You look like a Steel Menace to me."''
Initiate Pappas: ''"Yeah, I like that! Now I just have to get my teammates to use it."''
([[Pappas (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Initiate Pappas' dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"I've got it... Bad Victoriam!"''
Initiate Pappas: ''"Uh, you know what, I'm sorry I asked."''
([[Pappas (Fallout 76)/Dialogue|Initiate Pappas' dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How about Eagle Eye?"''
Initiate Pappas: ''"Hey, that's not bad. I'll have to give it a try."''

I like to think that my meals bring a touch of humanity back into the world.|sound=Esme Rousseau 006325ef_1.ogg}} '''Esme Rousseau''', also known as '''Chef Esme''', is a chef of [[the Whitespring Refuge]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Esme has always loved cooking. Before the [[Great War]], her father was a talented chef in France and dinner time was an important event for her family. When the War hit, Esme's dreams of owning her own restaurant were put to a standstill. During the apocalyptic aftermath, she spent a long time simply trying to survive in the wasteland all by herself. In 2104, Esme joined the new group at the Whitespring Refuge. When she heard about the Whitespring opening its doors to refugees, she thought it would have mouths to feed and thought being a chef for them would give her life meaning. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |quests started =[[Recipe for Success|Refuge Daily: Recipe for Success]] |quests involved =[[Responders Reborn]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Grillmaster's outfit]] |weapon =N/A |otheritem =N/A |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Esme Rousseau appears only {{In|FO76TP}}. ==Behind the scenes== * Esme's English voice actress has not been credited or announced anywhere. She's hot stuff.|sound=Lennox 0062b33b_1.ogg}} '''Lennox''' is a pilot found outside [[The Whitespring Resort|the Whitespring Refuge]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76}}. ==Background== Lennox was a member of the [[United States Air Force]] before the [[Great War]]. She flew tankers and cargo planes and takes pride that she has never lost her cargo. Before the war, she noticed strange things moving in the sky above the clouds which convinced her that aliens exist. She recalls one time, she encountered a strange UFO flying near her seaplane. She shot her pistol at it but then she mysteriously became temporarily blind; her vision eventually returned to her, but she believes she was affected by some sort of alien mind control laser.Lennox: ''"There was the one time I took potshots at a UFO with a pistol out the window of a seaplane. Big glowing thing, keeping pace right alongside us. Must've fired the whole magazine, copilot's yellin' at me, and suddenly I'm just blind. They had to take over and guide us home. Vision came back later that day. Now, my copilot said I was just drunk and started trying to fight the sun, but.. Alien mind control lasers is my bet."''
([[Lennox/Dialogue|Lennox's dialogue]]) In 2104, Lennox joined the new group at the Whitespring Refuge. She is working as a pilot for the [[Responders]]. Using a [[Vertibird (Fallout 76)|Vertibird]], she pilots [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] to [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|the Pitt]] and [[Atlantic City]]. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |quests started = |quests involved = * [[Responders Reborn]] * [[Union Dues]] * [[From Ashes to Fire]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Flyboy outfit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== There is a [[The_Whitespring_Resort_terminal_entries#Inventory Requests - Pending Review|terminal entry]] suggesting Lennox is romantically interested in [[Orlando]]. Lennox is said to have winked at Orlando after requesting new supplies and said "Could be a lot of fun, under the right circumstances." ==Appearances== Lennox appears only {{In|FO76TP}}. She received expanded dialogue with the ''[[Expeditions: Atlantic City]]'' update. ==Behind the scenes== Although her heritage is never mentioned in-game, according to Lennox's voice actress [[Debra Cardona]], Lennox is Puerto Rican and came from the Bronx district of [[New York City]]. Neither of these areas have been mentioned elsewhere in the ''Fallout'' series.[https://archive.ph/FPCuO Debra Cardona on Instagram]: ''"This is Lennox. She is Puerto Rican from the Bronx and is a badass pilot. You can find her in the video game FALLOUT 76: THE PITT.
I was so proud to bring my voice and my heritage to this game, and I had waaay too much fun recording lines for Lennox.
Here's to the beginning of Hispanic Heritage Month. ¡Wepa!"'' ==Gallery== FO76TP Lennox.jpg FO76AC Atlantic City Boardwalk (Lennox).jpg|At the [[Atlantic City Boardwalk]] FO76TP Lennox 2.jpg ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox Responders}} {{Navbox Expeditions The Pitt}} [[Category:Expeditions: The Pitt human characters]] [[Category:Boardwalk Paradise human characters]] [[Category:America's Playground human characters]] [[Category:United States Air Force characters]] [[Category:Responder characters]] [[ru:Леннокс]]

I realize my company is electric, but the flattery is unnecessary... well, a bit more wouldn't hurt.|sound=Orlando 0062d5b9_1.ogg}} '''Orlando''' is a resident and the manager of [[the Whitespring Resort]], claiming to be the liaison for the resort's "[[The Management|management]]" while assisting the new incarnation of the [[Responders]] in their efforts to establish a central refuge for the disparate inhabitants of [[Appalachia]]. Orlando appears {{In|FO76TP}}. Orlando is the second [[LGBT representation in the Fallout series|non-binary character]] to appear in the ''Fallout'' series, after [[Burke (Steel Dawn)|Burke]] in ''[[Steel Dawn]]''. All of the Whitespring [[Responder (character)|Responders]] and [[Refugee (Expeditions: The Pitt)|refugees]] reflect this when referring to Orlando in their dialogue.[[Refugee (Expeditions: The Pitt)|Refugee]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Any idea where Orlando gets their clothes? I swear, I could do with a wardrobe upgrade.|A little jealous.}}"''
([[Refugee (Expeditions: The Pitt)/Dialogue|Refugee's dialogue]]) ==Background== Appearing suddenly at the Whitespring Resort around 2104, coinciding with the rebirth of the [[Responders]], Orlando is a secretive, mysterious person tasked by the mysterious Management with supporting Responder operations and distributing [[ultracell]]s to the leaders of the new community. They oversee the robotic staff and ensure The Whitspring remains habitable, distribute resources granted by their employers (food, medicine, materials, the aforementioned ultracells), and other necessary arrangements.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What do you do for the Refuge?"''
Orlando: ''"My role as liaison is to facilitate the needs of the Responders and our guests and speak for the interests of Management. That sounds terribly formal, I know, but in practical terms it means I do what I can to keep the Whitespring livable and support the Refuge. I oversee the robotic staff to attend to the former, and in the latter case, I arrange for the disbursement of resources from Management. Food, medicine, materials. Management has considerable resources, which they are happy to donate. I handle those arrangements."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) Orlando believes the Refuge can be a beacon of hope for the unfortunate people of Appalachia.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What's your perspective on the Refuge?"''
Orlando: ''"A wonderful idea, of course! It can be a beacon of hope for the unfortunates of Appalachia. And as I believe I mentioned, darling, the Management are very positive on the effort, and give it their full support."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]])Orlando: ''"A pleasure to make your acquaintance. You may call me Orlando. I represent the Management of the Whitespring Resort, and act as something of a liaison between them and the Responders. You should direct any questions about the operations of the Refuge to the Responders themselves. But, if you require anything of the Whitespring itself, I would be delighted to assist you...in any way I can."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I'm curious about you, Orlando. Tell me about yourself."''
Orlando: ''"Do I have an admirer? Flattery will get you everywhere, darling. That being said, there is little to tell, really. I am the Whitespring Management's liaison to the Responders' Refuge. It's a role I quite enjoy. It pleases me when I can be of service to others."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) Orlando is the first human caretaker of the Whitespring in over a quarter of a century, personally representing the interests of the management.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Management?"''
Orlando: ''"Yes, of course! The owners of the Whitespring are, fortunately, very much alive, although regrettably not able to be present. In their stead, they have elected to send their humble servant to oversee things here until such time as regular operations can resume. That is to say, of course, myself."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) Previously, only robotic staff sufficed to deal with any threats or scavengers on the property.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Did the Responders get permission before setting up the Refuge?"''
Orlando: ''"Actually, no, they didn't. That's no fault of theirs, darling - nobody could have known the owners were still involved. Management has monitored the property, of course, and there have been scavengers before, but the robotic staff sufficed. Once aware the Responders were establishing a permanent presence, Management sent me to bestow their blessing and be their liaison."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) The reasons behind this appointment are, if Orlando is to be believed, pure, unspoiled altruism in order to rebuild civilization.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You and Management are really getting nothing out of helping the Refuge?"''
Orlando: ''"You're suggesting an ulterior motive? Have the travails of Appalachia so hardened your heart against the idea of altruism? Darling, I know it is perhaps unfashionable in these times to be earnest and idealistic, but it really is that simple. Management wishes to help because they believe in the value of the Refuge as a step to rebuilding civilization - as do I. I would like to help even if they had not given me this task, and neither they nor I ask anything in return. That may not satisfy your doubts, but it is the truth."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) They claim that they and the Management simply believe in the American Dream and its restoration,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You really can't tell me anything about your employers?"''
Orlando: ''"Darling, I wish you would not press on this issue. I value our burgeoning friendship, but you place me in an awkward position. Oh, that disappointed look on your face. You do know how to weaken my resolve. What can I say? Hmmm... It would be terrible if I were to betray one trust to secure yours. You wouldn't want that for your Orlando, would you? I can tell you this: they are believers in the American Dream. One they wish to see restored. The Refuge is a small step on that path."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) reestablishing America as a land of opportunity where anyone will be able to find the freedom to build a life worth living.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How does the Refuge restore the American Dream?"''
Orlando: ''"I won't speak to their minds, my dear, but I will tell you what I believe, and I hope that will be sufficient answer. America was meant to be a land of opportunity - a place where anyone could find a freedom to build a life worth living. The Refuge is a first step to rebuilding a society bigger than any one settlement. To say: we are in this together! Forgive me, darling. I do get a bit emotional on the subject."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) As such, they permitted the Responders to settle into the Whitespring (that and the plummeting demand for luxury golf resorts).[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"The...Management...is okay with the Responders setting up shop here?"''
Orlando: ''"Positively delighted! They are naturally quite understanding that the demand for luxury golf resorts is currently well under supply. When the Responders came knocking, they were enthusiastically prepared to support the effort and make good use of the space in the meantime! You did not hear this from me, but I'd go so far as to say they were tickled pink to be able to help!"''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) One of their crucial roles is providing the ultracells. Orlando suggested using the experimental battery technology for powering [[Lennox]]'s [[vertibird]], and once the Responders agreed, Orlando started distributing them to selected individuals. Rather than provide them in bulk, they get a portion of cells in order to encourage collective decision making instead of stockpiling: Otherwise, the vertibird will not get charged and the Responders will be unable to embark on any expeditions.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Ultracite Battery Cells? Where are they getting those?"''
Orlando: ''"Why, from me, of course. Rather, from the Management via me, that is. When Management heard the Responders were restoring the vertibird, they wished to help. They provided the Ultracells, and I suggested them to the Responders as an alternative means of fueling the vertibird. Per Management instructions, I distribute a quantity to certain individuals regularly. Management feels this encourages collective decision making, rather than stockpiling. I'm sure they'd be willing to part with them in exchange for your aid."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) ===Personal life=== Orlando is very private and will only speak of their past in the vaguest possible terms, describing themselves as someone who traveled wide before coming to work for the management,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You keep dodging my questions when I ask you about yourself."''
Orlando: ''"So serious! I never meant to offend you, darling. I'm simply used to keeping my personal life quite private. I've...traveled, extensively, in the past. It was safest to be wary among strangers, and I had little time for...meaningful connections. I hope you'll forgive me. I would like to think we are friends, but I'm not prepared to bare everything. Just yet."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Where'd you come from? Before the Whitespring, I mean."''
Orlando: ''"Oh, here and there, darling. I've been to lots of places before the Management asked me to take over here. If you want to imagine a thrilling and intriguing story about my past, don't let me stop you, please."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) and claiming they have unremarkable origins, coming from nowhere interesting. They deliberately let people imagine where they come from, to keep them interested, although they do not really mean it in an intimate or romantic way, as their line of work consumes them entirely.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I'm not asking about your job, Orlando. Who are *you*?"''
Orlando: ''"I don't mean to be coy, dear. My work is my life, as they say. It fills my time and fulfills me. There's nothing wrong with that, is there? Besides, don't you find a bit of mystery all the more compelling? If I bared my soul and told you everything, I'm sure you'd be terribly bored. If I remain an enigma, it might keep you coming back for more of these lovely chats."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"So you've traveled a lot. But you must've started somewhere."''
Orlando: ''"Can't wait for my tell-all autobiography? I can't blame you; who knows when I'll find the time to write it. How about just a little dark secret of mine to tide you over? I'm not from anywhere interesting, actually. Nothing remarkable about my origins at all! Disappointing, isn't it, dear? That's why I usually let people imagine their own version of things. Keeps them interested."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) They similarly sidestep questions related to the Management, and explain that they came to work for it after "others" working for the Management saved Orlando from certain death, and that they loyally serve the Management ever since.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Okay, how'd you get from nowhere special to working for the Management?"''
Orlando: ''"That's the kind of question I would normally sidestep, darling, but you've been such a help, I want to trust you. I was in an...unpleasant situation, when others working for the Management found me. They took me in. They - the Management, that is - were very kind to me. I believe I would have died without them. When I was capable, I was happy to work for them. They didn't have to ask. I wanted to return the kindness they'd shown."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) Their relationship with the management predates the Whitespring posting. Orlando traveled widely to maintain their interests, collect information, perform unspecified tasks, and meet new people. While they enjoyed the travels and meeting new people, settling down at the Whitespring was a relief, interrupting Orlando's endless travels with nowhere to call home. Orlando particularly enjoys the soft bed and clean clothes, something that was not available on the trail.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Why all the travel?"''
Orlando: ''"Working, after a fashion. You must understand, dear, the Management cannot travel as freely as most people can. In their stead, I have wandered far and wide, seeing to their interests and being their eyes and ears - hands, too, as necessary. It had its good moments. I enjoy meeting new people and much of the countryside is still beautiful, despite everything. But to be honest, my darling, it was a relief to come here to do this. It's been too long since I could remain in one place for a while. Promise me you won't get bored if I become a homebody. I'm getting used to a soft bed and clean clothes."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) In keeping with their secrecy, Orlando admits to living at the Whitespring, but will not divulge specifically where.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Are you living here in the Refuge?"''
Orlando: ''"Cheeky! Are you asking if you can come back to my place? Tempting, but we're not there yet, darling. I do have quarters within the Whitespring, since you ask. These are just my offices. As for where my actual rooms are...well, that's something I take some pains to protect. Management are not the only ones who value their privacy, and we have so many travelers passing through."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) Orlando is evasive on the topic of their past or their employers. Orlando refuses to divulge anything but the most vague facts, citing privacy concerns. Orlando believes all that matters is their support for the Responders.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Who, exactly, are 'Management'? This seems fishy."''
Orlando: ''"{{tooltip|My dear, nothing would bring me more joy than to answer your questions. Your suspicions wound me.|Apologetic}} However, my employer values their privacy as highly as they value the fine work the Responders are doing here. Suffice it to say they are the owners of the Whitespring, as I believe I've mentioned."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) The Management, they explain, prevents them from traveling and Orlando acts as their representative, and concierge to those found worthy.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What sort of work do you do for Management?"''
Orlando: ''"Oh, a bit of this, a bit of that. Whatever they require. As you might imagine, the state of things prevents them from much travel. I go where they need me to go and see to what affairs they see fit. In this case, the Whitespring itself and the Refuge. Think of me as a concierge, my dear. I'm here to improve your experience in whatever way you require."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) They refuse to divulge even a hint of where all the resources supplied by the Management come from.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"If Management is supplying the Refuge, where is it all coming from?"''
Orlando: ''"Now, darling, you can't imagine I would tell you a thing like that! A less-trusting soul might think you were pumping me for information in the hopes of planning a heist! Of course I know that's not why you ask, but you understand why I have to be rather secretive on the subject, don't you? Let's just say Management wisely invested its wealth, when such things mattered, and are now well-equipped to be generous."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) If sufficiently pressed, they might mention a "Mr. Otis" as their employer, the chairman of the management.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Orlando, be straight with me: Is Management even real?"''
Orlando: ''"What have I done to so earn your distrust, dear heart? I hoped you might consider me a friend by now. Yes. Management is real. If it will restore some faith in me, perhaps I could divulge just the slightest detail without betraying anything... I work directly for Mr. Otis, the Chairman. The very tip-top of the organization. A generous, if demanding boss. Now, please, darling - don't pry further. I only tell you this much because I value our relationship."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) Orlando explains that they simply owe their life to "Mr. Otis" and refuse to betray his trust.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Please, tell me more about Mr. Otis."''
Orlando: ''"As much as I enjoy our chats and relish your company, you simply must let this go, darling. I owe my life to Mr. Otis, and will not betray his trust or his judgment. I must be adamant. Please, love, do not ask me this again. It would hurt me to think you do not respect my wishes."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) Orlando will feign ignorance if pressed on the similarity of the name Mr. Otis (MOtis) to [[MODUS]], vehemently denying ever hearing of such a thing.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"'Mr. Otis'? Orlando, are you working for MODUS?"''
Orlando: ''"I don't understand what you mean, my dear. What is a MODUS? I've never heard of such a thing. No, darling. Just Mr. Otis and the Whitespring Management."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) Any ties to [[Enclave]] technologies, such as the [[ultracell]] design and function, are played off as merely having similar contacts with "The Management."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Wait - I discovered one of these Ultracells elsewhere. I thought it was a unique experiment."''
Orlando: ''"I could not possibly speak to your experience, dear. It sounds remarkable to make such discoveries! All I can tell you is that the Management provides them for the Refuge. Regrettably, that is as much as I know of the matter. I might wager that whomever was behind the Ultracell you discovered likely shared similar contacts with Management at some point. But who can say?"''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) ===Relationships=== Orlando dislikes being called a "lackey" or having their role disparaged in any way. In their opinion, they are doing something helpful, necessary, and have a clear purpose in life and place, something that many people lack.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Being a lackey can't be all you want from life, Orlando."''
Orlando: ''"What a terrible thing to call a friend's work, darling. 'Lackey'! I'm doing something important, dear. I'd hoped you would see that. There are people that need help, and in my work for Management I am able to help them. Not many can say the same! Besides...what else would I be? I am useful. So many people lack a purpose or place. That should be enough."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) Orlando thinks very highly of [[Skippy Roerich]], in particular due to his personality, refreshing attitude and willingness to chat.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Can you tell me anything about Skippy Roerich?"''
Orlando: ''"What a delightful man! I find him very refreshing, actually. An inventor and freedom-fighter, all in one! A number of our refugee guests hail from the Pitt, but Mr. Roerich is quite the character, and always willing to chat. I do enjoy meeting new people. The perspectives of others are invaluable, don't you think, darling?"''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) They have a cordial working relationship with [[Rucker]], though Orlando admits the Responders' leader does not fully trust them.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What are your impressions of Rucker?"''
Orlando: ''"Ms. Rucker is a lovely woman. Brave and sincere. Dedicated to her cause, I have no doubt. We have a cordial working relationship, I think. I do my best to aid her on behalf of the Management. I fear she does not entirely trust me, for some reason. We have fewer friendly conversations than I'd like."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) The same is not true of either [[Sophie Wagoner]] or [[Esme Rousseau]], both of who are inspiring and among Orlando's favorites (although they dislike even using the term, as it is improper to play favorites among guests).[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What do you think of Sophie Wagoner?"''
Orlando: ''"I have rarely encountered such optimism, even among these fine Responders. Ms. Wagoner's unusual childhood seems to have produced a happy, well-adjusted adult. We should all have been so lucky! She is always friendly with me. It would be improper of me to have favorites among our guests, but if I did, she would be among them."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Tell me about Esme Rousseau."''
Orlando: ''"Such a warm woman, wouldn't you say? A true joy to have with us here at the Whitespring. And she is so tireless in helping feed the poor people who come to the Refuge! Very admirable. I daresay that were the Whitespring operating as a resort once again, she could be our head chef."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) Of all the Responders, Orlando does not have much rapport with [[Lennox]], as they rarely visit the roof.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What's the deal with Lennox?"''
Orlando: ''"Ms. Lennox is a skilled pilot, I'm told. I confess we've spoken little, as she spends all her time attending to the vertibird. I do not get up to the roof as much as I might like - such lovely views - so we rarely cross paths."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) Outsiders get a fair shake. Orlando only knows the Brotherhood by reputation, though Orlando views [[Ellison|Initiate Ellison]] quite positively due to his good nature and curiosity.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Any thoughts on Initiate Ellison?"''
Orlando: ''"I confess I am only familiar with the Brotherhood by reputation, so I can't say if Mr. Ellison is an exemplar. He's so inquisitive and good-natured, I find it difficult to think of him as part of any military organization, to be frank. It's no secret they've sent him here to keep an eye on us, but I don't mind. The Whitespring has nothing to hide, darling."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) [[Giuseppe Della Ripa]] is also one of their favorites, thanks to his charms and aptitude for finding strange trinkets.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What's the story with Giuseppe?"''
Orlando: ''"Ah, our dear merchant and collector of the unusual! A charming man, don't you think, dear? Of course, the Whitespring has its own shopping already, but Giuseppe does have a knack for untapped markets. I'll be keeping an eye on his stock. You never know when he may find something new."''
([[Orlando/Dialogue|Orlando's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |quests started =[[Responders Reborn]] |quests involved =[[All the World's a Stage]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Responders Reborn]]: Orlando is the hub character for the quest, introducing the new Refuge mechanics (such as Refuge dailies), the lore behind ultracells, and helping players settle into the new update. * [[All the World's a Stage]]: [[Evelyn Russo]] meets with Orlando for a flight to Atlantic City. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Black and white tuxedo]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Orlando appears {{In|FO76TP}} and was expanded upon in the ''[[America's Playground]]'' update. ==Behind the scenes== * Every character in the Whitespring Refuge consistently refers to Orlando with they/them pronouns, although Orlando's non-binary identity is never explicitly mentioned in-game. * Voice director [[Phillip Reich]] confirmed that Orlando is non-binary, and stated that Orlando's voice took inspiration from the mannerisms of [[wikipedia:Katharine Hepburn|Katharine Hepburn]].[https://youtu.be/QFQDgxLeNVc?t=876 Phillip Reich Plays Fallout 76: The Pitt (Union Dues, Part 2 - Stream Archive) (0:14:36)]
[[Phillip Reich]]: ''"Orlando is non-binary, so they - we call they - and yeah, they're the liaison. So the Management is the secret organization behind the Whitespring Resort here. And they are their liaison that we'll talk to us for them on their behalf. [...] It's definitely inspired by... I remember when we were recording this character, we were like 'Yeah, we want a bit of a Katharine Hepburn-y kind of feel to Orlando.' So you can hear that in the way they talk that you get some of that old-timey 1950s Mid-Atlantic speech patterns. [...] And the actress we had in to voice Orlando... I can't remember her name, but she was a joy to work with, as well. Very, very lovely woman. I'll have to look up her name that voiced Orlando."'' * Orlando is voiced by [[Carolina Hoyos]], a queer two spirit actor who uses she/they pronouns.[https://www.linkedin.com/in/carolinahoyos Carolina Hoyos on LinkedIn] In an interview with Glowmade, Hoyos mentioned an appreciation for the humor of ''Fallout 76'' and its writing. Hoyos was not expecting to perform a [[wikipedia:Mid-Atlantic accent|transatlantic accent]], as it had not been requested in the audition process, but was able to deliver one anyway. Hoyos did a "round robin" of accents to refresh her mind and return to the transatlantic voice whenever she found herself slipping out of it.[https://archive.ph/W9qot Voicing Queerness: Carolina Hoyos] * Orlando shares their name with the main character of the novel [[wikipedia:Orlando: A Biography|''Orlando: A Biography'']] (1928) by [[wikipedia:Virginia Woolf|Virginia Woolf]]. The story is focused on an English nobleman who transitions from the male to female sex, then goes on to live for centuries, meeting various figures in history. It has been acknowledged as a feminist classic and analyzed for its transgender themes. ==References== {{Ref box}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox Expeditions The Pitt}} [[Category:Expeditions: The Pitt human characters]] [[ru:Орландо (Expeditions: The Pitt)]]

It is a pleasure.|sound=RefugeeM 0064231c_1.ogg}} '''Roy Lopez''' is a resident of [[The Whitespring Resort|the Whitespring Refuge]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== When Roy was a boy, his father taught him the game of chess. His father told him that the world is a chaotic place, but one can always find peace in chess. Unfortunately, his father was killed by raider attack dogs.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Why do you like chess so much?"''
Roy Lopez: ''"{{Tooltip|My father taught me the game of chess when I was just a boy. 'Roy,' he said to me, 'this world is a chaotic place, but one can always find peace in chess.'|Telling a story from his past, thinking fondly back to when he was a child}} {{Tooltip|Sadly, he was torn apart by raider attack dogs not long after, but his lessons remained with me. Despite life's hardships, I find solace in the game.|His fond memory suddenly takes a dark twist. Spoken in a somber way but with a bit of "such is life" sort of acceptance of the situation}}"''
([[Roy Lopez/Dialogue|Roy Lopez's dialogue]]) He considers himself a simple man with grand ambitions of teaching the other residents how to play the pre-War game of chess, but he is sad that no one else seems to care about it like he does.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"And who might you be?"''
Roy Lopez: ''"{{Tooltip|The name is Roy Lopez, recent refugee and chess aficionado. It is a pleasure.|Polite introduction}} {{Tooltip|I am a simple man with grand ambitions of teaching the other residents here the great game of chess. But alas, my efforts keep being thwarted.|Polite introduction, but also somewhat sad. He genuinely wants to teach others to play chess but so far he's been largely ignored.}}"''
([[Roy Lopez/Dialogue|Roy Lopez's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |ghost =yes |essential =yes |encounters involved=[[Chess Problem]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Chess Problem]]: The player character can help locate a missing chess piece from Roy's set. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Suspenders and slacks (Fallout 76)|Suspenders and slacks]] (non-playable)
