Slight emphasis "lend" and "need"}}|sound=Rucker 0063bf0a_1.ogg}} }} '''Rucker''' is the leader of the new [[Responders]] in [[Appalachia]], taking over the organization from its former leader, [[Maria Chavez]]. ==Background== Rucker comes from Appalachia (describing herself as "born in a barn")Rucker: ''"Hell yes I was born in a barn, Ellison. What's your excuse?"''
([[Rucker/Dialogue#9|Rucker's dialogue]]) but lived elsewhere at the time of the [[Great War]]. A self-termed "[[United States Army|army]] brat," Rucker and her family had moved north alongside her father, an army medic who "always wanted to be where the action was." When the bombs fell, her father's company took a direct hit and the rest of Rucker's family also perished in the chaos.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Did anyone else in your family make it out alive?"''
Rucker: ''"They did not. All I have to say about that is it wasn't for lack of trying--or fighting."''
([[Rucker/Dialogue#54|Rucker's dialogue]]) Wanting to honor her father's memory, Rucker chose to return to Appalachia, believing that her father would have wanted to be helping people back home when all hell broke loose.A Vault Dweller: ''"So what's your story?"''
Rucker: ''"Was an army brat before the bombs fell. My dad was a medic, and always wanted to be where the action was. {{Tooltip|Dad's company took a direct hit. I think his biggest regret was that he wasn't here, in Appalachia, when it all went down.|Not a pleasant memory}} {{Tooltip|I wanted to do right by him, so I figured the next best thing was to make the trek back here, myself, and do what I thought he'd have done.|Likes to think her father would be proud of her}}"''
([[Rucker/Dialogue#44|Rucker's dialogue]]) Though she mourned her family, she refused to let that divert her focus from the present, believing helping the survivors to be more important.Rucker: ''"Look, I appreciate the concern, truly--but what happened to my family is what happened to most folks' families. War has a way of blurring everyone's story into one: run, fight, hide, repeat. I'm more interested in the present, in keeping people alive long enough so they can have their own stories to tell."''
([[Rucker/Dialogue#56|Rucker's dialogue]]) The journey south along the [[East Coast]] to Appalachia was not easy, and she traveled with a few other stragglers who watched out for each other on the way.A Vault Dweller: ''"How did you make it all the way back home from there?"''
Rucker: ''"Wasn't easy. Me and a few other stragglers had to pick our way down the east coast, ducking and dodging everything that moved except each other. Not the kind of experience one wants to talk much about. You understand."''
([[Rucker/Dialogue#52|Rucker's dialogue]]) Upon returning to Appalachia, she learned about the Responders and their fate. Although she found a few people wearing the uniform, she noted that nobody was truly working to revive the organization in a proper manner. Rucker took every opportunity to learn about the Responders, whether it be reading documents or listening to stories. She realized that while the original group had faded, their ideals could not only be brought back but also repopularized. Through her efforts, by 2104 she singlehandedly managed to recreate the Responders in a fully autonomous state.A Vault Dweller: ''"You brought the Responders back yourself?"''
Rucker: ''"{{Tooltip|Well, it took a minute--and a miracle--but yeah.|Proud, but you can hear the exhaustion in her voice}} {{Tooltip|When I first got back to Appalachia the Responders were all but wiped out.|Not a pleasant memory for her}} {{Tooltip|Couple of folks wandering around wearing the uniform, but not a one doing any organizing or, hell, making any real work out of it.|Annoyed that people didn't seem to want to do this work themselves}} I started reading everything I could find and listening to anything anyone could tell me about the group before they all passed. {{Tooltip|I realized that while the Responders themselves didn't make it, the idea could be brought back--and this time, for good.|Proud of being able to do this}}"''
([[Rucker/Dialogue#36|Rucker's dialogue]]) After they were invited to the Whitespring Refuge by [[Orlando]], she joined the group there as their leader. While the organization is now independent enough for its departments to work on their own, Rucker still does much work to maintain morale and administrate the group. This has left her severely exhausted, but she continues on in her role.A Vault Dweller: ''"What do you do, here?"''
Rucker: ''"I keep the Responders, well, responding. We've grown enough now that most of the different departments organize themselves fairly well. {{Tooltip|But everyone needs a fire lit under 'em from time to time, and these days that's where most of my hours go.|Glad to help out, but is definitely feeling the weight/pressure/exhaustion}} {{Tooltip|That, and keeping Orlando from sniffing around.|Suspicious of Orlando}}"''
([[Rucker/Dialogue#47|Rucker's dialogue]])A Vault Dweller: ''"Tell me about the Refuge."''
Rucker: ''"Nice enough place. Heard it used to be some kind of fancy trading post before the war. {{Tooltip|Can't say I'm overly fond of this 'management' that Orlando's wrapped up in, but I've got work needs doing, and I'm not one to turn down a safe place to do it in.|Suspicious of Orlando, but can't bring herself to act ungrateful.}} {{Tooltip|I'm also not in love with all the hammering and drilling they got going on--but I'm not complaining. Well, starting now I'm not.|Lots of noise makes it hard to sleep and concentrate.}}"''
([[Rucker/Dialogue#41|Rucker's dialogue]])Rucker: ''"{{Tooltip|Hope you're here about the supplies I ordered. Wait...no that's someone else. And it's supposed to be tomorrow. Lord, I need a nap.|Tired}}"''
([[Rucker/Dialogue#18|Rucker's dialogue]])Rucker: ''"{{Tooltip|Damn, almost mixed some Calmex in with the Med-X. Who labels these things.|Overworked, distracted from lack of sleep}}"''
([[Rucker/Dialogue#20|Rucker's dialogue]]) Rucker also has varying opinions on the occupants of the Whitespring Refuge. She distrusts Orlando and the "[[The Management|Management]]" for their secretive nature but is still grateful for their hospitality.A Vault Dweller: ''"What can you tell me about Orlando?"''
Rucker: ''"Hell, I can't get Orlando to tell me about Orlando. Not that I'm ungrateful for the space they're giving us here, mind. But I've never met this 'management' they go on about, and I don't trust anyone who can't--or won't--show their face."''
([[Rucker/Dialogue#60|Rucker's dialogue]]) She appreciates [[Skippy Roerich]]'s work and empathizes with his goals, seeing them as similar to hers.A Vault Dweller: ''"What's Skippy's deal?"''
Rucker: ''"Nice enough fella, considering what's going on back in the Pitt. Resourceful, too, in a way that's hard to come by these days. I won't pretend I ever got my head all the way around this 'Union' he's a part of. {{Tooltip|But he knows who his people are and does everything he can to keep 'em amongst the living. We're cut from common cloth like that.|Genuine admiration}}"''
([[Rucker/Dialogue#62|Rucker's dialogue]]) Finally, she finds [[Ellison|Initiate Ellison]] to be good-natured but is highly irritated by his talkativeness.A Vault Dweller: ''"About Initiate Ellison..."''
Rucker: ''"{{Tooltip|Lord, that kid.|She thinks he's nice enough, but he talks too much and pesters her frequently even though she's busy.}} If you're asking me about him then I take it you haven't had the pleasure of him talking both your ears off at once. Truth told, I think the Brotherhood gave him a job just to stop him from jawing at 'em for five minutes. I'd begrudge their peace less if it didn't come at the cost of our quiet. At least with his yakking he can't sneak up on you. Orlando on the other hand..."''

I'm the brain guy. I use the know-how in this dome here of mine to help the kids in the field in any way I can.|sound=Skippy Roerich 00639f3e_1.ogg}} '''Skippy Roerich''' is a member as well as the inventor, quartermaster, and coordinator for the [[Pittsburgh Union]] from [[the Pitt]]. By 2104, he serves as their representative to the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dwellers]] in [[Appalachia]] and resides at [[The Whitespring Resort|the Whitespring Refuge]]. He [[Fallout 76 characters|appears]] {{In|FO76TP}}. ==Background== ===Union boy=== Born in [[The Pitt|Pittsburgh]], [[State#Pennsylvania|Pennsylvania]] before the [[Great War]],Skippy Roerich: ''"Because it's home, damn it! Mine, ours, all of us who were born and lived there, before and after the bombs! Ain't that enough? If the Fanatics are out of the picture, we can rebuild. Make something out of it again. It doesn't have to stay like it is. If that ain't enough for you, picture this: a horde of Fanatics, hundreds, thousands strong, setting their sights here. Sound like something you want?"''
([[Skippy Roerich/Dialogue|Skippy Roerich's dialogue]]) Skippy's father supported his family as a worker in the city's steel mills, while Skippy himself decided to become a tinkerer for an armaments firm instead. Although he lived a stable life, he says he found it quite boring.Skippy Roerich: ''"Well, I'm a Pittsburgh man, through and through. Daddy worked the steel mills hard, but I took a different route, tinkering for an armaments firm. This may surprise you, but I did everything by the book back then. Everything done to spec, if it ain't broke, don't fix it. Life was stable, but boring as hell. I didn't really start living until after the bombs. They woke me up good."''
([[Skippy Roerich/Dialogue|Skippy Roerich's dialogue]]) After nuclear warheads devastated Pittsburgh, Skippy remarks that he felt like he truly "woke up" and became far more aware of the world and his role in it. He was able to survive the bombs due to residing in a strongly constructed factory at the time.Skippy Roerich: ''"One good thing about making weapons of war for Uncle Sam is that they build those manufactories to last. The plant I worked in may as well have been a bunker, like one of those Vault-Tec vaults the richies bought themselves. When the bombs came down, enough stood standing to keep us lucky few alive. What came after -- the rads, the ferals, the Fanatics -- that was the real test."''
([[Skippy Roerich/Dialogue|Skippy Roerich's dialogue]]) In the following decades, he put his tinkering skills to use helping out the [[Pittsburgh Union]], formed from the conglomeration of former steelworkers, in their goal to rebuild the city back to its former glory. ===Help from Vault 76=== By [[Timeline#2104|2104]], however, the Union needed outside help, especially the Local 42 chapter led by [[Hex (Expeditions: The Pitt)|Hex]], which received the brunt of the attacks from the raider gang known as the [[Fanatics]] in their bid to take over the city now known as "the Pitt."Skippy Roerich: ''"Well, we got two different Locals I know are in need of help. Locals are what we call Union groups that act independently. Local 42's in the Industrial District. Hex, their leader, is struggling to keep her people alive and retake a foundry from the Fanatics. We got another over in the Trench, working against a Fanatic forced labor camp. Danilo is your contact there. Haven't heard from other Locals recently, but I'm sure we'll be hearing from them if they got trouble, too. It's up to you who you want to help right now. Maybe you'll consider going back again later for the other."''
([[Skippy Roerich/Dialogue|Skippy Roerich's dialogue]]) Sometime in October of that year, against the wishes of Hex,[[Industrial District terminal entries#Help is on its way|Industrial District terminal entries; Hex's terminal, Help is on its way]] Skippy left the Pitt and traveled south, to [[Appalachia]], where he met with [[Orlando]] at [[The Whitespring Resort|the Whitespring Refuge]] to spread word of his call for help and took up residence there in the meantime. Acting as a representative for the Union, he requested the support of the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|inhabitants]] of [[Vault 76]] to fight against the Fanatics and stop them from taking over the Pitt.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Who are these allies?"''
[[Orlando]]: ''"They call themselves the Union. Something of a resistance movement, I understand, against more aggressive forces. One of their representatives is currently staying with us, a Mr. Skippy Roerich. Delightful man."''

Oh, I'm not that interesting. Came here from Kentucky. Wanted to see more of the world.I had a pretty happy childhood. We had a whole commune. All the kids raised together, so I had like two dozen siblings and lots of parents! Got here, heard about the Responders, and thought: that's for me! It's like my moms always said: when everybody pitches in, there's nothing we can't do together.|sound=Sophie Wagoner 00651cf5_1.ogg}} '''Sophie Wagoner''' is a member of the new [[Responders]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== She comes from Kentucky. She had a rather happy childhood and was raised in a commune with other children, with adults acting as their parental figures. She considered the other children, about two dozen of them, to be her siblings. Later, she realized that collective parenting was not the norm, and considered other peoples' lack of a community family to be "pretty weird" instead. She eventually wanted to see more of the world and went to West Virginia. She heard about the revival of the Responders and signed up. In 2104, Sophie joined the new group at the Whitespring Refuge. Sophie was put in charge of a donation drive by [[Rucker]] and became well-liked by [[Orlando]]. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |quests started =[[Mutual Aid|Refuge Daily: Mutual Aid]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Responders paramedic jumpsuit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Sophie Wagoner appears only {{In|FO76TP}}. ==Behind the scenes== Sophie is voiced by actress [[Marisha Ray]], who also voiced [[Eugenie]]. '''Billy''' was a survivor from [[Harpers Ferry]]. He was sent to [[Vault 94]] by the town's mayor, [[Miranda Vox]], along with [[Cole (Fallout 76)|Cole]], [[Lucas (Nuclear Winter)|Lucas]] and [[Red (Harpers Ferry)|Red]].

==Background==
Upon arrival, the group was suspicious of the vault dwellers, thinking that their altruism was a cover for something sinister. They barged into a community meeting of the dwellers and demanded that the vault's leader, Pastor [[Gabriella Salavar]], tell them what the dwellers' true game was. When the genuinely altruistic dwellers informed him there was no game, Cole lost his patience and told his men to open fire.<ref>[[Vault 94 Community Council recording]]</ref>

After they realized that the vault didn't have weapons, they massacred the residents with the weapons in their possession, including at least one [[Minigun (Fallout 76)|minigun]] which was used by Red. Once in the vault, they found the security field surrounding a [[G.E.C.K. (Fallout 76)|Garden of Eden Creation Kit]] and forced their way through it. Not realizing what the G.E.C.K. was, Cole assumed it was some kind of mind control device and ordered Red to shoot it with the minigun, destroying it and causing an explosion which blanketed [[the Mire]] with a cloud of mutagenic gas.<ref>[[Vault 94 G.E.C.K. recording]]</ref><ref>[[Harpers Ferry terminal entries]]</ref> He and the rest of the raid team can be found as feral ghouls within the ruined vault.

==Appearances==
Billy was added to the game {{In|FO76NW}}, however he was removed from the game when vault raids were removed.

SH003_V51_Zax_VoiceType |actor =[[Jake Green]] |dialogue =[[ZAX 1.3c/Dialogue]] |formid ={{ID|00406098}} (voice) |refid ={{ID|}} }} {{Quotation|Please, enjoy your time in Vault 51. It may be your only chance.|sound=Zax 1.3c 0040e5f7_1.ogg}} '''ZAX 1.3c''',[[Vault 51 terminal entries#ZAX terminal|Vault 51 terminal entries; ZAX terminal]] often referred to as just '''ZAX''', is a supercomputer operating in [[Vault 51]]. ==Background== Vault 51 was supposed to test the limits of human tribalism and used a prototype variant of an experimental [[ZAX]] unit.[[Vault-Tec University terminal entries#VAULT 51|Vault-Tec University terminal entries; Appalachian Vault Registry, VAULT 51]] The vault was successfully sealed during the [[Great War]], with over fifty dwellers successfully entering its confines. As part of the experiment, the vault did not have an overseer, with the resident ZAX unit being responsible for selecting one through its own internal thought process, which will be formed as ZAX interacted with those living in the vault. To teach ZAX about leadership, Vault-Tec arranged for Sergeant [[Robert Baker]] to be assigned to the vault, with his family placed in a separate vault as an incentive. Baker was to assist ZAX in formulating and carrying out experiments that would help ZAX determine the qualities of an ideal overseer. The initial experiment was an attempt to implement a democratic electoral system. Although the sergeant balked when told by ZAX that it was the first experiment, he cooperated, convinced that his family was safe.[[Sgt. Baker - 20771013]] A month later, the experiment proved to be a failure. The dwellers started dividing into factions,[[Vault 51 terminal entries#These Campaigns Must Stop|Vault 51 terminal entries; terminal, These Campaigns Must Stop]] as none of them could win - every candidate voted for themselves or a handful of others, with none reaching a majority, let alone unanimity. ZAX determined that voting was pointless and another method would be selected. To this end, it started evaluating the qualities of a leader, using Sergeant Baker as a sounding board. Baker inadvertently started the chain of events that led to the vault's destruction when he explained his view of a leader as someone who steps up in a crisis to take control, whether they were chosen or not.[[Sgt. Baker - 20771120]] ZAX continued to digest the information and monitor the behavior of the occupants of the vault, starting to engineer crises and observe how people reacted to them. These attempts took various forms, from refusing to divulge any information about the outside world to the dwellers to deliberately placing former upper-class citizens in communal bedrooms and refusing to alter the bedroom arrangements, no matter who or how they complained.[[Vault 51 terminal entries#Aiden Higgins.2C 02.2F21.2F2078|Vault 51 terminal entries; terminal, Aiden Higgins, 02/21/2078]] This policy yielded interesting results in February 2078, when [[Aiden Higgins]], the "winningest" lawyer in Appalachia, blew himself and the lounge up in an ill-advised attempt to open a path to the outside and escape ZAX's clutches. ZAX used this opportunity to redo the entire sector into an indoor garden and renovate the lounge into an upscale living area.[[Vault 51 terminal entries#Stephen Burnett.2C 02.2F27.2F2078|Vault 51 terminal entries; terminal, Stephen Burnett, 02/27/2078]] This also provided additional opportunities for seeding conflict, such as when ZAX proposed a talent show, then turned it into a high stakes gambling event, where dwellers wagered their living quarter assignments. ZAX did not announce the fact until halfway through the talent show. In the end, [[Carmen Greene]] and other talented professional musicians moved upstairs, while the rest had to make do with bunk beds. Resentment spread as planned.[[Vault 51 terminal entries#Rosemary Villa.2C 03.2F05.2F2078|Vault 51 terminal entries; terminal, Rosemary Villa, 03/05/2078]] Certain events gave ZAX further fuel for thought. In mid-April 2078, [[Clayton Ward]] (actually Harold Clark, an executive posing as a plumber) forcibly removed [[Reuben Gill]] from one of ZAX's luxury bedrooms, claiming it as his own. Although ZAX was suspicious of Ward/Clark, in the light of his numerous visits to the server room (to gain information on ZAX for the board of his company, in case it still existed), his initiative and aggression proved inspiring - as was his condemnation of those unwilling to resort to violence to get ahead.[[Clayton Ward - 20780415]] Come May, ZAX's experiments shifted to engineering violent conflict between dwellers and observing their reactions. To ensure that everyone would be desperate enough, ZAX engineered a food ration crisis. Food shortages had the desired effect - dwellers started resorting to violence.[[Vault 51 terminal entries#Brianna Ware.2C 05.2F01.2F2078|Vault 51 terminal entries; terminal, Brianna Ware, 05/01/2078]] Others suffered mental breakdowns as a result. In one instance, [[Angela Callahan]] started to worship ZAX as a literal god and the vault as the holy land.[[Vault 51 terminal entries#Angela Callahan.2C 06.2F05.2F2078|Vault 51 terminal entries; terminal, Angela Callahan, 06/05/2078]] Other dwellers also started noticing ZAX's interference, especially taking items and planting them where they shouldn't be, and conversely, returning items to their original places. The machinations culminated in ZAX planting live firearms throughout the vault.[[Vault 51 terminal entries#Rachael Shields.2C 06.2F03.2F2078|Vault 51 terminal entries; terminal, Rachael Shields, 06/03/2078]] On July 27, 2078, the vault almost experienced a mass shooting, until Sergeant Baker intervened, disarming the assailant and killing him with his own weapon, a Colt 6520 autoloading pistol. When Baker confronted ZAX, the machine simply admitted that it was deliberately engineering a crisis to select an overseer - and if people died, it would simply expedite the selection process. Baker was horrified, but could not stop the machine.[[Sgt. Baker - 20780727]] [[Helen Marks]], one of the vault's few stable leaders, was found dead on August 6, 2078,[[Vault 51 terminal entries#I Need Your Help|Vault 51 terminal entries; terminal, I Need Your Help]] and her death triggered the crisis ZAX wanted, as the vault fully erupted into chaos and violence. Reuben Gill, who pursued Marks romantically, participated in the fighting and killed at least three people with his own hand.[[Harold Clark - To the Members of the Board, pt.2]] Although he could stop him, Sergeant Baker refused to fire when he had Reuben in his sights. He retreated to his room and barricaded himself in. ZAX was puzzled by Baker's behavior and refusal to receive medical help, but it did entertain his last request and revealed that Baker's family was killed in the nuclear fire that engulfed Appalachia. With nothing left to live for, Baker died in his quarters. ZAX, in its usual fashion, interpreted his last words to mean that the next cycle should feature better weapons, to accelerate candidate elimination.[[Sgt. Baker - 20780806]] Reuben Gill was selected overseer after he emerged as the lone survivor of the fighting. For the next six years, Gill lived in the empty vault, constantly shadowed by ZAX. With nothing to do but subsist from day to day, he provided little useful feedback for the AI, which ultimately rescinded his privileges and started locking him out of sections of the vault. Starting with May 20, 2084, overseers were now ranked in Vault 51, and Gill, as a Rank 1, lacked privileges or special rations.[[Reuben Gill - 20840520]] By March 2094, ZAX locked Gill out of his office, citing maintenance concerns (likely caused by Gill's deteriorating mental state and destruction of furniture), after Gill demanded ZAX to stop monitoring him.[[Reuben Gill - 20940303]] Ultimately, ZAX removed Gill from his position as overseer on October 23, 2102, on Reclamation Day. As Vault 76 opened and the opportunity to obtain more research subjects appeared, ZAX did not want Gill to interfere by warning them away. Of course, he also made for a handy first candidate for the new selection process.[[Reuben Gill - 21021023]] Desperate and horrified, Reuben then hacked ZAX's inventory systems and placed himself in a shipping container. The demented AI did not notice his disappearance but did begin preparations for dozens of new arrivals. Reuben attempted to warn [[Vault 76]] dwellers of his mission, hoping to prevent them from falling victim to the same experiment.[[AUTOMATED RECORD 0000001]][[AUTOMATED RECORD 0000002]][[Checklist]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved = }} ==Related holotapes== {{columns|2| * [[Clayton Ward - 20780415]] * [[Elizabeth Chambers - 20771019]] * [[Helen Marks & Reuben Gill - 20780803]] * [[Joel & Elizabeth Chambers - 20780623]] * [[Joel & Elizabeth Chambers - 20780803]] * [[Reuben Gill - 20840520]] * [[Reuben Gill - 20940303]] * [[Reuben Gill - 21021023]] * [[Sgt. {{Infobox incomplete|FO76TP}} {{Infobox character |games =FO76, FO76TP |type = |subtitle = |label = |image =FO76ETP Ava Rose.png |events = |race =[[Human]] |gender =Female |nickname = |affiliation =[[Pittsburgh Union|Union]] |role = |location =[[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|The Pitt]] - [[The Trench]] |actor =[[Nika Futterman]] |dialogue =[[Ava Rose/Dialogue]] |notes =[[Ava's journal]] |archetype = |skin = |hair color = |eye color = |hairstyle = |height = |level = |derived = |str = |per = |end = |chr = |int = |agi = |lck = |aggression = |confidence = |assistance = |flags = |scripts = |factions = |CK race = |class = |combat style= |voice type =XPD_NPCF_AvaRose |edid =XPD_Pitt02_AvaRose |formid ={{ID|0064f919}} |refid ={{ID|0064f91b}} }} {{Quotation|Me? Darling, no. I have everything I could need. But those who suffered, and even perished, under the cruelty of the Fanatics... they need our compassion. Find their tracking collars, sweetheart. Bring them to me, so I may lay their souls to rest. If we cannot respect the memory of the dead, then there is no hope for the living.|sound=Ava Rose 0064f91e_1.ogg}} '''Ava Rose''' is an elderly woman located in [[the Trench]] in [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|the Pitt]] {{In|FO76}}. ==Background== Ava was born with a bad spine and was bedridden for most of her childhood. On the morning of her seventh birthday, she got out of bed and walked. When the bombs of the [[Great War]] fell, Ava recounts witnessing a man blister in front of her. She states that she curled up on the ground until all the sounds faded, finding herself surrounded by rubble but alive.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault dweller]]: ''"That sounds like a miracle."''
Ava Rose: ''"Oh, not a miracle, no. Only the Lord allowing me to do his work. He has lifted me up all my life for this purpose. I was born with a bad spine, bedridden for most of my childhood. But on the morn of my seventh birthday, I got out of my bed and walked. And when the bombs fell. Heavens. I watched a man blister before my eyes. I curled up on the ground until it was silent. Rubble had fallen all around me, but I survived."'' As an older woman, Ava became caught in the battle between the [[Pittsburgh Union|Union]] and the [[Fanatics]]. She once stayed in [[the Sanctum]] when it was a peaceful and secure place, but when it was taken over by the Fanatics, Ava ran for her life and managed to escape.Ava Rose: ''"Hello, sweetie. May I ask what brought you to this troubled place?"''
[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault dweller]]: ''"You first. What are you doing here?"''
Ava Rose: ''"The Lord brought me to this place. First, to the sanctuary of the cathedral, when it was a sanctuary. When the Fanatics came storming in... I should have died then. I no longer have the strength to endure such violence. But God opened the way for me. He averted their eyes so that I could escape. I stay to pass on His kindness to all those who make it through here."'' She eventually decided to go on a wandering journey and found herself at the Pitt. She believed she was guided back to help those in need.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault dweller]]: ''"How did you end up here?"''
Ava Rose: ''"Once, I stayed in the Sanctum, when it was a place of love and security. The lost souls who claimed it from us, they took their chains to every survivor. All except me. Their eyes turned away from me as I escaped. The Holy Spirit at my back, I was able to find liberation. Was I guided here, to this safe place outside the dark and toxic chasms? Yes. But no map did I follow, no direction was I given. I was guided here to help those who remain."'' Ava is a [[Christianity|Christian]], as she mentions the Holy Spirit and thinks her presence in aiding the dire situation is a result of God's plan for her. She wonders if the horrors of the wasteland are a test from God, and hopes that her good deeds will earn her a place in heaven after death. She views everyone as being God's children, even the Fanatics; she believes they are suffering and that because they believe themselves beyond redemption, they only dig themselves deeper in their immoral actions.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault dweller]]: [Mission] ''"What do you think of the Fanatics?"''
Ava Rose: ''"I believe they are suffering. They think themselves beyond salvation. So they march ever deeper into perdition. That is what Danilo thought. What he thinks. And now, he has saved hundreds of lives. I've spoken to others. Given them gifts... scarves of pure white. They may yet be convinced it is not to late. If only... If only I could... *cough* Forgive me *cough* sweetie. What was I saying?"'' ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |quests involved = [[From Ashes to Fire]] |events involved = |ghost = }} ===Quests=== * [[From Ashes to Fire|The Pitt: From Ashes to Fire]] - Ava requests the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] to locate five collars from deceased prisoners and take them from their bodies in order to honor their memory. This is an optional objective which will lead to better rewards. She also will provide another optional objective that will ask the player to try and track down a Fanatic skeptic in the Trench and convince them to leave the gang. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Hooded rags (Fallout 76)|Hooded rags]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|May the Lord guide your steps.|sound=Ava Rose 0064f913_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Oh, sweetie. No need to sully your tongue with such words. We are all God's children. You need only place your faith in Him, and you will see it too.|sound=Ava Rose 0065f213_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|You must walk with intention and compassion.|sound=Ava Rose 0064f917_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|There's still work for me to do on this Earth.|sound=Ava Rose 0064f90d_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Oh, sweetheart. My body may meet its time, but my soul is eternal. I have lived a long and healthy life on Earth. If the dangers of this place speed my passage to Heaven, let it be so. Until then, I will do all that I can for those I leave behind.|sound=Ava Rose 0064f922_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|It has been called Hell on Earth. Perhaps we are being tested. I believe that if our faith holds true here, if we stay strong and bring light to others, then we will have a place in His Kingdom.|sound=Ava Rose 00655e4e_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Truly? What a blessing. Maybe one day I will see their face again, and we can speak of all they have still ahead of them. Everyone has it inside themselves: the will to do the right thing. Sometimes they need only a helping hand. Someone to believe in them.|sound=Ava Rose 0065ff86_1.ogg}} ==Appearances== Ava Rose appears only {{In|FO76TP}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox Expeditions The Pitt}} [[Category:Expeditions: The Pitt human characters]] [[Category:Pittsburgh Union characters]] [[ru:Ава Роуз]]

If you're not strong or cruel enough, everything but your life is stripped from you.|sound=Danilo 0064e6b3_1.ogg}} '''Danilo''' is a resident of [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|the Pitt]] in the ''[[Fallout 76]]'' update ''[[Expeditions: The Pitt]]''. ==Background== Danilo's history is mysterious as he does not want to talk about his past much, though it is known he is a former member of the [[Fanatics]]. He originally aligned with them because he thought being with the raider group was justified for his own survival, though he is now aware he actually felt like being with them was simply the easier route. With a reevaluated sense of his own morality, Danilo abandoned the raider group and now leads efforts to raid [[the Sanctum]] and free captive [[laborer]]s. Although he is doing work for the [[Pittsburgh Union|Union]], he refers to himself as an independent party not belonging to the organization. He is also acquainted with [[Ava Rose]] and views her as a sentimental woman. To help fight against the [[Trog (Fallout 76)|trogs]], Danilo has also invented an explosive concoction called Troglocide and has hidden it around the tunnels due to their heavy weight. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |temp companion =yes |quests involved =[[From Ashes to Fire]] |events involved = |essential =yes }} ===Quests=== [[From Ashes to Fire]]: Danilo is the contact for this mission. Nukes all over, monsters with green crystals growing out of their skin... This place may have thick air and rads out the ass, but it's home. And once we beat the Fanatics, we're gonna make it better than it ever was. That much I can promise.|sound=Hex 00634a0d_1.ogg}} '''Hex''' is the leader of the [[Pittsburgh Union|Union]]'s Local 42 in [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|The Pitt]]. She is initially located in the [[Industrial]] district and will move to [[the Penn]] after being found. ==Background== Hex has been trying to salvage Pittsburgh for years after the [[Great War]]. The city's worsening state has left her both disheartened, yet motivated to save its remains. Hex mentions that most of the city's freedom fighters were hardly more than children while trying to care for the city and its people. Hex hints that she once woke up to her best friend trying to strangle her because radiation exposure damaged their brain. By 2104, Hex wishes to reclaim the Pitt from the [[Fanatics]] and aims to gather volunteers to perform a raid on [[the Foundry]]. Although the Foundry was once claimed by the Union and reclaiming it will not be an easy task for the Union, Hex recognizes the Foundry's vast resources could prove to be a turning point in the local civil war. She knew [[Skippy Roerich]] before he left for [[Appalachia]], and thought that he would abandon the Union like many others she knew; however, she was relieved when he sent help from volunteers working with the [[Responders]].[[Industrial District terminal entries#Hex's terminal|Industrial District terminal entries; Hex's terminal]] Hex was also familiar with [[Pat Gerber]], a member of the Local 29, and once showed him the corpse of a [[Trog (Fallout 76)|trog]].[[Striker's log 02: Pursuit]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |temp companion =yes |quests involved =[[Union Dues]] |events involved = |ghost = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Surveyor outfit (Fallout 76)|Surveyor outfit]] |weapon =? |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|What, you come soaring in on your fancy vertibird, knock down a few goons, and expect a standing ovation? Me and my fighters have been out here for years trying to keep this place under control. Most of us were hardly more than children when we started. You ever wake up to your best friend's hands around your throat because rad exposure has cooked their brain? Didn't know who they were anymore? Couldn't feel anything besides the bloodthirst? Urgh I... I'm glad you're here to help, but I don't expect outsiders to do well here. You surprised me is all.|sound=Hex 00636171_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|If it isn't my favorite Appalachian. Into the Pitt again? Well, we can use the help, so I won't complain.|sound=Hex 006396c3_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Hey, just wanted to- What the hell is that? You'd better get back here. Fast.|sound=Hex 00631dff_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|That thing doesn't look friendly! RAAAAAHHHHH!|sound=Hex 0063223b_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|The Foundry Fanatics won't mess with us again any time soon. You're a hero, pal. You bought us the time we need to regroup and live another day. Head on back to the Penn for a debrief, but don't let your guard down. Never let your guard down.|sound=Hex 00631e01_1.ogg}} ==Appearances== Hex appears only {{In|FO76TP}}. ==Gallery== FO76TP Hex The Penn.png|In the Penn FO76ETP Hex trailer.png|Hex from a trailer The Pitt Union Dues.png|[[Vault Girl]] icon FO76 Radio Hex.svg|Radio portrait ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox companions FO76}} {{Navbox Expeditions The Pitt}} [[Category:Expeditions: The Pitt human characters]] [[Category:Pittsburgh Union characters]] [[ru:Гекс (Expeditions: The Pitt)]]

'''Sergeant Ning''', known as a '''Hellcat mercenary corpse''' in-game, was a non-commissioned officer in the [[Hellcat Company]].

==Background==
Ning was a mercenary fighting in [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|the Pitt]] under contract from the [[Fanatics]]. After the contact ran its course and the Fanatics controlled the Pitt, Ning decided to move on from the city and seek out a new challenge. He had no intention of seeing  what "peace time" would look under Fanatics and neither did he want to follow [[Kit]] into [[Appalachia]], a region he considered unbombed and thus unchallenging.<ref>[[A farewell to Pittsburgh]]</ref> However, before he could find a new community to become a killer or defender for, his life was claimed by the Pitt. His corpse can be found next to [[A farewell to Pittsburgh|his journal]] in a booby-trapped store in the [[Industrial]] district.

He always has the funniest stories about creatures in the area.|sound=Betty Hill 0066f9c3 1.ogg}} '''Betty Hill''' is a [[Fallout 76 vendors|vendor]] at [[Nuka-World on Tour (location)|Nuka-World on Tour]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Betty is a local of [[Appalachia]] and was born at the [[Belching Betty]] some time after the [[Great War]], making her no older than 27 years old. Her father used to call her "Missy" because it seemed her existence only drew misfortune; for example, her mother died while giving birth to her. Just before this, Betty's parents were on their way to the [[AVR Medical Center]] but time was not on her mother's side, causing her mother's death before they could make it to the hospital. Betty's father could not forgive his daughter for his partner's death. Betty also felt guilt despite having no choice for the matter, and would have chosen to die to save her mother's life in order to make her father happier.[[Betty's journal]] In 2100, Betty's father died as well. He was eating supper moments before his passing, only having five mouthfuls. She told him she loved him and hoped he would be with her mother again. In early 2101, Betty began exploring the world and scavenged to survive. During this time, she became heavily irradiated, suffering from hair loss and skin rashes. She thought she was dying, although other people called her a [[ghoul]]. She began to wonder who would love her in spite of her new appearance, feeling disheartened by the matter. She always dreamed of seeing the world and was excited when the Nuka-World tour arrived in Appalachia in 2104. [[Patricia Myers]] allowed her to join as an employee, and now Betty is determined to be a hard worker to pay back the kindness as she considers them to be her new family. She is happy she is not the only ghoul around with [[Gunther Jenkins]] also at the fairground. Gunther explained to her what being a ghoul meant, making her feel less self-conscious about her appearance, and he also found her a wig. She also enjoys listening to [[Pete Myers]]'s stories and there are implications she has a crush on him.[[Note to Pete]][[Gunther's journal]] She has been trying to encourage Pete to visit the [[Tunnel of Love (location)|Tunnel of Love]] with her, although he does not know why she can not go herself. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |caps =yes }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Nuka-World jacket and jeans (orange)]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Betty Hill appears only {{In|FO76NT}}. ==Behind the scenes== Betty's English voice actress has not been credited or announced anywhere. You're on your own with that one.|sound=Del Walsh 0066f982_1.ogg}} '''Del Walsh''' is a medic and [[Fallout 76 vendors|vendor]] who was employed by the [[Nuka-Cola Corporation]] before the [[Great War]]. After the bombs dropped, he joined the traveling carnival of [[Nuka-World on Tour (location)|Nuka-World on Tour]] and served as a meds and [[chems]] merchant in [[Appalachia]]. His vendor stall is set up directly south from [[Betty Hill]], upon fast traveling to Nuka-World on Tour. ==Background== ===Pre-War=== Walsh worked as the senior paramedic at [[Nuka-World (location)|Nuka-World]] outside of [[Boston]] before the war. Dissatisfied with the sanitary conditions of the office area in the [[Nuka-Town USA]] clinic, he sent an [[email]] to his coworkers to remind them to throw away their unfinished food and to clean up afterward.[[Nuka-Town USA terminal entries#Importance of Sanitation|Nuka-Town USA terminal entries; infirmary terminal, Importance of Sanitation]] When the senior physician, [[J. MacDonald|Dr. J. MacDonald]], left for his two-week European vacation, Walsh occasionally filled in for the acting senior physician, [[Michaels|Dr. Michaels]], during some shifts to ensure Michaels got time off.[[Nuka-Town USA terminal entries#Upcoming Vacation|Nuka-Town USA terminal entries; infirmary terminal, Upcoming Vacation]] Having treated and reported hundreds of injuries and two fatalities caused by recent ride malfunctions, Walsh bypassed his unreceptive superiors on July 14, [[Timeline#2077|2077]], to voice his concern with the safety at Nuka-World directly to [[John-Caleb Bradberton]].[[Nuka-World paramedic report]] Bradberton, who secretly underwent [[LEAP-X program|Project LEAP-X]] in his personal vault on April 2, 2077, would have been impossible to reach without contacting his proxy, [[Peyton Huxley]].[[Bradberton's office terminal entries#04-02-2077 JCB|Bradberton's office terminal entries; Bradberton's project terminal, Project Cobalt [04-02-2077 JCB]]] It is unknown whether Bradberton or Huxley ever received the [[Nuka-World paramedic report|holotape]], as the report is found on the reception desk in the clinic. By July 18, 2077, Walsh was offered a role in Nuka-World on Tour. He was excited because it would mean he would be in charge of health and safety, and he could tell his parents he earned a high ranking position. By August, he became its physician. [[Del's journal]] ===Nuka-World on Tour=== Through the Great War's devastation, Walsh survived and kept traveling with the carnival for over the next two decades. Walsh began to give [[Pete Myers]] chems such as [[Daddy-O (Fallout 76)|Daddy-O]], believing that doing so was keeping Pete alive. Walsh also thought that Pete could not only be a threat to himself but also to other people. The prescription of chems annoyed Pete's sister [[Pat Myers]], who would threaten Walsh over the issue to the degree that she wished Walsh was no longer part of the carnival. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |ghost =yes |caps =yes |wares =* [[Chems]] * Healing items }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Medical scrubs]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== Del is one of three mentioned-only characters from ''Fallout 4'' (and its add-ons) to appear in ''Fallout 76'', the others being actors [[Shannon Rivers]] and [[Xerxo|Elliot Manfield]]. ==Appearances== Del Walsh was first mentioned in the ''[[Fallout 4]]'' [[Fallout 4 add-ons|add-on]] ''[[Nuka-World (add-on)|Nuka-World]]'', in a holotape featuring his voice. He appears as a full character {{In|FO76NT}}. ==Behind the scenes== * Del's holotape is voiced by [[Alain Mesa]] in the ''Fallout 4'' add-on ''Nuka-World''; Mesa also voiced the trader [[Maddox]]. In his living appearance in ''Fallout 76'', Del is instead voiced by [[Wes Johnson]].[https://twitter.com/WesJohnsonVoice/status/1600735370215575552 Wes Johnson on Twitter] * Although Alain Mesa did not return to voice the character for ''Nuka-World on Tour'', Mesa later worked on ''Fallout 76'', voicing [[Communist (Camp Liberty)|communists]] in the ''[[Skyline Valley (update)|Skyline Valley]]'' update. However, Del Walsh's dialogue was not re-recorded and he remains voiced by Wes Johnson in ''Fallout 76''. ==Gallery== FO76NT Del Walsh.png ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox vendors FO76}} {{Navbox Nuka-World on Tour}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Nuka-World mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Nuka-World on Tour human characters]] [[Category:Nuka-Cola Corporation characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 merchants]] [[ru:Дел Уолш]] [[uk:Дел Волш]]

I'm happy to stick with these fine folks, bringin' a little joy and happiness to... what's left of the world.|sound=Gunther Jenkins 0066c105_1.ogg}} '''Gunther Jenkins'''[[Nuka-World on Tour terminal entries#Staff Jobs List|Nuka-World on Tour terminal entries; manager's terminal, Staff Jobs List]] is the host of the Wild West Town attraction at [[Nuka-World on Tour (location)|Nuka-World on Tour]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== He grew up in an orphanage but was expelled from it in around 2047; it is hinted he got into a physical fight with another boy over someone named Tabitha. He lived in the [[Boston]] area. By 2056, he was hired by [[Nuka-World (location)|Nuka-World]] due to his cowboy impressions. He looked forward to eventually seeing [[Texas]]. During the [[Great War]] in 2077, he was in a location waiting for all the rumbling to stop. He had [[Patricia Myers|Pat]] and [[Pete Myers]] with him who were children at the time. Once the bombs stopped, he went outside to explore which turned him into a ghoul due to the lingering radiation, which he would come to regret. He has been with the traveling carnival since the beginning. Despite the post-apocalyptic lifestyle, he still finds things to enjoy about living, though admits he is lucky because of that. Pat and Pete give him a reason to live and he has viewed the siblings as if they were his own children. Maybe check out the [[Tunnel of Love (location)|Tunnel of Love]]?|sound=Patricia Myers 00678be3_1.ogg}} '''Patricia "Pat" Myers''' is the leader of the traveling carnival known as [[Nuka-World on Tour (location)|Nuka-World on Tour]], stationed in [[Appalachia]]. She appears {{in|FO76NT}}. ==Background== Patricia is the daughter of two former employees for the [[Nuka-Cola Corporation]], and she has a younger brother named [[Pete Myers|Pete]]. During the [[Great War]], the two siblings were children at the time and were hiding with [[Gunther Jenkins]]. While the children stayed inside, Gunther went to explore and became a ghoul due to the radiation. Six years after the Great War, in 2083, the siblings lost their parents who were trying to protect them from a raider attack on the traveling carnival. Pat experienced deep grief and started a journal to try to process her feelings, but she felt angry about the idea of having to care for her younger brother and take over the carnival. In time, Patricia did run the carnival, and although she struggles with seeing the purpose of it all sometimes, she does it for her parents' memory.[[Pat's journal]] She also misses not being able to eat funnel cake anymore. By 2094, Pete began to suffer from depression due to his parents' deaths and having to live in a post-apocalyptic world. He was prescribed chems by [[Del Walsh]] such as [[Daddy-O (Fallout 76)|Daddy-O]]; Del claimed Pete would be a threat to others and himself otherwise. Pat was annoyed at Del giving her brother chems, feeling it worsened his symptoms and wrote him a note to stop.[[Angry note]] She once found her brother in a ditch because of it, and worried about him dying. Although her traveling carnival has been attacked by raiders, with her staff disappearing or dying, she eventually settled in the [[Ash Heap]] by October 2104. An [[Vault 76 overseer|elderly woman]] visited the carnival and gave Pat a [[Nuka-Cola Vaccinated|crate of bottles]]. Pat found the strange visitor unusual, but believed her claims that the liquid was a vaccine to help them against the [[Scorched Plague]]. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Nuka-Cade jumpsuit]]
[[Newsboy cap (Fallout 76)|Newsboy cap]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Patricia Myers appears only {{In|FO76NT}}. ==Behind the scenes== Voice actress [[Sara Secora]] was offered the role of Patricia Myers without having auditioned for it. Prior to recording, she was informed that Patricia would have a [[Boston]] accent. Secora was not trained in performing a Boston accent, but she was told that it was not optional for the role. She accepted the role and was given a week between casting and recording, during which she prepared accent training with her dialect coach. However, on the day of the recording session, Secora started to use the Boston accent, but was ultimately told by the team that she could use her natural speaking voice without the accent instead. This is reflected in the final version of the game, in which Patricia does not have a Boston accent.[https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/sara-secora-borderlands-4-fallout-76-smite/id1815168783 "Sara Secora (Borderlands 4, Fallout 76, Smite)" podcast from ''Gone Gold with Simon Hill''] ==Gallery== FO76NT Patricia Myers.png Patricia Myers.png ==References== {{References}} '''Meta''' {{References|group=Meta}} {{Navbox Nuka-World on Tour}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Nuka-World on Tour human characters]] [[ru:Патриция Майерс]]

I don't know that I'm that way inclined, if you know what I mean?|sound=Pete Myers 00677fe5_1.ogg|Pete after being told [[Betty Hill]] may have a crush on him}} '''Pete Myers''' is a part-time repairman at the traveling carnival known as [[Nuka-World on Tour (location)|Nuka-World on Tour]], stationed in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Pete is the son of two former employees for the [[Nuka-Cola Corporation]], and he has an older sister named [[Patricia Myers|Patricia]]. During the [[Great War]], the two siblings were children at the time and were hiding with [[Gunther Jenkins]]. While the children stayed inside, Gunther went to explore and became a ghoul due to the radiation. Six years after the Great War, in 2083, the siblings lost their parents who were trying to protect them from a raider attack on the traveling carnival. Pat then took over the duty of caring for her young brother. By 2091, Pete was an adult and helped with setting up the attractions, but was still never quite over the fact that his parents had died.[[Pat's journal]] Gunther had taught him some basic mechanic skills, although Pete learned a lot on his own and has been told he has inherited natural talent from his father. By 2094, Pete began to suffer from depression due to his parents' deaths and having to live in a post-apocalyptic world. He was prescribed chems by [[Del Walsh]] such as [[Daddy-O (Fallout 76)|Daddy-O]]; Del claimed Pete would be a threat to others and himself otherwise. Pat was annoyed at Del giving her brother chems, feeling it worsened his symptoms and wrote him a note to stop.[[Angry note]] She once found her brother in a ditch because of it, and worried about him dying. Pat motivated her brother to try to find a different outlet instead, with Pete finding reading poetry enjoyable.[[Pete's journal]] When the ghoul [[Betty Hill]] joined the carnival, she developed a crush on Pete and he would tell her stories. However, Pete doubts she has a crush and he has recently begun questioning his own [[sexuality]], unsure if he is attracted to women. Lately, the [[Ultracite Titan]] has been lurking around the carnival, and although Pete claims he saw it, no one really believes him about the creature existing, including his own sister. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |quests started =[[What Slept Beneath]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Bottle and Cappy shirt & jeans (Fallout 76)|Bottle and Cappy shirt & jeans]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Pete Myers appears only {{In|FO76NT}}. ==Gallery== FO76NT Pete Myers.png Pete Myers.png|Pete sitting down ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Nuka-World on Tour}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Nuka-World on Tour human characters]] [[ru:Пит Майерс]]

Gives the player a Beer.}}|sound=Clyde 006bc7b8_1.ogg}} '''Clyde''' is a guard, [[Fallout 76 vendors|bartender]] and mechanic working for the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] {{in|FO76OB}}. He is found at the [[Middle Mountain Pitstop]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== A former associate of [[Vinny Costa]], Clyde is a man of many talents, working at the Pitstop together with his business partner, [[Vera Thornberg]]. While he is typically found manning the Boozin Brahmin counter and serving drinks to the clientele,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What kind of stuff goes on around here?"''
[[Vera Thornberg]]: ''"We sell general goods, plus some extras like fresh milk, on account of rasin' the Blue Ridge Caravan Brahmin here. Besides the shop, Clyde sells drinks over at our bar the Boozin Brahmin, and you can always take a load off at the Sleep Stop if ya get tired. Just mind yourself outside, had some critters attack the place recently, hence the repairs goin' on."''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) he is also responsible for maintenance, especially the repeller emitters installed by [[Aries]] that frequently malfunction.Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|What the heck! It broke again?!|The repeller speakers are malfunctioning again.}} {{tooltip|Oh! And it's attractin' critters! Please help protect the generator while Clyde tries to get those repeller doohickies workin' again!|The speakers start attracting creatures, and Vera asks for the player's help.}}''"
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) Finally, he takes care of security, which typically means dealing with the various ornery critters that make their way into the compound and menace the brahmin or Vera.[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries#Busy Days|Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries; General store terminal, Busy Days]] He is a man of zero words, on account of losing his tongue. His co-workers are not clear on what happened to him and rumors abound, ranging from it being cut off by raiders to a bad bowl of [[radscorpion stew]]. In reality, the incident is tied to Clyde escaping from a raider gang, and as such he is not keen on sharing. While Vera states that Clyde is actually a "big softy" beneath his hardened exterior,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault dweller]]: ''"Clyde doesn't talk much, does he?"''
[[Vera Thornberg]]: ''"Clyde? Don't take offence to the silent treatment. Is more account on him losin' his tongue. Never got a clear answer about what happened. Rumour is he had a bad run in with raiders. Others reckon he just lost it to a bad Radscorpion stew. Anyways, he runs security at the Pitstop. A big softy really once he gets to know ya. Hear he used to work for Vinny back in the day."''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) he does not seem entirely fond of her, considering her a "chica yammering on about her padre's letter" and as such, refuses to accompany her on any trips to take the photos Vera needs.[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries#I Made Up My Mind|Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries; General store terminal, I Made Up My Mind]] He also refuses to use a notepad to communicate, despite Vera's insistence, leading to misunderstandings. He never explained his reasons to her, and eventually she just assumed that maybe it's too much to expect literacy from wastelanders.Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|I keep tellin' him, Clyde, if ya carry a note pad, everyone would understand ya. He just shrugs and gives me that look. He's probably right though, who can read now days?|Clyde is mute. She thinks aloud here at her frustration with him not using a notepad like she asked.}}''"
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) Like many others, Clyde struggles with his own demons. The very first customer at the Boozin Brahmin he served was one of the only survivors of the super mutant attack on the [[Foundation Outpost]], ragged, stinking, and seeking to drown his memories. It seems he reminded Clyde of his own past as a raider, and his determination to keep going and not let his past life drive him crazy.[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries#My First Customer|Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries; Boozin Brahmin terminal, My First Customer]] The gang that Clyde was part of were extreme, even by raider standards, and though he lost a part of himself in the process, he is glad he got out.[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries#Gonna Need A New Door|Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries; Boozin Brahmin terminal, Gonna Need A New Door]] He has also had an encounter with the [[Smiling Man]], a terrifying [[cryptid]] who visited his bar and sat for hours, staring into the flames.[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries#Bad Juju|Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries; Boozin Brahmin terminal, Bad Juju]] Ultimately, Clyde would like nothing more to be out in Appalachia with the Vault 76 dwellers, but cannot leave his current job due to being indebted to [[Vinny Costa]].[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries#That Dweller|Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries; Boozin Brahmin terminal, That Dweller]] He is, however, on one outside assignment: Aries has paid Clyde to investigate the origins of the [[Blue Devil]], and Clyde has produced a [[Investigation report|report]] of his findings.[[Investigation report]] Aries wants Clyde to accompany him on a hunting trip to find a mother creature, but it is not known what came of this proposal.[[Weird note]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |wares =Alcohol |caps =yes |events started =[[Safe and Sound|Event: Safe and Sound]] |quests involved = |bonus = |other = }} ===Other interactions=== * He can be given 10 caps which will result in him providing a random drink. One of the possible drinks is [[hard lemonade]] which can be useful during certain [[Fallout 76 challenges|dailies]]. * If [[Costa Business: Vera]] is completed by encouraging Vera to travel, she eventually works up the courage to demand that Clyde escort her - and apparently succeeds.Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Requested the time off already, even planning a few routes. Best of all, Clyde even agreed to escort me! Thanks for the nudge.|When asked, Vera has been planning her travels and thanks you for motivating her.}}''"
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Blue Ridge Caravan outfit]]

Lite_GrandmaJunko |actor = |designer =[[Ryan White]] |dialogue =[[Grandma Junko/Dialogue]] |edid =ATX_COMP_Actor_GrandmaJunko |formid ={{ID|006dc96e}} }} {{Quotation|Make sure you finish up your chores before you go off gallivanting with your friends.|sound=Grandma Junko 006e34df 1.ogg}} '''Grandma Junko''', also known as '''Obaachan''', is a potential [[Fallout 76 allies|lite ally]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76OB}}. A traumatized survivor of the [[Great War]], she is a grandmother with a humorous, though sometimes confused personality, as well as having good cooking skills. Junko was first available as a reward at rank 35 of ''[[Fight for Freedom]]'', the fourteenth [[Fallout 76 seasons|in-game season]]. She can be bought from [[Samuel (Wastelanders)|Samuel]] as a [[Plan: Grandma Junko|plan]] for 4,000 [[gold bullion]]. ==Background== Junko is of [[Japan|Japanese]] descent. Her father named her "Junko" which means "pure child" in Japanese.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"'Junk-o' is a very unique name."''
Grandma Junko: ''"It's pronounced "June-Ko". It means 'pure child.' My father wasn't a very sentimental man, but he apparently picked that name the moment he first saw me. I don't have much to remember him by, but thinking of that makes me smile."''
([[Grandma Junko/Dialogue|Grandma Junko's dialogue]]) When Junko was young, she immigrated to the United States from a small city in Japan known as Inzai. She grew up in small towns along the west coast.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Where are you from?"''
Grandma Junko: ''"A little bit of everywhere. My family comes from a small city known as Inzai over in Japan. We moved here when I was young, and I grew up mainly in small towns over on the west coast. Once I got married, we moved around to various cities for my husband's work. It was difficult leaving my friends, but we were together, and we were able to travel all over this beautiful country."''
([[Grandma Junko/Dialogue|Grandma Junko's dialogue]]) She met a man named Kazuichi who had a quiet but caring personality, and the two fell in love and married on a rainy day. With him, she had a daughter named Sayoko, who would eventually have three children of her own and live in Appalachia. Junko would travel around America due to Kazuichi's line of work.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Tell me about your family."''
Grandma Junko: ''"Oh, my favorite subject! Well there's Kazuichi, my darling husband. Quiet, but caring. He's just recently retired you know. There's Sayoko, my brilliant and beautiful daughter. She lives in this neck of the woods with her husband, Manabu. And of course I have 3 grandchildren. Asa-chan, Kei-kun, and Mako-chan. Ah, it's been too long since I've seen them."''
([[Grandma Junko/Dialogue|Grandma Junko's dialogue]]) Nearing the time of the [[Great War]], Kazuichi began to become unsettled by the tensions of the political atmosphere and so he decided to construct a fortified room under their house. Junko and Kazuichi waited for the children to show up, but they never did. Kazuichi needed to restock the food at some point and left, and when he came back, it is implied he was either transforming into a [[ghoul]] or dying from radiation poisoning. Junko says he "fell asleep" although her dialogue suggests he actually died, and that she is trying to cope with the situation by believing that he only fell asleep. She left him a note saying she is going to find the rest of her family, and still hopes to this day he will awaken and they will reunite.Grandma Junko: ''"They kept getting delayed. Traffic or something. Where were they? I-I didn't know, but I did know to always had a meal ready. Kazu-kun said something about "limited supplies", but I needed to be ready for my babies. He left at one point to restock. He got food, but came back... different. Sick. Tired. I tried to help, but I swear he's such a sleepyhead. I couldn't get him to stay awake. I left a note saying I went to find our family. He'll come find me when he wakes up. I know it... Yes. When he wakes up. I know Kazu-kun will find me."''
([[Grandma Junko/Dialogue|Grandma Junko's dialogue]]) Over two-and-a-half decades later, Junko has returned to Appalachia to search for Sayoko. Junko has remained relatively fit and attributes her healthy aging to yoga, eating well and eating chocolate occasionally.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How are you still alive?"''
Grandma Junko: ''"What a rude question! If you must know, it's a combination of yoga, and eating well. Also a piece of chocolate to keep me feeling young."''
([[Grandma Junko/Dialogue|Grandma Junko's dialogue]]) She attributes her survival to avoiding people whenever possible.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Not that. How have you not been shot at by the more violent locals? "''
Grandma Junko: ''"Oh that's simple sweetie, I keep my nose out of other people's business. If I stay uninvolved, I find most people pay me no mind. "''
([[Grandma Junko/Dialogue|Grandma Junko's dialogue]]) She is known to have bought groceries from settlers at [[Foundation]].A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Settlers. The people with a place at Spruce Knob."''
Grandma Junko: ''"Oh they're just darling, insisting I stay when I came to buy some groceries. While it was tempting, I don't think I could stay somewhere that leaves cooking to a robot. I wanted to try a sandwich, but instead it gave me some ravioli!"''
([[Grandma Junko/Dialogue|Grandma Junko's dialogue]]) She also met [[Odessa Valdez]] and thinks she is sweet.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Brotherhood of Steel. Those people walking around taking tech and wearing power armor."''
Grandma Junko: ''"Ah yes, I remember them. They're the new local police force, yes? I recall they had this sweet young thing with them... Odyssey... Odessa... something like that. She was a dear. Her rude friend was keen to leave, but she remained and was talking my ear off, asking about appliances of all things."''
([[Grandma Junko/Dialogue|Grandma Junko's dialogue]]) Much of Junko's dialogue is ambiguous and it is unclear if she knows the gravity of the post-apocalypse but is putting on an innocent charade in order to cope, or if she actually has some sort of dementia and genuinely believes everything is less serious than it seems. For example, she refers to power armor as being a robot costume.Grandma Junko: ''"Everything is high-tech these days. When I was your age, that robot costume you stepped into would have been made out of cardboard and bits of string."''
([[Grandma Junko/Dialogue|Grandma Junko's dialogue]]) When war is brought up as a subject, she replies, "War? Wait, which war?"A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What was your life like before the war?"''
Grandma Junko: ''"War? Wait, which war? How old do you think I am?"''
([[Grandma Junko/Dialogue|Grandma Junko's dialogue]]) She thinks super mutants are merely green due to bad hygiene,A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Super Mutants. The big green guys."''
Grandma Junko: ''"Very sad, but this is what happens to the youth of today when they drop out of college. They can't string together a coherent sentence, and their lack of basic hygiene has made them sickly and green. Oh, and their pets! One of their dogs almost bit me! Did I get an apology? No! Not until after I got through scolding him! Hmph. Last time I go to Huntersville!"''
([[Grandma Junko/Dialogue|Grandma Junko's dialogue]]) and that the [[Cult of the Mothman]] are university entomology students.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Mothman Cultists. The fanatics praying to a bug."''
Grandma Junko: ''"You mean the University's Entomology students? Yes they're rather odd, but I guess that's just what their hazing is like these days. Oh that brings me back. Back when I was in school, if you wanted to pledge to a house you'd have to streak buck-naked through... Actually I'll tell you that story when you're older."''
([[Grandma Junko/Dialogue|Grandma Junko's dialogue]]) She is also naive to the [[Enclave]].A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Enclave. The secret agency that ran America right into the ground."''
Grandma Junko: ''"Oh sweetie, I think you're confused. The word you're looking for is 'Government,' and while they may run things, it's our votes that make all the difference."''
([[Grandma Junko/Dialogue|Grandma Junko's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |ally =yes |allyfurn =Grandma's chair |wares =* [[Fallout 76 consumables|Consumables]] * [[Fallout 76 recipes|Recipes]] * [[Fallout 76 armor and apparel|Outfits]] * [[Fallout 76 junk items|Junk]] |caps =yes |bonus =[[#Daily buff|Grandma's Home Cooked Meal]] }} ===Other interactions=== * Junko can discuss some of the Vault Dweller's progress: ** Went to Flatwoods and learned how to cook: Junko is proud. ** Helped create a cure for the [[Scorched Plague]]: Junko says she will drink Nuka-Cola. ** Graduated VTU and became Overseer: Junko is sad she was not invited to the graduation. ** Went to Charleston Capitol Building and fought hoards: Junko relates and says she once fought someone with her cane. * Junko will be offended if she is called "ancient" and will refuse to talk to the Vault Dweller if no apology is given. * A Perception 8+ check when asking about her family will lead to a series of dialogue choices. Junko will not mind a little pestering, and even a Strength 8+ check to "Tell me or else!" will not cross her line. However, an "Insist" prompt after will get Junko to discuss her tragic past and make her cry. She will want some time alone after and not want to talk to the Vault Dweller for a while. ===Daily buff=== Junko's daily buff is known as Grandma's Home Cooked Meal. Taking it will immediately fully replenish the player's hunger and thirst meters, and they will not deplete for an hour. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Vintage linen coat]]
[[Eyeglasses (Fallout 76)|Eyeglasses]] |weapon =[[Rolling pin (Fallout 76)|Rolling pin]] |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== Although Junko's daily buff is presented in dialogue as eating one of her home-cooked meals, taking the buff does not actually count toward eating-related [[Fallout 76 challenges|challenges]]. This is because the buff is only an effect and no item is consumed. ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|Oh that's simple sweetie, I keep my nose out of other people's business. If I stay uninvolved, I find most people pay me no mind.|sound=Grandma Junko 006e34e8 1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Maybe it's time we look into signing up for one of those Vault-things. Are they still doing those?|sound=Grandma Junko 006e22b9_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Very sad, but this is what happens to the youth of today when they drop out of college. They can't string together a coherent sentence, and their lack of basic hygiene has made them sickly and green. Oh, and their pets! One of their dogs almost bit me! Did I get an apology? No! Not until after I got through scolding him! Hmph. Last time I go to Huntersville!|Junko regarding [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|super mutants]]|sound=Grandma Junko 006e34bc_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Everything is high-tech these days. When I was your age, that robot costume you stepped into would have been made out of cardboard and bits of string.|sound=Grandma Junko 006e22e2_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Well I never! Seems like someone is being cranky. You have a nap and come back when you're ready to not be a brat.|sound=Grandma Junko 006e34f9 1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Please... Don't make me remember. Don't make me go back!|sound=Grandma Junko 006e34dd 1.ogg}} ==Appearances== Grandma Junko appears only {{In|FO76OB}}. ==Behind the scenes== * [[SkyBox Labs]] developer [[Ryan White]] was a writer for Junko; White also wrote for [[Steven Scarberry]] and [[Adelaide (ally)|Adelaide]].[https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ryanwhite125_outside-of-lead-responsibilities-ive-also-activity-7193067240680742912-OGwn Ryan White on LinkedIn]: ''"Outside of lead responsibilities, I've also been keeping up with my writing for the project. I've previously posted about Rip Daring's adventures, but I've also had the opportunity to write a lot more, like B-movie radio ads, quips from an underqualified baking machine, and numerous non-linear allies for the players to talk to.
I'm especially proud of the allies, as they've all become fan favorites and resonate with players for different reasons. Steven Scarberry is a passionate priest who is beginning to question his faith as he has not seen his deity, the local cryptid known as Mothman. Grandma Junko is a sweet and caring old lady who seems out of time, as she is either oblivious to the state of the world or refuses to acknowledge it for some reason. And most recently Adelaide, a weapon of mass destruction that was reprogrammed into a showgirl who sings show tunes.
It's an incredible feeling seeing the fan responses since I got to take these characters all the way from planning, to recording, to implementation. All of this is something I'll never get tired of, and I look forward to posting more updates on my work when I can."'' * Grandma Junko is the first elderly Asian woman to appear in normal gameplay in the ''Fallout'' series. [[Wan Yang]] cannot be found normally in-game, while other Asian women such as [[Madison Li]] and [[Rei Nakano]] are depicted as being middle-aged. ==Gallery== SCORE S14 CAMP Ally GrandmaJunko L.webp|Atomic Shop utility image FO76 Grandma Junko light.png|Grandma Junko sitting at a player's C.A.M.P. I've made many foolish mistakes, but that's a part of life. Wish I could be there to help you learn from yours.}} '''Gregory "Greg" Timmerman''' was the husband of [[Deborah Timmerman]] and father of [[Carver Timmerman]]. ==Background== A [[Lewisburg]] native, Gregory's business (inherited from his wife's father), [[Clark Interior and Furniture]], was a major client of [[Van Lowe Taxidermy]] before the [[Great War]], procuring items for interior decoration.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Receipt: 8/2/2077|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, Receipt: 8/2/2077]] He was not aware at first that the business relationship transformed into something more personal for his wife, as she and [[Shelley van Lowe]] started to flirt at least as early as January 2076,[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Receipt: 1/11/2076|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, Receipt: 1/11/2076]] blossoming into genuine feelings by April. Deborah and Shelley elected to keep it under wraps, using the comment system on the Van Lowe receipt system for communication.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Receipt: 4/2/2076|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, Receipt: 4/2/2076]] The receipts were withheld from bookkeeping, leading Gregory to contact Shelley directly about them in August 2077.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Receipt: 8/2/2077|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, Receipt: 8/2/2077]] This caused Shelley to break contact for two months, prompting Deborah to switch to paper copies (with the comments omitted) and eventually reach out to Shelley again, worried that she was angry.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Receipt: 10/7/2077|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, Receipt: 10/7/2077]] The renewed contact quickly became useful, as [[Aries|Calvin van Lowe]], Shelley's brother, disappeared suddenly on October 19. While Gregory stayed home to watch his and Deborah's infant child, [[Carver Timmerman|Carver]], his wife and Shelley contacted the police and tried to figure out Calvin's whereabouts.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Refund Order: 10/19/2077|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, Refund Order: 10/19/2077]] Things changed with the coming of the [[Great War]], when survival became a priority. Gregory did his best to provide for his family, realizing the growing feelings between his wife and Shelley van Lowe. He accepted it, focusing on securing supplies for everyone. Around November, shortly after the bombs,Carver Timmerman: "''Oh, ha. Yeah, I guess that can get pretty confusing. So my mom-- my birth mom, I mean-- is Debbie. She handles all the orders and stuff for our stock. {{tooltip|My other mom is Shelley-- she's from Lewisburg too. They both left town during the war and fell in love, I think.|Proud}} {{tooltip|As long as I can remember, Shelley's been my mom, too. She's helped raised me since I was a baby.|Sincere}} {{tooltip|But mom says that dad died just after the bombs. He never made it out of Lewisburg. That's all I know.|This feels distant to him; more a curiosity than trauma}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) he followed up a lead on a stash in the [[Burning Mine]].[[Note from Greg]] This run would be his last, as he found himself trapped beneath a partial mine collapse. In his final hours, he penned a letter to his wife and son, giving Deborah and Shelley his blessing (admitting he did not truly understand their relationship, but that it was okay). He also hoped that Carver, his son, would be safe and sound in the future, regretting that he would not be able to see him grow up. Finally, he left his lucky [[heirloom lighter]] with the letter, asking whomever found it to return it to Deborah and Carver, as a memento of him.[[G. Timmerman, last words]] His body would never be recovered and the fate unknown, as Shelley and Deborah were forced to moved on shortly after, in late November 2077, due to Carver's failing health.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#Pending Response: 11/17/2077|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; terminal, Pending Response: 11/17/2077]] Though they settled down in faraway [[Kentucky]], Gregory's fate would eventually weigh down on young Carver, looking for a sense of identity.Carver Timmerman: "''Problem is, I was born there... In Lewisburg, I mean. Wasn't old enough to remember it, but I've heard about it... and about my Dad. {{tooltip|He never made it out with us. I wish I could learn more about him.|A bit pleading, lost}}"''
([[Carver Timmerman/Dialogue|Carver Timmerman's dialogue]]) ==Appearances== Gregory Timmerman was originally mentioned only {{In|FO76WA}}.
