I'll pay you!|sound=Luca Costa 006a09ea_1.ogg}} '''Luca Costa''' is an employee of the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] {{in|FO76OB}}. He is the central character in the [[Beasts of Burden]] event, during which he is found at the [[Sacramental Glade]]. When the event is not active, he can be found at [[Big Bend Tunnel east]]. ==Background== Luca is the nephew of [[Vinny Costa]]. Although now an adult, he appears to have been born either shortly before or after the [[Great War]]; Luca mentions that as a child, he once tried to befriend a [[Mirelurk (Fallout 76)|mirelurk]] he named "Scuttles," but it did not go well and the mirelurk died.Luca Costa: ''"Ooh I bet something real nasty is in there. Reminds me of when I tried to befriend a Mirelurk as a kid. Didn't go well. Rest in peace Scuttles."''
([[Luca Costa/Dialogue|Luca Costa's dialogue]])
'''Note:''' This line is heard during [[Beasts of Burden|Event: Beasts of Burden]]. Luca only recently started residing with his uncle Vinny, saying that he has been staying with him "a little while." As a result, Luca has been trying to find ways to contribute to the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]], for which Vinny works as a manager.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Tell me about yourself."''
Luca Costa: ''"Well firstly name's Luca. I help out around here, going with some of the caravans and the like. Vinny's my uncle, been staying with him a little while. Go on some of the routes sometimes, stretch my legs and all that. Been tryna contribute to Blue Ridge, I don't do much but I can make a half-decent explosive."''
([[Luca Costa/Dialogue|Luca Costa's dialogue]]) While Luca finds that being Vinny's nephew has its perks, as no one wants to "start shit" with the boss' relative, he also mentions that Vinny does not baby him and expects him to pull around his own weight.Vault 76 dweller: ''"What's it like being related to Vinny?"''
Luca Costa: ''"It's got its perks, no-one wants to start shit with the boss' nephew, y'know? But Vinny's not the coddling type either, I don't get a free pass."''
([[Luca Costa/Dialogue|Luca Costa's dialogue]]) Although he does acknowledge that his uncle Vinny can appear frightening, Luca believes that Vinny is not actually scary; he just seems tough. He even says that Vinny is "actually pretty cool."Luca Costa: ''"Uncle Vin' seems tough. And he is, but he's not scary. He's actually pretty cool."''
([[Luca Costa/Dialogue|Luca Costa's dialogue]]) That said, Luca does still want to avoid Vinny's wrath if at all possible if he screws something up.Luca Costa: ''"Oh man Uncle Vinny is gonna be SO pissed, thanks for nothin'."''
([[Luca Costa/Dialogue|Luca Costa's dialogue]])
'''Note:''' This line is heard if [[Beasts of Burden|Event: Beasts of Burden]] fails. Vinny, for his part, sees his nephew as an occasional nuisance with problems that can only be solved by a "boot up his ass,"Vault 76 dweller: ''"Really? The other members don't need help?"''
[[Vinny Costa]]: ''"Eh, everyone else is fine. {{Tooltip|Only thing that'll fix my nephew Luca's problems is my boot up his ass. Love the kid and all, but there's no talkin' sense to him.|Not a big concern for him}} As for Minerva and the big lug? She's our top performer, no troubles there-- and Tommy's a pro. {{Tooltip|I guess there's Aries, but, uh... I wouldn't ask my worst enemy to talk to that freak longer than they have to.|Side of the mouth}} {{Tooltip|You could always ask him what he's got going on, but, uh... Good luck with that.|But me? no thanks.}}"''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]])Vault 76 dweller: ''"How about the other members?"''
[[Vinny Costa]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Eh, everybody else is doin' all right. With Jo at the helm, we're normally runnin' pretty smooth. We're about back to that now, thanks to you.|Not TOO appreciative}} Granted, my nephew Luca will always be a pain, and Aries will always be a creep, but, uh... Let's see. Ah, right. There's Minerva and Tommy. Hard to pin down, but when I see 'em, they always seem chipper. She's got good deals, too. Make sure you peruse if you bump into her. Oh, and if ya see Tommy Ten-Toes... While I know he can't count that high, tell him he still owes me 50 caps."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) but the two are still family and any rifts between them are part of being related, and will always work themselves out.Vault 76 dweller: ''"She needed help sorting out some family issues. She's good now."''
[[Vinny Costa]]: ''"Well you know what they say, family's everything. You met my nephew? Drives me up the fuckin' wall sometimes, but that's family. Things'll work themselves out."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) One source of conflict between Luca and Vinny is the role that Luca plays at Blue Ridge. Luca struggles to find ways to help out with the company, though he does frequently join the caravans on their various trips. However, Luca has recently found a niche of creating homemade [[explosive]]s to sell. This initially stemmed from a hobby interest in chemistry, but he found that he was bad at making things that did not blow up.Vault 76 dweller: ''"Tell me more about these explosives."''
Luca Costa: ''"Started as a hobby, kept trying chemistry and I was pretty awful at making things that didn't blow up."''
([[Luca Costa/Dialogue|Luca Costa's dialogue]]) Luca markets them as a "multipurpose item" to use against hostiles or even for home renovations and landscaping.Vault 76 dweller: ''"You think people would buy them?"''
Luca Costa: ''"Sure they would! It's a multipurpose item, all sorts of things you can do with explosives. Seal off that molerat nest for good, defend your home, parties, home renovations, landscaping, only limit is what you can think of! Though it'd be good to have buyers who don't turn out to be cultists every once in a while."''
([[Luca Costa/Dialogue|Luca Costa's dialogue]])
'''Note:''' This version of the line is said if the player has previously completed [[Beasts of Burden|Event: Beasts of Burden]]. However, Vinny is greatly concerned about the quality of the product and refuses to officially sell them on Blue Ridge's books. Although Luca insists that his explosives are up to par, Vinny wants to avoid any "mishaps," as accidental detonations would look bad on the business.Vault 76 dweller: ''"Why doesn't Vinny want to sell them?"''
Luca Costa: ''"He's worried about them not being up to par, but they're good quality. Uncle Vinny just doesn't want any, uh, mishaps. Accidental detonations and such. Says it'd look bad on the business. They're as safe as any other explosives. Mostly. Once it's foolproof I'll convince him."''
([[Luca Costa/Dialogue|Luca Costa's dialogue]]) Vinny dismisses them as "homemade cherrybombs,"[[Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries#%5BIntelligence_10+%5D_Recover_Deleted_Entries|Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries; Vinny Costa's terminal, Employee Complaints]] but Luca continues to sell them off the books as he aspires to have Vinny officially distribute his explosives.Luca Costa: ''"Once I get the recipe sorted I'm gonna convince Uncle Vinny to start distributing my explosives. Who doesn't need a bomb every now and then."''
([[Luca Costa/Dialogue|Luca Costa's dialogue]]) As a result of this dispute over the quality of Luca's explosives, Luca has been assigned to the [[Cranberry Bog]]. Although Luca is unnerved by sightings of [[Cultist (Fallout 76)|cultists]] and hostile [[robot]]s in nearby [[Watoga]], Vinny says he will only consider reassignment once Luca stops selling the bombs "under the table." However, Luca is none too dissuaded by his uncle's disapproval, and continues to see himself as a young entrepreneur trying to make a profit, which leads into the [[Fallout 76 events|public event]] [[Beasts of Burden]]. While in the bog, Luca encountered a group of "traders," unaware that they were [[Cult of the Mothman]] members in disguise. Led by [[Adelaide (Cult of the Mothman)|Elder Adelaide]], the cultists tricked Luca by arranging a trade deal with him, upon which they ambushed him and seized his crude bombs, as well as his pack [[Brahmin (Fallout 76)|brahmin]], [[Moona Lisa]].Luca Costa: ''"So listen up... I arranged a meeting with some local traders. They were all like "hey, we wanna buy your bombs." Being the young entrepreneur I am, and a craftsman of the best artisanal bombs around, how could I resist? Anyway, turns out these guys were actually Cultists... They waylaid me and took the goods. I barely got out alive. I'm so SCREWED if Uncle Vinny finds out, so I need you to go get everything back, so I can get back before Uncle Vinny learns what's happened. I'll pay you!"''
([[Luca Costa/Dialogue|Luca Costa's dialogue]])
'''Note:''' This line is heard during [[Beasts of Burden|Event: Beasts of Burden]] after starting the event in Luca's dialogue.[[A blessed gift]] The proceedings of the event Beasts of Burden see the [[Vault 76]] [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|dwellers]] assisting an injured Luca, fighting back against the cultists, retaking the bombs via Moona Lisa and escaping the bog, even as an [[Ogua]] appears to attack.Luca Costa: ''"Hot damn, that was one big-ass turtle. Youse in one piece? But, hey, I did it! Ah, okay, we did it. Just, uh, don't tell Uncle Vinny bout this okay? Here's your reward: I owe you big!"''
([[Luca Costa/Dialogue|Luca Costa's dialogue]])
'''Note:''' This line is heard during [[Beasts of Burden|Event: Beasts of Burden]], after the [[Ogua]] is defeated and the quest ends. Although he initially naively attempts to take credit for the escape, Luca quickly realizes his mistake and says he owes the dwellers, offering them cheers for their help the next time they see each other.Luca Costa: ''"Hey, cheers for all the help with that, uh, 'trade deal'."''
([[Luca Costa/Dialogue|Luca Costa's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |wares = |caps = |events started =[[Beasts of Burden|Event: Beasts of Burden]] |quests involved = |bonus = |other = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Trucker uniform]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== * Luca seems to only appear at [[Big Bend Tunnel east]] in the night and early morning hours, and has dialogue relating to the current in-game time of day, though his exact schedule has not been verified. * In one of his idle lines, Luca will offer to show off and teach some knife tricks.Luca Costa: ''"If you ever need to kill some time I can teach you some cool knife tricks, just don't slice yourself. Hurts like a motherfucker."''

PlayerAllyFaction |class =BoSSoldierClass |combat style= |CK race =HumanRace |voice type =MOON_Herd_NPCF_Vera |actor =[[Natasha Chandel]] |designer =[[Reese Mills]] |dialogue =[[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue]] |edid =MOON_Herd_Vera |formid ={{ID|006906a4}} |refid ={{ID|006906a9}} }} {{Quotation|You know it's a shame about the Ferris wheel at the [[Tyler County Fairgrounds|Tyler County Fair]], my Daddy said he proposed to my Momma on it.|sound=Vera Thornberg 0069f39a_1.ogg}} '''Vera Thornberg''' is a general goods [[Fallout 76 vendors|merchant]] for the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] {{in|FO76OB}}. She is found at the [[Middle Mountain Pitstop]] in [[Appalachia]], and acts as the announcer and questgiver during [[Safe and Sound|Event: Safe and Sound]]. ==Background== The daughter of a pre-War trucker who worked for [[Joanna Mayfield]], Vera is a newly minted caravan worker, assigned to take care of the Middle Mountain Pitstop by [[Vinny Costa]].Vault 76 dweller: "''Who are you?"''
Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Name's Vera. Joined Blue Ridge a while back, now takin' care of the Brahmin here and runnin' the store. Oh and that's Clyde, he runs the bar.|Player asked who she was. She introduces herself and Clyde.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) While inexperienced, she is responsible for a vital part of Blue Ridge's operations in Appalachia, raising brahmin for use on the caravan trail, in addition to running the general store and looking after the stop.Vault 76 dweller: "''What kind of stuff goes on around here?"''
Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|We sell general goods, plus some extras like fresh milk, on account of rasin' the Blue Ridge Caravan Brahmin here.|Player asked what there is to do around here. She mentions her store and the local Brahmin.}} {{tooltip|Besides the shop, Clyde sells drinks over at our bar the Boozin Brahmin, and you can always take a load off at the Sleep Stop if ya get tired.|Player asked what there is to do around here. She mentions the bar and bed house.}} {{tooltip|Just mind yourself outside, had some critters attack the place recently, hence the repairs goin' on.|Player asked what there is to do around here. She mentions the damage on the grounds are due to some attacks by local creatures.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) She has a limited knowledge of the pre-War world, despite her father's stories, including a lack of clarity on what bed and breakfast means - although it also leads her to unorthodox solutions, such as creating [[ice cream]] by freezing [[brahmin milk]] with cryolators. She actually got the job through her father's connection to Joanna,Vault 76 dweller: "''So tell me about yourself."''
Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Who, me? Oh umm, not much to say really. Came from a bit back out west. My Daddy worked for Blue Ridge, drivin' trucks for Joanna.|Player asks about her. She mentions where she came from, her father having ties with Joanna got her the job.}} {{tooltip|Well, before the bombs I mean, when roads were in one piece and trucks weren't just explosive target practice.|Player asks about her. She expands on her father being a trucker before the bombs.}} {{tooltip|Bein' a rookie, Vinny set me up looking after the Brahmin here. Guess he doesn't think I'm ready to travel as a caravanner yet.|Player asks about her. She mentions her work, though she isn’t exactly thrilled with the job.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) and her placement at the pitstop was a favor to Joanna from Vinny.Vault 76 dweller: "''What can you tell me about Vera?"''
Vinny Costa: "''{{tooltip|She's our rookie. Set her up with an easy gig up at the Middle Mountain Pitstop as a favour to Joanna.|Asked about Vera. Exposition on the location.}} {{tooltip|Hearin' she has her head in the clouds lately, makin' all sorts of silly mistakes. Need someone to go snap her out of it.|Asked about Vera. Exposition on the problem.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) She found the job exciting initially, as she and Clyde set up the pitstop, burying the dead and setting up the bar, store, and the rest stop. She considered it a new start,[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries]], A New Start! and soon kept quite busy with caring for the brahmin and serving travelers and fellow workers, including [[Luca Costa]], Vinny's nephew, and [[Grahm]].[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries]], Busy Days Eventually, Vera settled into a routine, with her typical workday focusing on running the general stare and looking after the brahmin at the Pitstop, including milking them every morning.Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Hey early bird. Lucky you, got some freshly made Brahmin milk for sale. Why not try some to start the day?|Player entered her shop very early in the morning and walked up to her. She has freshly milked the Brahmin.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) However, it left little time for anything else,Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Kinda tough both runnin' the store and carin' for the cattle. *Sighs* Don't leave much time for anythin' else.|She is a little overworked and expresses that.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) and eventually, mistakes started to pop upVault 76 dweller: "''Any idea what's affecting her work ethic?"''
Vinny Costa: "''No clue. Was doin' a good enough job, but after a while she just kept makin' dumb mistakes, like she's gettin' distracted by somethin'."''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) ranging from relatively mild splashing of [[milk]] across her [[terminal]] to losing track of her herd or dumping the day's earnings into the outhouse.Vault 76 dweller: "''[Lie] Vinny knows about all the mistakes you made, so he sent me."''
Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Huh? He couldn't know about the time I lost the cattle, or when I got milk in the terminal? Not the day's earnings down the outhouse?|Player lied saying Vinny knows about all the mistakes they have been making. She panics and lists all the mistakes.}} {{tooltip|Clyde said he wouldn't tell anybody about that...|Player lied saying Vinny knows about all the mistakes they have been making. Clyde was the only one that knew, so she assumes he told him.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) The reason for her distraction is simple: she assumed that being a caravan worker would have involved traveling, rather than working the pitstop,Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Job hasn't turned out the way I thought it would. *Sighs* See the world they said...|Player has not completed her quest to solve her feeling stuck at the pitstop, unable to travel and get photos of her travels.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) in a seemingly endless loop of chores.Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|*Groans* Mornin' chores never get any easier.|It’s morning, and she is groaning about the chores she has to do as the Brahmin carer.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) As she grew up on her father's stories about being a trucker, listening to his sage advice (e.g. "It ain't about the destination, but the pitstops along the way.")Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|What did Daddy used to say? It ain't about the destination, but the pitstops along the way. Didn't say nothin' about getting stuck at one though...|Thinking aloud about a words of sage advice her father gave her. However, she feels she is stuck here at this Pitstop and can’t travel.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) and all-night hauling on the road, she feels stuckVera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|*Yawns* I can barely keep my eyes open. Not sure how Daddy pulled those all-nighters on the road.|It’s late at night and she is tired. She reminisces about her dad being a pre-war trucker.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) and a disappointment to her father. She wanted to share her travels with him, attaching photos of the places she visited across Appalachia, and this wanderlust has been distracting her, resulting in mistakes.Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Ya see, the problem is I've been fixin' to reply to my Daddy's last letter about my travels around Appalachia.|She expands on her distraction. She wants to send a letter back to her father, but needs photos showing she traveled.}} {{tooltip|But I've been stuck mindin' the shop instead of travellin' like he did, which is the whole reason I joined up, ya know.|She expands on her distraction. She got stuck at the Pitstop and never got to travel.}} {{tooltip|Been puttin' off replyin' to his last letter for some time now because I have no pictures of my travels to send back.|She expands on her distraction. She lacks the pictures to reply to her father’s letter, not wanting him to know she hasn’t traveled.}} {{tooltip|Oh hey, you get around a lot, right? Any chance you'd be willin' to take a few pictures for me?|She expands on her distraction. She figures the player gets around and could get the photos for her.}} {{tooltip|Would take a load off my mind if I could reply to this letter showin' him I actually get around out here.|She expands on her distraction. She expresses getting those pictures and replying to that letter will help her focus.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) Vinny has noticed the change and would like someone to fix the issue promptly, without violence, as his hide is on the line with Joanna if anything happens to Vera.Vault 76 dweller: "''Want me to rattle her cage a little? Make her see sense?"''
Vinny Costa: "''{{tooltip|While I appreciate the initiative *laughs*, Joanna would have my hide. Just go see what's makin' her mind wander and help put a stop to it.|Player asked if they should rattle her cage, but he knows he will get Joanna on his back if this is handled that way, so just asks you to go and help}}"''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) Between her father eagerly waiting to hear about her travels and the pitstop, she is very distracted. The situation is further complicated by the fact that the brahmin at the pitstop attract various predators[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries]], What Should I Do? and Vinny rebuffed Vera's suggestion to hire more guards for the pitstop or turning the brahmin into battle cattle with armor.[[Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries#Deleted Entries|Big Bend Tunnel terminal entries; Vinny Costa's terminal, Deleted Entries]] To combat this, [[Aries]] and Clyde have improvised a repeller system that uses soundwaves largely outside the range of human hearing to keep the animals at bay. However, the system malfunctions sometimes and attracts fauna, rather than repelling it.Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Sure hope these repeller doohickies do the trick for keepin' us safe. Specially after the last few incidents.|The repellers work, but they also break and attract creatures sometimes. She is voicing her worries aloud.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) As a result, the [[Vault 76 dweller]]s have to lend a hand every now and then to keep the wildlife contained.[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries]], Stupid Repellers! If they do not, Vera and Clyde evacuate the Pitstop and return with the herd to [[Big Bend Tunnel]], with Vinny none too pleased with the turn of events.Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Guess we're gonna have to head back to Big Bend for help Clyde. *Sighs* Vinny isn't gonna like this.|They stood around waiting for help that never came, so they gave up and on the pitstop and now will return to their base. Worried about boss though.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) ===Relationships=== Vera's most important relationship is with her father. She promised him that she would be traveling and would visit his old trucker route, making the photos particularly important for Vera.Vault 76 dweller: "''Do I look like a tourist? Just do your job right."''
Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|S-sorry. I'm trying my best, but I just can't seem to focus with this on my mind.|Player rebukes her as a tourist, and she apologises but makes it clear she won’t be able to focus till her problem is solved.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]])Vault 76 dweller: "''Sure, I'll get those photos for you."''
Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Oh, you're sweeter than a Nuka-Cola. I'll mark the locations on your map.|Player agreed to get the photos. She thanks the player and marks the locations.}} {{tooltip|A nice picture of a sign, or maybe a landmark would be great. Thanks again!|Player agreed to get the photos. She specifies a landmark or sign.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) They are not just some random landmarks: she specifically planned to visit stops from her father's pre-War trucker route and cheer him up, since he gave up traveling after her mother passed. Some are tied to her mother's memory, such as the [[Cow Spots Creamery]] (where her father kept buying ice cream just to meet her mother, despite him having unspecified "dairy problems")Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|My Daddy used to get a scoop at the creamery every time he was passin' through just to meet my Momma. Romantic considerin' his err... dairy problems.|As the player approaches, Vera reminisces about the photos they gave her on her quest. Photo of a icecream creamery where her father met her mother.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) or the [[Tyler County Fairgrounds]], where he proposed to her, atop the [[Ferris wheel (Fallout 76)|Ferris wheel]].Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|You know it's a shame about the Ferris wheel at the Tyler County Fair, my Daddy said he proposed to my Momma on it.|As the player approaches, Vera reminisces about the photos they gave her on her quest. Photo of a broken Ferris wheel.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) Others, like [[Mountainside Bed & Breakfast]], are just pleasant memories of the trucking.Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Been thinkin' about Daddy's Mountainside Bed and Breakfast pitstop. Wonder if the same folks still run it, or if it changed hands.|As the player approaches, Vera reminisces about the photos they gave her on her quest. Photo of a bed and breakfast motel.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) As such, photos would both provs that she traveled and help her father deal with the grief of losing his wife.Vault 76 dweller: "''Why did you want these photos again?"''
Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|I want to show my Daddy what his old trucker pitstops look like now after the bombs dropped.|Player asks why she wants the pictures again while tasked to get them. Reminder on she wants to show him his old pitstops after the bombs dropped.}} {{tooltip|He hasn't the mind to travel since Momma passed, so I want to send these back to cheer him up. And... to show I travelled like I said I would.|Player asks why she wants the pictures again while tasked to get them. Reminder on her wanting to cheer him up, and show she traveled.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) At the same time, Vera cannot just up and leave. She is a worker, not a fighter, but more importantly, she feels a sense of loyalty towards Joanna Mayfield for setting her up with the job, and doesn't want to disappoint her.Vault 76 dweller: "''What's so important about getting these photos?"''
Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Well I was plannin' on visiting the pitstops of my Daddy's old trucker route from before the bombs dropped.|Player asked why she wants the photos. She wanted to stop by her father’s old trucker pitstops from before the war.]}} {{tooltip|I know seeing those old places would just warm his heart, specially since he hasn't had a mind to travel since Momma passed.|Player asked why she wants the photos. She wants to use the photos to cheer up her father since he does not travel since Vera' mother died.}} {{tooltip|*Sighs* But, I can't just abandon my post after Joanna went to all the trouble getting it for me. Plus I'm not sure if I'd last one minute out there alone.|Player asked why she wants the photos. She does not want to abandon her job out of loyalty to Joanna, and she is no fighter, scared of creatures.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) She voiced her concerns to Vinny before, but he has not really given it any mind.Vault 76 dweller: "''Vera wanted some photos to send back to her father. I got them for her."''
Vinny Costa: "''{{tooltip|Right, I remember her sayin' somethin' like that. She musta felt cooped up. Huh. Appreciate ya gettin' her mind off it.|Player tells Vinny about what they did for Vera, and he remembers hearing her concerns a while back, then thanks the player for sorting the problem.}}"''
([[Vinny Costa/Dialogue|Vinny Costa's dialogue]]) Vera is also close with [[Clyde]], her co-worker, enough to realize that he is soft-hearted under his toughened exterior.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Clyde doesn't talk much, does he?"''
Vera Thornberg: ''"Clyde? Don't take offence to the silent treatment. Is more account on him losin' his tongue. Never got a clear answer about what happened. Rumour is he had a bad run in with raiders. Others reckon he just lost it to a bad Radscorpion stew. Anyways, he runs security at the Pitstop. A big softy really once he gets to know ya. Hear he used to work for Vinny back in the day."''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) However, despite the familiarity, Clyde still refuses to carry a notepad to communicate (Vera started thinking that he might be wise, given that wastelanders at large might not be able to read him)Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|I keep tellin' him, Clyde, if ya carry a note pad, everyone would understand ya. He just shrugs and gives me that look. He's probably right though, who can read now days?|Clyde is mute. She thinks aloud here at her frustration with him not using a notepad like she asked.}}''"
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) or agree to her suggestions of escorting her to the pitstops across Appalachia.[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries#I Made Up My Mind|Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries; General store terminal, I Made Up My Mind]] Finally, Vera is close with the brahmin she looks after. While she was still alive, her mother taught her a number of things about the brahmin, including her view that each head is its own individual. As such, she continues the tradition by giving each a pair of names, passing them to new brahmin whenever they are replaced by Blue Ridge.Vault 76 dweller: "''[Charisma 4+] So what's the deal with the Brahmin having two names?"''
Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Well, okay.|A charming player asks about the Brahmins with two names. A name per head.}} {{tooltip|Now my momma always said each Brahmin head was it's own special self, so of course I had to give each two names.|A charming player asks about the Brahmins with two names. She gave them double names because her mother taught her each head is their own individual.}} {{tooltip|Had fun pickin' their monikers. And of course once one "moos" on, seemed easier just lettin' the new one take over the mantle.|A charming player asks about the Brahmins with two names. She mentions she just passes on the names to the replacement Brahmin.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) The replacement takes place once the brahmin are fully raised by Vera, with her jokingly calling the moment "graduation" and passing the name to new calves when the grown brahmin are taken onto the caravan trail.Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Another Brahmin graduating soon. I'm so proud.|Thinking aloud. A Brahmin is almost fully raised, which means she will switch them out soon with another for "graduating", passing the names on.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) She does not mind taking care of the cattle (although she hates the "muck"), but would prefer to be on the caravan trail.Vault 76 dweller: "''What's caring for Brahmin like?"''
Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|*Sighs* It's not caravannin', but it's not all that bad. Cattle can be pretty cute, just gotta get used to early mornin' chores. Not a fan of the muck though.|She hints she’d rather be a caravanner, but says it’s not all that bad.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |wares =General goods |caps =yes |events started =[[Safe and Sound|Event: Safe and Sound]] |quests involved =[[Costa Business: Vera]] |bonus = |other = }} ===Quests=== * [[Safe and Sound|Event: Safe and Sound]]: Vera's pitstop comes under attack by ornery wildlife due to a malfunction of the repeller system and she needs the Vault dwellers' aid to clear the outpost. A different version of the event occurs if it has failed before on the server, where the first stage focuses on clearing the pitstop and retaking it. * [[Costa Business: Vera]]: Vera is distracted by the need to give her father a reply concerning her travels across Appalachia. She wants to include some photographs with her response. The three locations to photograph with the [[ProSnap Deluxe camera]] are the [[Mountainside Bed & Breakfast]], [[Cow Spots Creamery]] and the [[Ferris wheel (Fallout 76)|Ferris wheel]] at [[Tyler County Fairgrounds]]. **Once the player returns, they need to help Vera resolve her quandary:Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Oh these look swell! Not exactly how I imagined them, a bit more run down, but as to be expect I suppose...|She studies the pictures the player handed over.}} {{tooltip|*Sighs* Looking at these now, it dawns on me that I probably shouldn't be sending these back if I didn't take them.|She has a moral dilemma where she realises that would be lying if she sends these pictures}}"''
Vault 76 dweller: "''You sure? He'd probably love to see his old pitstops."''
Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|You're right, but I don't know what I should tell him. I mean it's cheatin' ain't it? I never went there.|During her moral dilemma the player tries to convince her that her father would still like to see the pictures regardless who took them.}}"''
Vault 76 dweller: "''It's not cheating. It's just a preview of places you're planning to visit."''
Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Yeah, you're right. He'd appreciate seeing them, and I can let him know I still plan to visit them, eventually.|The player convinces her she can write back back to her father saying the pictures are just a preview of places she plans to visit, telling the truth}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]]) whether to send the photos and lie that she has been traveling, tell the truth and burn the photos, or send them anyway and explain that they are previews of her travel. While the decision has no gameplay impact, it does affect how Vera feels, ranging from giving up entirely,[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries]], I Give Up... guilt over lying to her father,[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries]], Finally Sent The Letter realizing that the photos were about helping him, not her,[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries]], Sent The Letter Finally!!! to feeling motivated to visit these locations if she admits the truth, but keeps the photos as a memento.[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries]], Sent The Letter Finally! In this case, she will actually gather enough courage to ask for time off and get Clyde to escort her. Her father supports her either way.Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Uhuh, got a reply too. He wrote about how proud he was of me for travellin' out there. *Sighs* I feel like such a big coward and fraud for lyin'...|When asked, Vera feels down about lying to her father, because she got a letter where she praised her highly, leaving her feeling guilty.}}"''
([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]])Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Yup, he replied too. Reassurin' me that I don't need to travel. ([[Vera Thornberg/Dialogue|Vera Thornberg's dialogue]])Vera Thornberg: "''{{tooltip|Yeah, and he replied saying not to worry about travellin' and to make the most of this place. *Sighs* Maybe he's right, I guess I'm not cut out for it.|When asked, Vera feels down because her father convinced her to not worry about travelling.}}"''

{{Infobox character |games =FO76 |image =Fo76_Auto-miner_DU-K3.png |race =[[Protectron (Fallout 76)|Protectron]] |sex = |affiliation =[[Hornwright Industrial]] |role =Miner |location =[[Abandoned mine site Kittery]] |quests =[[Lode Baring]] |alignment = |level =26 |derived =[[Hit Points]]: 150
[[Action Points]]: 10 |special ={{SPECIAL|0,7,0,0,0,0,0}} |class =Protectron |combat style=Default |CK race =RobotRace |factions =MTR08_AutoMinerFaction |confidence =Foolhardy |assistance =Helps Allies |aggression =Unaggressive |actor =[[Wes Johnson]] |dialogue =[[Auto-Miner/Dialogue]] |edid =Lvl_MTR08_Mine02_AutoMiner_Duke |formid ={{ID|003298f1}} |refid ={{ID|0038f0fe}} }} '''Auto-Miner DU-K3''' (codenamed '''Duke''') is a [[Protectron (Fallout 76)|Protectron]] operating in the [[abandoned mine site Kittery]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== [[Hornwright Industrial]] partnered with [[Atomic Mining Services]] to produce the Auto-Miner, in an effort to completely automate their mining operations while retaining only executive staff. The resulting loss of jobs led to large scale union action and attacks by Hornwright's previous human workforce against Auto-Miner operated mines and Hornwright-affiliated sites. In response to the Auto-Miner, and in an attempt to show the benefits of a human workforce, [[Garrahan Mining Company|Garrahan Mining]] funded the development of the [[excavator power armor]] and challenged Hornwright in a [[Charleston Herald - Man vs. Machine|heavily advertised contest]], which [[Charleston Herald - Hornwright Wins!|Hornwright won]] by 1.87 tons of ore. Garrahan was financially ruined by this loss, and desperation led to Garrahan firing some of its miners and replacing them with Auto-Miners. The laid-off miners then protested and even rioted, similarly to the Hornwright miner riots. Some Auto-Miners can be found outside of the [[Garrahan Mining headquarters]]. DU-K3 (Duke) is one of the Auto-Miners that needs to be repaired during the quest [[Lode Baring]]. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Lode Baring]] }} ==Appearances== Auto-Miner DU-K3 appears only {{In|FO76}}. {{Navbox robots}} [[Category:Fallout 76 robots and computers]] [[Category:Protectron characters]] [[ru:Автошахтёр DU-K3]]

I hope you don't get too lonely here all by yourself. Goodbye, MAIA.|sound=Barbara Elizabeth 003e62ad_1.ogg}} '''Barbara Elizabeth''' was the last pre-[[Great War|War]] mayor of the city of [[Watoga]]. Her corpse is present in the mayor's office in the [[Watoga Municipal Center]]. With her demise, Watoga finally succumbed to the lawlessness of the wasteland and the actions of the [[Scott Turner|Saboteur]]. ==Background== Watoga had an unusual way of governance, appointing random citizens to the office of mayor for an undefined period of time. Barbara Elizabeth served as the city's 134th and last mayor appointed before the Great War. A music teacher before her appointment, Elizabeth was faced with the evacuation of Watoga's citizens following both the saboteur's actions and the devastation of the Great War. She did all she could, but noted that she simply wasn't cut out for the task of dealing with such chaos, describing Watoga as a "dead city" with "people literally running around on fire" in her terminal entries.[[Watoga Municipal Center terminal entries#Mayor for a Day|Watoga Municipal Center terminal entries; Mayor's terminal, Mayor for a Day]] Her terminal entries reveal she tried to locate the saboteur to negotiate with them, but was severely injured during her search. Although she managed to make it back to her office and have one final conversation with [[MAIA]], she eventually succumbed to these injuries and died. As a precaution before her search, she issued an executive order for the automated mayoral selection process to appoint anyone who entered her office as a "[[Mayor for a Day]]" to finish her job if she failed, and ordered MAIA to reward whoever took up her mantle with the contents of a supply cache as a reward for doing so. The cache contains eight [[Stimpak (Fallout 76)|stimpaks]], three [[Blood pack (Fallout 76)|blood packs]], and thirteen [[Pre-War money (Fallout 76)|pre-War money]]. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Patched suit (Fallout 76)|Patched suit]] |weapon = |otheritem =Random chems
[[Pre-War money (Fallout 76)|Pre-War money]] |ondeath = }} ===Quests=== [[Mayor for a Day]]: She posthumously tasks the player character to assume the office of mayor of Watoga for one day and to locate and deal with the saboteur, offering them her supply cache as a reward. ==Appearances== Barbara Elizabeth appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==References== {{references}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Watoga characters]] [[Category:Pre-War politicians]] [[ru:Элизабет Барбара]]

Dr. '''Blake Saunders''' was a scientist and researcher in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
Dr. Saunders conducted research on a [[Radiation|radioactive]] crater located halfway between [[the Freak Show]] and the [[monorail elevator]] in the [[Savage Divide]]. He recorded the amount of rads found in the area's environment over a week-long period. He tore his [[Hazmat suit (Fallout 76)|hazmat suit]] on February 20, causing the radiation to seep into his body and, two days later, started vomiting blood. Slowly realizing his fate, Blake hoped that his partner [[Robert (mentioned)|Robbie]] would have better luck than he did. By February 23, the day he saw a [[Yao guai (Fallout 76)|bear]] in the wilderness, Blake accepted that he would soon die, and resolved to see one last sunrise. His [[Skeleton (Fallout 76)|skeleton]] still sits outside of the crater.<ref>[[Research note (Fallout 76)|Research note]]</ref>

==Appearances==
Blake Saunders' skeleton appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''.

'''Chally the moo-moo''' is a [[Brahmin (Fallout 76)|pack brahmin]] that travels with [[Grahm]] throughout [[Appalachia]]<!-- in [[Timeline#2102|2102]]-->.

==Background==
Chally ''(pronounced like "Charlie" and "Wally")''<ref>[[Grahm/Dialogue|Grahm's dialogue]]: script notes</ref> the moo-moo travels with Grahm, a [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|super mutant]] who is extremely affectionate towards him.<ref>[[Grahm/Dialogue#27|Grahm's dialogue]] refers to Chally with male pronouns</ref>

From time to time, Grahm will make a remark that one of them has a "pile" nearby, though he quickly remembers that it was actually "not a good stuff pile." He will sometimes also mention that some [[greens]] are needed for Chally.

It is located in the basement of [[Riverside Manor]], located behind a secret door. ==Background== Cryptos is a modified [[RobCo Industries]] computer mainframe originally built by RobCo for a canceled [[Defense Intelligence Agency]] project before being sold to [[Frederick Rivers]]. Frederick modified it to optimize martial arts training for his wife [[Shannon Rivers]], who was preparing to portray the hero [[Mistress of Mystery]] in the upcoming [[Silver Shroud]] television series. After the [[Great War]], the Rivers founded the [[Order of Mysteries]]. Fredrick and two members reprogrammed Cryptos to automate functions for the Order. Cryptos can automate the registration of initiates, mentor and mission assignments, and promotions. It was also interfaced with an automated fabricator to authorize and log the fabrication of order equipment. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |ghost = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Initiate of Mysteries]] * [[Novice of Mysteries]] * [[Seeker of Mysteries]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Behind the scenes== The Greek root word ''kryptos'' means "hidden" or "mysterious." ==Appearances== Cryptos appears only {{In|FO76}}. {{Navbox robots}} [[Category:Fallout 76 robots and computers]] [[ru:КРИПТОС]]

'''Ford''' is a deceased man in [[Appalachia]] whose corpse is found during the random encounter [[Dead and Dismembered]].

==Background==
At one point, Ford was made a deputy by [[Boomer (Fallout 76)|Boomer]], a malfunctioning robot at the [[Southern Belle Motel]]. Ford was tasked with finding and turning in bombs but decided to keep them for himself instead. He tried to disarm the bombs on his own but detonated one while doing so, killing himself in the process.<ref>[[Ford's holotape]]: ''"Found some ridiculous robot in Berkeley Springs that upgraded me to a deputy. Jokes on him, I guess. Like I'm going to go grab these bombs and turn them in like some honorable citizen. I'm keeping these babies for myself. Wiring's a bit gunked up, but I think I can make them work. Just going to disarm this switch here to make sure it doesn't -- *explosion*"''</ref>

A specialized Mister Handy unit, Sweetwater was created for receiving visitors, working in a gift shop and for the brewing of a [[Sweetwater Special Blend|special blend of tea]] with an exquisite taste and delicate aroma. In communicating with the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]], Sweetwater will declare that he lacks a special ingredient for tea - [[honey]]. Be sure to donate to my campaign now. Hahaha... Seriously.|sound=Grafton mayor 00143523_1.ogg}} The '''Grafton mayor''' is an [[Computer#Artificial intelligence|AI]] in [[Appalachia]]. He is of a similar design to [[MAIA]]. ==Background== The former computerized assistant to the actual mayor of Grafton, the Grafton mayor elected himself to the position after the [[Great War]] in a 1-0 vote, as the previous mayor "stopped showing up to work."Grafton mayor: ''"{{tooltip|I used to be the mayor's assistant, but when he stopped showing up for work, I ran for office.|Proud of his step up in the world.}} {{tooltip|I'm eminently qualified and the town unanimously elected me, one to zero.|proud of his accomplishment}} {{tooltip|Unfortunately, you are a wee bit early for tourist season. |falsely apologetic}} {{tooltip|But this is your lucky day. Help us get ready for the upcoming flood of eager tourists, and I'll knock a whole 5% off the cost of all attractions!|TV game show announcer. persuading the player that this horrible deal is actually a wonderful one}} {{tooltip|We have four major attractions around here, Wavy Willard's, the Clarksburg Shooting Range, Prickett's Fort, and the Black Bear hunting lodge.|upbeat, proud, TV game show announcer}} {{tooltip|Go out there and get each of them ready. I'll wait here. Because I don't have legs. And I can't move.|He's apologetic rather than sad that he doesn't have legs. He just can't help himself from trying to explain it further. Pause between each line.}}"''
([[Grafton mayor/Dialogue|Grafton mayor's dialogue]]) He is the voice of [[WGRF Grafton]] and can be heard broadcasting during various [[Fallout 76 quests#Daily quests|daily quests]] such as [[Grafton Day]]. Grafton's last human mayor, [[Gloria McNamara]], noted the computer had become increasingly erratic before the war, asking for a cup of coffee before it would produce reports, "even though it doesn't have a mouth!"[[Grafton terminal entries#Work order|Grafton terminal entries; Grafton mayor's terminal, Work order]] The Grafton Mayor and his servant robots are unaware of the occurrence of the Great War. He is fervently obsessed with keeping Grafton's traditions and tourism industry intact and tasks the player character to perform several maintenance tasks in the quest [[Bureau of Tourism]], in anticipation of a large number of tourists in the near future, despite most of humanity having been wiped out. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = * [[Bureau of Tourism]] * [[Buried with Honor]] * [[Dogwood Die Off]] * [[Grafton Day]] * [[Pass the Buck]] * [[Protest March]] * [[Swarm of Suitors]] |quests involved = }} ==Notes== * The Grafton mayor, as a mayoral assistant, is a MAIA (Mayoral Artificially Intelligent Assistant), sharing the same model as the MAIA in [[Watoga]]. * Despite Gloria McNamara being the last human mayor of Grafton, in dialogue the Grafton mayor refers to their preceding mayor as male. ==Appearances== The Grafton mayor appears {{In|FO76}}, introduced in the ''[[Wastelanders]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox AI}} [[Category:Fallout 76 robots and computers]] [[Category:Computer characters]] [[ru:Мэр Графтона]] [[uk:Мер Графтона]] [[zh:Grafton mayor]]

Guaranteed.|sound=Grahm 002ba3cd_1.ogg}} '''Grahm''' is a friendly [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|super mutant]] [[Fallout 76 vendors|merchant]] and chef living in [[Appalachia]] with his [[Brahmin (Fallout 76)|pack brahmin]] companion, [[Chally the moo-moo]]. ==Background== Little is known of Grahm's history prior to 2102, other than what minute information he offers in his dialogue. He mentions someone he refers to as "Smarty," whose advice guided Grahm into becoming a merchant.Grahm: ''"Smarty say once, "Murder is just okay. Trades? So good. Things break if you just take." Think about it."''
([[Grahm/Dialogue|Grahm's dialogue]])Grahm: ''"Smarty said once, "Trade better than kills. Easy. Live to trade again." Think about it."''
([[Grahm/Dialogue|Grahm's dialogue]]) By 2102, Grahm would be one of, if not the only, remaining live humanoids that was both sapient and friendly towards humans in Appalachia. As [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Dwellers]] of Vault 76 re-entered the world and swept into [[Appalachia]], Grahm found much enjoyment in trading with them. Grahm travels with 'Chally the moo-moo' (''rhymes with "alley"'') and considers trading to be a game with the brahmin.Grahm: ''"Moo-moo, you need good name. You remind me of... I dunno. Something. Someone. Huh. I like you, moo-moo. {{Tooltip|Gonna call you Chally. Quiet, you follow me. You a good friend. Carry my trades. Never go away, Chally. Me and you, always.|Trying to say "Charlie" but can't quite. "Chally" rhymes with "Wally"}} Chally and Grahm, Grahm and Chally. Good friends on the road."''
([[Grahm/Dialogue|Grahm's dialogue]]) He puts a great deal of personal responsibility into the overall wellbeing of Chally and will frequently engage in one-sided conversation with her on their travels. A long time ago during a warm day, Grahm used to spend time with his friends and cook meat. Since then, he has felt alone, remembering the old days. Due to that, Grahm decided to cook meat again for his new friends he had made across [[Appalachia]].Grahm: ''"Grahm remember time, long ago. Weather get hot, go outside, cook meat. Delicious meat. Share with friends. Friends love meat and Grahm love friends. Grahm miss that. So Grahm start Meat Week. Together we meat-cook, we meat eat, we meat-share. Humans are Grahm's friends, we meat eat together. But no eat human meat. Grahm is good. Grahm don't do that."''
([[Grahm/Dialogue|Grahm's dialogue]]) According to Grahm, the first Meat Week was on a sunny day that made the super mutant want to spend time outside and cook. Grahm began to have more and more of these "meat days" and wanted to come up with a name for them. Eventually, after tossing out "Meat Many Days," he decided on "[[Grahm's Meat-Cook|Meat Week]]."Grahm: ''"Grahm tell humans story of first Meat Week. Sunny weather make Grahm want cook meat good. So Grahm do. Grahm have many meat days. Want to name it. Try "Meat Many Days." No, bad words. So Grahm think "Many days... Day... Week... Meat... Week. Grahm do Meat Week! Wahaha! That great day. Like now. Now great day. Great Meat Week."''
([[Grahm/Dialogue|Grahm's dialogue]]) Sometime after [[Reclamation Day]], Grahm and Chally hosted their "Meat Week" event close to Vault 76, with an express invitation toward the Vault Dwellers. Here, Grahm would prepare a grand cookout, with Dwellers assisting him in his grilling, in exchange for various prizes he'd collected through trading in the past year. As of 2103, Grahm has become acquainted with many of the newly-arrived people in Appalachia, such as [[Ayla]] and [[Sofia Daguerre]].Grahm: ''"Hey. Hey you. You different than the other squishies. You seem fresh. Not stinky. How so not stinky?"''
[[Sofia Daguerre]]: ''"Oh, uh, well. Okay. Thanks? It's probably because I haven't been irradiated and soaked with all the despair yet. No doubt I'll probably start... stinking... soon though. Being in space kept me safe from a lot of things for a while."''
Grahm: ''"SPACE?! You're from... the MOON?! Or... the SUN?! Or... the little TWINKLES?!"''
Sofia Daguerre: ''"{{Tooltip|The Space Station, yes, but... before it crashed. All that is in the past though --|Interrupted}}"''
Grahm: ''"Can you take Chally to Space? Chally want to fly someday. Grahm okay with the ground. But Chally have dreams."''
Sofia Daguerre: ''"Uh... I haven't been able to get in touch with the USSA ---"''
Grahm: ''"What do Space people eat? You eat meat? Space meat?! MOON MEAT?"''
Sofia Daguerre: ''"{{Tooltip|Moon... meat? No. I eat grains, plants, mushrooms... I don't eat meat. Wait... do you think the moon is made of meat?|Interrupted}}"''
Grahm: ''"Oh! Greenies. Like Chally. SEE? Chally is ready for SPACE! Chally is going to the MOON!"''
Sofia Daguerre: ''"{{Tooltip|Er... well. I doubt that we could find a helmet ---|Interrupted}}"''
Grahm: ''"Chally isn't Moo-Moo for long! Soon Chally is MOON-MOON!"''
Sofia Daguerre: ''"{{Tooltip|Why not? Dream big or don't dream at all... um. I gotta get back to... literally anything else now.|Interrupted}}"''
([[Grahm/Dialogue|Grahm]] and [[Sofia Daguerre/Dialogue|Sofia Daguerre's dialogue]]) {{Inline quote|sound=Astronaut_Grahm_Chally_Chat.ogg}} He is fond of stopping by the new farms and settlements that have sprung up, likely due to the new business opportunities they bring.[[Ayla's plans]] His business is well-known around Appalachia, mostly for the novelty of a super mutant who sells goods, with even the scavengers of [[Emmett Mountain disposal site]] having heard of tales of the friendly super mutant trader.[[Marion Copeland]]: ''"I heard there's a Super Mutant in Appalachia who's all about business. Now there's a guy with his priorities straight."''
([[Marion Copeland/Dialogue|Marion Copeland's dialogue]]) [[Maul]], another super mutant, also knows Grahm.[[Maul]]: ''"Maul know Grahm. He have pet too, and not eat. Maul like this. Not every food goes in stomach."''

He will then either head down the road to the southeast, or up the road towards [[Monongah]]. You can tell if a server is freshly created by either looking at the time in the [[Pip-Boy 2000 Mark VI]]'s Data tab, with it being close to 11:00 A.M. on a new server; or, while loading into a server, the message "Building World" will appear for a fresh server. ==Notes== * Grahm takes damage from enemies, and can be downed, but he will never die and quickly recovers from an attack. Grahm will not respond to attacks from player characters, but, he will fight enemies that are present along his route, which can be used to the player character's benefit by leading enemies toward Grahm. * At night, Grahm will eventually stop moving. * When Grahm is near [[Hillfolk Hotdogs]], he can say that this place is familiar, the meat he smells is familiar, and meat is where the home is. * [[Julie (Wastelanders)|Julie]] of [[Appalachia Radio]] has been in contact with Grahm, who has repeatedly asked for songs about meat, with "[[Butcher Pete (Part 1)|Butcher Pete]]" being the closest one she can find.[[Julie (Wastelanders)|Julie]]: ''"I'm told there's a certain traveling merchant out there who really, really loves meat. He's asked for songs about it and this is about as close as I can get. Enjoy! "Butcher Pete": how much should we read into this song? You make the call! You know him, you love him: here's Roy Brown, with "Butcher Pete". I'm sorry, what's that? It's a metaphor? Ohh, you don't say!"''
([[Julie.txt|Julie's dialogue]]) * [[Torr Buckner]] in ''[[Fallout 2]]'' also referred to brahmin as "moo-moos." ==Appearances== Grahm appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==Behind the scenes== * Three different voice actors have performed the role of Grahm, including [[Ray Chase]], [[Chip Joslin]] and [[Dave Fennoy]], all of whom also voice generic super mutants in ''Fallout 76''. ** Grahm does not have his own unique [[Fallout 76 voice types|voice type]], and his dialogue is instead shared between all three generic super mutant voice types. When ''Fallout 76'' was released in 2018, Grahm had dialogue from the voice types CrSuperMutant02 and CrSuperMutant03, which were performed by Joslin and Chase respectively. Both voice types may be used when dialogue lines are heard from Grahm when he is encountered as a traveling merchant. ** The voice type CrSuperMutant01, performed by Fennoy, initially did not have lines recorded for Grahm. However, when Grahm received new dialogue as part of Meat Week with the ''[[Nuclear Winter]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]] in 2019, all of the voice lines were recorded by Fennoy. Although Fennoy did not record for Grahm's traveling merchant lines, all of Grahm's dialogue for Meat Week is voiced by Fennoy. Fennoy also voiced Grahm as part of dialogue from the ''[[Wastelanders]]'' update in 2020, including lines such as his conversation with [[Sofia Daguerre]]. ** When ''Fallout 76'' was released in 2018, both Chase and Joslin promoted the role of Grahm on social media.[https://twitter.com/raychase/status/1062860339723722754 Ray Chase on Twitter]: ''"Out today officially - I play Grahm the friendly Super Mutant and many others in Fallout 76! Happy Reclamation Day, Vault Dwellers!"''[https://twitter.com/chipjoslin/status/1062726127364464640 Chip Joslin on Twitter]: ''"Here's one of the seven characters I voice named Grahm. Thanks to the talented people at Blindlight, Bethesda and my amazing team at Arlene Thornton and Associates! Pick up the game and let's play"'' Joslin was described as an "alternate" voice for Grahm in a ''Twinfinite'' article upon the game's release.[https://twinfinite.net/gallery/fallout-76-voice-actor-voice-cast/7/ Meet the Voice Actors of Fallout 76’s Voice Cast] * Quest designer [[Carl McKevitt]] contributed to the writing of Grahm's Meat Week dialogue, though he did not create the character.BGS_Carl ([[Carl McKevitt]]) [https://web.archive.org/web/20230508205404/https://i.imgur.com/uBL3Dpz.png on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord] ==Gallery== Grahm and Chally in Ash Heap.png|Grahm in the Ash Heap FO76 Grahm and Chally in Forest.png|Grahm in the Forest FO76WL Grahm Crater.png|Grahm at [[the Crater]] FO76OB Blue Devil vs Grahm.png|Grahm in combat with a [[Blue Devil]] FO76 Grahm downed.png|Grahm after being downed Primal Cuts Meat-Cook.png|As depicted in [[Grahm's Meat-Cook]] Atx camp floordecor plushie grahm l.webp|Grahm [[plushie]] ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox vendors FO76}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Fallout 76 merchants]] [[Category:Fallout 76 super mutant characters]] [[es:Grahm]] [[fr:Grahm]] [[it:Grahm]] [[ru:Грэм (Fallout 76)]] [[uk:Грем (Fallout 76)]] [[zh:Grahm]]

Dr. '''Isaac Hammond''' was the chief research scientist of the [[ATLAS Program]], a military weather modification project before the [[Great War]].

==Background==
Hammond was devoted to his research at the [[ATLAS Observatory]]. He worked with [[Marcs]].<ref>[[ATLAS research log 104]]</ref>

Despite making progress in his goals, the [[the Citadel|Pentagon]] decided to shut down the project. When the project's Army advisor [[James Oberlin]] informed Hammond, he flew into a rage before being restrained by Military Police until he finally calmed down and promptly walked out of the ATLAS Observatory, dismissed from his position.<ref>[[ATLAS Observatory terminal entries]]</ref><ref>[[ATLAS decommission reports]]</ref>

Five months after the ATLAS program was shut down and the bombs fell, Hammond returned to the observatory and attempted to finish the project, as he believed it would help the post-apocalyptic world. He reactivated the facility's security robots to aid in his work. Hammond did not survive to finish his work and died in the observatory, his [[Skeleton (Fallout 76)|skeleton]] being found in the ATLAS substructure.

==Notes==
At launch, Hammond's skeleton was found in the normal ATLAS Observatory interior, next to [[ATLAS research log 293|ATLAS research log #293]] and the [[ATLAS director's password]]. However, with the ''[[Steel Dawn]]'' update, his skeleton was moved to the ATLAS substructure. [[Odessa Valdez|Scribe Odessa Valdez]] will make a comment upon discovering his skeleton in [[Mother of Invention]], wishing to give him a proper burial.

==Appearances==
Isaac Hammond's skeleton appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''.

Welcome to the Pumpkin House, one of the most popular attractions in Appalachia. I'm Jack, the caretaker here!"''
([[Jack O' Lantern/Dialogue#8|Jack O' Lantern's dialogue]]) ==Background== According to the [[pumpkin carving automation notes]] found inside the Pumpkin House, several robots were re-programmed by the proprietors to carve jack o' lanterns for [[Halloween]]. The [[Mister Handy (Fallout 76)|Mister Handy]] designated as the greeter was given the name "Jack O' Lantern." Even long after the Great War, Jack continues to maintain the property due to a Priority 0, designating his task and mandate as: Gather pumpkins and prepare for the festival."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Why are you still maintaining this place?"''
Jack O' Lantern: ''"{{Tooltip|Because my programming demands it.|But he loves it}} "Priority 0: Gather pumpkins and prepare for the festival." See, the mandate couldn't be clearer."'' ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started =[[Trick or Treat?|Daily: Trick or Treat?]] |quests involved = }} ===Other interactions=== First time visiting the Pumpkin House, speaking with Jack has him ask to find him some pumpkins to carve, triggering the daily quest [[Trick or Treat?|Trick or Treat]]. Returning with the aforementioned pumpkins results in Jack giving the player character three [[pumpkin grenade]]s and 10 packages of [[radioactive pumpkin seeds]], used to make more via a [[tinker's workbench]], along with the recipe/crafting plans for making pumpkin grenades. Whenever the miscellaneous objective to visit Jack at the Pumpkin House appears, the quest can be done again for more seeds to make more pumpkin grenades. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Jack O' Lantern appears {{In|FO76}}. ==Behind the scenes== The name "Jack O' Lantern" has a rather rich history. According to an Irish myth, there was once a man named Stingy Jack, whom tricked the devil into not claiming his soul but was forsaken by God and forbidden entry into heaven. Due to this, Jack's soul was given a burning coal by the devil to light his way, which he apparently put inside a carved out turnip, and has been wandering the earth ever since. As the tradition goes, the Irish would carve out vegetables and put a piece of coal or something of the like inside to scare off Jack's spirit. When some Irish immigrated to America, they found pumpkins, which they believed to be a perfect vegetable for their tradition. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox robots}} [[Category:Fallout 76 robots and computers]] [[Category:Mister Handy characters]] [[ru:Джек-Фонарь]]

'''Kassie''' was a student in [[Appalachia]] prior to the [[Great War]].

==Background==
Kassie wrote a [[Postcard to parents|postcard]] to her parents, who were planning to visit her in the near future. She intended to pick them up when they arrived and take them to a newly-opened restaurant. However, her plans were ruined by the onset of the Great War, and she died at the [[monorail elevator]].<ref>[[Postcard to parents]]</ref>

He wanted to travel to [[Chicago]] after the War, but his brothers disagreed, instead wanting to travel south to find out if any of their other relatives survived.[[Shawn's journal]]: "''Lowell wants us to pack up and head that way. Who gives a shit about Chicago? I always thought we should travel more south to see if any of our cousins survived.''" Possibly as revenge, Lowell hid the key to the granary where the brothers had been hoarding supplies. With this act he unwittingly condemned John and Shawn to die of an infected leg and radiation sickness respectively.[[John's last words]]: "''My leg got pretty tore up. There's some medicine stored in the granary storage. I'm not gonna make it.''"[[Shawn's journal]]: "''Radiation sickness has taken the best of me. (recites poem for two minutes)|sound=MAIA 003e62ba 1.ogg}} '''MAIA''' ('''Mayoral Artificial Intelligence Assistant''') is a [[Computers#Artificial Intelligences|computer system]] tasked with assisting the mayor of the city of [[Watoga]]. ==Background== Developed alongside the Voice of Watoga at the [[RobCo Research Center]],[[RobCo Research Center terminal entries#MAIA Project|RobCo Research Center terminal entries; MAIA Project]] MAIA was activated around [[Timeline#2042|2042]] to assist the mayor of the city of [[Watoga]] with their daily tasks. Programmed with information pertinent to the governing of a city, MAIA's knowledge databanks comprised of decades worth of news articles.[[Watoga Municipal Center terminal entries#Selection Committee Letter Archived|Watoga Municipal Center terminal entries; Engineering terminal, Selection Committee Letter Archived]] As time went by and new mayors were appointed, many executive orders and personal laws were made for various reasons, from transportation preferential treatment acts to the Mayor for a Day executive order.[[Watoga Municipal Center terminal entries#List of Pertinent Executive Orders|Watoga Municipal Center terminal entries; List of Pertinent Executive Orders]] The Verbal Laws and Ordinances executive order made it so that the mayor could make proclamations, orders, ordinances, and laws by speaking directly to the AI.[[Watoga Municipal Center terminal entries#Verbal Laws and Ordinances|Watoga Municipal Center terminal entries; Verbal Laws and Ordinances]] The "Suck It, Future Mayor's!" executive order enabled previous laws made by the then-acting mayor could never be undone and were made permanent.[[Watoga Municipal Center terminal entries#Suck It, Future Mayor's!|Watoga Municipal Center terminal entries; Suck It, Future Mayor's!]] Finally, after the Watoga virus had been activated by a disgruntled RobCo employee, [[Scott Turner]], throwing the automated city and systems into chaos, Barbara Elizabeth, the 134th and last mayor of Watoga, made her final executive order, stipulating that all who made it to the office would be made mayors based on a weekly lottery of all Watoga citizens, later simplified to just those who stepped into the mayor's office, to try and fix the problem of rogue robots.[[Watoga Municipal Center terminal entries#Mayor for a Day|Watoga Municipal Center terminal entries; Mayor for a Day]][[Mayor for a Day]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started =* [[Mayor for a Day]] |quests involved = }} ===Quests=== * [[Mayor for a Day]]: There is some kind of emergency in Watoga. One can help alleviate the issues, acting as mayor, if they reach the former mayor's office. ===Other interactions=== * When approached, MAIA will appoint the player character mayor of Watoga and start the [[Mayor for a Day]] quest. She will play an audio log containing her final moments with Watoga's last mayor, [[Barbara Elizabeth]]. ==Appearances== MAIA appears only {{In|FO76}}. ==Notes== MAIA is similar in design to the [[Grafton mayor]]. ==Behind the scenes== MAIA's voice actor, [[Lauri Fraser]], is credited as the "Chief of Staff" in the ''Fallout 76'' credits. I don't even want to look at you until you're donning the standard-issue fatigues and helmet!|sound=Master Sergeant Gutsy 00345ac2_1.ogg}} '''Master Sergeant Gutsy''' is a [[Mister Gutsy (Fallout 76)|Mister Gutsy]] operating at [[Camp McClintock]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== In May [[Timeline#2077|2077]], Camp McClintock switched from using human drill sergeants to train recruits to using Mister Gutsy model robots, with only a single human sergeant, [[O'Malley (Fallout 76)|O'Malley]], staying on to monitor them. The Master Sergeant Gutsy was in charge of the other robots. Although multiple Mr. Gutsies malfunctioned on the job, the [[United States Army|Army]] decided that the kinks were worked out and that O'Malley's services were no longer required. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started =* [[Back to Basic]] |quests involved =* [[Start your training at Camp McClintock]] }} ===Other interactions=== The Master Sergeant Gutsy, as the head of Camp McClintock, is in charge of training new recruits who wish to join the United States Army, but will only permit them to begin their training if they are wearing a set of Army fatigues and helmet, otherwise, he'll refuse to train them. Once they are properly dressed, he orders them to complete three training missions before moving on to the [[Live Fire Training Exercise]], regarding patriotism, marksmanship, and agility. Once the recruits complete the three tests and the live-fire exercise, he will officially welcome them into the U.S. Army as privates, which is necessary for them to join the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]] and be granted access to the [[Enclave (Fallout 76)|Enclave]]'s military wing of [[the Whitespring bunker]], per the instructions of [[MODUS]]. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Campaign hat]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Master Sergeant Gutsy appears only {{In|FO76}}. {{Infobox character |games =FO76 |name =Brother Moncrief |image =FO76 Skeleton Brother Moncrief.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |affiliation =[[Cult of the Mothman]] |role =Member |location =[[Landview Lighthouse]] |events =[[The Path to Enlightenment]] |notes =[[Brother Moncrief's note]] |actor = |edid =NPCM_BrotherMoncrief (voice type) |formid ={{ID|0052863f}} (voice type) }} {{Quotation|{{tooltip|Gather now, faithful followers of the most wise and beneficent Mothman. Let us light his holy beacon with the radiance of the fireflies. Let our beacon pierce the darkness and summon forth his divine presence, that we may commune with him and partake of his wisdom.|Reverent, a call to worship}}|sound=Brother Moncrief 0052863c_1.ogg}} '''Brother Moncrief''' was a member of the [[Cult of the Mothman]]. His voice can be heard on a recording during [[The Path to Enlightenment|Event: The Path to Enlightenment]]. ==Background== Brother Moncrief was a [[Cultist (Fallout 76)|cultist]] who vocally theorized about some sort of ''"physical light of the Mothman."''''"I wonder if Brother Moncrief was able to find the physical light of the Mothman that he theorized about."'' ([[Steven Scarberry/Dialogue|Steven Scarberry's dialogue]]) He wrote a note to the High Priestess of his cult while taking shelter at [[Landview Lighthouse]]. There, he observed [[Firefly|fireflies]] while they were mating and collected their [[bioluminescent fluid]] to light the lamp, hoping to summon the [[Mothman]].[[Brother Moncrief's note]] After calling in vain to nearby cultists for aid in a ritual to summon the [[Mothman|wise and beneficent Mothman]],[[The Path to Enlightenment|Event: The Path to Enlightenment]] voice-over: ''"Gather now, faithful followers of the most wise and beneficent Mothman. Let us light his holy beacon with the radiance of the fireflies."'' Moncrief decided to perform the ritual by himself. While gathering their bioluminescent fluid, aggressive fireflies attacked the cultist, inflicting fatal wounds which forced him to abandon his quest.[[The Path to Enlightenment|Event: The Path to Enlightenment]] voice-over: ''"A lone cultist tried to summon the Wise Mothman by lighting the Old Lighthouse lamp. His plan to use the bioluminescent fluid from the fireflies might have succeeded had he not succumbed to his wounds."'' His [[Skeleton (Fallout 76)|skeleton]] can be found lying on a [[Sleeping bag (Fallout 76)|sleeping bag]] on the top floor of the lighthouse. He is remembered positively by [[Steven Scarberry]], so he was probably a member of the [[Cult of the Mothman|Followers of the Winged One]] sect. ==Notes== * Moncrief's relationship to the cults is somewhat unclear. ** He referred to his would-be savior as "the wise and beneficent Mothman." It is unclear if he sought to summon [[Mothman|any Mothman]] or the [[Wise Mothman]] specifically. *** He hoped to "commune with him and partake of his wisdom."[[The Path to Enlightenment|Event: The Path to Enlightenment]] voice-over: ''"Let our beacon pierce the darkness and summon forth his divine presence, that we may commune with him and partake of his wisdom."'' ** His note is addressed to a High Priestess. ** Whenever [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] lit the lighthouse beginning in 2102, the [[Wise Mothman]] would visit them. *** The larger sect, the [[Cult of the Mothman|Followers of the Winged One]], hold the Wise One to be an agent of false prophecy.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Interpreter Clarence walked me through the steps of the ritual."''
[[Steven Scarberry]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Oh, my apologies, I didn't realize that we were discussing the false prophet.|Interpreter Clarence walked me through the steps of the ritual.}} When people say 'Mothman' I assume they're talking about the 'Holy Mothman', and not the purple liar. {{Tooltip|But please, do go on. Tell me of the the stories of their glorified butterfly.|Sarcastic and a bit rude towards the Enlightened. Insulting the Rival cult and their beliefs}}"''
([[Steven Scarberry/Dialogue|Steven Scarberry's dialogue]]) Their beliefs were shaped in the post-War period by a figure known as the [[First Priestess of the Wood]].[[His Priestess]] They have been hostile to the Wise Mothman since returning to the region in 2103. *** The opposing sect, [[the Enlightened]], revere only the Wise Mothman, which they believe to be an individual mortal being with [[Psychic|profound metaphysical capabilities]]. However, they are not known to have a High Priestess, or anything of the sort. They posture in opposition to religious behavior, and style themselves with secular titles such as Observer and Interpreter. **** The event itself is called "[[The Path to Enlightenment]]," possibly alluding to [[the Enlightened]], who were not revealed until the ''[[Night of the Moth]]'' update. ==Appearances== Brother Moncrief appears only {{In|FO76}}. ==Gallery== Fo76 Brother Moncrief note.png ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Cult of the Mothman}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Cult of the Mothman characters]] [[fr:Moncrief]] [[ru:Брат Монкриф]]
