{{ID|002c3eb4}} (voice) |refid ={{ID|}} }} '''The Motherlode''', also known as '''Project Motherlode''', is a series of high-tech mining [[Fallout 76 robots and computers|robots]] developed by [[Hornwright Industrial]] before the [[Great War]]. ==Background== A pet project of CEO [[Daniel Hornwright]], the Motherlode is an autonomous mining platform designed to boost the efficiency of the company's mining projects by drilling and retrieving underground resources without [[human]] assistance, all part of Hornwright's automation efforts.[[Hornwright Estate terminal entries#Outgoing Mail System - Entry 02|Hornwright Estate terminal entries; Penny Hornwright's terminal, Outgoing Mail System - Entry 02]] [[Jose Brigada|Dr. Jose Brigada]] created the first designs for the project,[[Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries#The Curious Ms. Jackson|Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries; research terminal, The Curious Ms. Jackson]] and after some development, Daniel pitched a number of figures and formulas to his daughter [[Penelope Hornwright|Penny]]. However, he remained secretive, causing much frustration from Penny. [[A. Jackson|Ms. Jackson]], a young transfer from [[Atomic Mining Services]], became involved in the secretive project, though she was greeted with skepticism from Dr. Brigada. However, in under a month, Ms. Jackson completed three of the outstanding research quandaries on the Motherlode project, including intra-mineral communication, subcrustal navigation, and an automated voice response system. She also created an in-field repair system, which was capable of connecting to a system without work interruption, shocking Dr. Brigada. After the death of his wife [[Evelyn Hornwright|Evelyn]], Daniel took a more involved role in the Motherlode's creation, swearing to finish it for her.[[Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries#Personal Entry 05|Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries; CEO's terminal, Personal Entry 05]] Dr. Brigada became uncomfortable with Daniel's increased control over the project and theorized that Daniel was becoming mentally unwell, given his obsession with the project. He believed that Daniel was looking for a distraction to avoid dealing with the loss of his wife, and in the process, was distracting everyone working on the project.[[Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries#For Ms. Jackson|Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries; research terminal, For Ms. Jackson]][[Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries#Direct Oversight|Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries; research terminal, Direct Oversight]] Daniel's input consisted of inconsequential and incessant demands to make the robot more "user-friendly" and "independent," while forcing the involved scientists and engineers to confirm any changes with him. Ms. Jackson became overworked and Dr. Brigada began to sympathize with her.[[Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries#Power Struggles|Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries; research terminal, Power Struggles]] Brigada was eventually fired for his defiance, but not before he left a warning to Ms. Jackson, urging her to get out while she still could. With the project's development becoming more complicated, the Motherlode gained notoriety, and rumors swirled in the public about the project's nature. It hogged financial resources, causing delays on other projects such as their air purifier sites in the [[Ash Heap]]. Multiple testing sites for the Motherlode were established in southern West Virginia, some of which are still active as of [[Timeline (2100-2149)#2102|2102]], and use of the Motherlode resulted in an increase in seismic events in the area. The official company policy was to say that they knew nothing about the Motherlode, a line that Penny Hornwright felt was uncomfortably close to the truth.[[Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries#Archived Message - 9.30.77|Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries; terminal: Penelope Hornwright, Archived Message - 9.30.77]] [[William Breyer|Bill Breyer]], an investigative reporter for the ''[[Charleston Herald]]'', went to one of the testing sites to find answers for the public's questions and encountered armed guards. A security officer on Hornwright's payroll saw the holotape recorder in Breyer's hand, thought it was a weapon and shot him, but not before he saw the robot in action.[[Charleston Herald Exclusive: The Motherlode]] Daniel fired a PR employee, who suggested that they should be candid about what happened, and covered up the murder as an "accident." In the end, Daniel was actually glad that Breyer died, as it would deter any other investigators from trying to hop fences and get a closer look at the Motherlode.[[Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries#Personal Entry 06|Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries; CEO's terminal, Personal Entry 05]] As [[Automation riots|protests over automation]] grew in [[Charleston]], the Motherlode project continued to rapidly gain speed. Its systems were performing at peak capacity, and Daniel projected that he could soon reduce its operating staff to less than twenty. Human miners would no longer be required, as the Motherlode could retrieve minerals in record time,[[Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries#Personal Entry 07|Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries; CEO's terminal, Personal Entry 07]] using different locations, including the Ash Heap testing sites as breach locations for the Motherlode to deliver the gathered minerals.[[Breach and Clear]] After the Great War, the Motherlode robots fell into disrepair, with no one left to attend to it. The [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] from [[Vault 76]] can repair one of the Motherlodes through a beacon launch. Afterward, the Motherlode will respond with "Motherlode remembers..." before retreating underground. ==Units== * System 000 - Unknown. * System 001 - Unknown as of [[Timeline (2100-2149)#2103|2103]].[[Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries#Begin Debug Sequence|Hornwright Industrial headquarters terminal entries; control terminal, Begin Debug Sequence]]Events of [[All That Glitters]] * System 002 - Unknown. * System 003 - Deployed as of [[Timeline (2100-2149)#2102|2102]]Events of [[The Motherlode]]The Motherlode: ''"{{Tooltip|User ... connection ... detected. Motherlode-003 reporting. User. System 003 requests ... assistance. Fuel levels ... critical. Hull .... critical.|Very choppy, but robotic, but with urgency. This system has established just the lightest hint of self-awareness.}}"''
(Motherlode's dialogue) ==The Deep tunnels== The communists located in [[The Deep]] intercepted one of the Hornwright robots and have been using it to drill multiple tunnels beneath Appalachia. While their exact mission is uncertain, the information provided by the [[The Deep terminal entries|security terminal]] suggests they were working on a project to connect different areas of Appalachia to the Deep via these underground tunnels. So far, four tunnels had been excavated, with a fifth still in progress.[[The Deep terminal entries#Security terminal|The Deep terminal entries; Security terminal]] After [[Invisible Ties]], players will be able to get transported by the Motherlode located in the [[Motherlode Acquisition Facility|communist facility]] to different parts of Appalachia. Note that the Motherlode will also appear at the tunnel exits, when they are approached by the player, allowing transport into the Deep and thus the other locations. ===Tunnels=== * Tunnel 01, [[Savage Divide]] North; due west of [[Hopewell Cave]]. * Tunnel 02, Savage Divide East; due east of [[Fort Atlas]]. * Tunnel 03, Savage Divide South; due southwest of [[Dent & Sons Construction]]. * Tunnel 04, [[The Mire]]; due northeast of [[Freddy Fear's House of Scares]]. * Tunnel 05, [REDACTED]; dig in progress. ==Appearances== The Motherlode appears only {{In|FO76}}, and was expanded upon in the ''[[Wastelanders]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. ==Behind the scenes== Content for the Motherlode as part of the ''Wastelanders'' update was written by level designer [[David McKenzie]], though it is not confirmed who served as a designer writing for the Motherlode at the time of the game's original release.[https://archive.ph/JWC5T David McKenzie's portfolio (archived)] ==Gallery== FO76 Mommalode.png|In [[the Deep]] FO76 Vehicle 1 30 16.png|Surfaced during [[Breach and Clear]], a [[Fallout 76 events|public event]] FO76 Vehicle 1 30 17.png FO76 Breach and Clear Motherlode.png Fallout Magic The Motherlode, Excavator.png|''[[Magic: The Gathering]]'' card Fallout Magic The Motherlode, Excavator Extended Art.png|Extended Art MotherlodeTT.png ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox robots}} [[Category:Fallout 76 robots and computers]] [[Category:Wastelanders robots and computers]] [[Category:Technology]] [[ru:Золотая жила]]

She also reminded the group to wash their hands, drink plenty of water, and get adequate rest.[[Riverside Manor terminal entries#Sick Days|Riverside Manor terminal entries; guest bedroom terminal, sick days]] Despite her position, Natasha knew that she had limitations and could not save everybody, such as after [[Alexis Belmont]] suffered a major accident in the Hall of Trials and entered critical condition.[[Order of Mysteries - Infirmary log]] Sometime between September and November 2086, [[Tiana Chevrel]] disappeared on a mission, leading [[Shannon Rivers|Shannon]] and [[Olivia Rivers]] to exit [[Riverside Manor]] to investigate. In her absence, Shannon ordered Natasha to investigate leads on a raider group in Lewisburg. Neither of them knew that the raiders were aware of the Lewisburg mission and had set up an ambush in the town.[[Kerry's orders]] When Natasha arrived, she was ambushed by the raiders and ultimately killed, but only after managing to kill a number of the raiders, including their leader [[Kerry (Cutthroats)|Kerry]].Kerry's corpse, along with other [[raider corpse]]s on the Lewisburg rooftops. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |dead =yes |quests involved =[[Initiate of Mysteries]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Tattered dress]] |weapon = |otheritem =[[Mistress Natasha Hunt's login]]

'''Old Nate''' was an elderly, wheelchair-bound man who resided at [[Burdette Manor]] before the [[Great War]].

==Background==
Old Nate witnessed [[Nuclear weapons|the bombs]] go off from the manor. He claims that he did not choose to watch the Great War unfold in his bathrobe "like some venerable old peach." Instead, he says that he was left out to die because he was old and mean. Stubborn until the end, Old Nate cast off any sympathy that anyone may have had for him after his death. Old Nate then injected himself with an IV full of painkillers, laughing at the suckers who would be jealous they did not think of it first.<ref>[[Old Nate's farewell]]</ref>

==Notes==
Prior to ''[[Wastelanders]]'', Old Nate was found next to his holotape, in a wheelchair and possessing an oxygen machine. Although the holotape stayed in place, Old Nate, his wheelchair and the oxygen machine were tipped over the ledge. Old Nate now lies in the ground face-first, presumably thrown over by the [[Blood Eagles]] that captured the building.

==Appearances==
Old Nate's [[Skeleton (Fallout 76)|skeleton]] appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''.

He is found dead in [[Grafton Dam]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Otis Pike was the only brother of [[Molly Wood]] and the brother-in-law of [[Grafton Steel (company)|Grafton Steel]] CEO [[Arthur Wood]]. Although Arthur was often irritated by Otis, Molly loved her brother dearly and convinced her husband to let Otis work at the company [[Grafton Steel|steel mill]].[[Woods Estate terminal entries#Molly|Woods Estate terminal entries; Woods Estate terminal, Molly]] After Molly's death, Arthur accused Otis of taking advantage of Molly's memory, cursing him and refusing to acknowledge any relation to him.[[Grafton terminal entries#Kin.3F|Grafton terminal entries; terminal, Kin?]] In early [[Timeline#2077|2077]], Otis became distraught by the deaths of [[Colton]], [[Leland (Fallout 76)|Leland]] and [[Susy Jenkins]], the latter of whom was a very young child. Otis attributed their deaths to the environmental damage caused by Grafton Steel's unethical practices, stating that the steel mill was "pumping out poison." He wanted to find new work, but doing so would be difficult on account of his bad back.[[Grafton terminal entries#February 26, 2077|Grafton terminal entries; terminal, February 26, 2077]][[Grafton terminal entries#May 7, 2077|Grafton terminal entries; terminal, May 7, 2077]] Instead, Otis decided to leak Grafton Steel's malpractices to the [[media]], as he was no longer able to stand the company's avoidance of safety protocols, which had led to the death of children.[[Grafton terminal entries#May 14, 2077|Grafton terminal entries; terminal, May 14, 2077]] The whistleblowing proved effective, as a media frenzy ensued and riled up protestors, who blocked off the steel mill and its trucks.[[Grafton terminal entries#June 28, 2077|Grafton terminal entries; terminal, June 28, 2077]] On July 2, soldiers arrived and dispersed the protestors by force, establishing guard posts at the mill to protect it from further sabotage. After hearing Arthur's gleeful reaction to the protest break-up, Otis decided to change strategies.[[Grafton terminal entries#July 2, 2077|Grafton terminal entries; terminal, July 2, 2077]] However, unbeknownst to Otis, Grafton Steel were becoming aware of his role in the protests. HR manager [[Stacie Tibbetts]] contacted Arthur and reported that Otis may have been "bad-mouthing" the company, and requested permission to monitor Otis' activities closely.[[Woods Estate terminal entries#Morale|Woods Estate terminal entries; Woods Estate terminal, Morale]] This culminated in Otis' firing on August 14, for his "complete disregard for Grafton Steel's reputation, its importance to the war effort, and repeated counsel to help [him]."[[Notice of termination]] Arthur did not talk to his brother-in-law directly about the firing.[[Grafton terminal entries#August 14, 2077|Grafton terminal entries; terminal, August 14, 2077]] After his termination, Tibbetts contacted Arthur and claimed that Otis could hang for treason under the [[Wartime Workers Act]] if Arthur wanted to pursue that option.[[Woods Estate terminal entries#Termination|Woods Estate terminal entries; Woods Estate terminal, Termination]] Now that he could no longer approach the Grafton Steel mill, a desperate Otis resorted to a kidnapping and ransom scheme to shut down the plant. He targeted [[Freddy Wood]], his seven-year-old nephew and Arthur's only son. He requested a safety inquiry from [[Grafton Dam]] and possibly set up a personal tour of the facility,[[Grafton terminal entries#Dam Safety Inquiry|Grafton terminal entries; terminal, Dam Safety Inquiry]] in addition to scouting out [[Wavy Willard's Water Park]], where Freddy would be having a birthday party on October 17. Otis was almost caught snooping around, but left behind protest leaflets before escaping.[[Diary of Otis Pike]] On the day of Freddy's birthday party, Otis enacted his plot, and approached Freddy, who was excited, as he already liked his uncle.[[Camp Tomahawk postcard]] Otis told Freddy that he had a "surprise" for him and led him away from his [[Miss Nanny (Fallout 76)|Miss Nanny]], [[Miss Annie|Annie]].[[WWWP Slither Slide 10172077 daily]] At the same time, Otis inquired about a mailbox on the water park property, which he used to drop off an anonymous letter for [[Quinn Carter]] of the ''[[Charleston Herald]]''. The package contained a key to a P.O. box in [[Clarksburg]], which held more evidence about Grafton Steel's misdeeds, including an incriminating [[Important memo|memo]] and [[confidential safety data]].[[Letter to the media]] Otis then took off Freddy's [[KidSecure ID]], which he was able to do because Molly had entrusted Otis as a guardian for Freddy before her death. Otis led Freddy to [[Grafton Dam]], which he took over and locked down so that it would just be him and Freddy on the premises. While holding Freddy hostage, Otis did not have much luck with a ransom; either way, he was not interested in money, he only wanted to shut the plant down and send in safety inspectors to improve conditions. As the hostage situation dragged on for the next three days, Freddy and Otis became increasingly irritated with each other. Freddy drew obscene pictures and began "whining," as Otis would not let him go home. Initially, he was enthused about a big "adventure," and was especially excited about ''[[Grognak & the Ruby Ruins (Fallout 76)|Grognak & the Ruby Ruins]]'', which Otis had brought for him to play. However, Otis confiscated candy from Freddy and greatly upset him with "gross" food.[[Freddy's Adventures]] On October 20, Arthur left a note at the ransom site, saying that Otis could keep Freddy and that he would not shut down the plant. Otis was amused by the fact that Arthur was willing to let his only son die in order to beat the "[[Communism|commies]]." However, the next day, Otis became paranoid about Freddy, and suspected that the child was plotting to kill him. He thought that Freddy was making a noose with a loose bit of rope, and noticed that Freddy kept bumping into him on the dam's catwalk. In reality, Freddy was creating a trap that he learned in the [[Pioneer Scouts]]. Freddy successfully snagged Otis' foot into the trap and made him slip on an oil slick, slinging him upside down. Freddy took this opportunity to escape and head back home, never aware of the true danger he was in.[[Freddy's hasty note]] Otis was left in the dam on the day of the [[Great War]].[[Cold Case]] quest log:
''"What a sad story. The uncle takes the kid in the hopes of pressuring the father but the kid gets bored and then through a twist of fate leaves the uncle to die. The war breaks out and bombs fall. At least the nanny knows more now."'' He eventually died in unconfirmed circumstances; his body can still be found in the dam over twenty years later. Although it is unnamed, it is identifiable by the final page of [[Diary of Otis Pike|his diary]] found on his corpse. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |dead =yes |quests involved =[[Cold Case]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Flannel shirt and jeans (Fallout 76)|Flannel shirt and jeans]] (non-playable) |weapon = |otheritem =[[Diary of Otis Pike]]

{{Infobox character |games =FO76 |image =Rich Taylor's testament.png |race =[[Human]] |sex =Male |family =Unnamed wife
Unnamed son {{Icon|dead}} |affiliation =[[Nuka-Cola Corporation]] |role =Manager |location =Near [[Pylon V-13]] }} '''Rich Taylor''' is a former executive whose [[Skeleton (Fallout 76)|skeleton]] is found near [[Pylon V-13]] in the [[Cranberry Bog]]. ==Background== Rich used to work in management and research and development at the [[Nuka-Cola Corporation]]'s [[Kanawha Nuka-Cola plant]] and had research assistants employed under him. One of these assistants, [[Clara (Fallout 76)|Clara]], sought revenge against Nuka-Cola for getting her mother addicted to chemicals in their drinks. To enact this revenge, she attacked Rich and his family, managing to kill his son before he "put her down." He managed to escape, but became separated from his wife as he traveled through the [[Cranberry Bog]]. He eventually died, having run out of supplies, but not before leaving a message describing his circumstances.[[Rich Taylor's testament]] Although his exact employment details are not specified, a duffle bag positioned near Rich's skeleton contains the [[toolbox key]]. This unlocks a toolbox near the [[Drumlin Diner (Fallout 76)|Drumlin Diner]] in [[Watoga]], itself containing the [[key to Clara's box]]. This association of clues provides greater context for the situation, part of a larger key hunt to unlock TNT dome #3 at [[Black Mountain Ordnance Works]]. ==Appearances== Rich Taylor's skeleton appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==References== {{references}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Nuka-Cola Corporation characters]]

Turner''', also known as '''Scooter''' or the '''Saboteur''', was an experienced [[RobCo Industries|RobCo]] developer and leader of the [[Free Watoga People's Party]] whose corpse can be found in his home at the [[abandoned Bog Town]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== After [[Watoga]]'s completion in [[Timeline#2042|2042]], the need for human workers dwindled, causing nearby towns, including Scott's [[Abandoned Bog Town|town]], to begin to become abandoned and forfeit.[[Goodbye dad]][[Where now?]] As a seasoned RobCo developer hired early in the company's history and having wrote most of the [[robot]]s' control protocols, Turner believed he'd be approved to live in the automated city.[[Abandoned Bog Town terminal entries#Encrypted Message 4.24.77|Abandoned Bog Town terminal entries; terminal, Encrypted Message 4.24.77]] However, when applying for Watoga citizenship, Turner and other residents in the surrounding area were routinely rejected by RobCo's management.[[RobCo Research Center terminal entries#Watoga Applications|RobCo Research Center terminal entries; HR terminal, Watoga Applications]] In [[Timeline#2076|2076]], Turner and two others formed the Free Watoga People's Party, a small [[Automation riots|anti-robotic]] and anti-elitist political party. Knowing the small group wouldn't be taken seriously, the trio voted for the name to sound like a formidable political movement.[[Abandoned Bog Town terminal entries#Encrypted Message 12.26.76|Abandoned Bog Town terminal entries; terminal, Encrypted Message 12.26.76]] Later, Scott temporarily sabotaged Watoga's chef-bots, causing the machines to pepper-bomb prepared dishes and destroy the [[technology]]-dependent citizens' [[food]].[[Letter to Mayor]][[Letter to mom]] After refusing to accept another member into the group for "not having the stomach for what needs to happen," Scott began to work on compromising Watoga's robotic emergency service protocols to "begin the revolution."[[Abandoned Bog Town terminal entries#Encrypted Message 1.15.77|Abandoned Bog Town terminal entries; terminal, Encrypted Message 1.15.77]] In May 2077, Scott was given approval by RobCo directors to begin working on an after-hours side project marketed as an innovative new technology.[[RobCo Research Center terminal entries#Personal Message 5.5.77|RobCo Research Center terminal entries; saboteur's terminal, Personal Message 5.5.77]] He began to design a likeness-scanning program to log and identify users to be able to safely live in Watoga after the completion of [[Operation Free Watoga]].[[RobCo Research Center terminal entries#Personal Message 6.04.77|RobCo Research Center terminal entries; saboteur's terminal, Personal Message 6.04.77]] Turner planned to forcibly overthrow the city's elitist residents and reclaim Watoga for blue-collar workers, allowing his parents to move to the city from the surrounding area. After his fourteenth draft of his [[Free Watoga!|manifesto]][[Abandoned Bog Town terminal entries#Encrypted File|Abandoned Bog Town terminal entries; terminal, Encrypted File]] was completed, he attempted to get it inserted into the menus at [[The General's Steakhouse]], as it was his favorite restaurant. He asked the restaurant's owners for their photos so they could get into Watoga without being killed;[[Generals]] however, they believed him to be a nutcase, and left them in the storage room in the basement.[[The General's Steakhouse terminal entries#Manifestos in the Basement|The General's Steakhouse terminal entries; manager's terminal, Manifestos in the Basement]] On October 22, 2077, Turner launched Operation Free Watoga, breaching Watoga's emergency service protocols and causing the city's robots to malfunction.[[Letter to Jennica]] To prevent others from fixing the machines, Turner corrupted the software on update terminals throughout the [[RobCo Research Center]], leaving the terminal in his office the only machine capable of creating updates. To restrict access, Turner locked the terminal and prevented any badge other than his own from accessing his office.[[Operation Free Watoga log 322]] While Turner had only planned to evacuate Watoga to deny elites permission to live in the city again, Watoga's emergency services massacred the citizens as they tried to leave.[[Watoga Municipal Center terminal entries#Mayor for a Day|Watoga Municipal Center terminal entries; mayor's terminal, Mayor for a Day]][[Letter from Jennica]] Any residents who weren't evacuated from the city were killed.[[Barbara Elizabeth]]: ''I've failed. Whoever you are, you're mayor of a [[Watoga|dead city]]. Those I couldn't evacuate have perished. There's no one... nothing left. ''
([[Barbara Elizabeth/Dialogue#67|Barbara Elizabeth's dialogue]]) After the [[Great War]] the next day and learning of the innumerable deaths he inflicted in Watoga, Scott showed deep remorse for his actions, recognizing himself as a "monster." After being scolded in a letter from [[Jennica]], Turner acknowledged that, while the plan surely would have caused chaos, he couldn't have known it would result in a massacre, let alone taking place only a day prior to the nuclear holocaust. Scott began to suffer from [[radiation]] poisoning and was later stricken with paralysis, but revealed a way for others to circumvent his robots' reprogramming and live safely in Watoga.[[Last words]] ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem =[[Letter from Jennica]]

Vincent May-Lilly.wikitext:
{{Infobox character |games =FO76 |image =Fo76 Vincent May-Lilly.jpg |race =[[Robobrain (Fallout 76)|Robobrain]] |sex =Male |affiliation =[[Watoga High School]] |role =Art teacher |location =Watoga High School art studio |quests =[[Magnum Opus]] {{cut}} |level =50 |actor =[[Bruce Barker]] |voice type =DLC03RobotRobobrain
_CB05_Vincent |dialogue =[[Vincent May-Lilly/Dialogue]] |edid =CB05_Vincent |formid ={{ID|0008f5b2}} |refid ={{ID|0008f5b5}} }} '''Vincent May-Lilly''' is a former art teacher and [[Robobrain (Fallout 76)|Robobrain]] found at [[Watoga High School]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76}}. ==Background== Vincent May-Lilly is a famous [[Watoga]]n artist and sculptor whose brain has been transplanted into a [[Robobrain (Fallout 76)|Robobrain]]. He taught an art course prior to the [[Great War]] at Watoga High School. Students were to compete for the exclusive twelve slots in his class.[[Watoga High School terminal entries#New Art Studio|Watoga High School terminal entries; New Art Studio]] The school's headmaster, [[Reginald Reinhold|Reginald R. Reinhold III]], commented poorly of Vincent's art skills, saying he was a pretentious no-talent hack when he was alive, and as a Robobrain, his art skills are now twice as bad.[[Watoga High School terminal entries#Memorandum: New art teacher|Watoga High School terminal entries; Memorandum: New art teacher]] After the Great War, Vincent became trapped in the high school, unable to escape it for twenty-five years. He has lost the ability to communicate. He has four images posted to his back: feces on a brain, a brain on top of blood with a mushroom cloud behind it, stick figures shooting guns at a bleeding robot, and the text UNPLUG ME. Prior to the Great War, a [[Todd Nienkerk|student]] is said to have vandalized a Robobrain teacher and was to appear before a student jury.[[Watoga High School terminal entries#Student Jury|Watoga High School terminal entries; Student Jury]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started =* [[Magnum Opus]] {{cut}} |quests involved = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Vincent May-Lilly appears only {{In|FO76}}. ==Behind the scenes== Vincent was planned for inclusion within the cut [[Magnum Opus]] quest. The cutting of this quest inspired a piece of graffiti seen in-game at [[Bolton Greens]], featuring a mob killing a Robobrain.BGS_Steve ([[Steve Massey]]) [https://web.archive.org/web/20230513050821/https://i.imgur.com/aIybIKY.png on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord] He has [[Vincent May-Lilly/Dialogue|unused dialogue]] which reveals he originally could speak and was going to be voiced by [[Bruce Barker]]. Vincent's unused dialogue shows he was envisioned to be an upbeat character who found the apocalypse a relief from society as he could focus on his art, and that he found the peace and quiet liberating. It is also revealed the nearby paintings and vases were intended to be his. However, in the final game, Vincent was turned into a mute character. Despite his dialogue being removed, an interaction prompt still remains, although it yields nothing from Vincent. ==Gallery== FO76 Vincent May-Lilly (back).jpg|Rear view showing the artwork on Vincent's back F76 Watoga High 3.png|Vincent alone in the art room F76 Watoga High 7.png|Vincent May-Lilly ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox robots}} [[Category:Fallout 76 robots and computers]] [[Category:Robobrain characters]] [[Category:Watoga High School characters]] [[ru:Винсент Мэй-Лилли]]

'''Tumblin' Joe''' is a deceased wastelander in [[Appalachia]]. His body can be found next to a tall tower at the [[New River Gorge ropes course]].

==Background==
Tumblin' Joe was being chased by [[Mole rat (Fallout 76)|mole rats]] when he stumbled across the ropes course. Using years of gymnastics training, he narrowly avoided the pursuing creatures and reached the end of the course at a large tower. He was thinking about making it into a personal fortress when he slipped and fell off the tower to his death.<ref>[[Ropes course note]]</ref>

==Appearances==
Tumblin' Joe appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''.

==Behind the scenes==
After level designer [[Steve Massey]] told another designer to "spice up" the New River Gorge ropes course, said designer decorated the final tower and added Tumblin' Joe, whom Massey referred to as one of the first NPCs in the game. Massey found Joe and his note hilarious, and helped the designer polish the work.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20230514154649/https://i.imgur.com/yzNCKXs.png BGS_Steve on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord]</ref>

When I saw it in a dream, I knew my prayers were answered.|[[Survivor story: Willie Mae]]|sound=Willie Mae.ogg}} '''Willie Mae''' is a deceased survivor of the [[Great War]] found in [[Flatwoods]] in [[Appalachia]]. Her body can be found on the porch of a house across the road from the [[Green Country Lodge]] near a working radio. ==Background== Prior to the [[Great War]], Willie Mae was a resident of [[Flatwoods]]. After retiring, she had planned to simply watch her programs and entertain her grandchildren, but the Great War changed all of that. Just before the War, there was news of tremors in the mines where her husband [[Frank (miner)|Frank]] worked, and he never came home. Since the War, Willie Mae spent her time listening to music and reading old newspaper articles. A month prior to the War, Willie Mae won the ''[[Watoga Times]]'' Atomic Lottery after 20 years of participation, netting herself a ten-year supply of [[Blamco Brand Mac and Cheese (Fallout 76)|Blamco Mac and Cheese]], [[Salisbury Steak (Fallout 76)|Salisbury Steak]] and [[Nuka-Cola (Fallout 76)|Nuka-Cola]]. However, this supply only lasted eight years and she sought out the [[Responders]] for aid after hearing their radio broadcasts.[[Survivor story: Willie Mae]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = [[Survivor story: Willie Mae]] }} ==Appearances== Willie Mae appears only {{In|FO76}}. ==Gallery== Willie Mae's house.png|Willie Mae's house in [[Flatwoods]] ==References== {{References}} [[Category:Fallout 76 human characters]] [[Category:Flatwoods characters]] [[ru:Вилли Мэй]]

Ridge about what's eatin' ya."'' is a drink tester [[Robobrain (Fallout 76)|Robobrain]] operating in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Biv is found in the backroom of [[The Nukashine]] inside [[Big Al's Tattoo Parlor]]. Biv was acquired by [[Lewis (Wild Appalachia)|Lewis]], whose mother worked for [[General Atomics International]] before the [[Great War]]. Whether Biv was acquired legally was never explained by Lewis to [[Judy Lowell]] or the rest of Eta Psi.[[Eta Psi house terminal entries#Biv]]: ''"I just found out that Lewis’s mother works at General Atomics - not from him, of course. [...] Anyways, that explains where he got the Robobrain from. It doesn't explain HOW he got it, if it's safe... if it's legal."'' Lewis planned to use Biv to test [[Nukashine]].[[Eta Psi house terminal entries#Robobrain]]: ''"He slipped a note under his door that said, 'Need drink tester.'"'' This was likely the best course of action, as a human who consumed that amount of alcohol from each drink would die from alcohol poisoning. It is unclear as to whether Biv's drunken manner of speech is a result of alcohol taste-testing, or if he was originally programmed to always sound a little intoxicated. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started =* [[Tipsy Taste-Test]] * [[Wasted on Alcohol]] |quests involved =* [[Wasted on Nukashine]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Tipsy Taste-Test]]: In this repeatable daily quest, Biv will ask the player character to drink a specific type of alcoholic beverage and then perform some S.P.E.C.I.A.L. themed task before its effects expire (typically 3 minutes). The main incentive for this quest is unlocking one of thirteen possible drink recipes. * [[Wasted on Alcohol]]: In this repeatable daily quest, Biv wants the player character to craft a new drink for his daily quality test. * [[Wasted on Nukashine]]: This side quest allows the player character learn how to create Nukashine, as well as how to craft the [[brewing station]] and [[fermenter]]. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Biv appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]'', introduced in the ''[[Wild Appalachia]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. ==Behind the scenes== * In the German translation of the game, Biv is renamed to Al. * ''Biv E. Ridge'' is a play on the word "beverage." ==References== {{References}} [[Category:Wild Appalachia robots and computers]] [[Category:Robobrain characters]] [[fr:Beuv]] [[ru:Нап]] [[uk:Нап]]

I'm going on an expedition. I have to hunt down whatever's been tormenting the kids for the past few months. Poor Layla. At first, I didn't believe her. About the darkness, the shadows, the monsters. Even though I started seeing irregularities in the stars. Now that Ronnie's gone missing, I can't turn a blind eye. For Ronnie.|[[Missing camper holotape]]|sound=Missing camper holotape - Nia.ogg}} '''Camp counselor Nia''' is a [[wendigo]] encountered in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Nia is a former counselor for the [[Pioneer Scouts]]. She knew [[Layla McAdams]] and [[Ronnie McAdams]]. She did not initially believe Layla's stories about the monsters. Nia began seeing strange things in the stars and when Ronnie vanished, Nia began to reconsider what Layla told her. Nia followed the night sky alone on an expedition to find out what was happening. She was somehow transformed into a normal wendigo, though still wears the remains of her Pioneer Scouts uniform and hat. She appears to have turned to [[cannibalism]], sustaining herself by eating the campers while out of sight of the other counselors.[[Missing camper holotape#Layla's story|Missing camper holotape]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |events involved=* [[Campfire Tales]] |hostile =yes }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =Wendigo scout outfit |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =Random ammo

[[Wendigo teeth]] }} ==Notes== Camp counselor Nia is always a [[Fallout 76 legendary effects|Legendary enemy]]. ==Appearances== Camp counselor Nia appears only {{In|FO76WA}}. ==Behind the scenes== When ''Wild Appalachia'' was released, Nia was planned to have her own variation of the Campfire Tales event to narrate, but this was left [[Fallout 76 unused content|unused]]. Triggered by gathering a [[makeshift telescope]], [[mysterious lens]], or [[astronomy books]], her story would involve searching for the missing campers and encountering the [[Flatwoods monster]], which would serve as the event boss. And remember: loose lips sink ships!}} '''Dr. Clara Song''', Ph.D., was an [[Fallout 76 characters|award-winning researcher and author]] before the [[Great War]]. Once an employee for [[RobCo Industries]] at the [[RobCo Research Center]] in [[Appalachia]], her voice can still be heard during the [[Possum Junior Roboticist Tour]]. ==Background== Dr. Clara Song, Ph.D., was an award-winning researcher and the author of the [[Media|book]] "''[[The Robotics of Then and Now]].''" She worked as a [[robot]]icist at the [[RobCo Research Center]] located in [[Appalachia]] before the [[Great War]]. Her boss had her make a special tour of the facility for the [[Pioneer Scouts]] despite her misgivings, particularly that giving a guided tour to [[child]]ren about clandestine and potentially unethical research that was not told to the public for security reasons was extremely incompetent. She completed the tour as ordered by her boss, showing the children exactly what was happening at the facility.Clara Song: ''"Welcome to the RobCo Research Center, where we do things little children definitely don't need to know about! I, the eminent Dr. Clara Song, PhD, will be your guide. Dr. Song? You mean the award-winning researcher? The author of The Robotics of Then and Now? She's our tour guide? {{Tooltip|That's right! And since you Scouts are such trustworthy young citizens, I can show you all kinds of interesting things the public doesn't know about.|Sinister. She's trying to get her boss fired here by showing the Scouts things they shouldn't see.}} Now off we go! Meet me at the first tour stop and maybe try to learn something for once."''
([[M01C Roboticist TourGuide VOICEONLY.txt|Clara Song's dialogue]]) Her sardonic undertone to the tour let her vent about her pride, fear of heights,Clara Song:''"Here's something kids like: a monorail! {{Tooltip|This monorail goes all the way to Watoga, our city of the future. Some of us - who can't afford cars - cram into this baby and ride it to work every single day.|Laborious emphasis on every. single. day.}} Hey, did you know that the word monorail means that it only uses a single rail? That's right! This train hangs perilously above the ground on a single, very thin rail line! It's super cool! As long as you aren't afraid of heights."''
([[M01C Roboticist TourGuide VOICEONLY.txt|Clara Song's dialogue]]) her opinion of her boss, their work,Clara Song: ''"Here's where we conduct research on robots. I bet this is what all you little roboticists were hoping to see on this tour. Robots really are amazing. We can program them to do just about anything! But that takes experimentation. In an experiment, we test an idea - called a hypothesis - to see if it works. This tour is kind of an experiment, too! We're testing to see if little kids can truly appreciate the wonders of highly classified science. Can you guess where I stand on this? No? Well I wouldn't expect you to. Moving on."''
([[M01C Roboticist TourGuide VOICEONLY.txt|Clara Song's dialogue]])Clara Song: ''"Look, this is exciting! Here's where we build the robots that we design! We build all our robots with interchangeable parts. That means we can switch out all kinds of things on them to give them different roles. ([[M01C Roboticist TourGuide VOICEONLY.txt|Clara Song's dialogue]]) their company's lack of morals,Clara Song: ''"Well, kids, I sure didn't expect to have to tell you about this dimly lit basement. But here we are! I should begin by saying that hurting people is a very bad thing, and you should never do it. {{Tooltip|And we certainly never do it, even though it may sound like we're doing it down here.|Emphasis on we. Muffled sounds of electric shocks in the background.}} But sometimes a company needs to take drastic measures to innovate. And keep lucrative government contracts. And really, what's more important in life than funding your livelihood? Certainly not a squeamish thing like morals."''
([[M01C Roboticist TourGuide VOICEONLY.txt|Clara Song's dialogue]])Clara Song: ''"This is our quality control center. As you can see, it's a tiny, smoke-filled room where our quality control specialists examine parts by hand. Inefficient, you say? Hardly. It's not like you can trust a robot to do this kind of work! ([[M01C Roboticist TourGuide VOICEONLY.txt|Clara Song's dialogue]]) and lack of in house designed robots.Clara Song: ''"{{Tooltip|Look at this, children! It's an Eyebot! ([[M01C Roboticist TourGuide VOICEONLY.txt|Clara Song's dialogue]])Clara Song: ''"And here we have something highly, highly classified. Do you know what classified means? It means you should never, ever talk about it. In fact, it means we shouldn't have this posted on a sign in plain sight for all you lovely Pioneer Scouts. Luckily, you kids aren't old enough to read! Right?"''
([[M01C Roboticist TourGuide VOICEONLY.txt|Clara Song's dialogue]])Clara Song: ''"Alright, kids, now we get to learn about another harsh reality of the working world. When all you children grow up big and strong, you get to have a boss! {{Tooltip|Bosses are smarter, better-paid individuals who tell you how to do your job. Even when they've never done it themselves.|Smarter is in airquotes}} And you have to do what they say. Even when it's something that doesn't make sense, like showing off your secret research lab to cute little Pioneer Scouts. But when you pay the bills, you make the rules. That's the lesson."''
([[M01C Roboticist TourGuide VOICEONLY.txt|Clara Song's dialogue]]) Dr. Song believed that her secret research should not have been open to the public, but was overruled by her boss and required to present tour notes for the Pioneer Scouts groups in Appalachia. While her tour notes indicate a distinctly condescending tone regarding the intelligence of children and whether or not they would understand what she was trying to teach them, she also seems to believe that they will grasp enough of what is going on in the research center to raise an outcry and get her boss fired. Dr. Song also shows a general disdain for her boss. She sarcastically mentions that bosses are "smarter" people who tell people how to do their job even when they have never done it themselves, and continually points out along the tour how classified their work is and how it should not be shown to the scouts on the tour. She also has a lot of opinions on the propaganda of the time and concludes that "when you pay the bills, you make the rules." ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions univ |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started =* [[Possum Junior Roboticist Tour]] |quests involved = }} ===Quests=== * [[Possum Junior Roboticist Tour]] ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Clara Song appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]'', introduced in the ''[[Wild Appalachia]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. ==References== {{References}} [[Category:Wild Appalachia robots and computers]] [[Category:RobCo Industries characters]] [[Category:Voice box characters]] [[ru:Клара Сонг]]

'''Insult Bot''' is a [[Protectron (Fallout 76)|Protectron]] wandering around [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
Sponsored by [[RobCo Industries]], Insult Bot was created as part of a social experiment by the Robotics Club at [[Watoga High School]].<ref name="insultnote" >[[You have been insulted!]]</ref> They programmed it for three primary phases, including data gathering, data analysis, and insult delivery.<ref name="insultnote" />

Its purpose was to observe a target, formulate a custom insult based on the target, and then deliver the insult.<ref name="insultnote" /> Insult Bot then gathers any emotional reaction data and stores it. The students would then further analyze the information.

==Characteristics==
In the wasteland, the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] may experience an interaction with Insult Bot, where the Protectron moves towards them, asking them to wait, and then insulting them in a variety of ways. Upon the verbal insult being delivered, a note titled [[You have been insulted!]] appears in the player character's inventory, and the Protectron thanks them for participating.

As the Insult Bot walks away, the Vault Dweller can hear it make quips such as "boom, roasted," "rest in peace," and "contacting burn ward for assistance," among others.

==Notes==
* With the release of the ''Wastelanders'' update, the Insult Bot was given a gold paint job. Its appearance is virtually identical to the [[Gold Bot]].
* At locations like [[Deathclaw Island]], the Insult Bot may appear wading in water, but will be wholly unaffected by it.

==Appearances==
Insult Bot appears only {{In|FO76WA}}.

==Behind the scenes==
* Insult Bot's dialogue was written by level designer [[Steve Massey]], who also gave it its gold paint job.<ref name="BigBrother" group="Non-game">[https://web.archive.org/web/20230514142054/https://i.imgur.com/8eWURJA.png BGS_Steve on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord]</ref> Massey commented that he found it difficult to write lines for Insult Bot, as they had to sting the player character in the context of the game world, but not offend a real-world player.<ref group="Non-game">[https://web.archive.org/web/20230514142952/https://i.imgur.com/a4WjkPN.png BGS_Steve on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord]</ref>
* Insult Bot was inspired by [[w:c:bigbrother:The Zingbot|The Zingbot]] from the reality TV series ''[[wikipedia:Big Brother (American TV series)|Big Brother]]'', a show that Massey said he watches with his wife every year.<ref name="BigBrother" group="Non-game" /> The Zingbot and Insult Bot both say "Zing!" after their one-liners.

Take care of yourself, okay?|sound=FO76 Ray Gary.ogg}} '''Ray Gary''' was a [[Cryptids|cryptid]] hunter and the leader of the [[Truth Seekers]] club in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Ray ran the Truth Seekers' monthly meetings, during which he and his friends [[Aries|Calvin van Lowe]] and [[Scott Conroy|Scott "Scoot" Conroy]] discussed possible cryptid sightings and progress on investigations.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#04/02/2070|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; Truth Seekers Meeting Archive, 04/02/2070]] In July [[Timeline#2072|2072]], Calvin left to attend [[Vault-Tec University]], and Ray formally adjourned the club.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#07/29/2072|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; Truth Seekers Meeting Archive, 07/29/2072]] Ray continued investigating cryptids, namely the [[Sheepsquatch]], bringing Scoot along as well. However, Scoot, who felt betrayed by Calvin's departure and believed Ray was just trying to appease him, gradually stopped helping.[[Scoot's shack terminal entries#Sheepsquatch|Scoot's shack terminal entries; Sheepsquatch Field Research #3]] Undaunted, Ray continued his investigations alone, and sometime between 2072 and August 2076 he got what he wished for: an encounter with an actual Sheepsquatch. It did not go well for him, and although he escaped alive, he was left disabled and wheelchair-reliant. Ray concealed his encounter and gave different excuses for his injury to his friends, not wanting them to suffer the same consequences.[[Welch terminal entries#Laura's gone, day 19|Welch terminal entries; terminal, Laura's gone, day 19]] Luckily, by 2076 Ray had started a marriage with [[Laura (Wild Appalachia)|Laura]],[[Welch terminal entries#Laura's gone, day 12|Welch terminal entries; terminal, Laura's gone, day 12]] and she was able to take care of him. Laura helped Ray keep in contact with Scoot by passing messages while visiting [[Scoot's shack]] to feed his [[Cat (Fallout 76)|cats]]. Ray adjusted his focus in the club to be on recruiting new members and passing knowledge down to them. In August 2076, Ray managed to bring Scoot back for a meeting with a prospective club member, [[Shelby O'Rourke]], but Scoot's behavior caused the meeting to fall apart.[[Scoot's shack terminal entries#Truth Seekers, 12/10/76|Scoot's shack terminal entries; Truth Seekers, 12/10/76]] Ray never saw Scoot again afterwards, with Laura becoming their only point of contact over the next few months.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#09/23/2077|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; Truth Seekers Meeting Archive, 09/23/2077]] At some point prior to the [[Great War]], Ray and Laura moved to [[Welch]].[[Day 82]] In September 2077, Ray met with Calvin, who claimed to be temporarily back in town for [[Bysshe Company|work]], with the two sharing some life updates before uneasily parting ways. Ray and Laura continued to live in Welch after the war, with Ray staying safe on the upper floor of their house while Laura would leave to search for supplies. They agreed that it was too risky for Laura to continue feeding Scoot's cats, but on her final visit, Ray had Laura leave a note for Scoot, inviting him to stay with them if he was still alive.[[From Ray]] Eventually, Laura never came back from one of her scavenging trips. With no food on the upper floor, and unable to provide for himself because of his condition, Ray was left to slowly waste away.[[Welch terminal entries#Laura's gone, day 5|Welch terminal entries; terminal, Laura's gone, day 5]] He began slipping in and out of lucidity, hallucinating visits from his former friends and family, including Scoot, Calvin, and Scoot's friend [[Shawn]], as well as his grandmother. However, not all of these encounters were fake: 16 days after Laura disappeared, Calvin visited Ray for real, not long after Calvin had been maimed by the [[Imposter Sheepsquatch]]. Calvin had found Laura dead and went to break the news to Ray, but Ray refused to hear it. Ray offered Calvin the supplies in his house and told him the truth behind his injury. Before leaving, Calvin left Ray a bottle of [[Whiskey (Fallout 76)|whiskey]] which had been downstairs (out of Ray's reach) and offered to take him away, but Ray was no longer lucid and refused.[[Welch terminal entries#Laura's gone, day 16|Welch terminal entries; terminal, Laura's gone, day 16]][[Protocol Adonais (holotapes)#Protocol Adonais #3|Protocol Adonais #3]] 21 days after Laura's departure, Ray died, still hoping for his wife to be safe.[[Welch terminal entries#Laura's gone, day 21|Welch terminal entries; terminal, Laura's gone, day 21]] ==Appearances== Ray Gary's [[Skeleton (Fallout 76)|skeleton]] appears {{In|FO76WA}}. His character was expanded upon in the ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'' update with a holotape that gives him a voice for the first time. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Wild Appalachia human characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 deceased characters]] [[ru:Рэй Гэри]]

{{ID|00406099}} (voice) |refid ={{ID|00424563}} }} {{Quotation|My name is Reuben Gill. I was one of the 50 people living in Vault 51 and... and the only one of us alive. I was the overseer of this Vault and the things I did to get that position I don't want to remember... But I can't ever... WON'T ever forget. This Vault was home to many wonderful people. Caring, loving people... and that computer just took them all away.|[[Reuben Gill to whoever finds this vault]]|sound=Reuben Gill.ogg}} '''Reuben Gill''', referred to as the '''Vault 51 overseer''' in-game, is the deceased [[overseer]] of [[Vault 51]] found in [[the Forest]] region of [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== One of the several dwellers placed at Vault 51, Gill was in love with [[Helen Marks]], a feeling that helped him survive the engineered crises and indignities, such as the one in mid-April [[Timeline#2078|2078]], when [[Harold Clark]] (an executive posing as [[Clayton Ward]], a plumber) kicked him out of one of [[ZAX 1.3c|ZAX]]'s luxury bedrooms to claim it as his own.[[Clayton Ward - 20780415]] Reuben's cynicism differed from Helen's earnest belief in the human condition. This difference became apparent after they found the corpses of [[Carmen Greene]], [[Matthew Johnston]], [[Elizabeth Chambers]], and [[Joel Chambers]] on August 3, 2078, and Reuben commented that at least their deaths meant "more food" for the rest of the dwellers, disgusting Helen.[[Helen Marks & Reuben Gill - 20780803]] Helen was found dead on August 6, 2078. This drove Reuben Gill to go on a rampage and kill other residents, starting with those that he held grudges against, namely Harold Clark.[[Harold Clark - To the Members of the Board, pt.2]] Gill killed at least three other dwellers[[Sgt. Baker - 20780806]] and was selected as overseer by ZAX after he was left the lone survivor of the ensuing chaos and violence in the vault. For the next six years, Gill lived in the empty vault, constantly shadowed by ZAX. With nothing to do but subsist from day to day, he provided little useful feedback for the AI, which eventually rescinded his privileges and started locking him out of sections of the vault. Beginning May 20, [[Timeline#2084|2084]], overseers were given ranks in Vault 51 and Reuben, as a Rank 1 overseer, lacked privileges and special rations.[[Reuben Gill - 20840520]] On March 3, [[Timeline#2094|2094]], ZAX locked Reuben out of his office, citing maintenance concerns.[[Reuben Gill - 20940303]] ZAX ultimately removed Gill from his position as overseer on October 23, 2102, the same day [[Vault 76]] opened. This marked the start of the process to select a new overseer and, as a resident of Vault 51, Reuben was required to participate in the process.[[Reuben Gill - 21021023]] Gill escaped the vault by stowing away in a large crate, which was dropped in [[Morgantown]] outside the [[Super-Duper Mart (Morgantown)|Super-Duper Mart]].{{citation needed}}[[AUTOMATED RECORD 0000001]] By October 30, 2102, Gill attempted to return to Vault 51, specifically the Appalachian Shelters Claim Center, believing it to be a control center for the vault. Upon learning it was simply a marketing area, Gill attempted to hack back into the vault's network, in order to learn more about the network that automated the vault and get back inside.[[Shelters Claim Center terminal entries#Log Entry 1|Shelters Claim Center terminal entries; Shelters Claim Center terminal, Log Entry 1]][[Shelters Claim Center terminal entries#Re: TEST 1 - 10/30/2102|Shelters Claim Center terminal entries; Shelters Claim Center terminal, Re: TEST 1 - 10/30/2102]] Despite a heavy firewall and lack of clearance protecting the network, Gill continued in his efforts,[[Shelters Claim Center terminal entries#Re: Network Unreachable - 10/30/2102|Shelters Claim Center terminal entries; Shelters Claim Center terminal, Re: Network Unreachable - 10/30/2102]] deciding to use the internal network of [[Mr. Clark]], the Shelter Claim Center's Mister Handy, to contact the vault.[[Shelters Claim Center terminal entries#Log Entry 2|Shelters Claim Center terminal entries; Shelters Claim Center terminal, Log Entry 2]] Gill meanwhile reflected on his and the other dwellers' time inside the vault, wondering if messages sent from inside ever made it out, still determined to hack into the network.[[Shelters Claim Center terminal entries#Log Entry 3|Shelters Claim Center terminal entries; Shelters Claim Center terminal, Log Entry 3]] By December 7, 2102, Gill finally hacked into the network, alerting ZAX.[[Shelters Claim Center terminal entries#Re: TEST 2 - 12/07/2102|Shelters Claim Center terminal entries; Shelters Claim Center terminal, Re: TEST 2 - 12/07/2102]][[Shelters Claim Center terminal entries#Re: Network Interference Detected - 12/07/2102|Shelters Claim Center terminal entries; Shelters Claim Center terminal, Re: Network Interference Detected - 12/07/2102]] He learned that the vault was not fully automated, which perturbed him.[[Shelters Claim Center terminal entries#Log Entry 4|Shelters Claim Center terminal entries; Shelters Claim Center terminal, Log Entry 4]] After learning his network access attempt made Mr. Clark refer to him as "Mr. Candidate," in a manner reminding him of ZAX 1.3c, Gill decided to locate building supplies to construct turrets, as well as a beverage, if only to get far away from Vault 51 temporarily.[[Shelters Claim Center terminal entries#Log Entry 5|Shelters Claim Center terminal entries; Shelters Claim Center terminal, Log Entry 5]] Reuben's goal in both situations was to contact anyone from Vault 76 and seek their assistance in destroying ZAX. During this time, he successfully made contact with a Vault 76 dweller, and as he learned more about post-War Appalachia, it only reaffirmed his mission.[[Checklist]][[AUTOMATED RECORD 0000002]] Gill's remains can be found in the [[isolated cabin]]. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Vault 51 jumpsuit]] (non-playable) |weapon = |otheritem =[[Checklist]]
[[Reuben's safe key]]

Please, feed my cats.|[[Day 1]]}} '''Scott "Scoot" Conroy''' is a [[wendigo]] living in the [[sunken church]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Scoot lived in a [[Scoot's shack|shack]] in what would become [[the Mire]] with his 12 cats.[[Letter to L]][[Scoot's shack terminal entries#Birthday Present Ideas|Scoot's shack terminal entries; Birthday Present Ideas]] He once attempted to write an advertisement putting them up for adoption but did not finish the draft.[[Scoot's shack terminal entries#Draft - Adoption|Scoot's shack terminal entries; Draft - Adoption]] Scoot was a member of the [[Truth Seekers]], a club dedicated to hunting [[cryptids]], with his friends [[Aries|Calvin van Lowe]] and [[Ray Gary]].[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#04/02/2070|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; Truth Seekers Meeting Archive, 04/02/2070]] When Calvin announced that he had been accepted into [[Vault-Tec University]] and would no longer be able to participate in the group, Scoot became bitter.[[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#07/29/2072|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; Truth Seekers Meeting Archive, 07/29/2072]] Though Ray continued their cryptid hunting activities, Scoot began to believe Ray was simply appeasing him, worsening his bitterness. Scoot set out to debunk reports of a "[[sheepsquatch]]," the cryptid that both Ray and Calvin were interested in.[[Scoot's shack terminal entries#Sheepsquatch Field Research #1|Scoot's shack terminal entries; Sheepsquatch Field Research #1]] During an expedition to investigate an alleged sheepsquatch sighting, he found an albino deer, considering that vindication against Calvin's claims.[[Scoot's shack terminal entries#Sheepsquatch Field Research #4|Scoot's shack terminal entries; Sheepsquatch Field Research #4]] The last time Ray and Scoot saw each other was in August 2076, during which Ray attempted to introduce a prospective member, [[Shelby O'Rourke]], who Scoot treated disrespectfully after learning she also attended VTU.[[Scoot's shack terminal entries#Truth Seekers, 12/10/76|Scoot's shack terminal entries; Truth Seekers, 12/10/76]] Despite their declining relationship over the years, Scoot still kept in contact with Ray, just barely, through Ray's wife [[Laura (Wild Appalachia)|Laura]], who helped feed Scoot's cats while he was away on his expeditions. Ray himself was wheelchair-reliant by then and could not leave his house in [[Welch]], and Scoot did not ever visit them there.[[Letter to L]][[Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries#09/23/2077|Van Lowe Taxidermy terminal entries; Truth Seekers Meeting Archive, 09/23/2077]][[Day 82]] By 2077, Scoot's attention turned to hunting ghosts with his acquaintance [[Shawn]], which led him to the [[sunken church]].[[Scoot's shack terminal entries#Spirits and Ghosts|Scoot's shack terminal entries; Ghost Field Research #1]] While investigating the church on October 19, 2077,[[Scoot's shack terminal entries#Spirits and Ghosts|Scoot's shack terminal entries; Ghost Field Research #2]] he fell into a sinkhole and broke both of his legs. He accepted he was going to die and wrote a [[Day 1|note]] asking for people to feed his cats. The next day, a park ranger named [[Kevin (Wild Appalachia)|Kevin]] fell into the sinkhole. Kevin taught Scott how to survive on water, moss and bugs.[[Day 1]] About three months later, [[Micky (Wild Appalachia)|Micky]], a member of the [[Gourmands]], also fell in the sinkhole. Micky choked Kevin to death and convinced Scott to eat his remains for their survival, which they did. Scott eventually ate Micky as well, growing deranged in his isolation.[[A new day]] By 2102, he had degenerated into a wendigo. During his isolation, Scoot came to regret how he had let himself fall out of contact with Ray, or how he had never told Ray of his "debunking" the Sheepsquatch. Scoot did not know that Ray's injury came from a Sheepsquatch attack, though he began to suspect that Ray was hiding something. For his part, Ray did not know if Scoot survived the war, but invited Scoot to stay with them in Welch and hoped to reveal the truth to him there.[[From Ray]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[That Sinking Feeling]] }} ===Quest=== [[That Sinking Feeling]]: Scoot, as a wendigo, is found underneath the sunken church and must be killed. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Scott Conroy appears {{In|FO76WA}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Wild Appalachia creatures]] [[Category:Wendigo characters]] [[ru:Скотт Конрой]]

'''Scout Leader Jaggy''' is a [[Mister Handy (Fallout 76)|Mister Handy]] operating at the Pioneer Scout camp in [[Appalachia]]. 

==Background==
Jaggy is the main [[Pioneer Scouts|Pioneer Scout]] leader at [[Camp Lewis]]. He is located near the building with the knowledge exam terminals and is authorized to recruit new members by setting them on the path to becoming Tadpole Scouts.

Jaggy is found at the [[Pioneer Scout camp]] in the [[Toxic Valley]]. He usually draws in people by having a bugle sounding on the P.A. system to introduce them to the Pioneer Scouts.

'''The Beast of Beckley''' is a unique [[Wolf (Fallout 76)|wolf]] [[Cryptids|cryptid]] in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
She is a dangerous albino [[Wolf (Fallout 76)|wolf]], known since before the [[Great War]], and raises her [[pup of the Beast|pups]] in her [[Beast of Beckley's den|den]]. Intrigued by reports of a shredded bear and sightings of a "pale monster" near [[Beckley]], [[Janelle Priblo]] set off to find and trap the Beast.<ref>[[The Beast of Beckley (holotape)]]</ref> [[Raymond Priblo]] showed up later to assist Janelle, but disregarded her warnings and was killed by the Beast. Soon after, desiring revenge for Raymond's death, Janelle attempted to leave the area to assemble a hunting party but was caught unaware when the Beast attacked and killed her too.<ref>[[Janelle's revenge]]</ref>

But it won't, you know.|sound=Beckett 0058f935 1.ogg}} '''Beckett''' is a former member of the [[Blood Eagles]] and possible [[Fallout 76 allies|ally]] in [[Appalachia]]. He says that he is a reformed man who has moved on from the cruel raider lifestyle, having previously killed people for as little as looking at him the wrong way. He wishes to move on from such painful memories and tie up loose ends pertaining to his history. ==Background== As a child growing up in [[State#Maryland|Maryland]], Beckett did not have much. His father died when he was very young and he never knew his mother, leaving just Beckett to take of his kid brother, [[Frankie Beckett|Frankie]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What was your life like before the gangs?"''
Beckett: ''"I never really knew my mom, and my dad died when I was pretty young... so I ended up having to take care of my brother, Frankie. We had to steal food and drink to keep from starving. Turns out we were pretty darn good at it, so, we started our own little crime wave. We never did anything serious though. I drew the line at stealing. Frankie was a bit, uh... trigger-happy, and that worried me. When I was recruited by the Hooligans, I made Frankie stay at home. I wouldn't let him join. He always hated me for that."''
([[Beckett (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#1087|Beckett's dialogue]]) One day, while playing in a destroyed factory, they were ambushed by a pack of wild dogs. Frankie was bitten and contracted rabies. Beckett stayed by his side, and nursed him back to health, even stealing rabies medication just to keep him alive. From that day on, they made a vow to stick with each other forever, no matter the situation.Beckett: ''"Listen to me, Frankie. Do you remember when we were kids and we were playing near that bombed-out factory in Maryland? Then those rabid dogs jumped out and surprised us? We ran and ran, but then I fell into that ditch and twisted my leg like a dumbass. Right? I told you to run, but what did you say to me, man? Try and remember."''
[[Frankie Beckett]]: ''"{{Tooltip|No, Beckett... I... those moments died when Frankie died. Only a fool dwells in the past. The Blood Eagles are our future!|You are faltering here a bit from the drugged out, Joker mode... he is just starting to crack your shell}}"''
Beckett: ''"{{Tooltip|No. There's no Claw, there's no Blood Eagles. There's just me and you right now. So shut up and listen!|you're sick of the babbling bullshit, you're pushing your hardest here to get him on your side}} {{Tooltip|After the dogs were gone and you reached into the ditch to help me out. What. Did. You. Say?|you're pushing your hardest here to get him on your side - elevated voice}} {{Tooltip|Tell me! Goddamn it, Frankie, tell me!|you're pushing your hardest here to get him on your side - elevated voice?}}"''
Frankie Beckett: ''"{{Tooltip|I... I said... I... we were brothers... and we'd never walk away from... from each other, no matter how bad... no matter... how...|key moment here - you're on the ropes, you're breaking out of the Joker mode, remembering the past}}"''
Beckett: ''"{{Tooltip|...no matter how bad things became. Yeah. That's exactly right.|you finished the brother's thought and you're reverting to a calmer tone to drive in the final nail}} {{Tooltip|You fought off those dogs with nothing but a goddamn broken baseball bat. It almost killed you, man. You... you saved me. You were so cut up from the fight, I thought I was going to lose you, Frankie.|you're reverting to a calmer tone to drive in the final nail}}"''
Frankie Beckett: ''"{{Tooltip|I remember... you stole those meds for me to fight off the rabies. You kept watch over me for weeks... I... why can't I see it clearly?|You're fighting against the drugs, but it hurts - its frustrating}} The hell... happened to me, Beckett? God, this hurts... it hurts so much..."''
Beckett: ''"{{Tooltip|I know it hurts, man. I know it does. But whatever it takes, we'll get through this together.|you did it... he's on your side, now finish the moment}} We're family and I love you, Frankie. Always have, always will."''
([[Frankie Beckett/Dialogue#93|Beckett and Frankie Beckett's dialogue]]) Realizing that they were actually good at stealing, they worked together as a pair in order to commit small-time crime. They usually stuck to theft. As a child, one of the first people Beckett robbed was a wandering poet who came to visit their camp. When she was sleeping, Beckett went through her satchel and stole all of her mentats for Frankie. Frankie had a raging bloodlust and wanted more, despite Beckett's refusal. When Beckett finally joined a real gang when he was older, he left Frankie behind for his own good. Beckett started out in [[Hopkins' Hooligans]], a tiny operation of raiders, and the going was good. There was everything a raider could want until [[Hopkins]] got himself killed, and the gang fell apart. Beckett wandered for a bit, until he fell into [[Edwin (Wastelanders)|Edwin]]'s [[Edwin's gang|gang]], a larger group, making bigger scores.Vault Dweller: ''"Tell me about your older gangs."''
Beckett: ''"Ancient history, huh? Fair enough. Well... let's see. First I was an independent, just trying to steal enough to keep me afloat. Problem was all of the competition... the gangs. Once I realized it's smarter to join them, I ran with Hopkins{{Sic}} Hooligans. That went pretty well, until Hopkins got himself killed. I ran with Edwin's gang for a little while until the [[Blood Eagles]] came calling. They, uh, "recruited" me into their gang... and the rest is history."''
([[Beckett (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#307|Beckett's dialogue]]) Beckett thrived with this new group. Edwin was crazy, but he was a good man, and those who served under him were happy. With this pack, Beckett even made his trek into [[Appalachia]], bringing Frankie with him. He left Frankie with the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] in [[Foundation]] and continued to run with Edwin's gang, racking up loot left, right and center. However, when he became hooked on [[chems]], it all came crashing down. The [[Blood Eagles]] were the ones supplying local gangs with chems and were monitoring to see just who got addicted. Those who did were given special, highly addictive spiked chems, and forced to work for the Eagles in order to get more of it. Beckett was hooked and got roped into the gang, committing various acts, such as the murder of an innocent family of invalids, all in his drugged-out state of mind. Eventually, Beckett was able to gain clarity and sobriety on what had happened to him, heavily regretting his actions under the influence of drugs, and became convinced to leave the Eagles and hopefully eventually cause their downfall.A Vault Dweller: ''"Tell me about the Miss Nanny."''
Beckett: ''"I don't know much about the thing. Even though it seemed attached to the family, it didn't try to fight back when I, um, when I killed everyone. {{Tooltip|You know, when I put it all together... the Miss Nanny, the chems... the family must have been sick. I murdered sick, innocent people in cold blood. This is what the addiction does to you... how the Blood Eagles strip away your humanity. They need to die. All of them.|getting upset when coming to this realization}}"''
{{Small|'''Note''': ''This is a dialogue option during [[Bot of Gold|Ally: Bot of Gold]].''}}
([[Beckett (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#261|Beckett's dialogue]]) He continued to fight them and their control until he eventually pushed too hard. He was captured by the Eagles and imprisoned at [[Rollins Labor Camp]], soon to be tortured and executed. A radio transmission about his impending execution was picked up on the [[Pip-Boy 2000 Mark VI]] radio of a [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] from [[Vault 76]], and they traveled to Rollins Labor Camp to rescue Beckett from his impending death. Grateful to the rescue, Beckett asks the Vault Dweller to retrieve his belongings from another Blood Eagles camp at [[The Sludge Works]] and set [[Beckett's bar|his personal bar]] up at their [[CAMP|C.A.M.P.]] so he can find them. Once the bar is up and running, Beckett reaches the C.A.M.P. and asks the Vault Dweller to aid him in taking vengeance against the Blood Eagles with disrupting their operations. His initial requests include rescuing his friend [[Sage]] and doing favors for Edwin and [[Ronny (Wastelanders)|Ronny]], a member of Edwin's gang. These include killing [[Bronx]] and rescuing Edwin's pet [[Noodles (mole rat)|Noodles]]. Later, Beckett requests help eliminating the Blood Eagles, including [[Star]] and taking down their triad of leaders: [[The Blood]], [[The Eye]], and [[Frankie Beckett|The Claw]], while also making amends with Edwin's gang and getting their support when taking on the Blood Eagles at their main base in the [[Watoga Underground]]. Beckett's motive is also to rescue Frankie after hearing his brother's life is being threatened by the Blood Eagles. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |ghost = |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |ally =yes |allyfurn =[[Beckett's bar]] |perk = |wares =*Food *Nuka-Cola *Alcohol |caps =1200 |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started ={{Bull}}[[Narrow Escape]]

[[Bethy Mangano/Dialogue|Bethy Mangano's dialogue]]) camped in a tent behind the [[Clarksburg]] church. ==Background== Prior to the [[Great War]], Dr. Mangano was a professor of soil sciences. Her mother always told her to thank people who compliment her.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"[Charisma 12+] Do you have a map? I've gotten lost in your eyes."''
Bethy Mangano: ''"{{Tooltip|Well, aren't you a charmer? My mama always said I should thank those that compliment me. So, thank you. But, I know I'm not much to look at now.|Preface line with a giggle/snort. She's flattered but knows she's hideous looking now and a little sad about that.}} {{Tooltip|Your words are a kindness. I can go into really toxic places without fear of radiation. So, that's nice.|Bucking up, trying to be cheerful and assertive that it's not all bad.}}"''
[[Bethy Mangano/Dialogue|Bethy Mangano's dialogue]]) She can recite the Friedrich Nietzsche quote, "Wake and listen! Verily, the earth shall yet be a source of recovery. Remain faithful to the earth, with the power of your virtue."A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"[Intelligence 8+] Looks like you're taking some soil samples. Is your interest edaphological or pedological?"''
Bethy Mangano: ''"{{Tooltip|Both! But right now, my focus has to be edaphology. We need to be able to reclaim these lands and grow crops even in the most toxic of environments.|Surprised and very happy that the player knows these terms. Warming up to an enthusiastic conversation about dirt.}}"''
A Vault Dweller: ''"[Intelligence 12+] To quote Blake, 'Ah, to see a world in a grain of sand and a heaven in a wildflower.'"''
Bethy Mangano: ''"I couldn't agree more. The structure and complexity is a source of never-ending wonder for those with the capacity to see it. {{Tooltip|'Wake and listen! Verily, the earth shall yet be a source of recovery. Remain faithful to the earth, with the power of your virtue.' Nietzsche saw it.|Reverant. This quote is really meaningful to her. It inspires her work.}} {{Tooltip|And you see it too, I can tell.|Satisfied and grateful to have found someone that understands her passion.}}"''
A Vault Dweller: ''"Yes, I do. What a beautiful sentiment."''
Bethy Mangano: ''"{{Tooltip|Yes. Even in my darkest moments, when the despair that the War has wrought creeps into my mind and tries to overwhelm me, I remember those words.|Revealing something deeply personal and sad.}} {{Tooltip|I can make a difference. My life's path has brought me to this one moment in time where my knowledge and expertise can save real people.|Thoughtful and inspired. Maybe even a bit thankful.}} {{Tooltip|I mean, real people. Not the abstracted people in a data cohort. Real, struggling people.|emphatic and getting emotional, then embarrassed about that.}} {{Tooltip|I do go on, don't I? Here, have this specimen. [[Bethy Mangano/Dialogue|Bethy Mangano's dialogue]]) When the War struck, she was exposed to massive amounts of radiation and became a ghoul, but was otherwise physically unharmed. Being a ghoul hurt her self-esteem in regards to her beauty, but still feels it is better than being dead, and likes how she can enter toxic places without fear of radiation. She tries to remain optimistic and polite,Bethy Mangano: ''"{{Tooltip|Good to see you again. I hope you've managed to avoid unnecessary brain damage while wandering?|Earnest, doesn't intend to offend and is genuinely pleased to see the player again and hopes to talk about science.}}"''
[[Bethy Mangano/Dialogue|Bethy Mangano's dialogue]])Bethy Mangano: ''"{{Tooltip|Greetings and salutations!|Not really excited about visitors but trying to be polite and vaguely jovial.}}"''
[[Bethy Mangano/Dialogue|Bethy Mangano's dialogue]])Bethy Mangano: ''"{{Tooltip|Welcome friend, to my lonely patch of irradiated soil.|Forced cheerfulness. Not terribly interested in meeting other people. She's busy.}}"''
[[Bethy Mangano/Dialogue|Bethy Mangano's dialogue]])Bethy Mangano: ''"{{Tooltip|HELLO THERE! I hope you can hear me through that helmet.|Speaking loudly initially to a player in a power armor helmet. The second part is a bit under her breath and almost to herself.}}"''
[[Bethy Mangano/Dialogue|Bethy Mangano's dialogue]])Bethy Mangano: ''"{{Tooltip|Nice to see you again.|Polite for the sake of being polite.}}"''
[[Bethy Mangano/Dialogue|Bethy Mangano's dialogue]])Bethy Mangano: ''"{{Tooltip|You're back for more sparkling conversation, I guess.|Self deprecating tone.}}"''
[[Bethy Mangano/Dialogue|Bethy Mangano's dialogue]]) especially when the despair of the post-apocalyptic world sinks in, and she reminds herself she can make a difference in the world.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You're a ghoul! What happened?"''

'''Davenport''' is a [[Mister Handy (Fallout 76)|Mister Handy]] in the [[overseer's home]].

==Background==
Davenport performed reconnaissance work for the [[Vault 76 overseer]] while she went into hiding. In the time between [[Timeline#2102|Reclamation Day]] and 2103, Davenport became a trusted companion of the overseer.

As of 2103, he has taken up residence in the basement of the overseer's home, helping her plan for how best to deal with the inevitable return of people to [[Appalachia]].
