==Behind the scenes==
* Between his name, role, and the fact that he is always floating next to a prominent map, he is probably named for [https://theadventurezone.fandom.com/wiki/Davenport Davenport the navigator] from ''[https://theadventurezone.fandom.com/wiki/Campaign_1:_The_Balance_Arc?so=search The Adventure Zone]'', a podcast by [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Brother,_My_Brother_and_Me the McElroy Brothers]. The character is in turn named for a fan, [https://mbmbam.fandom.com/wiki/Drew_Davenport Drew Davenport].
** There was previously a large tribute to the McElroy Brothers in the form of the [[riverside cottage]], which alludes heavily to the ''Fallout 4'' episodes of the ''Monster Factory'' web series.
** The McElroy Brothers are prominent West Virginians, and were honorarily considered mayors of Huntington for one day in 2017, when they held a parade to improve public perception of tarantulas.
** Season 2 of ''The Adventure Zone'' takes place in West Virginia.

Doctor Dorothea Dias lives again!|sound=Doctor Dias 00407f27_1.ogg}} '''Doctor Dias''' is a pre-[[Great War|War]] scientist in the [[RobCo Research Center]], whose still-living brain remains preserved there. ==Background== At some point before the war, Doctor Dias devised the Encephalon Extraction Program, a part of RobCo Industries' Semi-Autonomous Immobile Weapon Platform Research. The project ensured that the entire research team of the facility would have their brains scooped and suspended in a biomedical solution which would keep their cognitive functions intact and ready to be used for several lifetimes.[[RobCo Research Center terminal entries#Good news, everyone!]] The project was approved by [[RobCo Industries|RobCo]], despite the ethics department and the other scientists objecting to the idea. Her [[Doctor Dias's brain|brain]] was one of the ones that were removed and stored in preservation vials, but because of the Great War, it was never installed into a [[robobrain]]. The player character can choose between hers and two more brains to install into a robobrain. She is incredibly proud and arrogant, and despite being the leader of the RobCo team which designed the [[Automated turret (Fallout 76)|automated turrets]] used in [[Vault 79]], she relishes the opportunity to one up her original work on the turrets by dismantling them. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO4 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Duty Calls]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Duty Calls]]: Dr. Dias is one of three brains who can be chosen for installation into a robobrain, the others being [[Gina Bailey]] and [[Greg Goldstein]]. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Doctor Dias appears only {{In|FO76WL}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} {{Navbox cyborgs}} [[Category:Wastelanders robots and computers]] [[Category:Robobrain characters]] [[Category:RobCo Industries characters]]

'''Dylan Rhodes''' is a man living in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
Dylan is a former miner from [[Welch]]. He grew up in the town before it was destroyed by mining under orders of [[Atomic Mining Services]] and the subsequent [[Great War]]. Dylan intends to live out his remaining years in what's left of Welch and see where it leads him.

He also has become very anti-social, not wanting to spend much time speaking with visitors due to his bitterness over his job being taken over by automatons. He also mentions everyone he ever loved and cared about is dead.

Frida Madani.wikitext:
{{Infobox incomplete|FO76}} {{Infobox character |games =FO76, FO76WL |image =FO76 Frida Madani.jpg |race =[[Ghoul]] |sex =Female |affiliation =[[Garrahan Mining Company]] (pre-War) |role =Receptionist (former) |location =[[Garrahan Estate]] |level = |derived = |actor =[[Artemis Pebdani]] |dialogue =[[Frida Madani/Dialogue]] |edid = |formid ={{ID|00599459}} |refid ={{ID|0059945b}} }} {{Quotation|I've got a better house than I could ever afford, and all it took was the apocalypse.|sound=Frida Madani 0059944d_1.ogg}} '''Frida Madani''' is a [[ghoul]] in [[Appalachia]] {{In|FO76WL}}. She can be found in the lobby of the [[Garrahan Estate]]. ==Background== Frida used to work at the [[Garrahan Mining headquarters]] as a receptionist before the [[Great War]], getting to know the company executives well enough to occasionally be invited to high-class events.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Did you know the Garrahans?"''
Frida Madani: ''"I did, and better than a lot of people, in fact. I worked at Garrahan HQ before the war. A receptionist. I got to know some of the higher-ups pretty well. Get in with people like that and you get invited to a cocktail party or two."''
([[Frida Madani/Dialogue#29|Frida Madani's dialogue]]) This position also made her privy to some of the Garrahan family's internal affairs, such as [[Isaac Garrahan]]'s sloth obsession.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Must have been fun while it lasted, though."''
Frida Madani: ''"{{Tooltip|I can vouch for that. Their parties were a hoot.|Laughing}} But money can create as many problems as it solves. Sometimes more. You don't hear about poor kids developing sloth obsessions, for instance."''
([[Frida Madani/Dialogue#33|Frida Madani's dialogue]]) She is mixed about her feelings regarding the Garrahan family, as she dislikes how they profited off their miners' labor to live in luxury while billing themselves as champions of the working class, but notes that they were friendly in-person and she herself had a comfortable job, as well as a soft spot for the family.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What's your opinion of the Garrahans?"''
Frida Madani: ''"I have mixed feelings. They lived a life of luxury up there, built on the backs of those hard working miners of theirs. On the other hand, they paid my salary and were friendly enough in person. I wasn't exactly slaving away in the pits, either, so how resentful can I be? Especially now that I'm alive and they're long gone."''
([[Frida Madani/Dialogue#26|Frida Madani's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"They got what was coming to them."''
Frida Madani: ''"In some ways, you're right. I have a soft spot for the Garrahans, but I can't deny that their wealth came at a cost. They tried to bill themselves as the champions of the working stiff, but none of their miners lived like this."''
([[Frida Madani/Dialogue#36|Frida Madani's dialogue]]) After the Great War, around the time when the [[Scorched Plague]] ravaged Appalachia, she managed to escape to the [[East Coast|coast]]. However, the conditions and radiation there were far worse than Appalachia, turning her into a ghoul.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How did you survive the War?"''
Frida Madani: ''"I was lucky. I hid, and when those red monsters showed up, I fled east. But the coast is bad. Very bad. It was hit a lot harder than home was. So when people started flooding back, I came back as well. I wasn't unscathed, of course. I became what I am today. A ghoul. And that hasn't made life any easier."''
([[Frida Madani/Dialogue#23|Frida Madani's dialogue]]) She is frustrated at the discrimination she faces as a ghoul and fears turning [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|feral]] eventually.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What's life like as a ghoul?"''
Frida Madani: ''"For one thing, you're never given the benefit of the doubt. Something's stolen? Instant suspect. I guess it's hard to keep an open mind about someone that looks like they'd eat you at the first opportunity, but it's still frustrating. But the worst part? Every time you see one of those feral monsters, you wonder. What separates them from me? Will that be me, someday? That's hard to live with."''
([[Frida Madani/Dialogue#19|Frida Madani's dialogue]]) When people went west, Frida decided to go with them. As of [[Timeline#2103|2103]] Frida spends her time wandering around the ground floor of the [[Garrahan Estate]] and digging through the Garrahans' former belongings, such as drinking plenty of [[Vivian Garrahan]]'s wine collection.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"[Luck 4+] Think they left anything good laying around here?"''
Frida Madani: ''"{{Tooltip|Well, now that you mention it, I did happen to chance upon some of Vivian Garrahan's old vintage.|tip=Viv = Vivian Garrahan}} {{Tooltip|She always did know her wine. Here, have some. I've had plenty already.|Gives player a bottle of wine}}"''
([[Frida Madani/Dialogue#16|Frida Madani's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved = }} ===Effects of player's actions=== Passing a [[Luck (Fallout 76)|Luck]] 4+ check will prompt her to give the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] a bottle of [[Wine (Fallout 76)|wine]] which she claims is some of Vivian Garrahan's vintage. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = [[Hooded rags (Fallout 76)|Hooded rags]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|Interested in the lives of the rich and famous?|sound=Frida Madani 0059944f_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|You got that right. Get lost!|sound=Fritz 005994b3_1.ogg}} '''Fritz''' is a former [[Crater Raiders|Crater Raider]] living at [[the Whitespring]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Once a raider, Fritz has denounced that type of life, in favor of the posh and fancy lifestyle of the pre-[[Great War|War]] elites, largely because he is bored. He dresses in a golf outfit he found on one of the bodies in the Whitespring, and spends his days at the [[The Whitespring driving range|driving range]] just down the road from [[the Whitespring Golf Club]]. He puts on a fake [[United Kingdom|British]] accent, yet if a speech check is passed, the player character can remark on the curiosity of the situation, leading to him abandoning the accent and confessing his ruse, before returning to the facade.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"[Perception 4+] Love your little get-up. Did you loot it off some bodies around here?"''
Fritz: ''"Get-up? Well, I never-! Alright, you got me. I'm a Raider who's got nothing better to do, okay? I spend my days fending off irradiated montrosities to survive, anyway. Why not make some fun out of it?"'' ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved = }} ===Other interactions=== Fritz will engage in dialogue about himself and the perks of being wealthy, on top of providing background information about the Whitespring. If a [[Perception (Fallout 76)|Perception]] check of 4 is successfully completed, he will reveal himself, though he will continue to speak in his phony accent, even after this check is passed. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Golf outfit]]

My robot body doesn't seem to experience pain. That's different. I can't feel anything actually.|sound=Gina Bailey 0056bf12_1.ogg}} '''Gina Bailey''' is a pre-[[Great War|War]] employee of the [[RobCo Research Center]] whose still-living brain remains preserved there in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Gina is a RobCo intern who committed suicide by electrocuting herself. Her [[Gina's brain|brain]] was one of the ones that were removed and stored in preservation vials, but because of the Great War, it was never installed into a [[robobrain]]. The player character can choose between hers and two more brains to install into a robobrain. As part of the RobCo team which designed the [[Automated turret (Fallout 76)|automated turrets]] used in [[Vault 79]], Gina is familiar with the technology and can easily create tools to disarm them. She can be helped by convincing her to hurt RobCo by helping dismantle the turrets with Charisma 8+ or by adjusting her brain's dopamine and serotonin levels with Intelligence 12+. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Duty Calls]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Duty Calls]]: Gina is one of three brains who can be chosen for installation into a robobrain, the others being [[Dorothea Dias|Doctor Dorothea Dias]] and [[Greg Goldstein]]. ==Appearances== Gina Bailey appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]'', introduced in the ''[[Wastelanders]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. {{Navbox Wastelanders}} {{Navbox cyborgs}} [[Category:Wastelanders robots and computers]] [[Category:Robobrain characters]] [[Category:RobCo Industries characters]]

Gilbert Hopson.wikitext:
{{Infobox character |games =FO76, FO76WL |image =FO76 Gilbert Hopson.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |family =[[Millicent]] - wife {{Icon|dead}} |affiliation = |role =Researcher |location =[[Vault-Tec University]] |quests = |level =66 |derived = |actor =[[Chris Ciulla]] |dialogue =[[Gilbert Hopson/Dialogue]] |edid =W05_GilbertHopson |formid ={{ID|00596e59}} |refid ={{ID|00000000}} }} {{Quotation|Ah, what a magnificent place this once was. The very epicenter of learning here in Appalachia. Truly, nothing is as valuable as a good education.|sound=Gilbert Hopson 00596e44_1.ogg}} '''Gilbert Hopson''' is a former teacher from [[Monroe (location)|Monroe, Connecticut]]. He can be found outside the entrance of [[Vault-Tec University]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Before the war, Gilbert taught high school history and literature, considering it a great joy, even if he taught only a few interested students.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What did you do before the war?"''
Gilbert Hopson: ''"{{Tooltip|I was a teacher. History and literature were my subjects. It always brought me great joy to illuminate the eager minds of children.|Cheerful, a happy memory}} Well, for the few who were interested, at any rate. High school students are easily distracted, I'm afraid."''
([[W05 Gilbert Hopson.txt|Gilbert Hopson's dialogue]]) He and his wife, [[Millicent]], enjoyed Sunday bicycle rides and pint samplings at the local brewery.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Where are you from?"''
Gilbert Hopson: ''"{{Tooltip|Up north. Connecticut. A small town called Monroe, named for the fifth president of the United States.|Happy to make conversation and reminisce}} It was quite lovely, especially in the autumn. My wife and I used to ride the bicycle trails on Sundays and then visit the local brewery for a pint. {{Tooltip|Ah, I do miss those days. And I miss my Millie, may she rest in everlasting peace.|A note of sadness about losing your wife}}"''
([[W05 Gilbert Hopson.txt|Gilbert Hopson's dialogue]]) After the [[Great War]], Millicent passed away, due to cancer likely caused by [[radiation]]. Due to her passing, Gilbert was left depressed, but decided to set himself on a mission. Once he had adapted to the post-War world, he decided to visit every great learning institution in [[United States of America|America]] that remained intact, bringing him to VTU for the time being.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What brings you to Appalachia?"''
Gilbert Hopson: ''"{{Tooltip|That's a bit of a story. Not long after the war, I lost my wife Millicent to cancer, likely brought on by the radiation.|Looking back with sadness}} Every day I questioned whether to go on living at all. Without her, the days were empty, devoid of any purpose beyond the simple need to survive. But in time, once I'd learned to adapt to living in the world after the bombs, I decided to set a new goal for myself. I set out to visit those great American centers of learning that still remained intact. I've always felt at home in such places. And so, here I am, at least for a while."''
([[W05 Gilbert Hopson.txt|Gilbert Hopson's dialogue]]) Despite the rumors and controversies about the company and the nature of the [[Vault]]s, Gilbert considers the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] to effectively be the saviors of the remnants of humanity, as Vaults allowed for rebuilding and survival, dismissing the rumors as normal for any large corporation. However, the one fault he has for the company lies in its corporate branding of the university.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you think about the Vault-Tec corporation?"''
Gilbert Hopson: ''"{{Tooltip|Well, I'd start by saying that without Vault-Tec, humanity would be lost. The Vaults saved precious lives and gave us a chance to rebuild.|Proud}} Now, we all heard about the rumors and controversies, but what large corporation doesn't have to cope with such things from time to time? {{Tooltip|As far as I'm concerned, the only real blemish on Vault-Tec's record is the rather shameless corporate branding on display here at VTU.|Disdain, haughty disapproval}}"''
([[W05 Gilbert Hopson.txt|Gilbert Hopson's dialogue]]) By [[Timeline#2103|2103]], Gilbert stands outside of the main building of [[Vault-Tec University]] near his camp, which is behind the VTU statue. He had met with the [[Vault 76 overseer]] recently, having a pleasant conversation with her, and is able to tell the player about it.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"I'm here to meet someone, a woman with glasses and gray hair. Have you seen her?"''
Gilbert Hopson: ''"Not only have I seen her, we had a pleasant conversation just a short while ago. She went inside the school. I do hope she's safe."''
([[W05 Gilbert Hopson.txt|Gilbert Hopson's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions univ |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Overseer, Overseen]] }} ===Effects of player's actions=== * Using the [[Intelligence (Fallout 76)|Intelligence]] 8+ option upon one's first meeting impresses him enough[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"[Intelligence 8+] As Benjamin Franklin once said, an investment in knowledge pays the best interest."''
Gilbert Hopson: ''"{{Tooltip|Well said! Well said, indeed! It's so good to meet a fellow devotee of the humanities.|Enthusiastic}} I don't mind saying that enlightened minds such as yours and mine are in desperately short supply of late."''
([[W05 Gilbert Hopson.txt|Gilbert Hopson's dialogue]]) that upon using the next Intelligence 8+ option available, he will happily hand over some supplies to the [[Vault 76]] [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"[Intelligence 8+] Got any supplies you could share with a fellow enlightened mind?"''
Gilbert Hopson: ''"{{Tooltip|Normally, I'd have to politely refuse your request, but I think we've forged a bond, you and I.|Friendly}} {{Tooltip|We're like two sailors navigating a stormy ocean of ignorance on a dark night, seeking the bright beacon of knowledge to guide us to safe harbor.|Waxing poetic}}"''
([[W05 Gilbert Hopson.txt|Gilbert Hopson's dialogue]]) * With [[Strength (Fallout 76)|Strength]] 8+, one can instead rob Gilbert and demand that he hand over the supplies, as the player character "will hit a man with glasses."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"[Strength 8+] I need supplies and you're going to give them to me, because I will hit a man with glasses."''
Gilbert Hopson: ''"{{Tooltip|Now now, there's no need for violence. I'm happy to help.|A bit flustered and scared, you've just been threatened}} {{Tooltip|After all, as Dickens once wrote, no one is useless in this world who lightens the burdens of another.|Flustered, intimidated. You've been threatened into giving the player supplies.}} Here, have these with my compliments."''
([[W05 Gilbert Hopson.txt|Gilbert Hopson's dialogue]]) ===Other Interactions=== If spoken to during the quest [[Overseer, Overseen]], he will mention meeting the [[Vault 76 overseer]] and direct the player to her location. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Eyeglasses (Fallout 76)|Eyeglasses]]
[[Patched three-piece suit (Fallout 76)|Patched three-piece suit]]
[[Trilby hat (Fallout 76)|Trilby hat]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notable quotes== * {{inline quote|Welcome once more to the hallowed grounds of Vault-Tec University.|sound=Gilbert Hopson 00596e4e_1.ogg}} * {{inline quote|I imagine this campus was quite lovely once.|sound=Gilbert Hopson 00596e51_1.ogg}} * {{inline quote|You can almost hear the hustle and bustle of students gathering, talking, and rushing to get to class.|sound=Gilbert Hopson 00596e52_1.ogg}} * {{inline quote|The school's quite intact. That's a pleasant surprise.|sound=Gilbert Hopson 00596e53_1.ogg}} * {{inline quote|This institution was quite prestigious in its day.|sound=Gilbert Hopson 00596e54_1.ogg}} ==Appearances== Gilbert Hopson appears {{In|FO76WL}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[ru:Гилберт Хопсон]]

I guess I'm free? Like, they can't do anything worse to me-this is actually a huge relief. I feel like I could do anything!|sound=Greg Goldstein 0056bf0c_1.ogg}} '''Greg Goldstein''' is a pre-[[Great War|War]] employee of the [[RobCo Research Center]] whose still-living brain remains preserved there in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Greg is described as a "truly unremarkable" and "perfectly normal mind" to talk to, as long as the extraction of [[Greg's brain|his brain]] didn't traumatize him.[[Greg's brain]] message description: ''"This is a truly unremarkable brain, in the best possible sense. Assuming the extraction process didn't traumatize him, Greg Goldstein should be a perfectly normal mind to talk to."'' In fact, Greg's pre-War job in [[RobCo Industries]]' Immobile Weapons Research team has left him extremely neurotic, unstable and fearful of his boss Dr. [[Dorothea Dias]], who dictated the designers' testing to her exact specifications and changed them every day. His brain extraction was scheduled for October 23, 2077, the day of the Great War, but he obeyed even with the bombs falling because he feared Dr. Dias more than the apocalypse.Greg Goldstein: ''"I came in to the office when the bombs were falling because I was scheduled and I feared her more than the Great War."''
([[Greg Goldstein/Dialogue#125|Greg Goldstein's dialogue]]) As part of the RobCo team which designed the [[Automated turret (Fallout 76)|automated turrets]] used in [[Vault 79]], Greg is highly familiar with the technology and can easily create tools to disarm them. His experiences at work have left him with little goodwill for his boss and his workplace, and if installed into a [[Robobrain (Fallout 76)|Robobrain]], Greg intends to seize the opportunity to take his revenge on both.Greg Goldstein: ''"I bet her brain is stored somewhere. Might as well go destroy it or maybe... hmm... experiment on it! Yeah!"''
([[Greg Goldstein/Dialogue#156|Greg Goldstein's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Duty Calls]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Duty Calls]]: Greg is one of three brains who can chosen for installation into a Robobrain, the others being [[Gina Bailey]] and [[Dorothea Dias]]. He can be used to produce [[RobCo tools|military spec RobCo tools]] to disarm [[Vault 79]]'s automated turrets. ==Appearances== Greg Goldstein appears only {{In|FO76WL}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} {{Navbox cyborgs}} [[Category:Wastelanders robots and computers]] [[Category:Robobrain characters]] [[Category:RobCo Industries characters]]

I've even met some people who say they came from there, and honestly, I believe them. It's so interesting, people living underground for years and then the doors open and suddenly there's this whole new world to explore. So, did I guess right?|sound=Heather Ellis 0057757c_1.ogg}} '''Heather Ellis''' is a resident of [[Flatwoods]] in [[Appalachia]] trying to resurrect and continue the legacy of the [[Responders]]. ==Background== Heather traveled to Appalachia with [[Paige]] and the rest of the original [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|settlers]] of [[Foundation]]. After some time, she decided to go out on her own and explore, although the trip from Foundation to Flatwoods was incredibly dangerous,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Tell me about Foundation."''
Heather Ellis: ''"It's a community of settlers up in the mountains to the east. It's a nice enough place, I guess. That being said, it's a hell of a dangerous trip trying to get there. I barely made it out of the mountains alive. If I were you, I'd keep to the forest until you're ready to deal with some seriously nasty stuff."''
([[Heather Ellis/Dialogue|Heather Ellis' dialogue]]) hoping to discover something about herself in the process. Although the Responders were wiped out by the [[Scorched]] prior to 2103, Heather discovered their story when she arrived in Flatwoods after following the Responders' radio broadcast. Admiring their purpose, she decided to stay in Flatwoods to see what else she could learn.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Tell me about yourself."''
Heather Ellis: ''"Me? There's not that much to tell, really. I came in with Paige and the rest, and stayed up at Foundation for awhile. It was nice. But eventually I wanted to go my own way, you know? Get out and see some places I've never seen, figure out who I am. When I heard the message on the radio about Flatwoods, I was curious to meet the Responders, so I made my way here. Of course, they were long gone by then, but I was interested in the work they'd been doing. The more I learned about them, the more I admired them. I decided to stay here and see what else I could learn. That's pretty much my story."''
([[Heather Ellis/Dialogue|Heather Ellis' dialogue]]) Although the Responders were killed during the Scorched attack of [[Morgantown Airport]], Ellis considers the group to have been very noble and brave for not running away, instead heroically sacrificing themselves to save others and help them survive in order to do what was right.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"They must really have cared about helping people to set up a training program."''
Heather Ellis: ''"{{Tooltip|Absolutely! Even in the face of an atomic holocaust, the Responders only thought about helping other people. They saved a lot of lives, and even when everything looked hopeless, they didn't stop trying to do what was right.|Admiration, hero worship}} {{Tooltip|It's a real tragedy that they're all gone now. People like us will never have the chance to thank them for everything they did.|Admiration, hero worship, a bit sad}}"''
([[Heather Ellis/Dialogue|Heather Ellis' dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Doesn't look like training saved any of them."''
Heather Ellis: ''"{{Tooltip|That's a really insensitive thing to say. Those people risked their lives every day to help people survive. I think they were incredibly noble. And yes, as far as anyone knows, they were all killed when the Scorched attacked their base at Morgantown Airport. But that death wasn't a failure, it was a sacrifice, and a really heroic one, if you ask me. They could have run, but they didn't.|Surprise and disappointment,the player has criticized your heroes}} I guess you must not have been around when the Responders were here, or you'd know all of this."''
([[Heather Ellis/Dialogue|Heather Ellis' dialogue]]) She also wears a Responder outfit she found in a nearby house, out of sentimental and admirable values for what the Responders were and stood for, hoping to one day see a new generation of Responders.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What's with the Responder outfit?"''
Heather Ellis: ''"I found it in one of the houses. It fits great, and it's really comfortable and pretty durable, too. I'd also be lying if I said it didn't have some sentimental value for me. I've admired the Responders ever since I first heard about them. {{Tooltip|What they stood for - helping people no matter what - that was really important.|Admiration}} Who knows, maybe someday there can be a new generation of Responders. I'd like to see that."''
([[Heather Ellis/Dialogue|Heather Ellis' dialogue]]) She can be found near the Flatwoods Church with her [[Dog (Fallout 76)|dog]], [[Chloe (Wastelanders)|Chloe]]. During her time at Flatwoods, she has met several [[Vault 76]] dwellers[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"[Perception 4+] You've got a good eye. What gave it away?"''
Heather Ellis: ''"To be honest, you don't really have the look and feel of someone who's spent their life out here in the wilds. The other people I've met from Vault 76 seemed a little more... how to put it... wide-eyed. Inexperienced. Still figuring things out, you know? They also tend to look healthier, more well-fed, and their skin's not so rough and calloused."''
([[Heather Ellis/Dialogue|Heather Ellis' dialogue]]) and become familiar with nearby areas of interest.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Anything interesting you can tell me about this area?"''
Heather Ellis: ''"Yeah, there's a couple of places around here that qualify as interesting, at least to me. The Agricultural Research Center is infested with Feral Ghouls and homicidal robots, but you can find some good scrap in there if you're up to it. The New River Gorge Resort to the east is the same story, maybe minus the robots. Oh, and I found a note about a place called Gauley Mine, which I think is northeast of here. I'm {{sic}} haven't checked it out yet."''
([[Heather Ellis/Dialogue|Heather Ellis' dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved = }} ===Other interactions=== She can be asked multiple questions about Flatwoods and her past. She also notes that coming to Flatwoods from [[Foundation]] was difficult and advises the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|player character]] not to go up there until they are properly equipped. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Responders paramedic jumpsuit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Notes== Heather was the first known living Responder added into the game, alongside [[Fire Breathers|Fire Breather]] [[Tiffany Brantley]]. Later, new living Responders such as [[Rucker]] and [[Sophie Wagoner]] would be added to [[the Whitespring Refuge]] with the ''[[Expeditions: The Pitt]]'' update. ==Appearances== Heather Ellis appears {{In|FO76WL}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} {{Navbox Responders}} {{Navbox Foundation}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Responder characters]] [[Category:Settler characters]] [[Category:Flatwoods]] [[ru:Хэзер Эллис]]

'''Isela Mejia''' is a woman exploring the [[wasteland]] in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
Curious explorers from the ruins of Virginia, Isela and [[Lacey Drummond|Lacey]] have set themselves up outside of [[Vault 76]], seeking answers for the questions that brought them to Appalachia in the first place. They heard news on a broadcast about a buried treasure, but the details of it were vague. Prior to their arrival, in exchange for a lead about the treasure, the two were apparently scammed out of the last of their [[Cap (Fallout 76)|caps]] by a man at [[the Wayward]], who Lacey recalls being named "Carter". Isela and Lacey have not been in Appalachia for long, but noticed the area was hit hard; despite this, she mentions Appalachia is still better than their previous travels.

'''James Addison''' is a deceased member of [[the Whitespring Resort]] staff whose body can be found in [[the Deep]] in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
After the Whitespring Resort suffered several minor earthquakes for unknown reasons, James became convinced that they were unnatural and set off to find their source despite being mocked by his coworkers. Diving into the cave systems below the Whitespring, he came across the [[Motherlode Acquisition Facility]], but mistook it for an "underground spaceship."

He decided that it was necessary to tell the [[Last President of the United States|president]] about his discovery and believed that he would be commended as a hero on his return.<ref>[[President's eyes ONLY]]</ref> However, he died before he could tell anyone of his discovery.

Jonah Ito: ''"My parents are long gone. Killed during the War. {{Tooltip|My sister, Kaede, was a Brotherhood Knight. The best of them, without a doubt. She was so determined to see the world through to a better future.|Kai-ey-day}} So she fought for it, here at Fort Defiance. Now I get to see the future, and she doesn't."''
([[Jonah Ito/Dialogue#10|Jonah Ito's dialogue]]) After the Great War, Kaede joined the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]] to help fight the [[Scorched]], asking her brother to join with her. Jonah refused his sister's offer to join and instead ran away.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Aren't you worried about your safety?"''
Jonah Ito: ''"Why should I be? I've got nothing to live for anymore. {{Tooltip|When the Scorched came to Appalachia, I ran away. Kaede wanted me to join the Brotherhood with her, but I was afraid to fight. Afraid to die.|Kai-ey-day}} Now I see it's better to die for something than to live for nothing."''
([[Jonah Ito/Dialogue#16|Jonah Ito's dialogue]]) When the Brotherhood fell to the Scorched, his sister died, making her last stand at [[Fort Defiance]],[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What's wrong?"''
Jonah Ito: ''"{{Tooltip|It's... It's my sister... (sob) I thought I was over this already.|The player's question suddenly unleashes another torrent of tears}} She took her final stand here... at Fort Defiance. I should have been here with her. I'm such a coward."''
([[Jonah Ito/Dialogue#30|Jonah Ito's dialogue]]) and leaving Jonah with a deep hatred of the creatures.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you know about the Scorched?"''
Jonah Ito: ''"{{Tooltip|That they're monsters. They'll kill anything and everything that isn't them! And for what? What's the reason?|Overwhelmed by anger}} What's the reason that my sister had to die? {{Tooltip|Sorry... It just feels so cruel. To answer your question, I don't know much.|Regaining his composure}}"''
([[Jonah Ito/Dialogue#19|Jonah Ito's dialogue]]) By [[Timeline#2103|2103]], Jonah can be found mourning his sister in Fort Defiance. Jonah mourns his sister's death and regrets not joining the fight with her. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved = }} ===Other interactions=== {{Missing data|Charisma check|FO76}} Passing a Strength 4+ check on first meeting him to try and get him to toughen up will prompt him to refuse, but also hand over several random aid items. ==Inventory== {{Missing data|Inventory|FO76}} {{Inventory |apparel =[[Winter jacket and jeans (Fallout 76)|Winter jacket and jeans]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Jonah Ito appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]'', introduced in the ''[[Wastelanders]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. ==Behind the scenes== Jonah's surname Ito, as well as his sister's name Kaede, are of [[Japan|Japanese]] origin. '''Kelemen''' is a deactivated [[Mister Handy (Fallout 76)|Mister Handy]] at [[Vault-Tec University]] in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
A Mister Handy playing the role of apprentice to [[Brass|Head Engineer Brass]], Kelemen rushed in to fix the reactor to prevent radiation from overrunning the vault. Worried about contamination, [[Loris|Doctor Loris]] sealed the reactor wing with him inside, dooming Kelemen to death. This would become the bone of contention between Loris and her well-trained medical staff and the engineers. For his part, Kelemen and [[Estella]] sacrificed their lives to save the vault.

'''Agent Kensington''' is a [[glowing one]] and [[United States government|federal agent]] in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
Agent Kensington was a member of an unknown spy agency stationed at Listening Station 4D-20, which was secretly located in the basement of the farmhouse at [[Solomon's pond]]. Kensington worked with [[Sawyer Lang]] and [[Enrique Gómez]] and had a security level of 5, which allowed access to the holotape repair terminal located inside the basement.<ref>[[Solomon's pond terminal entries#Holotape repair terminal|Solomon's pond terminal entries; holotape repair terminal]]</ref> At some point either during or after the [[Great War]], Kensington became a [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)#Glowing one|glowing feral ghoul]], though remained at the listening station.

'''Lacey Drummond''' is a woman exploring the [[wasteland]] in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
Curious explorers from the ruins of Virginia, Lacey and [[Isela Mejia]] have set themselves up outside of [[Vault 76]], seeking answers for the questions that brought them to Appalachia in the first place. They heard news on a broadcast about a buried treasure, but the details of it were vague. Prior to their arrival, in exchange for a lead about the treasure, the two were apparently scammed out of the last of their [[Cap (Fallout 76)|caps]] by a man at [[the Wayward]] who she recalls being named "Carter". Lacey and Isela have not been in Appalachia for long, but noticed the area was hit hard; despite this, she mentions Appalachia is still better than their previous travels.

If you're going to destroy the world, at least do it properly and eliminate our parasitic species for good.|sound=Maram Ayari.ogg}} '''Maram Ayari''' is a [[robot]] enthusiast who lives in [[Watoga]]. ==Background== Maram is old enough to remember life before the [[Great War]]. A misanthrope, she never truly understood people and grew to believe that [[human]]s were inefficient and parasitic, mentioning that plenty of people were rude and judgemental to her. Before the Great War, she was fired after she told her boss that his code was terrible and needed to be reworked.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What's so bad about humans?"''
Maram Ayari: ''"I've never understood humans. They're always hurting each other. And they're really inefficient. If you're going to destroy the world, at least do it properly and eliminate our parasitic species for good. You know, before the War, I once got fired for telling my boss that his code was a pile of crap and needed to be reworked. But it was true!"''
([[Maram Ayari/Dialogue|Maram Ayari's dialogue]]) In contrast, she became obsessed with [[robot]]s, due to their straightforward, no-nonsense approach to their clearly defined purpose(s). She also thinks they are cute.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Why do you love robots so much?"''
Maram Ayari: ''"They exist for a purpose, and they do that purpose well. No if, ands, or buts about it. Well, sometimes there are 'ifs' and 'ands', but with any luck they're well-documented, and- Point is, robots always make sense. Anything they do, they do for a reason. I'd prefer if the whole world functioned that way. Plus, they're cutie-pies!"''
([[Maram Ayari/Dialogue|Maram Ayari's dialogue]]) Her obsession has long since become a fetish, as she has a particular love for the imposing [[sentry bot]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What's your favorite type of robot?"''
Maram Ayari: ''"Oh, dear. How could I possibly choose? Protectrons are charming. Simple, quaint design, marching ever forward on a single directive. But Handys are so versatile! So many possible attachments. Eh, but the human personality thing really drops their point value. Eyebots? Boring. Liberators - too political. Robobrains - creepy. Ohoho, Assaultrons... now those pack some grievous power. Buuut I don't like the humanoid body. {{Tooltip|I got it. Sentry Bots. Massive. Commanding. Powerful. Really the whole package.|THICC}}"''
([[Maram Ayari/Dialogue|Maram Ayari's dialogue]]) She eventually traveled to [[Watoga]], snuck past the robots protecting [[MAIA]] and [[Mayor for a Day|made the robots not view her as a threat]]. Now that the robots are running with her as an exception to their "kill everything" directive she resides at the [[Watoga Transit Hub]] and spends her time tinkering with robots. She enjoys role playing as a robot and uses the term "fleshlings" in reference to other people who encounter her. She is perfectly happy with living out her days in Watoga and never encountering human beings again. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Mayor for a Day]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Mechanic jumpsuit (Fallout 76)|Mechanic jumpsuit]]

The currency's changed, but the truth hasn't.|sound=Marion Copeland 00577df0_1.ogg}} '''Marion Copeland''' is the leader of a group of [[Scavenger (Wastelanders)|scavengers]] at the [[Emmett Mountain disposal site]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Born to a mining family, Marion never saw herself taking on the trade.Marion Copeland: ''"My parents were miners, but I never saw myself digging around in a cave when I was younger."''
([[Marion Copeland/Dialogue|Marion Copeland's dialogue]]) Instead, she took to the managerial aspect of industrialized trade.Marion Copeland: ''"I hear caravans are starting to reach Appalachia, now. That's good for people and for business."''
''"Normally you'd buy low and sell high, but in our case we're "buying" for nothing and selling for as much as we can get."''
''"I heard there's a Super Mutant in Appalachia who's all about business. Now there's a guy with his priorities straight."''
([[Marion Copeland/Dialogue|Marion Copeland's dialogue]]) Following the [[Great War]], in [[Timeline (2100-2149)#2103|2103]] Marion and her scavengers came to Appalachia following the influx of people attracted by rumors of [[Gold (Fallout 76)|gold]]. Although she acknowledges that most wastelanders rely on some amount of scavenging to survive, she and her crew like to take on jobs that require coordination and perseverance, specifically choosing to go to more dangerous places and pick them clean to sell the assets off to the highest bidder. To that end, they are currently decontaminating the [[Emmett Mountain disposal site]] to retrieve any useful materiel and untapped valuable minerals.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Looking to take anything in particular?"''
Marion Copeland: ''"We know this place has its fair share of untapped mineral resources. That will be our biggest haul. Mining isn't all gold and silver. Ore veins can hold precious metals with all kinds of uses. {{Tooltip|Once we get them deconned, we can trade them to Spruce Knob and Crater for the supplies we need to survive.|deconned = decontaminated}}"''
([[Marion Copeland/Dialogue|Marion Copeland's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Tell me about your group."''
Marion Copeland: ''"We're scavengers. Most survivors are scavengers at some level, nowadays, but we like to take on the tough jobs. We go to the dangerous places and pick them clean. Then we sell what we take to the highest bidder."''
([[Marion Copeland/Dialogue|Marion Copeland's dialogue]])Marion Copeland: ''"The trick to scavenging is to scavenge where no one else will."''
''"A lot of people think of themselves as scavengers these days, but not many of us will go scrounging in places like this."''
''"So many have come to Appalachia for the gold. They don't see the value in what's just laying around until we show them what's for sale."''
([[Marion Copeland/Dialogue|Marion Copeland's dialogue]]) Although Marion and her crew were following others who entered Appalachia, they are independent operators. She also has a positive opinion of the [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|super mutant]] trader [[Grahm]]. She and her crew are welcoming towards people who can pull their weight,Marion Copeland: ''"You're welcome here. If you can pull your weight."''
''"We could use a heavy lifter. Can I count on you?"''
''"How do you feel about manual labor?"''
''"You'll go far if you stick with me. But I'm only keeping you if you contribute."''
''"You wanna learn how to survive? I'll tell you how. Sell to the highest bidder. Always."''
''"I'm not gonna ask why you're down here, but as long as you are... you want a job?"''
''"Spend a lot of time in radioactive dump sites?"''
''"Have much experience with scavenging?"''
''"I'm here if you want to talk business."''
([[Marion Copeland/Dialogue|Marion Copeland's dialogue]]) and she especially likes it if they are well prepared for their tasks.Marion Copeland: ''"{{Tooltip|Came prepared, I see.|Player is wearing a hazmat suit}}"''
''"{{Tooltip|You'll keep that suit on, if you know what's good for you.|Player has a hazmat suit}}"''
{{Tooltip|You suicidal? Come back with rad protection if you want to survive down here.|Player is not wearing rad resist gear}}"''
{{Tooltip|No rad protection? Have fun being a mutant.|Player has no rad resist gear equipped}}"''
''"{{Tooltip|I guess I don't have to tell you how dangerous these rads are. Or do I?|Player has a mutation}}"''
([[Marion Copeland/Dialogue|Marion Copeland's dialogue]]) She has experience with both [[Foundation]] and [[the Crater]] [[Crater Raiders|raiders]]. In her opinion, the former are "good folks [but] poor negotiators," and the latter are "not as bad as you'd think."Marion Copeland: ''"{{Tooltip|You with that Spruce Knob group? Good folks, poor negotiators. But you didn't hear it from me.|Player is friendly with the Settlers}}"''
''"{{Tooltip|Been to Crater much? Not as bad as you'd think, when you get to know them.|Player is friendly with the Raiders}}"''

'''Professor-bot''' is a [[Protectron (Fallout 76)|Protectron]] at [[Vault-Tec University]] in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
A manifestation of [[Appalachia]]'s pursuit of automation, the Professor-bot was originally activated to assist the human faculty in carrying out their duties. After the [[Great War]] and activation of the [[vault]]s, the Professor-bot inherited the university and currently "runs" it. Although mandated to produce graduates, there have been no students since the Great War, and thus nobody to take the classes, much less graduate. However, the robot remains dedicated to its mission and following the rules, no matter how nonsensical they might appear. The [[Vault 76 overseer]] learns that the hard way while trying to [[Overseer, Overseen|access the VTU's restricted wing]], meeting with the robot's obstinate refusal to grant a former graduate access (and also learning that the robot dissented, wanting to fail her on her overseer examination).

However, Sage was involved in chemistry, being a chemist in the past, and continuing to invent and use his own [[chems]], gaining profound information out of using them.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"And how does Sage know this?"''

Last time I saw him, I was trying to get out of the Blood Eagles and he was joining a new cult.|Kind of disappointed that he didn't stop him, but beckett wasn't in a good place to help}}"''
([[Beckett (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#203|Beckett's dialogue]]) These cults included one which worshiped [[Tato (Fallout 76)|tatos]] and one which believed that everyone lived inside a terminal or AI program.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What kind of a cult are we talking about here?"''
[[Beckett (Wastelanders)|Beckett]]: ''"{{Tooltip|For a while he was into a Tato cult. They just... spoke to and then... ate Tatos. Um. I try not to judge you know. So... moving on.|He shakes his head, he doesn't know. Tato is a food.}} {{Tooltip|Then he was in a cult that believed we were all living in some kind of terminal program or robotic AI unit... I don't remember anymore. *sighs*|Shakes his head, just why. Sighs.}} {{Tooltip|Then he did some Mothman thing. Might still be his jam? Or maybe he's into some other cryptid now? It... doesn't matter, honestly.|Embarassed type pain}}"''
([[Beckett (Wastelanders)/Dialogue#205|Beckett's dialogue]]) None of his stays have lasted more than a month before Beckett is forced to bail him out.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"[Intelligence 8+] Are you sure Sage WANTS to be rescued?"''

'''Scott Malish''' is a deceased man in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
After the [[Great War]], Scott was harassed by the [[Raiders (Fallout 76)|early raider groups]] in Appalachia and was stalked by the [[Gourmands]]. To hide from his pursuers, Scott holed up in a trailer near a toxic dumping site in the [[Toxic Valley]]. He assumed that the [[radiation]] would keep the raiders away, and if he died, his corpse would be too irradiated for the Gourmands to feast on. Even if the [[Cannibalism|cannibals]] were stupid enough to eat him anyway, Scott hoped that the poisoning would eventually kill them. Now alone, Scott apologized to [[Peach (character)|Peach]] in writing, though he admitted that he still loved her. His corpse can be found lying in the trailer years later.<ref>[[Scott's letter]]</ref>

'''Tiffany Brantley''' is a [[Fire Breathers]] initiate residing in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
Tiffany can be found at the [[Charleston Fire Department]] studying for the Fire Breathers knowledge exam. She previously completed the fitness exam with ease, but is having trouble with the knowledge exam, and refuses to cheat by allowing an intelligent [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]] to give her answers or using [[Mentats (Fallout 76)|Mentats]] to get an edge. She is very enthusiastic about becoming a Fire Breather and fighting the [[Scorched]], claiming that it is her duty to do so.

[[Ra-Ra]] and [[Gail]] are the BEST!|sound=Sara Matthews 005e65cd_1.ogg}} '''Sara Matthews''' is a resident of [[The Retreat]]. ==Background== {{Quotation|I'm critical of everything but hold myself to the highest standard
SM|Writing above Sara's bed}} Sara joined the [[villager]]s of the Retreat because living in the treehouses there made her feel like "some sort of a fantasy character" and she is able to be who she wants to be,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you like about living in the Retreat?"''
Sara Matthews: ''"Living in a treehouse makes me feel like some sort of fantasy character. I'm happy to have found a place where I can be who I want to be. I do like to visit [[the Crater|Crater]] from time to time, though. [[Ra-Ra]] and [[Gail]] are the best."''
([[BS01 Dialogue SaraMatthews.txt|Sara Matthews' dialogue]]) regardless of what other people think.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Why are you wearing a [[Halloween vampire costume|vampire costume]]?"''
Sara Matthews: ''"Can't you tell that I'm the vampire queen of the universe? Wear what you want and be whoever you want to be, regardless of what other people think."''
([[BS01 Dialogue SaraMatthews.txt|Sara Matthews' dialogue]]) Sara views [[the Crater]] [[Crater Raiders|raiders]] rather highly, and even visits them occasionally. However, she views the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]] poorly, mainly on account of their name; she believes they should have picked a better word than "Steel" to describe themselves, as it is "cool and all, but kinda lame, right?"[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you think about the Brotherhood?"''
Sara Matthews: ''"Brotherhood of Steel? I mean, Steel is cool and all, but kinda lame, right? Should have been like... Brotherhood of Terror... Brotherhood of the Night... Like a [[w:c:elderscrolls:Dark Brotherhood|Dark Brotherhood]] or something."''
([[BS01 Dialogue SaraMatthews.txt|Sara Matthews' dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Halloween vampire costume]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Sara Matthews appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]'', introduced in the ''[[Steel Dawn]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. ==Behind the scenes== * Sara was named after [[Bethesda Softworks|Bethesda]] developer and QA tester [[Sara Matthews (developer)|Sara Matthews]], who passed away some time after the game's release. * Sara makes a reference to the [[w:c:elderscrolls:Dark Brotherhood|Dark Brotherhood]], an order of assassins from ''The Elder Scrolls'' games, another Bethesda Softworks series. * Sara was present in the [[Public Test Server]] for ''Steel Dawn'' but did not appear in the released version of the [[Fallout 76 updates|update]] until a later patch re-added her into the game. * A cut note called [[list of essentials]] is related to Sara. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Steel Dawn}} [[Category:Steel Dawn human characters]] [[Category:The Retreat characters]] [[ru:Сара Мэтьюз]]

I won't allow anyone to take that away.|sound=Pierce 005b681d_1.ogg}} '''Pierce''' is the leader of the [[Crater Raiders]]' [[War Party]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Before becoming a raider, Pierce states that he was studying hard in school for "a future that never came to be."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Is Sheena your second-in-command?"''
Pierce: ''"She's more than a rung in a hierarchy. Sheena plans our operations. She's got a head for strategy. Said she used to play Blast Radius on repeat as a kid, until she could beat everyone she knew, including the adults. Imagine that. World's gone to shit and people still find solace in games. At that age, I was... well, still in school, studying for a future that never came to be."''
([[Pierce (Steel Dawn)/Dialogue#3|Pierce's dialogue]]) Pierce was once held prisoner by the employer of [[Burke (Steel Dawn)|Burke]]. Although Burke acted as a guard, Pierce treated them with respect. [[Sheena]] arrived and the three decided to escape together.Burke: ''"My employer was holding Pierce prisoner. I was his guard. Even in that situation, Pierce treated me like a person. Not as a tool. He saw me. When Sheena arrived, we all escaped together. The rest is history."''
([[Burke (Steel Dawn)/Dialogue#206|Burke's dialogue]]) Pierce is one of the three raiders that inhabit [[the Crater war room]], along with Burke and Sheena, that [[Meg Groberg]] assigned to fight the Brotherhood. Pierce was the one to start the [[War Party]], considering it a family, with his part being to talk and inform others about why they do what they do, and how important their efforts are.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You run this place?"''
Pierce: ''"Run? Look, I'm not some kind of CEO or general. This is a family. Everyone does their part. Mine is the talking. Letting people know what we're doing all this for, how important it is. I may have started this effort, but it's the War Party who moves it forward. And if you're not a part of it, I'd caution you to stay out of it's way."''
([[Pierce (Steel Dawn)/Dialogue#126|Pierce's dialogue]]) Although Meg was initially unsure if she should trust him with the responsibility of that fight, she realized that Pierce had a "silver tongue" and could easily recruit people to rally behind the cause of fighting the Brotherhood.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Is Meg involved in any of this?"''
Pierce: ''"Meg has enough on her plate without the Brotherhood to deal with. I came to her one day with an army of Raiders, rarin' to fight. She looked at me and said, "What are you waiting for? This ain't no democracy. Just don't get Crater in trouble and we're good." So here we are. The War Party."''
([[Pierce (Steel Dawn)/Dialogue#24|Pierce's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"He's doing an admirable thing, fighting against the Brotherhood."''
[[Meg Groberg]]: ''"Heh. Yeah, he is. I wasn't sure at first if I should trust him with the responsibility of that fight. But the boy's got a silver tongue. Next time I looked, he already had people rallying. And I ain't one to stop my people from following what they believe in."''
([[Meg Groberg/Dialogue#401|Meg Groberg's dialogue]]) Although the War Party is small, Pierce assures that the Party has support from dedicated Craterites, as well as mercenaries.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What about the rest of Crater?"''
Pierce: ''"We have plenty of support. Not everyone wants to be directly involved, but those who do are ready to risk life and limb. There's also your fair share of mercenary Craterites just looking for caps. But considering the Brotherhood could probably pay better, I suspect those mercs have an ounce of loyalty they're not willing to admit to."''
([[Pierce (Steel Dawn)/Dialogue#7|Pierce's dialogue]]) == Personality == {{Quotation|But I suppose yours goes something like this. You were a wayward soul, lost, looking for purpose... Then the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force|Brotherhood of Steel]] came along and put a badge of honor on your chest. Made you feel like you really mattered. So now, you'll do anything for them. Like risking your life to come to Crater and ask about those weapons you confiscated. Well, here's my backstory. The Brotherhood of Steel pointed their guns at my face and stole my property. So that property is their problem now. I'm not telling you a damn thing.|Pierce to the Vault Dweller}} Sheena calls Pierce stubborn and tight to his morals, while Burke calls Pierce kind. Pierce admits he does not really understand Burke identifying as non-binary. Despite this, Pierce uses Burke's they/them pronouns, acknowledging that it makes Burke happy in the end.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"I don't understand."''
Pierce: ''"You know something? I don't either. Not fully, anyways. We all have a public perception in this world. Sometimes it doesn't match what we feel inside. And sometimes there's nothing we can do about that."''
([[Pierce (Steel Dawn)/Dialogue#11|Pierce's dialogue]]) Pierce has a deep hatred for the [[Brotherhood of Steel]], seeing all the bad they do and predicting that they will keep demanding more from people.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Who says the Brotherhood is going to take anything away?"''
Pierce: ''"The Brotherhood thinks of itself as our saviors. They'll take what they believe is righteous. And when we refuse to give it, they'll strike us down. It starts small. Food and supplies. A home base. They offer protection in return. And hope. Hope is powerful enough to make you blind. So when they start asking for more - when they start setting rules, occupying homes, taking lives... Then it's too late. We can't let it get that far."''
([[Pierce (Steel Dawn)/Dialogue#132|Pierce's dialogue]]) He also refers to the [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force]] as fascists and tyrants.Pierce: ''"Hold on, let me get this straight. You barged in here looking to reclaim "your property", only to tell me you don't know where it came from? This is almost too good to make up. I knew my feeling about the Brotherhood was right, but you just keep on confirming it. Here's the thing. I don't talk about Raider affairs on "Brotherhood territory". That's what this is now, right? If you really want to know, you can let me go and come talk to me in Crater. I deal with reasonable individuals, not an entourage of fascists with their guns pointed at my face."''
([[Pierce (Steel Dawn)/Dialogue#145|Pierce's dialogue]]) He also believes that the Raiders and the [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] are similar, as both groups of people looking for homes.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Are there any other threats in Appalachia?"''
Pierce: ''"Besides the obvious Scorched and mutant life? Foundation, maybe. But it will be a long time before they start asking for more. They're like us, in some ways. Just looking for a home. But don't tell Meg I said that."''
([[Pierce (Steel Dawn)/Dialogue#135|Pierce's dialogue]]) He believes that Crater is the home for the raiders, wishing to keep Crater as its own place in Appalachia, free from others who may want to take their own space, create their own rules, and enforce said rules on others.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What are you trying to do here?"''
Pierce: ''"We're here to ensure that there remains a place for Crater in Appalachia. The more people come here, the more they'll want to take their own space, set their own rules. And then force those rules on others. Crater is our home. Our freedom. Our future. I won't allow anyone to take that away."''
([[Pierce (Steel Dawn)/Dialogue#123|Pierce's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential =yes |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved =* [[Property Rights]] * [[Missing Persons]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Property Rights]]: Upon entering the Makeshift Vault, the Vault Dweller is confronted by Pierce. Pierce dislikes [[Daniel Shin]] attempting to take the equipment by force, even backtalking at Shin. Shin calls Pierce a simple-minded brute, disappointing Pierce. Pierce will instead turn to the "forward scout" and engage in conversation. One can elect to use either Perception 8+ or Charisma 8+ to talk him down, either by pointing out his hopeless position or appealing to his sense of self-preservation. However, if the [[Vault 79]] raid has already been completed by siding with the Raiders, one can choose to tell Pierce how they helped during the raid, and after realizing Meg thinks highly of the Vault Dweller, Pierce won't turn hostile. But, if the Dweller chose to take all of the gold bullion for themselves at the end of the Vault 79 raid, Pierce will refuse to listen. If the player chooses to take the weapons by force, backtracks by saying Pierce can keep the vault and the weapons, or exits the dialogue system, a battle ensues though Pierce will survive at the end. Shin will order Pierce be let go, once he realizes that Pierce - surrendered or not - will not reveal where the weapons came from, unless he is allowed to return to the Crater. Pierce will be found at the Crater war room, hidden in a broken-off piece of the station due north of the main encampment, with Sheena and Burke. Pierce will refuse to negotiate no matter what, so Sheena will offer the Vault Dweller a deal. * [[Missing Persons]]: Marcia is found speaking with Pierce, whose reaction toward the Vault Dweller is dependent on their previous interactions during Property Rights. Passing a Perception 12+ check allows for noting that Sheena and Burke are missing from the war room, which leads Marcia to admit that they went to [[AMS corporate headquarters]] in [[Watoga]]. With the secret out, Pierce makes it clear that Marcia is not coming back to [[Fort Atlas]], and instead has to look for Sheena and Burke. Hate!|sound=Bloodhound 007969da_1.ogg}} '''Bloodhound''', also known as '''Theta Vanguard''',[[Fallout 76 voice types|Voice type]]: "Theta Vanguard" ([[Editor ID]] RD01_NPCF_Brute, [[Form ID]] {{ID|007969FF}}) real name '''Danielle Reeves''', is a hostile member of the [[Enclave (Fallout 76)|Enclave]]'s [[Enclave Epsilon Squad|Epsilon Squad]] at the [[Gleaming Depths (location)|Gleaming Depths]] {{in|FO76GD}}. ==Background== Formerly a private in the [[Enclave]], Danielle Reeves was the vanguard of [[Enclave Epsilon Squad]] and a close-quarters combat specialist, with the codename designation Bloodhound.[[Gleaming Depths terminal entries#Enclave Squad Epsilon|Gleaming Depths terminal entries; Vulcan security terminal, Enclave Squad Epsilon]] Their detachment was deployed to the research laboratory for [[Project Vulcan (Enclave)|Project Vulcan]] due to the importance of the project, as laid out by then-Secretary [[Thomas Eckhart]]. They were described as an elite task force, and their presence was a luxury rarely afforded to extant research facilities.[[Gleaming Depths terminal entries#Reinforcements|Gleaming Depths terminal entries; Vulcan security terminal, Reinforcements]] On April 23, [[Timeline#2085|2085]], the squadron had their first contact with an outside threat: red humanoids with crystalline growths, otherwise known as the [[Scorched]]. A week later, [[Elliot Tisdale|Wasp]] and [[Helena Blum|Python]] assaulted their superior officer and were killed by automated turrets at the facility. An autopsy suggested that they had contracted a disease from the hostiles they encountered, which would be the [[Scorched Plague]]. On June 7, 2085, it was reported that the rest of Epsilon Squad had been showing signs of infections. They were voluntarily quarantined for study, and the Enclave's scientists had no known cure for the plague.[[Gleaming Depths terminal entries#Incident Reports|Gleaming Depths terminal entries; Vulcan security terminal, Incident Reports]] Bloodhound still resides at the [[Gleaming Depths (location)|Gleaming Depths]] as a [[power armor]]-bound enemy alongside [[Lynx]] and [[Vulture (Gleaming Depths)|Vulture]], where the three surviving members of the squad are suspended in tanks, having apparently fully turned into enraged, Scorched hostiles. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |quests involved =[[Raid: Gleaming Depths]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Raid: Gleaming Depths]] ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =Bloodhound [[Vulcan power armor]] |weapon =[[Chainsaw (Fallout 76)|Chainsaw]] (with "[[Cauterizer (Fallout 76)|Cauterizer]] paint" appearance) |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== Although the [[Gleaming Depths terminal entries]] indicate that Bloodhound and the rest of the squad were diseased with the Scorched Plague, in terms of gameplay Bloodhound is not classified as a [[Scorched]] and is not a valid enemy for the [[Zealot's Legendary mod (Fallout 76)|Zealot's Legendary mod]]. {{Infobox character |games =FO76,FO76GD |image =FO76GD EN06 Guardian 1.png |race =[[Sentry bot (Fallout 76)|Sentry bot]] |affiliation =[[Enclave (Fallout 76)|Enclave]] |role =Facility security
Boss enemy |location =[[Gleaming Depths (location)|Gleaming Depths]] |quests =[[Raid: Gleaming Depths]] |dialogue =[[EN06 Guardian/Dialogue]] |level = |special ={{SPECIAL|0,100,0,0,0,0,0}} |derived = |aggression =Very Aggressive |confidence =Foolhardy |assistance =Helps Allies |factions =RD01_Enc01_GuardianBotFaction |class =RobotClass |combat style=csGuardianBot |CK race =SentryBotRace |actor = |edid =RD01_Enc01_GuardianBot |formid ={{ID|00771D8C}} |refid ={{ID|00770F41}} }} {{Quotation|Victory is inevitable.|sound=EN06 Guardian 0079696b_1.ogg}} The '''EN06 Guardian''' is an emplaced [[Enclave (Fallout 76)|Enclave]] [[Sentry bot (Fallout 76)|sentry bot]] in the [[Gleaming Depths (location)|Gleaming Depths]] {{in|FO76GD}}. ==Background== In an effort to protect the facility now housing the promising [[Project Vulcan (Enclave)|Project Vulcan]], Enclave technicians extensively modified and scaled a base sentry bot to guard its most vulnerable entrance. ==Characteristics== The EN06 Guardian is an extremely capable robotic defense system, consisting of the top half of a [[sentry bot]] affixed to an elevated platform in the center of the room. It is large and bigger than any other robot sentry bot, equipped with an Ultragenetic Shield Generator, which provides it invulnerability to any attacks. It is capable of electrifying the floor surrounding it, causing immediate death to anyone who steps foot within close range, and upon overheating disperses a blast of energy that will also immediately kill anything caught in it. The only safe place from this event is behind the blast doors. In addition to its close range armaments, the Guardian is also equipped with ranged attacks. It will occasionally utilize and switch between a three-barrel gatling laser or more concentrated and damaging but less frequent single beams. In addition to these, it is equipped with homing missile launchers and a unique plasma ball attack. One is especially susceptible to these long range attacks if they do not take cover behind a pillar. The EN06 Guardian's chassis is painted in black with yellow accents and has the white 13-star roundel of the [[Flag of the United States|U.S. flag]] on its upper torso. It has 600,000 health. The Guardian deals * 122 energy for autolasers * 158 physical for missiles * 188 energy for the platform's plasma projectiles ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |quests involved =[[Raid: Gleaming Depths]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Raid: Gleaming Depths]]: The EN06 Guardian is the first boss enemy that must be defeated during this quest; taking down the Guardian is an involved process and requires careful coordination from a team. ** The EN06 Guardian has two health bars, one for its overall health and one for the Ultragenetic Shield Generator. ** Melee is not possible with this enemy, as getting too close will cause immediate death. Instead, ranged attacks must be used. ** The EN06 Guardian has its Shield Generator on its back, which is targetable in [[VATS|V.A.T.S.]] When the shields are active, the generator is the only part of the robot that will take damage; all other areas will be invulnerable. ** The Ultragenetic Shield Generator can be also damaged by shooting explosive weapons at the platform EN06 Guardian is standing on. ** When the Shield Generator is taken down, the team will be able to deal damage to the Guardian itself. However, after some time, the Generator will overheat due to the damage it has suffered, and if the player does not take shelter in time in one of three marked (A, B, C) shelters on separate sides of the room, they will be instantly killed by the resulting meltdown, regardless of having taken cover behind something. The doors of each shelter will be destroyed due to the severity of the meltdown, and no shelter can be used twice. ** After one meltdown period has occurred, the shields will be restored and must be disabled again. This cycle repeats until the player has defeated the EN06 Guardian, allowing them to move on to the next encounter. ** The base of the EN06 Guardian's platform has four circuits that are revealed when approached by a player. If broken, they cause the EN06 Guardian to short circuit, dealing a small chunk of damage through its shielding. These circuits repair themselves after each meltdown period, allowing them to be broken again. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =EN06 Guardian's armor blade |weapon =Especially modified three barrel laser minigun
Personalized rapid fire three barrel homing missile launchers
Modified large rapid firing plasma ball blasters |otheritem =Ultragenetic shield generator |ondeath =Fusion cells }} ==Appearances== The EN06 Guardian appears only {{In|FO76GD}}. ==Gallery== FO76GD EN06 Guardian 2.png|The Guardian with its light on FO76GD EN06 Guardian 3.png|The Guardian launching an attack {{Stub|FO76GD}} {{Navbox creatures FO76}} [[Category:Fallout 76 robots and computers]] [[Category:Gleaming Depths robots and computers]] [[Category:Sentry bot characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 Enclave characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 boss enemies]] [[ru:Страж EN06]]

She succeeded Dr. Gaines as the project leader on July 31, [[Timeline#2080|2080]]. Over the years, disturbances among the Enclave staff, including illness, sudden panic attacks, violent outbursts, and even [[cannibalism]] were attributed to the sonic experimentation with Ultracite. On August 23, [[Timeline#2085|2085]], Dr. Wright was apprehended and held to an Enclave military tribunal for her role in the experiments. She was found guilty and executed the next day.[[Gleaming Depths terminal entries#Incident Reports|Gleaming Depths terminal entries; Vulcan security terminal, Incident Reports]] ==Appearances== Esther Wright is mentioned only {{In|FO76GD}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Enclave}} [[Category:Gleaming Depths mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 Enclave characters]] [[ru:Эстер Райт]]

{{Infobox character |games =none |mentions =FO76,FO76GD |type =mentioned |image =Enclave Symbol (FO3).png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |affiliation =[[Enclave]] |role =Scientist |dod =July 31, [[Timeline#2080|2080]] |status =Deceased |dod verified=yes |location =[[Gleaming Depths (location)|Gleaming Depths]] |nicknames = |holotapes = |notes =[[Final preparations]]
[[The Gleaming Depths (note)|The Gleaming Depths]] }} '''Doctor Robert Gaines''' was a scientist and member of the [[Enclave (Fallout 76)|Enclave]] in [[Appalachia]], working at a research facility in what became known as the [[Gleaming Depths (location)|Gleaming Depths]]. ==Background== Dr. Robert Gaines was the lead scientist of [[Project Vulcan (Enclave)|Project Vulcan]], a research project focused on studying the properties of "ultragenetic resonance," or more specifically, sound-regulating [[ultracite]] crystals.[[Gleaming Depths terminal entries#Ultragenetic Resonance|Gleaming Depths terminal entries; Vulcan lab terminal, Ultragenetic Resonance]] Initially, Gaines advocated for using [[radiation]] treatment in the experiments, while [[Esther Wright|Dr. Esther Wright]] stood for using sonic wave manipulation.[[Project Vulcan log 02: Direction]] Dr. Wright's methods proved to be successful, and she believed that Dr. Gaines was "finished" professionally. Furthermore, she made ominous allusions towards lessening his influence over the project.[[Project Vulcan log 03: Breakthrough]] On July 31, [[Timeline#2080|2080]],[[Gleaming Depths terminal entries#Incident Reports|Gleaming Depths terminal entries; Vulcan security terminal, Incident Reports]] Dr. Gaines died during one of his experiments. One of the creature test subjects became so enraged that it broke free and mauled several staff members, and killed Dr. Gaines.[[Gleaming Depths terminal entries#Animal Testing|Gleaming Depths terminal entries; Vulcan lab terminal, Animal Testing]] Security chief [[John Holloway|Captain John Holloway]] lamented Dr. Gaines' death, saying that he liked Gaines the most out of all the "eggheads."[[Vulcan security log 02]] After his death, Dr. Esther Wright took over the project. Even after his death, Dr. Gaines' influence still hung over the experiments in the Gleaming Depths' research facility. Dr. Wright built on Dr. Gaines' previous research, seeing it as ironic given their rivalry,[[Project Vulcan log 04: Ultragenesis]] and continued to blame him as the facility descended into chaos.[[Project Vulcan log 05: Disaster]] His pet snake, Butch, eventually transformed into the gigantic [[Ultracite Terror]].[[Butch (note)]] ==Appearances== Robert Gaines is mentioned only {{In|FO76GD}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Enclave}} [[Category:Gleaming Depths mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 Enclave characters]] [[ru:Роберт Гейнс]]

HumanRace (attack race) |class =raiderClass |voice type =NPCM_GHL00_GenericGhoul01 |edid =GHL00_Dave |formid ={{ID|007BB073}} |refid ={{ID|007BB077}} }} '''Dave''' is a [[ghoul]] who is a member of the [[Revenants]] at [[Radiant Hills]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76GW}}. ==Background== Dave is one of the [[Revenants]], a faction of ghouls who prioritize self-preservation and protecting their fellows against outsiders.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Let's talk about your methods for acquiring resources."''
[[Maddox Mullen]]: ''"You mean our raids. Like the one dear Leamon found himself in the middle of. We don't pretend to be saints. If we can avoid violence, we do. But, if it's between our safety and theirs, we protect ourselves. {{Tooltip|I hope you can understand something as simple and necessary as that.|A little prickly. Not interested in disagreement on this point}}"''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) They reside at the settlement of [[Radiant Hills]], where Dave is found. He wears casual clothes and frequently hangs around the reactor area of the bunker there. Dave is also significantly taller than most other wastelanders.See [[#Notes|notes]]. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |essential =yes |ghost =yes |quests involved = |quests started = }} ==Inventory== {{Missing data|Inventory|FO76}} {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon =[[Combat shotgun (Fallout 76)|Combat shotgun]] |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== * Dave has an unusually increased height (over 1.2x) and is noticeably taller than any other character in game, standing at least a full head taller than the player character. Another resident of Radiant Hills, [[Guy (Ghoul Within)|Guy]], is similarly tall, though not as much as Dave. * Dave does not have unique voice lines when spoken to, and instead shares dialogue with [[Revenant (character)|generic Revenants]]. ==Appearances== Dave appears only {{in|FO76GW}}. ==Behind the scenes== Dave is a reference to [[Bethesda Game Studios]] character artist [[David Jennison]], who worked on the model for the [[Fallout 76 playable ghoul|playable ghoul]] feature. Jennison appeared in the [[Fallout Day Broadcast|2024 Fallout Day Broadcast]] in a full model ghoul head, in-character as Dave the Ghoul.[https://www.si.com/videogames/features/fallout-76-ghoul-update-hands-on-preview Fallout 76 Ghoul hands-on - Bethesda's next free update lets you ghoulify yourself] ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox Ghoul Within}} [[Category:Ghoul Within ghoul characters]] [[Category:Revenants characters]] [[ru:Дейв (Ghoul Within)]]
