Mutated produce that would kill anyone else becomes gourmet for ghouls.|sound=Ernie Navarro 007a109a_1.ogg}} '''Ernie Navarro''' is a [[ghoul]] gardener and member of the [[Revenants]] at [[Radiant Hills]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76GW}}. ==Background== Ernie is something of an oddity among the [[Revenants]] at [[Radiant Hills]]. Despite many of the [[ghoul]]s there being tough, uncompromising fighters, Ernie is the opposite: he is a gentle, wide-eyed pacifist.Ernie Navarro: ''"Anyway, I'm Ernie. I might seem like an odd one among all these tough fighters. More of a lover, myself. It's symbiotic."''
([[Ernie Navarro/Dialogue|Ernie Navarro's dialogue]]) In his life, Ernie has experienced bullying and feeling isolated from the world. He was the target of discrimination after becoming a ghoul, and he believes that those who singled him out for it were troubled people looking for outlets to pass on their bad feelings. Nevertheless, he was able to find his own peace and let the tough times remain in the past.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Come on, tell me the full story. It sounds like you went through some tough times before."''
Ernie Navarro: ''"Well, yeah, I did. But those times aren't important anymore. There will always be people out there, troubled people, who are looking for some way to pass on how they feel. For some of those people... my condition gave them an excuse to target me. I was pretty isolated, to be honest. But I still found my peace. Always will. Not worth it to hold onto things like that."''
([[Ernie Navarro/Dialogue|Ernie Navarro's dialogue]])Ernie Navarro: ''"Or, uh... Well, I hope you're not here to bully me."''
([[Ernie Navarro/Dialogue|Ernie Navarro's dialogue]]) Though he is not concerned with leaving his own legacy, Ernie does want to bring joy to those around him and wishes to leave the Earth better than he found it.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Is that it? Do have{{sic}} any goals?"''
Ernie Navarro: ''"My greatest goal is to bring joy to the people around me. If I can do that, and then they do the same, well... Then it's almost like there were dozens of me! I'm not worried about any sort of legacy, though. Only the legacy of the Earth. If I can somehow manage to leave it better than I found it, that's a victory."''
([[Ernie Navarro/Dialogue|Ernie Navarro's dialogue]]) His peace-loving nature makes him an odd fit for the Revenants, but he finds Radiant Hills much more peaceful and nicer than his past life.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What were you doing before you came here?"''
Ernie Navarro: ''"Oh, not too much. Mostly farming and cooking. Sharing, when I could. Same things I'm doing here. Here's a lot nicer, though. More peaceful."''
([[Ernie Navarro/Dialogue|Ernie Navarro's dialogue]]) The town he was living in before Radiant Hills was raided by the Revenants, who found Ernie and saw that he was a ghoul. They offered Ernie a chance to run with them; although he was initially wary of falling in with a group of bandits, he was convinced by [[Maddox Mullen]] to join under the promise of safety and community among fellow ghouls.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How did a gentle soul like you end up with these outcasts?"''
Ernie Navarro: ''"It's kind of a funny story, but they raided my town. Saw I was a ghoul, and better yet how rough I was looking, and they offered to take me along with them. I was hesitant to run with a bunch of raiders, even with their promise of safety. It was Maddox who convinced me. Said they were a family. All ghouls, all looking out for each other. Long as they don't force me to start shooting people, I can live with that."''
([[Ernie Navarro/Dialogue|Ernie Navarro's dialogue]]) Having convinced Ernie to settle in Radiant Hills in the first place, Maddox has granted Ernie an exception to [[Kevan Asherton]]'s combat training.[[Asher's training notes]] Ernie is happy to be a part of the community so long as he is not forced to "start shooting people," which he finds an agreeable arrangement. Ernie's pacifism has garnered attention at the settlement (for example, Asher wants to further discuss the terms of Ernie's exemption from combat training) and he has been called a pushover at times. However, fighting is simply not in Ernie's nature, as he prefers to take the blows, move on and leave the fighting to someone tougher, like Asher. Ernie believes both lovers and fighters are needed in the world, and he falls within that first camp.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What are you, some kind of pushover? There's got to be something that gets on your nerves."''
Ernie Navarro: ''"Yeah, I've been called that. Been told to fight back. Stand up for myself. I don't know if it's weakness or strength, but that's just not who I am. It's not worth it. I'll take the blows and move on. Leave the fighting to someone like Asher. We need people like him just as much as we need people like me, don't you think?"''
([[Ernie Navarro/Dialogue|Ernie Navarro's dialogue]]) Ernie's responsibilities at Radiant Hills include tending to the garden, where several [[Mutations|mutated]] plants have flourished due to the [[radiation]], similar to [[Flux|nuked flora]]. Ernie tends to a variety of flowers, fungi, fruits and vegetables, with the most resilient of plants having evolved from the radiation. Many of the plants Ernie brought to the camp died, but those that survived have since thrived. This gives the ghouls an unusual but still restorative palate, with ghouls' ability to eat most anything being rather useful,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Tell me about the garden."''
Ernie Navarro: ''"We've got everything here. Flowers, fungi, fruits, and veggies. But only the most resilient plants survive here with the radiation. The ones that are able to evolve. It's truly amazing. When I started bringing plants in here, I half expected all of them to die. Most did. But some... Well, they grew to become the flourishing garden you see here today. And one great thing about being a ghoul? We can eat practically anything. Mutated produce that would kill anyone else becomes gourmet for ghouls."''
([[Ernie Navarro/Dialogue|Ernie Navarro's dialogue]]) and everyone at the settlement is provided for with the food.Ernie Navarro: ''"We may not eat fancy, but everyone gets a plate."''
([[Ernie Navarro/Dialogue|Ernie Navarro's dialogue]]) Ernie is experienced at his job as well, as he was previously a farmer and cook at his last settlement. His interest in flora is also scientific, and he has performed extensive research on the Revenants' nearby location of [[Point Repose]], including its out-of-region plant life and the effects of radiation from decomposing [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|feral ghouls]] on the soil there.[[Observations of Point Repose]] He does, however, also enjoy the simple pleasures of his work, taking joy in talking to the plantsErnie Navarro: ''"{{Tooltip|Live on, little sprout. You'll find a way.|Talking to a plant}}"''
([[Ernie Navarro/Dialogue|Ernie Navarro's dialogue]]) and using rad rose tea to soothe anxiety.Ernie Navarro: ''"Have you ever tried rad rose tea? Good for anxiety."''
([[Ernie Navarro/Dialogue|Ernie Navarro's dialogue]]) He is grateful for his place in lifeErnie Navarro: ''"Look at all this. Tough friends, safe shelter. So much to be grateful for."''
([[Ernie Navarro/Dialogue|Ernie Navarro's dialogue]]) and encourages others to stop and enjoy the flowers every once in a while.Ernie Navarro: ''"Stop and enjoy the flowers."''
([[Ernie Navarro/Dialogue|Ernie Navarro's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |essential =yes |quests involved = |quests started = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =Overalls underarmor |weapon =[[Combat shotgun (Fallout 76)|Combat shotgun]] |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== Although he is present at Radiant Hills' exterior, Ernie will not be available for dialogue with a [[human]] player character; one must complete [[A Fresh Pair of Genes]] to [[Fallout 76 playable ghoul|become a ghoul]] in order to open a conversation with Ernie. ==Appearances== Ernie Navarro appears only {{in|FO76GW}}. ==Bugs== {{Platforms|pc}} Ernie and [[Regular Debbie]], the two unique named characters found at the Radiant Hills exterior, may not spawn correctly and might not be able to be found anywhere at the location, as of the [[Public Test Server]]. One potential solution is to first fast travel to Radiant Hills' interior, then take the elevator up to the exterior.{{Verify|verified}} ==Gallery== FO76 PTS Radiant Hills 11.png|Ernie's garden at Radiant Hills ==References== {{References|2}} {{Navbox Ghoul Within}} [[Category:Ghoul Within ghoul characters]] [[Category:Revenants characters]] [[ru:Эрни Наварро]]

HumanRace (attack race) |class =raiderClass |combat style= |voice type =NPCF_GHL00_JayeVo |edid =GHL00_JayeVo |formid ={{ID|007A0E9B}} |refid ={{ID|007A0E9D}} }} {{Quotation|Remember the days when you could walk up to someone and get judged by the qualities of your face? How bright your eyes were, the cleanliness of your skin, how much of a smile you were willing to crack. You do remember. Because those days are still here. A stranger approaches in the Wasteland, and they need to make a judgment: friend or foe. Well, most see the face of a monster and find that... a little hard to trust. Even those who aren't actively hostile, well, they aren't likely to offer you the same opportunities as the next lucky human. You want those opportunities back? Come to me and I'll make sure they never know it's a walking corpse that's talking to them.|sound=Jaye Vo 007a0eaa_1.ogg}} '''Jaye Vo''' is a member of the [[Revenants]] at [[Radiant Hills]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76GW}}. ==Background== Jaye grew up in poverty before the [[Great War]], and found refuge in pre-War fashion magazines. The power of beauty and fashion compelled Jaye, giving her confidence and a desire to strive for greatness.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How'd you come to be such a fashion connoisseur?"''
Jaye Vo: ''"Pre-war magazines. I was obsessed with them growing up. All I had ever seen before was filth. Nobody cared about... anything, except fighting over the next scrap. No dignity, no ambition. Then one day I found this fashion magazine. There was page after page of these women dressed in all shapes and colors. Confident and beautiful... they were almost from another world! You looked at them and could tell that they had strived for something. And that made me want to strive for something. Beauty has power. The power to amaze, to inspire, to transform. I... Well, unfortunately, not everyone has that power available to them. But I still try, you know. To give ghouls the power to live normally, even if they can't... amaze, anymore."''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) Though she worked toward this goal of being beautiful before the [[Nuclear weapons|bombs]] dropped,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Do you really think those fashion models were happy? Most performances have a price."''
Jaye Vo: ''"Of course they have a price. I never rolled out of bed looking like a fashion icon, even before the whole... ghoul development. Anything worthwhile has a price. Isn't it still better to shoot for greatness? And I mean that regardless of circumstances. I may not be beautiful anymore, but I can still create beauty."''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) post-War [[radiation]] and the process of [[ghoul]]ification transformed her dramatically. Although she does somewhat lament losing the traditional notion of beauty in her face and body from becoming a ghoul,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"It sounds a bit like you had your dream taken away from you. I'm very sorry to hear that."''
Jaye Vo: ''"Ugh. I'm disgusted at myself for vomiting out my personal issues. Thanks for the sympathy, but do me a favor and forget I said anything sentimental. The point is, fashion is art. Whatever avenues for expressing that are unavailable to me now, I can still learn, invent, and share it with others. Who knows? Maybe one day the whole Wasteland will be wearing the Vo catalogue. And they'll never know that I'm a ghoul."''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) she rejects any pity given her way.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Ghoul or not, I think you're still beautiful."''
Jaye Vo: ''"Oh, please. Spare me the pity. I don't want to hear one more time that it's the inside that counts. I look like what I look like. And yeah, most days I'm not too happy about that. It's completely unfair. Why me, out of all the ungrateful bastards out there who would gladly sell their whole head of hair for a roasted Radrat? But I'd rather face reality than pretend I can still be the next Marilyn Monroe. It's not like I can't still create things that are beautiful."''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) Rather than delude herself by pretending to be the "next [[Marilyn Monroe]]" with a ghoulified face, Jaye prefers to face reality and instead focus on creating beautiful things and sharing them with others. She aspires for the "Vo catalogue" to one day spread throughout the [[wasteland]], even if people have no idea the fashion was designed by a ghoul. She sees fashion as an art form, and even if not all of its avenues are open to her now that she is a ghoul, she can still continue to learn, invent and share her style with others. However, deep down, she does still wish she could be "normal" and human again, even if this is not an opinion shared by some other ghouls.Jaye Vo: ''"{{Tooltip|So they don't care to fit in. Well, what about me, huh? What if I want to be normal?|Letting out the frustration at her ghoul appearance. Some of the other ghouls are okay with their fate, but she wishes she could be human again}}"''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) She continues to resent her ghoul appearanceJaye Vo: ''"{{Tooltip|Yes, I can. I can cover it all up. What's the point if I can't?|Letting out the frustration at her ghoul appearance}}"''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]])Jaye Vo: ''"{{Tooltip|Won the genetic lottery, just to get shot in nuclear Russian roulette. Some luck.|Letting out the frustration at her ghoul appearance}}"''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) and has some slightly judgmental tendencies, if others have not consulted her for their fashion choices.Jaye Vo: ''"{{Tooltip|You look like you could use a makeover.|Judgmental}}"''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]])Jaye Vo: ''"{{Tooltip|Don't leave home without stopping by. Trust me.|Judgmental. Subtly insulting the player's look}}"''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) Jaye has since joined the faction known as the [[Revenants]], which accepts only ghoul members. There, in addition to her existing talents as a stylist, she also serves as the group's "disguise expert,"[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I don't know who you are, but you can dress me up if you'd like."''
Jaye Vo: ''"{{Tooltip|Well, let me take you up on that offer.|FWIW, Jaye's flirting indicates her interest in dressing the player up, not in the player themselves}} Jaye Vo, resident stylist and, nowadays, disguise expert. If you're heading into 'society for regular humans' and want to blend in, I'll set you up."''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) creating clothes that ghouls can use to obscure their face, hiding behind masks and other similar items, so that humans are more willing to trust them, without having to confront a monstrous, irradiated face.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Tell me more about this 'disguise' service you offer."''
Jaye Vo: ''"Remember the days when you could walk up to someone and get judged by the qualities of your face? How bright your eyes were, the cleanliness of your skin, how much of a smile you were willing to crack. You do remember. Because those days are still here. A stranger approaches in the Wasteland, and they need to make a judgment: friend or foe. Well, most see the face of a monster and find that... a little hard to trust. Even those who aren't actively hostile, well, they aren't likely to offer you the same opportunities as the next lucky human. You want those opportunities back? Come to me and I'll make sure they never know it's a walking corpse that's talking to them."''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) During her time with the faction, she befriended [[Eugenie]], another ghoul who later left the group; at least one letter from [[Kevan Asherton]] to Eugenie provided an update on Jaye, specifically her discovery of a guitar and subsequent inability to tune it.[[Eugenie's letter]] At some point, Eugenie wrote Jaye a letter encouraging her to continue her pursuits in fashion. However, Eugenie also addressed Jaye's insecurities about being a ghoul, reassuring Jaye that becoming a ghoul was not her fault and that she is okay how she is. Eugenie encouraged Jaye to return to her family at some point to show them what she had become; even if they were no longer proud of her, it would let Jaye know that they were no longer "worth a damn."[[Letter to Jaye]] Residing in [[Radiant Hills]], Jaye has set up a studio in her own corner of the bunker where she works on clothes, disguises and other items,Jaye Vo: ''"{{Tooltip|One more decorative stitch and I'm going to look like a patchwork quilt.|Annoyed at how ragged her clothes are getting}}"''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) such as her own homemade shoes.Jaye Vo: ''"Like my shoes? It pains me to say it, but... they're homemade."''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) She is frequently in search of [[Cloth (Fallout 76)|cloth]] and other fabrics,[[Maddox Mullen]]: ''"Fertilizer for Ernie, cloth for Jaye, oil for Asher... and I don't even know where to start with Parthenia's list."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]])Jaye Vo: ''"{{Tooltip|Can't they find a single yard of clean cloth? I can only do so much with rags.|Annoyed at how ragged her clothes are getting}}"''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) resorting to more creative methods when supplies run low.Jaye Vo: ''"{{Tooltip|Could rip off the couch covering and use that... but it probably needs an acid bath first.|Trying to get creative about where to find fabric}}"''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) She dismisses common wasteland fashion as "overdone,"Jaye Vo: ''"Wasteland chic is so overdone."''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) and says that her fellow ghouls can be the canvas for her art, if they so desire.Jaye Vo: ''"I'm the artist; you're the canvas. We've got a lot to work with here."''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) She remains committed to the belief that, in spite of the world's many disadvantages, the right attitude can take a person anywhere.Jaye Vo: ''"Work it, sweetheart. The right attitude will take you anywhere."''
([[Jaye Vo/Dialogue|Jaye Vo's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |essential =yes |quests involved = |events started = }} ===Other interactions=== After transforming into a ghoul during the quest [[A Fresh Pair of Genes]], the player must speak to Jaye Vo and acquire a disguise in order to continue with [[Fallout 76 factions|main faction quests]], if they have not already been completed. The disguise consists of a [[Drifter outfit (Fallout 76)|drifter outfit]] and a [[Sack hood (Fallout 76)|sack hood]] variant. Once the disguise has been equipped, the player can also use [[Power armor (Fallout 76)|power armor]] alongside it. One must select the dialogue option with Jaye to equip the disguise, do whichever quests they would like, and then return to Jaye at Radiant Hills to remove the disguise. Jaye's disguise is necessary for interacting with the following quest lines: * [[Enclave (Fallout 76)|Enclave]] (original quests) * [[The Wayward]] (''[[Wastelanders]]'') * [[Vault 76 overseer]] (''Wastelanders'') * [[Crater Raiders]] (''Wastelanders'') * [[Foundation]] [[Settlers (Wastelanders)|Settlers]] (''Wastelanders'') * [[Secret Service (Fallout 76)|Secret Service]] (''Wastelanders'') * [[Brotherhood First Expeditionary Force]] (''[[Steel Dawn]]'' and ''[[Steel Reign]]'') ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Ratty skirt (Fallout 76)|Clean ratty skirt]] (unique variant) |weapon =[[10mm pistol (Fallout 76)|10mm pistol]] |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== She wears a unique, clean version of the [[Ratty skirt (Fallout 76)|ratty skirt]] that cannot currently be acquired for use by the player. ==Appearances== Jaye Vo appears only {{in|FO76}}. She was first mentioned in the ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'' update, as part of [[Eugenie's letter]], before making a full appearance in the ''[[Ghoul Within]]'' update. ==Behind the scenes== Although not clarified in-game, [[Jonathan Rush]] stated during the [[Fallout 76 March 2025 developer AMA|March 2025 developer AMA]] that Jaye's disguises also include ways to mask a ghoul's smell and hide their voice, which is why other face-hiding apparel cannot supplant Jaye's work.[[Fallout 76 March 2025 developer AMA|''Fallout 76'' March 2025 developer AMA]]
[[Jonathan Rush]]: ''"Jaye is an absolute master of disguises. Like, for us to think, 'oh, we could just do Jaye's work by just putting on a Fasnacht mask' is doing Jaye an immense disservice. Jaye is good at what they do—they're excellent, as a matter of fact. They can mask that smell, they can hide your voice—there's no limit to what Jaye can do."'' ==Gallery== Fallout 76 Ghoul Within Jaye Vo Full.png|A unique red variant of the ratty skirt worn by Jaye Vo ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox Ghoul Within}} [[Category:Once in a Blue Moon mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Ghoul Within ghoul characters]] [[Category:Revenants characters]] [[ru:Джей Во]]

If you can even call them that.|sound=Kevan Asherton 007a0c32_1.ogg}} '''Kevan Asherton''' is a [[ghoul]] who was a co-founder of the [[Revenants]], living at [[Radiant Hills]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76GW}}. ==Background== Kevan reveals very little about his past prior to becoming a [[ghoul]], though he makes it very clear that his ghoulified form is something that he resents. However, this is not simply due to the nature of being a ghoul itself, but rather because of the societal changes and the universal mistrust associated with being a ghoul.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Why do you hate being a ghoul so much?"''
Kevan Asherton; ''"Humanity has two sides, you know. Especially before the War, you only ever see one side of most. The one that wants to be a friend. Then there's the other side. The one that doesn't care much about being a friend. The one that strives to protect itself and what it holds dear. If you're smart, you'll listen to that side when it speaks up. Most people do. It's what we're doing here, and what they'll always do to us. Neither any better than the other. Just different."''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"So, what is it that bothers you? Humans and ghouls working against each other?"''
Kevan Asherton: ''"Humans against ghouls. Humans against other humans. Even ghouls against ghouls. We're all the same in our mistrust of one another."''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]]) At some point after turning into a ghoul, Kevan fell in with [[Lucy Harwick]]'s group of survivors, who were trying to create a place for ghouls to live at [[Valley Galleria]]. After the ghouls began being hunted down by [[Duncan McKann]], a trio including Kevan, [[Elmira]] and [[Maddox Mullen]] split off from the main group and headed east, instead of going to [[Dyer Chemical]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dwellers]]: ''"How did this sanctuary for ghouls come to be?"''
[[Maddox Mullen]]: ''"It's not the happiest story, but it's a part of who we are. I'll start at the beginning. Valley Galleria, right here in Appalachia. A group of ghouls lived there openly. Others didn't like that so much. A hunter named Duncan McKann was planning to wipe us out. Lucy, who led the survivors there, decided to move everyone out before the attack. Duncan tracked them, of course. If you go to Dyer Chemical, well... you'll see what happened. Me, Asher, and Elmira had broken off from the group. Instead of fleeing north to Dyer, we went east. Covered our tracks well. The idea was to find a place we could start fresh, establish a new identity. One that people wouldn't mess with. You've heard about how we do things."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) This proved to be the right move, as Lucy's group were eventually killed, while Kevan, Elmira and Maddox covered their tracks and escaped.[[Lucy's holotape]] The three engaged in raiding to try and survive, as well as gather supplies to make their escape from the area. For their final raid on a camp, they intended to keep things quiet and with minimal damage before anyone knew they had been there. However, the group was not used to such tactics at the time and things went awry. The residents of the camp were alerted to the ghouls' presence, and Elmira chose to make a distraction. She ripped off her mask and thrust herself into the camp's spotlights, and the wastelanders there assumed she was feral. Elmira was killed by the wastelanders, and her sacrifice bought the others, including Kevan, enough time to escape without more casualties.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You needed a place to hide. So you came here."''
Maddox Mullen: ''"We were lucky to find this place. Unfortunately, not all of us made it here. We needed to save up enough resources to make our escape from the area, so we planned one final raid. It was supposed to stay quiet - in and out before anyone knew we were there. But at the time, we weren't used to working that way. The camp got alerted. Elmira... decided to cause a distraction. She tore off her mask and ran in front of the spotlights. They thought she was feral. Bought us enough time to get out while they scanned the entrance for more of "her kind". All we can do now is try to honor her sacrifice. Live on the way she would have wanted us to."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) The survivors eventually came across an abandoned, inactive missile silo far to the north, in the [[Savage Divide]]. The settlement became known as [[Radiant Hills]]. It was heavily irradiated, perfect for a community of ghouls, and had a non-functional, leaking nuclear warhead inside. The faction has since grown to include more ghouls seeking refuge, and its co-founders, such as Kevan, honor Elmira's sacrifice.[[Elmira's dream]] Kevan is responsible for security, heading up guard duty at the settlement, and conducts combat training to better prepare the other Revenants for any threat that may come their way.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What do you do around here?"''
Kevan Asherton: ''"Security. I watch the perimeter, and make sure everyone gets combat training. Even the ones who are damn near hopeless as fighters. Long as they try, they'll get there."''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]]) Kevan was also responsible for setting up the affiliated location of [[Point Repose]], a nearby sanctuary for ghouls going feral to have a place to do so in peace, without harming others.[[Welcome to Point Repose]] It was initially built up by Kevan to accommodate one woman who started to show signs of going feral, and he did so entirely of his own volition without anyone asking him to create such a place.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Don't be dramatic. I'm a ghoul now, too, and I deserve an explanation."''
[[Maddox Mullen]]: ''"All there is to explain is that one of us started to show signs. So Asher built a place where she could be comfortable... without endangering the others. Nobody asked him to do it. Nobody made an agreement as to who, or when, someone should go in. They decide. {{Tooltip|That's all there is to it.|Putting a stern cap on this topic. He won't say anything else about it.}}"''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) Point Repose is kept as a sacred place for the Revenants, somewhere for its members to go and eventually be at rest if things ever go bad.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I don't mean to be insensitive, but doesn't treating it as taboo make it worse?"''
[[Maddox Mullen]]: ''"It keeps it sacred. To know that there's a place for you, if things ever go bad... That brings comfort. But trying to reason out how, or why, when there is no reason to it... only brings pain. I say this to you because I can tell you're working through it. But please, don't talk about it with the others. Let them be at peace."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) ===Ideology and personality=== [[File:FO76GW Kevan threat.png|thumb|250px|Kevan threatening [[Leamon Price]].]] Kevan has a dim view on life as a ghoul. He believes it to be an overall negative, and is distrustful of humans after facing discrimination. As a result, he aims to protect his fellow ghouls in spite of their poor circumstances, at the same time rejecting outsiders and dealing with them by whichever means necessary, including violence.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"This act of mercy could go a long way for human sentiment toward ghoulkind, don't you think?"''
Kevan Asherton: ''"That's a god damn stupid thing to believe in. Some kind of future utopia where ghouls are accepted by all. No matter how much progress we make, there will always be somewhere that thinks different. Because the fact is there are ferals, and we look a hell of a lot like them. And the fact is we just don't know what makes someone feral or not. The best we can hope for is a place just for us. Safe, and separated. Nevermind what's best for them. It's best for us."''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]])[[Leamon Price]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Okay. Yeah. I like that option.|Still feeling uncertain/unsteady. Maybe a little breathy. But coming around.}} {{Tooltip|I mean, if it's between a painful death and... a makeover...|Trying to convince himself. Becoming more uncertain again at the end, thinking about a ghoul's flesh}}"''
Kevan Asherton: ''"Don't take this lightly, simpleton. Living life as a ghoul... You'll regret you were ever born at all."''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton]] and [[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price's dialogue]]) Kevan acknowledges that ghouls and humans living together peacefully could occur, but says those who initiate an attempt are taking a big risk, and he does not want to compromise the safety of his people for such a gamble.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What if our survival instincts are outdated? Sometimes they cause unnecessary violence."''
Kevan Asherton: ''"Sometimes they do. Other times, they save our lives. And you never know which it's gonna be. Some here believe in a world where ghouls and humans can overcome our differences. That type of thing has happened before. But the first people to do it take a big risk. I'm not willing to take that risk. Some view that as selfishness. So here I am between other ghouls who think I'm close-minded, and humans who think I'm a monster. You just can't win. All I want is be acknowledged with dignity, from somewhere. That's all any of us want. For what we're doing to be appreciated. For our deficiencies to be forgiven. If you can even call them that."''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]]) Kevan is willing to kill outsiders in order to protect not just the Revenants themselves, but also their own identities as ghouls. Kevan and the other Revenants go to great lengths to avoid being seen, otherwise they could be hunted down.Kevan Asherton: ''"{{Tooltip|Anyone else? How many have you told? That we're ghouls?|Yelling, losing his cool. This is bad}}"''
[[Madeline Keene]]: ''"A few of the crew, okay! I don't... I don't know how many, I was just... terrified. Leamon told a different story. Didn't think you were ghouls, but... something else entirely. Everyone's on different sides about it. They think we're exaggerating about a raider attack. You have to believe me. Please!"''
Kevan Asherton: ''"God damn it. You think I want to kill you? But one misjudged act of mercy could mean the death of everyone I care about. {{Tooltip|*sigh* The killing of your crew... That wasn't supposed to happen. Most times, we take the resources we need and get out with none the wiser.|Finally cooling off a little bit. Assessing the situation.}} But we can't afford to be seen. Because sooner or later someone gets the idea to hunt us down. I can't let that happen again."''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton]] and [[Madeline Keene/Dialogue|Madeline Keene's dialogue]]) [[File:FO76GW Kevan kills Madeline.gif|thumb|250px|Kevan murders [[Madeline Keene]].]] While Kevan openly admits to raiding and killing, he believes it to be justified out of a desire to protect his fellow ghouls, and says that he and the other Revenants try to avoid collateral damage when possible, rather than just exploiting others for the sake of it, specifically contrasting them to the [[Crater Raiders]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I would feel better about Leamon becoming a ghoul if he didn't have to join a bunch of no-good bandits."''
Kevan Asherton: ''"If that's what you think of us, so be it. Just means you haven't been listening to me. You think we're any worse than those lowlifes at Crater, exploiting anyone they can for profit? Just 'cause they act proud of it doesn't make it right. We've done everything we can to avoid unnecessary deaths. Theirs, and ours. This is the conclusion we ended up at."''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]]) Kevan says he would agree that murder of innocents is not justified, and knows that many will see him and the other Revenants as mere bandits and murderers, but he believes the Revenants are merely "paying back the injustice that was already dealt."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Tough. Nothing justifies the murder of innocents."''
Kevan Asherton: ''"{{Tooltip|I have to say I agree with you. We're only paying back the injustice that was already dealt.|Emphasis on "in" in injustice}}"''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]]) To that end, Kevan is a firm adherent to the Revenants' policy of not leaving witnesses, stemming from their desire to survive without disturbance and failed previous attempts at doing things the "nice way."[[Leamon Price]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Now hold on a second! I'm not so sure about this.|Finally asserting himself}} Look, I am not one to judge too much by appearances. So what if your skin is a bit... loosely attached? But am I to understand it right that you all live in hiding and... and go out to steal people's things in the night? And if they see you, then... then it's over for them?"''
Kevan Asherton: ''"We tried it the nice way! People died. Ghouls. On account of nothing but our 'loosely attached skin'. So don't you for one second think of us as some kind of monsters for trying to survive. It was people thinking of us as monsters that drove us to this messed up reality."''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton]] and [[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price's dialogue]])Kevan Asherton: ''"{{Tooltip|Witnesses aren't permitted. Which means we need to do something about you two. Figure out what that is, or I will.|Menacing}}"''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Wait! Don't shoot!"''
Kevan Asherton: ''"{{Tooltip|Unfortunately I've got no choice, newcomer. It's our code and the only reason we've survived so long. No witnesses.|Emphasis on each word of "No witnesses"}}"''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]]) Kevan has a cold and gruff exterior, and acknowledges that he is not one for conversation.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You're not much of a conversationalist."''
Kevan Asherton: ''"Yeah, maybe not."''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Just fine?"''
Kevan Asherton: ''"What do you expect me to say? That I'm jumping over rainbows on a pony? I'm fine. Next question."''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]]) He is not interested in making friends,Kevan Asherton: ''"We're not friends. Just in case that wasn't clear."''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]]) and believes many other Revenants may be getting too "soft."Kevan Asherton: ''"Everyone's getting soft."''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]]) He refuses to let himself fall into carelessnessKevan Asherton: ''"{{Tooltip|Can't get careless.|Reminding himself}}"''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]]) and expects others to show up on time for important things, such as his combat training routines.Kevan Asherton: ''"Whoever doesn't show up to training will get my boot."''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]]) However, beneath his rough surface, Kevan does have a soft side, which [[Parthenia Blankenship]] teasingly acknowledges.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What about me? Do you accept humans?"''
[[Parthenia Blankenship]]: ''"Well... no. But if you prove yourself a friend to us by helping Leamon, who does become a ghoul... I think we can convince Asher to let you off. He's warm and fuzzy beneath the frown."''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) This is best seen in Kevan's interactions with [[Eugenie]], a former member of the Revenants who left Radiant Hills. Kevan and Eugenie disagree on many things, including how the proceeds of her [[Fallout 76 vendors|mercantile]] ventures were being used, but the two remain on good terms nonetheless.[[Eugenie's letter]][[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"It'd help if you could tell me why you left."''
[[Eugenie]]: ''"Let's just say I didn't like what they were doing with their cut of the business."''
([[Eugenie/Dialogue|Eugenie's dialogue]]) Eugenie is grateful to still be in contact with Kevan, who musters up plenty of will to send friendly letters, which is not something in his nature. Eugenie has tried to convince Kevan and Maddox that she is living proof that ghouls and humans can live and work together without issue, but she also acknowledges that they will likely never change their viewpoint, and that is okay with her. Eugenie is grateful to Kevan for taking care of everyone at Radiant Hills, but also reminds him to take care of himself, too.[[Eugenie's response]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |essential =yes |quests involved =* [[Leap of Faith]] * [[A Fresh Pair of Genes]] |events started = }} ===Quests=== * [[Leap of Faith]]: Kevan is encountered at the [[hillside cavern]] during this quest, as he holds up [[Leamon Price]] and the player character at gunpoint. However, [[Parthenia Blankenship]] calms him down and sends Kevan and the player character to the [[Emmett Mountain side tunnel]] to acquire irradiated ore for her experiments into expediting ghoulification. There, Kevan is willing to kill [[Madeline Keene]] for coming across their activities; Kevan can either be encouraged to kill her, or dissuaded with [[Strength (Fallout 76)|Strength]] or [[Charisma (Fallout 76)|Charisma]] of 8+. At the end of the quest, there is an optional objective to speak to Kevan to get his opinion on whether or not Leamon should become a ghoul; he believes Leamon taking that choice would be a mistake. * [[A Fresh Pair of Genes]]: Kevan will discourage the player character from becoming a ghoul. However, if one decides to go through with the transformation anyway, Kevan will have new dialogue, saying he does not understand the choice but will protect the player character, now that they are a ghoul, all the same. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Winter jacket and jeans (Fallout 76)|Winter jacket and jeans]]
[[Green military utility cap]]
[[Bandana (Fallout 76)|Camo bandana]] (quest-only) |weapon =[[Combat rifle (Fallout 76)|Combat rifle]] |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Kevan Asherton appears only {{in|FO76}}. He was first mentioned by the nickname "Kev" in the ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'' update, as part of [[Eugenie's letter]], before making a full appearance in the ''[[Ghoul Within]]'' update. ==Gallery== FO76 PTS Emmett Mt side tunnel 8.png|Confrontation with [[Madeline Keene]] during [[Leap of Faith]] FO76GW Leap of Faith final.jpg|Kevan in the laboratory with [[Leamon Price]] and [[Parthenia Blankenship]] ==References== {{Ref box}} {{Navbox Ghoul Within}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Once in a Blue Moon mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Ghoul Within ghoul characters]] [[Category:Revenants characters]] [[ru:Кеван Эшертон]]

I... don't want to die just yet.|sound=Leamon Price 0078deab_1.ogg}} '''Leamon Price''' is a wounded scavenger in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76GW}}. ==Background== A country bumpkin to his core, Leamon grew up under the care of his mother, whom he speaks of fondly.[[Parthenia Blankenship]]: ''"This way, my dear test subject. Into the lab, where the excitement happens!"''
Leamon Price: ''"Er... Miss Parthenia, is it? We're still holding off on the operation 'til later, aren't we?"''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"Of course! Don't you worry the unburnt hairs on your smooth little scalp. They look very soft, by the way."''
Leamon Price: ''"Ah, well, thank you kindly! I do make sure to comb it out every morning, like my mama taught me."''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"{{Tooltip|What's it like, having a mama?|Intellectual curiosity}}"''
Leamon Price: ''"Oh, it sure is nice. She takes care of ya, listens to ya, makes you feel real special."''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"I see. And does that provide any benefits to the scientific process?"''
Leamon Price: ''"I'm not too familiar with what that is, but I bet your mama it does! {{Tooltip|That is, I mean...|Awkwardly realizing she doesn't have a mama to bet on, so that might have been a bit insensitive}}"''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"If 'mama's love' is capable of providing scientific benefits, that would be truly remarkable. I wonder if the effects could be synthesized..."''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price]] and [[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) He enjoys the simple things in life, such as playing board games like [[Blast Radius board game (Fallout 76)|Blast Radius]],[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Your dream is as good as wasted if you take this step. Better to retain your humanity until the last."''
Leamon Price: ''"Well, that's the sign I was looking for. It ain't much but I'm proud of the life I lived. I sure am grateful for the opportunity you offered me, Ms. Parthenia. It was a pleasure getting the chance to meet you. All of you. I think I'll head back to Emmett Mountain and see if I can't manage a few good nights of beer and Blast Radius with the crew."''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price's dialogue]]) making him a frequent patron of [[Nuka-World on Tour (location)|Nuka-World on Tour]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"[Charisma 8+] I'd be happy to provide protection, but I'd need compensation for equipment maintenance."''
Leamon Price: ''"{{Tooltip|Oh boy! This sounds like my very own private security!|A little too excited. It's something fancy he never thought he'd have.}} Only issue is, uh, I don't got much to pay you with. Kinda sorta "invested" my last paycheck in the Nuka-World arcade. Oh, oh, but! I do have this big ole block of ore I found on the last operation! It kinda looks like a spaceship, if you squint! Quality stuff!"''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price's dialogue]]) However, Leamon also has a much more meaningful dream that he uses as a goal in life: to find something to live for, specifically people to live for, whom he can make proud.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What is your dream?"''
Leamon Price: ''"{{Tooltip|Well, it might sound funny, but... It's to find something to live for. People to live for. To make them proud.|Emphasis on "find" - finding something that missing}} But I can't do that if I become something I don't recognize anymore."''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price's dialogue]]) As an adult, Leamon has fallen in with several different groups. One such example was a crew that were frequent [[chems|chem]] users, and Leamon did not fit in well with them, especially given his aversion to needles and, logically, [[Psycho (Fallout 76)|Psycho]]. The crew would take chems at every opportunity, including for things as simple as looking for a [[Manta Man]] figurine in editions of [[Hubris Comics]], which Leamon thought was a rather unusual thing to go manic over.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I think you should become a ghoul and keep chasing your dream. There are ways to make it work."''
Leamon Price: ''"{{Tooltip|You reckon?|Hopeful}}"''
[[Parthenia Blankenship]]: ''"Oh, certainly. Multitudes of ways. But if you're dead you've got zilch."''
Leamon Price: ''"You're darned right about that, aren't you, Ms. Parthenia? Alright. I've still got lots to live for, and it ain't no good giving up. But I get squeamish with needles. My last crew sure would rip me a new one about that. Too chicken for Psycho, they said. Well, who needs to go all manic for a Manta Man figurine scavenger hunt? They'd inject every chem they had and then tear apart Hubris Comics like animals. After all that, they never did find the collector's edition! Anyway, the point is you'll have to stick me with that stuff before I change my mind."''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price]] and [[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) Even after this experience, jeering has followed Leamon elsewhere, such as from his acquaintance [[Harvey (Ghoul Within)|Harvey]], who called him a "useless lout" over Leamon's inability to open a jar of relish.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Let's cut to the chase. I'm just here because I heard your radio broadcast."''
Leamon Price: ''"So you did? I told that damned Harvey I wasn't no useless lout who couldn't even open a jar of relish!"''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price's dialogue]]) Despite this, Leamon carries on, still pursuing his dream.Leamon Price: ''"Say, isn't there anything else we can try? Some sort of miracle cure? Or heathen rituals performed on a stormy night? Truth is, I've still got a dream to chase. Never thought much of it, but now I've got the Reaper's shadow looming over me, it sure feels a lot more urgent than it ever did before. I... don't want to die just yet."''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price's dialogue]]) By [[Timeline (2100-2149)#2105|2105]], he has most recently fallen in with [[Marion Copeland]]'s group of [[Scavenger (Wastelanders)|scavengers]] extracting ore from the [[Emmett Mountain disposal site]], befriending other scavengers such as [[Madeline Keene]].[[Leamon's diary]][[Madeline Keene]]: ''"Y-You're not one of them, right? The bandits?"''
[[Kevan Asherton]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Sorry, lady, but you don't know what you're talking about.|Getting heated. How the hell does she know about us?!}}"''
Madeline Keene: ''"{{Tooltip|No, you are! The same ones that attacked Leamon and the others!|Heightened. Realizing as she speaks.}} {{Tooltip|I... I was out in the trees when it happened. Just for a few minutes. When I came back...|Distraught. Reliving the experience.}} {{Tooltip|I saw everything! All of you - ghouls, underneath those masks. Just a step away from feral!|Accusatory}} {{Tooltip|Why even hide it?|Hostile, accusatory}}"''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton]] and [[Madeline Keene/Dialogue|Madeline Keene's dialogue]]) Unbeknownst to him, his exposure to [[radiation]] there has affected his blood, greatly shortening his lifespan, likely due to insecure use of radiation gear such as [[Hazmat suit (Fallout 76)|hazmat suits]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Are you okay?"''
Leamon Price: ''"Well, Doc here says I got radioactive blood on account of all my exposure to irradiated ore at Emmett Mountain."''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price's dialogue]])Leamon Price: ''"{{Tooltip|Wonder how folks are doing at Emmett Mountain. Wish I could warn 'em to zip tight that radiation gear.|GHOUL}}"''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price's dialogue]]) Making matters worse, Leamon and several other scavengers were the victims of an attack by a mysterious group of masked bandits, later revealed to be the [[Revenants]]. One night, while camping with the Emmett Mountain crew, Leamon had trouble sleeping and noticed shadows approaching their camp. He and [[Ryan (Ghoul Within)|Ryan]] alerted the others, which led the bandits to open fire on them, killing several scavengers and injuring Leamon.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Sounds scary. What are you talking about?"''
Leamon Price: ''"{{Tooltip|Well, I was out camping with some of my crew. Had trouble sleeping. I opened my eyes and saw these shadows creepin' over us.|With some drama at the end}} {{Tooltip|I done hollered like a madman! And right away, they started executing everybody. I got shot and thought I was dead right there.|Telling the story with frantic energy}} Well, they must have thought so too, because they left me there. {{Tooltip|I don't know where those bandits came from, but they ain't like no one else I've seen in Appalachia.|Shaking his head, hamming it up}}"''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price's dialogue]]) Afterwards, there was some debate among the scavengers as to what happened and the true nature of their assailants; while Madeline told some of the other scavengers that the attackers were, in fact, [[ghoul]]s, Leamon thought they were something else entirely, such as a much more dangerous force.Madeline Keene: ''"{{Tooltip|Wait! Oh god, wait!|Cowering as a gun is pointed at her}} {{Tooltip|L-Look, I... I spoke quickly, okay? I won't tell anyone else!|Panicked, quickly backtracking}}"''
[[Kevan Asherton]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Anyone else? How many have you told? That we're ghouls?|Yelling, losing his cool. This is bad}}"''
Madeline Keene: ''"A few of the crew, okay! I don't... I don't know how many, I was just... terrified. Leamon told a different story. Didn't think you were ghouls, but... something else entirely. Everyone's on different sides about it. They think we're exaggerating about a raider attack. You have to believe me. Please!"''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton]] and [[Madeline Keene/Dialogue|Madeline Keene's dialogue]])[[Distress signal (Ghoul Within)|Distress signal]] In response, other scavengers who were not present for the incident believe they may have been exaggerating about a simple [[Raiders|raider]] attack. Leamon, meanwhile, decided to seek treatment for his wounds from the [[Responders]] at [[the Whitespring Refuge]]. He also set up a [[Distress signal (Ghoul Within)|distress signal]] warning others in [[Appalachia]] about the bandits, using technical know-how he learned from his deceased friend [[Timmy (Ghoul Within)|Timmy]]. While being treated by the [[Responder medic]], Leamon learned that although his gunshot wound was not as serious as he first thought, he instead would receive a terminal diagnosis of radiation illness due to his time at Emmett Mountain,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I've seen better days. Sounds like you have too."''
Leamon Price: ''"Ain't no way I could have predicted I would come in here for a gunshot wound and come out with a terminal diagnosis of something else entirely. Though, speaking of the gunshot wound, it'd weigh on my conscience not to warn you. There's a gang of masked bandits out there! {{Tooltip|Ruthless they are, with scarred skin, and red eyes like rabid wolves. They ain't human, I tell you.|With some drama, as telling a storybook horror story}}"''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price's dialogue]]) having only one or two weeks left to live.Leamon Price: ''"You mean I ain't gonna make it?"''
[[Responder medic]]: ''"{{Tooltip|A week. Maybe two. I'm so sorry, Mr. Price.|Breaking the news that Leamon is going to die soon}}"''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price]] and [[Responder medic/Dialogue|Responder medic's dialogue]]) Being confronted with his mortality has made him fearful of death, and he feels that accomplishing his dream is a much more urgent matter, and he does not want to die before he feels satisfied. If the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dwellers]] hear Leamon's broadcast and offer to help him, they can follow up on the Responder medic's suggestion regarding rumors of a "radiation specialist" in the northern [[Savage Divide]],[[Responder medic]]: ''"{{Tooltip|I shouldn't even be saying this, but... I've heard some rumors. A "radiation specialist" up in the hills, north of the Savage Divide.|Hesitant to give a patient false hope}} I don't know what that means, or if they even exist. So just take it with a grain of salt."''
([[Responder medic/Dialogue|Responder medic's dialogue]]) which turns out to refer to the same bandits from the Revenants of [[Radiant Hills]] who attacked Leamon. This leads [[Parthenia Blankenship]] to pitch Leamon (and the Vault 76 dwellers) the idea of transforming into a ghoul.Events of [[Leap of Faith]] Leamon can either be encouraged to stay [[human]] and accept his mortality, at which point he says he will return to Emmett Mountain and spend his last few days with the scavengers in a version of himself he can be proud, or to become a ghoul via Parthenia's experimental procedure, after which he will join the Revenants and reside in Radiant Hills, looking for ways to make himself useful there and continue his dream.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How's that dream of yours coming along?"''
Leamon Price: ''"{{Tooltip|Doggone it, I sure have gone and embarrassed myself by yapping all about that. See, I thought I was done for! Well, I'm still dreaming, that's for sure. Folks 'round here are hot and cold. They act all standoffish. Next day they go and say they'll lay their life down for you, glaring all the way! I can't blame 'em, you know. They all got tough stories to tell, and mixed-up hearts beside. Even Miss Parthenia, chipper as she is. We get on best out of everybody. Like two pea plants growing in a field of corn. Real smart she is, too.|GHOUL}}"''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How's your new life as a ghoul?"''
Leamon Price: ''"{{Tooltip|Oh, not too bad. Sure beats being six feet under. Most folks are decent. No worse than the survivors on the surface. What I ain't used to is being stuck underground. I just ain't sure when the Sun rises or sets anymore!}} {{Tooltip|No one else around here seems to care, neither. That Maddox character? Pretty sure he don't sleep at all.|GHOUL. Whispering a rumor on the last line}} {{Tooltip|I'm just floating around all restless. Been trying to make myself useful, but Ms. Debbie has most everything covered as far as maintenance goes.|GHOUL}}"''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price's dialogue]])Leamon Price: ''"{{Tooltip|I-I can help out! If there's anything that needs doing.|GHOUL. A bit awkward, but well-intentioned}}"''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |ghost =yes |quests involved =[[Leap of Faith]]
[[A Fresh Pair of Genes]] |quests started = }} ===Quests=== * [[Leap of Faith]]: Leamon suffering an attack by the Revenants, as well as his subsequent radio broadcast and treatment at the Whitespring Refuge, are the inciting incidents for this quest. ** In dialogue at the Whitespring Refuge, the player can pass a check of [[Charisma (Fallout 76)|Charisma]] 8+ to offer their assistance to Leamon for compensation, at which point he gives them a [[lead ore]] in lieu of [[Cap (Fallout 76)|caps]]. The player character can also refuse to help, delaying the quest, or offer to help Leamon without the bargaining, as he travels to the [[hillside cavern]]. ** After encountering the Revenants, the quest concludes with the player character giving advice to Leamon, as to whether or not he should follow through on Parthenia Blankenship's offer to undergo an experimental procedure and become a ghoul, expanding his lifespan but transforming his body. If he is told to stay human, he will politely decline Parthenia's offer, and will eventually disappear from the game after the leaving, having returned to Emmett Mountain. If he is told to turn into a ghoul, he will accept Parthenia's offer and will become a ghoul, regardless of if the player character turns into one alongside him or not. * [[A Fresh Pair of Genes]]: If Leamon was encouraged to turn into a ghoul during the previous quest, he will be found in [[Radiant Hills]] after the player awakens as a ghoul, with new dialogue. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Miner uniform]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Leamon Price appears only {{in|FO76GW}}. ==Behind the scenes== During the [[Public Test Server]] for ''Ghoul Within'', Leamon had a head add-on applied that gave him a significant, gory wound on his neck. However, there was a bug that made it so Leamon's neck wound could appear on the player character. The detail was removed for the live release of the update, and Leamon's neck appears intact in-game. ==Gallery== FO76GW Kevan threat.png|Leamon being held hostage by [[Kevan Asherton]] FO76GW Leap of Faith final.jpg|Leamon in the laboratory with Kevan Asherton and [[Parthenia Blankenship]] FO76GW Leamon Price 02.png|Leamon exiting the [[hillside cavern]] FO76 PTS Leamon Price human.png|Leamon with neck gore during the PTS ==References== {{Ref box}} {{Navbox Ghoul Within}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Ghoul Within human characters]] [[Category:Ghoul Within ghoul characters]] [[Category:Revenants characters]] [[ru:Лемон Прайс]]

Whatever it is, I'm here for you.|sound=Maddox Mullen 0079ca56_1.ogg}} '''Maddox Mullen''' is a [[ghoul]] who was a co-founder of the [[Revenants]] and serves as the [[Fallout 76 factions|faction's]] ''de facto'' leader at [[Radiant Hills]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76GW}}. ==Background== Maddox was [[Birthdates|born]] on October 23, [[Timeline#2059|2059]]. During his childhood, he bounced around from foster home to foster home, and looked forward to going out on his own in the future as an adult. However, the [[Great War]] occurred on the day of his eighteenth birthday, and he became [[ghoul]]ified from the resulting [[radiation]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"So, what's your story?"''
Maddox Mullen: ''"Nothing's more important than what we're doing here and now. But our pasts shape us, lead us to the present. I know mine did. Growing up, I was tossed from foster home to foster home. Never knew my parents. Never needed to. I just wanted to get out on my own. Eighteen rolled around. I could have done with a regular birthday candle, but I got a little more than that. One big mushroom cloud on the horizon. The Great War. I was out on the cliffside watching it. Seeing the new world created right before my eyes. Not knowing how it would change me."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) Maddox describes this as "twisted karmic poetry," but he nevertheless saw it as a liberating experience.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Quite a tragic backstory you've got there. How long did it take you to come up with it?"''
Maddox Mullen: ''"You think I'm fishing for pity? There's nothing that could be more useless to me. I don't mind that any of that happened. The bombs dropping on my birthday was some kind of twisted karmic poetry. Watching that happen, for the first time I felt... unburdened."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) [[Nuclear weapons|Bombs]] dropping on the world put people on equal footing, which was therapeutic for Maddox, someone who had next to nothing to live for in the pre-War world.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"That must have been difficult."''
Maddox Mullen: ''"On the contrary. It was therapeutic. I had nothing. Nothing to go back to. Nothing to call my own. While everyone around me had homes, families, careers... The War wiped the slate clean. I could start my life on equal footing. All of us could."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) Maddox recognizes that his thoughts on the Great War could be seen as callous, but also does not shy from admitting that he has no love for the pre-War world that rejected him, even if life as a ghoul is not much better or is even worse.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"That's pretty messed up. A lot of people died, you know."''
Maddox Mullen: ''"Yeah, I get that. But I'm not going to lie and pretend that I shed any tears for a world that never wanted me. The kicker is that it still doesn't want me. Doesn't want any of us."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) After turning into a ghoul, Maddox fell in with [[Lucy Harwick]]'s group of survivors, who were trying to create a place for ghouls to live at [[Valley Galleria]]. After the ghouls began being hunted down by [[Duncan McKann]], a trio including Maddox, [[Elmira]] and [[Kevan Asherton]] split off from the main group and headed east, instead of going to [[Dyer Chemical]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dwellers]]: ''"How did this sanctuary for ghouls come to be?"''
Maddox Mullen: ''"It's not the happiest story, but it's a part of who we are. I'll start at the beginning. Valley Galleria, right here in Appalachia. A group of ghouls lived there openly. Others didn't like that so much. A hunter named Duncan McKann was planning to wipe us out. Lucy, who led the survivors there, decided to move everyone out before the attack. Duncan tracked them, of course. If you go to Dyer Chemical, well... you'll see what happened. Me, Asher, and Elmira had broken off from the group. Instead of fleeing north to Dyer, we went east. Covered our tracks well. The idea was to find a place we could start fresh, establish a new identity. One that people wouldn't mess with. You've heard about how we do things."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) This proved to be the right move, as Lucy's group were eventually killed, while Maddox, Elmira and Kevan covered their tracks and escaped.[[Lucy's holotape]] The three engaged in raiding to try and survive, as well as gather supplies to make their escape from the area. For their final raid on a camp, they intended to keep things quiet and with minimal damage before anyone knew they had been there. However, the group was not used to such tactics at the time and things went awry. The residents of the camp were alerted to the ghouls' presence, and Elmira chose to make a distraction. She ripped off her mask and thrust herself into the camp's spotlights, and the wastelanders there assumed she was feral. Elmira was killed by the wastelanders, and her sacrifice bought the others, including Maddox, enough time to escape without more casualties.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You needed a place to hide. So you came here."''
Maddox Mullen: ''"We were lucky to find this place. Unfortunately, not all of us made it here. We needed to save up enough resources to make our escape from the area, so we planned one final raid. It was supposed to stay quiet - in and out before anyone knew we were there. But at the time, we weren't used to working that way. The camp got alerted. Elmira... decided to cause a distraction. She tore off her mask and ran in front of the spotlights. They thought she was feral. Bought us enough time to get out while they scanned the entrance for more of "her kind". All we can do now is try to honor her sacrifice. Live on the way she would have wanted us to."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) The survivors eventually came across an abandoned, inactive missile silo far to the north, in the [[Savage Divide]]. The settlement became known as [[Radiant Hills]]. It was heavily irradiated, perfect for a community of ghouls, and had a non-functional, leaking nuclear warhead inside. The faction has since grown to include more ghouls seeking refuge, and its co-founders, such as Maddox, honor Elmira's sacrifice.[[Elmira's dream]] Maddox serves as the faction's ''de facto'' leader by [[Timeline#2105|2105]],[[Revenant (character)|Revenant]]: ''"Maddox says this is home. But how long until it's taken from us?"''
([[Revenant (character)/Dialogue|Revenants' dialogue]])[[Asher's training notes]][[Eugenie's response]] and has plans for expansion,Maddox Mullen: ''"This place will grow. A sanctuary for all ghoulkind. True sanctuary."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) perhaps by recruiting struggling ghouls at [[Foundation]], though he worries that it may be too early and could compromise the Revenants' safety.Maddox Mullen: ''"Need a plan for what's next. Too early for expansion. Could be ghouls struggling at Foundation..."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) Maddox continues to mentor the Revenants, and oversees acquiring supplies for individual members.Maddox Mullen: ''"Fertilizer for Ernie, cloth for Jaye, oil for Asher... and I don't even know where to start with Parthenia's list."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) ===Ideology and personality=== Maddox is committed to protecting the ghouls in the Revenants at any costs. He sees ghoulification as akin to a superpower,Maddox Mullen: ''"Wasn't a dream. Not to fear, though. The radiation messed a lot of things up. And it made us into superheroes."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) and believes that ghouls should lift each other up with reciprocal aid and look out for each other when the world and, in particular, unaffected [[human]]s beat them down.Maddox Mullen: ''"No more infected wounds. No more worrying about radiation. You're free, now. Unstoppable. And you're going to carry our cause: the dream of the ghouls. See, people will try to beat us down, because we have what they don't. And they're afraid of that. So we answer by living our lives to the fullest. Grasping everything we ever wanted in life, no matter who wants to keep us from it. Holding on tight. Protecting each other, and lifting up ghoulkind. It doesn't matter who you were before. You're one of us now. And we're gonna count on you, just as you can count on us."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]])Maddox Mullen: ''"Remember to look out for each other. You can be damn sure no one else will."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) Maddox is a realist who sees the harsh world of the [[wasteland]] for what it is, and he believes that those who want something should simply step up, act and take it.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I understand what you mean. It's not fair to be stuck on the back foot through no fault of your own."''
Maddox Mullen: ''"Yet, so many of us are. {{Tooltip|It took me a long time, but I finally realized it just doesn't matter what's fair or not. Because it is what it is, regardless.|A harsh truth. He's accepting of this, but that doesn't mean he likes it.}} No amount of philosophizing about what should be makes that the reality. If you want something, you just have to take it yourself. That's what we're doing here. Carving out a piece of the world where we can be safe and free."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]])Maddox Mullen: ''"Anything you've been mulling over? Here's your sign. Stop mulling and act."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) Maddox is aware that others may see the Revenants as nothing more than simple [[raiders]], but he believes that life is different enough for ghouls that it creates a different set of needs and circumstances for them.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dwellers]]: ''"Your story isn't that unique. You just sound like another group of raiders to me."''
Maddox Mullen: ''"Well, maybe you've been lucky so far. But I think you'll understand soon enough. What makes life different for ghouls. I'll be there when you do."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) He is firm in his choice of prioritizing protection of the Revenants over outsiders' safety; he claims to avoid violence when possible, but does not pretend to be a saint.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Let's talk about your methods for acquiring resources."''
Maddox Mullen: ''"You mean our raids. Like the one dear Leamon found himself in the middle of. We don't pretend to be saints. If we can avoid violence, we do. But, if it's between our safety and theirs, we protect ourselves. {{Tooltip|I hope you can understand something as simple and necessary as that.|A little prickly. Not interested in disagreement on this point}}"''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) However, he also declares that the Revenants should have "no mercy" for outsiders,Maddox Mullen: ''"No mercy for outsiders. Not anymore."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) and is willing to "take the fight to them" before disappearing without any outsider knowing what had happened.Maddox Mullen: ''"Take the fight to them. Then... disappear before they ever know it happened."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) Within Radiant Hills itself, however, Maddox is empathetic to fellow ghouls and believes that they deserve more than their current situation.Maddox Mullen: ''"Still not enough. They deserve more than this."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) He wants to make sure that the Revenants are never found or disturbed by the outside world, and that Radiant Hills remains as a sanctuary for them, even if it is at a potentially fatal expense for outsiders.Maddox Mullen: ''"If they find us... We'll make sure they never return home."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]])Maddox Mullen: ''"This is our sanctuary. No one's going to take it from us."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |essential =yes |quests involved =[[A Fresh Pair of Genes]] |quests started = }} ===Quests=== [[A Fresh Pair of Genes]]: Maddox is present when the player character [[Fallout 76 playable ghoul|awakens as a ghoul]], and he greets them in their new life. ===Other interactions=== If the player character has visited the location of [[Point Repose]], Maddox has a new dialogue option in which he initially pushes back on answering questions about it, saying Point Repose is a self-explanatory place they do not talk about,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Could I ask you about Point Repose?"''
Maddox Mullen: ''"We don't talk about that place. {{Tooltip|You can see what's going on there, can't you?|Patiently, thoughtfully, looking into the player's eyes to make sure they understand. But still stern about this topic.}} {{Tooltip|So don't make it harder for people than it already is.|Charismatic, empathetic, but still stern.}}"''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) though he will eventually explain its history and purpose if pressed on it.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Don't be dramatic. I'm a ghoul now, too, and I deserve an explanation."''
Maddox Mullen: ''"All there is to explain is that one of us started to show signs. So Asher built a place where she could be comfortable... without endangering the others. Nobody asked him to do it. Nobody made an agreement as to who, or when, someone should go in. They decide. {{Tooltip|That's all there is to it.|Putting a stern cap on this topic. He won't say anything else about it.}}"''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Ghoul bomber jacket]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== {{Note|(Note)}} Maddox confirms that he was born on October 23, [[Timeline#2059|2059]], by nature of his eighteenth birthday happening on the day of the [[Great War]]. The [[Pip-Boy 2000 Mark VI|Pip-Boy]] date was set to [[Timeline#2105|2105]] at the time of the release of the ''Ghoul Within'' update, which introduced Maddox as a character, making him 46 years old in 2105. ==Appearances== Maddox Mullen appears only {{in|FO76GW}}. ==References== {{Ref box}} {{Navbox Ghoul Within}} [[Category:Ghoul Within ghoul characters]] [[Category:Revenants characters]] [[ru:Мэддокс Маллен]]

I'm Madeline. But, uh, you should probably get back to the main operation.|Friendly, but a bit nervous}} Nobody's supposed to be back here without supervision. I just came to grab some tools.|sound=Madeline Keene 00798435_1.ogg}} '''Madeline Keene''' is a [[Scavenger (Wastelanders)|scavenger]] and member of [[Marion Copeland]]'s group at the [[Emmett Mountain disposal site]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76GW}}. ==Background== Madeline works alongside a group of scavengers extracting [[Radiation|radioactive]] ore from the [[Emmett Mountain disposal site]], led by [[Marion Copeland]].Events of [[Radiation Rumble|Event: Radiation Rumble]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Tell me about your group."''
[[Marion Copeland]]: ''"We're scavengers. Most survivors are scavengers at some level, nowadays, but we like to take on the tough jobs. We go to the dangerous places and pick them clean. Then we sell what we take to the highest bidder."''
([[Marion Copeland/Dialogue|Marion Copeland's dialogue]]) Madeline herself is a friendly woman who wants to stay out of trouble, and describes herself as just a "grunt" within the scavenging operation.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I'm not on the team, but I am here for irradiated ore."''
Madeline Keene: ''"I see. Well... I don't want any trouble. I'm just a grunt. Came in to grab some tools. I'll just say that Marion hasn't been kind to other scavengers digging around on her turf. Not without joining her crew first, anyway."''
([[Madeline Keene/Dialogue|Madeline Keene's dialogue]]) She is slightly on edge[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"[Lie] Yeah, just started today."''
Madeline Keene: ''"{{Tooltip|Welcome aboard! I'm Madeline. But, uh, you should probably get back to the main operation.|Friendly, but a bit nervous}} Nobody's supposed to be back here without supervision. I just came to grab some tools."''
([[Madeline Keene/Dialogue|Madeline Keene's dialogue]])Madeline Keene: ''"{{Tooltip|Hey, is that-? *frightened gasp* Ghoul!|Seeing Asher coming out of the tunnel}}"''
([[Madeline Keene/Dialogue|Madeline Keene's dialogue]]) after a group of masked [[raiders]] attacked the scavengers, injuring her friend [[Leamon Price]].[[Leamon's diary]]Madeline Keene: ''"Y-You're not one of them, right? The bandits?"''
[[Kevan Asherton]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Sorry, lady, but you don't know what you're talking about.|Getting heated. How the hell does she know about us?!}}"''
Madeline Keene: ''"{{Tooltip|No, you are! The same ones that attacked Leamon and the others!|Heightened. Realizing as she speaks.}} {{Tooltip|I... I was out in the trees when it happened. Just for a few minutes. When I came back...|Distraught. Reliving the experience.}} {{Tooltip|I saw everything! All of you - ghouls, underneath those masks. Just a step away from feral!|Accusatory}} {{Tooltip|Why even hide it?|Hostile, accusatory}}"''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton]] and [[Madeline Keene/Dialogue|Madeline Keene's dialogue]])Madeline Keene: ''"{{Tooltip|Wait! Oh god, wait!|Cowering as a gun is pointed at her}} {{Tooltip|L-Look, I... I spoke quickly, okay? I won't tell anyone else!|Panicked, quickly backtracking}}"''
[[Kevan Asherton]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Anyone else? How many have you told? That we're ghouls?|Yelling, losing his cool. This is bad}}"''
Madeline Keene: ''"A few of the crew, okay! I don't... I don't know how many, I was just... terrified. Leamon told a different story. Didn't think you were ghouls, but... something else entirely. Everyone's on different sides about it. They think we're exaggerating about a raider attack. You have to believe me. Please!"''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton]] and [[Madeline Keene/Dialogue|Madeline Keene's dialogue]]) During this attack, Madeline was out in the nearby woods around Emmett Mountain, and returned only a few minutes later to find the bandits raiding and attacking some of the scavengers. This was a frightening experience for Madeline, and she recognized that the people under the masks were [[ghoul]]s. There was some debate among the scavengers as to what happened and the true nature of their assailants; while Madeline told some of the other scavengers that the attackers were, in fact, ghouls, Leamon Price thought they were something else entirely, such as a much more dangerous force.[[Distress signal (Ghoul Within)|Distress signal]] In response, other scavengers who were not present for the incident believe they may have been exaggerating about a simple raider attack. Unbeknownst to Madeline, these attackers were the [[Revenants]], a secretive [[Fallout 76 factions|faction]] of ghouls, who do not wish to leave identifying witnesses.[[Kevan Asherton]]: ''"{{Tooltip|No one lives to identify the Revenants.|Menacing, with a hint of anger bubbling up. About to pull the trigger}}"''
([[Kevan Asherton/Dialogue|Kevan Asherton's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |essential = |killable =yes |quests involved =[[Leap of Faith]] |quests started = }} ===Quests=== [[File:FO76GW Hostage.png|thumb|right|Madeline being threatened]] [[Leap of Faith]]: Madeline is encountered at the [[Emmett Mountain side tunnel]] during this quest. While [[Kevan Asherton]] is extracting ore from the tunnel, Madeline comes in and converses with the player, who is standing guard nearby. When Kevan returns, Madeline panics, while Kevan believes it is necessary to kill her to protect the Revenants' secrecy. The player can agree with Kevan and let him kill her, convince him to let her live with [[Strength (Fallout 76)|Strength]] or [[Charisma (Fallout 76)|Charisma]] of 8+, or fail to change Kevan's mind altogether. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Emmett Mountain hazmat suit]] |weapon =[[Hunting rifle (Fallout 76)|Hunting rifle]] |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Madeline Keene appears only {{in|FO76GW}}. ==Gallery== FO76 PTS Emmett Mt side tunnel 8.png|Confrontation with [[Kevan Asherton]] during [[Leap of Faith]] FO76GW Kevan kills Madeline.gif|Kevan killing Madeline ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Ghoul Within}} [[Category:Ghoul Within human characters]] [[ru:Маделейн Кин]]
