[[Training plan]] |archetype =Afraid |skin =SkinCorpse |hair color ={{Tooltip|Deep brown|HairColor18DeepBrown}} |eye color ={{Tooltip|Blind|MaleEyesCorpse}} |hairstyle ={{Tooltip|Midlifer|HairMale09}} |facial hair = |height = |body = |level =6 |derived =[[Action Points]]: 50 |special ={{SPECIAL|0,0,0,0,0,0,0}} |aggression =Very Aggressive |confidence =Foolhardy |assistance =Helps Friends and Allies |CK race =HumanRace |class =Citizen |combat style=csRaiderRangedOffenseHigh |template =Loot_CorpseBase04 |voice type =SSE_NPCM_Magellan |edid =SSE_Magellan |formid ={{ID|0079AAA7}} |refid ={{ID|007A8D4D}} }} '''Magellan''' is a deceased member of [[Atlantic City]]'s [[The Showmen|Showmen]] found dead in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76GW}}. His corpse appears at [[Susan's cabin]]. ==Background== Magellan was a member of [[the Showmen]] who earned [[Cap (Fallout 76)|caps]] from busking on the [[Atlantic City Boardwalk|Boardwalk]], and gave himself an alias based on the explorer of the same name.[[Extortion!]] He was fascinated by the [[Overgrown]] in [[Atlantic City]] and wanted to learn how to train them.[[Letter of resignation (Susan's cabin)]][[Training plan]] However, he was conned by [[Sal Sticky Fingers]] and was duped into believing that he could talk with a scientist from the fictitious "All-American Institute of Botanical Humanoid Research." After discovering he had been tricked into wasting his caps, an angry Magellan left Atlantic City and took his act on the road.[[Extortion!]] After scratching off [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|the Pitt]] as a potential location to travel to,[[Magellan's log 2]] he ended up in [[Appalachia]], hauling a wagon with caged Overgrown (giving them names such as "[[Allistaire]]") that he was still trying desperately, and failing, to train.[[Magellan's log 1]] Magellan's caravan was protected by the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]], having paid for equipment from [[Luca Costa]],[[Bill of sale (Ghoul Within)|Bill of sale]] but Magellan fired his assistants [[Emeric]] and [[Jolie]] for wanting to get rid of the Overgrown. Magellan then foolishly chose to let the Overgrown out of their cages as part of his training methods. The Overgrown, including "Allistaire," killed him and presumably the nearby Blue Ridge guards, leading the Overgrown to spread out around [[Susan's cabin]] in [[Skyline Valley (region)|Skyline Valley]].[[Magellan's log 3]] As a result, Magellan was directly responsible for the Overgrown no longer being a threat exclusive to Atlantic City.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How did the Overgrown end up in Appalachia?"''
[[Black-Eyed Susan]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Overgrown...? Oh, you mean those plant hooligans? I have no idea. This whole time I thought they were some leftover superweapon the commies made.|Confused at first, she has never heard the term Overgrown before. Then realized what the player is talking about. Answering genuinely.}} {{Tooltip|Some kind of high-tech killer shrubbery. They don't have any buckets and bolts though. Strange.|Commenting on the strangeness of the creatures inhabiting the meadow.}} {{Tooltip|I don't know if it matters much, but I saw a broken down caravan a little ways from here. No one's come back to claim it. Maybe someone brought them here? I've certainly never seen them in Appalachia before.|Thinking aloud.}}"''

With your permission, of course. Is that flimsy human body of yours really doing you any favors?|sound=Parthenia Blankenship 00799d4e_1.ogg}} '''Parthenia Blankenship''' is a [[ghoul]] scientist and member of the [[Revenants]] at [[Radiant Hills]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76GW}}. ==Background== Parthenia grew up with her father, a general in the [[United States Armed Forces]],[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You mentioned you would tell me more about your past if I stuck around."''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"My father was a general, stationed on-site here at the silo. I was an adolescent bag of ailments. My health conditions kept me largely isolated and immobilized, and he was the only family I had. So I had an exception to stay here with him. Well, one day the War happened, and everything went terribly, terribly wrong. There was a very loud noise, lots of distant panic in other rooms, and then... Well, I noticed it was very quiet. {{Tooltip|When I finally left my room, the place was empty. I guess everyone evacuated, or... Well, I don't know.|The barest hint of sadness at the thought that her father abandoned her too}}"''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) and did not know her mother; motherhood and maternal care continues to be a foreign concept for her.Parthenia Blankenship: ''"This way, my dear test subject. Into the lab, where the excitement happens!"''
[[Leamon Price]]: ''"Er... Miss Parthenia, is it? We're still holding off on the operation 'til later, aren't we?"''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"Of course! Don't you worry the unburnt hairs on your smooth little scalp. They look very soft, by the way."''
Leamon Price: ''"Ah, well, thank you kindly! I do make sure to comb it out every morning, like my mama taught me."''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"{{Tooltip|What's it like, having a mama?|Intellectual curiosity}}"''
Leamon Price: ''"Oh, it sure is nice. She takes care of ya, listens to ya, makes you feel real special."''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"I see. And does that provide any benefits to the scientific process?"''
Leamon Price: ''"I'm not too familiar with what that is, but I bet your mama it does! {{Tooltip|That is, I mean...|Awkwardly realizing she doesn't have a mama to bet on, so that might have been a bit insensitive}}"''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"If 'mama's love' is capable of providing scientific benefits, that would be truly remarkable. I wonder if the effects could be synthesized..."''
([[Leamon Price/Dialogue|Leamon Price]] and [[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) Throughout her childhood, Parthenia suffered from various illnesses that left her continually sick and even immobilized. Her father was stationed on-site at a [[Nuclear missile (Fallout 76)|nuclear missile]] silo in northern [[Appalachia]], and they were given an exemption to let Parthenia reside at the silo, as her father was the only family she knew. On the day of the [[Great War]], Parthenia heard loud, distant noises and panic from other areas of the silo, but by the time she left her room, the facility was completely abandoned. Although she has her own theories about what happened, she acknowledges that it was much more likely a nuclear warhead at the silo failed to launch and began to leak [[radiation]], prompting the evacuation of the staff. However, she would prefer not to think about the reasons as to why she was left behind by her father in the evacuation.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"That's it? You really don't know where all the military staff went? What about your father?"''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"I have only theories. Perhaps the loud noise I heard indicated the successful creation of a vortex... {{Tooltip|...Which sent the entire military staff hurtling through space and time, never to be seen again!|With gusto! What a exciting theory!}} {{Tooltip|But more likely it was the nuclear warhead failing to launch, falling off of its supports, and cracking open.|Switching back to a fast-paced, neutral tone}} Thus beginning the slow process of filling this entire place with increasingly deadly levels of radiation. Sufficient reason for a full-scale evacuation, I would think. {{Tooltip|As for my father... I'm not sure I can explain why he would leave me behind. Well, I could, but...|A greater hint of sadness here. She knows she was unwanted. A burden.}} {{Tooltip|In any case, it's not important now. Books have always been a better friend to me than anyone else. And it remains that way.|Snapping back with a bit of defiance. No time for sadness. Only science!}}"''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) Left alone at the silo, Parthenia continued as she had always been: preferring the company of books to people. However, she also now had access to the military's papers and other resources at the silo, including laboratory equipment. Alongside this was an assortment of research chemicals, with which she was excited to experiment. Parthenia discovered that one such chemical had regenerative effects on the body. Her investigation into this mysterious chemical eventually led her to tap into the process of [[ghoul]]ification.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What happened then?"''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"I was alone like I had always been. Taking care of myself. Reading. Learning. And now, all of their military resources were at my disposal. Books, research documents, laboratory equipment. A whole new playground for knowledge! Most intriguingly, I found an assortment of chemicals ripe for experimentation. I soon found that one of these chemicals had fascinating effects on the human body... Regenerative effects. My analysis and experimentation with this chemical led to the highly functioning flesh chassis you see before you today. I ailed no longer. I was reborn! Fantastic, isn't it?"''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) According to Parthenia, this chemical had little documentation on it stored at the silo, leading her to suspect that it did not originate there. Although there were some scientists working at the silo, there was not a full-scale research operation occurring there before the Great War.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Did you find out anything else about the chemical?"''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"Well, I could describe its molecular structure, but I suspect that's not what you're asking. Documentation on the substance was mysteriously lacking. As such, I'm not sure if it even originated here. There were some scientists here, but as far as I can tell, not a full-scale research operation. In short, your hypothesis is as good as mine."''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) As a result, Parthenia did not become a ghoul by natural means, such as the much more common method of exposure to radiation in the [[wasteland]], or even the effects of the Great War.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Wait, what? You didn't become a ghoul naturally?"''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"Of course not! I've been holed up here in the silo for most of my life! But at present, all of that is besides the point. We have priorities, yes? If you're still here after Leamon's crisis is resolved, I'll tell you all the glimmering details of my unconventional past."''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) Instead, she voluntarily became a ghoul following her research into the regenerative properties of the chemical, with which she is familiar enough that she can describe its molecular structure. As such, Parthenia has developed a method to spur on and even expedite the process of ghoulification. By [[Timeline (2100-2149)#2105|2105]], this process involves the synthesis of the chemical's base formula with irradiated ore to stimulate a reaction in the [[human]] body, delivered via inhaler. The malfunctioning, inactive nuclear warhead at the silo is leaking radiation, and a heavy dose from exposure to its chamber quickens the process of becoming a ghoul, in conjunction with the inhaler's reaction in the body.Parthenia Blankenship: ''"{{Tooltip|What I need is irradiated ore. It's the only material with the right nuclear structure for massive simultaneous extraction.|Back to business. A little excited about "massive simultaneous extraction". Science is great!}} I have the base formula here already, but this version is incomplete. I need the ore to trigger the final reaction."''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I'm ready! Turn me into a ghoul!"''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"Thrilling! The procedure is quite simple. Just pick up that inhaler and give it a puff. You may feel something like a rush of exhilaration. Just over there is a chamber containing a nuclear warhead. It's leaking... heavily. You are to walk inside the chamber. The heavy dose of radiation will stimulate the reaction already happening inside your body and thus expedite it. This will be painless, but will likely cause you to lose consciousness. By the time you awake, the transformation will be complete. Try not to panic when that happens. You will still be you, of course. Just... improved. At your own pace, then. I will, of course, monitor the entire procedure."''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) When the [[Revenants]] discovered the missile silo where Parthenia lived,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You needed a place to hide. So you came here."''
[[Maddox Mullen]]: ''"We were lucky to find this place. Unfortunately, not all of us made it here."''
([[Maddox Mullen/Dialogue|Maddox Mullen's dialogue]]) Parthenia became a part of their faction, although she is somewhat distant from the other ghouls that make up their members. Many ignore Parthenia unless they need something from her, but she has gotten along well with [[Kevan Asherton]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I was more meaning to ask how you're getting along with everyone..."''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"{{Tooltip|Well, mostly everyone ignores me unless they need something.|Matter of fact, unbothered}} Every now and then Asher will sit nearby and pretend to sharpen his knife. So, I'd say we're getting along."''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) She has even forayed into dentistry while helping the other ghouls,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What do you think of the other ghouls?"''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"There's a fascinating range of deterioration among them. Ghouls created naturally - if you can call it that - they tend to go through a more gradual process. Ms. Vo has been a ghoul for the good part of her nascent life, and only just lost her first tooth! She was remarkably bent out of shape about it. Came to me in tears, requesting an immediate implant. I think the operation went well for being my very first foray into the dental field."''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) and serves as their "doctor-in-training."Parthenia Blankenship: ''"Why don't you wait over there for now? Your condition presents a unique learning opportunity, so it is incumbent on this doctor-in-training to run some tests before the transformation."''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) Although some Revenants do avoid Parthenia due to her eccentricities,[[Revenant (character)|Revenant]]: ''"{{Tooltip|I should have Parthenia look at this, but... err... Maybe it will resolve itself.|Concerned about a strange growth, but more concerned Parthenia will do something crazy to them}}"''
([[Revenant (character)/Dialogue|Generic Revenants' dialogue]]) nevertheless, she appreciates what the Revenants have done by setting up [[Radiant Hills]] on top of and within the silo, seeing it as a safe paradise for ghouls like herself,Parthenia Blankenship: ''"{{Tooltip|The solution here is that you join us. A safe paradise for ghouls, hidden from the dangers of the outside world.|Very casually, and positively, presenting this major life change. The choice is obvious to her}} {{Tooltip|It's not like you have much choice. So what do you say?|Matter of fact}}"''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) and even as a "beacon of civilization."Parthenia Blankenship: ''"{{Tooltip|What's to worry about? We are a beacon of civilization here.|Dismissive of concerns}}"''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) She wants to continue her experimentation into the effects of ghoulification and even create more ghouls to subsequently treat and study them.Parthenia Blankenship: ''"We need more ghouls. I need to make more ghouls. I mean, the science is fascinating. Ghoulification cures countless ills - even terminal ones - but it has side effects. Flesh falling off is an obvious one, but there can be joint pain, loss of smell, loss of sight, degradation of the vocal cords, and so on. I mean, this is a completely new medical field we're inventing here, and I'm the only doctor they've got. I need data! I need subjects! With application and study, I could treat these ghouls - maybe one day bring them back to the quality of life that people like Asher wish for. They'd be happy, and more resilient to the Wasteland than any human! And you could be one of them!"''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) She says that she could write a book on the subject as one of the wasteland's most experienced and knowledgeable experts on ghoulification.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Fascinating! I reckon you're quickly becoming the foremost expert on ghoulism."''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"I reckon you reckon right! That is one of my goals, after all. A ghoul goal, you could call it. Better healthcare for all of ghoulkind. That makes me sound all kinds of benevolent, doesn't it? Do you think they'll write books about my discoveries? 'Delving into Ghoul Physiology'... by Parthenia Blankenship! That does it! I'll be writing the book myself!"''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) ===Personality and ideology=== Despite her attempts to improve healthcare for and increase scientific understanding of ghouls, Parthenia can, at times, be overzealous. The Revenants' leader, [[Maddox Mullen]], has had to restrain Parthenia's enthusiasm and mandates that she can only perform experiments with test subjects' consent. This is something that Parthenia has trouble understanding, displaying a struggle with boundaries on her part.Parthenia Blankenship: ''"{{Tooltip|Well, don't be shy. I only perform experiments with consent. Maddox insisted.|Inviting at first. Then mocking, like a chastised child who thinks it's really stupid.}}"''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) In general, Parthenia speaks from a matter-of-fact and direct perspective, even if it is occasionally blunt enough to be at the expense of social graces.Parthenia Blankenship: ''"{{Tooltip|Find anything out there? Never mind. I don't think I'm particularly interested.|Jolly and matter of fact. Not intentionally rude}}"''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) What may be difficult subjects for others will be obvious and straightforward for her, and she speaks primarily from her own point-of-view as a result.Parthenia Blankenship: ''"{{Tooltip|It's nothing at all to be ashamed about. Tongue pustules are a perfectly normal, if uncommon, side effect.|Not sure why anyone would be embarrassed about tongue pustules}} At least according to my hypothesis. Which, unfortunately, shall remain unproven this day."''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) By comparison, when she is discussing scientific subjects that greatly interest her, she quickly lights up and speaks eagerly.Parthenia Blankenship: ''"{{Tooltip|Unless you're growing pustules under your tongue which I haven't gained the privilege of seeing yet. Well, are you?|Speaking quickly. Impatient. Eager to examine the issue if there is one.}}"''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You know what? Sounds great, Parthenia. Let's just... move on to the next topic."''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"Ooh, what's the next topic? Ventricular microbiology?"''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) Parthenia believes that becoming a ghoul is a net benefit, and she has a very positive outlook regarding the process of ghoulification.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"This is crazy! Who in their right mind would become a ghoul on purpose?"''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"The better question is, who wouldn't? By any measure, becoming a ghoul is a net benefit."''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) In contrast to those who are more pessimistic, like Kevan Asherton, Parthenia sees the ghoul life as the good life; it resolved her issues with frequent adolescent illness and provided an enduring lifespan.Parthenia Blankenship: ''"{{Tooltip|These are prime candidates for the gift of an enduring, affliction-free existence! We must welcome them!|Extremely excited about this prospect}} Disposing of them would be terribly wasteful."''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) She is firm enough in this belief that she would be genuinely puzzled as to how or why anyone would disagree with the notion of becoming a ghoul, though she understands people may need time to consider such a big choice and change.Parthenia Blankenship: ''"{{Tooltip|Will the irradiated one go all-in on a new lifespan? Or is being human so important as to die for?|Puzzled as to why anyone would choose the second option}} No need for a final answer just now, by the way. There are some preparations to make before we can finalize anything."''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I'm going to stay human for now, thanks."''
Parthenia Blankenship: ''"{{Tooltip|Suit yourself. I'll be here if you change your mind.|Disappointed and not afraid to show it, but quick to move on}}"''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) She continues to search for willing test subjects for her scientific pursuits, and has at least given consideration to the thought of ghoulifying all of Appalachia, even if she rejects it on the basis of never being able to "get away with it."Parthenia Blankenship: ''"No, no, now that's just ridiculous, Thenia. Ghoulifying all of Appalachia? You'd never get away with it!"''
([[Parthenia Blankenship/Dialogue|Parthenia Blankenship's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |essential =yes |ghost =yes |quests involved =[[Leap of Faith]] |quests started =[[A Fresh Pair of Genes]] }} ===Quests=== * [[Leap of Faith]]: Parthenia appears during this quest after Kevan Asherton holds up [[Leamon Price]] and the player character. Rather than having Kevan kill them, Parthenia instead proposes the idea that Leamon (and the player character, if they wish) transform into a ghoul. The player character and Kevan acquire irradiated ore from the [[Emmett Mountain side tunnel]] to use in Parthenia's formula, and she creates the inhaler for Leamon to use, if he is encouraged to become a ghoul. * [[A Fresh Pair of Genes]]: Parthenia starts this quest, in which she gives the player character the opportunity to become a ghoul. After they accept this offer and undergo her method of ghoulification, she is present for the player character's reawakening in the Radiant Hills clinic as a ghoul. ===Other interactions=== Parthenia resides in the laboratory in the [[hillside cavern]] interior, which is connected to a cave entrance, as well as to [[Radiant Hills]]. Although she briefly appears in Radiant Hills' clinic after completing [[A Fresh Pair of Genes]] to greet the player after transforming into a ghoul, after the quest, she returns to the hillside cavern laboratory permanently. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Radiation quack outfit]] |weapon =[[10mm pistol (Fallout 76)|10mm pistol]] |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Parthenia Blankenship appears only {{in|FO76GW}}. ==Behind the scenes== Parthenia is voiced by [[Abby Espiritu]], although the role is not listed in the in-game credits.[https://archive.ph/gY2X5 filipinohollywood on Instagram]: ''"Other credits include - Video Games: “Elegg” (NIKKE), “Poppy” (Pokémon Masters EX), “Parthenia Blankenship” (Fallout 76 - Ghoul Within)."'' In a pre-release, preview article by ''TheGamer'', Parthenia's voice actor was initially misidentified as [[imdb:nm2103271|Corina Boettger]], and this error was subsequently repeated in other sources based on the original reporting.[https://web.archive.org/web/20241219220437/https://www.thegamer.com/fallout-76-ghoul-preview/ Fallout 76 Ghoul Preview - A Transformative Update For The Appalachian Wasteland] (original version; archived December 19, 2024) Boettger denied that they voiced Parthenia after the release of ''Ghoul Within'',[https://archive.ph/7hu0C Corina Boettger on Twitter]: ''"Hey @thegamerwebsite do you know something I don't know. I'm 99% sure I am not in fallout 76... unless you truely know something I don't..."'' and ''TheGamer''{{'}}s mention of Boettger was subsequently retracted.[https://archive.ph/BdXgn Fallout 76 Ghoul Preview - A Transformative Update For The Appalachian Wasteland] (updated version; archived March 21, 2025) Parthenia's true voice actor, Abby Espiritu, was not announced until several weeks after the release of ''Ghoul Within''. In localized versions of the game, Parthenia's voice is dubbed by Sophie Ouaknine in French, among other languages. ==Gallery== FO76GW Leap of Faith final.jpg|Parthenia in the laboratory with [[Leamon Price]] and [[Kevan Asherton]] ==References== {{Ref box}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox Ghoul Within}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Ghoul Within ghoul characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 scientists]] [[Category:Revenants characters]] [[ru:Парфения Бланкеншип]]

But I don't mind takin' a break to chat.|sound=Regular Debbie 007a11c3_1.ogg}} '''Regular Debbie''' is a [[ghoul]] associate of the [[Revenants]] at [[Radiant Hills]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76GW}}. ==Background== Debbie was born and raised in [[The Pitt|Pittsburgh]] before the [[Great War]]. She worked in the city's heavy industry and was affiliated with the [[Pittsburgh Union]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Tell me about yourself."''
Regular Debbie: ''"'Tell me about yourself?' What is this, a job interview? A blind date? I know ol' Deb's a catch, but buy me dinner first. Not a lot to tell, really. Born and raised in Pittsburgh, before the bombs. Worked in the plants, you know? Got this extra-strength tan when they blew the city to bits. And hey, I've kept my looks ever since!"''
([[Regular Debbie/Dialogue|Regular Debbie's dialogue]]) She was laboring in the factory where she was employed when the [[Nuclear weapons|bombs]] dropped, but happened to be below ground in a lower level of the facility. This saved her from being killed in a direct strike, but [[radiation]] was still able to seep down and affect her. By the time she managed to free herself out of the rubble and get back to the topside, the process of [[ghoul]]ification was already underway.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"If I can ask - what happened, when the bombs hit? How'd you survive?"''
Regular Debbie: ''"The city got blown all to hell, that's what happened! What do you think happens when it gets nuked repeatedly? Ah, relax. I know what you meant. Me, I was in the factory when it happened. One of the lower levels, actually below ground. Only reason I wasn't instantly toast, probably. But, radiation doesn't care. Wasn't deep enough, too close to the blast itself, I dunno. Shoulda died, and fast, but I didn't. Didn't know why, didn't care, and I wasn't gonna wait to die of thirst or whatever. By the time I dug free of the rubble, I was already startin' to change into the beaut you see before you. Lucky me, right?"''
([[Regular Debbie/Dialogue|Regular Debbie's dialogue]]) The first thing that Debbie did in the aftermath of the Great War was check on her family and friends to see if they survived. However, her parents' block had been completely obliterated, and she found her sister in a nearly unrecognizable state. Her own home had been destroyed, and Debbie was left without the people she cared about, or even her own skin.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What about family or friends? You must have had somebody."''
Regular Debbie: ''"This ain't somethin' I normally talk about. I say what I think and I'll take on anyone that's got a problem with that, but... Bein' unafraid like that isn't the same as bein'... Hell, I ain't got the words for it. Yeah. I had family. Friends, too. I didn't mention it right away, but the first thing I did when I got free was go looking for them. Hopin' they'd survived, somehow. I had, why couldn't they? Stupid. My folks...their whole block was ash. My sister's place was one blackened wall and... what was left... It wasn't her any more. The bombs took everything. Everyone I cared about, my home, even my friggin' skin. This...this is all that's left."''
([[Regular Debbie/Dialogue|Regular Debbie's dialogue]]) However, Debbie survived in spite of this misfortune, as she found new places to use as shelter and scavenged for supplies, which resulted in her getting in more than a few fights. Although many left the city, those who stayed, including Debbie, worked to rebuild, and helped get many of the industrial factories running again. Some may have questioned the purpose of restarting these facilities, but Debbie says it gave the survivors something to work toward, giving them a sense of normalcy, not to mention the factories' manufacturing capabilities opening the doors to trade.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What did you do when you got free from the rubble?"''
Regular Debbie: ''"It was...bad. A lot of the city was just...gone. Rubble, blown all over the damn place by the blasts. The rest was mostly on fire. Not a lot of survivors, not above ground, anyway. A lot of those were sick, dying. Pukin' up their own guts, fallin' apart...worse. I... I got by. Found places to shelter, scavenged for supplies in the wreckage, like most of the survivors. Got in some fights. Lots of people who could, left. The rest of us who stayed started to rebuild. Some of the factories were still standing, so we got them running. Seems stupid, maybe, but it gave us something to do. We could make things. Trade with other survivors. It's what we knew. When you go through that... Afterwards, something that felt normal and gave living structure - you cling to that."''
([[Regular Debbie/Dialogue|Regular Debbie's dialogue]]) It was around this time that Debbie earned her nickname: while working on a job post-War, Debbie was called "Ghoul Debbie" to differentiate her from another woman named [[Debbie (human)|Debbie]], who was an unaffected [[human]]. She had a forceful "talk" (using her boots and fists) with the other workers who were calling her by this name, and emphasized the point that there would soon be more ghouls than humans due to the radiation in the area. This assertive rebuttal from Debbie led others to start calling her "Regular Debbie," which she liked, and the name stuck.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I have to ask about the name."''
Regular Debbie: ''"All right, fine. So I was workin' this job, and there was another Debbie, and she wasn't a ghoul. Some of the guys started calling me 'Ghoul Debbie', you know, so they knew which they were talkin' about. So I had little chat with them. The boots and fists kinda chat, you know the type. Told 'em with all the rads around pretty soon there'd be more of us ghouls than them. After that, folks started calling me 'Regular Debbie'. I thought that was pretty funny, so I let 'em. It stuck."''
([[Regular Debbie/Dialogue|Regular Debbie's dialogue]]) Due to heavy nuking of Pittsburgh in the Great War, the city had a significant ghoul population, both normal and [[Feral ghoul|feral]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Are there a lot of ghouls in The Pitt?"''
Regular Debbie: ''"{{Tooltip|Like you wouldn't believe. Not all of them as good lookin' or as fun to talk to as me, of course.|Casually playful}} But yeah, we got a mess. Mostly the crazy cannibal type, you know the ones, but a lot like me, too. Odds of a person turnin' ghoul are pretty bad, but you nuke a city that hard, you're gonna end up with a bunch."''
([[Regular Debbie/Dialogue|Regular Debbie's dialogue]]) However, Debbie still experienced discrimination from people who were scared of ghouls and thought they would all eventually go feral. Although the normally-violent [[Fanatics]] gang had made promises to treat ghouls well, Debbie recognized this as a trap and saw how many ghouls who joined them turned into [[Slavery|slaves]] or corpses, and avoided this fate for herself.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How are ghouls treated in The Pitt?"''
Regular Debbie: ''"How do you think? Everybody's scared of us, even if we talk and act just like we used to. Some tolerate us better'n others, but mostly they think we're gonna go feral eventually. Fanatics talked a big game, said they were different. Liars. Ghouls that go to them end up basically slaves. Or dead."''
([[Regular Debbie/Dialogue|Regular Debbie's dialogue]]) Debbie says that being a ghoul has been hard, as she recognizes others' fears about going feral, but she tries to hold onto her own principles and make herself useful, at the same time rejecting anyone who gives her grief.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Has being a ghoul been hard for you?"''
Regular Debbie: ''"Hard? Yeah, you could say that. Nobody's had it easy, but smoothskins ain't gotta deal with lookin' like this. I make myself useful, I kick the ass of anybody that gives me too much grief, I get by all right. But you get reminded, every day, even if you don't look at yourself. Your best pals look at you sometimes and you can see 'em wondering: 'Is today the day your brain shuts off and you eat my face?' 'Round here you don't have to deal with that. But out there? It never goes away."''
([[Regular Debbie/Dialogue|Regular Debbie's dialogue]]) Despite trying to make her home a better place post-War, Debbie could not stay in Pittsburgh forever. The city became [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|the Pitt]], a violent hellhole that only got worse and worse, despite their efforts to the contrary. Debbie came to believe that her true home was long gone, and once she came to terms with that, she felt that it was time to leave. Heading out with no real direction in mind, she eventually came across a group of ghouls while on the road. They turned out to be the [[Revenants]], who explained their history of having been hunted down and targeted, with which Debbie empathized. The Revenants told Debbie that they were on their way to set up a more permanent home for themselves and needed help with construction. Debbie found assisting the Revenants in exchange for a place to live to be a good deal. However, she has rejected multiple offers from leader [[Maddox Mullen]] to be a true member of the [[Fallout 76 factions|faction]], as she does not think their secretive, [[Raiders|raiding]], outcast lifestyle is for her.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How did you leave the Pitt and end up here?"''
Regular Debbie: ''"I stayed a long time in Pittsburgh. Clingin' onto home, or at least... the idea of it. But truth was that Pittsburgh became The Pitt. It wasn't home no more, much as I tried to believe it was. Home was gone. Once I finally came to terms with that, it was time to leave. Don't know where to, even now. I was on the road in God knows where when this gang of ghouls visited me in the night. I was shocked to see so many ghouls outside The Pitt. Less shocked when they started explaining things. How they were hunted, then hunted again. Said they was going somewhere to set up permanently, and they needed all the help they could get. Didn't seem like too bad a gig: helping out in exchange for food and shelter. Maddox is under some kind of spell thinking I'm going to join up permanently. This kind of life ain't for me. I'll happily risk my hide in exchange for freedom."''
([[Regular Debbie/Dialogue|Regular Debbie's dialogue]])Regular Debbie: ''"Bunch of outcasts living underground. Can't say it's for me."''
([[Regular Debbie/Dialogue|Regular Debbie's dialogue]]) Nevertheless, Debbie remains an associate (albeit not a full-time member) of the Revenants and resides in [[Radiant Hills]], where she helps build up the settlement as the leader of their construction efforts. This includes restoring the buildings above ground near the missile silo, as well as setting up fortifications and defenses for the area's perimeter.Regular Debbie: ''"Name's Debbie. Folks call me Regular Debbie. Just roll with it. Came out of The Pitt, and now I'm here fixing the place up for the crew. Got all kinds of things breaking after being all but abandoned for two decades. And fortifications to build. But I don't mind takin' a break to chat."''
([[Regular Debbie/Dialogue|Regular Debbie's dialogue]])Regular Debbie: ''"I prefer the term 'Chief Construction Officer'. Ah, I'm kidding you. This place is already constructed, mostly. Got all kinds of leaks and code violations, though. Don't worry yourself about it. Debbie's got it all fixed up."''
([[Regular Debbie/Dialogue|Regular Debbie's dialogue]]) She has also casually interacted with [[Kevan Asherton]]'s combat training, in which she showed up late but proceeded to strike every target in record time, showing exceptional marksmanship. However, she was also chastised by Kevan for "excessive personal conversations."[[Asher's training notes]] Although she is glad to have left the Pitt behind,Regular Debbie: ''"Glad to be out of that hellhole."''
([[Regular Debbie/Dialogue|Regular Debbie's dialogue]]) Debbie does still occasionally wonder about the old factory where she used to work, and hopes it is still under the control of the Union.Regular Debbie: ''"Wonder how the factory's doing? Still Union, I hope."''
([[Regular Debbie/Dialogue|Regular Debbie's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |essential =yes |quests involved = |quests started = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Settler welder outfit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== Although she is present at Radiant Hills' exterior, Debbie will not be available for dialogue with a [[human]] player character; one must complete [[A Fresh Pair of Genes]] to [[Fallout 76 playable ghoul|become a ghoul]] in order to open a conversation with Debbie. ==Appearances== Regular Debbie appears only {{in|FO76GW}}. ==Behind the scenes== {{FO76CC}} {{See also|Regular Debbie (cut)}} [[Regular Debbie (cut)|Regular Debbie]] was originally going to be a resident of [[The Whitespring Resort|the Whitespring Refuge]] as part of the ''[[Expeditions: The Pitt]]'' update, but her appearance was cut. This early incarnation of Regular Debbie's character shares much of her background, such as being a ghoul from the Pitt, but the character was rewritten for the Revenants and has some differences. They are listed on separate pages to differentiate between the cut and live versions of Regular Debbie, which also have different dialogue trees. {{FO76CC|end}} ==Bugs== {{Platforms|pc}} Debbie and [[Ernie Navarro]], the two unique named characters found at the Radiant Hills exterior, may not spawn correctly and might not be able to be found anywhere at the location, as of the [[Public Test Server]]. One potential solution is to first fast travel to Radiant Hills' interior, then take the elevator up to the exterior.{{Verify|03:52, 6 March 2025 (UTC)|type=bug}} ==References== {{References|2}} {{Navbox Ghoul Within}} [[Category:Ghoul Within ghoul characters]] [[Category:Revenants characters]] [[Category:Pittsburgh Union characters]] [[ru:Настоящая Дебби]]

([[Dottie (Gone Fission)/Dialogue|Dottie's dialogue]]) is a [[ghoul]], [[Conspiracy theory|conspiracy theorist]] and potential [[Fallout 76 allies|lite ally]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76GF}}. Dottie is available to purchase as a reward during the twenty-first in-game [[Fallout 76 seasons|season]], ''[[Gone Fission (season)|Gone Fission]]''. ==Background== Dottie was born before the [[Great War]] and when the bombs fell, her parents took her to a bunker under their house where she grew up and spent a majority of her young life. She learned many of her conspiracy theories from her parents, which seems to be where the basis of her beliefs began. At some point, her parents began to be more secretive and act strangely before one day leaving without explanation; not long after, the bunker began to flood with water and Dottie was forced to flee and leave it behind. After leaving, it is not known where she went, though she claims to have tried to share her theories to various other people she has encountered. She made it her life goal to uncover "hidden truths" and find her parents to get answers. It is unknown when she became a ghoul, though she does not seem to know what a ghoul is, rather thinking that her transformation is a result of puberty.Dottie: ''"{{Tooltip|Oh come on, don't be coy. You know what happened. You get to a certain age and then puberty happens.|Context: she's confusing the effects of radiation with puberty.}} Hair stops growing, your baby nose falls out so the adult one can grow in. Still waiting on that last one. Don't worry, it's completely natural, and it happens to everyone at some point. Some later than others. {{Tooltip|In fact, it happened to my parents around the same time as me. Weird coincidence huh?|Oblivious to how weird her logic is}}"''
([[Dottie (Gone Fission)/Dialogue#106|Dottie's dialogue]]) ===Beliefs=== Dottie talks about many nonsensical conspiracy theories, believing in many crazy ideas while also being oblivious to many of the actual secrets of the pre-War world, even claiming [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] was "the only trustworthy company." She has heard of organizations like the [[Enclave (Fallout 76)|Enclave]], however, she does not believe in it, and seems to blame many things on [[Nuka-Cola]] and the [[United States government|government]]. While she does occasionally get close to the truth in rare cases (such as [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|super mutants]] originally being planned as super soldiers), she is wrong when it comes to a vast majority of her theories. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |quests started = |essential =yes |ally =yes |allyfurn =[[Dottie's strange boxes]] |wares =Junk items, Outfits, Weapons, [[Harpoon (Fallout 76)|Harpoons]], [[U.S. Covert Operations Manual (Fallout 76)|''U.S. Covert Operations Manual 5'']], [[CAPS ARE CAP-ITALISM?]], [[TOYING WITH US!]] |caps =yes |bonus =Unshakeable Beliefs: * +1 [[Endurance (Fallout 76)| Endurance]] and [[Intelligence (Fallout 76)| Intelligence]] * +30 [[Energy Resistance (Fallout 76)|Energy Resistance]] |other = |romanced = }} ===Daily buff=== Dottie provides the following buffs for 1 hour when the player is ready to “learn” her Unshakeable Beliefs: * Increases [[Energy Resistance (Fallout 76)|Energy Resistance]] by 30 * Increases [[Endurance (Fallout 76)| Endurance]] and [[Intelligence (Fallout 76)| Intelligence]] by 1 ===Other interactions=== The player character can flirt with Dottie, which she responds to by being flustered and trying to move on quickly.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"[Flirt] Since we're doing an under cover investigation, how about we investigate under some covers?"''
Dottie: ''"O-o-oh, w-well I uh think-- OH! Oh-oh no. I- I had heard reports about 'love' being in the air. I didn't know it was weaponized already. Hoo-boy. Let's NOT take some deep breaths and maybe this psychological warfare will pass. I'm going over here to... hahaha pretend this didn't happen. Let me know when... that is out of your system."''
([[Dottie (Gone Fission)/Dialogue#44|Dottie's dialogue]]) The flirting cannot advance beyond this, though it does unlock a new idle dialogue line.Dottie: ''"{{Tooltip|They didn't mean anything by it. How could they? I mean, it was the chemicals... Right?|Context: Talking to herself, trying to explain why the player flirted with her.}}"''

DSSBNUD, or Dottie's Stock of Significantly Benign Non-Confidential and Unrestricted Documents!"''
([[Dottie (Gone Fission)/Dialogue|Dottie's dialogue]]) * Dottie's shop name was originally going to be DCOUTTSYFFTSOL, or "Dottie's Collection Of Universal Truths That Set You Free From The Shackles Of Lies." However, this proved to be too awkward to pronounce as an [[Acronyms and Abbreviations in Fallout|acronym]].Dottie: ''"I was going to call it 'Dottie's Collection Of Universal Truths That Set You Free From The Shackles Of Lies' but DCOUTTSYFFTSOL is awkward to say."''
([[Dottie (Gone Fission)/Dialogue|Dottie's dialogue]]) ==Appearances== Dottie appears only {{in|FO76GF}}. ==Behind the scenes== * Much of Dottie's dialogue contains references to real-world [[Conspiracy theory|conspiracy theories]] and conspiracy culture: ** Dottie references [[wikipedia:Moon landing conspiracy theories|Moon landing denialism]] by responding with her own theory: the [[Moon]] itself is fake.Dottie: ''"{{Tooltip|I've heard some people say that the missions to the Moon were faked. They're missing the big picture. The Moon itself is fake.|Starts dismissive, ends confidently.}}"''
([[Dottie (Gone Fission)/Dialogue|Dottie's dialogue]]) ** When Dottie says "you've never once unhinged your jaw to moisten your eyeballs," this is a reference to the [[wikipedia:Reptilian conspiracy theory|reptilian conspiracy theory]], which alleges that the powers controlling the world are lizard-people who take human forms; some lizards are famously able to unhinge their jaw like Dottie says. The script notes for her dialogue confirm the reference to reptilian conspiracy theories is intentional. * When Dottie finishes presenting one of her conspiracy theories, she may end the dialogue by saying ''"Nothing more to it. It just works."''Dottie: ''"{{Tooltip|Nothing more to it. It just works.|Said to cap off a conspiracy theory rant}}"''
([[Dottie (Gone Fission)/Dialogue|Dottie's dialogue]]) This is a reference to [[Bethesda Game Studios]]' E3 2015 presentation, in which [[Todd Howard]] said "it just works" in regards to ''[[Fallout 4]]''{{'}}s [[Fallout 4 settlements|settlement]] system. "It just works" later became a meme for Bethesda games as a whole, often in a sarcastic reference to frequent in-game glitches. * Dottie's conspiracy theories, in combination with her heavy distrust of an ominous "Government" and her distaste of taxes,Dottie: ''"You're probably gonna meet a fate worse than death, you know. Like being trapped in the deep abyss. Or paying taxes."''
([[Dottie (Gone Fission)/Dialogue|Dottie's dialogue]]) appears to satirize libertarianism by playing on the intersection of anti-government sentiment and conspiracy culture. * Although Dottie explains that, in-universe, her name is a reference to [[Morse code]], "dotty" is a term that can also mean someone who is mad or eccentric. ==Gallery== Score s21 camp ally dottie l.webp|[[Atomic Shop]] image depicting Dottie in [[Vault Girl]] format Score s21 camp ally dottie c3.webp|Atomic Shop image Score s21 camp ally dottie c2.webp|Dottie's ally object Score s21 camp ally dottie c1.webp|Dottie with her boxes FO76GF_Dottie_Fish.png|Fish with camera lens eyes ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Gone Fission}} {{Navbox vendors FO76}} {{Navbox allies FO76}} [[Category:Gone Fission characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 allies]] [[Category:Fallout 76 merchants]] [[ru:Дотти (Gone Fission)]]

One minute I was -|Lucid and panicked, interrupted by pain after 'was'.}} *Pained yelp* {{tooltip|What I be meanin' to say is that we've traveled in from the East, sampling as many catches as this place has to offer.|Forcing himself to appear calm.}} {{tooltip|And now we're looking to share this ancient art form and sell quality equipment to fine customers, such as yerself.|overly-friendly.}}|sound=Raymond Clark 007b929e_1.ogg}} '''Captain Raymond Clark''' is one of two traveling [[Fallout 76 vendors|merchants]] operating at the [[Fisherman's Rest]] in [[Appalachia]]. He appears {{In|FO76GF}}. ==Background== Raymond Clark was born the son of [[Deidre (Gone Fission)|Deidre]] and a ship's officer, and continued in the same line of work as both his father and grandfather.[[Captain's logs#Captain's log #1|Captain's log #1]] He captained a ship with a crew that would go out and fish and return to ports to sell their catches. Raymond would sometimes sell their catches for less than they were worth, but he felt bad for those on shore and wanted them to "fill their bellies for a night", if nothing else. At some point, after noticing the sea and its creatures were getting more and more hostile, eventually a storm rolled in that lasted for at least three days and nights.[[Diary excerpts#Excerpts #1|Diary excerpts #1]] Raymond ultimately woke up onshore afterwards, recording that he had terrible visions, though he was unsure if they were memories or nightmares. The "same figure" was "always lurking in them" and he noted that it became hard to tell what was real or not, and that afterward he felt "strange urges".[[Diary excerpts#Excerpts #2|Diary excerpts #2]] By the time he is encountered by the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] in [[Timeline (2100-2149)#2105|2105]], Raymond appears to be in a precarious situation. Though he works with [[The Fisherman]] for the supposed goal of reintroducing [[Fallout 76 fishing|fishing]] to wasteland society, he frequently drops hints of something more nefarious going on but always appears to suffer from severe head pain conveniently right before he can delve into the details. What he is able to deliver suggests there is more than meets the eye when it comes to the Fisherman and their "ship" [[Linda-Lee]].A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"That fish thing pointed me to you."''
Raymond Clark: ''"{{tooltip|Oh. Him. He's truly a monstrous crea-|Disdainful then cut off by searing pain in head}} *Pained Moan* He's truly a fine specimen, isn't he? A gentle soul."''
([[Raymond Clark/Dialogue|Raymond Clark's dialogue]])A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Who is the creature I just spoke with?"''
Raymond Clark: ''"{{tooltip|He's some kind of a-|Lucid and scared}} *Pained groan* He's a swell fella, just looks a little different from you and me, is all!"''
([[Raymond Clark/Dialogue|Raymond Clark's dialogue]])A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What is this place? Some kind of freak show?"''
Raymond Clark: ''"I'd be careful making those kinds of japes around here, friend. Ya never know who might take it the wrong way..."''
([[Raymond Clark/Dialogue|Raymond Clark's dialogue]])A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Is that a giant crab back there?"''
Raymond Clark: ''"{{tooltip|That monster is the one that-|Momentarily lucid and absolutely terrified. Stopped by head pain}} *pained grunt* That elegant crustacean is the Linda-Lee. She was... is... a mighty fine vessel. She deals with the fish that my friend no longer wants, and she carries us from place to place."''
([[Raymond Clark/Dialogue|Raymond Clark's dialogue]])Raymond Clark: ''"{{tooltip|Thank ye for catchin' more fish. We needed more... bait.|Ominous. Vague as to what "bait" means.}}"''
([[Raymond Clark/Dialogue|Raymond Clark's dialogue]]) The few details he is able to give indicates they arrived on board the [[Hermit crab (Fallout 76)|giant hermit crab]] from somewhere east and started collecting samples of marine wildlife the whole way. However, he does not quite remember what they do with their catches afterward.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How did you get here?"''
Raymond Clark: ''"{{tooltip|In truth, I haven't the slightest inkling. One minute I was-|Lucid and panicked, interrupted by pain after 'was'.}} *Pained yelp* What I be meanin' to say is that we traveled in from the East, sampling as many catches as this place has to offer. And now we're looking to share this ancient art form and sell quality equipment ot fine customers, such as yourself."''
([[Raymond Clark/Dialogue|Raymond Clark's dialogue]])A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you do with all the fish?"''
Raymond Clark: ''"{{tooltip|We... we... Hmm, my mind's a fog on that one. But never ye mind that. Bring us the fish we ask for, and maybe it'll jog me memory.|He tries to remember, but can't. Hopeful on the last line.}}"''

Fishing_Fisherman_VendorFaction |CK race =FishermanRace |class =raiderClass |combat style= |actor =[[Jesse Burch]] |designer =[[Gus De Tommaso]] |voice type =Fish_NPCM_Fisherman |edid =FISH_Vendor_TheFisherman |formid =007AC576 |refid = }} {{Quotation|{{Tooltip|He's some kind of a -|lucid and scared.}} {{Tooltip|*Pained groan*|Very painful for him.}} {{Tooltip|He's a swell fella, just looks a little different from [[Human|you and I]], is all!|Enthusiastic, but still in some pain.}}|sound=Raymond Clark 007aecd8_1.ogg|[[Raymond Clark]]}} '''The Fisherman''' is one of two traveling [[Fallout 76 vendors|merchants]] operating at the [[Fisherman's Rest]] in [[Appalachia]]. He appears {{In|FO76GF}}. ==Background== To date, nothing is known about the Fisherman's origins or history in the wasteland. His [[Mutations|mutated]] appearance evokes characteristics of the [[Mirelurk (Fallout 3)#Mirelurk king|mirelurk kings]] found in the [[Capital Wasteland]] and the [[lakelurk]]s found in the [[Mojave Wasteland]], but any connection is currently unknown. At some point prior to [[Timeline (2100-2149)#2105|2105]], [[Raymond Clark]] became acquainted with the Fisherman and the [[Hermit crab (Fallout 76)|hermit crab]] [[Linda-Lee]] that serves as their "ship" carrying them across the post-nuclear [[East Coast]].A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Is that a giant crab back there?"''
[[Raymond Clark]]: ''"{{tooltip|That monster is the one that-|Momentarily lucid and absolutely terrified. Stopped by head pain}} *pained grunt* That elegant crustacean is the Linda-Lee. She was... is... a mighty fine vessel. She deals with the fish that my friend no longer wants, and she carries us from place to place."''
([[Raymond Clark/Dialogue|Raymond Clark's dialogue]]) By that year, they had come from somewhere to the east of [[Appalachia]] and set up at [[Fisherman's Rest]], catching specimens of wasteland marine life for unknown purposes as well as allegedly embarking on a mission to reintroduce [[Fallout 76 fishing|fishing]] to wasteland society.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How did you get here?"''
[[Raymond Clark]]: ''"{{tooltip|In truth, I haven't the slightest inkling. One minute I was-|Lucid and panicked, interrupted by pain after 'was'.}} *Pained yelp* What I be meanin' to say is that we traveled in from the East, sampling as many catches as this place has to offer. And now we're looking to share this ancient art form and sell quality equipment ot fine customers, such as yourself."''
([[Raymond Clark/Dialogue|Raymond Clark's dialogue]]) However, Clark has hinted that there is more to the Fisherman and a nefarious reason for their activities, but he has been unable to give details due to experiencing severe head pain conveniently right before he can explain.A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"That fish thing pointed me to you."''
[[Raymond Clark]]: ''"{{tooltip|Oh. Him. He's truly a monstrous crea-|Disdainful then cut off by searing pain in head}} *Pained Moan* He's truly a fine specimen, isn't he? A gentle soul."''
([[Raymond Clark/Dialogue|Raymond Clark's dialogue]])A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Who is the creature I just spoke with?"''
[[Raymond Clark]]: ''"{{tooltip|He's some kind of a-|Lucid and scared}} *Pained groan* He's a swell fella, just looks a little different from you and me, is all!"''
([[Raymond Clark/Dialogue|Raymond Clark's dialogue]])A [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What is this place? Some kind of freak show?"''
[[Raymond Clark]]: ''"I'd be careful making those kinds of japes around here, friend. Ya never know who might take it the wrong way..."''
([[Raymond Clark/Dialogue|Raymond Clark's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |ghost =yes |none = |quests started = |essential =yes |ally = |allyfurn = |wares =[[Fallout 76 fishing|Bait]], [[Fallout 76 plans|plans]], and [[Fallout 76 recipes|recipes]]. |caps =yes |bonus = |other = |romanced = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon =[[Meat hook (Fallout 76)|Meat hook]] |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== In a Bethesda Discord AMA, members of the ''Gone Fission'' development team declined to confirm whether there is a connection between the Fisherman and the aquatic creatures he strongly resembles, but indicated that more might be revealed with additional content, as well as their desire to let the mystery unfold on its own.'''[https://www.theduchessflame.com/post/gone-fishing-ama-fallout-76-transcript Gone Fishing AMA – Fallout 76 Transcript]'''
[[Richard Stanford|Rich Stanford]]: ''"We’re on lore questions. And the next one is from Flackals... In the latest fishing update, we got to meet the mysterious Fisherman, his unwilling assistant Captain Raymond, and his partner/mobile home Linda Lee. My question is — what exactly is the Fisherman? Many people have speculated on what he could be. Is he some kind of sapient Mirelurk King, implying that he’s an animal that’s somehow achieved human-level intelligence? Or is he a severely mutated human being that’s lost his ability to speak somewhere along the way? Perhaps he’s just a wasteland wacko in a very convincing-looking fish suit? Inquiring minds would like to know."''
[[Jonathan Rush|Jon Rush]]: ''"Well, I am a member of the inquiring minds that want to know. But like my previous answer — that’s where all the fun lies. In getting those questions and thinking about those questions and just having them in your head. If everything were just exposition — this is exactly where it comes from, this was its date of birth, and its genetic makeup — it takes all the mystery out of it, right? So perhaps down the road with more fishing updates, more of their story will unfold. Or perhaps not. That’s kind of part of the fun. Those are great questions. I love how you're thinking, but I don’t want to do the character or the story a disservice by trying to lay out the exact details of who that being is and what they’re doing."''
[[Danielle Bartholomew]]: ''"Yeah. So, stay tuned."'' ==Appearances== The Fisherman appears only {{in|FO76GF}}. ==Behind the scenes== [[Double Eleven]] developer [[Gus De Tommaso]] was one of the designers who worked on content for the Fisherman, writing for the narrative of Fisherman's Rest and ''Gone Fission'' as a whole.[https://gusdetommaso.journoportfolio.com/fallout-76/ Gus De Tommaso's portfolio] ([https://archive.ph/pbxaO archived)] ==Gallery== FO76GF The Fisherman Front Render.png|Render front FO76GF The Fisherman Back Render.png|Back FO76GF The Fisherman Front Unclothed Render.png|Unclothed render front FO76GF The Fisherman Back Unclothed Render.png|Back ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group="Non-game"}} {{Navbox Gone Fission}} {{Navbox vendors FO76}} [[Category:Gone Fission characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 merchants]] [[ru:Рыболов]]

Want any?|sound=Axel 0078c96c_1.ogg}} '''Axel''' is a [[child]] who could be hired as a decorator at the [[Milepost Zero (location)|Milepost Zero]] branch of the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76MZ}}. Recruiting Axel cost 125 [[Supplies]]; he also came with his [[Sentry bot (Fallout 76)|sentry bot]] companion [[Gyro]]. The Milepost Zero gameplay was discontinued with the ''[[Burning Springs (update)|Burning Springs]]'' update. As of that update's release, Axel can no longer be recruited and thus does not appear anywhere in-game. ==Background== {{Section|FO76MZ}} ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |ghost =yes |quests involved = |events started = }} ===Upgrades=== All upgrades for Milepost Zero characters, including Axel, are handled through dialogue with [[Marley]], specifically the option to give an employee more resources. With Axel, his tiered upgrades give more options for decoration sets. Each theme gives a different look and aesthetic for the Milepost Zero interior, though the changes are purely decorative and have no other effects. * Tier 1 (initial hiring, default): 125 [[Supplies]] to hire Axel * Tier 2: 150 Supplies ** After upgrading to tier 2, the note "[[Surveying report]]" appears on the table near [[Marley]]. * Tier 3: 200 Supplies ** After upgrading to tier 3, purchasing any theme from Axel will unlock a dialogue option in which he gives the player the [[Plan: Axel's snow globe|plan]] for his snow globe. ===Decoration sets=== At Tier 1, two decoration themes are available from Axel: * Blue Ridge (0 Supplies, default) * Military (40 Supplies) Tier 2 and Tier 3 unlock one theme each: * Tier 2: Antiques (40 Supplies) * Tier 3: Cultist (40 Supplies) ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =Child tattered clothes |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== When purchasing a decoration set from Axel, the interior may not have automatically reset like it did when hiring crew members from [[Marley]]. Exiting and re-entering the Milepost Zero interior would implement the changes. ==Appearances== Axel appears only {{in|FO76MZ}}. He was [[Fallout 76 removed content|removed]] from the game with the ''[[Burning Springs (update)|Burning Springs]]'' update. ==Behind the scenes== {{FO76CC}} * In the game's files, Axel has a system set up to offer a daily miscellaneous quest. The quest would have offered one of several rewards at random, including [[Vault-Tec bobblehead (Fallout 76)|bobbleheads]], [[Fallout 76 magazines|magazines]], common or rare [[Fallout 76 junk items|junk items]], [[Fallout 76 consumables|food items]], or the [[Plan: Axel's snow globe|plan]] for his snow globe. However, this quest is not implemented in-game and cannot be accessed in any way through Axel's dialogue, and was later marked in the files as cut content. {{FO76CC|end}} * Until [[Fallout 76 patch 1.7.15.12|patch 1.7.15.12]] (update 55), Axel's snow globe was unobtainable as a result of the aforementioned cut content. With patch 55, the [[Plan: Axel's snow globe|plan]] was made accessible through Axel's tier 3 dialogue. ==Bugs== {{Platforms|pc}} Axel's dialogue would frequently bug on his opening line, and would close out without accessing the player prompts. It could take several tries to access Axel's dialogue tree without the conversation closing. This was reportedly fixed with [[Fallout 76 patch 1.7.15.12|patch 1.7.15.12]] (update 55).{{Verify|patched}} ==Gallery== FO76MZ Milepost Zero Axel and Gyro.jpg|Axel and Gyro FO76MZ Milepost Zero Axel Decorations 01.jpg|Decorations FO76MZ Milepost Zero Axel Decorations 02.jpg|Decorations {{Stub|FO76MZ}} [[Category:Milepost Zero human characters]] [[Category:Blue Ridge Caravan Company characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 removed characters]] [[ru:Аксель (Milepost Zero)]]

'''Collector Murmrgh''' is a [[mole miner]] [[Fallout 76 vendors|vendor]] who was intended to be recruited at the [[Milepost Zero (location)|Milepost Zero]] branch of the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76}}. Recruiting Murmrgh was meant to cost 200 [[Supplies]], but the character remained [[Fallout 76 cut content|cut content]].

Previously known in the files as '''Grrmrrgh''', Murmrgh was never able to be recruited in the live game, but had been in the game's files since the ''Milepost Zero'' update's release. Like [[Windy Park]], Murmrgh appeared in the [[Public Test Server]] and the patch notes indicated that Murmrgh was intended to appear in a future release. Murmrgh and Windy were both referenced on the [[Milepost Zero terminal entries]] in-game. However, the ''[[Burning Springs (update)|Burning Springs]]'' update officially discontinued the Milepost Zero gameplay, making Collector Murmrgh cut content. Although Windy was retooled for ''Burning Springs'', Collector Murmrgh was not.

Although not a normal vendor with a trading menu, Murmrgh would offer eight "mystery crates" to purchase with [[Supplies]] through the dialogue tree.
* 10 {{icon|supplies}} - Basic Mystery Crate
* 25 {{icon|supplies}} - [[The Forest|Forest]] Mystery Crate
* 25 {{icon|supplies}} - [[Toxic Valley]] Mystery Crate
* 25 {{icon|supplies}} - [[Savage Divide]] Mystery Crate
* 50 {{icon|supplies}} - [[Skyline Valley (region)|Skyline Valley]] Mystery Crate
* 50 {{icon|supplies}} - [[Ash Heap]] Mystery Crate
* 100 {{icon|supplies}} - [[The Mire|Mire]] Mystery Crate
* 100 {{icon|supplies}} - [[Cranberry Bog]] Mystery Crate
Each mystery crate would award random loot tied to the region it was named after (except for the basic crate, which had more general loot). This would include modified weapons and plans the player did not yet know.
