([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) is an imported goods [[Fallout 76 vendors|merchant]] who could be hired at the [[Milepost Zero (location)|Milepost Zero]] branch of the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76MZ}}. Recruiting Ineke cost 150 [[Supplies]]. The Milepost Zero gameplay was discontinued with the ''[[Burning Springs (update)|Burning Springs]]'' update. As of that update's release, Ineke can no longer be recruited and thus does not appear anywhere in-game. ==Background== ===Childhood=== Ineke hails from the [[Atlantic Ocean|North Atlantic]] region of [[Europe]].{{Ref|(Note 2)}} Her family consisted of her father and a sister, as well as several cousins; she never knew her mother.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Do you get on with your folks?"''
Ineke: ''"My father is a great man. He was a baker and oh, the delicacies he would create... I miss them every day! The lemon meringue tarts were heavenly. My mother, however, is a mystery. I never knew her."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Do you have siblings?"''
Ineke: ''"Just a sister, though we walk very different paths. When I left for the ocean, she was unemployed and chasing her passion for art. I used to write to her when we docked up after a delivery, and she would write back during the layover. But that was a long, long time ago. Before the wasteland. She had her head in the clouds. I miss her fondly."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) Ineke's father ran a bakery, which had been passed down in his family for at least two generations. He would frequently bake pastries and share them amongst the family, which made him a favorite relative of Ineke's cousins. Ineke herself still considers her father the best man she has ever known.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"That bakery sounds impressive..."''
Ineke: ''"t was! It originally belonged to my grandfather, and his father before him. Pretty yellow flowers in the window and the smell of fresh bread... It is one of the things I miss the most about home. Before I went away. Before war."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"I feel that Axel would like your father."''
Ineke: ''"Unfortunately, I fear you are correct. My father was always very paternal, even towards annoying children. He was a favorite among my cousins. He would make delicious desserts and we would all share them together, as a family. He is... the best man I know."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) Growing up, Ineke was also close with her sister, and the two of them often played together, exploring nature, camping in the woods, or even chasing boats down canals.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What sort of things did you do growing up?"''
Ineke: ''"My sister and I used to chase boats down canals and wander through forests and build camps together in the woods. Those memories... though they are aging, they are precious to me."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) However, while Ineke had an adventurous spirit, she was still a realist. In comparison, her sister's aspirations were less practical, or even fanciful, although this did not seriously affect the sisters' relationship. Ineke also loved her homeland, not just because of her family, but also many other things: "the food, the open fields, bike rides, and the people."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What was your favorite thing about it?"''
Ineke: ''"The food, the open fields, bike rides, and the people. It is the homeland of myself, after all. I cannot imagine the war was kind to it."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]])
{{Small|'''Note''': ''In this dialogue, the subject of the question is Europe.''}} ===Career=== Despite her love for her family and her home, wanderlust eventually took hold of Ineke. At the age of 22, she joined a large international shipping company in search of freedom on the open sea.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What sort of cargo did you move?"''
Ineke: ''"Everything and anything. I was part of a big company that shipped all across the globe. We would travel to pick up supplies and then travel further to deliver them. Ah, the places I visited. Simply beautiful. But, anyway, we shipped food, furniture, fur, tools, hats and even a telescope! Bunch of junk, but something is always going to be someone's treasure!"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) Starting out, the brunt of her work was as physical labor on cargo ships in the North Atlantic, scrubbing decks and moving boxes.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Tell me more about your time before coming here."''
Ineke: ''"So curious, I love that about you! My work before the war was similar to what we are doing now. I was moving cargo on a large ship out on the North Atlantic sea."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) The work was hard, but it allowed Ineke to see the world, and also to learn English from her crewmates.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You don't sound like you're from around here?"''
Ineke: ''"I have always been a woman of the world. My mother tongue is just one of the many languages I've grown up hearing. I ended up learning most of my English from the people I travelled with for work."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) Over time, she worked her way up the ranks and "made the changes [she] wanted to see," but not always through official or honest means. Still, Ineke's crewmates listened to her, and eventually, she became the captain of a ship with her own crew of twenty.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Did you work with a crew?"''
Ineke: ''"Yes, I did. There were a few of us. Myself and twenty others from all around the world, each with our own reasons for being out there. A ship is a good place to run from your old life."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) This was not Ineke's goal, but she took it on as an opportunity for further adventure.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You were the captain?"''
Ineke: ''"You sound surprised. I was good. People listened to me, and I worked hard. I just sought the freedom of the open ocean. To be a leader was never really my intention, but sometimes opportunities arise, and we must grasp the bull by the horns or risk missing out."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) As captain, Ineke mainly continued the business of traveling to one port to pick up shipments and then shipping them to other, more distant ports. Most of their cargo was innocuous: foodstuffs, furniture, apparel, tools, and "even a telescope." However, this was not always the case. Under Ineke, the crew occasionally conducted "extra" shipments, smuggling narcotics and rarely weapons or exotic animals.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What sort of things were you doing?"''
Ineke: ''"We would occasionally do an... extra shipment or two. Narcotics. Addictive substances that partners would pay a lot for. Sometimes weapons too, or even rare animals. I like to think I would not involve myself with that sort of work anymore. Marley would not like it much. But, even if I did, you are not a snitch anyway, are you?"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) Between all the excitement, Ineke still cherished her homeland, and would exchange letters with her sister every time she came ashore on layover after a delivery. ===Post-War=== Ineke and her crew happened to be at sea when the Great War struck, and so were spared from the nuclear exchange. From the ship deck, Ineke had a first hand view of the rest of the world burning, which she considers something that no one should ever have to live through. In particular, she recalls that despite the destruction, the end of the world was "eerily quiet" from their position.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You don't seem fond of your time at sea..."''
Ineke: ''"That ship was the love of my life. But the bombs... well, that isn't something anyone should have to live through. I was out there when they fell, and saw it all from on deck. It was eerily quiet amidst all that disaster. We watched cities burn. {{Tooltip|Well, I was having a nice day. Thanks for dredging all that up. Just kidding, I don't mind. Not a damn thing we can do about it now, anyway.|Pause and small laugh before "Just kidding".}}"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) The crew stayed at sea for some time but were forced to dock as their resources ran out. They chose to dock at [[Baltimore]], [[Maryland]], because it was relatively close to where they were buoyed and several of the crew also had family there.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"How did you end up in America?"''
Ineke: ''"We ran out of resources and had to dock somewhere, didn't we? Ended up in Baltimore. It was close to where we buoyed up, and a few of the crew had family there."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) This arrangement worked for a few months without serious problems, with Ineke and her crew continuing to live on the docked ship. However, supplies soon ran low, and some of the crew -- tasting power for the first time -- "took it into their own hands" to acquire more supplies through [[raiders|raiding]] and stealing, if not worse.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What happened when you came to shore?"''
Ineke: ''"We docked in Baltimore, and held up well enough there for a few months. But, it was a brand new world, and power was in reach for people who had never tasted it before. Eventually supplies started running low, so they took it into their own hands to deal with the problem. Situations like that can turn even the nicest people into the nastiest bastards..."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) Ineke understood the harshness of the wasteland and beared with her crew's actions for a while. However, eventually, she could no longer stand by how they were taking advantage of defenseless people (often those who needed supplies more than they did) and chose to leave the ship; a few others with similar concerns also left, but most of the crew chose to stay and continue their raiding lifestyle.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Do you know what happened to your crew?"''
Ineke: ''"Most stayed on the ship, the ones that could handle that sort of dynamic. Some strong ones, but mostly weaklings. I am not trying to preach about injustice. The wasteland is hard, I get it. But these people took advantage of those who needed far more than they did. Those who couldn't defend themselves. People who were dying, old folk, children, single mothers... people who didn't get a choice. It was a little too much, even for me. But, it was a lifetime ago now. Best not to dwell, or my own sanity may not forgive me."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) Since then, Ineke has traveled the wastes, taking on the role of an imported goods merchant: acquiring items (junk, scrap, and miscellany) from around the globe and selling them on to whoever would have them. In this way, she claims to offer to her customers a "taste of the world" and also the feeling of a less-changed past world.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Can you tell me more about your job as an imported goods merchant?"''
Ineke: ''"{{Tooltip|I'm glad you asked. I acquire items from around the globe, and sell them on.|"Acquire" sounds slightly shifty.}} {{Tooltip|I can offer common and rich folk a taste of the world... for a few caps, of course.|Proud}}"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"So you're expecting to just sell the rest of the old junk now?"''
Ineke: ''"You must consider that, in times like these, people long for treasures that make them feel like the world has not changed so much. I say clinging to the past is for fools, but each to their own, hm? Besides, nobody is making you buy them. If you don't like it? Leave it."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) She still sells essential goods such as food and clothing.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Do you sell useful stuff too?"''
Ineke: ''"Yes, of course. I have some clothes, food, and I think I saw some spare scrap, too. That piqued your interest, didn't it?"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) She has developed a web of connections who keep her informed of scavenging sites and potential inventory.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"I always have time for you, Ineke."''
Ineke: ''"Good answer! I like you. Some of my connections got in touch; we went out this morning to collect some new merchandise. You have been a good friend, so I want to give you first choice. Come trade with me anytime, or just stop by for a chat!"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Do you still talk to any of them?"''
Ineke: ''"A few, yes. The good ones. We keep in touch via letters, usually moved by different caravans. They let me know if they stumble on any other abandoned loot, then I can take my cut as a thanks for the years on the ocean. I admire their loyalty."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) Ineke enjoys this lifestyle, as her adventurous spirit has not quieted despite the dangers of the wasteland; in her words, she would rather be shot than live predictably.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Planning on sticking around long?"''
Ineke: ''"Eh, we will see! This job is comfortable... But being tied down means being stuck in a routine, and I would rather be shot than live predictably. Let us see where life takes us, hm?"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) This is helped by the fact that she has no family in the former [[United States of America|United States]] and does not plan to change that anytime soon;[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"No family around here, then?"''
Ineke: ''"Just me, and I don't plan on changing that anytime soon. Though, perhaps these fine people count as family now!"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) it also helps that she dislikes children.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you think of Axel?"''
Ineke: ''"I do not like children. They are insufferable little creatures. Very loud, and whiney. Axel is... marginally more likeable, but perhaps this is just because I must see his face every day."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) ===Shenandoah=== :''Note: the following section is partially based on gameplay progression in Milepost Zero.'' In 2105, a few weeks before the events of ''Milepost Zero'', Ineke came to [[Shenandoah National Park]] and met [[Marley]], the supervisor of the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]]'s [[Skyline Valley (region)|Skyline Valley]] branch. Marley offered Ineke a deal: work under Blue Ridge as a merchant in exchange for a quiet life. Ineke was hesitant about joining a new crew but eventually decided the opportunity was too good to pass up.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You know Marley?"''
Ineke: ''"Well enough. I met her when I arrived in Shenandoah a few weeks back. {{Tooltip|She offered me work selling my wares in exchange for a quiet life.|Pause before "quiet life". Thinking about her past.}} I wasn't sure I wanted to hang with a new crew just yet... but it was too good to pass up."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) As part of this, Ineke claims to have stopped trading in illicit goods, since Marley would not condone it... although she may still be doing so, more discreetly.[[Theodore (Milepost Zero)|Theodore]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Imported goods? Is that what they're calling narcotics these days?|About Ineke, the imported goods merchant. Mutters to himself.}}"''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) With the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] of [[Vault 76]] helping Blue Ridge set up their new branch, Ineke soon moved into their branch headquarters at [[Milepost Zero (location)|Milepost Zero]] on [[Skyline Drive]]. Ineke is initially unsure about how long she plans to stay with Blue Ridge, as she does not like to be tied down in one place for too long. However, Ineke is interested in the Vault Dwellers, as she can see that they have had their own lives of adventure. She is all too happy to stay and hear their stories, to the point of giving them fairer prices than she usually would as an incentive.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Seems everyone in this company has a story. What's yours?"''
Ineke: ''"Aha, no small talk; straight to the chase! Worry not, I wear my heart on my sleeve. But there is plenty of time to trade tales. That glint in your eye tells me you have a few of your own, hm?"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What sort of stories are you interested in hearing about?"''
Ineke: ''"Adventures! I want to hear about places traveled, food you have eaten, drinks enjoyed, people, friends, enemies, lovers... I have lived through plenty myself, but I'm ready to kick back for a little while. Still, that itch for life... it never truly disappears, does it?"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What sort of prices?"''
Ineke: ''"I could have been tempted to charge you high prices, but you intrigue me! I see some interesting tales behind those eyes. Do not worry, you can expect me to cut you a fair deal. Caps will come and go, but stories will stay long after we are both in the ground."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) However, as the trading operations at Milepost Zero grow in scale, Ineke ends up enjoying the location and the company of her colleagues (to varying degrees).Ineke: ''"This is the life. Good beer, good company."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) Although she still gets the "familar itch for adventure" every so often,Ineke: ''"Storm looks terrible today... Ah, it gives me that familiar itch for adventure."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]])Ineke: ''"Ah, warm days like these make me long for cider and the open ocean."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) she ultimately decides to stay at Milepost Zero for the foreseeable future.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Decided to stick around?"''
Ineke: ''"{{Tooltip|I have grown rather fond of this place, and these people too. So yes, for now they are stuck with me!|Laughs at end of sentence.}}"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) ==Relationships== {| class="va-table" ! colspan="2" style="text-align:center;" |Relationship table |- ! style="text-align:center;" |Family | Ineke was close with her father and sister, as mentioned above. Ineke still thinks of her father as the best man she knows, and she kept regular communication with her sister through letters. Ineke thinks her sister had her "head in the clouds;" when Ineke left for the sea, her sister was unemployed and trying to pursue a career in art. Ineke does not know what happened to her family during the Great War. She has come to terms with the fact that she will never see them again, but prefers to think that they are still alive.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Have you spoken to your family since the war?"''
Ineke: ''"I wrote down everything I wanted to say. It was... cathartic. But there is no way to send it halfway around the world, of course. My father, he will be so old now. But I like to hope my sister has found a safe space to take care of him."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) |- ! style="text-align:center;" |Former crew |Ineke is no longer in contact with most of her former ship crew, namely the ones who chose to stay in [[Baltimore]] as raiders. She does still keep in touch with the ones who left, and they send each other letters through caravans. These crew members are still grateful to Ineke for the many years on the sea together and they are part of her merchant connections: when they find abandoned loot, they let Ineke take a cut. Ineke is grateful for their continued loyalty. |- ! style="text-align:center;" |Marley |Ineke and [[Marley]] keep a cordial working relationship. Marley prefers to keep her personal life to herself; Ineke respects Marley's professionalism but thinks she would be better off "living a little more," maybe with her help.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you think of Marley?"''
Ineke: ''"{{Tooltip|She is a smart girl. Knows what she wants and keeps her head down. I respect that.|Marley is Ineke's boss at HQ.}} She needs to live a little more, though! The girl is too quiet....seems she could do with an adventure, away from the business. Ineke will sort her out."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) As the Milepost Zero branch grows, Marley does open up more, which Ineke appreciates.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Marley seems to be coming out of her shell."''
Ineke: ''"Indeed! A fine leader that girl is proving to be. I wonder what her plans are, beyond this place."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) |- ! style="text-align:center;" |Josie |Ineke believes that [[Josie (Milepost Zero)|Josie]] is too much of a dreamer (perhaps similarly to her own sister), but likes that she is eager to prove herself useful and wants to get to know her more.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you think of Josie?"''
Ineke: ''"{{Tooltip|Ah yes, Josie. She spends so much time in that head of hers...perhaps too much, hm? But it is endearing to see someone so eager to prove themselves.|Talking about Josie - a Brahmin Tamer who works at HQ.}} I hope to know more about her."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) Ineke does wish for Josie to achieve her dreams, and feels it would be "wasted potential" if she gave up for any reason.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Josie doesn't seem to be doing well."''
Ineke: ''"{{Tooltip|It is a shame to see such wasted potential in that girl. She had big dreams but... it seems her vices got the better of her.|Player gave another character, Josie, drugs in tier 2.}}"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) Ineke also believes that Josie is interested in Marley, but does not intend to gossip about it.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Josie is fitting in well here."''
Ineke: ''"{{Tooltip|I think it took her a little while to warm to the Brahmin, but she seems to be finding her place here.|Talking about Josie, a Brahmin Tamer at HQ.}} I see the way she looks at Marley, too. But you know me; I am not one to gossip."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) |- ! style="text-align:center;" |Axel |[[Axel (Milepost Zero)|Axel]] is a child, and Ineke dislikes children. She calls Axel "marginally more likeable" but attributes this to necessity since they are coworkers and have to interact daily. Axel himself doesn't realize this, and he actually thinks he and Ineke are best friends.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Ineke seems to like you a lot..."''
[[Axel (Milepost Zero)|Axel]]: ''"Ineke is awesome! We're practically best friends."''
([[Axel (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Axel's dialogue]]) As Milepost Zero develops, Ineke does start to warm to Axel a little; she still finds him annoying, but appreciates his "gusto." However, their "friendship" is still very one-sided.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Have you warmed to little Axel yet?"''
Ineke: ''"{{Tooltip|Warmed, no. I am tolerating him, we will say.|Lighthearted}} Is he still irritating? Yes, that fact remains indisputable. But I like him enough. He has... gusto."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Ineke mentioned you earlier..."''
[[Axel (Milepost Zero)|Axel]]: ''"Wow, really, what did she say?"''
Vault Dweller: ''"I think your friendship is a little... one-sided."''
Axel: ''"Oh...does she think she likes me more than I like her? That's silly. I think she's awesome!"''
([[Axel (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Axel's dialogue]]) |- ! style="text-align:center;" |Theodore | Ineke finds [[Theodore (Milepost Zero)|Theodore]] handsome even though he is a [[ghoul]]; in her words, this makes him likeable despite his "mediocre" personality. Ever perceptive, Ineke can see Theodore is troubled by his family situation with Marley and hopes he can find peace.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you think of Theodore?"''
Ineke: ''"{{Tooltip|He is a handsome man. This makes him likeable, even if his personality is mediocre.|Talking about Theo - a ghoul gunsmith who works in HQ. Marley is his daughter - their relationship is rocky.}} I do not know his story, but I can see he seeks peace, especially in his kinship with Marley... But yes, that is none of my business. Or yours either, my prying friend."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) As Milepost Zero develops, Ineke comes to admire Theodore more and more.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You and Theodore seem to get on well."''
Ineke: ''"The more I admire him, the more handsome he gets. He still looks lonely, but I believe he is finding a home here. It seems fate has been kind to him in his older age, and I'm not just talking about his looks!"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) Theodore also enjoys Ineke's company since they are the only "real adults" among Milepost Zero's full-time staff, though it is unclear if he is aware of how she feels.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Ineke is really fond of you."''
[[Theodore (Milepost Zero)|Theodore]]: ''"{{Tooltip|She's nice enough. Good to bond with a real adult, you know? Stops me going completely insane.|Talking about Ineke, the imported goods merchant.}}"''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) |- ! style="text-align:center;" |Windy |[[Windy Park|Windy]]'s [[cryptids|cryptid]] stories are intriguing to Ineke, who suspects she would rather bring monsters to Milepost Zero than keep them away.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"What do you think of Windy?"''
Ineke: ''"She intrigues me, much like you do! I do suspect she is more interested in seeking monsters, rather than keeping them away. {{Tooltip|It is no skin off my nose. Just make sure she does not lure any monsters here, hm?|Talking about Windy - a Cryptid Hunter who works in HQ.}}"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) Ineke does not actually believe most of Windy's stories but does not particularly care if they are true or not.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Windy seems... interesting?"''
Ineke: ''"Ah yes, now that's a girl with a story! I cannot say I believe most of them, but eh, who am I to dispute fact from fiction. These monsters she seeks, do they interest you too?"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) Windy doesn't seem to have any particular opinion of Ineke, but she has made special requests for merchandise from Ineke.[[Special order]] |} ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |ghost =yes |wares =* Unique CAMP and outfit [[Fallout 76 plans|plans]] * [[Fallout 76 junk items|Bulk junk]] (Tiers 2+3) |caps =yes |quests involved = |events started = }} ===Milepost Zero upgrades=== All upgrades are done through [[Marley]], specifically her dialogue option to give a vendor more supplies. {| class="va-table" ! style="text-align:center;" | Tier ! style="text-align:center;" | Cost ! style="text-align:center;" | Benefits |- | style="text-align:center;" | 1 |150 [[Supplies]] | * Initial hiring; vendor unlocked |- | style="text-align:center;" | 2 |250 Supplies | * Vendor inventory includes more unique plans and [[Fallout 76 junk items|bulk junk]] * The note [[Special order]] is placed on a table in Windy's corner of Milepost Zero * Ineke gains a dialogue branch to ask more about her life on a cargo ship |- | style="text-align:center;" | 3 |500 Supplies | * Vendor inventory includes more unique plans and bulk junk * Ineke will give the [[Plan: Ineke's snow globe|plan]] for [[Ineke's snow globe|her snow globe]] in dialogue (may currently be [[#Bugs|bugged]]) * Ineke gains dialogue branches to ask more about her family and her time in Europe |} ===Effects of player's actions=== Some of Ineke's other dialogue also changes based on her own upgrade tier as well as the other Milepost Zero merchants' upgrade tiers. This mainly affects the dialogue options on Ineke's opinions of her coworkers and of Milepost Zero. Once the upgrade tiers of Ineke and at least one other merchant have been maxed out, she will say that she plans to stay. These options are mostly fixed, but one particular response changes depending on how Josie was upgraded. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Blue Ridge trader outfit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== ;Trivia * Although Ineke doesn't necessarily believe in cryptids, she finds them "beautiful ''and'' dangerous." Because of this, she wouldn't mind if they were hunted and killed.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"Those creatures should be left to roam, not hunted."''
Ineke: ''"{{Tooltip|Yes, but these creatures are beautiful and dangerousl.{{sic}} I would much rather have one dead on my floor than alive with my head in its mouth, hm?|Emphasis on "and" in "beautiful and dangerous".}}"''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) * Ineke has a phobia of [[clown]]s, even as an adult.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]: ''"You'd never catch me fighting those beasts."''
Ineke: ''"Ah, you are less brave than you look then! That is fine, we all have our own aversions. It is nothing to be ashamed of! Between you and me, I am deathly afraid of clowns, but tell anyone and I will probably kill you."''
([[Ineke de Haan/Dialogue|Ineke's dialogue]]) ;Clarifications * {{Note|(Note 1)}} Since Ineke must have joined the ship before the Great War, this reference puts a rough lower bound on Ineke's age, given by 22 years before the war and 28 years from the war to 2105, when ''Milepost Zero'' is set. * {{Note|(Note 2)}} It is not specified in-game where in Europe Ineke is from. However, Ineke's first name and family name are both of Dutch origin, suggesting that she may hail from Belgium or the Netherlands. ==Appearances== Ineke de Haan appears only {{in|FO76MZ}}. She was [[Fallout 76 removed content|removed]] from the game with the ''[[Burning Springs (update)|Burning Springs]]'' update. ==Bugs== * {{Platforms|pc}} After recruiting Ineke, her shop inventory may not immediately appear, and it will seem as though she has nothing for sale at tier 1. This bug may also occur with [[Theodore (Milepost Zero)|Theodore]].{{Verify|verified}} * {{Platforms|pc}} Although the [[Plan: Ineke's snow globe|plan]] for Ineke's snow globe is supposed to be given by Ineke in her tier 3 dialogue, a bug has been reported in which the plan will not be added to the player's inventory, making the plan and the snow globe inaccessible. This bug has been reported even after [[Fallout 76 patch 1.7.15.12|patch 1.7.15.12]] (update 55) in October 2024.[https://www.reddit.com/r/fo76/comments/1ga4d66/axels_snow_globe_works_still_cant_get_inekes/ "Axel's Snow Globe works. Gonna start worrying more about them on the roads than you soon enough.|sound=Josie 0079337b_1.ogg}} '''Josie''' is a [[Brahmin (Fallout 76)|brahmin]] tamer who could be hired at the [[Milepost Zero (location)|Milepost Zero]] branch of the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76MZ}}. Recruiting Josie cost 100 [[Supplies]]. The Milepost Zero gameplay was discontinued with the ''[[Burning Springs (update)|Burning Springs]]'' update. As of that update's release, Josie can no longer be recruited and thus does not appear anywhere in-game. ==Background== {{Section|FO76MZ}} ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |ghost =yes |quests involved = |events started = }} ===Brahmin upgrades=== Josie offers a number of upgrades for the brahmin that appears in [[Caravan: Skyline Drive]], via changing their diet. Tier 1 is available by default after unlocking her (hire cost: 100 [[Supplies]]), while Tier 2 is unlocked from upgrading Josie in conversation with [[Marley]]. Tier 3 is unlocked at no cost via dialogue with Josie after she is upgraded to Tier 2; reach the option to offer her either [[Addictol (Fallout 76)|Addictol]] or [[Calmex (Fallout 76)|Calmex]] and she will be upgraded to Tier 3 after the conversation ends. The effects are permanent and stack with each other; they will apply to caravans run by the player (not other caravans that one participates in). ====Tier 1 (default)==== * Wasteland Hay: Improves health, costs 25 [[Supplies]]. * Rad-free Alfalfa: Improves health, costs 70 Supplies. * Cattle Encourager: Increases speed, costs 100 Supplies. ====Tier 2 (200 Supplies)==== * Thorn Feed: Reflects damage, costs 100 Supplies. * Irradiated Corn: Improves health, costs 150 Supplies. * Cattle Inspirer: Improves hurrying speed, costs 250 Supplies. ====Tier 3 (dialogue progression)==== * Pre-War Vitamins: Improves health, costs 250 Supplies. * Enhanced Thorn Feed: Reflects damage, costs 300 Supplies. * Cattle Spurer: Improves hurrying speed, costs 500 Supplies. * Endurance Crop: Provides health regeneration, costs 500 Supplies. ===Other interactions=== Josie has a dialogue option to name the brahmin that appears in [[Caravan: Skyline Drive]]. After selecting it, a menu will appear, on which the player can assign a prefix and suffix (e.g. "Old" and "Buttercup" to name the brahmin "Old Buttercup") to give the brahmin a two-word name. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Apocalyptic farmer outfit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Josie appears only {{in|FO76MZ}}. She was [[Fallout 76 removed content|removed]] from the game with the ''[[Burning Springs (update)|Burning Springs]]'' update. ==Behind the scenes== Josie's English voice actress has not been credited or announced anywhere. In localized versions of the game, her voice is dubbed by Angelina Tramm in German, among other languages. ==Gallery== FO76MZ Josie.png|Portrait {{Stub|FO76MZ}} [[Category:Milepost Zero human characters]] [[Category:Blue Ridge Caravan Company characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 removed characters]]

Can't afford to replace you yet.|sound=Marley 0078c2d5_1.ogg}} '''Marley''' is the former supervisor of the [[Milepost Zero (location)|Milepost Zero]] branch of the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76}}. The Milepost Zero gameplay was discontinued with the ''[[Burning Springs (update)|Burning Springs]]'' update. As of that update's release, Marley no longer appears anywhere in-game. However, she remains mentioned on the notes [[To Windy]] and [[Southern route]]. ==Background== Marley is the daughter of [[Jessica (Milepost Zero)|Jessica]] and [[Theodore (Milepost Zero)|Theodore]]; her father used to work as a weapons contractor, while her mother worked for Blue Ridge.Theodore: ''"Got offered the tech contractor job. Was working full time. Lived on site. {{Tooltip|And through that, I met Marley's mum, Jessica. She used to work for Blue Ridge. Long time ago now.|Brief 'er' and pause before "Marley's mum".}}"''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) Marley's parents devised plans to ride out any potential global conflict in a remote survivalists' shack.Marley: ''"Wasn't born yet. Mom moved to some remote shack out here in the wilderness before dad left, and well, here I am. Glad I got her genes, she was a strong woman dealing with all that by herself."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]])[[Theodore (Milepost Zero)|Theodore]]: ''"Had a... had a plan. We were gonna move out to the wilderness. Found a little house. Wasn't much, but would have been enough to avoid the brunt of the bombs and the fallout."''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) However, before the bombs dropped, Theodore had taken an opportunity to work at [[Vault 63]] for [[Hugo Stolz]],[[Theodore (Milepost Zero)|Theodore]]: ''"I worked hard and was good at it. Earned that title. Only quit for more money and better security. Opportunity to work with Vault-Tec, and some big-shot from the board of directors at that. {{Tooltip|I was just a stupid kid. Didn't know what I was talking about.|Bitter.}}"''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) and was whisked away to the vault against his will and held there permanently. As a result of Theodore's absence, Marley resented him, even as Jessica told her that he had been taken away by [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]].Marley: ''"Apparently some rich guy took him before the bombs fell, that's why he couldn't be around for my mom. Tripping over his own words to explain himself. I didn't want to hear any of it, truth be told. Anyway, you want to hear more? Talk to him. Not gonna involve myself with it. He's here for a job and that's the end of it."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]])Marley: ''"I'd be lying if I said I wasn't a little intrigued by the Vault... where he's been... all that stuff. Mom did say they took him, so he's gotta be telling the truth. It's just... what do I do with that truth? But, these are my problems. I'll deal with them in my own time and in my own way. Don't let it concern you."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]]) After the Great War, Marley encouraged her mother, Jessica, to return to Blue Ridge after the company had reorganized itself in the post-apocalypse, with the two of them seeking security as Theodore was still gone.Marley: ''"{{Tooltip|Here just to pry? Fine. Let's get it out of the way.|Sigh before fine. Not aggressive, just a little tired.}} Mom used to work for Blue Ridge, back before the war. Ended up back there when I was just a kid. They left a flyer and we followed. Wanted some security, considering dad didn't bother sticking around."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]]) Although Jessica found a living making clothes and trucking along on caravans, she eventually retired from the work due to her declining health; she still stuck around for Marley's sake, but soon died.Marley: ''"Had to convince her to seek them out after the war, but yeah, she worked at Blue Ridge again for a while after we found them. Made some clothes from nothing and sold them on, eventually did some trucking too. She was a real talent. She quit out eventually. It was all a little too much for her. Bombs took their toll, physically and mentally. She chose to stick around though, for me. Anyway, she's gone now."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]]) In Jessica's absence, [[Joanna Mayfield]] stepped up as a mentor figure for Marley, showing her how to take care of herself when Jessica could no longer do so. Marley also learned about trading, bartering and running a caravan business from Joanna, becoming her protege in the post-War operation of Blue Ridge.Marley: ''"She earned my respect. She's a smart cookie. Taught me all I know about trading, bartering,selling,{{sic}} working with clients. Also taught me how to look after myself, when mom couldn't no more."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]]) Around [[Timeline (2100-2149)#2105|2105]], several members of Blue Ridge were sent south to re-establish trade routes in the [[Shenandoah National Park|Shenandoah]] regionMarley: ''"Trade routes used to run through here, back in the old days. Joanna wanted to re-establish that; apparently, it was good business."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]]) and set up camp at [[Naked Creek]]. The caravanners were under the direction of Marley, who was left to run operations while Joanna promised to be in touch soon. The scouts generally thought Marley was "all right," though at least one employee thought she seemed "pretty cold."[[Southern route]] Many caravanners abandoned the project due to the activation of the [[Vault 63 weather machine]] and the subsequent storm wreaking havoc on the region, while many of those who stayed, including the group at Naked Creek, were killed by dangers in the wasteland. With guards and merchants alike in Shenandoah having either run off or ended up dead, Marley's operation was reduced to just herself and [[Luke (Milepost Zero)|Luke]]. Based at [[Milepost Zero (location)|Milepost Zero]] in the far south, Marley's branch of the caravan business is on the edge of being shuttered by Joanna by the time the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dwellers]] encounter her.Marley: ''"{{Tooltip|A bunch of them bailed cos of that damn storm... but some stayed. The loyal ones.|Marley on past attempts to set up a Shenandoah Blue Ridge branch.}} Not that it did much for them. Most of the remaining guys went out to make a delivery, but it didn't turn out so well... Anyway, with everyone gone, most of the merchants took off too. Ain't nobody wanting to work with a failing spin off when they could just travel a bit further for the real deal back in Big Bend. After that, it was just me and Luke. I'd gather from the suppliers we had left, and he'd make the deliveries. He was a good guy. One of the best."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]]) Recently, Marley's father, Theodore, escaped from his captivity in Vault 63 and found his way back to Blue Ridge, confirming his identity by talking about Jessica and Marley. This leads Marley and her father to reunite, if cautiously, at Milepost Zero.Marley: ''"Not till recently. He showed up at Big Bend Tunnel babbling some crap about being taken into a Vault by this rich guy. Joanna was just gonna chuck him out, but he mentioned my mom's name... and a daughter. I'll let you put two and two together."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]]) At first, she is unsure if he even is her father and if she can believe his claims.Marley: ''"Joanna said he's still at Big Bend, but wants to come to our headquarters. Does some work with guns apparently. She thinks he'd be a good asset here. Says I should give him a chance. I trust the woman with my life, but there's so much to consider here. I mean, shit, how can we even be sure he's my dad? And if he is? Well, he should've stayed in that vault. Least there he would have been outta sight and mind, not groveling at the door of my business."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]]) Marley eventually comes to recognize that Theodore is telling the truth, and they begin to work towards repairing their relationship.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How are things going with Marley?"''
Theodore: ''"Getting there one step at a time. Gonna take a while to patch things up but... it's moving. Can see parts of myself in her. {{Tooltip|Jessica too... Don't look at me like that. Anyway, did you actually want something? Or just here to waste time?|Embarassed.}}"''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |ghost =yes |quests involved =[[A Bump in the Road]] |events started =[[Caravan: Skyline Drive]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Settler mechanic outfit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== Marley must be roughly 28 years old in 2105. She mentions she was born after the Great War, while Theodore was abducted by Hugo before the Great War began. This places her birth year in either 2077 or 2078. ==Appearances== Marley appears only {{in|FO76}}. She was first mentioned in [[Southern route|a note]] introduced in the ''[[Skyline Valley (update)|Skyline Valley]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]], before making a full appearance with the ''[[Milepost Zero (update)|Milepost Zero]]'' update. She was then [[Fallout 76 removed content|removed]] from the game with the ''[[Burning Springs (update)|Burning Springs]]'' update, but was also mentioned as the author of the note [[To Windy]]. ==Bugs== {{Platforms|pc}} Marley gives out the [[Plan: Marley's snow globe|plan]] for her snow globe after the player has recruited one crew member at Milepost Zero, then asks her to run another caravan. However, after this happens for the first time, her dialogue to give out this plan may play again on subsequent dialogue interactions, resulting in the player receiving another copy of the plan, despite it already being known. There was no known fix for this bug, and the plan could be acquired, essentially, an infinite amount of times. This bug was present on the [[Public Test Server]] for ''Milepost Zero'', but was not fixed for its live release. It was reportedly patched with [[Fallout 76 patch 1.7.15.12|patch 1.7.15.12]] (update 55).{{Verify|patched}} ==Gallery== FO76MZ Marley keyart.png|Keyart depiction of Marley FO76MZ Marley.png|Portrait FO76MZ Marley and Joanna.png|With [[Joanna Mayfield]] during [[A Bump in the Road]] ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} [[Category:Milepost Zero human characters]] [[Category:Skyline Valley mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Burning Springs mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Blue Ridge Caravan Company characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 removed characters]] [[ru:Марли]]

I'm done talking about it. Find your drama elsewhere.|Theodore regarding the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]]|sound=Theodore 0078bb38_1.ogg}} '''Theodore''', or '''Theo''' for short, is an [[Fallout 76 ammunition|ammo]] [[Fallout 76 vendors|merchant]] who could be hired at the [[Milepost Zero (location)|Milepost Zero]] branch of the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76MZ}}. Recruiting Theodore cost 150 [[Supplies]]. The Milepost Zero gameplay was discontinued with the ''[[Burning Springs (update)|Burning Springs]]'' update. As of that update's release, Theodore can no longer be recruited and thus does not appear anywhere in-game. However, he remains indirectly mentioned on the note [[To Windy]]. ==Background== Hailing from England in the [[United Kingdom]],[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How you liking this side of the pond?"''
Theodore: ''"Not that different from England. Same rain, same ground. Well just about."''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) Theodore moved to the [[United States of America|United States]] working as a weapons technology contractor before the [[Great War]].Theodore: ''"School, graft, luck. Started out as a military tech contractor. Long time ago now, mind."''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) He initially did contract work with the [[United States Armed Forces]],Theodore: ''"Yeah. Designed weapons for the forces. Helped out with the making of some of them, too."''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) before he took an opportunity to work with [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] under a board member's supervision, later revealed to be [[Hugo Stolz]].Theodore: ''"I worked hard and was good at it. Earned that title. Only quit for more money and better security. Opportunity to work with Vault-Tec, and some big-shot from the board of directors at that. {{Tooltip|I was just a stupid kid. Didn't know what I was talking about.|Bitter.}}"''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) In pre-War times, Theodore enjoyed fishing,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Well, what do you like to do for fun?"''
Theodore: ''"Haven't thought about that in years. Used to be a keen fisher. Nothing like an early rise, nice coffee and open lake. Can't imagine I'd like much of what I would catch nowadays, though."''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) and he still appreciates spending quiet time alone, as well as a cold [[Beer (Fallout 76)|beer]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How do you relax?"''
Theodore: ''"I enjoy the quiet. A good sit down by myself, no pressure of talking. Cold beer too, if there's one going."''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) While working as a contractor, Theodore met a woman named [[Jessica (Milepost Zero)|Jessica]], who worked for the [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]], and fathered a girl named [[Marley]].Theodore: ''"Got offered the tech contractor job. Was working full time. Lived on site. {{Tooltip|And through that, I met Marley's mum, Jessica. She used to work for Blue Ridge. Long time ago now.|Brief 'er' and pause before "Marley's mum".}}"''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) Theodore and Jessica devised plans to ride out any potential global conflict in a remote survivalists' shack.Theodore: ''"Had a... had a plan. We were gonna move out to the wilderness. Found a little house. Wasn't much, but would have been enough to avoid the brunt of the bombs and the fallout."''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]])[[Marley]]: ''"Wasn't born yet. Mom moved to some remote shack out here in the wilderness before dad left, and well, here I am. Glad I got her genes, she was a strong woman dealing with all that by herself."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]]) However, before the bombs dropped, [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] officials under Hugo's direction whisked him away to Vault 63 against his will, where he was held indefinitely.[[Marley]]: ''"Apparently some rich guy took him before the bombs fell, that's why he couldn't be around for my mom. Tripping over his own words to explain himself. I didn't want to hear any of it, truth be told. Anyway, you want to hear more? Talk to him. Not gonna involve myself with it. He's here for a job and that's the end of it."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]])[[Marley]]: ''"I'd be lying if I said I wasn't a little intrigued by the Vault... where he's been... all that stuff. Mom did say they took him, so he's gotta be telling the truth. It's just... what do I do with that truth? But, these are my problems. I'll deal with them in my own time and in my own way. Don't let it concern you."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]]) Hugo held Theodore prisoner in Vault 63 for twenty years, not even bothering to learn Theodore's name, with Theodore essentially [[Slavery|enslaved]] as a weapons technician for the vault.Theodore: ''"Guards got word from Hugo that he wanted one of the weapons I made... that bloke ain't a fool, though. He knew the rest of the vault was dangerous, so sent me instead. For someone of his status, he's a pretty big coward. "Send the guy who made it" he said. Guy kidnapped me for twenty years and didn't even bother learning my name."''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) There, he became [[ghoul]]ified when radiation affected the rest of the residents. Theodore's work for Stolz involved designing unorthodox weapons that he thought would be useful in a post-War world.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What sort of work were you conducting down there?"''
Theodore: ''"Still worked with weapons, obviously. Hugo wanted to branch out and create some new guns for security purposes. Soon had us experimenting with... more unorthodox designs."''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]])Theodore: ''"Needed me to design more weapons for them for them in a post-war world. Hugo playing God, as per usual."''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) Theodore only managed to escape a few years prior to [[Timeline (2100-2149)#2105|2105]], and has not traveled far since then, only going a few miles north into Appalachia.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Don't suppose you've seen much of the fallout?"''
Theodore: ''"Can't say I have. Only left the vault a few years back, and I ain't gone much further than a few miles north."''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) He has adopted a standoffish, cold exterior, reluctant to discuss his past with Vault-Tec.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"[Charisma 4+] Can't have been that bad. What was so horrible about it?"''
Theodore: ''"{{Tooltip|Evil bastards using their power to manipulate people into compliance. I'm done talking about it. Find your drama elsewhere.|Willing to share, then dismissive when he opens up. Leads with a sigh.}}"''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) Theodore's daughter, Marley, came to resent him in his absence, as she only knew that Vault-Tec had taken him away, not aware of the full extent of his abduction. Jessica eventually died after continuing work for Blue Ridge post-War,[[Marley]]: ''"Had to convince her to seek them out after the war, but yeah, she worked at Blue Ridge again for a while after we found them. Made some clothes from nothing and sold them on, eventually did some trucking too. She was a real talent. She quit out eventually. It was all a little too much for her. Bombs took their toll, physically and mentally. She chose to stick around though, for me. Anyway, she's gone now."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]]) and [[Joanna Mayfield]] emerged as a mentor figure for Marley.[[Marley]]: ''"She earned my respect. She's a smart cookie. Taught me all I know about trading, bartering,selling,{{sic}} working with clients. Also taught me how to look after myself, when mom couldn't no more."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]]) Some time after Jessica's death, Theodore went to Blue Ridge and confirmed his identity by talking about Jessica and their daughter, leading Theodore and Marley to eventually reunite, if cautiously, at [[Milepost Zero (location)|Milepost Zero]].[[Marley]]: ''"Not till recently. He showed up at Big Bend Tunnel babbling some crap about being taken into a Vault by this rich guy. Joanna was just gonna chuck him out, but he mentioned my mom's name... and a daughter. I'll let you put two and two together."''
([[Marley/Dialogue|Marley's dialogue]]) Marley eventually comes to recognize that Theodore is telling the truth, and they begin to work towards repairing their relationship.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How are things going with Marley?"''
Theodore: ''"Getting there one step at a time. Gonna take a while to patch things up but... it's moving. Can see parts of myself in her. {{Tooltip|Jessica too... Don't look at me like that. Anyway, did you actually want something? Or just here to waste time?|Embarassed.}}"''
([[Theodore (Milepost Zero)/Dialogue|Theodore's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |ghost =yes |quests started =[[Unconventional Weaponry]] |events started = }} ===Upgrades=== All upgrades for Milepost Zero characters, including Theodore, are handled through dialogue with [[Marley]], specifically the option to give an employee more resources. * Tier 1 (initial hiring, default): 150 [[Supplies]] to hire Theodore * Tier 2 (250 Supplies): Better merchant inventory and access to the quest [[Unconventional Weaponry]], leading to the [[V63 laser carbine]]. Tier 3 is automatically unlocked at no cost upon conclusion of Unconventional Weaponry. Theodore will sell V63 laser carbine mod plans in his inventory afterward, and has new dialogue. ===Quests=== * [[Unconventional Weaponry]]: Theodore mentions a [[V63 laser carbine|weapon]] he was working on during his time in [[Vault 63]], and the player can retrieve its schematics. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Black-rim glasses (Fallout 76)|Black-rim glasses]]
[[Settler welder outfit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== It is never explicitly stated if Theodore and Jessica wed before the Great War; Theodore refers to her as "Marley's mum" and not his wife, indicating that they may not have married. ==Appearances== Theodore appears only {{in|FO76MZ}}. He was [[Fallout 76 removed content|removed]] from the game with the ''[[Burning Springs (update)|Burning Springs]]'' update, but was also indirectly mentioned in the note [[To Windy]]. ==Bugs== {{Platforms|pc}} After recruiting Theodore, his shop inventory may not immediately appear, and it will seem as though he has nothing for sale at tier 1. This is not intended, and he should have items for sale after being recruited. A definitive fix is not known, but reports have suggested that exhausting his available dialogue, as well as reloading the Milepost Zero interior a few times may help. This bug may also occur with [[Ineke]].{{Verify|verified}} ==Gallery== FO76MZ Theodore.png|Portrait ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox vendors FO76}} [[Category:Milepost Zero ghoul characters]] [[Category:Burning Springs mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Blue Ridge Caravan Company characters]] [[Category:Vault-Tec characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 merchants]] [[Category:Fallout 76 removed characters]] [[ru:Теодор (Milepost Zero)]]

We raise them here, break them down, and train the poor bastards for combat in the field or the arena.|“poor bastards” is meant to communicate empathy here - the Beastmaster is resigned to her role but part of her despises doing this to living creature}} The ones I've got are almost ready; all that's left is to fit them with their armor. This will make a lot of noise, so be ready for uninvited guests. They always come.|sound=Beastmaster Lina 0081f247 1.ogg}} '''Beastmaster Lina''',[[Don't feed the deathclaws!]][[Quit your crying!]] known in-game simply as '''Beastmaster''', is a member of the [[Rust King's Army]] and a [[Deathclaw (Fallout 76)|deathclaw]] tamer in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76BS}}. She is the primary character in the [[Fallout 76 events|public event]] [[Gearin' Up]]. ==Background== Beastmaster Lina became affiliated with the Rust King's Army through her father, who owned a center for training police [[dog]]s before the [[Great War]]. Lina herself grew up around dogs and developed skills for training animals much like her father.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Is training Deathclaws hard?"''
Beastmaster Lina: ''"{{Tooltip|Like any other wild animal: punishments and rewards, start young enough and you're golden. I grew up around dogs, so I had a head start, too.|Frosty. Player has touched on a sore subject.}} My Dad used to train police dogs, had his own little center and everything. Taught me all there was to know so that I could take over one day. {{Tooltip|In a way I did, I suppose... Oh well. Next question?|momentarily lost in thought at “in a way I did”}}"''
([[Beastmaster Lina/Dialogue|Beastmaster Lina's dialogue]]) Because [[the Rust King]] sees deathclaws as kin,[[The King's witness#VI|The King's witness, VI]] he specifically wanted animal trainers to tame the beasts and turn them into warriors, hence why he sought out and recruited Lina's father into the army.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How did you end up in the Rust King's Army?"''
Beastmaster Lina: ''"I have useful skills, and ''m{{sic}} a survivor. Both are something he likes. Strangely enough, I wasn't even that good when I started, my Dad was. It was him the Rust King wanted. {{Tooltip|And then he went and did something dumb and unnecessary. I didn't. The rest is history.|choking up a bit at “dumb and unnecessary”, then quickly regains composure}}"''
([[Beastmaster Lina/Dialogue|Beastmaster Lina's dialogue]]) Although Lina's father worked for the Rust King in this capacity for a time, he apparently "did something dumb and unnecessary," implying that he was killed afterward. Lina was not as confident about her own animal training talents, but took over as beastmaster following the incident involving her father. The Rust King keeps Lina around because of his respect for her skills and her self-proclaimed status as a survivor, not to mention the fact that she did not make the same unspecified mistake her father did. Lina runs her deathclaw-taming operation out of [[Jackson Junkyard]], close by to [[The Rust Kingdom (location)|the Rust Kingdom]]. At the junkyard, Lina is in charge of raising deathclaws, taming the wild beasts, and training them for use in combat, either in the Rust Kingdom's arena for gladiatorial purposes, or for general use in the field by patrols of [[Rust raider]]s.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What is this place?"''
Beastmaster Lina: ''"{{Tooltip|This is where the Rust King gets his Deathclaws from. We raise them here, break them down, and train the poor bastards for combat in the field or the arena.|“poor bastards” is meant to communicate empathy here - the Beastmaster is resigned to her role but part of her despises doing this to living creature}} The ones I've got are almost ready; all that's left is to fit them with their armor. This will make a lot of noise, so be ready for uninvited guests. They always come."''
([[Beastmaster Lina/Dialogue|Beastmaster Lina's dialogue]]) Despite the difficulty of handling giant dangerous creatures like deathclaws, Beastmaster Lina has found success in this venture, seeing it like training any other wild animal by using punishments and rewards. Lina forges armor that is tailor-made for each deathclaw, and it is near-impossible to remove once placed on the beast. Not all deathclaws survive the procedure of having armor placed on them, but Lina sees it like culling the weak, while enhancing the strength of the deathclaws hardy enough to withstand the installation of the armor. On top of this, the deathclaws with armor "stay pissed off forever."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How does one make armor for a Deathclaw?"''
Beastmaster Lina: ''"By not caring about their feelings on the matter. I forge the armors myself, tailor made for each Deathclaw. It never comes off once put on. It's another way the weak are culled, and the deadly are made even deadlier. Those who survive the procedure are truly strong... and they stay pissed off forever."''
([[Beastmaster Lina/Dialogue|Beastmaster Lina's dialogue]]) She even maintains "starvation training" for the deathclaws, and threatens to serve up anyone who messes with the beasts as their "first meal." In some respects, Lina adopts a philosophy of might making right, similar to the Rust King himself:[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"[Start Event] I'll help you. What do you need?"''
Beastmaster Lina: ''"The Rust King despises weakness - the frail must die or grow stronger, and the strong must maintain their edge. This place is the crucible for both. Our Deathclaws are tested by combat, but I fit them with armor first. You'll need to gather some metal for me, like the piece in that barrel. This will not be easy. This place will test you as well."''
([[Beastmaster Lina/Dialogue|Beastmaster Lina's dialogue]]) the armor-fitting process for the deathclaws requires the tamers to "not [care] about their feelings on the matter," and she is more than willing to permit the killing of other Rust raiders who intrude on her operation.Beastmaster Lina: ''"You can go ahead and execute all of those guys. Might is Right, after all. Heh, maybe in future they might stay out of my junkyard."''
([[Beastmaster Lina/Dialogue|Beastmaster Lina's dialogue]])Beastmaster Lina: ''"I don't care if they're flying the King's colors. They knew the risks, they'll pay the price."''
([[Beastmaster Lina/Dialogue|Beastmaster Lina's dialogue]]) However, Lina is not totally without empathy in her position; a part of her still feels a tinge of regret for what she must do to condition these living beings, lamenting that her training is based almost entirely on violence (or the mere threat of it).Beastmaster Lina: ''"That's a big one! Almost a shame to have to put her down... but she should make for a hell of a test for our 'trainee'."''
([[Beastmaster Lina/Dialogue|Beastmaster Lina's dialogue]])Beastmaster Lina: ''"Used to be there was more to training animals than violence or the threat of violence. Oh well."''
([[Beastmaster Lina/Dialogue|Beastmaster Lina's dialogue]]) She even sees particularly valuable trainee deathclaws as being worth more than the lives of other [[human]]s around her.Beastmaster Lina: ''"That Deathclaw is more valuable than all of us put together, you idiot. Keep. It. Alive!"''
([[Beastmaster Lina/Dialogue|Beastmaster Lina's dialogue]]) Nevertheless, she is still committed, or perhaps resigned, to her role as beastmaster, and does her job well on top of everything, as she says that no one else in the Rust King's Army could do what she does.Beastmaster Lina: ''"None of those knuckle draggers can do what I do. Sure hope they understand that."''
([[Beastmaster Lina/Dialogue|Beastmaster Lina's dialogue]]) Although she has several [[Rust raider#Variants|deathclaw handlers]] working under her, Lina keeps them on a short leash and forces them to undergo trials which they must survive, in order to prove themselves worthy of working with the deathclaws that she has trained. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |dead = |quests started = |quests involved = |events started =[[Gearin' Up]] |events involved = |essential =yes |essential until = |ghost =yes |hostile = |temp companion = }} ===Quests=== * [[Gearin' Up|Event: Gearin' Up]]: During this [[Fallout 76 events|public event]], Beastmaster Lina tasks the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dwellers]] with collecting scrap metal with which to create armor for a trainee deathclaw. This deathclaw must then be protected against waves of hostile, crazed [[Rust raider]]s intruding on [[Jackson Junkyard]], as well as other creatures such as [[snallygaster]]s and even other stray, untamed deathclaws. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Deathclaw tamer outfit|Deathclaw tamer hat]]
[[Deathclaw tamer outfit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Appearances== Beastmaster Lina appears only {{In|FO76BS}}. ==Gallery== FO76BS Beastmaster.png ==References== {{References|2}} {{Navbox Burning Springs}} [[Category:Burning Springs human characters]] [[Category:Rust King's Army characters]] [[ru:Укротительница]]

([[Gregory Dixon/Dialogue|Gregory Dixon's dialogue]]) at other times, he also shows fear and cowardice when intimidated.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"[Strength 8+] You don't get the caps, but she still walks away free. Or, I'll kill you."''
Gregory Dixon: ''"Okay! Sure! Yeah, yeah. Whatever you want! {{Tooltip|Keep your caps anyway... didn't want them.|{like he's mumbling to himself} }}"''
([[Gregory Dixon/Dialogue|Gregory Dixon's dialogue]])Gregory Dixon: ''"{{Tooltip|Oh no, not you again.|Scared}}"''

([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) On top of his manipulative and usurious ways, Gregory is also occasionally lecherous; the only tinges of sympathy that he has for his clients come when he finds them physically attractive. ([[Gregory Dixon/Dialogue|Gregory Dixon's dialogue]])Gregory Dixon: ''"Well, I won't complain; caps are caps! {{Tooltip|Oh, if I'm honest, I was really looking forward to seeing her... pretty face again.|{A little creepy} }} She owes me a good amount, you willing to pay in full?"''
([[Gregory Dixon/Dialogue|Gregory Dixon's dialogue]]) [[Magpie]], one of Gregory's clients seeking to free herself from his debt, summarizes Gregory's character by calling him "creepy" and a "bad guy."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Hell yeah! I made sure he did."''
[[Magpie]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Urgh! You're twisted! I know he was a bad guy, but you're reveling in killing someone.|{Really disgusted} }}"''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) However, she still wants to avoid violence in escaping his debt, as she believes worming out a deal with Gregory would be a much better solution.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I paid off some of your debt, but could keep some myself."''
[[Magpie]]: ''"Hey if you managed to worm a deal then that's great! Thank you, I really appreciate it."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |dead = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Insurrection]] |events started = |events involved = |essential =yes |essential until =the player triggers aggression with him and attacks during [[Insurrection]] |ghost = |hostile = |temp companion = }} ===Quests=== * [[Insurrection]]: The player character is tasked with freeing [[Magpie]] of her debt to Gregory Dixon. ** Gregory will ask for a payment of interest. The player character can fork over 60 caps, convince him to let it go with [[Charisma]] 8+, or attack him and his thugs. Once the thugs are killed and one enters Gregory's office, he will still insist on the interest. The player character has another chance to pay it, intimidate him with [[Strength]] 8+, or kill Gregory. ** If the player character admits to and revels in killing Gregory, Magpie will refuse to join [[Eugene (Burning Springs)|Eugene's]] plan out of disgust. If the player character resolves her debt peacefully, Magpie will sign on to the doomed revolution. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Brahmin pant suit]] (non-lootable) |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Gregory Dixon appears only {{In|FO76BS}}. ==Behind the scenes== {{FO76CC}} A cut [[Highway Town terminal entries#Cut entries|series of entries]] on the terminal in Gregory's office would have expanded on his character, assuming they were intended to be written by Gregory. However, these entries were left unimplemented. They would have included writings regarding a lustful pursuit of [[Lacey Brown]], as well as a number of [[conspiracy theory|conspiracy theories]] about the [[Burning Springs (region)|Burning Springs]] and [[Appalachia]] regions, including ones about cyborgs from [[Vault 76]] and the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]]'s end goals, where the [[United States government|pre-War federal government]] is hiding, intelligent wasteland creatures, the [[Mothman]] actually just being a [[human]], and [[cannibalism]] by [[the Rust King]]. The author implies he was part of a group of like-minded "truth-seekers" and would have had a [[Bus (Fallout 76)|bus]] he called his "Fortress of Truth" that he was working toward repairing. On a lighter note, he also would have expressed a joy in collecting pre-War music records, searching for any music [[holotape]]s that would pass through Highway Town. A remnant of this last note can be seen in the header of the information station terminal that appears in-game, which refers to it as the "Transit Tunes Terminal."{{Cut}} [[Highway Town terminal entries#Personal Logs|Highway Town terminal entries; Personal Logs]]{{Cut}} [[Highway Town terminal entries#Music Collection|Highway Town terminal entries; Music Collection]] {{FO76CC|end}} ==Gallery== FO76BS Gregory Dixon unobscured.png|Gregory in his office ==References== {{References|2}} '''Non-canon''' {{References|group=Non-canon}} {{Navbox Burning Springs}} [[Category:Burning Springs human characters]] [[Category:Highway Town characters]]
