{{ID|0084b2c1}} (Rust Kingdom arena) }} {{Quotation|{{Tooltip|Oh cool. *cough* We're on a first name basis.|{sarcasm} }} Most killers don't learn their victims name, so you're clearly not here to hurt me.|sound=Fo76BS Magpie 00815e59 1.ogg|Magpie}} '''Magpie''' is a sharpshooter and former [[Raiders|raider]], taking refuge in [[The Chop Shop (Burning Springs)|the Chop Shop]]'s diner basement in the [[Burning Springs (region)|Burning Springs]] region of [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76BS}}. ==Background== Magpie grew up in [[Ohio]] and has lived there for much of her life.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Where are you from?"''
Magpie: ''"Ohio. I grew up here, felt only fitting to eventually die here too. *coughing* Didn't feel like leaving."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) As a child before the [[Great War]], Magpie enjoyed patronizing [[the Buckeye Diner]], although she noted that the food declined in quality at some point.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Why did you come to this diner?"''
Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|It was my favorite as a kid. *cough* The food got crappier at some point, but I always liked it.|{reminiscent} }} {{Tooltip|Plus there's a nice yummy benefit of a basement filled with preserves!|{Snarky, playful} }}"''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]){{Ref|(Note)}} Although she does not mention what happened to her parents, Magpie did have a younger brother, who eventually came to live in [[Highway Town]] after the apocalypse.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"So, why did you leave the raiders?"''
Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|Can't a girl just do something without being questioned all the time?|{joking} }} Sorry, I'm just messing with you. I had a little brother, lived in Highway Town. {{Tooltip|He always saw the best in people. The best in this shitty world. I wanted to be more like him, get away from all the violence.|{hiding sadness about her brother} }}"''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) Meanwhile, Magpie fell in with a different crowd; more specifically, she became a [[Raiders|raider]]. She joined the [[Rust King's Army]] and became known for her proficiency with firearms, widely recognized as a skilled sharpshooter and marksman.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Who is the girl?"''
[[Eugene (Burning Springs)|Eugene]]: ''"Her name is Magpie. She was a raider for the Rust Kingdom, before she left and went into hiding. {{Tooltip|I'm not sure what caused her to run. But she's very good with a gun; one of the best.|{Emphasis on “very”} }}"''
([[Eugene (Burning Springs)/Dialogue|Eugene's dialogue]])[[Eugene (Burning Springs)|Eugene]]: ''"After you've recruited the muscle, we need a sharpshooter too. {{Tooltip|An ex-raider and an expert marksman - easily has the biggest kill count in the area. We definitely need her skills for this fight. Name's Magpie.|{Impressed} }} Last I heard, she's held up at the old diner - been there a while. She's going nowhere, find Leonard first."''
([[Eugene (Burning Springs)/Dialogue|Eugene's dialogue]]) Magpie saw the Rust King's Army as a family in their own right; despite their penchant for brutality, she found a place in their "twisted, weird family." She interacted with people who became raiders because they felt as though they had no other options, as well as those who made a conscious decision to adopt the lifestyle.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What was it like, in the raiders?"''
Magpie: ''"Surprisingly, not that bad. Pretty brutal sometimes, but they were almost like my family. A twisted, weird family. If I'm honest, I think a lot of them were raiders because they didn't feel like they had a choice. Others, though. Definitely had a choice."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) She also became familiar with [[Eugene (Burning Springs)|Spike]], a raider from another gang who, she says, did "horrific" things.Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|I just wanted you to pay off my debt. Not kill the man. That wasn't the deal. This... violence. It's not something I want to be a part of. And Spike? I'm not working with you. Someone who can do things as horrific as you...That's not something you should get involved with either.|{Angry} }} You're both on your own for that fight. Seems like you don't need me anyway."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) [[The Rust]], a toxic phenomenon affecting the [[Burning Springs (region)|Burning Springs]] region post-War, eventually claimed Magpie's brother as a victim, as he was struck with a serious illness to which he eventually succumbed.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Where is your brother now?"''
Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|Ugh... I thought the past tense would make it obvious. He's gone. He uh... He was just too sick.|{Sad} }} He didn't deserve that, but the world is cruel."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) Magpie has had a fair amount of time to process her brother's death, and while she still considers it a sore spot, she no longer puts herself down over the subject, remarking that her brother would not want her to be sad over his passing.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I'm sorry."''
Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|Hey, it's all cool. I've had a long time to deal with it. It's still sore, sure, but there's no point in beating myself up.|{Sadly optimistic} }} He wouldn't want me to be sad about it, anyway. He was never sad. I want to be more like that."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) After her brother's death, Magpie became inspired by his positive attitude in life, always wanting to make the best out of a difficult world, and sought to separate herself from the violent life in which she had found herself. To that end, Magpie abandoned the Rust King's Army and went into hiding. However, at some point, Magpie became afflicted with the same illness, caused by the Rust, that her brother suffered from, a common phenomenon in Burning Springs. This has left her with a noticeable dry cough and a poor diagnosis for her future, harboring many of the same symptoms that her brother had.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What sickness?"''
Magpie: ''"All this coughing *cough*, it's what he had too. {{Tooltip|We don't really know what it is, but it seems like a lot of people have the same symptoms around here.|{Curious} }}"''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) Magpie attempted to scrounge up the [[Cap (Fallout 76)|caps]] she would need to acquire medicine, mostly via gambling; she also took out a loan of 178 caps (with interest) from [[Gregory Dixon]] in Highway Town. However, she was never able to acquire exactly what she needed and ended up indebted to Gregory.[[Highway Town terminal entries#Customer Records|Highway Town terminal entries; information station, Customer Records]][[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Why do you owe this guy all those caps?"''
Magpie: ''"I needed the caps to get medicine. For obvious reasons. I tried a couple things, mainly gambling. But, it wasn't enough."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) She hunkered down in the basement of the Buckeye Diner, inspired by her childhood memories there, while also noting the advantages of hiding in a basement filled with preservatives. However, by [[Timeline (2100-2149)#2105|2105]], the area surrounding [[The Chop Shop (Burning Springs)|the Chop Shop]] has become overrun with [[Rust raider]]s practicing [[cannibalism]], forcing Magpie to stay hidden in the basement, setting up traps and killing any Rust raiders who venture down.Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|Gotta make sure those traps are set up again.|{Talking to herself} }}"''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) She refuses to leave, having staked her claim on the area by virtue of being there first.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Why are you staying down here with all these raiders?"''
Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|Not my fault those cannibals took over. I moved in first, and I'm not leaving.|{Stubborn} }}"''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) All the while, her debt to Gregory Dixon remains an albatross around her neck, to the point she says that she would be hunted down if she did reemerge.Magpie: ''"I... I got into some shady crap, okay? Now some creepy guy is waiting for any sign of me out there. At best, I lose a few fingers. At worst, I go to an early grave. Either way, I'm not a fan of that."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) Although she is committed to separating herself from, at the very least, unjustified killing,Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|Wait what? You... *cough* You killed him? This... This isn't what I wanted. Why did you do that? I asked you to pay off my debt. I... Did... Did he suffer?|{Conflicted, she doesn’t like the idea of undeserved death} }}"''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) she is still recognized in the area for her skills as a marksman. Although she lacks confidence in her combat skills since becoming sick,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How do you feel about fighting again, this time in a revolt?"''
Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|A revolt? Hah, I might've been a good fighter a while ago, but I don't do that anymore.|{Hesitant} }} {{Tooltip|Anyway, sounds like a one-way ticket to an early grave. If I'm not killed by... you know, something else.|{Hesitant to explain} }}"''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) Magpie's notoriety makes her a potential candidate for assisting a revolution against [[the Rust King]]. [[Eugene (Burning Springs)|Eugene]] (in reality, Spike) even claims she may have the highest kill count in the region, though it is unclear if this is true, or an attempt on his part to incentivize recruiting her to the revolution.[[Eugene (Burning Springs)|Eugene]]: ''"To go against someone like that, we need more people. There's three of them, in the surrounding area, that are notorious for killing his men. Lucky for you, one of them is right here in Highway Town. Head down to the Underbelly below. {{Tooltip|There's a room at the far end, with an American flag. Inside, an intercom will ask you for a password; it's "Brahmin".|{Explaining next steps of quest} }}"''
([[Eugene (Burning Springs)/Dialogue|Eugene's dialogue]]) Magpie can be convinced to see the revolution as a way for her to potentially do something good for once,Magpie: ''"No kidding. {{Tooltip|Spike, I mean... "Eugene", filled me in on the details of this revolt.|{Correcting herself} }} {{Tooltip|I'm not opposed to helping. It's time I do something good, for once. It's what my brother would want. You'll all probably die without me there anyway.|{Determined, like she has a purpose again} }} {{Tooltip|But I'm not happy about working with a liar like Eugene.|{"Eugene" said snarky} }} I'll see you in the Kingdom, hero."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) especially with the potential for an early death from the Rust's illness looming; additionally, Magpie believes it would be what her brother would want her to do. She aims to free herself from debt before joining, though she grapples with an internal conflict over the use of violence to attain such ends. ===Personality=== {{Quotation|Well I hope it's been fun getting to know me *cough* I am fairly cool.|Magpie|sound=Fo76BS Magpie 0081e4c7 1.ogg}} Despite her difficult circumstances, Magpie maintains a warm sense of humor, as most conversations feature her being snarky,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Are you Magpie?"''
Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|Oh cool. *cough* We're on a first name basis.|{sarcasm} }} Most killers don't learn their victims name, so you're clearly not here to hurt me."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) joking[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You keep coughing. Are you sick or something?"''
Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|Sick of your bullshit.|{Joking} }} Sorry, bad joke."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) and playful.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"It sounds like a sticky situation, I'm gonna need more incentive."''
Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|It's almost adorable that you think I can give you anything more. I haven't got anything for you other than my *coughing* sick fighting skills!|{Playful} }}"''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) She will sarcastically refer to the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]] with the nickname of "hero."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Let me help."''
Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|Okay, hero.|{"hero" is sarcastic} }} I owe a guy some money."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) She enjoys singing and humming to herself,Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|*singing*|{Singing “doo” notes of a random tune, like she’s keeping busy} }}"''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]])Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|*humming*|{Lightly humming a random tune to herself} }}"''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) but also indulges in gambling, as she suffers from an addiction to it; she uses her dire straits as an explanation for her gambling, but also admits that she enjoys it on its face,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"So, gambling, huh?"''
Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|Look, I had to do it. But I'd be lying if I said part of me didn't really like it.|{gambling mindset} }}"''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) and she applies her gambler's mindset to even the most mundane of topics.Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|I bet 50 caps that there'll be a dust storm tomorrow... If I had them. Or had someone to bet with.|{Sad she can’t bet with anyone} {Talking to herself} }}"''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) Keeping her brother's memory in mind as her inspiration, Magpie has resolved to cast aside her violent past and model her future behavior after him and his cheery disposition. However, she is still more than capable of and very willing to defend herself, given she is stuck in a basement with cannibals on the other side of the door.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I can get you out of this rotting basement."''
Magpie: ''"This rotting basement is the only thing standing between me, and the barrel of a gun."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) She is also willing to kill and fight again when joining the plan to overthrow the Rust King.Magpie: ''"I'm excited to fight with you."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) Her struggle with violence comes from trying to stop herself from causing undeserved death; she wants to be free from her debt to Gregory Dixon but is hesitant to use violence to solve the issue in that particular case. With her new mindset, she is especially repulsed at the idea of reveling in such violence.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Hell yeah! I made sure he did."''
Magpie: ''"{{Tooltip|Urgh! You're twisted! I know he was a bad guy, but you're reveling in killing someone.|{Really disgusted} }}"''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) Even if Gregory is a "bad guy," Magpie knows the old version of herself would, in fact, have just killed him, and therein lies the origin of her hesitance, as she attempts to move on from her raiding days.Magpie: ''"He's some loan shark, hiding out in an office in Highway Town. When I was trying to find some caps to pay him off, I found this old note that talked about a good chunk of 'em. {{Tooltip|But, I couldn't journey that far. Not without help.|{Embarrassed}} {{Tooltip|Old me would've just killed him. But now... I'm not so sure.|{hesitant, lost in thought} }} {{Tooltip|So you find those caps, pay him off, and we're good. Got it? Here's the note.|{shaking off zone out} }} I'll be waiting here for when you're back."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) Nevertheless, Magpie may be led to believe that overthrowing the Rust King and fighting in a revolution against the raiders would be the right thing to do, seeing it as a newly discovered purpose in life, to do some good in spite of her likely shortened lifespan. Alternatively, if Gregory Dixon is killed and his death is celebrated, Magpie may be turned off of the revolution entirely, disgusted with the notion of playing God, much like the Rust King himself.Magpie: ''"Well it wasn't up to you to play God! You're as bad as the Rust King."''
([[Magpie/Dialogue|Magpie's dialogue]]) This is especially demotivating given Spike, now using the alias of Eugene, is the one formulating the plan, and Magpie is ultimately right to distrust him.Events of [[When the Rust Settles]]. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |dead = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Insurrection]]
[[When the Rust Settles]] |events started = |events involved = |essential =yes |essential until = |ghost =yes |hostile = |temp companion = }} ===Quests=== * [[Insurrection]]: Magpie is the third and final potential recruit for [[Eugene (Burning Springs)|Eugene's]] rebellion plan against [[the Rust King]]. Magpie tasks the player with freeing her of her debt before she can join the revolution. ** If the player frees Magpie of her debt peacefully (or lies and tells her that they did), she will agree to join the revolution. ** If the player kills [[Gregory Dixon]] (or lies and tells her that they did), she will refuse to join the revolution out of disgust. * [[When the Rust Settles]]: If Magpie joined the revolution in the previous quest, she will be found dead in the [[The Rust Kingdom (location)|Rust Kingdom arena]], following Eugene's betrayal. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Treasure hunter outfit]] (non-lootable) |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Notes== * {{Note|(Note)}} Although not explicitly stated that Magpie's adolescence was in the pre-War period, the Buckeye Diner was a pre-War establishment and the [[Buckeye Diner's ledger]] indicates their change in ingredients to [[human]] meat occurred in June [[Timeline (2050-2099)#2077|2077]], aligning with Magpie's statement about when the food got "crappier." * A note titled [[Magpie's song]], containing poetry written by Magpie, is found in the game's files and appears to be associated with the quest [[Insurrection]], but it has no reference records and was not implemented in the live release of ''Burning Springs''. * Magpie will always die if she is convinced to join Eugene's revolution in the wake of his betrayal; thus, the way to ensure she survives the events of the quest line is to actually upset her by killing Gregory Dixon. Although she does live if she refuses to join the revolution, Magpie disappears from the game world after [[When the Rust Settles]] and cannot be spoken to again. ==Appearances== Magpie appears only {{In|FO76BS}}. ==Gallery== FO76BS No Kings, No Masters Eugene and Magpie.png|Magpie and [[Eugene (Burning Springs)|Eugene]] during [[Insurrection]] FO76BS Moose Magpie dead.png|Magpie's corpse at the bottom of a skewer during [[When the Rust Settles]] ==References== {{Ref box}} {{Navbox Burning Springs}} [[Category:Burning Springs human characters]] [[ru:Сорока]]

Take a look around, and then tell me if it was.|sound=Fo76BS Rattler 00847ed7 1.ogg}} '''Rattler''' is a gun-for-hire residing in [[Highway Town]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76BS}}. ==Background== Although he describes himself humbly as nothing more than a "thug with a gun" and "nobody special,"[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Who are you?"''
Rattler: ''"Me? Nobody special, a thug with a gun. But this is Highway Town. You can make a livin' and a killin' being a thug with a gun."''
([[Rattler/Dialogue|Rattler's dialogue]]) Rattler is a well-spoken and intelligent individual.Rattler: ''"To what do I owe the pleasure?"''
([[Rattler/Dialogue|Rattler's dialogue]]) He was raised by parents who were anarchists, and who believed that self-governance was a better form of society than that of the [[United States government|pre-War federal government]]. Rattler believes that the [[Great War]] is proof that such forms of leadership had failed, and that it is better for places to run themselves.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"No place runs itself."''
Rattler: ''"You know, my folks, when they were still around, used to think that people running themselves would do a better job than the government ever did. That having someone in charge wasn't doing anybody any favors, or protecting us from anything. Take a look around, and then tell me if it was."''
([[Rattler/Dialogue|Rattler's dialogue]]) Although his parents eventually died, Rattler still holds true to these beliefs, and as such, it made the uniquely self-governing settlement of [[Highway Town]] an attractive place to live.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Do you like it in Highway Town?"''
Rattler: ''"I don't like 'towns' to begin with. Always someone on top, stepping over others. Highway Town is different though. And it hasn't folded on itself yet, so... you could say I'm fond of it."''
([[Rattler/Dialogue|Rattler's dialogue]]) Rattler has taken up work as a mercenary, a common profession in Highway Town. He also appreciates the [[Bounty hunter|bounty hunting]] business that thrives in Highway Town, seeing bounties as a means to a "cleaner" [[wasteland]],[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"My kind of town then."''
Rattler: ''"Nice. Might wanna check on the posted bounties! We could all do with a... cleaner Wasteland."''
([[Rattler/Dialogue|Rattler's dialogue]]) though Rattler himself also relishes time off from his own hunts.Rattler: ''"So nice not to be out on a hunt for once."''
([[Rattler/Dialogue|Rattler's dialogue]]) Although "troublemakers" in Highway Town are usually killed, Rattler recognizes that Highway Town can be a dangerous place without centralized leadership. Rattler believes that the way to counteract this is to find well-paying work; for mercenaries like Rattler, there are plenty of jobs, if unscrupulous ones, to take on in the [[Burning Springs (region)|Burning Springs]] region. Rattler says that if Highway Town ever became too chaotic and destabilized by "troublemakers," then no tears should be shed over a place that was too broken to go on, just like pre-War [[United States of America|America]].[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How do you maintain order then?"''
Rattler: ''"By shooting troublemakers. They are usually in the minority. And if they are ever in the majority, maybe this place has become too broken to go on, and no tears will be shed. After all, ain't that what happened to America?"''
([[Rattler/Dialogue|Rattler's dialogue]])Rattler: ''"Trouble will always find you in Burning Springs. Make sure you're paid for it."''
([[Rattler/Dialogue|Rattler's dialogue]])Rattler: ''"For folks like us, there will always be work in Burning Springs."''
([[Rattler/Dialogue|Rattler's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |dead = |quests started = |quests involved = |events started = |events involved = |essential =yes |essential until = |ghost =yes |hostile = |temp companion = }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Mercenary outfit (Fallout 76)|Mercenary outfit]] (non-lootable) |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Rattler appears only {{In|FO76BS}}. ==Behind the scenes== Rattler's appearance was altered between the first and second published patches for the ''Burning Springs'' [[Public Test Server]], similar to many other Highway Town characters. Although his outfit stayed the same, he was given a slightly re-sculpted face and a different hairstyle. ==Gallery== FO76BS Rattler PTS.png|Rattler's initial appearance in the [[Public Test Server]] ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Burning Springs}} [[Category:Burning Springs human characters]] [[Category:Highway Town characters]]

And if you want in, you will fix your tone going forward.|{emphasis on decide} }}|sound=Fo76BS Runt 0083fcbf 1.ogg}} '''Runt''' is a member of the [[Rust King's Army]] living in [[Highway Town]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76BS}}. ==Background== Runt is an unpleasant and disagreeable person who has taken up residence in the maintenance closet of [[Highway Town]], on assignment from [[the Rust King]].Runt: ''"{{Tooltip|Could've given me a few guards at least. I'm in hostile territory.|{anxious} }}"''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) He is looked down upon by other wastelanders in the settlement, such as [[Millstone]], who sees the cramped, lowly living space as befitting of Runt's character.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I am looking for a guy named Runt."''
[[Millstone]]: ''"{{Tooltip|That loser? I'd give you some free advice, but I don't think you'd care for it.|{random short coughs throughout} }} His "office" is the maintenance closet near the town's elevator. Easy to overlook, just like its resident."''
([[Millstone/Dialogue|Millstone's dialogue]]) As a follower of the Rust King and a member of his [[Rust King's Army|raider army]], Runt is in charge of recruitment for the Rust King's Army, acting as a conduit for people in the Rust King's territory to have a chance to prove themselves to the warlord, to see if they are worthy.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Does everybody have to prove themselves to the Rust King?"''
Runt: ''"Everyone. Such is the way of the strong. The closer you are to the top, the taller the stack of bodies you've climbed to get there. {{Tooltip|It's a crucible. Constant competition. It's... not a system that rewards finesse, but it's made the Rust King's Army what it is today.|{slightly disdainful -the Rust King’s Army is feared but he specifically cannot be too successful in it.} }}"''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"'Runt'? I can see that. How come you were able to join?"''
Runt: ''"{{Tooltip|The Rust King isn't some jumped up thug. And he wants the best in the land for his army.|{insulted and quietly fuming} }} {{Tooltip|I know people, and I can tell who can make it. So I decide who can make it. And if you want in, you will fix your tone going forward.|{emphasis on decide} }}"''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) Runt claims to have been managing people for years, and looks for dedication in potential recruits.Runt: ''"{{Tooltip|Which, annoyingly, you've been doing so far.|{the first sentence is mumbled - reluctant recognition for the player’s prowess} }} But how does he know this isn't a fluke? I've been managing people for years now, and my answer is very simple: dedication. So I found you some more things to take a crack at, stuff for real hands-on professionals. Do them, and I'll make sure the Rust King hears of it."''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) In practice, this means Runt can, perhaps indefinitely, offload his dirty work to anyone seeking to prove themselves to the Rust King. Since Runt is the one who is trusted by the Rust King, and not the recruits, it is essentially his word against theirs. Runt holds his position within the Rust King's Army as a bargaining chip, arguing that the recruits should not whine about performing tasks assigned to them. This is because Runt will put in a good word for them if they do this dirty work without complaint; if they do complain, it will be at their own risk, as Runt says the Rust King "hates whining."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You couldn't handle half of those jobs, Runt."''
Runt: ''"I wouldn't have to. The Rust King trusts me already. It's you who has to prove yourself."''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You're just offloading your wet work onto me. Will you steal the credit, too?"''
Runt: ''"If you go whining to the Rust King, it's your word against mine. It will also be your head: the Rust King hates whining. But if you complete my jobs, I might just decide to put in a good word for you! Now go and do as you're told."''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]])Runt: ''"{{Tooltip|Conquering hero back with the spoils! Or something.|Not actually happy or encouraging, senses the opportunity to offload a lot of dirty work onto the player.}}"''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) Runt lives up to his nickname, as he is not exactly physically capable, and he is far from being able to display any of the brute force seen elsewhere in the Rust King's Army.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Toughest, you say? Looks like I'm in the right place."''
Runt: ''"{{Tooltip|Hmph, of course. Brute force is always in vogue around here.|{annoyed and envious - brute force is something he doesn’t possess} }}"''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) The Rust King himself refers to Runt as a "weasel."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You'll be watching me?"''
[[The Rust King]]: ''"Yes. You may be strong, but you have much to learn. There is a scrapheap of a town in the north. Head there, and keep an eye out for a weasel named Runt. He lives up to his name, but he can offer you work and a chance to prove your loyalty to me."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) Even if Runt could not handle most of the tests of strength he assigns to others, he is nonetheless trusted by the Rust King to recruit only the best for the army. Runt says that the Rust King's Army only accepts the toughest and deadliest into the ranks of its raiders,Runt: ''"The Rust King's Army keeps its edge by only accepting the toughest and the deadliest. {{Tooltip|Name's Runt, and you're not getting any further without me.|{audibly uncomfortable when saying his name} }}"''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) and he describes himself as the Rust King's "voice" to manage the "pawns."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"This isn't what we agreed upon."''
Runt: ''"'Agreed upon'. You are a pawn, idiot. You are the Rust King's subject, and I'm his voice. The King says jump, you ram the goddamn ceiling. So run along, and do as you're told."''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) Despite boasting about this, Runt knows that he cannot advance too far into the Rust King's Army, as he is not fit to fight in the competitive crucible of [[Burning Springs (region)|Burning Springs]]. This leaves him to make the most out of his current position, as he constantly talks down to those who happen to be lower than him on the totem pole, refusing to let them get a leg-up on him and demanding they do as they are told.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You're making this up as you go!"''
Runt: ''"A thrilling theory, sadly not to be explored. If you wish to prove yourself to the Rust King, you'll do as you're told."''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) Even if a recruit does show themself to be a worthy fighter, Runt is reluctant and hesitant to recognize their prowess, avoiding the subject by assigning them the next, seemingly random, trial to prove themself. However, Runt is also insecure about his relationship with the Rust King, believing that his talents are not being adequately recognized and that he is being treated too poorly when the Rust King would, allegedly, "achieve nothing" without him.Runt: ''"{{Tooltip|Treats me like a dog, the bastard. He'd achieve nothing without me.|{annoyed} }}"''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) He argues to himself that he could help the Rust King rule, seeing himself as deserving of better uses than his current role,Runt: ''"{{Tooltip|I could help him rule. I could be so much more useful than this.|{referring to the Rust King} }}"''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) and he does not enjoy being surrounded by people he sees as "brutes and morons," believing himself to be superior to others.Runt: ''"Brutes and morons, everywhere. I'm surrounded by them."''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) On top of his belittling, dismissive personality, Runt is virulently discriminatory toward [[ghoul]]s, referring to them as "freakshows"Runt: ''"{{Tooltip|Oh, it's the freakshow again.|{Talking to a ghoul.} }}"''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) and "muties," while also sarcastically expressing surprise when a ghoul shows basic intelligence.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Fine. Doesn't seem like I have a choice."''
Runt: ''"{{Tooltip|Whoa, it can think! Maybe it can follow simple directions too?|{Talking to a ghoul.} }} Go and do as you're told, mutie. Don't make me repeat myself."''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) This is actually at odds with the Rust King's own philosophy, who himself does not discriminate between [[human]] and ghoul, only interested in what someone can bring to the table on their own merits.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Are Ghouls welcome in your army?"''
[[The Rust King]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Humans, Ghouls... You tiny things are all the same. I don't care what you look like, only what you can offer me.|Dismissive.}}"''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) Nonetheless, Runt, by himself, seems to have low expectations for ghouls, calling it an "uphill battle" for one to make an impression.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You don't even know who I am."''
Runt: ''"{{Tooltip|You're a Ghoul. The Wasteland chewed you up and spat you out.|{Talking to a ghoul.} }} And now you want to impress the Rust King. You're looking at an uphill battle, freak."''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) Runt always dies at the end of the quest [[Might Makes Right]], as he is killed by [[Eugene (Burning Springs)|Eugene]] to set his plan into motion; Eugene says that he could not risk Runt catching on to "what's coming." Eugene also remarks that Runt would likely have kept sending the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]] on "wild goose chases."[[Eugene (Burning Springs)|Eugene]]: ''"Yes, I did. You do realize he was just going to keep sending you on those wild goose chases, right? Call it drastic, but I couldn't risk him catching on to what's coming."''
([[Eugene (Burning Springs)/Dialogue|Eugene's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |dead = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Might Makes Right]] |events started = |events involved = |essential =yes |essential until =his scripted death occurs at the end of [[Might Makes Right]] |ghost =yes |hostile = |temp companion = }} ===Quests=== * [[Might Makes Right]]: The [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]] is tasked with seeking out Runt in this quest, at which point he assigns several "Test of Might" and "Test of Dominance" [[Fallout 76 challenges|challenges]] for the player character to prove themself. At the end of the quest, Runt is killed by [[Eugene (Burning Springs)|Eugene]] to make way for his stated plan to rebel against the Rust King. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Raider demolisher outfit]] (non-lootable) |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Notes== Runt's death at the end of [[Might Makes Right]] is scripted and cannot be prevented. ==Appearances== Runt appears only {{In|FO76BS}}. ==Gallery== FO76BS Highway Town maintenance closet.png|In the maintenance closet FO76BS Runt dead.png|Found dead at the end of [[Might Makes Right]] ==References== {{Ref box}} {{Navbox Burning Springs}} [[Category:Burning Springs human characters]] [[Category:Highway Town characters]] [[Category:Rust King's Army characters]] [[ru:Шкет]]

Why do you care?|Aggressively}}|sound=Fo76BS The Exec 008404c5 1.ogg}} '''The Exec''', formerly known as '''Tony''', is a [[ghoul]] and former [[Abraxodyne Chemical]] executive living in [[Athens]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76BS}}. ==Background== Before the [[Great War]], the Exec was Tony, a businessman who had a seat on the executive board of [[Abraxodyne Chemical]]. He looks back on his pre-War life fondly, embracing the capitalist mindset of "making money hand over fist."The Exec: ''"Way back when, before the bombs and before I'd turned into sentient roadkill, I was actually a very important man. I had a seat on the board of Abraxodyne Chemical. You know, the detergent company? Boy, were we living it up, making money hand over fist. But then our head of Marketing, Amrita, started sticking her nose where she shouldn't. It became a problem. {{Tooltip|I was in charge of making sure company business stayed private. So, when Amrita wouldn't stop prying, I had her taken care of.|emphasis on 'taken care of'}} {{Tooltip|What's it to you, though? Why do you care?|Aggressively}}"''
([[The Exec/Dialogue|The Exec's dialogue]])The Exec: ''"Look, I'm a business man. Always have been, always will be. How about we settle this with some caps and call it a day, huh?"''
([[The Exec/Dialogue|The Exec's dialogue]]) Tony also concepted the "Abraxo-bucks" initiative, held as a contest by Abraxodyne for the public to collect tickets with rewards for the winners. However, due to insufficient cost projections prior to the contest's approval, the company soon realized they could not have "so many winners" and were forced to reconfigure the contest and discourage the likelihood of someone collecting enough tickets.[[Abraxodyne tapes#Abraxodyne tape 12|Abraxodyne tape 12]] Tony was initially skeptical of the company's venture into [[Project Meadow Breeze]], using the company's chemicals to produce a military-grade weapon, and he wanted to scrap the project after the first round of testing failed. However, he changed his opinion after seeing the projected revenue from a contract with the [[United States Armed Forces]], joking that perhaps they had a "national duty" to protect the military, in a boon for both "morale and market share."[[Abraxodyne tapes#Abraxodyne tape 11|Abraxodyne tape 11]] While on the board, Tony was in charge of securing company secrets and controlling the flow of information, making sure Abraxodyne's business stayed private. After details regarding Project Meadow Breeze were nearly leaked to a reporter (who was subsequently "caught and dealt with" before anything negative was published), Tony led efforts to uncover the mole within the company. He threatened to ramp up Abraxodyne's internal investigation unless this mole immediately came forward, which they did not.[[Abraxodyne tapes#Abraxodyne tape 13|Abraxodyne tape 13]] It was soon determined that this mole was [[Amrita]], the head of Abraxodyne's marketing division. Using his powerful position on the board of Abraxodyne Chemical, Tony ordered that Amrita should be eliminated, in order to protect the company's interests and private business. The company discretely hired a hitman to kill Amrita, who would pick up equipment from Tony's [[Executive's apartment|apartment]] before "disposing" of the whistleblower.[[Bodhi]]: ''"{{Tooltip|This note detailed instructions for a hitman to collect equipment from a nearby apartment, and 'dispose of the whistleblower target'.|Defeated and trembling}} {{Tooltip|So this is how they chose to deal with my beloved daughter! My little girl... gone.|distraught}}"''
([[Bodhi/Dialogue|Bodhi's dialogue]]) Although they were successful in silencing her and keeping Project Meadow Breeze under wraps, it was all for naught, as the bombs dropped not long after, which Tony sees as a reason not to care about the past anymore.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I can keep silent about all this, for a price..."''
The Exec: ''"*chuckle* You think I give a damn who knows about this stuff? Who cares anymore? The whole world's a smoldering wreck!"''
([[The Exec/Dialogue|The Exec's dialogue]]) He further defends his actions regarding Amrita's murder for two reasons: he claims that the [[Meadow Breeze Sprayer]] and its [[Prototype ABX03|prototypes]] were never intended to actually be used and were only deterrents to help the troops,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Even for the weapon you authorized? Project 'Meadow Breeze'?"''
The Exec: ''"That? We never really intended for it to be used. We built it as a deterrent to help our troops, is all."''
([[The Exec/Dialogue|The Exec's dialogue]]) and that the board members had to toe the company line and he would have been "next" if he did not deal with Amrita.The Exec: ''"What do you want from me? To tell you that I'm sorry? That I regret it? Well I don't. Yeah, shady shit went on, but Amrita wasn't the only one affected by it. The board had an iron grip on its members and we all had to toe the line. If I didn't take care of Amrita, I'd have been next. Then who would've been there to care of my wife and daughter? I'll never apologize for looking after my family, even if some people got hurt along the way."''
([[The Exec/Dialogue|The Exec's dialogue]]) Before the bombs dropped, he had a wife and daughter whom he wanted to protect, and he says that he was just looking after his family in his actions. However, at some point, Tony's wife ran off with another Abraxodyne executive, [[Kerry (Burning Springs)|Kerry]], and took their daughter with her. He now regards them with vitriol, claiming that he once worked sixteen hours per day for them, all of it apparently having been for nothing. He does not know where they are now after the bombs, nor does he know whether they are alive or dead.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Where are your wife and daughter now?"''
The Exec: ''"{{Tooltip|God knows. She ran off with that scumbag Kerry, and took my baby girl with her. Some thanks for working sixteen hours a day for them, huh? Hope they're happy, if they ain't already worm food by now.|Vitriol}}"''
([[The Exec/Dialogue|The Exec's dialogue]]) Tony survived the Great War but became a [[ghoul]], and he clearly resents the current state of his body,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I'm sorry to intrude, but I'm looking for information."''
The Exec: ''"Yeah? Well I'm looking for a time machine and a dermatologist. Looks like we're both out of luck. Now buzz off!"''
([[The Exec/Dialogue|The Exec's dialogue]]) calling himself "sentient roadkill" and a "rotten scab."The Exec: ''"Well looky here, a fellow rotten scab wasting away in this cesspit town."''
([[The Exec/Dialogue|The Exec's dialogue]])
'''Note:''' This line is played only if the player character is [[Fallout 76 playable ghoul|also a ghoul]]. He lives a secluded life in his old pre-War apartment in Athens, as one of its few non-feral residents,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I thought this block was abandoned."''
The Exec: ''"Yeah, well, not every every ghoul in Athens has gone feral just yet. Get out of here, and leave me in peace."''
([[The Exec/Dialogue|The Exec's dialogue]]) where he has set traps to ward off visitors, whom he makes clear are unwelcome.The Exec: ''"Waltz right in to my apartment, why don't you. Clear off!"''
([[The Exec/Dialogue|The Exec's dialogue]])The Exec: ''"Can't you see this place is occupied? Get out of here, you bum."''
([[The Exec/Dialogue|The Exec's dialogue]]) He holds absolutely no regret over how he handled the situation with Amrita before the bombs, justifying her murder for a variety of reasons, and maintains an irritable disposition, all while still clutching to a businessman's negotiating mindset.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Make me a deal and maybe I'll have mercy on you."''
The Exec: ''"A businessman at heart, huh? I respect that. I can offer you caps, and plenty of them."''
([[The Exec/Dialogue|The Exec's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |killable =yes |essential = |essential until = |ghost = |ghost until = |quests started = |quests involved =[[Dirty Laundry]] |encounters = |wares = |caps = }} ===Quests=== [[Dirty Laundry]]: After collecting the final segment of the 65 [[Abraxodyne intel]] needed for the quest, [[Bodhi]] points the player to the location of the [[executive's apartment]], where the Exec has secluded himself. The player can confront him over Amrita's death, and has several options in dealing with him. * Taking [[Cap (Fallout 76)|caps]] in exchange for silence. * Letting him go freely. * Attacking and killing him. ==Inventory== {{Missing data|Inventory|FO76}} {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Notes== It is never explicitly stated that the Exec is Tony from the Abraxodyne tapes. However, there are several strong connections that indicate they are the same character: they share a voice actor ([[Tony Daniels]]), were both board members for Abraxodyne Chemical, and the Exec says he was in charge of controlling the flow of information within the company, which is the exact role that Tony fulfills in Abraxodyne tape 13. ==Appearances== The Exec appears only {{In|FO76BS}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Burning Springs}} [[Category:Burning Springs ghoul characters]] [[Category:Abraxodyne Chemical characters]] [[Category:Athens characters]]

It's that simple.|Doesn't need to prove himself.}}|The Rust King|sound=The Rust King 00830aa8 1.ogg}} '''The Rust King''' is an intelligent [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|super mutant]] and warlord leading the [[Rust King's Army]] [[Fallout 76 factions|faction]] operating in [[Burning Springs (region)|Burning Springs]]. He appears as a major character and antagonist {{in|FO76BS}}. ==Background== ===Origins=== The Rust King's origins are shrouded in mystery, although it is known that he was once a subject of the [[Enclave]] from an unknown location of theirs, held prisoner and intended to be transported somewhere by [[Vertibird (Fallout 76)|vertibird]]. After being awoken by turbulence, the super mutant thrashed violently and broke free of his constraints, causing the vertibird to crash. Although the Enclave personnel were killed, the super mutant survived and left the [[Enclave vertibird crash site|crash site]], beginning to forge a new path in the [[Burning Springs (region)|Burning Springs]] region of [[Appalachia]].[[EV-21 blackbox recording]] Now let loose into the wasteland, the super mutant's intelligence and thirst for blood made for a deadly combination, and he quickly rose to power in the Burning Springs region.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What do you know about the Rust King?"''
[[Moose (Burning Springs)|Moose]]: ''"Oh God, I hate calling him King. I don't know how he ended up here, but he turned this entire area into his personal playground pretty quickly."''
([[Moose (Burning Springs)/Dialogue|Moose's dialogue]]) He sought to build an empire in Burning Springs,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Can you tell me more about where we are?"''
The Rust King: ''"This is my empire of rust and steel. I built it from the ashes of this Wasteland, and now it stands tall."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) seeing it as akin to rearing a child, with the blood being spilled throughout the [[wasteland]] as analogous to his seed.[[The King's witness#VI|The King's witness, VI]] His status as a super mutant allowed him to go wherever he pleased without needing to concern himself with [[radiation]] or other deadly threats that made [[human]]s vulnerable.[[The Rust Kingdom terminal entries#Founding our home|The Rust Kingdom terminal entries; Tales of the Rust Kingdom, Founding our home]] He started out launching attacks on settlements himself; at some point around or after [[Timeline#2080|2080]] or [[Timeline#2082|2082]],{{Ref|(Note 1)}} sightings of him were noticed by the [[Ash Cavers]], with three reports in three months, and he eventually killed one of their guards while she was wearing [[power armor]]. [[Franklin Metter]] speculated that whatever killed her was intelligent, and may have been probing their territory.[[Ash Cave terminal entries#Security Concerns|Ash Cave terminal entries; Professor Metter's terminal, Security Concerns]] At one point, he began attacking the denizens of [[Highway Town]], wreaking destruction on the settlement and forcing them to rebuild, weaker each time.[[The King's witness#IV|The King's witness, IV]] Eventually, he invited many of its residents to join him, making up the ranks of his [[Rust King's Army|army]]. The Rust King declared that only the strongest among them would survive; parents and children alike killed each other in battle after being given this ultimatum and weapons to boot. Those who refused to participate became the first victims of the Rust King's army.[[The King's witness#VII|The King's witness, VII]] ===Becoming king=== Over time, the Rust King amassed a large following, directing his army in a conquest over southeastern, [[Appalachia]]n [[Ohio]]. He spared Highway Town from further incursions of his wrath, allowing them to grow so that a worthy challenge could rise up and face him from the life of the settlement. [[Runt]] describes this arrangement as the Rust King allowing Highway Town to exist for as long as they do not stand against him.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Highway Town doesn't seem to be under the Rust King."''
[[Runt]]: ''"He allows Highway Town to exist because Highway Town won't stand against him. This arrangement can continue indefinitely. The people of this dump should pray that it does."''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) [[Rust raider|Raiders]] admired the Rust King for his strength and joined the membership of the Rust King's Army, while others joined seemingly out of necessity as the raiders' power grew, viewing resistance as futile.[[He's called the Rust King]] The Rust King and his army settled into their headquarters after hearing whispers of a [[Deathclaw (Fallout 76)|deathclaw]] nest at an old [[Abraxodyne Chemical]] plant. The Rust King and his men battled against the creatures as part of his growing conquest; many raiders died in the fight, while the Rust King himself incurred injuries that would have killed lesser men. The Rust King is alleged to have beheaded the deathclaws' matriarch with his bare hands, before adopting the [[Deathclaw egg (Fallout 76)|eggs]] left behind. The chemical facility was christened [[The Rust Kingdom (location)|the Rust Kingdom]], over which the brutal, intelligent warlord ruled as king. The Rust King views deathclaws as kin, seeing similarities between his and their abilities as hunters. He directed the eggs to be raised into trained fighters, and the Rust King's Army has since become known for their taming and training of deathclaws.[[Highway Town settler]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Those raiders are trying to tame Deathclaws! Fools are gonna get themselves killed.|Emphasis here is on “trying”, as if it’s the most impossible thing in the world.}}"''
([[Highway Town settler/Dialogue|Highway Town settlers' dialogue]]) Despite the difficulty of the task, they have found success in this venture, as the Rust King even sought out skilled animal trainers to join the fold.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"How did you end up in the Rust King's Army?"''
[[Beastmaster Lina]]: ''"I have useful skills, and ''m{{sic}} a survivor. Both are something he likes. Strangely enough, I wasn't even that good when I started, my Dad was. It was him the Rust King wanted. {{Tooltip|And then he went and did something dumb and unnecessary. I didn't. The rest is history.|choking up a bit at “dumb and unnecessary”, then quickly regains composure}}"''
([[Beastmaster Lina/Dialogue|Beastmaster Lina's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Is training Deathclaws hard?"''
[[Beastmaster Lina]]: ''"{{Tooltip|Like any other wild animal: punishments and rewards, start young enough and you're golden. I grew up around dogs, so I had a head start, too.|Frosty. Player has touched on a sore subject.}} My Dad used to train police dogs, had his own little center and everything. Taught me all there was to know so that I could take over one day. {{Tooltip|In a way I did, I suppose... Oh well. Next question?|momentarily lost in thought at “in a way I did”}}"''
([[Beastmaster Lina/Dialogue|Beastmaster Lina's dialogue]]) The deathclaws are raised at [[Jackson Junkyard]], close by to the Rust Kingdom,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What is this place?"''
[[Beastmaster Lina]]: ''"{{Tooltip|This is where the Rust King gets his Deathclaws from. We raise them here, break them down, and train the poor bastards for combat in the field or the arena.|“poor bastards” is meant to communicate empathy here - the Beastmaster is resigned to her role but part of her despises doing this to living creature}} The ones I've got are almost ready; all that's left is to fit them with their armor. This will make a lot of noise, so be ready for uninvited guests. They always come."''
([[Beastmaster Lina/Dialogue|Beastmaster Lina's dialogue]]) and they are brought back to participate as fighters in an arena. This arena was set up within the old Abraxodyne facility as entertainment for the Rust King,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What happens to the weak folk?"''
The Rust King: ''"I give them a great honor. They kneel and use their bare hands to build my kingdom, or serve as entertainment in the arena. They are good because they are replaceable."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) while also allowing captives and fighters to prove their worth to the Rust King.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Cut to the chase. Why am I here?"''
The Rust King: ''"{{Tooltip|You're here to fight in my arena. My soldiers thought you were an impressive creature.|Genuine.}} I planned to see how long you could last against my beasts, but then I heard that you were scheming in your cell. {{Tooltip|Which man did you recruit as your ally?|Very domineering.}}"''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Why'd you join them?"''
[[Silas (Burning Springs)|Silas]]: ''"{{Tooltip|I found this place after trackin' down some thief. I trailed his guts on the arena floor, and the Rust King was real impressed. He said...|Excited, then gets nervous after ‘He said’.}} Oh, I'm saying too much. Too much."''
([[Silas (Burning Springs)/Dialogue|Silas' dialogue]]) Although the Rust King describes the arena as a method of culling the weak, [[Beastmaster Lina]] jokingly speculates that he probably "just gets off on bloodshed."[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What's the Arena?"''
[[Beastmaster Lina]]: ''"And now I know you're a newcomer. Everybody knows the arena! That dome the Rust King is set up in - it's his arena for staging fights. Prisoners, creatures, his own men trying to prove themselves - all fight and die there. It's the culling of the weak, or so the Rust King says. Probably just gets off on bloodshed, truth be told."''
([[Beastmaster Lina/Dialogue|Beastmaster Lina's dialogue]]) Early on in the Rust King's conquest, he saw the strategic value of [[Fort Steuben]] after it had been scouted out by members of his army. The Rust King dispatched a war party to take over the fort, which was inhabited at the time. The denizens fought back and a siege ensued, with the combat lasting overnight. Once morning had passed, the Rust King's Army had reduced their defenses and stormed the fort, killing many of its inhabitants and claiming the territory for the Rust King. The survivors were sent to the Rust Kingdom's arena. Fort Steuben was a starting point for further conquests, as the kingdom grew in size and seized control of more locations around Burning Springs.[[The Rust Kingdom terminal entries#Siege of Fort Steuben|The Rust Kingdom terminal entries; Tales of the Rust Kingdom, Siege of Fort Steuben]] In December [[Timeline#2089|2089]], the Rust King met with Franklin Metter of the Ash Cavers. Metter, who was ill, dying and seeking a legacy, agreed to fold the Ash Cavers into the Rust King's ranks, where they continue to survive.[[Ash Cave terminal entries#12/15/2089|Ash Cave terminal entries, Professor Metter's terminal, 12/15/2089]] Other locations, such as the church at the [[South Ohio Evacuation Center]], could be used a source of prey to teach the "young" of the Rust King's Army, and would eventually be annexed into their territory.[[The King's witness#V|The King's witness, V]] Eventually, the bounds of the Rust King's territory hit the [[Ohio River]]. He took interest in potentially conquering lands east of the river, but became disinterested when scouts reported that Appalachia was weak, and the [[Cult of the Mothman|cultists]] of [[Point Pleasant]] were more interested in worshiping a [[Mothman|bug]] for strength. The cultists became a mild nuisance after the [[North Road Bridge]] was reconstructed and they attempted to assault the Rust King's Army. The Rust King commanded that extra fortifications be built to mark the border of his kingdom, leading to the construction of [[Checkpoint Canyon]] and suppressing the cultists' ill-fated advance.[[The Rust Kingdom terminal entries#Fortification of Checkpoint Canyon|The Rust Kingdom terminal entries; Tales of the Rust Kingdom, Fortification of Checkpoint Canyon]] ===Warlord of Burning Springs=== As of [[Timeline#2105|2105]],{{Ref|(Note 2)}} the Rust King still enjoys near-complete dominance over the Burning Springs region, and he uses his army of raiders as "pest control" to deal with "vermin" in his lands.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What do your soldiers do?"''
The Rust King: ''"Pest control. They help to keep my land in order by dealing with the vermin."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) However, as his power only grows, the Rust King has found moments to contemplate. After capturing a [[Christianity|Christian]] priest, the Rust King allowed this preacher to live and told them that he wanted his own scripture to be written in his name.[[The King's witness#III|The King's witness, III]] The priest produced a number of writings detailing their travels with the Rust King, before the king eventually commanded them to spread this scripture north of [[Athens]].[[The King's witness#VIII|The King's witness, VIII]] The priest refused, but was spared anyway, as they attempted to scatter and leave behind their writings. However, the priest came to believe that they themself carried the Rust King's scripture, not their writings.[[The King's witness#IX|The King's witness, IX]] As such, the priest self-immolated in a final act of defiance against the Rust King.[[The King's witness#X|The King's witness, X]] The story of the priest is one demonstration that not all wastelanders believe in the Rust King's power. [[The Ghoul]] sees him as just another example in a long line of those seeking to be tyrants, believing the Rust King to hold "delusions of grandeur" and proclaiming that all kings fall eventually.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What do you know about the Rust King?"''
[[The Ghoul]]: ''"Some overgrown green bastard with delusions of grandeur? Not the first would-be king I've seen in the Wasteland. Doubt he'll be the last. He doesn't interfere with my business, I've got no reason to get involved with his. All I know is kings fall, and all crowns rust."''
([[The Ghoul/Dialogue|The Ghoul's dialogue]]) Many current residents of Highway Town believe that they could topple the Rust King if only the disparate, independent [[bounty hunter]]s populating the settlement would unite.[[Highway Town settler]]: ''"All these bounty hunters running around, if only they could unite we could stick it to the Rust King."''
([[Highway Town settler/Dialogue|Highway Town settlers' dialogue]]) The Rust King has a vision for the future, and he seeks a conqueror to advise him and help him rule the wasteland, believing someone like this to be necessary "for what [is] to come."The Rust King: ''"For what's to come, I need a conqueror. You, 'Eugene', boast too much for someone who didn't do the work. {{Tooltip|But you, champion. Your resolve is firm.|Talking to the player.}} Now, we must deal with this mutt."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) To this end, the Rust King has started doing something he previously did not:[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Have you tested others like you've tested Eugene and I?"''
The Rust King: ''"No. The schemer came to my attention first. When I heard rumors of his wit, I sought a worthy opponent and had my men track him down. I told him to prove to me that his value outweighs that of any member of my army. His pathetic attempts to avoid a fight amused me... for a time. Just as my patience ran thin, you arrived. A skilled warrior from beneath the earth. He must have assumed you'd be easy prey. Ha! It's clear he was a coward from the start."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) he seeks to pit captives against each other in a battle of wits, rather than just entertainment for the arena, as part of a test to determine who is worthy to stand beside him and help mold the wasteland in his and his champion's image.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Why didn't you tell me that you were making Eugene my competitor?"''
The Rust King: ''"He knelt at my throne after you left my arena. He claimed that he could prove himself to be a skilled hunter, and wished to stalk his prey. It turned out to be nothing but sniveling cowardice."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I'm excited for what we will do together."''
The Rust King: ''"I knew I made the right choice. Together we will re-shape this Wasteland in our image. I will see you again soon, champion."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) This eventually leads to a potential confrontation between [[Eugene (Burning Springs)|Eugene]], [[Silas (Burning Springs)|Silas]] and a particular [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]] with great promise.Events of [[Welcoming Committee]] and [[When the Rust Settles]]. ===Personality and ideology=== {{Quotation|Plans are for schemers. I rule what I see. I will kill what I want, when I want. I continue to forge my might for whatever may come. You are a part of that.|The Rust King}} Above all else, the Rust King believes in the supremacy of the strong over the weak.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"A Super Mutant leading humans? I haven't seen that before."''
The Rust King: ''"{{Tooltip|Who cares what I am? The weak follow the strong, or they die. It's that simple.|Doesn't need to prove himself.}}"''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) He adheres to the principles of the survival of the fittest[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I enjoyed the violence of it all."''
The Rust King: ''"Yes. Killing comes naturally to those of us fit to survive."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) and the belief that might makes right.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What are your plans now?"''
The Rust King: ''"Plans are for schemers, like the one that is now pulp between my fingers. I rule what I see. I will kill what I want, when I want. I continue to forge my might for whatever may come. You are a part of that."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) Despite this, he recognizes that strength comes in many forms, and thus allows soldiers in his army who are not physically fit, but may be talented in other ways, such as deception ([[Ava (Burning Springs)|Ava]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"If you value strength. why do you have people like Ava in your army?"''
The Rust King: ''"Strength comes in different forms. Ava's tricks have dealt with many of our problems."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) or recruitment ([[Runt]]).[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"'Runt'? I can see that. How come you were able to join?"''
[[Runt]]: ''"{{Tooltip|The Rust King isn't some jumped up thug. And he wants the best in the land for his army.|{insulted and quietly fuming} }} {{Tooltip|I know people, and I can tell who can make it. So I decide who can make it. And if you want in, you will fix your tone going forward.|{emphasis on decide} }}"''
([[Runt/Dialogue|Runt's dialogue]]) He does not discriminate between [[human]] or [[ghoul]], and only focuses on what an individual can bring to him.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Are Ghouls welcome in your army?"''
The Rust King: ''"{{Tooltip|Humans, Ghouls... You tiny things are all the same. I don't care what you look like, only what you can offer me.|Dismissive.}}"''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) He wants his army to comprise the best in the land, and believes those strong enough to compete should prove their worth. If he believes that they are not worthy of serving under his banner, then they have no purpose to him and should be disposed of.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Tell me about yourself."''
The Rust King: ''"{{Tooltip|I am the Rust King. I test people's resolve to see if they are worthy of their place in my kingdom.|Matter of fact.}}"''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"So I'm your champion instead?"''
The Rust King: ''"For as long as you prove worthy. If that changes, I'll step on your skull myself."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) He sees Burning Springs as containing vermin, and his soldiers as the pest control dealing with the vermin. He believes that murder and violence should come naturally to those who are fit to survive in the wasteland. He lacks compassion, seeing kindness and heart as weaknesses,The Rust King: ''"{{Tooltip|We will remove that kind heart, then you will be a good soldier.|Player has just killed many enemies in the arena.}}"''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"We shouldn't have killed him."''
The Rust King: ''"When will you discard that heart of yours? Luckily your other traits outweigh your weaknesses."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) and values strong warriors over those who are merciful.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I've changed my mind. I want to be your warrior."''
The Rust King: ''"A smart choice, champion."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) He also declares his hatred for liars and stolen glory,The Rust King: ''"{{Tooltip|I hate liars. I despise weaklings. Stolen glory is an early grave in my kingdom.|Emphasis on 'despise'.}}"''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) much like his distaste for cowardice. Despite claiming to scorn ego[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"That fight was nothing."''
The Rust King: ''"{{Tooltip|Strength is your ally, but you are not the strongest here. Watch your ego. That's how great warriors fall.|Impressed, but stern.}}"''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) and arrogance (or at least unearned examples of these),[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Neither of them."''
The Rust King: ''"You think you're a lone wolf? I've never seen such arrogance from someone so small. Let's see how far you are willing to go for your freedom. Kill Silas, and I will consider letting you live."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) much of what the Rust King declares is self-serving and hinges on his pre-assumed greatness,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I want to leave. Let me go, now."''
The Rust King: ''"{{Tooltip|I don't care what you want. This is my domain, and unless you take it from me, you will kneel.|Dismissive. Knows he is the strongest.}}"''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]])[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You think highly of yourself."''
The Rust King: ''"Why shouldn't I? I take what I want, whenever I want it, and I crush those who would oppose me. The weak hide what they are. The strong have no need."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) needing others to prove their worth to him. Much of the Rust King's intelligence lies within knowing how to display and use his strength to his advantage, successfully controlling his kingdom and terrorizing the people of Burning Springs, to the point that they feel they have no other options but to join his army, lest they become a victim of it. However, one weakness of the Rust King's rule is a nearly tunnel-visioned focus on the present. He declares his state of being as killing what he wants, when he wants, but actually spurns long-term planning, instead preferring to focus on what he sees in the here and now. Although he has a vague vision of the future and some strategic acumen, he outright says that "plans are for schemers" and is confident in his ability to maintain his might "whatever may come." While this confidence is seemingly earned given his tenure thus far, the Ghoul believes that the Rust King and his "delusions of grandeur" will eventually fall, like all kings do. The Rust King is so confident in the supremacy of the strong and their qualities that even if the Vault 76 dweller outright declares their intention to go against him,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"Don't get in my way, or you'll end up just like them."''
The Rust King: ''"Bite and bark! You would be a good soldier."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) ignore his rule,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I'm not interested in being a part of this anymore."''
The Rust King: ''"That's not something for you to decide. As long as you breathe, you live in my world. I deem you my champion. That is a fact."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) or even attempt to challenge his throne outright,[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I'd like to challenge you next."''
The Rust King: ''"You are funny. Maybe someday you will die under my heel, but I've seen enough of you for now."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) he brushes it off as simply humorous, believing that someone of the dweller's caliber and strength will come to their senses eventually, even in the face of straight-forward rejection of his principles. In fact, the Rust King invites opposition, saying that he hungers for rebellion, and any attempts to stifle such a challenge would be an insult to his strength.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"So you were aware of the revolutionists?"''
The Rust King: ''"No. If I had known that Eugene planned to stifle their efforts, I would have killed him from the start. I don't fear rebellion, I hunger for it. Let the strong rise up and face me. To hinder their potential is an insult to my strength."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) This does not mean he will tolerate defiance indefinitely, however.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I'm not your champion. Using me makes you no better than Eugene."''
The Rust King: ''"Watch your tongue. Don't compare me to such an insect. Soon we will meet again, and you'll decide where you stand. If you defy me then, I'll be the last enemy you ever make. The choice of life or death is yours, champion."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) Nonetheless, the Rust King also scoffs at overt and performative servility toward him.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"I bow before you, Your Majesty."''
The Rust King: ''"You think that pathetic attitude will make me spare you? You have a lot to learn here."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) The Vault 76 dweller can criticize how the Rust King intends to use his desired champion, comparing him to the schemers he claims to detest, which the Rust King strongly rejects as a comparison to an insect. This speaks to the Rust King's confidence in his own dominance, seeing his conquests as comparable to stepping on ants, and that no one could possibly win against him.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"You must have quite the kill count."''
The Rust King: ''"Do you count the ants you step on? Nobody wins against me."''
([[The Rust King/Dialogue|The Rust King's dialogue]]) Until that day comes, the Rust King continues to use Burning Springs as his playground, waging a path of war wherever his army goes. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |quests involved =[[Welcoming Committee]]
[[When the Rust Settles]] |quests started =[[Might Makes Right]] |essential =yes |ghost =yes }} ===Quests=== * [[Welcoming Committee]]: The Rust King is first met during this quest. After an initial introduction, followed by either surviving [[The Rust Kingdom (location)|the Rust Kingdom's]] arena gauntlet, or killing [[Silas (Burning Springs)|Silas]], the player may talk at length with the Rust King, before being sent out of the arena. * [[Might Makes Right]]: The Rust King starts this quest, dismissing the player from the Rust Kingdom arena and sending them to [[Highway Town]] to meet [[Runt]] and undertake a number of tasks to prove one's worth. * [[When the Rust Settles]]: Following [[Insurrection|the previous quest]], the player and [[Eugene (Burning Springs)|Eugene]] set into motion a plan to overthrow the Rust King, which encounters a fatal complication. After surviving another, more dangerous bout in the arena, the player must deal with Eugene, after which they may converse with the Rust King again. The Rust King declares that they will meet again, before the player is removed from the arena once more, ending the quest. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =Rust King crown
Burn_RustKingArmourBody01 |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== * {{Note|(Note 1)}} The [[Ash Cave terminal entries]] first mention the [[Ash Cavers]] seeking to use power armor in [[Ash Cave terminal entries#08/01/2080|an entry]] dated to August [[Timeline#2080|2080]], while in [[Ash Cave terminal entries#04/18/2082|another entry]] dated to April [[Timeline#2082|2082]], [[Franklin Metter]] writes that they "find [them]selves wanting for power armor." The [[Ash Cave terminal entries#Security Concerns|Security Concerns]] terminal entry is undated, but mentions that a guard was killed while wearing power armor by the Rust King (or the "green man"), implying that it occurred at some point around or after 2080 or 2082, based on the other entries' reports of the Ash Cavers' availability to power armor. * {{Note|(Note 2)}} [[Timeline#2105|2105]] is the in-game year set on the [[Pip-Boy 2000 Mark VI|Pip-Boy]] as of the release of the ''Burning Springs'' update. ==Appearances== The Rust King appears only {{in|FO76BS}}. ==Gallery== FO76BS The Rust King standing.png|Standing during [[When the Rust Settles]] ==References== {{Ref box}} {{Navbox Burning Springs}} {{Navbox characters FO76}} {{Navbox antagonists}} [[Category:Burning Springs super mutant characters]] [[Category:Rust King's Army characters]] [[Category:Antagonists]] [[ru:Ржавый Король]]

However, the role of Windy is not listed in the in-game voice acting credits. * Windy's original name is 바람 (''baram''), which means "wind" in Korean and was given to her by her grandparents. {{FO76CC}} * Windy was originally intended to be a cryptid-focused merchant who could be hired at [[Milepost Zero (location)|Milepost Zero]] for 300 Supplies, but she did not make it into the final version of that update and had a complicated development history. ** Prior to the live release of ''Milepost Zero'', recruiting Windy was disabled in the August 9, 2024, update to the [[Public Test Server]], with the patch notes saying she had been temporarily cut, due to bugs with her dialogue. Although she was featured in the trailer and her room was still present in Milepost Zero, she was not accessible and could be recruited in the live game. A Tweet from [[Bethesda Softworks|Bethesda]] Support stated "We do not have any official information on Windy [Park] at this time."[https://archive.ph/5wgrl Bethesda Support on Twitter]: ''"We do not have any official information on Windy Parks{{sic}} at this time."'' ** Recruiting Windy was later re-enabled in the Public Test Server alongside [[Collector Murmrgh]]; the PTS patch notes on October 10, 2024, indicated that they were confirmed to be coming to the game.[https://archive.ph/5R295 PTS Update Notes - 10/10] However, she was removed yet again (as well as Murmrgh) in the PTS update on November 15, which was said to be the last patch before the live release of the ''[[Gleaming Depths (update)|Gleaming Depths]]'' update. Windy was still not accessible on the live game and did not make it into the release of ''Gleaming Depths'' in December 2024 or ''[[Ghoul Within]]'' in March 2025. However, she and Murmrgh were referenced on the [[Milepost Zero terminal entries]] in-game. ** Eventually, Windy's appearance at Milepost Zero was scrapped in favor of her appearance at Highway Town in the ''Burning Springs'', for which she received a reworked dialogue tree and become a [[gold bullion]] vendor. {{FO76CC|end}} ==Gallery== FO76MZ Windy Park trailer.png|In the ''Milepost Zero'' trailer ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Stub|FO76BS}} {{Navbox vendors FO76}} [[Category:Burning Springs human characters]] [[Category:Blue Ridge Caravan Company characters]] [[ru:Уинди]]

{{Infobox character |games =FO76,FO76BS |image =FO76BS Xander Brown.png |displayname =Rust Raider |shortname =Xander |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |nickname = |affiliation =[[Rust King's Army]]
