Warehouse staff (pre-War) |location =[[Super Duper Mart (Burning Springs)|Super Duper Mart]] |status =Deceased |notes =[[Xander's journal]]
[[Rehabilitation scheme note]]
[[Staff assignments]] |hair color ={{Tooltip|Red dye|HairColor30Red}} |eye color ={{Tooltip|Hazel bloodshot|MaleEyesHumanHazelBloodshot}} |hairstyle ={{Tooltip|Soldier of Fortune|HairMale43}} |facial hair ={{Tooltip|Prospector|BigBeard10}} |level =1+ |special ={{SPECIAL|0,4,0,0,0,5,0}} |aggression =Very Aggressive |confidence =Foolhardy |assistance =Helps Friends and Allies |factions =Burn_RustRaiderFaction |CK race =HumanRace |class =raiderClass |edid =BURN_Loot_CorpseRustRaiderSDM02 |formid ={{ID|0082def5}} |refid = }} '''Xander Brown''', known in-game as a '''Rust raider''', was an employee at the [[Super Duper Mart (Burning Springs)|Super Duper Mart]] in [[Burning Springs (region)|Burning Springs]], who became a member of the [[Rust King's Army]] after the [[Great War]]. His corpse appears {{in|FO76BS}}. ==Background== ===Pre-War=== Before the [[Nuclear weapons|bombs]] dropped, Xander was convicted for grand theft auto and imprisoned for some time. He was eventually let out on parole and entered into a prisoner rehabilitation scheme, in which prior offenders would be assigned employment at a [[Super Duper Mart (Burning Springs)|Super Duper Mart]] to facilitate their reentry into society.[[Rehabilitation scheme note]] In his role as a warehouse worker,[[Staff assignments]] Xander was looked upon favorably by the store's management, who reviewed his performance and wrote that he was a good worker and knowledgeable about the warehouse, as well as someone who did not complain about his working hours or pay. Xander was thus considered for a salaried role with a 2% increase of his current hourly pay, and would receive increased hours to boot.[[Super Duper Mart terminal entries (Burning Springs)#Xander|Super Duper Mart terminal entries; Super Duper Mart manager's terminal, Xander]] He was also asked to perform extra duties that required discretion, such as searching the trash to prevent loss of product when [[Matilda Green]] was suspected of stealing from the pharmacy.[[Super Duper Mart terminal entries (Burning Springs)#Matilda|Super Duper Mart terminal entries; Super Duper Mart manager's terminal, Matilda]] However, behind the scenes, Xander was continuing to participate in illegal activity. He worked with shift supervisor [[William Barlow|William "Bill" Barlow]] (himself convicted for gang-related activities) to traffic some unspecified contraband through the store's warehouse, for sale to a "high value client," all while avoiding the interference of store management.[[Delivery note]] ===Post-War=== In May of an undated year in the post-War era, Xander and Bill reunited at the Super Duper Mart, which had fallen into disrepair after the nukes. Xander was surprised to see Bill and speculated that he had remembered the location of a "stash" on the premises of the store, "just like old times." By this point, [[the Rust King]] was already growing powerful in the [[Burning Springs (region)|Burning Springs]] region, and in June, Bill took charge of a group of survivors, including Xander, who had set up at the Super Duper Mart. Bill, holding to the principles of "survival of the fittest," declared that they would have a place in [[Ohio]] under the Rust King, paying tribute to the warlord and eventually joining the [[Rust King's Army]]. Xander liked the sound of this, seeing it as their path to living however they wanted in the [[wasteland]].[[Xander's journal]]The presence of [[Rust raider]] corpses and [[:File:FO76BS Super Duper Mart RKA decal.png|Rust King's Army]] graffiti affirm that those at the Super Duper Mart joined the Rust King's Army. That September, the newly-strengthened raiders at the Super Duper Mart under Barlow, including Xander, began capturing [[Feral ghoul (Fallout 76)|feral ghouls]] in the region and storing them in the store's freezers, to give to the [[The Rust Kingdom (location)|Rust Kingdom]] for use in the Rust King's combat arena. They also sold a few feral ghouls to the residents of [[the Buckeye Diner]] at [[The Chop Shop (Burning Springs)|the Chop Shop]]. In early October, the group was attacked by a pack of feral ghouls from [[Athens]], who managed to break down the defenses and kill some of the raiders. As Bill directed the group in rebuilding their barriers, Xander pondered on the sentience of the feral ghouls. Two days after the feral ghoul attack, the group suffered another massive blow when [[Radscorpion (Fallout 76)|radscorpions]] attacked the premises, breaking through concrete and devastating the raiders. Writing "we didn't stand a chance," Xander witnessed some of the group members die after everyone scattered during the attack. Xander himself was stung by a radscorpion and hid in the secure storage of the Super Duper Mart's warehouse, where he eventually perished. ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |none = |dead =yes }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Rust raider light outfit]] (non-lootable) |weapon = |otheritem =[[Xander's journal]] |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== There are two corpses at the Super Duper Mart whose names appear as "[[Rust raider|Rust Raider]]" in-game. One is a female corpse, while the other is a male corpse in the secure storage that holds [[Xander's journal]] in its inventory. This latter corpse's NPC record has the short name "Xander," but it is not used in-game, as Xander's dead body has no spoken dialogue. ==Appearances== Xander Brown's corpse appears only {{in|FO76BS}}. ==Gallery== FO76BS Note Xanders Journal Location PTS.png|Secure storage with Xander's corpse ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Burning Springs}} [[Category:Burning Springs human characters]] [[Category:Fallout 76 deceased characters]] [[Category:Rust King's Army characters]] [[Category:Super Duper Mart characters]]

{{For|about=the character found at the [[World of Corn]]|the [[Collectron]] variant|Cobby Collectron}} {{Infobox character |games =FO76,FO76BS |image =FO76BS Cobby.png |race =[[Protectron]] |gender =Male programming |affiliation =[[Abraxodyne Chemical]] |role =Museum mascot |location =[[World of Corn]] |quests = |special ={{SPECIAL|0,7,0,0,0,0,0}} |derived =[[Hit Points]]: 346-7020 |level =14+ |actor =[[Wes Johnson]] |dialogue =[[Cobby/Dialogue]] |aggression =Aggressive |confidence =Foolhardy |assistance =Helps Friends and Allies |flags =LinkTerminalRobot
NoDisintegrate
NoStaggerSpell |perks =ImmuneToPoison
ImmuneToRadiation |factions =RobotFaction |class =RobotClass |CK race =ProtectronRace |voice type =Burn_Cornbot_RobotProtectron |designer = |edid =Burn_Cornhenge_Cornbot |formid ={{ID|007fe5fb}} |refid ={{ID|00804709}} }} {{Quotation|{{tooltip|Can you imagine a world without corn?|Wistful, spoken as if such a thing were utterly impossible and hard to imagine.}}|sound=Cobby 007fe5f1 1.ogg}} '''Cobby''' is a unique [[Protectron (Fallout 76)|Protectron]] found at the [[World of Corn]] in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76BS}}. ==Background== {{Main|World of Corn}} Cobby was the mascot of the [[World of Corn]], a museum on [[Corn (Fallout 76)|corn]], owned and operated by [[Abraxodyne Chemical]] to push a corporate agenda, including promotion of its pesticide prodcuts. As a [[Protectron]] decorated to look like an ear of corn, Cobby acted as a guide for visitors to the World of Corn, leading them through the facility and dispensing facts related to corn.Cobby: ''"Corn reaches for the sun! Corn stalks can grow taller than thirty feet! Can you imagine if you were thirty feet tall? You could if you were a corn stalk."''
([[Cobby/Dialogue|Cobby's dialogue]]) Cobby was found to be popular with [[child]]ren, and bolstered Abraxodyne's objectives of increasing company reputation. Advertising employees developed ideas for a [[Media|radio serial]] featuring Cobby; it is not stated if it ever entered production, but site administrator [[Ian Bentley]] hoped to acquire commercial airtime for the series during ''[[The Silver Shroud (franchise)|The Silver Shroud]]''.[[World of Corn terminal entries#Cobby's Appeal|World of Corn terminal entries; World of Corn administrator terminal, Cobby's Appeal]] Because of Cobby's value to the World of Corn, Bentley aggressively managed Cobby's presence; at one point, he left a scathing harangue directed at employees who did not turn Cobby off at the end of the day, citing concerns of wear-and-tear and "asset depreciation."[[Hey idiots]] Although the World of Corn was abandoned in the wake of the [[Great War]], Cobby was left on-site, and he still roams the premises by [[Timeline (2100-2149)#2105|2105]], talking about corn and defending the museum from various nearby hostile [[Fallout 76 creatures|creatures]]. At some point, a [[Rust raider]] from the [[Rust King's Army]] scavenged the World of Corn, but was attacked and stung by [[Radscorpion (Fallout 76)|radscorpions]] that had burrowed in the cornfield area of the property. As he died, the raider lamented, "the last thing I hear is going to be corn trivia," referring to Cobby.[[The mound]] ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |killable =yes |locations =[[World of Corn]] }} ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath =empty }} ==Notes== A different version of Cobby is available at [[CAMP]]s as a [[Collectron]], the [[Cobby Collectron]]. This Collectron collects corn, corn-related consumables, and other vegetables, into the [[Cobby Collectron station]]. ==Appearances== Cobby appears only {{In|FO76BS}}. ==Gallery== FO76BS World of Corn 04.png|Cobby inside the museum FO76BS World of Corn 06.png|Cobby in the Protectron pod FO76BS Cobby dead.png|Cobby, after being killed, with a destroyed shell ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Burning Springs}} {{Navbox robots}} [[Category:Burning Springs robots and computers]] [[Category:Protectron characters]] [[ru:Кукуру]]

Perhaps you can recommend a local peculiarity?|sound=Smiling Man 0068eb5e_1.ogg}} The '''Smiling Man''', also known as '''Indrid Cold''', is a mysterious person [[Fallout 76 random encounters#The Smiling Man|randomly encountered]] in [[Appalachia]] {{In|FO76MI}}. ==Background== The Smiling Man's face rests in an exaggerated, unsettling smile, which appears to be wider than should be possible. He wears an antiquated dark gray suit. He claims he is either "seeking a seeker who cannot be found" or teases he may simply be lost. His comments suggest he is returning to Appalachia, possibly from before the [[Great War]], as he says much has changed during his absence. He claims to want only happiness for you.[[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault 76 dweller]]: ''"What do you want from me?"''
Smiling Man: ''"Not from you. For you. I want only happiness for you."''
([[Smiling Man/Dialogue|Smiling Man's dialogue]]) At some point, he came across [[Steven Scarberry]], who felt the Smiling Man had a cold personality. Steven, a pilgrim of the [[Cult of the Mothman]], later speculated that they may be looking for similar things.[[Steven Scarberry]]: ''"{{Tooltip|A very friendly man. While his personality was cold, he could not shake his smile. I feel as though we were looking for similar things.|Remembering a previous adventure}}"''
([[Steven Scarberry/Dialogue|Steven Scarberry's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |quests started = |essential = |ally = |allyfurn = |wares = |caps = |bonus = |other = |romance = |encounters =[[Fallout 76 random encounters#The Smiling Man|The Smiling Man]]
(scene-type encounter) }} ===Other interactions=== If the Smiling Man is attacked, he will disappear in a burst of shadow identical to a fleeing [[Mothman]]. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel =[[Jack gourdon outfit|Jack gourdon black outfit]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Notes== * A cartoon depiction of the Smiling Man appears on the scoreboard for ''[[Rip Daring and the Cryptid Hunt]]'', the twelfth in-game [[Fallout 76 seasons|season]], which also features several other cryptids. * The Smiling Man seems to identify himself as the historical figure Indrid Cold. He introduces himself as "Indrid," and states "I am Cold" when his coat is commented upon. He never says that his full name is "Indrid Cold," though his delivery and the capitalization of Cold imply it is his surname. * His comment ''"Ever dance with a devil under a blue moon?"'' foreshadows the [[Blue Devil]], a [[Cryptids|cryptid]] added in the ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'' update. * One [[The Whitespring Resort terminal entries#5473162|terminal]] at the [[The Whitespring Resort|Whitespring Refuge]], added in the ''[[Expeditions: The Pitt]]'' update, may have been foreshadowing the Smiling Man. Purportedly, a catatonic patient was left with the [[Responders]] by a passing figure only identified as "[[Bob (Expeditions: The Pitt)|Bob]]." People repeatedly mentioned feeling cold around this unmoving patient, until the night he suddenly disappeared. Nobody saw the patient depart or formally discharged him. A second commentator immediately criticized the report as a "ghost story."[[The Whitespring Resort terminal entries##5473162|The Whitespring Resort terminal entries; clinic terminal, #5473162]]:
''"[PATIENT ID# 5473162]''
''Admitted to clinic unconscious and with no visible external trauma, signs of internal injury, or evidence of illness beyond their unconscious state. Patient was brought in by an individual who only gave their name as "[[Bob (Expeditions: The Pitt)|Bob]]", and who departed suddenly before more information could be taken. Patient was breathing steadily and heartrate was normal.''
''Intravenous fluids were administered along with vitamin injections. Resources for feeding a comatose patient were unavailable and attempts to manually feed them were unsuccessful, but the patient showed no signs of starvation despite this lack of nutrition. During two weeks of observation, no change in the patient's state was noticed.''
''Clinic staff reported feeling oddly cold when near the patient, and several accused the patient of somehow being responsible for the sudden failure of a number of pieces of electrical equipment in the vicinity. Two weeks after admission, the patient's bed was found empty during the night shift attendant's rounds. A search of the Refuge and its grounds found no sign of the patient, nor could any witness to their departure be located.''
''[ADMINISTRATOR NOTE: Can we please keep the [[Cryptids#Ghost|ghost]] stories out of our medical records? We're in a big drafty building with a bunch of salvaged equipment, and people come and go all the time without any of us noticing. We're supposed to be doctors, damn it.]"'' * One of [[Clyde]]'s terminal entries at the [[Middle Mountain Pitstop]] mentions a strange man who visited the bar, describing him as "grinning from ear to ear, wider than should be possible." While this may reference the Smiling Man, the mysterious customer in the entry is also described as not speaking a single word, unlike the Smiling Man.[[Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries#Bad Juju|Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal entries]] ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|I am Cold. You may call me Indrid. What are you called?|sound=Smiling Man 0068eb65_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|I see the moon, and the moon sees me.|sound=Smiling Man 0068eb55_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|Ever dance with a devil under a blue moon?|sound=Smiling Man 0068eb6c_1.ogg}} * {{Inline quote|You have my thanks for your time and company. Before I forget, I must go. I do hope to see you again.|sound=Smiling Man 0068eb6f_1.ogg}} ==Appearances== The Smiling Man appears only {{In|FO76MI}}. ==Behind the scenes== ===Real-life context=== [[File:User Anachorite Image Comics Indrid Cold.png|thumb|220px|As depicted by Image Comics[https://aiptcomics.com/2022/01/12/mothman-indrid-cold-department-of-truth/ The true origin of the Mothman legend]]] * The Smiling Man, better known by his given name [[w:c:themothman:Indrid Cold|Indrid Cold]], is an Appalachian urban legend associated with the Mothman. Cold himself is sometimes described as a [[cryptid]]. ** In November 1966, a West Virginia resident named Woodrow Derenberger reported seeing a light on the road ahead of him. Supposedly, when he approached it, Woodrow met a man whose unnerving smile did not ever fade. The man spoke telepathically to Woodrow and asked for his name. The man introduced himself as Cold, and assured Woodrow that he meant no harm and wished him only happiness.[https://dailyyonder.com/woodrow-derenberger-and-the-legend-of-indrid-cold/2021/12/03/ Local Lore: Woodrow Derenberger and the Legend of Indrid Cold] This is why the Smiling Man in ''Fallout 76'' says ''"I want only happiness for you."'' ** He was described as standing with his arms crossed over his chest and his hands tucked under his armpits (as if to keep them warm), gesturing with his elbows. This aspect is not reflected in the animations or text of the game. ** The same month, the Mothman was first spotted in Point Pleasant. Ufologist [[wikipedia:John Keel|John A. Keel]] first connected the two in his 1970 book ''Strange Creatures from Time and Space'', which was later used as the basis for his 1975 book ''[[wikipedia:The Mothman Prophecies|The Mothman Prophecies]]''. ** Fortean researchers and ufologists generally hold Indrid Cold to be a non-human or illusory entity. *** In the film adaptation of ''The Mothman Prophecies'', Indrid is depicted only in silhouette. He is briefly seen with the wings of a moth. *** As discussed in the book, Derenberger later reported being visited by Men in Black, which are similarly understood in UFO lore to be deeply uncanny pseudo-humans. [[The Emissary]] appears to be based on the legend of the Men in Black. ** Skeptics claim that the encounters were embellished significantly by John Keel and Gray Barker compared to the initial details of Derenberger's reports. ===Cultural references=== * One of the Smiling Man's idle lines is ''"Yesterday upon the stair, I met a man who wasn't there. He wasn't there again today. Oh, how I wish he'd go away."'' This is a direct quote from the 1899 poem "[[wikipedia:Antigonish (poem)|Antigonish]]" by [[wikipedia:William Hughes Mearns|William Hughes Mearns]]. The poem is about a ghost in a haunted house. * Another one of the Smiling Man's idle lines is ''"Ah, but this is wondrous strange."'' This is a quote from [[William Shakespeare]]'s ''[[wikipedia:Hamlet|Hamlet]]'', act 1 scene 5, in which the eponymous main character says, ''"O day and night, but this is wondrous strange!"'' *One of the Smiling Man's greetings is ''"I've heard the moon can be belewe and I trust that to be true."'' "Belewe" is an unusual term; it is actually an Old English spelling for "blue," and is associated in astronomy with [[wikipedia:Blue moon|blue moons]]. The first written usage of the term "blue moon" in English contained this "belewe" spelling. * Another one of the Smiling Man's greetings is ''"Ever dance with a devil under a blue moon?"'' This is a reference to a similar line from the 1989 film ''[[wikipedia:Batman (1989 film)|Batman]]'', said by the Joker: ''"Ever danced with the devil in the pale moonlight?"'' ===Development=== * The Smiling Man's appearance changed slightly from the [[Public Test Server]] to the live release of ''Mutation Invasion''. In testing, he had warm black hair and blue "hazy" eyes; this was changed to dark brown hair and blue "pale" eyes for the live release. * [[Steven Scarberry]] alludes to having met the Smiling Man. Steven and the Smiling Man share the same voice actor, [[Robbie Daymond]]. ==Gallery== The Smiling Man.png|Close-up FO76 Smiling Man encounter.png|Found in the Ash Heap FO76 Smiling Man aim.png|Found in the Ash Heap FO76 Smiling Man disappears 2.gif|Disappearing if he is attacked FO76 Smiling Man disappears.gif|Disappearing if he is attacked Smiling Man scoreboard.png|As depicted on the ''[[Rip Daring and the Cryptid Hunt]]'' scoreboard ==References== {{References}} '''External links''' {{References|group=Ext}} [[Category:Fallout 76 random encounter characters]] [[Category:Mutation Invasion characters]] [[Category:Mythical figures]] [[Category:Cryptids]] [[Category:Insect characters]] [[ru:Улыбающийся человек]]
